# Android app (s3-android)

Status (2026-11-05, android-integration-1): **the original S3.EXE is playable on the emulator** (AVD `s3_api35`,
x86_64, release APK with arm64-v8a + x86_64). Same point as desktop s3run:

| Step | Result on the emulator |
| --- | --- |
| Launch -> main menu 800x600x16 | < 1 s, all buttons, logo, "Version 1.60" (intro AVI is skipped, no error dialog any more) |
| Tap "Single Player: Scenario" | Game Setup with the map-selection popup (Random / World size) on top |
| Tap the popup's OK | Game Setup |
| Tap Game Setup OK | players screen |
| Tap players OK (same position as Game Setup OK) | loading (3 threads, 640x480x16), in game after about 20-25 s |
| In game | castle, settlers, AI thread messages, music `MCI cdaudio play tracks 7..8` |
| Tap build menu, category, building, then a ghost site on the map | construction site placed (stakes + flag) |
| One-finger drag on the map | map scrolls with the finger (see Controls) |
| Home, then reopen | pause/resume, game continues where it was (2026-11-08: in a game it keeps running in the background, see Background play) |

Screenshots (local only, not in git): `scratch/android-shots/attempt1-1.png` (menu), `-2` (Game Setup), `-5` (in game),
`-6`/`-7` (build menu, placement markers), `-9` (construction site), `-16` (after resume).

Performance (x86_64 emulator, 4 vCPU, release): menu idle; loading ~125 M guest instructions/s; in game about
**30 presents/s at ~95 M instructions/s**, engine thread ~77-92 % of one core, `android_main` ~11 %. RSS ~200 MB.
Desktop showed ~48 presents/s at a similar instruction rate on another random map, so frames cost more here
(HYPOTHESIS: busier map; not profiled). The game stays responsive. A real arm64 phone was not tested yet.

**End-to-end verification 1 (2026-11-05)**: release APK with both ABIs on emulator-5610, the whole flow by
`adb shell input`: menu -> Single Player -> popup OK -> soft keyboard (`ABC` button) typing into the game name ->
Game Setup OK -> players OK -> in game (~25 s) -> build menu, Woodcutter's Hut, tap a ghost site -> construction
site -> computer icon -> Save Game -> slot 1 ("Game Saved") -> Back (harmless) -> Home + reopen (game continues) ->
drag scroll -> Quit Game -> YES -> Game Statistics (tap) -> main menu -> Load Game -> entry -> saved game loads and
continues. The cursor shows on every screen. In game ~102 M instr/s, ~30 presents/s, process ~96 % CPU, RSS 225 MB.
Screenshots `scratch/android-shots/verify1-*.png` (list in [status.md](status.md)).

Tap coordinates used for testing (emulator screen 2400x1080, landscape): menu 800x600 is drawn at scale 1.8 with x
offset 267 buffer px, so `screen = ((267 + gx) * 1.8, gy * 1.8)`: Single Player: Scenario `778 423`, map popup OK
`1615 841`, Game Setup OK and players OK (same spot) `1795 1021`. In game 640x480: scale 2.25, offset 214: build menu `538 376`.
Both mappings put the 4:3 frame at the same screen x (480), so a screenshot does not tell which mode is active:
**Load Game is 800x600** (entry `300 126` in 800x600 = screen `1020 227`; using the 640x480 formula misses).
More in-game taps (640x480 game coords): first category `25 200`, first building `37 237`, computer icon `21 452`,
Save Game `68 225`, slot 1 `40 244`, Quit Game `68 420`, YES `38 420`; Game Statistics: tap anywhere.

Code: `port/crates/s3-android` (crate `s3-android`, library `libs3android.so`), `port/android/` (manifest, icon),
`port/scripts/build-apk.sh`, `port/scripts/run-emulator.sh`.

## App facts

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Package / label | `com.settlers3port.app` / "Settlers 3 Port" |
| Activity | `android.app.NativeActivity`, `lib_name` = `s3android`. No Gradle. Since 2026-11-08 `hasCode=true`: one small Java class `com.settlers3port.app.GameService` (background play foreground service, `port/android/java`, javac + d8 in `build-apk.sh`) |
| SDK | minSdk 26 (AAudio), targetSdk 35, landscape (`sensorLandscape`), fullscreen theme, keep-screen-on flag |
| ABIs | `arm64-v8a` (phones) and `x86_64` (emulator). The `.so` files are stripped and stored uncompressed (`extractNativeLibs=false`), aligned for 16 KiB pages |
| Game dir | `/sdcard/Android/data/com.settlers3port.app/files/game` (= `getExternalFilesDir()/game`). The user copies their own install there. **The APK contains no game files** |
| Data dir | `/sdcard/Android/data/com.settlers3port.app/files/data` (registry JSON, overlay of written files, saves). `jit.txt` there containing `1` switches the optional arm64 JIT on at the next engine start (perf-jit, [cpu.md](cpu.md#jit-optional-aarch64-perf-jit-2026-11-07); logged as `jit: true`) |
| Log tag | `s3port` (`adb logcat -s s3port`) |
| Launcher icon | **Default: our own adaptive icon** (`res/drawable/ic_launcher.xml` = background `ic_launcher_bg` navy radial gradient, foreground `ic_launcher_fg` roman numeral "III" in white serif letters with a red outline, `ic_launcher_mono` for themed icons). Style inspired by the Settlers United launcher icon ("III" over "IV"), drawn from scratch as vector paths, no game or SU pixels, no "Settlers" wordmark. Safe for published APKs. **`--game-icon` (personal builds only)**: `build-apk.sh` extracts the 32x32 4 bpp `RT_ICON` (id 11, Settlers III crest) from the user's local `game-files/gog-s3-ultimate/S3.EXE` (override `S3_ICON_EXE`) with `tools/s3_icon.py` into `port/target/apk/icon-res/drawable-*dpi` and links it as an aapt2 overlay. That APK contains Ubisoft artwork: never publish it |
| Dev switches | Files in the data dir read at engine start: `jit.txt` (`1` = arm64 JIT on), `fps-cap.txt` (frame cap, `0` = unlimited; default 60) |
| Signing | debug keystore `port/target/debug.keystore` (generated by build-apk.sh, password `android`, gitignored) |

Uninstalling the app deletes `files/` including the pushed game copy (normal Android behaviour for app-specific dirs).
On the rooted test phone the copy can be kept across a reinstall (e.g. new signing key): `su` `mv` `files/game` and
`files/data` to `/data/media/0/s3port-backup`, uninstall + install + launch once, `mv` them back, then
`chown -R <new uid>:ext_data_rw` and `chcon -R <context of the new files dir>` (`ls -laZ`; the MLS categories change
with the uid). Done 2026-11-07.

## Build

```sh
cd port
scripts/build-apk.sh                 # release, arm64-v8a + x86_64 -> target/apk/settlers3port.apk
scripts/build-apk.sh --abi x86_64    # emulator only (faster)
scripts/build-apk.sh --shell         # without the `engine` cargo feature: status screen/input/audio only
```

`--shell` exists because the other crates are edited in parallel and are sometimes briefly broken; the shell
build (`cargo build -p s3-android --no-default-features`) depends only on `s3-runtime`. Sizes: release
`libs3android.so` about 4.6 MB per ABI after `--strip-debug`; the APK with both ABIs is about 9.3 MB.

Steps in the script: `cargo ndk -t arm64-v8a -t x86_64 --platform 26 build --release -p s3-android`
(`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=port/target`, `-j 4`), `aapt2 compile/link` with `platforms/android-35/android.jar`, add
`lib/<abi>/libs3android.so` (stripped with the NDK's `llvm-strip --strip-debug`, `zip -0`), `zipalign -P 16 4`,
`apksigner sign` + `verify`. Runs on Linux and on Windows Git Bash (2026-11-07: SDK `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Android\Sdk`, NDK prebuilt `windows-x86_64`, `.exe`/`.bat` tool suffixes, `python` instead of `python3`, libs added with Python `zipfile` stored since there is no `zip`). Tools: build-tools 36.0.0, NDK 27.2.12479018, cargo-ndk 4.1 in `~/.cargo/bin`.
The script refuses to build with less than 2 GB free disk.

Host unit tests (letterbox math, MotionEvent -> pointer events, audio ring/resampler, key map + chars, status and first-run screens, Host impl):
`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=port/target cargo test -p s3-android -j 4` (on Windows add `--lib`: the cdylib cannot link the GLES/EGL symbols for the host).

## Emulator (our AVD only)

`scripts/run-emulator.sh` manages **only** AVD `s3_api35` on console port 5610 (`adb -s emulator-5610`).
Never use other AVDs or `emulator-5600` (other projects).

```sh
scripts/run-emulator.sh start            # create AVD if missing, boot headless (-no-window, swiftshader, -no-audio)
scripts/run-emulator.sh install launch   # install target/apk/settlers3port.apk, (re)start the app
scripts/run-emulator.sh push             # copy game files (see below)
scripts/run-emulator.sh logcat           # dump the app log (logcat 30 = follow for 30 s)
scripts/run-emulator.sh shot menu        # -> scratch/android-shots/menu.png
scripts/run-emulator.sh tap 1200 540     # tap in screen pixels (the emulator screen is 2400x1080 in landscape)
scripts/run-emulator.sh stop             # force-stop the app, emulator keeps running
scripts/run-emulator.sh kill-emulator    # shut down s3_api35
```

AVD: `system-images;android-35;google_apis;x86_64`, device `pixel_6` (1080x2400), `hw.ramSize=3072`,
`disk.dataPartition.size=6G`, 4 cores. `S3_EMU_AUDIO=1 scripts/run-emulator.sh start` boots with host audio
(off by default so a night run makes no noise). Cold boot takes about 45 s. The emulator log is written to
`scratch/emulator-s3_api35.log`.

## Game files on the device

`run-emulator.sh push` copies from `GAME_DIR` (default `game-files/gog-s3-ultimate`) only what the game reads
(per [wine-trace.md](../reverse-engineering/wine-trace.md)):

- `S3.EXE`, `regs.cmd` (the GOG registry defaults; the registry HLE imports it from the game dir on first
  start, logcat: `registry: applied 48 values from .../regs.cmd`), the small top-level `*.DAT` marker files (`DATA.DAT`, `S3CD1.DAT`, `S3GOLD1.DAT`, ...);
- `GFX/*.f8007e01f.dat` only: the RGB565 set (118 MB). The port always reports a 565 primary surface, so the
  555 set (`*.7c003e01f.dat`) is never opened;
- `SND`, `MUSIC` (the Ogg CD tracks), `S3` (intro AVI, missions), `Map/SINGLE`, `Map/TUTORIAL`;
- without `--minimal`: also `S3QOTA`, `S3MCD`, `Map/MULTI`, `Map/User` (about 1.2 GB in total; `--minimal` is
  about 0.6 GB).

Not copied: Windows DLLs (our HLE replaces them), `Save/` (the user's saves), manuals, editor, launcher files.
The script checks free space on the device first. On a real phone use the same target directory, either
`adb push` or a file manager with access to `Android/data` (newer Android versions restrict this; adb always
works).

**Since 2026-11-08 the launcher (below) replaces the first-run screen**; the engine no longer waits for files by
itself. Old behaviour, kept in `run_engine` / `screen.rs` for tests: **First-run screen** (android-ux, verified on the emulator): while any of `S3.EXE`, `GFX`, `SND`, `Map`
(`frontend::REQUIRED_PARTS`, case-insensitive) is missing, the app shows a plain "Game files needed" screen
(`screen::first_run_screen`) with the folder as the user sees it (`Android/data/com.settlers3port.app/files/game/`,
highlighted), the full path, what to copy, which parts are still missing, the `adb push` command and the hint that
Android 11+ file managers cannot open `Android/data`. It checks again every 2 s; once everything is there it waits
3 s more (a push may still be running) and starts by itself (verified: moved the game dir away and back while the
app ran). Screenshot: `scratch/android-shots/ux-firstrun-s.png`.

## Launcher (home screen, 2026-11-08)

User request: our own screen first, not straight into the game. `launcher.rs` (platform independent, tested on
the desktop) records a window-resolution `s3_mods::layer::DrawList` (same recorder/fonts as the in-game overlay);
`android.rs` publishes it with `Shared::set_launcher(Some(list))` and the presenter (`present.rs`) draws it over a
plain 4x4 fill frame instead of the game. The activity loop feeds it the first finger (window px), Back and typed
characters; it returns `Request::{Play, Keyboard(bool), Quit}`. Sizes are in dp (`density_dpi / 160`, capped so
~330 dp of height fit), the page scrolls by dragging (scroll bar on the right), and it is redrawn on every window
size change (fold / unfold) and only republished when the list hash changes.

- **Home**: title + version, game files card (`REQUIRED_PARTS` present / which are missing, S3.EXE version from
  sha256: GOG 1.60 = supported, 3,842,048 bytes other = "1.60 build, patches off", else unknown; folder),
  **Play** (green; grey "Play (game files missing)" opens Game files), Settings, Game files, Quit, last message
  ("The game was closed ..." or the engine error). Wide windows (>= 640 dp) use two columns.
- **Settings**: buttons with the in-game labels (UI: Classic Touch / Mobile HUD, Screen, Filter, FPS counter,
  FPS limit (+ display Hz like the game menu), FPS position, Fast speed, Game time, Unit paths, Group buttons,
  Vibration, HUD - / HUD n% / HUD +); each tap edits and saves `mods-settings.json` (`Settings::save`) at once.
  "Internet multiplayer relay" text field (soft keyboard; Enter or a tap elsewhere saves `relay-url.txt`,
  "Default" deletes it = built-in LAN relay). `run_engine` reads `relay-url.txt` at every start (and clears
  `S3_RELAY_URL` when it is gone). 3 / 2 / 1 columns by width.
- **Game files**: card, **Start / Stop upload server**, Check again, and while the server runs the address
  `http://<phone Wi-Fi IP>:8080/?k=<token>` in large text plus a QR code (`qrcode` crate, MIT/Apache, no default
  features), received files / MB, current file + bytes, last error; adb / MTP hints. Files are re-checked every
  2 s (server on) or 5 s.
- **Back**: sub-page -> Home (or ends relay editing); on Home it quits (finish + `process::exit`).
- **Play** spawns the engine thread (`run_engine`) and hides the launcher. When the engine run ends
  (`Shared::engine_end`: Exit Game, engine error/panic) the activity joins the thread, clears the frame slot and
  shows the launcher again with a message; settings are reloaded (the game menus may have changed them). Play
  again builds a **new `Engine` in the same process** (process-wide statics are only caches/queues: fonts, menu
  layout cache, haptics queue, embedded relay port).
- Scripts: `am start -n com.settlers3port.app/android.app.NativeActivity --ez play true` skips the launcher once
  (if the files are there); `run-emulator.sh` and `tools/phone-fps.sh` pass it.
- Debug / tests: `<data dir>/game-dir.txt` (one absolute path) replaces the game dir (test the missing-files
  state or uploads without touching the real install).
- Desktop preview of every page at the Fold4 sizes: `S3_LAUNCHER_PREVIEW=<dir> cargo test -p s3-android --lib
  launcher_preview -- --ignored` (PNGs; put them under `scratch/`).

**Web upload** (`upload.rs`, std::net only, a thread per connection): binds `0.0.0.0:8080` (or the next free of
8080-8089, else any), token = 6 random chars, needed on every request (403 page otherwise). Routes: `GET /` page,
`GET /status` (missing parts, files, bytes), `GET /stat?path=` (size or -1, the page skips files with the same
size), `POST /upload?path=` (raw body, Content-Length required, `Expect: 100-continue` handled, max 4 GiB per
file). Paths: `/` or `\` separated, no `.`/`..`/empty/`:`/control chars, <= 12 parts; each part reuses an existing
entry of another case (`gfx/` + `GFX/x`), written to `<name>.upload-part` then renamed. The page (no external
resources): folder picker (`<input webkitdirectory>`) or drag and drop of the folder; the root is the folder that
holds `S3.EXE` (shortest path; else the single top folder), only files below it are sent, one XHR per file with a
progress bar, MB/s and a log; it polls `/status` every 5 s and says when all required parts are there. The phone
IP: `s3_net::lan::primary_ipv4()` if private, else the first private interface address. No zip upload (would
need an unzip crate; the folder upload covers it). The Android folder picker (ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE) needs
an `onActivityResult`, i.e. a Java activity of our own: not done yet.

## Runtime design

**2026-11-05 (display agent): presentation moved to a third thread**, the EGL/GLES render thread
(`present.rs`, `gl.rs`): GPU scaling with display modes Fit / Fill / Stretch / Native wide, sharp-bilinear filter,
high refresh rate request, cutout area used, engine never waits for the display. The activity thread now only
handles lifecycle and input (touch mapping through `s3_mods::display::Viewport`). Details:
[display.md](display.md). The description below is the older two-thread design; the frame/status parts now go to
the render thread.

Two threads (`crates/s3-android/src`):

- **Activity thread** (`android.rs`, `android_main`): polls android-activity events, owns the `ANativeWindow`
  and the AAudio stream, turns input into `HostEvent`s, draws.
- **Engine thread** (`frontend.rs`, `run_engine`, 16 MiB stack): waits for `S3.EXE`, builds `s3_engine::Engine`
  with `AndroidHost`, calls `run_for_ms(16)` in a loop. It sleeps while paused. A panic or a machine stop is
  caught; the stop reason and `Engine::summary()` are shown on screen and written to logcat.

They share `frontend::Shared`: the newest frame (`present` copies into a reused buffer and wakes the activity
loop through `AndroidAppWaker`), the input event queue, the status (phase/title/body), pause and quit flags, and
the audio ring.

**Presentation** (`layout.rs`): the window buffer geometry is set to the game resolution widened (or heightened)
to the window's aspect ratio, format `R5G6B5`. The frame is copied unscaled into the middle with black bars and
the compositor scales the buffer to the screen. Example: 800x600 on a 2400x1080 screen gives a 1334x600 buffer
with the frame at x offset 267. The geometry is recomputed on window init/resize and on game mode changes
(640x480 in game, 800x600 in menus). To learn the real window size, the geometry is first reset to 0x0.

**Status screen** (`screen.rs`): colour bars, grid and corner markers (red top-left, green top-right, blue
bottom-left, white bottom-right) plus text in the 8x8 `font8x8` font (MIT). It is shown before the first
frame: "Starting", "Game files missing" with the copy instructions, the engine stop reason. If the engine stops
after it has drawn frames, the reason is drawn as a panel over the last frame. The app never shows a black screen.

**Lifecycle** (menus; in a game see Background play below): `Pause` -> `HostEvent::Pause`, the engine thread stops running slices, AAudio is paused,
rendering stops. `Resume` -> `HostEvent::Resume`, AAudio restarts. The guest clock (`Host::now_ms`) does not
advance while paused, so game timers do not jump. `TerminateWindow` drops the window (the engine keeps its
frames). `Destroy` sets quit and joins the engine thread.

**Audio** (`audio.rs`): `Host::queue_audio(samples, rate, channels)` is converted to 44100 Hz stereo i16 (linear
interpolation, mono duplicated) and pushed into a lock-free SPSC ring (1 s). The AAudio data callback
(shared mode, `PCM_I16`, 2 channels, 44100 Hz) pops from it and plays silence on underrun. Overflow drops new
samples. `audio_queued_frames` reports the ring fill in the caller's rate for mixer pacing. An AAudio error
callback (device change) reopens the stream. If AAudio cannot open, the app runs silent.

## Background play (2026-11-08)

User request: a game that was not closed keeps running when the app goes to the background; an ongoing
notification shows that it runs and the game time; game messages ("coal found", tutorial text, chat) come as
notifications while in the background.

| Situation on `MainEvent::Pause` | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| In a game (`Shared::in_game` = `s3_mods::res::in_game`, a game frame within the last second) | **Game keeps running**: no `HostEvent::Pause`, the engine keeps running slices. Frame cap lowered to 10 fps (`frontend::background_fps`, restored on resume; nobody sees the frames, the logic does not depend on them). **Sound muted** (AAudio stream paused; the ring is cleared on resume so no stale sound plays). Foreground service started |
| Menus (not in a game) | Old behaviour: engine paused, guest clock stopped |
| Background, then the game is no longer in a game for 5 s (game ended, statistics, main menu) | Service stopped, engine paused like in the menus |
| `Resume` | Service stopped (its notifications go with it), frame cap restored, audio ring cleared + stream restarted |
| Swiped away from recents | `GameService.onTaskRemoved` kills the process (the user closed the game) |

Parts:

- `port/android/java/com/settlers3port/app/GameService.java`: the only Java code. Intents (explicit component, not
  exported): `START` (`startForegroundService`, extra `game_ms`): `startForeground` with type `specialUse`
  (API 34+; manifest `<property PROPERTY_SPECIAL_USE_FGS_SUBTYPE>`) and a partial wake lock (the game also runs with
  the screen off); `UPDATE` (`startService`): re-sync the chronometer; `EVENT` (`startService`, extra `text`, lines
  joined with `\n`): one notification in channel "Game events" (IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT, group, InboxStyle for several
  lines, BigText for one, auto-cancel). `stopService` -> `onDestroy` releases the wake lock and removes the ongoing
  and all event notifications. Ongoing notification: channel "Game running" (IMPORTANCE_LOW), title
  "Settlers III — running", `setUsesChronometer(true)` + `setWhen(now - game_ms)` (counts up by itself), tap opens
  the app (launch intent, `FLAG_IMMUTABLE`). Small icon `res/drawable/ic_notify.xml` (our monochrome "III", cropped).
- Manifest: `FOREGROUND_SERVICE`, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_SPECIAL_USE`, `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`, `WAKE_LOCK`.
- `bgservice.rs` (JNI from the activity thread): `start` runs synchronously inside the `Pause` handler, while the
  activity is still visible, which Android 12+ requires for a foreground-service start. `update`, `event`, `stop`.
  `ask_notification_permission`: `requestPermissions(POST_NOTIFICATIONS)` on Android 13+ at the first focus in the
  menus, once per install (marker `data/notification-permission-asked.txt`). Without the permission the service
  still runs; Android only hides its notifications.
- Game time: `[0x7dfd48]` (logic tick counter, +1 per 64 ms of game time) * 64, read by the engine thread after each
  slice (`frontend::sync_background` -> `Shared::game_ms`). The chronometer counts wall time; with fast speed
  (2x-8x) or the in-game pause it drifts, so `background::Background::drift` re-syncs (`UPDATE`) when it is off by
  more than 3 s.
- Messages: `s3_mods::messages::take_new_lines()` (process-wide queue, filled by the composite hook: a line text not
  shown in the previous frame is new; max 32 kept). The engine drains it every slice; only while
  `Shared::background` the lines go to `Shared::bg_lines`. The activity loop coalesces them
  (`background.rs`: at most one notification per 4 s, up to 6 newest lines each, consecutive duplicates dropped).
  The render thread keeps drawing game frames in the background (10 fps), so the hook still sees the lines.
- Build: `build-apk.sh` step 3 `javac --release 11 -classpath android.jar` + `d8 --release --min-api 26` ->
  `classes.dex` in the APK (JDK 25 on the dev PC works).

Verified on the Galaxy Z Fold4 (2026-11-08, journal "Background play"): service foreground (`dumpsys activity
services`: `isForeground=true`), chronometer notification, tap returns to the game, message notification from the
tutorial, game time keeps advancing with the screen off (1 s game per 1 s wall at 1x). Not yet exercised: drift
re-sync at fast speed, the 5 s out-of-game pause, swipe-away. The engine's 10 s log line shows
`game time N s (background)`. Screenshots (local only): `scratch/android-shots/bg/`.

## Foldables, resizing (2026-11-08)

The activity is `android:resizeableActivity="true"`. With `false`, unfolding a Galaxy Z Fold4 while the game ran
kept the app in **size compatibility mode**: still at the cover screen's size, scaled and letterboxed on the inner
screen (`dumpsys activity activities`: `mSizeCompatScale=0.93955094 mSizeCompatBounds=Rect(0, 482 - 2176, 1331)`).
Now the window follows the display: `MainEvent::WindowResized` / `ConfigChanged` (handled without a restart,
`configChanges` lists screenSize etc.) -> `Presenter::set_window` -> new EGL surface size -> viewport, window
layer and zoom aspect follow (`zoom::aspect` from the published window size). Verified on the Fold4: inner screen
2176x1812 full screen in game (120 fps); `wm size 1300x2176` while in game -> the frame re-laid out for 2176x1300
at once, `wm size reset` -> back. Split screen / pop-up windows are allowed now too. Not tested: an actual
fold/unfold while in game (needs the person; same code path), and whether Samsung's "continue apps on cover
screen" setting keeps the app running when folding.
The full-screen menu layouts were made for wide screens; on the near-square inner screen they are placed small
in the middle (works, could use layouts for ~1.2:1).

## Controls

Since 2026-11-05 the activity thread only reports fingers: every MotionEvent becomes raw `HostEvent::Pointer`
events (`touch.rs`: Down/PointerDown -> Down, Move -> Move for every pointer with a changed position,
PointerUp/Up -> Up, Cancel -> Cancel for all; game pixels via the letterbox). Gesture recognition and what a gesture
does run in `s3-mods` on the engine thread, identical to the desktop `s3run --inject` touch commands:
**see [touch.md](touch.md)** (in game: tap = select / move / attack / place, ✕ or two-finger tap = cancel, drag = camera
with inertia, long-press-drag = box select, pinch = resolution zoom; no long-press right click). Menus: tap = left
click, drag = left drag, two-finger tap = right click, three-finger tap = soft keyboard. Not yet tried on the
emulator/phone (multi-touch needs a real device or emulator console gestures): unit-tested + desktop-verified.

Former mapping (`TouchMapper`, removed): tap = left click, long press = right click, map drag = mirrored right drag.

The 60 ms gap between button down and up is there because the game also polls the button state
(DirectInput buffer, GetAsyncKeyState). A real mouse (ChromeOS, DeX, emulator with mouse) is passed through
directly: move, left/right/middle buttons.

**Letterbox buttons: removed 2026-11-07** (user request). There used to be ESC / ABC / RMB buttons in the black bars
(`overlay.rs`, android-ux). Their functions are covered without them: Back = Esc, three-finger tap = soft keyboard
(`Shared::keyboard_req`), two-finger tap = cancel; menus via the UI modes (Classic: floating Menu, HUD: menu sheet).
`s3_mods::set_right_next` ("next tap = right click") still exists in s3-mods but nothing on Android arms it now.

Keys (`keys.rs`): Back -> `VK_ESCAPE` (the IME takes Back first while it is open), hardware
keyboard letters, digits, arrows, Enter, Space, Tab, Backspace, Delete, Shift/Ctrl/Alt, F1-F12, PgUp/PgDn,
Home/End/Insert, comma, period. Volume keys stay with the system.

Text: for every key-down the character is taken from Android's `KeyCharacterMap` (key code + meta state, via
android-activity `device_key_character_map`) and sent as `HostEvent::Char` after the `Key` event
(`keys::char_for_key`): printable characters, plus Enter 0x0D, Backspace 0x08, Esc 0x1B, Tab 0x09 like Windows'
TranslateMessage. Once the host sends any Char, USER32 stops synthesizing WM_CHAR itself (`host_chars`), so all
chars come from the host. Keys with a character but no VK mapping get a plausible VK (`keys::vk_for_char`) or
only the Char.

**Soft keyboard**: `ABC` button or three-finger tap. On the UI thread: `InputMethodManager.showSoftInput(
activity.getCurrentFocus(), 0)` (the NativeActivity content view, like `ANativeActivity_showSoftInput`) /
`hideSoftInputFromWindow`; visibility from `getRootWindowInsets().isVisible(WindowInsets.Type.ime())`. The IME
has no real InputConnection (NativeContentView), so Android's fallback connection turns typed characters into
plain key events, which arrive through the normal input queue. Verified on the emulator (Gboard): Game Setup
"Name of the Game" field: 4x soft Backspace deleted "game", soft `h` `i` typed, `adb shell input text "Bob1"`
(Shift meta for the capital) gave "Player's hiBob1" (`scratch/android-shots/ux-ime-s.png`, `ux-typed-s.png`).
The game window is not resized for the IME (it covers the lower half; the field in Game Setup stays visible).
Note: with the emulator's `hw.keyboard=yes` the soft keyboard still showed.

**Back / Esc in the game itself** (same on desktop s3run, so game behaviour, not Android): in the **main menu**
Esc = "Exit Game": the guest calls ExitProcess. The app then closes itself (`Shared::guest_exited` ->
`Activity.finish()`, then `process::exit(0)` after `android_main` returns, so the next launch starts clean) —
like Back at the root of any Android app (verified; relaunch reaches the menu again). **In game Esc does not
open a menu** in the port (the manual lists "Esc: Exit game"; desktop s3run with `key 0x1B` in game shows no
dialog either). The in-game menu (save / end game) is the "computer" icon at the bottom of the left panel
(640x480 game ~(19,453), screen ~(525,1015)); it works since the save-load fix (gdi32 1 bpp DIB sections: the panel
text is drawn as a mask; before that the panel looked empty), see [user32-gdi32.md](user32-gdi32.md). So Back does
not open the in-game menu; Back in game is harmless (the game keeps running); use the computer icon for Save / Quit.

**Immersive fullscreen**: status and navigation bars are hidden (`WindowInsetsController.hide(systemBars())`,
behaviour "show transient bars by swipe"; fallback for API < 30: `setSystemUiVisibility(0x1706)` sticky
immersive). Re-applied on window init and on every focus gain. Android shows its one-time "Viewing full screen"
hint on the first start. `FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON` stays set while the activity is in front.

**UI-thread calls without Java code** (`uithread.rs`): View/IME calls must run on the Java main thread, but
`android_main` runs on its own thread. A Unix socket pair's read end is registered on the Java main looper
(`AndroidApp::java_main_looper().add_fd_with_callback`); `UiThread::run` queues a closure and writes one byte, the
looper then calls us on the UI thread, where the closure gets a JNI env (jni 0.22, the version android-activity
uses) and the activity object. Java exceptions are cleared and logged.

Arrow keys (hardware keyboard, `adb shell input keyevent DPAD_RIGHT`) also scroll the map (verified).

Not done yet: pinch zoom; IME-aware layout (moving the game above the keyboard).

## Multiplayer (relay)

The APK has the `INTERNET` permission. The relay URL is read once at engine start from
`/sdcard/Android/data/com.settlers3port.app/files/data/relay-url.txt` (one line, e.g. `ws://10.0.2.2:7788/` for a
relay on the PC that runs the emulator); default `ws://127.0.0.1:7777/`. Then the game's own "Multi-player Game: LAN"
menu lists "Internet (Settlers 3 Port)". Verified: the emulator joined a desktop-hosted game and played it by taps in
both UI modes (ux-verify1, [integration-log.md](integration-log.md)). In-app setting: launcher Settings ->
"Internet multiplayer relay" (2026-11-08; read at every game start).

## Install for users (phone)

1. Install the APK (`adb install -r -g settlers3port.apk`, or copy it to the phone and open it; allow unknown sources).
2. Start the app once (it creates its folder and shows "Game files missing").
3. Copy the **contents** of your GOG install folder (the folder that contains `S3.EXE`, `GFX`, `SND`, `MUSIC`, `Map`,
   `S3`, ...) to `Android/data/com.settlers3port.app/files/game/` on the phone's internal storage. With a PC:
   `port/scripts/run-emulator.sh push` logic, or simply `adb push <GOG folder>/. /sdcard/Android/data/com.settlers3port.app/files/game/`.
   Android 11+ file managers often cannot open `Android/data`; adb or a PC USB connection (MTP) usually can.
   Minimum: `S3.EXE`, `regs.cmd`, top-level `*.DAT`, `GFX/*.f8007e01f.dat`, `SND`, `MUSIC`, `S3`, `Map`.
4. Open the app again (or wait: it checks every 2 s). Saves and settings go to `.../files/data/`.

Uninstalling the app deletes both folders.

`docs/porting/architecture.md`:

```md
# Port architecture (binding contract)

Status: implemented; the game runs on desktop and Android (2026-11-06, see [status.md](status.md)). Contract written 2026-11-05. Code: `port/` (Cargo workspace, GPL-3.0-or-later).
Approach: our own host = PE loader + x86-32 **interpreter** (iced-x86 decoder) + **HLE** of the Win32/DirectX
APIs S3.EXE uses. The user's own `S3.EXE` and data run unmodified; nothing of the game is shipped.

## Crates

| Crate | What | Owner after foundation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `s3-mem` | `GuestMemory`: 4 GiB host reservation, typed reads/writes, strings, `Regions` (VirtualAlloc bookkeeping), `Heaps` (HeapAlloc) | runtime |
| `s3-cpu` | `Cpu`: x86-32 interpreter, decoded-block cache, eager EFLAGS, `fpu.rs` (x87 + MMX movq/movd/emms, see [x87-fpu.md](x87-fpu.md)) | cpu |
| `s3-runtime` | `Machine` (memory + threads + scheduler), thunk `Registry`, `ThunkResult`, `call_guest`, `HandleTable`, SEH, COM helpers, `Vfs`, `Host` trait, `FrameBuffer`, `HostEvent`, input state | runtime |
| `s3-pe` | PE32 parse/load, imports via the registry, `find_resource` / `load_string` | runtime |
| `s3-win32` | one module per DLL: kernel32, user32, gdi32, advapi32, shell32, rpcrt4, ole32, winmm (`_inmm` alias), comctl32, comdlg32, wsock32, wininet | per-DLL agents |
| `s3-dx` | ddraw, dsound, dinput, dplay: COM objects, blitter, software audio mixer, input pump, CLSID factories ([directx-hle.md](directx-hle.md)) | dx agents |
| `s3-engine` | `Engine::new(host, exe)`: registers modules, loads PE, creates the main thread, installs `s3-mods`; `run_slice`, `run_for_ms`, `summary` | runtime |
| `s3-mods` | Mod/hook framework: guest-address hooks, struct views, guest calls, per-exe-sha256 patch sets, overlay drawing, touch gestures + fallback touch->mouse, settings JSON ([mods.md](mods.md)) | mods |
| `s3-desktop` | `s3run` binary: headless or minifb window, PNG screenshots, input injection | desktop |
| `s3-frontend` | Mobile frontend parts shared by Android and iOS (plain rlib): `Shared` state + `AndroidHost`, engine thread body, launcher + upload server, touch -> pointer events, audio ring, status screen, GLES bindings and renderer (`glrender`: draws into any current GL context) | android / ios |
| `s3-android` | `libs3android.so` (NativeActivity via android-activity): lifecycle, EGL presenter (`present.rs` on `glrender`), input, AAudio, background service; re-exports `s3-frontend` modules under their old paths. See [android.md](android.md) | android |
| `s3-ios` | `libs3ios.a` (staticlib) for the Swift shell `port/ios`: C API (`port/ios/Sources/CS3iOS/include/s3ios.h`). See [ios.md](ios.md) | ios |

Dependency direction: `s3-mem` <- `s3-cpu` <- `s3-runtime` <- `s3-pe`, `s3-win32`, `s3-dx` (s3-dx does not depend on s3-win32; they meet through `s3_runtime::gdi` and `s3_runtime::audio`) <- `s3-engine` <- frontends.

## Memory map (guest addresses, `s3_mem::layout`)

| Range | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `0x00000000-0x0000FFFF` | NULL guard: the CPU raises `AccessViolation` (-> guest exception 0xC0000005) for any access here |
| `0x00010000-0x003FFFFF` | low arena: process parameters, command line, environment blocks |
| `0x00400000-0x007ECFFF` | S3.EXE image (fixed base, no relocations), region kind `Image` |
| `0x10000000-0x6FFFFFFF` | VirtualAlloc / heap segments (first fit, 64 KiB granularity) |
| `0x70000000-0x7EFFFFFF` | thread stacks (default size = PE stack reserve, 1 MiB) |
| `0x78000000+i*0x10000` | fake HMODULEs of HLE DLLs (not mapped; only handle values) |
| `0x7F000000-0x7FFEFFFF` | system area: TEB of thread slot `i` at `0x7FFDE000 - i*0x1000`, PEB at `0x7FFDF000` |
| `0xFFF00000-0xFFFFEFFF` | thunk page: each HLE function is one address (`THUNK_BASE + index`) |
| `0xFFFFF000` | `MAGIC_RETURN`: return address used by host->guest calls |

The whole 4 GiB window is mapped read/write (`MAP_NORESERVE`), so guest accesses never fault on the host.
`Regions` only answers Win32 questions (VirtualQuery, overlap, free space). Released/decommitted ranges are
zeroed with `madvise(MADV_DONTNEED)` on host-page-aligned parts (Android may use 16 KiB host pages).
Heaps keep their metadata on the host side (guest overruns cannot corrupt it); blocks are 8-byte aligned,
heap handle = guest address of the first segment, `GetProcessHeap` = `mem.process_heap()`.

## CPU (`s3-cpu`)

> Details of the integer interpreter (decode cache, threaded dispatch, exact semantics, tests, MIPS):
> [cpu.md](cpu.md). Changes since the foundation: cpuid reports **no MMX** (family 5 model 2), `jcxz`/CX loops,
> BCD ops, the popfd mask, and privileged instructions raise `GeneralProtection`.

- `Cpu { regs: [u32; 8] (EAX..EDI in encoding order, consts EAX..EDI), eip, eflags, fs_base, gs_base, fpu, instructions, cache }`.
- `run(&mut mem, max_instructions) -> CpuExit`:
  `Thunk(addr)` (EIP entered the thunk page; ESP points at the return address), `ReturnMagic`, `Budget`,
  `Halt`, `Fault { eip, kind, detail }` (EIP rewound to the faulting instruction), `Interrupt(n)` (`int3` = 3),
  `Hook(eip)` (EIP reached an address in the installed `HookAddrs`; see [mods.md](mods.md)).
- Decode cache: basic blocks (<= 64 instructions, end at any control flow) keyed by start EIP, one cache per
  `Cpu` (i.e. per guest thread; TODO share it if memory becomes an issue). `invalidate_range` /
  `Machine::invalidate_code` after code writes. S3.EXE does not modify its code (see s3-exe.md).
- Implemented: full i386/i486/Pentium integer set used by MSVC6 code (mov/movzx/movsx/lea/xchg, push/pop(ad/fd),
  call/ret/jmp/jcc/loop*/jecxz, ALU + inc/dec/neg/not, all shifts/rotates incl. rcl/rcr/shld/shrd, mul/imul
  (1/2/3 op)/div/idiv (#DE), cbw/cwde/cwd/cdq, setcc/cmovcc, bt*/bsf/bsr/bswap, xadd/cmpxchg/cmpxchg8b,
  enter/leave, string ops with rep/repe/repne (fast paths for forward movs/stos), xlat, lahf/sahf, flag ops,
  cpuid (Pentium, no MMX/SSE; see cpu.md), rdtsc (host time at 200 MHz), int/int3/into/hlt/ud2).
- Anything else goes to `fpu::exec` (x87 + MMX subset, see [x87-fpu.md](x87-fpu.md)); it returns `None` for anything
  it does not handle -> `FaultKind::Unimplemented` with the mnemonic and disassembly.
- Helpers for new instructions: `read_op/write_op(ins, i, size)`, `op_size`, `ea`, `rd/wr` (NULL check),
  `alu_add/alu_sub/alu_logic/set_szp/cond`, `get_reg/set_reg` (iced `Register`).

## Thunk ABI

1. The PE loader writes a thunk address into every IAT slot (`Registry::resolve_import`). Unknown imports get an
   *auto stub* (no handler).
2. Guest `call [IAT]` pushes the return address and jumps to the thunk; the CPU exits with `Thunk(addr)`.
3. `Machine::dispatch_thunk` counts the call, traces it, and runs the handler `fn(&mut Machine) -> ThunkResult`.
   No handler => machine stops with `UNIMPLEMENTED dll!name (called from 0x...)`.
4. `ThunkResult`:
   - `Return { eax, pop_bytes }` — EAX = value, pop return address, then `pop_bytes` (stdcall `4*nargs`, cdecl 0).
     Helpers: `ThunkResult::stdcall(eax, nargs)`, `ThunkResult::cdecl(eax)`.
   - `Return64 { eax, edx, pop_bytes }`.
   - `Done` — the handler already set EIP/ESP (e.g. RaiseException redirecting into SEH dispatch).
   - `Block` — the thread waits; EIP stays on the thunk and **the handler is called again** on the next
     scheduling round. Handlers that may block must not have side effects before deciding to block.
     `m.thread().block_since` holds the host ms when the wait started (for timeouts).
   - `Exit(code)` (ExitProcess), `ExitThread(code)`, `Error(msg)` (stop the machine).
5. COM methods are ordinary thunks named `Interface::Method` in the implementing DLL
   (`ddraw.dll!IDirectDrawSurface::Flip`); `this` is `m.arg_u32(0)`.

Registry API: `register(dll, name, handler)` (replaces), `declare(dll, name)` (stub, keeps a handler),
`declare_all`, `set_ordinal`, `lookup`, `lookup_ordinal`, `alias("_inmm.dll", "winmm.dll")`,
`module_handle(dll)` / `module_name(hmod)` (fake HMODULEs for LoadLibraryA/GetProcAddress), `describe(addr)`.
DLL names are normalized (lower case, `.dll` added, path stripped).

## Calling-convention helpers (on `Machine`)

`arg_u32(i)`, `arg_i32(i)`, `arg_ptr(i)` (= `[esp + 4 + 4*i]`), `arg_str(i)` (ANSI, `None` for NULL),
`arg_wstr(i)`, `return_address()`, `set_last_error(v)` / `last_error()` (TEB+0x34), `cpu()`, `thread()`,
`current_tid()`, `now_ms()`, `log(level, msg)`, `present(&fb)`.
Guest memory: `m.mem.read_u32/write_u32/...`, `read_cstr/write_cstr`, `read_wstr/write_wstr`, `slice/slice_mut`,
`alloc(size)` / `free(p)` (process heap, zeroed) for runtime-owned guest buffers.

Module state: `let st = m.state::<MyState>();` then `st.borrow_mut()` (type must be `Default + Send`). The guard
must not be held across `call_guest` (re-entry panics with a clear message).

## Host -> guest calls

`m.call_guest(addr, &[args]) -> u32` (WndProc, enum callbacks, timer callbacks, SEH unwind handlers):
pushes args + `MAGIC_RETURN`, runs the current thread until `ReturnMagic`, then restores **all** registers
(including ESP), so stdcall and cdecl callees both work. Nested calls are fine. While the callee blocks, the
other threads run (`run_others`). A thread inside `call_guest` (`nested > 0`) is skipped by the top-level
scheduler. Limitation: if thread B, run from inside A's nested wait, itself blocks inside a nested call waiting
for A, they deadlock (logged as no progress; not seen yet).

## Threads and scheduling

Cooperative green threads on one host thread. `Machine::create_thread(entry, param, stack, suspended)` builds
the stack (`[esp] = s3port.dll!thread_exit`, `[esp+4] = param`), the TEB (SEH list = -1, stack base/limit,
self, ids, TLS pointer = TEB+0xE10 with 64 slots, PEB, LastError) and a `Thread` kernel object handle.
`run_slice(max_instructions)`: polls host input into `m.input`, runs services (`add_service`, host-side
periodic hooks such as an audio mixer), then round-robins runnable threads with `quantum` instructions each
(default 200k). Blocked threads are retried each round. Returns `Ran(n)`, `Idle` (everything blocked; the
frontend sleeps) or `Stopped` (`stop_reason()`: `Exited`, `Unimplemented`, `Fault`, `Error`, `Quit`).
Waits: `m.is_signaled(h)` / `m.try_acquire(h)` implement Event (manual/auto), Mutex (owner + recursion),
Semaphore, Thread (signaled when exited). Critical sections are implemented by kernel32 on the guest struct
(owner/recursion), blocking when contended, with direct hand-off on Leave.
Generic waits: `m.poll_wait(&handles, wait_all, timeout_ms) -> WaitPoll` (Ready/Timeout/Failed/Pending; return
`ThunkResult::Block` on Pending) — use it for any waiting API (user32 MsgWaitForMultipleObjects too).
Frontends idle through `Machine::idle(ms)` (= `Host::idle` unless the multi-core mode is on). Experimental
multi-core mode (`Machine::enable_mt`, s3run `S3_MT=1`, never in s3det): the presenting guest thread runs on a
second host thread under a big HLE lock, see [multicore.md](multicore.md). `Machine::run_observer` is an analysis
hook around each scheduling turn (`s3det --write-trace`).
`m.pulse_event(h)`; waitable timers are `KernelObject::Timer`. Details: [kernel32.md](kernel32.md).

## Exceptions (SEH)

CPU faults become guest exceptions (0xC0000005 with [write, addr], 0xC0000094, 0xC000001D, 0xC0000096,
int3 -> 0x80000003). `seh::raise_exception` writes EXCEPTION_RECORD + CONTEXT (0x2CC bytes) below ESP and calls
the FS:[0] chain handlers **in the guest** with return address `s3port.dll!seh_handler_return`
(ContinueExecution resumes from the CONTEXT, ContinueSearch goes to the next frame; no handler = machine stops
with "unhandled exception"). MSVC `__except` handlers unwind via `RtlUnwind` (implemented in kernel32 with
`seh::rtl_unwind`, which calls handlers with EXCEPTION_UNWINDING via `call_guest`) and jump away; stale
dispatch records are dropped on the next raise. `kernel32!RaiseException` is implemented (C++ `throw`).
Unimplemented instructions are **not** turned into exceptions; they stop the machine.

## Handles

`m.handles`: `insert(KernelObject)`, `insert_named`, `open_named`, `get/get_mut`, `get_other::<T>()` for
module-owned objects (`KernelObject::Other("file", Box<T>)`), `duplicate`, `close`. Handles start at 0x100,
step 4. Pseudo handles: `CURRENT_PROCESS = -1`, `CURRENT_THREAD = -2`.

## VFS

The guest sees the game at `C:\S3` (`GUEST_GAME_DIR`), module path `C:\S3\S3.EXE`, command line `S3.EXE`.
`m.vfs.components(path)` normalizes (drive letters, `\`/`/`, `.`/`..`, relative to `cwd`); any other drive root
(CD paths) maps to the game dir too. `resolve_read` checks `data_dir/overlay/` first, then `game_dir`, both
case-insensitive. `resolve_write` returns an overlay path (creating parents); `copy_up` copies a game file into
the overlay before read/write opens. `list_dir` merges both; `wildcard_match` for FindFirstFile; `set_cwd`.
The game dir is never written; deletes/renames of game-dir files are recorded as whiteouts
(`data_dir/overlay-whiteouts.txt`). File ops: `remove_file`, `rename`, `copy`, `create_dir`, `remove_dir`, `create_path`.
Memory-mapped file views: `s3_runtime::mapfile` (mmap into the guest window). PE resources: `s3_runtime::resources`.

## Host trait (frontends)

```rust
pub trait Host: Send {
    fn present(&mut self, fb: &FrameBuffer);            // RGB565 width*height
    fn poll_events(&mut self) -> Vec<HostEvent>;        // MouseMove{x,y} MouseButton{button,down} Key{vk,down} Char Quit Pause Resume
    fn queue_audio(&mut self, samples: &[i16], rate: u32, channels: u16) {}
    fn audio_queued_frames(&self) -> usize { 0 }
    fn now_ms(&self) -> u64;
    fn game_dir(&self) -> PathBuf;
    fn data_dir(&self) -> PathBuf;
    fn log(&self, level: LogLevel, msg: &str) {}
    fn idle(&mut self, ms: u32) {}                      // all threads blocked
}
```
Mod extension points (`Machine::ext`, `s3-runtime/src/ext.rs`): hook dispatch, an input filter in front of `m.input`
(raw `HostEvent::Pointer` touch events go to the `s3-mods` gesture recognizer), and an overlay step in `present`
(guest frame -> overlay -> cursor). See [mods.md](mods.md).
Input consumers (USER32 queue, DirectInput) read `m.input` (current mouse/buttons/keys) and
`m.input.events_since(&mut cursor)` (each keeps its own cursor; start with `cursor_now()`).
`Machine::present` composes the mouse cursor (`s3_runtime::cursor::CursorState`) into a host copy of the frame before
`Host::present`; `Machine::refresh_cursor` re-presents when only the cursor changed (see [user32-gdi32.md](user32-gdi32.md#cursor-drawing)).
`NullHost` is the headless implementation used by tests.

## COM

`m.com.register_class(clsid, name, factory)`; `ole32!CoCreateInstance` looks the CLSID up and calls
`factory(m, iid) -> Result<iface_ptr, HRESULT>`. Helpers: `m.com_vtable(dll, iface, &METHODS)` (cached),
`m.com_new_object(vtable, size)` (layout `[vtbl][refcount][impl...]`), `Machine::com_addref/com_release`
handlers, `Guid::parse("...")` (const), `Guid::read/write`, Display as `{XXXXXXXX-...}`.
Registered: CLSID_DirectDraw (IDirectDraw/IDirectDraw2), CLSID_DirectPlay, CLSID_DirectPlayLobby; all DirectX
methods are implemented, see [directx-hle.md](directx-hle.md).

## Audio output

The DirectSound mixer service in s3-dx is the only caller of `Host::queue_audio` (44100 Hz stereo i16). Other
producers (winmm waveOut / CD music) push PCM into `m.state::<s3_runtime::audio::AudioStreams>()`; the mixer
resamples and mixes them (details in [directx-hle.md](directx-hle.md)). `s3run --audio-wav <file>` records the host audio stream (and
`--audio-play` plays it with the cargo feature `audio-cpal`); `tools/wav_stats.py` analyses the WAV.

## Adding an HLE function

Example (`s3-win32/src/kernel32.rs`):

```rust
pub fn register(reg: &mut Registry) {
    reg.declare_all(DLL, NAMES);                // keeps UNIMPLEMENTED reporting for the rest
    reg.register(DLL, "GetTickCount", get_tick_count);
    reg.register(DLL, "HeapAlloc", heap_alloc);
}

fn get_tick_count(m: &mut Machine) -> ThunkResult {
    ThunkResult::stdcall(m.now_ms() as u32, 0)  // stdcall, no args
}

fn heap_alloc(m: &mut Machine) -> ThunkResult {
    let (h, flags, size) = (m.arg_u32(0), m.arg_u32(1), m.arg_u32(2));
    let p = m.mem.heap_alloc(h, size, flags).unwrap_or(0);
    ThunkResult::stdcall(p, 3)                  // pops 3 args
}
```
Rules: get the arg count right (wrong `pop_bytes` corrupts the guest stack; MSVC `wsprintfA` etc. are cdecl);
set LastError on failure where the game may check it; mark guesses as HYPOTHESIS in the docs; add a unit test
with a hand-assembled snippet when behaviour is subtle (see `s3-runtime/src/tests.rs`).

KERNEL32 is complete (all static imports + GetProcAddress targets such as the waitable-timer API); see
[kernel32.md](kernel32.md) for the semantics (scheduler waits, critical sections, timers, VFS file ops, mapped files,
locale). Older note: implemented in the foundation were kernel32 GetVersion (Win98 value 0xC0000A04), GetCurrentProcess/Thread/ThreadId,
GetTickCount, Get/SetLastError, ExitProcess, GetCommandLineA, GetModuleHandleA, LoadLibraryA/GetProcAddress/
FreeLibrary (HLE modules only; GetProcAddress returns 0 for undeclared names and logs), Heap*, Virtual*,
Interlocked*, RaiseException, RtlUnwind; ole32 CoInitialize/CoUninitialize/CoCreateInstance; winmm timeGetTime.

## USER32 / GDI32 / registry / WINMM (summary)

Details: [user32-gdi32.md](user32-gdi32.md). Interfaces for other crates:
- **Surface DCs:** `s3_runtime::gdi::{DcTarget, create_dc, release_dc}` (`s3-runtime/src/gdi.rs`); s3-dx calls
  `create_dc` in `IDirectDrawSurface::GetDC` with the surface memory and `release_dc` in `ReleaseDC`. gdi32 installs
  the implementation in `gdi32::register`.
- **Display mode:** s3-dx calls `s3_win32::user32::set_screen_size(m, w, h, bpp)` from `SetDisplayMode`
  (GetSystemMetrics, full-screen windows, WM_DISPLAYCHANGE).
- **Music:** winmm decodes CD music into `AudioStreams[winmm::MUSIC_STREAM_ID]`; the s3-dx mixer mixes it (single
  `Host::queue_audio` producer, fixed 2026-11-05). `set_external_music_mixer` + `mix_music` remain for a pull mixer.
- **Messages from other modules:** `s3_win32::user32::post_message(m, hwnd, msg, wp, lp)`.

## Building, testing, running

Always share the one target dir and cap jobs:

```sh
cd port
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$PWD/target
cargo build -j 4
cargo test -j 4                      # all crates; s3-pe also loads the local S3.EXE if present
cargo test -p s3-cpu -j 4            # one crate
./target/debug/s3run --headless --max-seconds 20 \
    --game-dir ../game-files/gog-s3-ultimate --data-dir ../scratch/data
S3_TRACE=calls S3_TRACE_LIMIT=500 ./target/debug/s3run --headless ...   # trace HLE calls with 4 args
./target/debug/s3run --game-dir ... --data-dir ... --screenshot out.png --inject "3000:click 400 300;9000:quit"
```

`profile.dev` uses opt-level 1 (deps opt-level 3) because the interpreter is too slow unoptimized.
`s3run` prints a summary at exit (instructions, thunk calls, presents, top called functions, stop reason);
exit code 0 = guest exited 0 or time limit, 3 = stopped with an error. `--screenshot-every-present` writes at
most 300 PNGs.

Android: `scripts/build-apk.sh` (APK, both ABIs) and `scripts/run-emulator.sh start install push launch shot`;
details in [android.md](android.md). cargo-ndk lives in `~/.cargo/bin`, which is not on the default PATH.

## Execution model

- **Decode cache**: basic blocks (at most 64 instructions, end at the first control-flow instruction or before the
  thunk page). Blocks live in an arena `Vec<Box<Block>>` (boxed, so addresses are stable and chaining can use
  pointers; `#[repr(C, align(64))]`, the fields read at every block entry share one cache line). A
  `HashMap<eip, index>` sits behind a direct-mapped 8192-entry L1 array `(eip, index)`. `Cpu::run` moves the cache
  out of the `Cpu` (`mem::take`) while it executes, so instructions are borrowed straight from the arena with no
  `Arc`/refcount per block. `invalidate_range` drops overlapping blocks, clears every chaining pointer and rebuilds
  the map (rare: S3.EXE has no self-modifying code). There is one cache per `Cpu`, i.e. per guest thread. Memory
  cost is about 72 bytes per decoded instruction (iced `Instruction` 40 + `Op` 32) plus one `Op` and ~128 bytes per
  block.
- **Threaded dispatch** (`fast.rs`, reworked 2026-11-05 by perf-cpu and 2026-11-07 by perf-interp, see
  [performance.md](performance.md)): at decode time each instruction gets a 32-byte `Op` record: handler
  `fn(&mut Cpu, &mut GuestMemory, &Op) -> bool`, next EIP, register numbers (8-bit: 0..3 = AL..BL, 4..7 = AH..BH),
  displacement, immediate (pre-extended) or branch target, EA form as a const generic (`[disp]`, `[base+disp]`,
  `[base+index*s+disp]`, `[index*s+disp]`; FS/GS and 16-bit addressing go generic). A `generic` op keeps the
  pointer to its iced `Instruction` (same block) in `disp`/`imm` (`Op::set_ins`). Every block's `ops` ends with a
  `block_end` sentinel. **Tail-call threading** (2026-11-07): each non-branch handler ends with
  `next(cpu, mem, op)` = call the handler of `op + 1`, which LLVM compiles to `ldr x, [op, #32]!; br x` (a sibling
  call; even without it the depth is bounded by 65), so a block runs as one chain of indirect branches with one
  prediction site per handler; control transfers (`call/ret/jmp/jcc`, always last) return `true` straight to the
  run loop, other blocks end at the sentinel. On aarch64-linux-android the hot handlers are frameless (e.g. `mov
  r32,[base+disp]` = 14 instructions including the dispatch); Windows ARM64 keeps a frame record (`stp x29,x30`).
  Specialised handlers: `mov` r,r / r,m / m,r / r,imm / m,imm for 8/16/32 bits, ALU `add/or/adc/sbb/and/sub/xor/cmp/
  test` in r,r / r,imm / r,m / m,r / m,imm for 8/16/32 bits, `movzx/movsx` (r32 from m8/m16/r8/r16), `lea`, `push`
  (r/imm/m), `pop r`, `call` (rel/r/m), `ret`, `ret imm16`, `jmp` (rel/r/m), all `jcc` (one handler per condition),
  `inc/dec r32`, `shl/shr/sar r32,imm8`, `nop`; since 2026-11-07 also `imul` (r32,r/m32 / r32,r/m32,imm / r/m32),
  `mul r/m32`, `cdq`, `cwde`, `shl/shr/sar` r8/r16 by imm8 and r8/r16/r32 by CL, `setcc r8`, `neg/not r32`,
  `inc/dec m32` (what the in-game profile still sent to the generic path, ~1.1 % of instructions). Everything else
  uses the generic `exec::step`.
- **Superinstructions** (2026-11-07): when a block ends with `cmp`/`test` (r,r / r,imm for 8/16/32 bits; m,imm for
  some sizes and `[disp]`/`[base+disp]`) or `dec r32` directly followed by a `jcc` with one of the 12 conditions
  `cond_fast` reads from the lazy state, the compare's `Op` gets a fused handler `cmp_jcc` (decode-time peephole,
  `fuse_cmp_jcc`). Its body is the compare handler followed by the `jcc` handler (branch target read from the
  `jcc`'s own `Op` behind it), so flags, faults and counts are those of the two instructions; it saves one dispatch
  and lets the compiler fold the condition into the fresh operands (`cmp r32,r32; je` = 18 aarch64 instructions).
  The pair still counts as 2 retired instructions (counts are per block).
  Rule: a fast handler must behave exactly like `step`. `Cpu::set_generic_only(true)` disables the fast handlers
  (debugging aid). The tests run every snippet through both paths.
- **Contract of a handler**: before a block runs, `cpu.eip` holds the address after its *last* instruction
  (`Block::end`): only the last instruction can branch and no other instruction reads EIP (the generic `exec::step`
  reads `cpu.eip` only for `call`/`ret`/`jmp`/`jcc`/`loop`, which end blocks). Branches overwrite it. A failing
  handler stores its exit in `Cpu::pending_exit` and its own `Op` address in `Cpu::fault_op` (cold out-of-line
  `av` / `generic_exit`, reached by a tail call so the fast paths need no stack frame) and returns `false`; the run
  loop (`block_exit`) computes the instruction index from `fault_op`; for a fault it rewinds EIP (and the fault's
  `eip`) to the faulting instruction, as Windows would report it, and does not count it; `Interrupt`/`Halt` count
  it and leave EIP after it. Fast handlers do not update `cur_ip`; the generic wrapper does (x87 uses it as the last
  instruction pointer).
- **Run loop**: per block: thunk/magic check, budget check, successor lookup, entry counter, one `special` test
  (hooked or native), then the first handler (which runs the whole block). Retired instructions are counted through
  the remaining budget only (`instructions = base + max - left`, stored before native calls and at exits). If the
  budget ends inside a block, its first `left` instructions run one by one through `exec::step` (`run_partial`,
  cold; same results as the fast handlers by their contract), so thread switches happen at exactly the same
  instruction counts. **Block chaining**: each block caches its last two successors (start EIP + block pointer;
  cleared by `invalidate_range`), skipping the L1 lookup; in game 98.8 % of block entries hit it
  (90 000 vms s3det: 528 M + 646 M hits, 14 M L1 lookups, 118 k map/decode lookups).
- **Native blocks** (`NativeBlock`, `Cpu::set_native_blocks`): host-registered native replacements of guest code
  regions, matched by `code_hash` of the code bytes, called at block entry with the remaining budget; see
  [performance.md](performance.md#native-fast-paths-s3-cpu-nativeblock-s3-mods-fastrs).
- **Flags**: **lazy** (2026-11-05). `add`/`sub`/`cmp` without carry-in, logic ops (`and/or/xor/test`) and `inc/dec` store
  `lk` (kind), `lsz`, `la`, `lb`, `lr` (and `lcf` = CF before inc/dec); `Cpu::eflags()` materialises, `set_eflags`
  replaces. Partial updates (`set_flag`, `set_szp`) materialise first. `adc/sbb` with carry-in and everything else
  stay eager. `jcc` reads conditions straight from the lazy state (`cond_fast`). The field `eflags` is gone: use
  `eflags()` / `set_eflags()` (or `Context`).

## Semantics notes (what is exact)

- All six status flags are exact for add/adc/sub/sbb/cmp/neg/inc/dec (CF preserved)/and/or/xor/test, shifts and
  rotates by any count (count masked to 5 bits; count 0 changes nothing; 8/16-bit rcl/rcr use count mod 9/17),
  shld/shrd, mul/imul (CF=OF), bt/bts/btr/btc (memory form with register offset addresses outside the dword,
  signed), bsf/bsr (ZF; destination unchanged for a zero source).
- `div`/`idiv`: #DE (`FaultKind::DivideError`) on zero divisor and on quotient overflow (including
  `INT_MIN / -1`). `aam 0` also raises #DE.
- String ops: `movs/stos/lods/scas/cmps` b/w/d with `rep`/`repe`/`repne`, DF honoured, fast paths for forward
  `rep movs` (memmove-equivalent when dst <= src or there is no overlap) and `rep stos`. A fault in the middle of a
  `rep` leaves ECX/ESI/EDI at the progress so far, with EIP at the instruction. `0x67` (SI/DI/CX) string ops are
  refused with `Unimplemented`; none exist in S3.EXE.
- `jcxz` (`67 E3`, tests CX; the blitters use it) and `jecxz`. `loop/loope/loopne` with a `0x67` prefix use CX.
- 16-bit addressing (`0x67` + `[bx+si]` etc.) wraps the effective address at 64 KiB.
- `pushfd/popfd`: popf can change CF PF AF ZF SF DF OF, AC (bit 18) and ID (bit 21), so the 486 and CPUID
  probes succeed. IF always reads 1. TF/IOPL/NT/RF/VM are not modelled.
- `cpuid`: leaf 0 = "GenuineIntel", max leaf 1. Leaf 1 = family 5 model 2 (Pentium), EDX = FPU|TSC|CX8,
  **no MMX** (bit 23 clear), so S3.EXE never selects its MMX copy routine (static-isa.md #8). This
  deliberately differs from the earlier "Pentium MMX" note in the architecture contract.
- `rdtsc`: host monotonic nanoseconds / 5 (a 200 MHz TSC).
- BCD (`daa/das/aaa/aas/aam/aad`) follow the Intel pseudo-code. `salc` is implemented.
- `int3` -> `CpuExit::Interrupt(3)`, `int n` -> `Interrupt(n)`, `into` -> `Interrupt(4)` if OF, `hlt` -> `Halt`.
  `ud0/ud1/ud2` and undecodable bytes -> `FaultKind::InvalidOpcode`.
  `in/out/ins/outs/iret/retf/lgdt/.../bound/arpl/lds/les/lfs/lgs/lss` -> `FaultKind::GeneralProtection`
  (only data decodes as these; see static-isa.md). Far `call`/`jmp` -> `GeneralProtection`.
- Not modelled: segment limits, alignment checks, 16-bit operand-size `call/ret` (IP truncation), `lock` atomicity
  (one guest thread runs at a time, so it is free).
- Memory: guest addresses below 0x10000 fault (`AccessViolation{addr, write}`). Everything else is plain host
  memory (the 4 GiB window plus a guard; s3-mem).

## x87 hook

Any mnemonic that the integer `match` does not handle goes to `fpu::exec(cpu, mem, ins) -> Option<R>`
(owned by the fpu task). `None` -> `FaultKind::Unimplemented` with the mnemonic and disassembly in `detail`.
The task contract named this hook `exec_fpu`. The existing `fpu::exec` signature was kept so that both agents'
code compiles.

## Performance

`cargo test --release -p s3-cpu -- --ignored --nocapture bench_mips`. The loop mixes loads, stores, ALU ops,
compare-and-branch, call/ret and push/pop.
