## Tests

`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=port/target cargo test -p s3-cpu -j 4` (on Windows ARM64 the two `fpu::golden` tests fail at
`f0a50f7` already: f2xm1 and the pure-function hash differ from the golden vectors, see
[determinism.md](determinism.md); open issue):
- `diff_tests.rs` (x86_64 hosts): add/adc/sub/sbb/cmp/and/or/xor/test (8/16/32), neg/not/inc/dec,
  shl/shr/sar/rol/ror/rcl/rcr by CL with counts 0..40, 63, 64, 255, 257 and by immediates, shld/shrd 16/32,
  imul 2-op, bsf/bsr, bt/bts/btr/btc, mul/imul/div/idiv 8/16/32 (including the #DE cases). Operands are about
  64 edge-case and pseudo-random values, with incoming flag states 0, CF and all flags set. Each case runs
  natively (inline asm, `popfq` -> op -> `pushfq`) and in the interpreter, through both the fast and the generic
  path. A deliberately broken parity table is caught, so the harness is sensitive.
- `fast.rs` `lazy_conditions_match_materialised_flags`: every lazy kind x size x condition x edge values, plus
  `cf()/af()/of()/flag()` against the materialised EFLAGS.
- `tests.rs`: control flow, imm8 sign extension, memory ALU forms, string ops (backward memmove, repe cmpsb,
  rep with ECX=0, a fault in the middle of a rep), `67 E3` jcxz, loops, BCD, pushfd/popfd probes, cpuid, int3/int n/
  ud2/invalid bytes/in, xlat, enter with nesting, xchg/cmpxchg/lock inc on memory, the FS-relative SEH prologue,
  0x66 16-bit operations, the 16-bit addressing wrap, and the MIPS benchmark (ignored).
- `tests.rs` (perf-interp, run on every host, unlike `diff_tests.rs`): `budget_stops_are_exact` (a loop with calls,
  imul, adc, cdq run with budgets 1/2/3/5/7/13 and in one go, fast and generic: each run retires exactly its budget,
  same final registers, flags, memory and count), `mid_block_exits_count_exactly` (faults/`int3`/`hlt` in the middle
  of a block and in the partial-block path: EIP and count), `imul_mul_cdq_forms_fast_vs_generic`,
  `shift_forms_fast_vs_generic`, `setcc_forms_fast_vs_generic` and `cmp_jcc_fusion_fast_vs_generic` (69 edge and
  pseudo-random values squared, two incoming flag states; every fused form x all 16 conditions, both outcomes).
  Mutations (wrong OF of `shr`, wrong imul overflow, fused branch never taken) are caught.

## JIT (optional, AArch64; perf-jit 2026-11-07)

**Switch.** Cargo feature `jit` (default on; compiled only for `target_arch = "aarch64"`; iOS builds must use
`--no-default-features`, Apple forbids JIT). At run time it is **off by default**: env `S3_JIT=1` or
`s3_cpu::set_jit_enabled(true)` (global), `Cpu::set_jit(Some(bool))` (per CPU, tests). `s3_cpu::jit_available()`,
`jit_enabled()`, `jit_stats()` (counters; `s3det` prints them when the JIT is on). Android: `<data dir>/jit.txt`
containing `1` ([android.md](android.md)). Debug: `S3_JIT_DUMP=1` appends
every compiled block (guest disassembly + `.inst` words) to `./s3jit.s` (assemble + `llvm-objdump -d` with the NDK
clang to read it), `S3_JIT_FBPROF=1` profiles fallback calls per form and exits to the run loop by reason (slow).

**What is compiled.** A block is compiled when the run loop has entered it 8 times (`jit::THRESHOLD`;
`Cpu::set_jit_threshold`) and it is not hooked. The translation covers exactly the decoded block (same
instructions, same `n`), so retired counts are unchanged by construction. One code arena of 16 MiB per decode
cache (per guest thread), allocated on the first compile; full arena, `invalidate_range` dropping anything,
`clear()` -> all JIT code is dropped (no JIT code runs at those points).

**Execution model** (all choices keep the interpreter's results bit-exact; `determinism.md`):
- Trampoline `enter(cpu, mem_base, code)` saves x19..x30, loads guest EAX..EDI into **x19..x26** (x27 = `Cpu`,
  x28 = guest memory base, x13 = remaining budget) and jumps into the block; every exit stores the registers and
  the budget back. The `Cpu` is `repr(C)`; the code uses field offsets (`offset_of!`).
- **Budget**: the run loop enters JIT code only when `n <= left` (like the fast path); every block re-checks
  `left >= n` on entry and otherwise exits with EIP = its start, so the run loop runs the partial block through
  `run_partial` exactly as before. Budget stops / thread switches happen at the same instruction counts.
- **Flags**: between blocks the flags are always in the `Cpu` in the interpreter's lazy format (`lk/lsz/la/lb/lr`
  + `lcf`, or `ef` with `lk = NONE`). Inside a block the compiler knows the last flag writer at compile time:
  `Lazy(kind, size)` with the operands in x9/x10/x11 (x12 = lcf for inc/dec), `Eager` (status bits in x9, from
  shifts/mul) or `Cpu` (unknown, e.g. at block start). Conditions (`jcc`, `setcc`) are evaluated with native
  compares of the (shifted) operands; from the `Cpu` state a helper (`jit_cond`) evaluates them; CF/AF for inc/dec
  and shifts are read inline from the `Cpu` state. The state is stored at block end, before helper calls and at
  side exits. For `LOGIC` the stored `la/lb` may differ from the interpreter's zeros; they are never read.
- **Faults**: every guest access first checks `addr < 0x10000`; on failure the code takes a **side exit before
  the instruction** (registers and flags as at its start) and the run loop continues the block from that `Op`
  with the interpreter handlers, which then fault (or not) exactly like the interpreter, including partial effects.
  #DE of `div/idiv` works the same way.
- **Coverage (native)**: everything with a fast handler except `adc/sbb` and 8/16-bit shifts by CL: `mov`
  (8/16/32, r/m/imm), `movzx/movsx`, `lea`, `push/pop`, `add/or/and/sub/xor/cmp/test` all forms and sizes,
  `inc/dec` r32/m32, `neg/not` r32, `shl/shr/sar` imm (8/16/32) and r32 by CL, `imul` (1/2/3 operands), `mul`,
  `cdq`, `cwde`, `setcc`, `jcc`, `jmp`/`call` (rel/r/m), `ret [imm]`; plus generic-path forms (they also store
  `cur_ip`): `loop`, `jecxz`, `67 E3` `jcxz`, `div/idiv` r/m32, `movzx r16,r/m8`, `inc/dec/neg` r8, `leave`,
  non-rep `movsb/movsd/stosb/stosd`, `mov` r32 <-> `fs:[..]`. Anything else (x87, `rep` strings, `adc/sbb`, ...)
  calls the interpreter handler for that single instruction (`jit_op` on a private `[op, block_end]` pair; registers
  and flags spilled/reloaded) and continues in JIT code; a failing fallback exits through `block_exit` as usual.
- **Linking**: a static successor that is compiled already gets a direct `b`; otherwise a per-EIP slot
  (`ldr`/`ldr`/`br`, the slot holds the exit stub until the target is compiled). Indirect targets (`ret`, `jmp/call`
  r/m, fallback branches) go through a 32768-entry direct-mapped `(eip, code)` table, a miss exits to the run loop.
  Thunk addresses and hooked blocks are never linked. Blocks with a **native fast path** get a stub that does
  what the run loop does at a block entry (budget 0 -> exit; else call the `NativeFn` with the budget, `instructions`
  set; declined -> block body, done -> continue at its EIP).
- **Code memory**: `VirtualAlloc` + `VirtualProtect(PAGE_EXECUTE_READ)` + `FlushInstructionCache` (Windows),
  `mmap` + `mprotect` + `dc cvau`/`ic ivau` (Linux/Android). W^X: only the pages being written are RW, then RX.
  Windows ARM64: the JIT frames have no unwind info, so a panic inside a helper called from JIT code aborts the
  process (helpers do not panic in normal operation).

**Tests** (`src/jit_tests.rs`, aarch64): `jit_matches_interpreter_on_random_programs` (1000 random programs: loops
over random mixes of all the forms above incl. 8/16-bit forms, memory forms with every EA kind, flag consumers,
forward branches, calls, pushes, faults (NULL accesses, #DE), string ops; each run on the interpreter and the JIT
with compile thresholds 0 and 2, in one go and in random budget slices of 1..400 instructions; after every slice
exit, registers, EIP, EFLAGS, observable lazy state, count and 1 MiB data + stack must be equal; mutations of a
condition code and of the `div` remainder are caught), `jit_respects_hooks_natives_and_invalidation` (hook hits,
native calls, self-modifying code + `invalidate_range`), `jit_native_stub_matches_interpreter` (a native fast path
that sometimes accepts, random slices; caught EIP not being set before the call), `a64::tests` (encodings checked
against clang, logical immediates).

**Found on the way**: block chaining used EIP 0 as "empty successor", so a guest jump to address 0 (NULL function
pointer) dereferenced a null block pointer and crashed the host instead of raising the guest fault. Empty is now
`u32::MAX` (never a block start).

## Hook point (2026-11-06, mods-w1)

`Cpu::set_hooks(Option<Arc<HookAddrs>>)`: decoded blocks end before any hooked address and blocks starting at one carry
`Block::hooked`; at block entry a hooked block exits with `CpuExit::Hook(eip)` unless `skip_hook_once(eip)` was called.
Cost: one byte test per executed block; `bench_mips` showed no measurable difference (details in [mods.md](mods.md)).
Test: `hook_exits_mid_block_and_skip_once`.

```

`docs/porting/determinism.md`:

```md
# Determinism (W5 prerequisite)

Settlers III multiplayer is **lockstep**: every peer runs the full simulation and only commands are exchanged.
All peers must compute bit-identical game state from identical inputs, on x86_64 desktops and arm64 phones.
This doc lists every source of nondeterminism in our emulator, what is fixed, how it is tested, and what is open.
Owner of the code parts: `port/crates/s3-cpu/src/fpu*.rs`; test tool `s3det`.

## Summary

| Source | Status |
| --- | --- |
| x87 basic arithmetic (`+ - * /`, `fsqrt`) | **Deterministic**: IEEE-754 binary64, correctly rounded on every host |
| x87 transcendentals (`fsin fcos fptan fsincos fpatan f2xm1 fyl2x fyl2xp1`) | **Fixed 2026-11-05**: pure-Rust fdlibm (`libm` crate, pinned), was host libm |
| `fprem`/`fprem1` | **Fixed**: exact integer long division (was host `fmod` via `%`), exact quotient bits |
| NaN results (sign/payload, two-NaN propagation) | **Fixed**: computed by our x87 rules, never by the host |
| f32 <-> f64 conversion of NaNs | **Fixed**: bit-level |
| `frndint`/`fist*` rounding | Deterministic (exact functions; NaN guarded) |
| FMA contraction | None: Rust never fuses `a*b+c`; verified 0 `fmadd/fmsub` in the aarch64 build of s3-cpu |
| Denormals / FTZ / DAZ / rounding mode of the host | Assumed IEEE default; checked at runtime by `fpu::math::host_float_env_check()` (s3det calls it; **frontends should too**, see open items) |
| 80-bit extended precision | Not modelled (f64 registers). Deterministic across our hosts; differs from real x87 only where the game relies on > 53-bit precision or the wide exponent range (see below) |
| `GetTickCount`/`timeGetTime`/waits/timers | Wall clock (`Host::now_ms`). Not part of lockstep state by design of the game (it runs on real PCs); deterministic in `s3det` (virtual clock) |
| `QueryPerformanceCounter` | Wall clock; only used by the blit benchmark at startup (picks a blitter, not simulation state). Virtual in `s3det` |
| `GetSystemTime`/`GetLocalTime`/time zone | Wall clock. **Seeds CRT `rand`** (`srand(time(NULL))`, see below). Fixed epoch in `s3det` |
| `rdtsc` | Wall clock (`exec.rs`), but **S3.EXE contains no `rdtsc`** (static census) |
| `CoCreateGuid`/`UuidCreate` | Host-time-seeded RNG (`rpcrt4::random_guid`). First divergence `s3det` found; deterministic in `s3det` |
| Thread scheduling | Round robin, instruction quanta: deterministic for a given clock + input history. In normal runs slices are wall-clock bounded, like on Windows; the game is built for preemptive scheduling, so simulation results must not depend on it (two-peer tests identical, multiplayer.md 6). The experimental multi-core mode (`S3_MT=1`, [multicore.md](multicore.md)) runs the draw thread truly in parallel; s3det never enables it; MP runs with MT peers: simulation tables identical at every tick |
| Uninitialised guest memory | Deterministic: the 4 GiB window is zero-filled by mmap, decommit/discard re-zeroes, heap reuse depends only on guest history |
| Directory listings (FindFirstFile) | Sorted case-insensitively in the VFS (`vfs.rs`), independent of the host file system |
| Host file timestamps | Not normalised (GetFileTime/FindFirstFile return host mtimes). Matter only if the game uses them in synced state (HYPOTHESIS: no; savegame list display only) |

## x87 model and why it is deterministic

Implementation: [x87-fpu.md](x87-fpu.md); this section is the determinism contract.

- **Registers are IEEE binary64 (`f64`).** Every operation produces exactly one IEEE result:
  `+ - * /` and `sqrt` are correctly rounded (round-to-nearest-even) on x86_64 (SSE2), aarch64, i686-SSE2 and wasm.
  Precision control PC=24 is applied by bit manipulation (`conv::apply_pc`); PC=53 and PC=64 both give f64.
  Rounding control RC is honoured by `fist*`, `frndint`, `fbstp`; arithmetic always rounds to nearest (the only RC
  changer in S3.EXE is the CRT `_ftol` at `0x61fe98`, which only does `fistp` while RC=truncate, see static-isa.md).
- **Relation to real hardware:** MSVC programs run with control word `0x027F` (PC=53, HYPOTHESIS for S3.EXE, the
  CRT sets it at startup). With PC=53 a real x87 rounds `+ - * / sqrt` to 53 bits like we do; remaining
  differences are (a) the wider exponent range of the 80-bit registers (intermediate overflow/underflow, double
  rounding of subnormal results), (b) values loaded from `m80` are rounded to 53 bits, (c) transcendentals
  (x87 uses its own microcode, < 1 ulp of the 64-bit result, and a 66-bit pi for argument reduction). This matters
  only for **PC crossplay** (W5 later): mobile + our desktop peers all run this same code and agree bit for bit.
- **Transcendentals** (`fpu_math.rs`): the `libm` crate (pure Rust port of musl/FreeBSD fdlibm, MIT), built with
  `default-features = false` so no arch-specific intrinsics are used, version **pinned with `=0.2.16`** in
  `s3-cpu/Cargo.toml`. fdlibm is not correctly rounded but is within 1 ulp, and it is a fixed sequence of IEEE
  basic operations, so its output depends only on the input bits.
  - `fsin/fcos/fptan/fsincos`: `libm::sin/cos/tan` (fsincos = fsin + fcos separately, so the results equal the
    single instructions). |x| >= 2^63: C2=1, operand unchanged (as hardware).
  - `fpatan`: `libm::atan2(y, x)`.
  - `f2xm1`: `expm1(p) + e*(1 + expm1(p))` where `p + e = x*ln2` exactly (Dekker product without FMA, plus the low
    part of ln 2) — within 1 ulp on the x87 domain [-1, 1] (tests: `exp2m1(0.5)`, `exp2m1(-0.25)`).
  - `fyl2x`: `y * libm::log2(x)`; `fyl2xp1`: `y * (libm::log1p(x) / ln2)` (two roundings, deterministic).
  - Accuracy compared to the old host-libm code: both are within ~1 ulp; results can differ in the last bit,
    which is invisible to the game (it only runs these in the CRT math functions; see "What feeds the simulation").
- **`fprem`/`fprem1`** (`math::fprem`): integer long division of the 53-bit significands, exact remainder for any
  exponent difference, quotient bits Q2/Q1/Q0 exact (the old code lost them for quotients >= 2^53). `fprem1`
  rounds the quotient to nearest even. Always the complete remainder (C2=0); real hardware reduces at most 63
  exponent bits per instruction and sets C2=1, which the CRT loops over — same final result.
- **NaNs**: x86 SSE creates `0xFFF8...` (negative quiet NaN = x87 "indefinite"), aarch64 creates the positive
  `0x7FF8...`, and when both operands are NaNs the host returns one depending on operand order, which LLVM may
  commute. We never let the host decide: `Fpu::finish` → `math::propagate_nan` (one NaN: that NaN quieted; two:
  the larger significand, tie → destination operand; SNaN raises IE), invalid operations → `INDEFINITE`
  (`0xFFF8_0000_0000_0000`, the x87 value). `fld m32`/`fst m32` convert NaNs bit by bit (`conv::f32_to_f64`,
  `conv::f64_to_f32`). `frndint` / `round_rc` return NaN inputs quieted without calling `floor/ceil/trunc/roundeven`
  (which are libm calls on baseline x86_64).
- **Float -> int** (`fist/fistp/fisttp`): round with RC (exact), range check, then `as` (exact for in-range
  values); out of range / NaN -> integer indefinite `0x8000...` + IE. Deterministic.
- **Host FP environment**: correct results need FTZ/DAZ off and round-to-nearest on the emulation thread. That is
  the default for Linux/Android/macOS processes on x86_64 and aarch64, but a library could change it on our
  thread. `fpu::math::host_float_env_check()` tests subnormal arithmetic, rounding and correctly-rounded
  division/sqrt at runtime.

### Golden vectors (`fpu_golden.rs`)

- `golden_x87_vectors`: 2048 pseudo-random operand pairs (several magnitude ranges + random bit patterns + a
  list of specials: ±0, ±inf, QNaN/SNaN, min/max subnormal, min normal, max) run through the **interpreter**
  (assembled loop, real decode/dispatch path) for 27 cases: `fadd fsub fmul fdiv fdivr`, PC=24 `fmul fdiv`,
  `fst m32`, `fsqrt fsin fcos fptan fsincos fpatan f2xm1 fyl2x fyl2xp1 fprem fprem1 fscale fxtract`,
  `frndint` in all 4 RC modes, `fcom`, `fxam`. Result bits and the status word of every item are hashed (FNV-1a)
  and compared with stored constants. 64-bit hosts only (needs the 4 GiB guest window).
- `golden_x87_int_conversions`: `fist m16/m32`, `fistp m64` in all 4 RC modes.
- `golden_pure_functions`: the numeric layer alone (math::*, conv::* incl. f80 conversion, ldexp, PC rounding),
  no guest memory, so it also runs on 32-bit hosts.
- Verified 2026-11-05: identical hashes on x86_64 (debug and release) and **i686** (`--target
  i686-unknown-linux-gnu`, pure layer). aarch64: the test binary cross-compiles
  (`--target aarch64-linux-android`, NDK `aarch64-linux-android26-clang` linker) and contains no FMA instructions,
  but has **not been run yet** (no qemu-aarch64 on this PC, no phone). To run it on a device:
  ```sh
  adb push port/target/aarch64-linux-android/debug/deps/s3_cpu-<hash> /data/local/tmp/s3cpu
  adb shell /data/local/tmp/s3cpu golden
  ```
- **If a hash changes**: on a new host only → real determinism bug, do not update the constant. After an
  intended change in fpu*.rs or a `libm` bump → update the constants in the same change and note it here: it
  breaks multiplayer compatibility between app versions (the lobby must compare a "sim version").

## What feeds the simulation (static RE, S3.EXE GOG sha256 `00a925cf…`)

- No `rdtsc`, no SSE (static-isa.md). x87 is mostly float constant initialisers, `_ftol` (44 callers) and a few
  CRT math functions; HYPOTHESIS (unchanged): the simulation itself is integer.
- **CRT `rand`** = `0x61f802` (MSVC LCG `x = x*0x343FD + 0x269EC3`, state per thread at `_getptd()+0x14`),
  **`srand`** = `0x61f7f5`. `srand` is called twice, both times with `time(NULL)` (`0x61f6a7`, built from
  `GetLocalTime`/`GetSystemTime`/`GetTimeZoneInformation`): in `0x431780` (app/object init called from
  `0x40cee0`) and in `CDrawThread` init `0x4932e0` (string "Menus::CDrawThread::Initialisier..."). Because the
  state is per thread, each `srand` only seeds the calling thread. `rand` has 16 direct callers (`0x40fb40`,
  `0x40ff70`, `0x410370`, `0x410acd`, `0x431ab0`, `0x47fea0`, `0x483760`, `0x4c7730`, `0x4d3050`, `0x548fb0`,
  `0x5492a0`, `0x5499b0`, `0x549bd0`, `0x5ff4f0`, `0x6042e0`, `0x60bca0`; `0x40fb40` is the serial/registry code).
  Open (W2): which of them run on the logic thread and whether the game uses its own seeded RNG for the
  simulation (no other common LCG multiplier — `0x41C64E6D`, `0x08088405` — occurs in `.text`). A lockstep game
  must seed the simulation RNG from the host's game-start message, so HYPOTHESIS: the logic RNG is separate and
  network-seeded; the time-seeded CRT `rand` is used for UI/effects/map preview.
- Timing: `timeGetTime` 31 sites (animation, scrolling, network timing), `GetTickCount` 2 sites, QPC only in the
  blit benchmark; logic thread period 64 ms (`0x53d761`). Logic progress in MP is gated by network turns, not by
  local time (HYPOTHESIS until W5 runs two peers).

## Determinism test: `s3det`

`port/crates/s3-desktop/src/bin/s3det.rs` (binary `s3det`, in the `s3-desktop` package) runs the game headless
with a **virtual clock**: `now = (guest instructions executed) / ipms + 1 ms per idle slice` (default ipms =
150 000, i.e. a 150 MIPS guest CPU, about the desktop interpreter speed, so a run takes roughly real time). The
clock only advances between slices of ipms/4 instructions; every guest-visible time is a function of the
instruction count. It overrides (registry re-registration after load, no change to the HLE crates):
`QueryPerformanceCounter` (virtual µs, strictly increasing), `GetSystemTime`/`GetLocalTime`/
`GetSystemTimeAsFileTime` (2001-01-01 00:00 UTC + virtual time), `GetTimeZoneInformation` (UTC),
`CoCreateGuid`/`UuidCreate` (fixed-seed xorshift). Inject times are virtual ms.

Every `--hash-every` virtual ms it prints `vms= insns= presents= mem= cpu= bytes=`: `mem` hashes all committed
guest-writable pages (not file mappings: GFX/maps are read-only data), `cpu` hashes every thread's registers,
EIP, x87 registers/status/control and instruction count (env `S3DET_HASH_FULL=1` adds EFLAGS, FS base and the
x87 tag word / last IP / last data pointer; perf-jit). `--dump-at V --dump f` writes the hashed pages raw;
`python3 -I tools/memdiff.py a b` lists differing byte ranges.

```sh
cd port && CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$PWD/target cargo build --release -j 4 -p s3-desktop --bin s3det
cd .. && tools/determinism-test.sh port/target/release/s3det 75000   # two parallel runs, diff of hashes
```

Results (2026-11-05, x86_64 desktop, two runs **in parallel**, fresh empty data dirs):

1. First attempt: instruction counts and CPU hashes identical for 45 000 vms, memory hash diverged at 6 000 vms.
   `memdiff` → one 16-byte range at `0x7a7ac8` = a GUID from `CoCreateGuid` (host-time-seeded). Fixed in s3det.
2. After the GUID override: **60 000 vms (menu → scenario → random map 384 → in game), all 61 hash lines
   identical**, final `insns=5896666465 mem=94407f5976cfd7ec`, identical final screenshots, 47 s wall each.
3. `tools/determinism-test.sh` (75 000 vms, adds build menu → place building → right click in game): see
   "Latest run" below.

This proves the emulator (CPU, x87, HLE, scheduler) is a deterministic function of (game files, clock, inputs).
It does **not** yet prove two *different hosts* agree (needs the same run on an arm64 device; the hashes printed
by `s3det` are directly comparable across hosts because guest memory layout is host-independent) and it does not
test lockstep MP itself (two peers with independent wall clocks) — that is W5's job.

### Latest run

2026-11-05, `tools/determinism-test.sh scratch/determinism/target/release/s3det 75000`, two runs in parallel:
**IDENTICAL**, 76 hash lines, final `insns=7699350378 presents=1953 mem=a68d8effad5b92f2 cpu=8e27020e7e8bfa7b`
(56 MB of writable guest memory hashed per line), 60.7 s wall each. The final frame shows the game with the
build menu open (the placement click at 420 300 did not create a site — choose a free spot when extending the
script).

### JIT (perf-jit, 2026-11-07)

The optional AArch64 JIT ([cpu.md](cpu.md#jit-optional-aarch64-perf-jit-2026-11-07)) must not change any of the
above: same registers, EFLAGS (as the lazy model materialises them), memory, EIP, retired counts and the same
budget stop points. Checked on the Windows 11 ARM64 PC with the 90 000 vms inject of `tools/determinism-test.sh`:

- `s3det` at the JIT commit, `S3_JIT=1` vs the baseline binary of `e8042b2` (interpreter): all 91 per-second
  hash lines **IDENTICAL**, `insns=11886929367 mem=6e141c4900044d20 cpu=028473e586e3d37e`.
- Same binary `S3_JIT=0` vs `S3_JIT=1` with **`S3DET_HASH_FULL=1`** (new: the CPU hash then also covers EFLAGS,
  FS base, x87 tag word, last IP and last data pointer): **IDENTICAL**, 91 lines, `cpu=e584fa62bd32339a`.
- `S3_FAST=0` (no native fast paths) with the JIT: same `insns`/hashes as the interpreter.

Every JIT change must repeat this (and `cargo test -p s3-cpu jit` on an aarch64 host).

## Open items / recommendations

- **Golden vectors fail on Windows 11 ARM64** (found by perf-interp 2026-11-07, rustc 1.99.1 / LLVM 23.1.1,
  `aarch64-pc-windows-msvc`, already at commit `f0a50f7`, not caused by the interpreter work):
  `golden_x87_vectors` differs only in **`f2xm1`**, and `golden_pure_functions` gives `0xa8d2b319571e5c63`
  (expected `0x7d0c9df6e90f4fca`). The compiled `math::exp2m1` contains no
  FMA (checked in the asm), so the suspect is `libm::expm1` or a toolchain change since the constants were made on
  x86_64; HYPOTHESIS, unverified. If it is aarch64-specific, phones and x86_64 desktops would desync in lockstep
  wherever the game runs `f2xm1` on sim data. Next step: run the golden test on x86_64 with the same toolchain and
  on the phone (`adb shell`), then bisect the pure-function hash per function.

- **Frontends**: call `s3_cpu::fpu::math::host_float_env_check()` (re-exported as
  `s3_runtime::cpu::fpu::math`) on the emulation thread at startup and refuse multiplayer if it fails.
- **Run the golden vectors and `s3det` on an arm64 phone** (or emulator-5610 with arm64 translation, by an agent
  allowed to use it) and compare with the x86_64 hashes above. s3det on Android needs a small harness (the
  binary is desktop-only today); simplest: build `s3det` for `aarch64-linux-android` and run it via `adb shell`
  with game files in `/data/local/tmp` (HYPOTHESIS: works since it has no window/audio dependencies besides `png`).
- **Mods (W1)**: `s3det` does not install `s3-mods` patches. Once hooks change game behaviour, install the same
  patch set in s3det so the test covers it; hooks must themselves be deterministic (no host time, no HashMap
  iteration order, no host floats in sim-visible results).
- **MP sim version**: include the s3-cpu golden hash (or a constant derived from it) in the lobby handshake so
  peers with different FPU semantics refuse to play together.
- `rpcrt4::random_guid` and `hosttime` stay host-random/host-time for normal play (unique session GUIDs are
  wanted); only s3det overrides them.
- `rdtsc` (`exec.rs`) still uses the host clock; harmless for S3.EXE (never executed).
- Crossplay with real Windows PCs (later): needs either proof that sim state never touches the x87 (likely, to be
  confirmed by W2 with a watch on the logic thread's x87 usage) or a full 80-bit soft-float x87.

```

`docs/porting/directx-hle.md`:

```md
# DirectX HLE (`port/crates/s3-dx`)

Status 2026-11-05: DirectDraw, DirectSound, DirectInput 3 and DirectPlay stubs implemented; 16 unit tests
(`cargo test -p s3-dx -j 4`). Exercised by the real S3.EXE since integration round 1 (menu 800x600x16, in game
640x480x16, WaitForVerticalBlank pacing, DirectInput mouse, DirectSound mixer; see
[integration-log.md](integration-log.md)). DirectPlay is still only stubs (multiplayer menus not exercised). What the game uses comes from [directx-surface.md](../reverse-engineering/directx-surface.md)
(static) and [wine-trace.md](../reverse-engineering/wine-trace.md) (runtime).

## Files

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `lib.rs` | `register_all(reg)` (exports + every interface method get a handler), `register_factories(m)` (CoCreateInstance classes + the two services below), `stubs!` macro for constant-result methods, HRESULT constants |
| `ddraw.rs` | DirectDraw: IDirectDraw, IDirectDraw2, IDirectDrawSurface/2/3 (one vtable), IDirectDrawPalette, IDirectDrawClipper; exports DirectDrawCreate, DirectDrawEnumerateA, DirectDrawCreateClipper; factory CLSID_DirectDraw |
| `blit.rs` | pure pixel code: `fill`, `blt` (clipping, nearest stretch, mirror, src/dst colour key ranges, memmove-safe overlap), `to_framebuffer` (16-bit 565/555, 8-bit + palette, 24/32-bit -> RGB565) |
| `dsound.rs` | DirectSound: IDirectSound, IDirectSoundBuffer; exports DirectSoundCreate, DirectSoundEnumerateA; `mixer_service` |
| `mixer.rs` | pure mixer core: dB/pan -> gain, `mix_voice` (8/16-bit, mono/stereo, linear resampling, looping), `mix_stream` (external PCM queues), clamping |
| `dinput.rs` | DirectInput 3: IDirectInputA, IDirectInputDeviceA (SysMouse, SysKeyboard); export DirectInputCreateA; `pump_service`; VK -> DIK table |
| `dplay.rs` | DirectPlay 6 COM plumbing: IDirectPlay4A, IDirectPlayLobby3A (per-method arg counts tables); factories CLSID_DirectPlay / CLSID_DirectPlayLobby; exports; lobby/group stubs |
| `dplay_net.rs` | IDirectPlay4A over our relay (`s3-net`): connections, sessions, players, Send/Receive, DPSYS messages, SetEvent; see [multiplayer.md](multiplayer.md) section 5 |
| `tests.rs` | vtable offsets vs S3 call sites, every method has a handler, blit/mixer unit tests, full COM flows through `call_guest` |

## Object model

- Every interface object is guest memory `[vtbl][refcount][...]` from `Machine::com_new_object`; vtables come from
  `Machine::com_vtable(dll, iface, METHODS)` (thunks named `ddraw.dll!IDirectDrawSurface::Blt` etc., so
  `S3_TRACE=thunks` shows COM calls by name).
- Host-side state per module in `Machine::state::<T>()`: `ddraw::DdState` (display mode, surfaces, palettes,
  clippers, the visible primary, a reused FrameBuffer), `dsound::DsState`, `dinput::DiState`. Keyed by the guest
  interface pointer. Guards are never held across `call_guest`.
- IDirectDraw objects store a "core" pointer at `+8`; `QueryInterface(IID_IDirectDraw/2)` returns a new interface
  object with the other vtable. IDirectDraw v1 has its own `SetDisplayMode` handler (3 args vs 5 in v2).
- Surfaces: `QueryInterface` for IID_IDirectDrawSurface/2/3 returns the same pointer (vtables are prefix
  compatible: v1 = 36 methods, v2 +3, v3 +SetSurfaceDesc).
- Release: surfaces free their pixel memory (VirtualAlloc region) and a flip chain when the refcount reaches 0;
  sound buffers free PCM memory when the last duplicate goes; DirectDraw/DirectSound/DirectInput/DirectPlay
  objects themselves are never freed (few, may be aliased).

## DirectDraw behaviour

- Display mode: starts as 800x600x16 (`DEFAULT_MODE`); `SetDisplayMode` accepts 8/16/32 bpp and 320..4096 x
  200..4096 (custom game resolutions, [resolution-zoom.md](resolution-zoom.md)). `EnumDisplayModes` offers 640x480,
  800x600, 1024x768 at 8 and 16 bpp (filtered by the DDSD).
- Port extension `DDSDM_PORT_LOGICAL` (`0x8000_0000` in the `IDirectDraw2::SetDisplayMode` flags): sets a
  "logical" size <= the mode; the primary surface is then presented cropped to it (top-left), surfaces are untouched.
  A real mode change clears it. Used by the zoom (s3-mods `res.rs`) to change the game size without the game's
  display re-setup. Test: `ddraw_logical_size_crops_present`.
  16 bpp = RGB565 (masks F800/07E0/001F), which makes the game choose `GFX/*.f8007e01f.dat`.
- `CreateSurface`: primary takes the current mode size; `DDSCAPS_FLIP` + `DDSD_BACKBUFFERCOUNT` builds a chain
  (back buffer reachable with `GetAttachedSurface(DDSCAPS_BACKBUFFER)`); offscreen needs WIDTH+HEIGHT and may give
  a pixel format (bpp, 555 detection). Reported caps get `SYSTEMMEMORY` or `VIDEOMEMORY|LOCALVIDMEM`, primaries
  `VISIBLE` (+`FRONTBUFFER` with a chain). Pitch = width*bytes rounded up to 4.
- `Lock` returns the pixel pointer (offset by the rect), the full DDSD and never fails/blocks; `Unlock`,
  `GetDC`/`ReleaseDC` are always allowed (no busy tracking).
- **Presentation**: whenever the visible primary is written by `Blt`, `BltFast`, `Unlock`, `ReleaseDC`,
  `SetPalette`/palette `SetEntries` (8-bit), or `Flip` (rotates the pixel pointers through the chain), the primary
  is converted to RGB565 and passed to `Machine::present` (counted in `stats.presents`). S3's menu path is
  BltFast(offscreen -> primary), the game path Blt(back buffer -> primary) after WaitForVerticalBlank.
- `Blt`: `DDBLT_COLORFILL` (fx+0x50), ROP BLACKNESS/WHITENESS as fills, other ROPs (SRCCOPY) copy;
  `KEYSRC`/`KEYDEST` use the surface keys, `*OVERRIDE` the DDBLTFX keys (ranges), `DDBLT_DDFX` mirroring,
  stretching nearest-neighbour, destination clipped to the surface (also without a clipper; real DirectDraw would
  return DDERR_INVALIDRECT without one — lenient on purpose). `BltFast` honours `SRCCOLORKEY`/`DESTCOLORKEY`.
  `DDBLT_WAIT/ASYNC` are irrelevant (synchronous). `GetBltStatus`/`GetFlipStatus`/`IsLost`/`Restore` = DD_OK.
- `WaitForVerticalBlank(BLOCKBEGIN|BLOCKEND)` is S3's frame pacer (`WaitVBlank`=1). Since 2026-11-05 it is a
  **frame limiter** (perf-cpu): it blocks the calling guest thread (ThunkResult::Block) until `1000/cap` ms after its
  previous release, or returns at once if the frame was late (the old 60 Hz grid turned a 17 ms frame into 30 fps).
  Cap: default 60, env `S3_FPS_CAP` (0 = none), `ddraw::set_fps_cap`; see [performance.md](performance.md).
  `GetScanLine` / `GetVerticalBlankStatus` still use a simulated 60 Hz clock. `BLOCKBEGINEVENT` -> DDERR_UNSUPPORTED.
- `GetDC` uses the gdi32 bridge `s3_runtime::gdi::create_dc(DcTarget{addr,pitch,width,height,bpp,rgb565})`
  (installed by s3-win32 gdi32); returns DDERR_CANTCREATEDC if no hook is installed. `ReleaseDC` ->
  `gdi::release_dc`.
- Not implemented (E_NOTIMPL): overlays, BltBatch, DuplicateSurface. Palettes: 2/4/16/256 entries
  (DDPCAPS_1/2/4/8BIT), PALETTEENTRY dwords. Clippers only remember the HWND; `GetClipList` -> DDERR_NOCLIPLIST.

## DirectSound behaviour

- `CreateSoundBuffer`: primary (`DSBCAPS_PRIMARYBUFFER`, no data; its volume is the master volume; `SetFormat`
  stored, default 22050/2/16) or secondary (PCM tag 1, 1-2 channels, 8/16 bit; data in the process heap).
  `DuplicateSoundBuffer` shares the PCM memory (refcounted), own position/volume/pan/frequency.
- `Lock` handles wrap-around (two pointers), `DSBLOCK_FROMWRITECURSOR`, `DSBLOCK_ENTIREBUFFER`; primary Lock ->
  DSERR_PRIOLEVELNEEDED. `Play(LOOPING)`, `Stop` (keeps position), `GetStatus` (PLAYING|LOOPING),
  `Get/SetCurrentPosition` (write cursor = play + 15 ms), `Set/GetVolume` (-10000..0), `Set/GetPan`,
  `Set/GetFrequency` (0 = original, 100..200000), `GetFormat`, `GetCaps`.
- **Mixer** (`dsound::mixer_service`, registered as scheduler service `dsound-mixer`, runs once per
  `run_slice`): wall-clock paced, produces audio up to `LATENCY_MS` (60 ms) ahead of real time, at most 250 ms
  per call (longer stalls are skipped, not replayed). Output 44100 Hz stereo i16 -> `Host::queue_audio`. Gains:
  `10^(vol/2000)`, pan attenuates the opposite side the same way, master = primary volume. Play cursors therefore
  advance in real time even headless. Paused (`m.input.paused`) -> no output, pacing restarts on resume.
- **Device drift guard** (audio-verify, 2026-11-05): if the host reports a device queue
  (`Host::audio_queued_frames`, Android AAudio ring, s3run `--audio-play`), the mixer never lets it exceed
  `MAX_HOST_QUEUE_MS` (250 ms): frames above it are not produced this call (voices are delayed, not skipped;
  counted in `DsState::drift_cut_frames`). Nominal queue is ~60 ms, so this only acts on a slow/stalled device
  clock. Hosts without a device report 0 (pure wall-clock pacing).
- Every secondary `Play` is logged at Debug (`dsound: Play <buf> vol pan rate ch/bit bytes flags`, `s3run -v`) and
  counted in `DsState::voices_started`.
- **Other audio sources** (winmm waveOut / CD music): push interleaved i16 into
  `m.state::<s3_runtime::audio::AudioStreams>()` (`streams[id] = AudioStream { rate, channels, samples, gain }`);
  the mixer resamples and mixes them. This keeps a single producer for the host audio sink.
  (`s3-runtime/src/audio.rs` was added for this by the directx agent.)

## Audio verification (s3run `--audio-wav`, 2026-11-05)

How: `s3run ... --audio-wav ../scratch/audio/x.wav [--audio-wav-seconds 300]` writes exactly what reaches
`Host::queue_audio` (44100 Hz stereo i16; header rewritten every second, so a killed run still leaves a valid
file) and prints `audio timing: ... lead min/max/last, drift since 2 s, max gap between calls` at exit (lead =
audio produced minus wall time since the first block). Analyse with `python3 -I tools/wav_stats.py x.wav [--from
S] [--to S] [--window-ms N]` (RMS dBFS per window L/R, peak, clipped samples, silent windows, 2-200 ms zero gaps
inside signal). `S3_MUSIC_VOLUME=0` mutes the CD music to isolate effects. Optional real playback: build with
`--features audio-cpal` (cpal 0.15/ALSA, needs `pkg-config alsa`; off by default) and pass `--audio-play`.

Findings (GOG S3.EXE, menu -> random map in game, ~45 s runs):

- **Timing**: lead constant 59-60 ms from start to end (= `LATENCY_MS`), drift 0 ms over 40 s, 44.07 s audio for
  44.01 s wall; largest gap between mixer calls 39-67 ms (busy loading); no zero gaps inside the signal. The mixer
  keeps up headless at release speed. (A debug build is too slow: lead dips to -42 ms.)
- **Music** (MCI cdaudio track 7, from ~16 s when the game starts): -31 dBFS RMS L / -28 R, peaks ~8000, no
  clipping, continuous. The menu is silent: S3 plays no music there (same under wine: only Track07 at game start).
- **Effects** (music muted): first sounds 1-2 s after the map appears; ambient/worker sounds -35..-55 dBFS. The
  game creates 11 mono 22050 Hz 16-bit buffers (33939..251792 bytes) + `DuplicateSoundBuffer` per overlapping play,
  and plays them with `SetVolume(-2000)` `SetPan(+-...)` `Play(0)` (no looping, no `GetCurrentPosition`/streaming
  buffers: the play cursor is only relevant for `GetStatus` end detection). Pan 820 -> left 8 dB lower, visible in
  the per-channel RMS. Mixed peak with music < 8100: no clipping headroom issue.
- **Bug fixed**: winmm's music service queued music to `Host::queue_audio` *itself* while the DirectSound mixer
  also queued (two producers: music blocks were appended between mixer blocks, i.e. twice the audio per wall
  second, music and effects not overlapped, sink queues growing). Music now goes through
  `AudioStreams[MUSIC_STREAM_ID]` (see [user32-gdi32.md](user32-gdi32.md)); the mixer is the only producer.
- Quality checks (unit tests `mixer_resamples_22k_voice_smoothly_with_pan`,
  `mixer_passes_stream_music_through_unchanged_and_gapless`, `mixer_drift_guard_caps_host_queue`): 22050 -> 44100
  linear upsampling of a 441 Hz sine stays within 25 LSB of the ideal; 44100 Hz streams pass bit-exact; dB curve
  `10^(v/2000)` and pan law (opposite side attenuated by |pan|/100 dB) match DirectSound.

## DirectInput behaviour

- `CreateDevice(GUID_SysMouse | GUID_SysKeyboard)`, else DIERR_DEVICENOTREG. `SetDataFormat`,
  `SetCooperativeLevel` accepted (format not interpreted: mouse = DIMOUSESTATE layout, keyboard = 256 bytes).
- `SetProperty(DIPROP_BUFFERSIZE)` sets the buffer (0 = unbuffered, no events kept); overflow drops the oldest
  and returns DI_BUFFEROVERFLOW once.
- `Acquire` starts reading `m.input` from "now" (own cursor) and takes the current host mouse position as the
  reference for relative deltas. Host `MouseMove{x,y}` -> `DIMOFS_X/Y` deltas (same sequence number),
  `MouseButton` -> `DIMOFS_BUTTON0+i` (0x80 / 0), `Key{vk}` -> DIK scan code (table `vk_to_dik`).
- `pump_service` (service `dinput-pump`, also called at the start of GetDeviceData/GetDeviceState) converts new
  host events for every acquired device and sets the `SetEventNotification` event (handle table Event ->
  signaled), which wakes S3's main thread.
- `GetDeviceData(cb>=16, rgdod, &n, DIGDD_PEEK?)`, `GetDeviceState` (accumulated deltas, reset on read),
  `GetCapabilities`, `GetDeviceInfo`, `EnumDevices`. Not acquired -> DIERR_NOTACQUIRED.
- HYPOTHESIS: S3 moves its own cursor from the relative DirectInput deltas. As long as host positions are
  absolute and the game cursor started at the host position, the deltas reproduce the touch position; if the
  game clamps differently the cursor could drift (check on device; fix would be to resync on touch-down).

## DirectPlay behaviour

**Update 2026-11-05 (mp-dplay):** the IDirectPlay4A methods the game uses are now real and backed by our relay
(`dplay_net.rs`); the game's LAN multiplayer menu creates/joins sessions and runs lockstep games. Details, tests and
the two-instance desktop test: [multiplayer.md](multiplayer.md) sections 5-6. The paragraph below describes the
remaining stubs (lobby, groups) and the original stub behaviour.

Both CLSIDs create objects for any requested IID (IDirectPlay2..4 A/W share the IDirectPlay4A vtable prefix;
lobby 1..3). Enumerations (`EnumConnections`, `EnumSessions`, `EnumPlayers`, ...) succeed with no callbacks,
`Close`/`Initialize` succeed, `GetMessageCount` = 0, `Receive` = DPERR_NOMESSAGES, lobby
`GetConnectionSettings` = DPERR_NOTLOBBIED, everything else DPERR_UNAVAILABLE. `DirectPlayCreate` fails with
DPERR_UNAVAILABLE, `DirectPlayLobbyCreateA` returns a lobby object. Error code values are from memory of
dplay.h (HYPOTHESIS until multiplayer menus are exercised). Update 2026-11-05: S3.EXE's own HRESULT table (`0x7a03b4`)
confirms the values (DPERR_NOTLOBBIED = 0x8877042E); the full RE of the game's DirectPlay use and the plan for the
real implementation over our relay are in [multiplayer.md](multiplayer.md).

## Open points

- Runs against S3.EXE (menu + in game, 2026-11-05). Still watch for: unexpected QueryInterface IIDs
  (logged as warnings), Lock/GetDC on the primary, unknown Blt flags.
- Present happens on every primary write; if a frame is assembled from several Blts to the primary, the host sees
  intermediate frames (S3 does one full-screen Blt per frame, so fine).
- 16-bit 555 surfaces are only created if the game asks with a 555 pixel format; the display is always 565.

`docs/porting/display.md`:

```md
# Display: GPU presenter, full-screen modes, FPS counter

Status 2026-11-05 (workflow `wf_a446e364-b12`, agent `display`). User request: high FPS and full-screen display
options like Settlers United, an FPS counter setting. Related: [resolution-zoom.md](resolution-zoom.md) (custom game
resolutions, zoom), [android.md](android.md), [mods.md](mods.md), [ui-hud.md](ui-hud.md).

Everything here is **presentation only**: it never changes guest-visible memory, so lockstep multiplayer
([determinism.md](determinism.md)) is unaffected.

## Display modes (`s3_mods::display`)

| Mode | What it does | Touch mapping |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Fit` | aspect kept, whole frame visible, black bars (old behaviour) | bars clamp to the frame edge |
| `Fill` | aspect kept, fills the screen, overflow cropped (centred) | cropped strip is unreachable; mods anchor UI with `visible_game_rect` |
| `Stretch` | fills the screen, aspect distorted | linear per axis |
| `Native wide` (default) | the game renders at a custom resolution with the screen's aspect (res-zoom picks it with `Viewport::native_wide_size`), shown like `Fit` → no bars. Known 800x600 menu screens use a full-screen menu layout ([menu-layout.md](menu-layout.md)); other frames of another aspect are shown like `Fit` | like `Fit` / through the layout pieces |

The old ESC/ABC/RMB letterbox buttons were removed 2026-11-07; both UI modes have
their own menu buttons (Classic: floating Menu, HUD: menu sheet), and the RMB/keyboard functions are gestures
(two-finger tap = cancel, three-finger tap = keyboard), see [touch.md](touch.md).

Filters: `Nearest` ("Pixel"), `Linear` ("Smooth"), `SharpBilinear` ("Sharp", default): nearest inside each source
pixel, a one-screen-pixel linear band at the pixel edges → crisp but evenly sized pixels at non-integer scales
(800x600 → 2229x904 is 1.507x). At an exact integer scale it equals nearest; when downscaling it uses linear.

### The shared transform

`s3_mods::display::Viewport` is the **only** screen↔game transform. Frontends build it per shown frame
(`Viewport::for_frame_split(mode, pixels, game_w, game_h, win_w, win_h, scene.panel)`), map touches/mouse with
`window_to_game`, and publish it to the mods with `display::set_viewport(m, Some(vp))`. Mods read:

- `display::viewport(m)` / `display::window_size(m)` (None headless without `--window`),
- `display::visible_game_rect(m)`: part of the frame that is on screen (game px; the whole frame except in Fill),
- `display::display_settings(m)`; menus change settings with `set_display` / `cycle_mode` / `cycle_filter` /
  `cycle_fps` (persisted in `mods-settings.json`); `override_display` changes them for one run only (CLI).
- `display::frame_viewport(m)` / `s3_mods::draw_viewport(m)`: the viewport of the frame being drawn (published window
  size + mode + this frame's panel split), for the window layer.

### Classic panel at a constant size (`PanelSplit`, 2026-11-08 overlay-window)

UI mode A shows the original left panel. With zoom it used to scale with the render size (big when zoomed in, tiny
zoomed out). Now, in `NativeWide` with the custom resolution on, in game (`display::panel_split`), the scene
published with each frame carries `PanelSplit { w: [0x730f24], h: art height of the layout variant }`
and `Viewport::new_split` draws:

- the panel part (frame `x < w`, `y < h`) at `win_h / h`: the art always fills the screen height (Fold4 cover:
  136 px art at 480 -> 256 px, 176 at 600 -> 265 px, 216 at 768 -> 254 px wide on screen); the black strip the game
  leaves below the art at heights between the variants is not shown any more;
- the map part (`x >= w`) in the rest of the window. The zoom picks render widths so this part keeps the map's
  aspect (`zoom::classic_width`: `w + (win_w - w*win_h/h) * H / win_h`, multiple of 8; < 1.2 % off), and pinch / menu
  zoom anchor in map-view fractions (`zoom::anchor_camera_map`, `ResState::anchor_map`).

**One panel variant at every size (2026-11-08, phone report "the panel flickers while zooming").** Two causes,
both fixed and verified on the phone (screen recording of injected pinches, 1045 frames, panel unchanged):

1. With a variant per height the game swapped the panel art when the zoom crossed 600 / 768 (256 / 265 / 254 px on
   screen and a different arrangement), so pinching around a border made the panel jump. UI mode A now uses the
   640x480 panel at every custom size (`res::CLASSIC_VARIANT`, `res::variant_for_mode`; the only one that fits the
   whole Classic range from 480 up). Costs some sharpness (136 px art scaled to 256 px on the Fold4 cover).
2. Single frames without the split: the presenter only used the split when the latest scene was made for the
   frame's size (a frame of a new size often arrives first: now `display::panel_for_frame` carries the split over),
   and `panel_split` needed a game frame within the last second (`res::in_game`), which a big zoom step (full
   landscape redraw) can exceed: now `res::in_game_frame` (up to 10 s while the shown frame has a custom size).
   `S3_PANEL_TRACE=1` prints why `panel_split` returned none.

**Panel art past the panel width (2026-11-08).** The 640x480 panel's minimap frame has a diagonal right edge (up
to x 207 at the top) and leaves that reach a few px past `w = 136`; they lie in the map part and scaled with the
zoom ("the diagonal edge still moves"). `PanelSplit::overhang` lists them as 4-row bands (`y0, y1, x_end`, measured
from a frame with a black map behind; numbers only; runs of rows with the same `x_end`, since 4-row bands also
carried map pixels that moved during zoom); `quads()` adds one panel-scale quad per band on top of the
map part, and `window_to_game` / `game_to_window` use the panel scale there (`PanelSplit::art_right`). Classic
never goes below the art's height (480), so the map part is never larger than the panel scale and no copy of the
edge shows next to it. The Classic context chip starts right of the overhang.

**Zoom below the panel art (2026-11-08).** The 640x480 panel needs 480 frame rows, so UI mode A could not zoom in
past 480 while the Mobile HUD goes to 200. Now heights below 480 keep a 480 high frame and show only `crop_h`
rows of the map part (centred, matching width) over the whole map area (`zoom::classic_crop` ->
`PanelSplit::crop_h`, `Viewport::map_src`). Those are exactly the pixels a smaller render would show, at the same
scale; it costs a 480 high render and the crop is centred (pinching inside the crop zooms about the screen centre,
and the outer rows of the 480 view cannot be shown at the map's edges). Verified desktop + phone (200 high, 60 fps).

**Leaves at the panel edge (2026-11-08, second fix).** The leaves below the minimap reach up to x 144; the frame
showed them a second time in the map part at the map's scale, at other heights than the panel's, so they seemed to
move while zooming. Now only the minimap frame rows (< 156) are overhang bands; the map part starts at
`PanelSplit::map_x0` (`w + 9`, `display::map_skip`; `zoom::classic_width` adds the 9 columns) and the leaf tips are
cut at the panel edge. Phone recording: the edge is identical in all frames.

**Native wide fills the window (2026-11-08).** The render width is a multiple of 8, so the frame's aspect differed
from the window's by up to ~0.5 % and `Viewport::new` left 1-4 px bars whose width changed with every zoom step;
everything anchored to the shown frame (Mobile HUD bars, ✕, FPS counter) shifted by a few px per step ("the HUD
jitters"). Within 2 % `NativeWide` now stretches the frame to the whole window.

**xBR upscaling filter (2026-11-08).** Zoom shows fewer game pixels scaled up (4.5x at 200 px height), so the
1998 pixel art looks blocky. `ScaleFilter::Xbr` ("xBR (HD edges)") is a GPU pixel-art upscaler in the Android
presenter: `gl::FS_XBR`, our GLSL ES 1.00 version of Hyllian's xBR level 2 (single pass at any scale, 21 nearest
taps, luma-weighted edge detection, 30/45/60 degree edge blends with a one-output-pixel smoothstep; bvec logic as
0/1 floats). Falls back to sharp bilinear when the shader does not compile (logged) and on the desktop CPU scaler.
Fold4 cover at 240 px height: compiles on Adreno, 120 fps with xBR and with sharp (no visible cost); edges of
units, buildings and rocks become smooth, ground texture looks "painted". Cycle it with "Filter" in the HUD
settings / Classic (CLI `--filter xbr`).

**AI upscaling filter (2026-11-08).** `ScaleFilter::Ai` ("AI (Anime4K)"): the small CNN x2 upscaler of Anime4K
v3.2 (`Anime4K_Upscale_CNN_x2_S`, https://github.com/bloc97/Anime4K, **MIT**, license text kept in the generated
file) on the GPU. `tools/anime4k_to_gles.py` converts the mpv user shader into GLSL ES 3.00 fragment shaders
(`s3-frontend/src/anime4k.rs`, generated: 4 conv passes + depth-to-space); `s3-frontend/src/upscale_ai.rs` runs
them per presented game frame: 4 passes at the frame size into RGBA16F textures (ping-pong, FBO), then
depth-to-space into an RGBA8 texture of twice the frame size (= bilinear frame + the network's luma residual),
which the presenter draws instead of the frame (same normalized coordinates, so the Classic split / quads work).
Needs a GLES 3 context: the presenter now asks for an ES3-capable config + context and falls back to GLES 2
(then and on any shader / framebuffer error: sharp bilinear, logged once). Used only when the frame is shown at
>= 1.2x and not for menu layouts. Fold4 inner screen (2176x1812) at 400 px height: 120 fps like sharp bilinear;
units, buildings and rocks look smooth and detailed instead of blocky (softer than xBR). Cycle with "Filter" in
the HUD settings or the Classic menu's floating buttons (new "Filter" button there).

Filters are chosen per drawn part (`present.rs` `Gles::use_filter`, 2026-11-08): with the Classic panel split the
panel quad (2-4x) and the map quad (any zoom) each get the program for their own scale, so xBR / AI also apply to
the original panel; the AI network runs when any part or a menu layout is enlarged >= 1.2x.

**Frame insets (2026-11-08).** The Classic magnifier used to copy 64x40 frame pixels into a layer image (CPU,
nearest), so the display filter never applied to it. Now it records `Layer::frame_inset(src, x, y, w, h)`
(`Cmd::FrameInset`): a transparent hole in the layer plus the source rectangle (in the item hash, so moving the
finger republishes). Frontends draw `DrawList::insets()` after the frame and before the layer: Android with the
same texture (AI output or frame) and `use_filter` for the inset's scale, desktop with
`display::draw_insets_xrgb`. Phone (AI, inner screen): the magnified building is smooth; outline and name stay on
top (later layer commands).

**Plan, not started: HD sprites (option 2).** If shader upscaling is not enough: upscale the game's sprites and
landscape textures 2-4x with an AI model (Real-ESRGAN class) **generated locally from the user's own files** (never
distributed: derived game assets), and render the game at 2x internally. Needs a native draw path for sprites,
landscape, shadows, selection marks in a 2x frame (our fast paths `fast_tile`, `fast_land_rows`, sprite rows are the
starting points), hit testing / mouse at 2x, and per-animation consistency (AI upscaling flickers between frames,
palette). Generation is slow on a phone (desktop tool + copy is more realistic). Biggest work item of the port so far.

**FPS limit and FPS counter position (2026-11-08).** `DisplaySettings::fps_limit` (30 / 60 / 120 / 144, plus the
display's refresh rate when it is above 144, `display::fps_limit_options`; default 60) is applied to the
DirectDraw frame limiter (`s3_dx::ddraw::set_fps_cap`) at install and on change (`display::apply_fps_limit`); a
developer override wins (env `S3_FPS_CAP`; Android `fps-cap.txt` sets that env). `DisplaySettings::fps_pos`
(auto / top left / top centre / top right / bottom right / bottom centre / bottom left) places the counter in the
free area: right of the Classic panel, below the HUD's resource strip, above the HUD's bottom bar. Both are
cycled with one tap: Mobile HUD Menu > Settings ("FPS limit", "FPS position"), Classic Menu floating buttons
("FPS limit", "FPS pos"). Desktop: 144 -> 82-86 fps (desktop speed), counter bottom right above the bar.

**Cursor in the window layer (2026-11-08).** `s3_runtime::cursor` drew the game's Windows cursor into the presented
frame, so it grew, shrank and moved with the zoom. With a window layer, `cursor_layer::CursorMod` sets
`CursorState::disabled` and blits the same image (RGBA copy per HCURSOR, XOR pixels as their colour) at
`game_to_window(mouse)` minus the hot spot, at `Layer::ui` scale (its size in a 600 px high frame), last (on top).
The window position is kept while the game position does not change, so a zoom does not move it on screen.
Without a window layer (old frontends) the frame cursor stays.

**Panel texts in the window layer (2026-11-08, panel-text).** The game draws its in-game texts (panel labels and
numbers, save slots, "Settlers / > 20 % Carriers", tooltips, clock, end banner, map labels) with `DrawTextA` into a
1-bpp DIB and copies its set bits onto the frame (RE: game-state-ui.md section 6 "Text DIB composite"). Enlarged
2-4x with the Classic panel these were blocky. `s3-mods/src/panel_text.rs` (GOG patch set, only while a frontend
shows the window layer):

- hook at the `DrawTextA` call `0x4a8725`: records string, rect, DT_* flags and the layout of the call in the DC's
  font (`s3_win32::user32::draw_text_layout`, the same code and font as our `DrawTextA`); the DIB clear
  `0x4d65e0` drops the records in its rectangle. The DIB still gets every text (guest state unchanged).
- hook at the composite `0x4d6740(x, y, w, h)`: when records lie in the rectangle, the copy onto the frame is skipped
  (`ret 0x10`) and they become frame texts clipped to that rectangle.
- lifetime: texts composited inside the panel renderer (call `0x4b2dc5`) stay until the panel redraws fully
  (`[snap+0x40] == 1` or `[gfx+0xf8] == 1` at that call), a new composite overlaps them, or the frame pixels under
  them change (hash in `draw_window`); all others (tooltip, clock, map labels) live for one frame (frame renderer
  `0x4b26c0` .. call `0x4b422f`). Dropped after 300 ms without a game frame (left the game).
- drawing: each line at `game_to_window` of its DIB position, size = font em size times the mapped line height,
  centred / right aligned like the game, colour RGB(230, 230, 230) with a black shadow (the game's colours). A text
  starting in the Classic panel (`x < PanelSplit::w`) is drawn wholly at the panel scale (the 180 px tooltip box at
  the panel's bottom reaches into the map part). The Classic magnifier draws the texts into its frame inset
  (`panel_text::draw_inset`).
- `S3_PANEL_TEXT=0` turns it off (comparison), `S3_PANEL_TEXT_LOG=1` logs every captured composite.

`window_to_game` / `game_to_window` / `scale()` (= map part) / `quads()` (source -> destination rectangles: one, or
panel + map) handle it, so touch mapping, the GPU presenter (one quad per part, sharp-bilinear scale per part), the
CPU scaler (`scale_to_xrgb`) and the mods agree. Fit, Fill, Stretch and menus (layouts) are unchanged.
`S3_PANEL_SPLIT=0` turns it off.

### Window overlay layer

Mods draw their UI at window resolution ([mods.md](mods.md) "Window layer"); the presenter blends the layer over the
game quad (Android: 2nd RGBA texture, only changed rows uploaded; s3run: CPU blend). The game frame contains only
game pixels (and the game's mouse cursor).

Gestures stay in game pixels (as before); thresholds (`touch.tap_slop` ...) are therefore in game pixels in every mode.

### Settings JSON (`<data dir>/mods-settings.json`)

```json
"display": { "mode": "NativeWide", "filter": "SharpBilinear", "fps_counter": "Off", "refresh_hz": 0 }
```

`mode`: `Fit` | `Fill` | `Stretch` | `NativeWide`; `filter`: `Nearest` | `Linear` | `SharpBilinear`;
`fps_counter`: `Off` | `Fps` | `Detailed`; `refresh_hz`: 0 = highest the panel offers, else e.g. 60 / 90 / 120.
Missing fields use the defaults (old files keep loading).

## FPS counter (`s3-mods/src/fps.rs`)

A mod (`FpsMod`, installed last so it draws on top of the HUD) that counts **real guest presents**
(`Machine::stats.presents`; overlay-only refreshes are not counted) and guest instructions over 500 ms windows.
Drawn small in the top-right corner of the visible game area (in the Mobile HUD at the top centre, since
2026-11-05 verify-fps1: top right it covered the full-screen map's "Close" and the "Back to HUD" button) (Bold 11 px, dark backdrop; green ≥ 55 fps, yellow
≥ 30, red below). `Fps`: "60 fps". `Detailed`: + "16.7 ms (max 33)" frame time avg/worst, "100 MIPS", and on Android
"disp 120/120 Hz" = presenter swaps per second / panel refresh rate. Toggles: settings JSON, `s3run --fps`, and the
UI modes' menus (they call `display::cycle_fps`).

## Android presenter (`s3-android/src/present.rs`, `gl.rs`)

Before: the activity thread copied the frame into an `ANativeWindow_lock`ed RGB565 buffer sized with the window's
aspect (letterbox) and the compositor scaled it; Fit only, and drawing ran on the input thread.

Now a **render thread** (`s3-present`):

1. The engine's `Host::present` copies the frame into `Shared::frame` and signals `Shared::frame_cv`; it never waits
   for the display (no vsync wait, no GL on the engine thread). The activity thread is no longer woken per frame.
2. The render thread waits on `frame_cv` (or 250 ms), copies the newest frame, uploads it as an RGB565 texture
   (`glTexImage2D` once per size, then `glTexSubImage2D`, `GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT_5_6_5`: no CPU conversion or scaling),
   draws one quad placed by the `Viewport` with the selected filter (sharp bilinear = fragment shader
   `gl::FS_SHARP` on a `GL_LINEAR` texture), the letterbox buttons as small textures (re-rendered only when size /
   state change), then `eglSwapBuffers` with swap interval 1. Only new frames are drawn (no redraws of the same
   frame), so at 60 game fps on a 120 Hz panel it swaps 60 times a second.
3. High refresh: after each new surface it calls `ANativeWindow_setFrameRateWithChangeStrategy(win, hz, DEFAULT,
   ALWAYS)` (API 31; `ANativeWindow_setFrameRate` on API 30; looked up with dlsym so the APK still runs on API 26).
   The activity thread additionally sets `WindowManager.LayoutParams.preferredDisplayModeId` / `preferredRefreshRate`
   to the mode with the current resolution and the highest refresh rate (or closest to `refresh_hz`), via JNI
   (`uithread.rs` `display_prefs`). The chosen rate is shown by the detailed FPS counter.
4. Full screen: the same JNI job sets `layoutInDisplayCutoutMode = ALWAYS` (API 30; `SHORT_EDGES` on 28-29), so the
   window covers the camera-cutout strip too (on the Fold4 cover screen the window was 2229 of 2316 px wide).
5. Window lifecycle: `Presenter::set_window(Some/None)` from `InitWindow` / `TerminateWindow` / resize waits until
   the render thread destroyed / created its EGL surface (Android requires the surface gone before
   `onNativeWindowDestroyed` returns). The EGL context survives window changes.
6. Fallback: if EGL/GLES init or surface creation fails, the render thread uses the old CPU path (Fit only) and
   publishes its `Letterbox` so touch mapping and button hits keep matching.

Touch mapping (`android.rs`): `Shared::viewport` (written by the render thread) → `Viewport::window_to_game`;
buttons via `overlay::hit_vp`. The engine thread forwards the viewport and display rates to the mods once per slice
(`frontend.rs` `sync_display`) and pushes the display settings to the presenter (`Shared::set_display`).

Measured on the phone (verify-fps1, 2026-11-05, Galaxy Z Fold4 cover screen): logcat `display: modes
[8:904x2316@120 9:...@96 10:...@60 ...] -> Some((8, 120))`, `present: GLES surface 2316x904 (window 2316x904)` (the
full panel width now, was 2229), `ANativeWindow_setFrameRateWithChangeStrategy(120) -> 0`; detailed counter
"disp 60/120 Hz" at 60 game fps. The `s3-present` thread uses ~10-14 % of one core (top) and 6.6 % of the process
cycles (simpleperf), the engine thread never waits for it. Native wide on the cover screen gives 1536x600 at the
default zoom (aspect 2316/904); HUD and Classic both fill the whole screen; Back closes the HUD full-screen map.
fps per mode and zoom: [performance.md](performance.md#phone-measurements). The FPS gain comes from the engine side
(perf-cpu + verify-fps1 fast paths), not from the presenter. The presenter's job is
to not get in the way: no blocking of the engine thread, vsync-paced swaps at the panel's high refresh rate.

## Desktop `s3run`

Window is resizable; the frame is scaled on the CPU into a window-size buffer with the same `Viewport` and filters
(`display::scale_to_xrgb`, per-axis tap tables; `minifb` `ScaleMode::UpperLeft`), mouse positions go through
`window_to_game`. Options (override `mods-settings.json` for this run, not saved):

```text
--display fit|fill|stretch|native   --filter nearest|linear|sharp   --fps off|fps|full   --window WxH
```

Headless with `--window WxH`: a simulated viewport for that screen size is published to the mods (so Native wide
and Fill can be tested headless). `shot f.png` writes the game frame at game resolution; `wshot f.png` writes the
window as the player sees it (frame scaled with the display mode / panel split + the mods' window layer) at the
`--window` size. Touch injects with a `w` prefix (`wtap`, `wpinch`, ...) take window pixels.

Example: `s3run --game-dir game-files/gog-s3-ultimate --data-dir scratch/d --window 2229x904 --display fill --fps full`.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p s3-mods display:: fps::` — viewport math for all modes on the Fold4 cover size, CPU scaler
  (nearest / sharp = nearest at integer scale / linear), sharp tap monotonicity, enum parsing, FPS windows.
- `cargo test -p s3-android` — viewport button layout / hit / button image, GL clip rect.
- Android build: `scripts/build-apk.sh --abi arm64-v8a` (cargo ndk); device verification is a separate phase.

```

`docs/porting/integration-log.md`:

```md
# Integration log (s3run against the real GOG S3.EXE)

Each round: build `s3run`, run it headless against the local GOG install, record how far the game gets, blockers
(by area: cpu-int, cpu-fpu, kernel32-runtime-pe, user-gdi-misc, directx, engine-desktop) and performance.
Screenshots stay local (`scratch/keep/`, gitignored): they show game graphics and must never be committed.

## How to run

```sh
cd port
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$PWD/target cargo build --release -j 4 -p s3-desktop
G="--headless --game-dir ../game-files/gog-s3-ultimate --data-dir ../scratch/data"
# main menu -> "Single Player: Scenario" -> map popup OK (630 467) -> Game Setup OK (730 567) -> players OK (730 567)
# -> random map 384 starts. One click per OK is enough (three OK screens; the two last OKs share a position).
I="1000:move 165 235;1200:click 165 235;3000:move 630 467;3200:click 630 467;5000:move 730 567;5200:click 730 567;7000:move 730 567;7200:click 730 567"
./target/release/s3run $G --max-seconds 40 --inject "$I" --screenshot ../scratch/keep/x.png
```

- `--screenshot-every-present <dir>` writes only the **first 300** presents (~100-900 KB each; delete the dir
  afterwards). `--screenshot <png>` writes the last frame at exit.
- `S3_SAMPLE=1` (added in r1): once per second prints, per guest thread, the millions of instructions executed in that
  second plus EIP and state (`[sample 17.1s] t4:73M@0xfff0020d/Blocked ...`). Cheap; use it to see which thread is busy.
- `S3_TRACE=calls S3_TRACE_LIMIT=100000000` traces every HLE call (pipe through `grep -v` of hot calls:
  `CriticalSection|TlsGetValue|LastError|HeapSize|IntersectRect|...`, and of `guest t5` AI debug strings).
- Inject coordinates are in the **current** display mode: 800x600 in menus, 640x480 in game.
- Touch inject commands (2026-11-06, raw pointer events through the s3-mods gesture recognizer, like Android):
  `tap x y`, `tap2 x y`, `drag x1 y1 x2 y2 [ms]`, `longpress x y [ms]`, `pinch cx cy scale [ms]`; `S3_MODS_DEBUG=1`
  draws fingers and gesture names. See [mods.md](mods.md#desktop-testing-s3run---inject-touch-commands).
- Useful in-game coordinates (640x480): build menu (house icon) `25 167`; first building category `25 200`;
  first building in the list `37 237`.
- Multiplayer (2026-11-05, mp-dplay): `port/scripts/mp-local-test.sh` drives two headless instances + a local relay
  through the LAN menu into one game; `--mp-hash FILE` (per-simulation-tick state hash), env `S3_RELAY_URL`,
  `S3_NET_NAME`, `S3_DPLAY_TRACE=1`, `S3_GAME_LOG=1` (game's own debug log), `S3_EXE_ARGS` (guest command line,
  e.g. `-netmon`). See [multiplayer.md](multiplayer.md) section 6.
- More inject commands (2026-11-05): `t:shot file.png` writes the current frame at time t (several per run, no need
  for `--screenshot-every-present`); `t:text abc` presses one key per character 120 ms apart (letters, digits, space,
  `-`; capitals with Shift). Careful: in game, letters are hotkeys (typing opened the build menu).
- Read-only memory inspection for RE (re-units, 2026-11-05): `t:xpeek EXPR LEN`, `t:xdump EXPR LEN FILE` (EXPR with
  `@` pointer steps, e.g. game data `0x700ffee0@0x3a0@0x2d280`), `t:scan VALUE [MAX]`; see
  [game-state-units.md](../reverse-engineering/game-state-units.md#tools).
- **Save/load round trip** (in game at ~45 s when other jobs run; it can take 16-45 s): computer icon `21 452` ->
  "Save Game" `68 225` -> slot 1 line `40 244` saves at once ("Game Saved", no name prompt; slots 2-8 are 21 px
  apart) -> computer icon `21 452` -> "Quit Game" `68 420` -> YES `38 420` -> Game Statistics (click anywhere,
  `400 300`) -> main menu (800x600) -> "Load Game" `165 355` -> first entry `300 126` -> saved game continues:
  ```
  I="$I;45000:click 21 452;48000:click 68 225;51000:click 40 244;53000:shot s1.png;54000:click 21 452;56000:click 68 420;58000:click 38 420;63000:click 400 300;66000:shot s2.png;67000:click 165 355;69500:shot s3.png;70000:click 300 126;95000:shot s4.png"
  ```
  Verified 2026-11-05 (see kernel32.md "Save / load").

Order of calls matches the wine trace (registry, CDAUDIO window, DDraw probe, 2 threads at menu, 3 at game start,
SetDisplayMode 800x600 -> 640x480, `WaitForVerticalBlank` pacing, Blt of the 536x582 world buffer). Guest C++
exceptions (`RaiseException 0xE06D7363`) are caught normally (20-40 per run, wine: 36).

### Fixed in r1

- **user-gdi-misc**: `SelectObject(CreateCompatibleDC(0), bitmap)` returned 0 because new DCs had `bitmap = 0`.
  S3.EXE (`0x4a8123` CreateCompatibleDC, `0x4a8233` SelectObject, then `FormatMessageA` + `throw`) treats 0 as an
  error; the second throw escaped -> `UnhandledExceptionFilter` -> CRT `MessageBoxA "abnormal program termination"`
  -> `ExitProcess(3)`. Fix: DCs start with stock `DEFAULT_BITMAP` (`gdi32.rs`), test
  `select_bitmap_into_memory_dc_returns_previous`.
- **engine-desktop**: `S3_SAMPLE=1` per-thread sampler in `s3run`.

### Open issues / blockers (none stop the game)

| Area | Problem | Evidence |

### Performance (desktop, release, one host core, other agents running)

- Menu: idle (threads blocked in `GetMessageA`/waits); ~10 M instructions total in 10 s.
- Loading (8-16 s): one thread at a time, ~130-165 M guest instructions/s.
- In game: ~48 presents/s (`WaitForVerticalBlank` paced); render thread ~70-85 M instr/s + AI ~20 M instr/s
  ≈ 90-110 M instr/s, **~60 % of one host core**. Android arm64 should be OK if it reaches >= 1/2 of that.
- Two early runs looked slower (loading picture still shown at 36 s); 7 later sampled runs all reached the game at
  16-17 s. HYPOTHESIS: those runs ran in parallel with other heavy jobs. Re-check on Android.

**Fixes made** (smallest change each):

1. `s3-mods/src/touch_game.rs` `layout()`: accepted only `panel_w > 0`, but mode B sets the panel width to 0, so
   touch-context thought no game was running and every gesture fell back to plain mouse mapping. Now `panel_w >= 0`
   (+ unit test `full_screen_hud_layout_is_all_map`).
2. **Multiplayer**: the global `[0x7e3408]` (`CGameData*`) stays **0** in a network game (VERIFIED on host and joiner
   with `peek`), while `[logic+0x3a0]` is valid. `touch_game::gd()` now falls back to the `[logic+0x3a0]` recorded by
   the `HandleInput` hooks (`note_logic`, touch.rs and ui_hud_game.rs); `ui_hud_game::gd()` uses the same fallback.
   Without it, touch play in MP could select (left click) but never move.
3. Android: manifest had no `INTERNET` permission; added. `s3-android/src/frontend.rs` reads the relay URL from
   `<data dir>/relay-url.txt` (sets `S3_RELAY_URL` before the engine starts).
4. Mode A had no way into mode B: while the Menu (page 7) is open, a "UI: Mobile HUD" button sits above "Close"
   (`ui_classic.rs` `FloatBtn::HudMode`; saves the setting, closes the menu).
5. Cosmetic: touch.rs no longer draws its ✕ placement cancel in mode B (the HUD banner has Cancel; the ✕ covered the
   resource strip). The invisible ✕ hit area top right still cancels placement in mode B.
6. `S3_TOUCH_TRACE=1` also prints each tap decision (`touch: tap (x,y) mode .. -> ..`, or why it fell back).

Not verified: pinch / two-finger gestures and long-press box select on Android (adb cannot do them; desktop + unit
tests only); real phone; attack on an enemy by tap; Android as MP host; desync hash on Android.

```md
# iOS app (no Mac: xtool on WSL)

Status 2026-11-08: the app builds and links without a Mac: `scripts/build-ios.sh` -> `port/ios/xtool/S3Mobile.app`
(Mach-O arm64, 10 MB, iOS 17.0+), SDK from `Xcode_27.2.xip` via `xtool sdk install` (no Apple login needed for
that). Signed and installed on the iPhone 2026-11-09 (`build-ios.sh --install`, patched usbmuxd below); first run pending. Target: iPhone,
iOS 17+, free Apple ID (re-sign every 7 days).

## Pieces

| Part | Where | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shared frontend | `port/crates/s3-frontend` | launcher, upload server, engine thread, `Shared`, touch -> pointer events, audio ring, GLES renderer `glrender` (also used by Android `present.rs`) |
| Rust core | `port/crates/s3-ios` | `libs3ios.a` (staticlib), C API `port/ios/Sources/CS3iOS/include/s3ios.h` |
| Swift shell | `port/ios` | SwiftPM package for xtool: `S3MobileApp.swift` (SwiftUI app, lifecycle), `GameView.swift` (GLKView + CADisplayLink, touches, UIKeyInput soft keyboard, hardware keys -> VK, haptics), `Core.swift` (paths, AVAudioEngine source node) |
| Build | `port/scripts/build-ios.sh` | cargo (Windows) then `xtool dev build` / `run` in WSL Ubuntu |

Why a separate `s3-frontend` crate: `s3-android` is a `cdylib`, and cargo builds every crate type of a dependency,
so depending on it from the iOS staticlib needed an Apple linker. A plain rlib avoids that; `s3-android` re-exports its
modules under the old paths (`crate::launcher`, ...).

Why OpenGL ES and not Metal: iOS 17 still ships OpenGLES.framework (deprecated, works), so the Android GLES renderer
is reused unchanged: GLKit makes the EAGLContext current and binds its framebuffer, then `s3ios_draw` runs
`Composer::draw_gl`. EGL stays Android only. The AI upscaler (GLES 3 compute-like passes) is Android only for now; the
AI filter falls back to sharp bilinear on iOS.

## Flow

- Main thread: CADisplayLink (up to 120 Hz) -> `s3ios_tick` (launcher requests, engine end, haptics, keyboard,
  `redraw` when frame/status/layer/display changed) -> `GLKView.display()` -> `s3ios_draw(drawableW, drawableH)`.
- Touches: UITouch -> ids in touch order; actions down / pointer down / move / pointer up / up / cancel, same as
  Android MotionEvents (`s3_frontend::touch::pointer_events`), window pixels = points * `contentScaleFactor`.
- Keyboard: three-finger tap / launcher text field -> `keyboard` in `S3Out` -> `becomeFirstResponder` (UIKeyInput).
  Hardware keyboard: `pressesBegan` -> HID usage -> VK (`s3ios_key`) + typed chars (`s3ios_char`).
- Audio: `AVAudioSourceNode` pulls interleaved i16 stereo 44100 Hz (`s3ios_audio_pull`) and converts to float.
- Background: scene phase not active -> `s3ios_set_background(1)`: the game pauses (no background play on iOS yet:
  iOS stops apps without a background mode), audio engine paused.
- Files: `Documents/Settlers3/` = game dir (Files app "On My iPhone > S3 Mobile", `UIFileSharingEnabled`,
  or the launcher's upload server), `Documents/Data/` = settings + `log.txt` of the last run. Both are deleted with
  the app (re-signing after 7 days keeps them).
- Game folder outside the app: launcher > Game files > "Choose game folder..." opens `UIDocumentPickerViewController`
  for a folder; `Core.usePickedFolder` starts security-scoped access, stores a bookmark in UserDefaults
  (`gameFolderBookmark`) and calls `s3ios_set_game_dir(..., 1)`; restored at every start. "Use app folder" forgets
  it. Such a folder (e.g. On My iPhone/Settlers3) survives deleting the app. Avoid iCloud Drive (files can be
  evicted). `S3Out.pick_folder` carries the launcher's `Request::PickFolder` / `UseAppFolder`.
- Pushing the game files from a PC: `python3 -P tools/upload_game_files.py <game folder> "<URL shown on the phone>"`
  (8 parallel connections, skips files already there): 1.6 GB in ~2 min at ~17 MB/s. A curl-per-file loop managed
  only a few files per second (process start + 2 requests per file, 1673 mostly small files).

## Setup (once, in WSL Ubuntu 26.04 aarch64)

Done on this PC 2026-11-08: apt `usbmuxd libimobiledevice-utils` + Swift build deps, swiftly + Swift 6.4.2,
xtool 1.24.0 at `~/.local/bin/xtool`. Remaining (user, needs Apple login):

1. Xcode `.xip` from developer.apple.com/download/all (used: 27.2). SDK: `xtool sdk install <path to .xip>`
   (done 2026-11-08; `swift sdk list` shows `darwin`).
2. Login (user, once): `xtool auth login` (or `xtool setup`) -> "Password" for a free Apple ID. Any Apple ID works, it
   does not have to be the one on the iPhone; xtool suggests a separate one because this login uses private Apple
   APIs. The iPhone is registered as a test device of that account.
3. iPhone over USB into WSL (verified 2026-11-09, iPhone 14 Pro `iPhone15,2`, iOS 27.2):
   - `winget install --exact dorssel.usbipd-win` (5.3.0 arm64), then elevated `usbipd bind --force --busid <id>`
     (`--force`: Windows' own composite/WPD driver holds the phone even without iTunes), `usbipd attach --wsl
     --busid <id>` (a WSL distro must be running).
   - Tap "Trust" on the phone; `ideviceinfo -k DeviceName` answers.
   - **usbmuxd 1.1.1 over usbipd-win breaks app uploads**: the phone logs `asyncReadComplete, message was too large
     (65536 bytes, max = 65535)` and xtool fails with `LockdownClient.Error.muxError` / hangs at Packaging
     (usbmuxd issue #247, open). Cause (HYPOTHESIS, fits the symptom): usbipd-win drops the separate zero-length
     packet usbmuxd sends after a transfer that is a multiple of wMaxPacketSize (512), so the phone merges two
     transfers. Fix: `port/ios/usbmuxd-usbipd-zlp.patch` (on usbmuxd 3ded00c) splits such TCP packets so no
     transfer needs a ZLP. Build in WSL (`./autogen.sh --without-preflight --without-systemd && make`, deps
     `libusb-1.0-0-dev libplist-dev libimobiledevice-dev libimobiledevice-glue-dev`), stop the stock daemon, run
     `sudo ~/usbmuxd-src/src/usbmuxd -f -v`. With it the install went through (Installing/Verifying 100%).
   - The iTunes relay of xtool issue #19 (Windows usbmuxd on port 27015) needs Apple Mobile Device Support, which
     is x64-only drivers: not available on this ARM64 PC.
   - On the phone: Settings > Privacy & Security > Developer Mode (appears after the first install attempt), and
     Settings > General > VPN & Device Management > trust the Apple ID's developer certificate.

```

## Known gaps / risks

- Only deprecation warnings (GLKView / EAGLContext, OpenGL ES deprecated since iOS 12).
- No JIT on iOS (W^X); the interpreter is the default anyway.
- LAN discovery uses UDP broadcast/multicast; iOS 14+ needs the local network permission (Info.plist text set) and
  multicast may need the `com.apple.developer.networking.multicast` entitlement (Apple approval) — HYPOTHESIS:
  broadcast to the subnet works without it. Joining by IP / relay URL does not need it.
- Launcher texts still talk about Android paths in places (Files page).
