`docs/porting/kernel32.md`:

```md
# KERNEL32 HLE and the runtime pieces under it

Code: `port/crates/s3-win32/src/kernel32.rs` (+ `kernel32_{sync,file,time,locale}.rs`, tests in
`kernel32_tests.rs`), runtime support in `port/crates/s3-runtime` (`machine.rs` waits, `handles.rs`, `vfs.rs`,
`mapfile.rs`, `hosttime.rs`, `resources.rs`, `seh.rs`). Status 2026-11-05: all 130 static KERNEL32 imports plus the
GetProcAddress targets have handlers; S3.EXE reaches the main menu and Game Setup headless (see "Integration").

## Identity the guest sees

| Question | Answer | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OS version | Windows 98: `GetVersion` = `0xC0000A04`, `GetVersionExA` = 4.10 build 1998, platform 1 (`" A"`) | game targets Win9x; consistent with the foundation choice |
| CPU / system | 1 × Pentium (586, level 5), 4 KiB pages, 64 KiB granularity, user range 0x10000-0x7FFEFFFF | `GetSystemInfo` |
| Memory | 256 MiB RAM, 192 MiB free (`GlobalMemoryStatus`; all values < 2 GiB for 32-bit math) | |
| Locale | LCID 0x0409, ANSI cp 1252, OEM cp 437; `GetLocaleInfoA/W` table for en-US (incl. `LOCALE_RETURN_NUMBER`) | game language comes from registry `Language` (registry.md), not the locale — HYPOTHESIS |
| Install dir | `C:\S3`, exe `C:\S3\S3.EXE`, command line `S3.EXE` (+ env `S3_EXE_ARGS` if set, debug only, e.g. `-netmon`), cwd `C:\S3` | VFS (architecture.md) |
| Drives | `GetDriveTypeA` = DRIVE_FIXED for every path, `GetLogicalDrives` = C: only, volume label `S3`, FAT32, 1 GiB free | wine-trace: fixed drive is accepted; no CD check |
| Temp dir | `C:\S3\TEMP\` (overlay) | |
| HLE DLL paths | `GetModuleFileNameA(hHLE)` = `C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM\<NAME>.DLL` | |
| Std handles | fake `0x10/0x14/0x18`, `GetFileType` = FILE_TYPE_CHAR, writes go to the log | MSVC CRT `_ioinit` probes them |
| Time | `GetTickCount` = host monotonic ms; QPC = 1 MHz host µs, strictly increasing; wall clock from the host with the host's UTC offset as time zone bias (no DST rules, TIME_ZONE_ID_UNKNOWN) | QPC must advance (blit benchmark 0x5c4280) |

## Threads, waits, timers (cooperative scheduler)

- `CreateThread` → `Machine::create_thread` (own stack + TEB; `CREATE_SUSPENDED` honoured). The stack argument is the
  initial **commit** like on Windows: the stack size is the PE reserve (1 MiB), or the argument rounded up to 1 MiB
  when it is larger, or the argument itself with `STACK_SIZE_PARAM_IS_A_RESERVATION` (0x10000). S3.EXE's
  `_beginthreadex` passes 0x1000; until 2026-11-05 that gave 64 KiB stacks, and the save-slot reader (256 KiB of
  locals, `FUN_004a5c80` via `_chkstk`) ran below the stack, so its SEH frames failed the frame check and the
  CFileNotFound exception for a missing `slot N.sav` became "unhandled" (crash when opening the Save menu).
  `ResumeThread`/`SuspendThread` count, `GetExitCodeThread`, `TerminateThread` (other threads), priorities are stored only.
- A blocking call returns `ThunkResult::Block`; the scheduler retries the handler every round. Generic wait:
  **`Machine::poll_wait(handles, wait_all, timeout_ms) -> WaitPoll::{Ready(i), Timeout, Failed, Pending}`** — also
  meant for user32 `MsgWaitForMultipleObjects` (check the message queue first, then call `poll_wait`; on `Pending`
  return `Block`). Timeouts count from the first call (`Thread::block_since`).
- Objects: events (manual/auto), mutexes (owner + recursion, `ERROR_NOT_OWNER`), semaphores (`ERROR_TOO_MANY_POSTS`),
  thread handles, **waitable timers** (`KernelObject::Timer`, due time in host ms, periodic re-arm, missed periods are
  not replayed). Named objects share one namespace (`ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS` when re-created).
- `PulseEvent` releases blocked waiters (all for manual-reset, one for auto) via `Thread::pulsed`, then leaves the
  event reset (`Machine::pulse_event`).
- **Waitable timers are provided** (CreateWaitableTimerA/OpenWaitableTimerA/SetWaitableTimer/CancelWaitableTimer), so the
  game takes its waitable-timer path (static-startup.md) and does not need `timeSetEvent`. Verified at runtime: both
  menu threads create a timer with period 500 ms (`SetWaitableTimer(h, due, 0x1f4, 0, 0, 0)` from 0x60d0e7).
  Completion routines (APCs) are ignored with a warning.
- `Sleep(n)` always yields (also `Sleep(0)`) and returns after ≥ n host ms.
- Critical sections live in the guest struct (`LockCount` -1 = free, `RecursionCount`, `OwningThread` = tid). A
  contended `Enter` blocks; `Leave` **hands ownership directly** to one blocked waiter (round robin from the leaving
  thread's slot) so a thread looping Enter/Leave cannot starve others under cooperative scheduling. A section owned by
  an exited thread is taken over (logged).
- TLS: 64 slots in the TEB (`TlsAlloc` zeroes the slot in all threads; `TlsGetValue` clears LastError like Windows).
- `DuplicateHandle` turns the `GetCurrentThread`/`GetCurrentProcess` pseudo handles into real handles.

## Files (all through the VFS)

- `CreateFileA` implements all five dispositions with the Win32 error codes (`ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` vs
  `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND`, `ERROR_FILE_EXISTS`, `ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS` as LastError on success). Read-only opens use the
  game file directly; any write access first copies the file into `data_dir/overlay` (`Vfs::copy_up`); creates go to the
  overlay. Directories open only with `FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`. Device names (`CON`, `\\.\`) fail.
- `DeleteFileA` / `MoveFileA` / `RemoveDirectoryA` on files that exist only in the game dir record a **whiteout**
  (`data_dir/overlay-whiteouts.txt`, lower-case game-relative paths); the game dir is never modified. The 19 `MoveFileA`
  calls in `Map\Multi` at startup (`A256-2_Quick3.map` -> `A256-2-Quick3.map` ...) fail with ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND
  (wine) or ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS (our GOG copy has both names); the game ignores the result.
- `FindFirstFileA` lists overlay + game dir merged (case-insensitive, overlay wins), with `.`/`..` first for wildcard
  patterns like Windows; WIN32_FIND_DATAA attributes are DIRECTORY or ARCHIVE, times = host mtime.
- `SetFileAttributesA` accepts and ignores attributes. `GetFileTime` = host mtime/atime; `SetFileTime` is a no-op.
- `S3_FILES=1` logs every CreateFileA / FindFirstFileA / Delete / Move / Copy / Create- and RemoveDirectoryA with the
  guest path, result and LastError at Info (`[files] ...`); filter out `Gfx|Snd|siedler` for readable output.

### Save / load (verified 2026-11-05, desktop headless)

What S3.EXE does (runtime, `S3_FILES=1`; code `FUN_0050ac40`, `FUN_0050b670`, `FUN_00509980`, file class
`FUN_004a5c80`/`FUN_004a5600` -> `FUN_00619610` = CreateFileA wrapper that throws `Win32::CFileNotFound*`, caught in
`FUN_004a5600`):

| Step | Calls |
| --- | --- |
| In-game: computer icon (bottom left) -> panel "Save Game" | reads `C:\S3\Save\slot 1.sav` .. `slot 8.sav` (GENERIC_READ, OPEN_EXISTING); missing slots fail with ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND, are caught and shown as empty lines |
| Click a slot line | `CreateDirectoryA("C:\S3\Save")`, `("C:\S3\Save\Multi")` (ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS: the GOG game dir has `Save\Multi`), then `CreateFileA("C:\S3\Save\slot N.sav", GENERIC_READ\|WRITE, CREATE_ALWAYS)` -> overlay `data_dir/overlay/Save/slot N.sav` (~4.6 MB for a fresh random 384 map), panel says "Game Saved". **No name is asked**: slots are fixed, the list shows the save time + map name |
| Main menu -> Load Game | `FindFirstFileA("C:\S3\Save\*.sav")` (merged overlay + game dir), reads each listed file's header; list shows "Game Clock" (host local time of the save) and "Map Name" |
| Click the entry | reads the slot file, switches to 640x480 and continues the saved game |

File type tag in the header is 0x0b (`FUN_004a5c80` accepts 10 or 11; a checksum over the data follows the tag).
`Save\Multi\*.mps` (the user's multiplayer saves) stay visible through the merged listing; they are used by the
multiplayer load path only (`Save\Multi\`, `Multi\temp.mps`), not by the single-player Load Game list.
Test: `kernel32_tests::save_slots_overlay_and_game_dir`. Evidence (local): `scratch/keep/rt1-saved.png`,
`rt2-menu.png`, `rt3-loadlist.png`, `rt4-loaded.png`.
- **Memory-mapped files**: `CreateFileMappingA` + `MapViewOfFile` `mmap` the host file (MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_FIXED) into a
  64 KiB-aligned guest region (`s3_runtime::mapfile`), so the ~230 MB of GFX files cost no RAM until touched (important
  on Android). Pages wholly past EOF stay anonymous zero pages. Writes through a view are private (not written back) —
  HYPOTHESIS: the game never writes through views. Mapping a size larger than the file does not grow it (logged).
  Pagefile-backed mappings (`INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE`) share one zeroed block between views. `UnmapViewOfFile` puts
  anonymous pages back and releases the region. Falls back to copying when `mmap` fails.

## Memory, process, errors

- `VirtualAlloc/Free/Query/Protect`, `Heap*` map onto `s3-mem` (foundation). `LocalAlloc`/`GlobalAlloc` families are
  fixed blocks from the process heap (handle == pointer). `IsBad*Ptr` check that every page is committed and not in the
  NULL guard.
- `GetModuleHandleA`/`LoadLibraryA`/`GetProcAddress` know the exe and the HLE modules only (other DLLs fail with
  `ERROR_MOD_NOT_FOUND`); `GetProcAddress` returns 0 for names no HLE module declares (logged `not declared`).
- `IsProcessorFeaturePresent` (CRT looks it up via GetProcAddress) matches our CPUID (Pentium P54C): TRUE only for
  `PF_COMPARE_EXCHANGE_DOUBLE` (2) and `PF_RDTSC_INSTRUCTION_AVAILABLE` (8); FALSE for FDIV errata (0), FPU
  emulated (1), MMX (3), SSE/3DNow and unknown features. `user32!GetLastActivePopup(hwnd)` returns hwnd.
- Environment: `GetEnvironmentStrings[W]` return the block built by `process.rs`; `Get/SetEnvironmentVariableA` work on a
  host-side copy (the block is not rebuilt).
- `CreateProcessA` fails with `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` (only used for the 565→555 converter / external tools);
  `TerminateProcess(self)` = exit.
- `RaiseException` → `seh::raise_exception` (guest-side dispatch over FS:[0]; continuable exceptions return to the
  caller when a handler answers ContinueExecution); `RtlUnwind` → `seh::rtl_unwind`. Tested with hand-assembled
  handlers (nested frames, unwind callbacks, `__except`-style jump to a continuation).
- `SetUnhandledExceptionFilter` stores the filter; `UnhandledExceptionFilter` logs code + address, calls the stored
  filter, otherwise returns EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER (the CRT then exits).
- `OutputDebugStringA` → host log (`[guest tN] ...`, first 2000 lines at Info, then Debug).
- `FormatMessageA`: system codes → short English text or `Error N`; `FROM_STRING` copies without inserts (HYPOTHESIS:
  enough for the game's error dialogs); `ALLOCATE_BUFFER` supported.

## Resources

`s3_runtime::resources` (moved from s3-pe, which re-exports it): `find_resource`, `find_resource_entry` (HRSRC = guest
address of the `IMAGE_RESOURCE_DATA_ENTRY`), `load_string`, `ResId`, `rt`. kernel32 `FindResourceA` / `LoadResource` /
`LockResource` / `SizeofResource` use them; user32 `LoadStringA`/`LoadIconA`/`LoadCursorA` should too.

## Strings and code pages

cp1252 tables both ways (0x80-0x9F mapped like Windows; CP_UTF8 honoured); `MultiByteToWideChar`/`WideCharToMultiByte`
with the usual size-query and `ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER` semantics, default char + used-default flag;
`GetStringTypeA/W` (CT_CTYPE1 via Unicode classes, CT_CTYPE2 approximate); `LCMapStringA/W` (upper/lower, a simple
sort key: 2 bytes per unit, upper-cased with NORM_IGNORECASE); `CompareStringA/W` (ordinal, optional ignore-case —
not linguistic, HYPOTHESIS: fine for the CRT's `strcoll`/`stricmp` uses); `lstr*`.

## Tests

`cargo test -p s3-win32 -j 4` runs `kernel32_tests.rs` (no game bytes): thread + event handoff, wait timeouts and
WaitForMultipleObjects any/all, named objects, mutex recursion, critical-section mutual exclusion with 2 threads
yielding inside the lock, SEH raise + RtlUnwind of nested frames, continuable RaiseException, PulseEvent, Sleep, TLS,
periodic waitable timer, QPC monotonicity, files (case-insensitive read, overlay writes, cwd, find, move/delete
whiteouts, mapped views), save slots in the overlay next to the game dir's `Save\Multi`, CreateThread stack
reserve, version/module/locale/string conversions/memory checks.

## Integration (headless, 2026-11-05)

With kernel32 complete, the CRT start-up and WinMain run through; the next stops were in other modules
(`ole32!CoInitializeEx`, `wsock32!htons/htonl/WSACleanup`, `winmm!mciSendCommandA`, `ole32!CoCreateGuid`). With
temporary local stubs for those (not committed), S3.EXE reaches the **main menu** (800x600x16, 3 threads, the intro
video fails with the game's own "Error during video play" box because MCI was stubbed to fail) and, with injected clicks,
**Game Setup**, and with two more clicks (map OK, setup OK, lobby OK) an **actual in-game map** (Random 384, 640x480x16,
6 guest threads, 8.1 G instructions / 150 s, ~2000 presents, 55 caught C++ exceptions, ~10 k WaitForSingleObject /
7 k SetEvent per 150 s). 44+ GFX files are memory-mapped at startup; menu threads are woken by 500 ms waitable timers.
After the temporary stubs were removed (the owning agents had implemented those functions meanwhile) a plain
headless run reaches the menu again without stopping.

`docs/porting/menu-layout.md`:

```md
# Full-screen menu layouts (menu-fill, 2026-11-07)

User request: the pre-game menus must fill the phone screen (no black bars), cropping and re-arranging as needed
("not everything has to stay"). Related: [display.md](display.md) (display modes, the shared `Viewport`),
[android.md](android.md).

## Problem

S3.EXE draws every menu as a fixed **800x600** (4:3) frame. The test phone (Galaxy Z Fold4 cover screen) is
2316x904 (~2.56:1): `Fit` leaves ~640 px black bars, plain `Fill` keeps only 312 of the 600 rows and cuts buttons
(main menu buttons span y 18..574). So each known screen gets its own **layout**.

## Design (`port/crates/s3-mods/src/menu_layout.rs`)

- A `MenuLayout` = canvas size (game-pixel units) + background + `pieces` (source rect of the frame -> position on
  the canvas, same size) + `neutral` game point + `probes`.
- The canvas is fitted into the window (one uniform scale); the background (plain colour, or a stretched source
  rect) covers the whole window first -> no bars. Plain colours are used on purpose: the game draws the **mouse
  cursor into the frame**, so a tiled / stretched part of the frame repeated the cursor all over the window.
- **Detection** (`detect`): each probe is the expected 4x4 block mean (8-bit RGB, tolerance 14 per channel) at a
  static spot. All but one probe must match (the cursor can cover one). Probes avoid buttons (hover / pressed
  states) and include spots that the screen's popups cover, so a popup over a menu -> no layout -> normal `Fit`
  (never unusable). Only 800x600 frames, only in display modes `NativeWide` (default) and `Fill`.
- **Viewport**: `Viewport::for_frame(mode, pixels, w, h, win_w, win_h)` returns a viewport with
  `layout: Some(..)`; `window_to_game` maps through the pieces (outside every piece -> `neutral`, a spot without
  buttons), `game_to_window` maps a game pixel to its piece (not shown -> far off screen), `bars()` is zero,
  `visible_game_rect` is the whole frame. Touch input therefore needs no change.
- **Rendering**: Android GPU presenter (`present.rs`): `glClearColor` = background colour, then one quad per piece
  (vertex shader `u_uv` sub-rectangle, works with the sharp-bilinear shader). CPU (`s3run` window, previews):
  `render_xrgb` (nearest).
- Presentation only: guest memory is never touched (lockstep MP unaffected).

## Responsive: whole screen when it fits (2026-11-08)

The layouts drop decoration (helmets, logos, version) so the buttons are big on a ~2.56:1 phone. On other
shapes that is not needed. Every layout has a whole-frame variant (`<name>-full`, `menu_layout::FULL_LAYOUTS`:
the 800x600 frame 1:1, the bars filled with the screen's background colour, same detection). For every frame the
viewport picks with the current window size (`menu_layout::choose`): the whole frame when it can be shown at
least `FULL_PREFER` = 0.8 times as big as the re-arranged layout, else the layout. So it follows folding,
split screen and resizing at once.

| Window | Shape | Main menu |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fold4 cover 2316x904 | 2.56:1 | layout (2.69 vs 1.51 px per game px) |
| 20:9 phone 2400x1080 | 2.22:1 | layout |
| 16:9 1920x1080 | 1.78:1 | whole menu (1.80 vs 2.23) |
| 16:10 tablet 2560x1600 | 1.6:1 | whole menu |
| 4:3 tablet 2048x1536 | 1.33:1 | whole menu |
| Fold4 inner 2176x1812 | 1.2:1 | whole menu (VERIFIED on the phone) |

`s3run --layout-preview frame.png out.png WxH` shows the choice for a window size. Tested by
`menu_layout::tests::responsive_choice`.

## Screens (GOG S3.EXE 1.60)

| Layout | Screen | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `main-menu` | main menu | 13 buttons in two columns (7 + 6, original gaps kept), laurel logo right; helmets, Blue Byte logo, version text dropped. Popups ("Campaign: Normal" info, "Internet connection not detected") -> `main-menu+msg-box` (see Popups) |
| `choose-race` | Campaign -> Choose a Race | title + the three race cards side by side |
| `choose-race-mcd` | Mission CD Campaign | band y 60..372 of the painting, title / Egyptians / Romans labels moved into it |
| `choose-race-amazon` | Amazon Campaign | band y 90..402, title / Amazons / Others moved into it |
| `map-picker` | Single Player: Scenario (map popup over Game Setup) | tabs + list, options/preview, Cancel/OK |
| `game-setup` | Game Setup | blocks in three columns |
| `players` | player list / MP waiting room | race icons + map info top, list (first ~9 rows), status + Cancel/OK bottom |
| `lan-game` | Multi-player Game: LAN | lists left, title / status / Back / Join / New in a right column. Popups "Before connecting, a provider has to be selected!", "First select a game" -> `lan-game+msg-box` |
| `load-game` | Load Game | upper 330 rows of the list (~14 entries), buttons right |
| `briefing` | campaign mission briefing | text panel left, map right, tip text + Cancel/OK below |
| `credits` | Credits (text scrolls up over the helmet relief) | middle band y 144..456 of the frame (every line passes through it), 2.9x on the Fold4 cover |
| `statistics` | end-of-game Game Statistics (user report 2026-11-08: was a small 4:3 box with black bars) | title, header and the first 10 player rows (y 0..302), closed by the table's bottom border (y 578..600); 2.8x on the Fold4 cover. Any tap leaves the screen (game behaviour). An 11th row (blue Score bar at `255,310`, `statistics_has_row`) -> `statistics-20` (all 20 rows, 1.7x). Tall windows: `statistics-full` / `statistics-20-full`. The cells are bars (light blue = share of the column's best value), so probes avoid them. Our "Statistics over time" charts are drawn on top: [Statistics over time](#statistics-over-time-end_statsrs) |
| `loading` | 640x480 loading screen before a map (laurel + helmets) | kept whole, sides filled with its beige |

Window bands above / below a canvas (tall windows, e.g. Fold4 inner 2176x1812 with `main-menu-full`) are filled
with the background colour; `MenuLayout::band_tiles` repeats edge strips there (`menu_layout::band_quads`, used by
the CPU renderer and the GLES presenter). The main menu's Greek-key borders repeat every 62 rows, so they now run
along the whole window height (user report 2026-11-08; checked with `--layout-preview` at 2176x1812, 2316x904,
2048x1536).

Not covered (shown as before): any screen not listed, a popup over an unlisted screen. Lists are cut at the
bottom (Load Game, players): long lists need the game's own scrolling. Other main-menu entries: **Exit Game** quits
at once (no confirm dialog in the game); **Online Help** / **Tips & Tricks** call `ShellExecuteExA("open",
"C:\S3\Manual\main.htm" / "C:\S3\Tips\main.htm")`, which our shell32 HLE refuses, so they do nothing (the
menu stays; no popup).

## Popups (menu-pass, 2026-11-08)

User report: with multiplayer not working the game shows an error popup, and then the mobile layout broke: a popup
missed the screen's probes, so the frame fell back to plain `Fit` (small, black bars) until it was closed.

- All main-menu / LAN popups seen so far are one **message box**: the stone dialog at `200,160 400x200` with one OK
  button (`MSG_BOX`): "Internet connection not detected." (Internet, without touching DirectPlay), "Before connecting,
  a provider has to be selected!" (LAN New Game without a connection), "First select a game" (LAN Join Game), the
  "Campaign: Normal" skill text. Identical pixels over every screen (checked with `--layout-probe`).
- `detect` checks the popups **first**: popup probes (stone frame, empty lower text area, not the text or OK) match
  and some screen's probes **outside** the popup rectangle match (`matches_outside`, >= 2 left, no miss with < 4)
  -> `with_popup(screen, popup)` = layout `"<screen>+msg-box"`: the screen's canvas (same scale, nothing jumps) and
  background, only its thin edge strips (<= 32 px wide: the Greek-key borders), and the whole dialog **centred**.
  The cut-around screen pieces looked broken (half buttons, sliced logo) and the buttons under a modal box do
  nothing anyway. Built once per pair and leaked (`&'static` like the static layouts); `by_name` finds it.
- Tall windows: `choose` -> the screen's full variant (`full_variant` of a composite = the screen's), which shows
  the popup in place at full size.
- A popup over an unknown screen (or in game) -> no layout, as before.
- Size: the dialog is 1077x539 window px on the Fold4 cover (2.69x), the OK button 270x60.

Headless `s3run --window`: the published viewport (used by `w`-prefixed touch injects and the mods) now goes through
the last frame (`Viewport::for_frame_split`), so `wtap` hits what `wshot` shows on layout screens (before it mapped
through plain Fit).

## Tools

```sh
# screenshots (local only: game graphics, never commit): scratch/keep/menus/
s3run --headless --game-dir ../game-files/gog-s3-ultimate --data-dir ../scratch/d --max-seconds 9 \
  --inject "1000:move 165 355;1200:click 165 355;4000:shot ../scratch/keep/menus/load.png"
s3run --layout-preview frame.png out.png 2316x904 [layout-name]   # render through the detected (or named) layout
s3run --layout-probe frame.png 390,40 400,300                       # print pr(..) lines for new probes
```

Add a screen: take a shot, measure rectangles (any image viewer), add a `MenuLayout` + push it to `LAYOUTS`, pick
4-6 probes (static, no buttons, at least one under the screen's popups), check every shot in
`scratch/keep/menus` with `--layout-preview` (it prints the detected layout), run
`cargo test -p s3-mods --lib menu_layout`.

## Verified

- 2026-11-08 (menu-pass) headless `wshot` at 2316x904 and 2176x1812: Internet error popup big and centred (cover) /
  in place over the whole menu (inner); `wtap` on OK closes it at both sizes; LAN popups; Credits band; all 57 local
  shots (scratch/keep/menus, scratch/menu-pass/s) detect the expected layout at both sizes.

- 2026-11-07 desktop previews of all screens at 2316x904; all 32 shots detect the right layout, popup shots -> Fit.
- 2026-11-07 phone (Fold4 cover, 2316x904): main menu full screen; tap on the moved "Load Game" (window 884,235 ->
  game 166,355) opened Load Game, shown with its layout. Tutorial loading screen (`loading`) full screen.

## Statistics over time (`end_stats.rs`, 2026-11-08)

User request: "make the scoreboard like Settlers United made it". SU adds a "View Extended Game Stats" button to
the end-of-game statistics that opens charts per category against game time ([settlers-united](../settlers-united/README.md)).
Our own version (no SU code or assets):

- Mod `end_stats::EndStatsMod` samples the game's per-player statistics records (`0x7acfac + id*0x44`, see
  [game-state-ui.md](../reverse-engineering/game-state-ui.md) section 5) every 10 s of game time (game clock
  `0x7dfd48`), at most 720 samples (then every second one dropped, interval doubled). In-game score = the game's
  formula, gold halved like the screen. When the statistics screen shows, it takes the final values (the game's
  stored score + ranks). Read only; nothing is saved. A history starts with each game / loaded save in the session.
- On the `statistics*` layouts: a gold button "Statistics over time" bottom right (+ hint "Tap anywhere else to
  continue"). Tap -> full-window sheet: tabs Score / Settlers / Buildings / Food / Mines / Gold / Manna /
  Soldiers / Battles, a line per player (colour by rank), axes Count / Game time, legend = the game's own player
  rows (rank, team, name copied from the frame with `frame_inset`) + final value. Close button or Back closes it.
  While it is open no touch reaches the game (its click would leave the screen). Desktop mouse clicks go to the
  game directly (button is touch-only; `wtap` in headless runs).
- Only with a layout display mode (Native wide / Fill: the screen must be detected).

## Stone background (2026-11-08)

The window area around the stone screens' pieces (LAN, Load Game, Scenario setup / players / map picker, race
choice, briefing, their `-full` variants) is no longer a flat grey: `Background::Stone` draws our own generated
stone texture (`s3-mods/src/stone.rs`: tileable 256x256 value noise + diagonal cracks rising to the right, colours
sampled from the game's stone screens; no game asset). One texel per game pixel, aligned to the canvas, so its grain
matches the pieces. CPU renderer: `render_xrgb`; GLES: `Gles::draw_stone` (`GL_REPEAT` texture). Not a tile of the
frame: clean stone patches there are only ~40 px (panels, vines).

## Finger scrolling of lists (2026-11-08)

`s3-mods/src/menu_scroll.rs`: a vertical one-finger drag starting on a known list (`LISTS`: list rect, arrow points,
row height in 800x600 game pixels; now the map picker) is turned into clicks on the list's scroll arrows, one per
row of finger movement. Taps still select.

# Product vision: a real mobile Settlers 3 (not just an emulator)

Set by the user on 2026-11-06. Running S3.EXE is the foundation, not the goal.

## Requirements (user)

1. **Easy start:** the user gives the needed game files (folder or zip) and plays. No adb, no manual copying.
2. **Online play like Settlers United:** lobby, friends, internet matches.
3. **Easy mobile UI like JSettlers:** large touch targets, gestures, readable on a phone.
4. **Patch the game for touch instead of simulating desktop input.** Example: right-click must not need a long press and
   a wait. Rendering and logic may be patched so fingers work naturally. ESC/RMB buttons are a stopgap.

## Technical basis we already have

We own the CPU interpreter and every OS API, so we can do everything Settlers United's `s3.dll` does, plus more,
without shipping a modified exe:

- **Hooks:** run host code when EIP reaches an address (function entry or call site). Read and write game memory, and call
  game functions. Patches are applied in memory at load time, keyed by the S3.EXE sha256 (GOG `00a925cf…`).
- **Render layer:** we compose every presented frame ourselves (the cursor already works this way). A native mobile HUD
  can be drawn on top or replace parts of the original UI. The game frame can be cropped and scaled (e.g. hide the original
  left panel, zoom the map).
- **Network:** DirectPlay is our HLE, so multiplayer sessions can run over our own transport.

## Workstreams (proposed)

| # | Workstream | What | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| W1 | Mod/hook framework | `s3-mods` crate: address hooks, memory views of game structs, calling game functions, per-exe-hash patch sets, debug overlay | CPU hook point (cheap EIP check at block entry) |
| W2 | Game-state RE | Selection list, unit/building types, camera/viewport, cursor mode (build placement, attack…), panel/menu state, player resources, command functions (move, build, destroy, priority) | REA/Ghidra on S3.EXE + runtime memory inspection |
| W3 | Touch input v2 | **Context-aware tap:** units selected + tap on ground = move (right-click semantics); tap on own unit = select; in build mode tap = place, second tap/✕ = cancel. Two-finger pan, pinch = zoom (scaled frame), long-press-drag = box select, double tap = select all of a type | W1 + W2 |
| W4 | Mobile HUD | Native, large-button UI rendered by us: build menu as a bottom sheet with categories, selected-unit card, resource/stats panels, game menu (save/load/quit) — calling game functions instead of clicking the original panel. Option to hide the original left panel and use the full screen for the map | W1 + W2 |
| W5 | Online multiplayer | DirectPlay 6 HLE over our own relay/lobby server (Rust, WebSocket/QUIC); rooms, invites. S3 MP is lockstep, so **determinism across devices** is needed: x87 results must be bit-identical on arm64 and x86_64. That means our own deterministic transcendental functions (no host libm), identical rounding, and desync detection | Server hosting; decision on crossplay |
| W6 | Launcher (Tauri 2 + Svelte 5) | Folder/zip picker via SAF, validate by hash, import into app storage, settings, i18n, account/lobby UI | — |
| W7 | Real-device tuning | arm64 phone performance, battery, thermal, interpreter speedups | a phone |

## Decisions (user, 2026-11-06)

- **Online:** our own network first (mobile + our desktop app, own lobby/relay). Crossplay with Windows players
  (Settlers United / aLobby, real DirectPlay) comes later. Design the protocol layer so PC crossplay can be added.
- **UI:** play on the original panel is the preferred direction. Deliver **two selectable alternatives** so the user can compare:
  - **A "Classic Touch"**: the original panel and game UI, patched for touch. Context-aware taps (no long-press right-click),
    larger hit areas, gestures, the panel scaled for readability.
  - **B "Mobile HUD"**: a native large-button HUD (JSettlers-like) on top of or instead of the original panel.
  Both modes can be switched in settings and are shown side by side with screenshots: [ui-modes.md](ui-modes.md).
- Multi-agent workflows approved for W1-W5.

## Workstream status (2026-11-06, after the mobile UX + online workflow)

| # | Status | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| W1 Mod/hook framework | **done**: CPU hook exit, `s3-mods` (hooks, guest calls, struct views, patch sets by sha256, overlay, gestures, settings), touch inject in `s3run`; overhead < 1 % | [mods.md](mods.md) |
| W2 Game-state RE | **done for UX needs**: units/buildings/tiles/selection/commands, camera, layouts, panel pages, build list, strings. Open: panel goods counters, building cost tables, some good/settler ids (HYPOTHESIS), simulation RNG location | [game-state-units.md](../reverse-engineering/game-state-units.md), [game-state-ui.md](../reverse-engineering/game-state-ui.md) |

`docs/porting/mods.md`:

```md
# Mod / hook framework (W1, `s3-mods`)

Status: implemented 2026-11-06 (agent `mods-w1`). Code: `port/crates/s3-mods`, hook point in `s3-cpu`, extension
points in `s3-runtime/src/ext.rs`, wiring in `s3-engine`. Vision and workstreams: [mobile-vision.md](mobile-vision.md).

The framework lets host code change the running game without shipping a modified exe: hooks at guest addresses,
typed views of game memory, calls into game functions, per-exe patch sets, an overlay drawn on every frame, and a
touch pipeline (gesture recognizer -> mods -> fallback touch->mouse) that runs before the game sees input.

## Layers

```
frontend (s3run / Android)  --HostEvent::Pointer{id,phase,x,y,wx,wy}-->  Machine::run_slice
   -> MachineExt::event_filter (s3-mods)
        captured pointer? -> that mod only
        else GestureRecognizer -> TouchEvents -> Mod::observe (all) -> Mod::on_touch (top first)
              unconsumed -> fallback::TouchMouse -> mouse HostEvents -> m.input (USER32 / DirectInput)
guest CPU  --EIP hits hooked addr-->  CpuExit::Hook(eip) -> Machine::dispatch_hook -> hooks::dispatch (closures)
guest Flip/Blt -> Machine::present -> window layer (Mod::draw_window records a draw list -> SceneSlot -> frontend)
                -> [frame overlay (Mod::draw on a copy), only if a mod wants_draw_frame] -> cursor compose -> Host::present
service "s3mods" (each run_slice): long-press timing, delayed mouse-ups, Mod::tick, overlay-only refresh
```

## CPU hook point (`s3-cpu`)

- `HookAddrs` (= `HashSet<u32>`) installed per CPU with `Cpu::set_hooks(Option<Arc<HookAddrs>>)` (clears the
  decode cache). `Machine::set_hook_addrs` pushes one set to every thread, and `create_thread` gives it to new threads.
- `decode_block` ends a block **before** any hooked address and flags blocks that start at one (`Block::hooked`), so a
  hook can sit anywhere (function entry, call site, mid-function), not only at block starts.
- At block entry: `if blk.hooked { exit CpuExit::Hook(eip) unless hook_skip == eip }`. One byte test per executed
  block. After a `Continue` hook the runtime calls `Cpu::skip_hook_once(eip)` so the original code runs once.
- Hooks on thunk addresses are not supported (use the thunk registry instead).

## Runtime extension points (`s3-runtime/src/ext.rs`)

`Machine::ext: MachineExt` holds plain function pointers (state lives in `m.state::<T>()`):
`hook_dispatch(m, eip) -> HookFlow {Continue, Redirected}`, `event_filter(m, HostEvent, &mut Vec<HostEvent>)`,
`overlay_wanted(m) -> bool` (cheap, per present), `overlay_compose(m, &mut FrameBuffer) -> bool` (frame-space
overlay) and `window_overlay(m, &FrameBuffer)` (window layer, 2026-11-08 overlay-window: called with the raw guest
frame on every present and refresh; the frame is not copied or changed).
`Machine::refresh_overlay()` re-runs the window layer for the last guest frame (when the game is idle) and re-presents
the frame only for frame-space overlays; `Machine::last_frame_size()`. `Stats::hooks` counts dispatched hooks.
Host event: `HostEvent::Pointer { id, phase: PointerPhase::{Down,Move,Up,Cancel}, x, y, wx, wy }`: game pixels
(`x`, `y`) and window pixels (`wx`, `wy`; negative = unknown, then the mods map the game point through the viewport);
`InputState` ignores it (game consumers never see raw touch).

## Hooks (`s3_mods::hooks`)

```rust
s3_mods::add_hook(m, 0x0060_d9e0, "my-mod", |c| {        // c: HookCtx { m, eip }
    let this = c.reg(s3_cpu::ECX); let a0 = c.arg(0);       // args at a function entry: [esp+4+4i]
    c.on_return(|p| { let v = p.eax; p.set_eax(v + 1); });   // post-call callback (function entry only)
    HookFlow::Continue                                      // or c.return_from_function(eax, stdcall_args) / c.jump(a)
});
s3_mods::hooks::commit(m);   // push the address set to the CPUs (install/patch sets do this for you)
```

- Several hooks per address run in registration order; the first `Redirected` ends the chain.
- `return_from_function(eax, n)`: skip the original function (pop return address + `n` dwords, EAX = value).
- `on_return`: replaces `[esp]` with the trampoline thunk `s3mods.dll!post_call_return` and keeps a per-thread LIFO of
  `(entry_esp, real return)`. On return the newest frame with `entry_esp < esp` is ours; newer frames were abandoned by
  exception unwinding and are dropped. Caveat: code that reads its own return address would see the trampoline
  (HYPOTHESIS: MSVC6 code in S3.EXE does not do that).
- Hooks fire again for guest calls made from inside the hook (recursion: guard with a flag, see tests).
- `remove_hooks(m, name)`, `remove_hooks_all`, `hook_stats(m)` (address, name, hits), `hook_time_ns(m)`.

## Calling game functions (`s3_mods::call`)

`call_stdcall`, `call_cdecl`, `call_thiscall(m, f, this, args)`, `call_fastcall`, `call_virtual(m, this, index, args)`.
All use `Machine::call_guest` (runs on the current thread, restores every register incl. ESP); thiscall/fastcall also
restore ECX/EDX. Call from hooks, or queue with `s3_mods::defer(m, |m| ...)`: deferred work runs at the next **safe
point** hook on the guest main thread (`add_safe_point(m, addr)`; the GOG set registers two, below). Calling from
input/overlay callbacks runs on whatever thread is current: avoid.

## Typed memory views (`s3_mods::view`)

`GuestPtr<T>` (`get/set/index`) for `u8/i8/u16/i16/u32/i32/f32`, and

```rust
s3_mods::guest_struct! { pub struct Player { 0x00 => id / set_id: u32, 0x24 => wood / set_wood: u16 } }
let p = Player::at(addr); let w = p.wood(&m.mem); p.set_wood(&mut m.mem, w + 10);
```

## Patch sets (`s3_mods::patchset`)

`install` hashes S3.EXE (own dependency-free SHA-256, `sha256.rs`) and applies the patch set whose `exe_sha256`
matches; any other exe runs **unpatched** with a warning log (`mods: unknown S3.EXE (sha256 …); game patches
disabled`). Input/overlay/settings stay active for every exe. `patch_bytes(m, addr, expect, new)` writes bytes only if
the original bytes match, then invalidates decoded code. `S3_MODS=0` or settings `patches_enabled: false` disable sets.

| Set | Exe | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gog-base` | GOG `00a925cfdcfc3349b5d0f3b8a4c312f01b813e363b4464f6f3d6de17804d950b` | safe points at `0x60d9e0` ("message waiting?" test in Run `0x404860`) and `0x60d740` (GetMessage/Dispatch step), see [static-startup.md](../reverse-engineering/static-startup.md) §3 |

Measured (2026-11-06, desktop): the two safe points were hit 39-123 times in a 40-45 s run (menu + ~25 s in game),
because the main thread mostly sleeps in `GetMessageA` in game. So deferred work can wait up to a few seconds in game.
Next (W2): find a safe point that runs every frame or tick (for example the logic thread's 64 ms tick) on a thread
that may call the game functions we need.
HYPOTHESIS: both addresses run only on the main thread (deferred work also checks the main thread id).

W2/W3/W4 add their hooks to `gog_base` (or new sets) in `patchset.rs`. UI mode A registers its hooks
(`0x524fa0` HandleInput, `0x42c820` gfx ctor) and its mod from `ui_classic::install(m, gog)` in `install`, see
[ui-classic.md](ui-classic.md). UI mode B registers its hooks (`0x4c6d70` layout, `0x54bec0` landscape buffer,
`0x4b4d00` panel render, `0x4ff170` ScreenToMap, `0x524fa0` HandleInput, `0x5faaa0` text lookup) and its mod from
`ui_hud::install(m, gog)`, see [ui-hud.md](ui-hud.md). Several hooks on one address (both modes use `0x524fa0`) chain.

## Window layer (`s3_mods::layer`, 2026-11-08 overlay-window)

All mod UI (Mobile HUD, touch feedback, FPS counter, Classic floating buttons / bubble / chip, debug overlay) is drawn
into a **window-resolution layer**, not into the game frame. Before, it was drawn into the guest frame and scaled with
it, so zoom (= the game's render size) changed its size and sharpness, and below ~280 px the HUD lost its icons.

- `Mod::draw_window(m, l: &mut Layer, frame: &FrameBuffer)` (when `wants_draw()`): window pixels; `frame` is the raw
  guest frame (read-only: icon sampling, the Classic magnifier). `s3_mods::draw_viewport(m)` = the `Viewport` of this
  frame (`vp.game_to_window(gx, gy)` for map-anchored effects, `vp.dst_rect_clipped()` = window part that shows the
  game, `vp.scale()` = window px per game px of the map). `l.ui()` = window height / 600: sizes in "px of a 600 px
  high frame" times `ui()` look like before, at every zoom level.
- `Layer` API (same as the old `Canvas`): `fill_rect`, `stroke_rect`, `fill_rounded_rect`, `stroke_rounded_rect`,
  `fill_circle`, `ellipse_ring`/`ring`, `blit`/`blit_scaled(&ImageRef = Arc<Image>, ...)`, `blit_image(Image, ...)`
  (one-off, pixels hashed), `blit_map` (the game's sheared minimap shape), `line`, `text(x, y, px, Weight, Rgba, str)
  -> width`, `text_centered`, `text_box` (text on a rounded box), `set_clip`/`reset_clip`; `overlay::measure_text`.
  **Text API for other mods** (e.g. redrawing the game's own messages in this layer): `text` / `text_centered` /
  `text_box` with `measure_text`, sizes in window px (`12.0 * l.ui()` etc.).
- Recording only: each call appends a command with its clipped bounds and an FNV hash (`DrawList`). After all mods drew,
  the list is compared with the last one (hash + length + panel split + frame size); only a changed list is
  published (`SceneSlot::publish`, frontend registered it with `s3_mods::set_layer_sink`). Images are identified by
  their `Arc` pointer (the previous list keeps a reference, so an address is never reused while compared).
- Frontend: `LayerRaster::update(&list)` -> the changed rectangle: union of the bounds of commands that appeared or
  disappeared (multiset of hashes; whole union if only the order changed); it is cleared and every command that
  touches it is redrawn in order (premultiplied RGBA8). Android uploads only those rows as a second texture and
  blends it (`GL_ONE, GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA`); s3run blends on the CPU over the row spans that have content
  (`blend_onto_xrgb`); the Android CPU fallback samples it into its letterbox buffer (`blend_onto_rgb565_scaled`).
- `Mod::draw(m, &mut Canvas)` + `wants_draw_frame()` still exist for frame-space drawing (game pixels, costs a frame
  copy); no shipped mod uses it. `Canvas` and the layer raster share one rasterizer (`layer::Surf`).
- Touch hit tests of window UI use `s3_mods::touch_window_pos(m, &ev)`: the window position of the pointer behind the
  event (raw events: that pointer; taps / long press: the last pointer; two-finger gestures: centroid).
- Text: fontdue with the bundled Liberation Sans (Regular/Bold, SIL OFL 1.1, from `s3-win32/assets/fonts`), glyphs
  cached (shared by the engine thread for measuring and the render thread for rasterizing).
Order on screen: guest frame (incl. the game's mouse cursor) -> window layer.

## Mods and touch input

```rust
pub trait Mod: Send {
    fn name(&self) -> &str;
    fn observe(&mut self, m, ev: &TouchEvent) {}                     // sees everything, cannot consume
    fn on_touch(&mut self, m, ev: &TouchEvent) -> ModEvent { Pass }   // Consumed | Pass
    fn wants_draw(&self) -> bool { false }  fn draw_window(&mut self, m, l: &mut Layer, frame: &FrameBuffer) {}
    fn wants_draw_frame(&self) -> bool { false }  fn draw(&mut self, m, c: &mut Canvas) {}   // game-pixel overlay
    fn needs_redraw(&self) -> bool { false } fn tick(&mut self, m, now_ms: u64) {}
    fn on_key(&mut self, m, vk: u32, down: bool) -> ModEvent { Pass } // host keys, top first (2026-11-05)
}
s3_mods::add_mod(m, Box::new(MyHud::default()));   // later mods are on top (get events first)
```

Mods are stored in `ModsState` and taken out while called, so a mod may call the mods API and guest code.
Key events (`HostEvent::Key`, Windows VK; Android Back = `VK_ESCAPE`) go through the input filter to `Mod::on_key`
(top first); a `Consumed` key never reaches the game (Mobile HUD: Back closes the full-screen map / sheets). Keys a
mod pushes itself with `m.input.push` do not pass the filter.
Consuming a raw `Down` **captures** the pointer: its Move/Up go only to that mod and the recognizer forgets it (HUD buttons).

### Gesture recognizer (`gesture.rs`, pure Rust, unit tested)

Frontends deliver raw pointer events only; desktop inject and Android share this code. Events (game pixels, f32):
raw `Down/Move/Up/Cancel`; `Tap` (one finger, <= `tap_max_ms` 500, moved <= `tap_slop` 8 px); `DoubleTap` (extra
event after the second Tap within 300 ms / 24 px, so taps never wait); `LongPress` (held >= 500 ms without moving, fired
by the service tick); `Pan {phase Begin/Update/End, fingers 1|2, x, y, dx, dy (since last), start, after_long_press}`;
`Pinch {phase, cx, cy, scale}` (with a two-finger Pan); `TwoFingerTap`, `ThreeFingerTap`. A second finger landing
on a running one-finger pan or long press ends that gesture.

### Fallback touch->mouse (`fallback.rs`)

**W3 (2026-11-05):** for the GOG exe the `touch-context` mod ([touch.md](touch.md)) sits above the fallback and
handles in-game gestures (and all long presses); the fallback only sees what it passes (menus, RMB-armed taps,
three-finger taps). Android now sends raw pointers too (old `TouchMapper` removed).
Unconsumed gestures map like the former Android mapper: Tap = left click (button-up 60 ms later), LongPress / TwoFingerTap = right click (`long_press_right_click`
setting), ThreeFingerTap = keyboard request (`take_keyboard_request`), one-finger Pan = left drag, or right drag on the
in-game map (x >= 170, not 800x600), mirrored and halved = "grab" scrolling. `set_right_next(m, true)` = RMB button.
Android sends `HostEvent::Pointer` since 2026-11-05 (`s3-frontend/src/touch.rs`, RMB/keyboard flags via
`Shared::keyboard_req` <-> `s3_mods::take_keyboard_request`; the RMB flags went with the letterbox buttons 2026-11-07).

## Settings (`settings.rs`)

`<data_dir>/mods-settings.json`, loaded at install, saved atomically with `s3_mods::set_settings(m, s)`; missing fields
use defaults, a broken file falls back to defaults with a warning.
`{ version, ui_mode: "ClassicTouch"|"MobileHud", patches_enabled, debug_overlay, hud_scale,
touch: { long_press_ms, tap_max_ms, tap_slop, double_tap_ms, double_tap_slop, long_press_right_click, context } }`
(`context` = W3 context-aware touch, default on, see [touch.md](touch.md)).
`display: { mode, filter, fps_counter, refresh_hz }` = display mode / scaling filter / FPS counter, see
[display.md](display.md) (`s3_mods::display`: the shared screen<->game `Viewport`, `visible_game_rect(m)` for
anchoring overlay UI in Fill mode; `s3_mods::fps`: the FPS counter mod).
`res: { enabled, zoom_level }` = custom game resolution / zoom level, see [resolution-zoom.md](resolution-zoom.md)
(`s3_mods::res`: GOG patch + switch, `s3_mods::zoom`: levels, pinch, `zoom_in/zoom_out/set_level/label` for menus).
`S3_MODS_DEBUG=1` turns on the built-in debug overlay (finger circles + last gesture label).

## Desktop testing (`s3run --inject` touch commands)

Screen coordinates = game pixels (800x600 menus, 640x480 in game): `tap x y`, `dtap x y`, `tap2 x y`, `tap3 x y`,
`drag x1 y1 x2 y2 [ms=300]` (moves every 16 ms), `drag2 ...` (two fingers 60 px apart), `fling ... [ms=120]`,
`longpress x y [ms=800]`, `lpdrag x1 y1 x2 y2 [hold=700] [ms=400]`, `pinch cx cy scale [ms=300]`
(fingers 80 px apart -> 80*scale). Code: `s3-desktop/src/touch_inject.rs`. Example (menu -> in game by taps, map drag, build menu tap):

```sh
I="1200:tap 165 235;3200:tap 630 467;5200:tap 730 567;7200:tap 730 567;30000:shot a.png;31000:drag 400 300 300 250 400;33000:shot c.png;34000:tap 25 167;36000:shot e.png"
S3_MODS_DEBUG=1 ./target/release/s3run --headless --game-dir ../game-files/gog-s3-ultimate --data-dir ../scratch/x --max-seconds 40 --inject "$I"
```

Verified 2026-11-06: the game reached the in-game view by taps only. The drag scrolled the map with the finger, the tap
opened the build menu, and the debug overlay showed the finger and the "Pan1 Update" / "Pan2" labels.
Screenshots were in `scratch/mods-w1/` (local only).

## Performance

- CPU microbenchmark `bench_mips` (small blocks, worst case for a per-block check), with vs without the `blk.hooked`
  test (copy of s3-cpu without it), 3 interleaved runs: 189.4/189.0/188.7 vs 185.5/183.4/180.8 MIPS: no measurable
  cost (the difference is code-layout noise).
- In game (`S3_SAMPLE=1`, sum of guest M instr/s over all threads, samples >= 25 s). gog-base hooks on vs `S3_MODS=0`,
  two runs **in parallel** so host noise is shared: 97.2 vs 97.0 and 95.0 vs 94.9 M/s. The overhead is within noise, < 1%
  (target < 2%). Sequential runs differed by up to 10% between runs because of other jobs on the host; do not compare
  them.
- Hook callbacks: ~40-120 dispatches per run in total. The cost is dominated by what a hook does (a `HashMap` lookup
  plus a closure clone per hit).

## Tests

`cargo test -p s3-mods` (19 + doctest): SHA-256 vectors, settings round trip/partial/broken files, gestures (tap,
double tap, long press + drag, slop, pinch, 2/3-finger taps, cancel), fallback mapping, overlay primitives/text/blit,
guest struct views, and machine-level tests on hand-assembled code: skip a stdcall function, post-call trampoline
changing EAX, mid-block hook, guest calls (stdcall/cdecl/thiscall/virtual) from a hook incl. re-entry, deferred work at a
safe point, touch pipeline (fallback click, pointer capture by a mod, overlay on present, key passthrough).
`s3-cpu`: `hook_exits_mid_block_and_skip_once`. `s3-desktop`: `inject_touch_parsing`.

`docs/porting/multicore.md`:

```md
# Multi-core execution (perf-mt)

Status 2026-11-07 (perf-mt): design + RE + measurements done; option A (true parallel guest execution of the draw
thread) is implemented as an **experimental prototype behind `S3_MT=1` (default off)**. It is correct (unit test,
lockstep MP runs with MT peers identical, default mode bit-identical) but gives **no reliable fps gain** on the dev
PC; the reasons and the way forward are below. Related: [architecture.md](architecture.md) (single-threaded
`Machine`), [performance.md](performance.md), [determinism.md](determinism.md), [multiplayer.md](multiplayer.md).

## Starting point (measured)

All guest threads are cooperative green threads inside one `Machine` on one host thread. In game (HUD, 2316x904
window, zoom 10 = 1944x760, `S3_FPS_CAP=0`, Windows ARM64 dev PC, throttling off, commit `e8042b2`, random map):

| What | Per second | Per frame (348 fps) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| draw thread `CDrawThread` (t4) guest instructions | ~2 800 M ("guest equivalent", fast paths included) | ~8 M |
| logic thread `CLogicThread` (t5) | ~780 M | |
| time in `Cpu::run` (all threads) | 707 ms | 2.0 ms (draw ~1.56, logic ~0.44) |
| host time in HLE handlers (`S3_HOST_PROF=1`) | ~250 ms | ~0.78 ms |
| - overlay copy + HUD compose (`apply_overlay_to`) | | 0.48 ms |
| - cursor + `Host::present` | | 0.06 ms |
| - 4 plain `Blt`s landscape ring buffer -> back buffer | | 0.20 ms |
| - primary surface -> `FrameBuffer` | | 0.05 ms |
| everything else (services, waits, critical sections, hooks) | ~60 ms | ~0.15 ms |

So the draw thread's own path (its guest code + the HLE work in its thunks) is ~2.3 ms of the ~2.9 ms frame; the
logic thread is ~0.45 ms (15 %). That bounds what moving the draw thread to its own core can give: **at most ~+18 %**
(frame = max(draw path, logic) instead of their sum), before any synchronisation cost.

## How the game synchronises draw and logic (RE, VERIFIED with `S3_TRACE=thunks` / `S3_TIMELINE`)

The render snapshot (`[logic+0x3d0]`, 0xc7720 bytes, see [resolution-zoom.md](resolution-zoom.md)) is
**triple-buffered** (three buffers rotate, e.g. `0x1a08f920`, `0x1ab07660`, `0x1a980000` in one run):

- Logic thread: the tick loop (`0x53e540..0x53e6f5`) calls the snapshot fill `0x51f110` up to five times per
  pass (between the simulation sub-steps `0x4e7810`, `0x4e05e0`, `0x4e9670` and after the AI). The fill first asks
  `0x51f0b0` whether the draw thread wants a new snapshot (vtable call on `[logic+0x3d8]`, a waitable); only then it
  fills its private buffer `[logic+0x3d0]` (allocated lazily with `new(0xc7720)`) and publishes it in `0x51f0e0`:
  `[logic+0x3d0] = InterlockedExchange([logic+0x3cc] /*shared slot*/, [logic+0x3d0])`, then
  `SetEvent([logic+0x3d4])` ("snapshot ready", event handle 0x45c in our runs). The shared slot lives on the main
  thread's stack (`0x700ffeb0`: the app object is a WinMain local).
- Logic idle wait: `WaitForMultipleObjects(2, [timer 64 ms, "want next" event], FALSE, t)` at `0x4631e1` (generic
  waitable-bag loop `0x463100`).
- Draw thread (`0x42c710`, one frame): `0x42c780` waits for "snapshot ready" (`WaitForSingleObject(0x45c, 500)`
  from `0x60c090`), takes the newest snapshot with `[draw+0x5c] = InterlockedExchange([draw+0x58], [draw+0x5c])`,
  signals "want next" (`SetEvent(0x458)` via `0x42cf80`), renders `0x4b26c0(snap)` and presents
  (`WaitForVerticalBlank`, `Blt`/`BltFast` to the primary). Paused branch (`[draw+0x68]`): exchange, `SetEvent`,
  `Sleep(60)`.
- Timeline of one frame (MT run, µs): `t4 WaitForVerticalBlank 42`, `t4 BltFast(primary) 795`,
  `t4 WaitForSingleObject -> 0 898`, `t4 InterlockedExchange 985`, `t4 SetEvent 1007`, `t5 WaitForMultipleObjects
  -> 1 1072`, `t4 BltFast x2 1371/1401` (landscape), `t5 InterlockedExchange 1692`, `t5 SetEvent 1715`, `t5
  WaitForMultipleObjects BLOCK 1892`, `t4 WaitForVerticalBlank 3298`.

So the game is already a **two-stage pipeline**: the logic thread fills snapshot N+1 while the draw thread renders
snapshot N, and both handovers are HLE calls (`InterlockedExchange` + auto-reset events), i.e. synchronisation
points we control.

## Options

### A. Draw thread on its own host thread (true parallel guest execution) - prototype, see below

The presenting guest thread runs its `Cpu` on a second host thread; the main host thread keeps the cooperative
scheduler for all other threads. Guest memory is shared; everything else in `Machine` is guarded by one big HLE
lock, released only while a CPU executes guest code. Expected gain: up to ~+18 % (Amdahl, above); effort: medium
(done). Risks: guest data races are those the game has on a multi-core PC; handovers are HLE calls under the lock
(mutex = acquire/release, so x86-TSO vs arm64 ordering does not matter there); `lock inc/dec` (6 sites, all on the
CRT locale counter `[0x7eaab4]`, `0x627f24..0x62c164`) run non-atomically in the interpreter (a lost update only
matters for a later `setlocale`, startup only); mod hooks on the draw thread (resolution switch `0x4c7490`,
`0x4b4d00`, `0x4b366a`, `0x4b2b34`) race with the logic thread as they already do at quantum boundaries.

### B. Pipeline host-side work (guest scheduling unchanged)

Move overlay compose + cursor + `Host::present` (0.54 ms/frame) out of the draw thread's present thunk onto a
presenter host thread. Gain: up to ~0.55 of ~2.9 ms (+15-20 %) **in the default single-thread mode too**, no
determinism risk (frames are output only). Obstacle: the overlay (`overlay_compose(&mut Machine, ..)`, every HUD /
Classic widget) reads game state through `Machine` while drawing, so the overlay must first be split into "record
a display list under the machine" (cheap) and "rasterise the list" (the 0.48 ms) - `s3_mods::overlay::Canvas` has
12 drawing calls plus 3 direct pixel accesses (`ui_classic.rs` magnifier read, `ui_hud.rs` icon sampling read,
`ui_hud_minimap.rs` pixel writes). The host also needs a `Send` present sink (desktop: the `Shared` frame slot;
Android: the GL presenter's slot). Medium-large effort in s3-mods (owned by the UI agents).
**Done 2026-11-08 (overlay-window)** for the overlay part: mods record a display list in window pixels
(`s3_mods::layer`), the frontend rasterizes only changed rectangles (Android: render thread, 2nd texture). The frame
copy + compose left the engine thread (see [mods.md](mods.md) "Window layer", measurements in
[performance.md](performance.md)); the cursor compose + `Host::present` copy are still on it.

### C. Others

- C1: deferred present in the MT mode (done, part of the prototype): the draw worker only queues the frame; the main
  host thread composes it. Moves the work off the draw thread but the main thread then holds the big lock while
  composing, so the draw thread waits for the lock instead (measured below). Needs B's display list to pay off.
- C2: split the 4 landscape blits (0.2 ms) over helper threads: identical bytes, deterministic, <= ~5 %.
- C3: audio mixing on its own thread: the mixer service is ~0.5 % of the time.
- C4: arm64 JIT (other agent): orthogonal; makes the guest part smaller, so the host part (B) matters more.

## Determinism argument

Lockstep MP needs every peer's **simulation** (logic-thread state: settlers, buildings, piles, economy, RNG
`gd+0x2d2dc`, world tiles) to be a function of the game setup and the network command stream only.

1. The normal (non-`s3det`) mode already interleaves threads by host timing (wall-clock `run_for_ms` slices, host-time
   waits/timers, the frame limiter), and two-peer runs are identical: the simulation does not depend on the draw
   thread's progress. MT makes the interleaving finer (true concurrency); it only adds a new kind of dependency if
   the logic thread reads memory the draw thread writes, or if HLE state the draw thread changes feeds the
   simulation other than through commands.
2. What the draw thread writes (write-set trace, below): its stack/TEB, render-side heap blocks, a redraw-flag array
   and blitter function pointers in `.data`, the hit-list double-buffer index, the shared snapshot slot (through
   `InterlockedExchange`). **Nothing in the game-data block `gd`** (simulation).
3. The one draw -> logic data path is the on-screen hit list (`[0x7dfd64]` = buffer index flipped by the renderer
   at `0x4b3f5e`, list at `0x7ade0a`, read by the click code `0x533b3a..`): clicks become player commands, which
   lockstep executes at agreed ticks on every peer - exactly as with the original game on two PCs.
4. `s3det` never enables MT (only `s3run` does, on `S3_MT=1`), so the deterministic single-thread scheduler stays the
   reference; with MT off the scheduler code path is the old one (checked: identical s3det hashes and instruction
   counts).

Conditions for the parallel mode: (a) the draw thread never writes simulation memory, (b) logic reads of render-side
memory do not feed simulation state, (c) HLE state the draw thread changes reaches the simulation only via the
command queue. (a) is checked by the write trace, (a)-(c) end to end by MP runs with MT peers against default peers.

## Prototype (`S3_MT=1`, s3run only)

Code: `port/crates/s3-runtime/src/mt.rs` (+ hooks in `machine.rs`), `s3_mem::GuestMemory::alias_view`, s3run
`main.rs` (`S3_MT=1` calls `Machine::enable_mt`).

- **Who goes to the worker**: the first non-main guest thread that presents 30 frames in a row (`mt_note_present`;
  in a game the menu draw thread and later `CDrawThread`; one worker at a time, a new one after the thread exits).
  Its `Cpu` is moved to the worker (a placeholder with mirrored counters stays in `Machine::threads`,
  `Thread::offloaded`).
- **Big lock** (`BigLock`): held by the main host thread all the time (frontend code included) except (1) while it
  runs guest code of a *runnable* top-level thread (`run_cpu_unlocked`: the CPU is moved out of the thread table,
  `Thread::running_unlocked`, executed on a second alias view, then moved back) and (2) while idling
  (`Machine::idle`, used by `Engine::run_for_ms` and `call_guest` waits). The worker takes it for every thunk, hook,
  fault and every 16th budget exit (budget exits need no HLE state: dropping the lock for each of them cost ~40
  lock trips per frame).
- **Wakeups** (`Wake`): an epoch counter bumped by every non-blocking thunk dispatch; waiters spin-yield 300 µs
  (`S3_MT_SPIN_US`), then sleep until a bump or the timeout. On Windows the condvar timeout follows the 15.6 ms system
  tick (measured: the draw thread's 1 ms waits took 15 ms), so Windows polls with 100 µs `thread::sleep` steps
  (high-resolution timer).
- **Deferred present**: on the worker, `present_owned` only queues the frame (`mt_defer_present`, a newer frame
  replaces an unpresented one); the main thread composes and presents it in `run_slice` (`mt_flush_present`) at least
  600 µs later (`S3_MT_PRESENT_DELAY_US`), when the draw thread is usually in its long lock-free render stretch.
- Diagnostics: the run summary prints per-thread `Cpu::run` time and an `mt:` line (lock waits, idle, worker waits,
  lock hold time, frames presented / dropped); `S3_MT_DEBUG=1` logs worker waits > 1.5 ms; `S3_TIMELINE=<host ms>`
  prints µs timestamps + args of every completed HLE call for 200 ms; `S3_HOST_PROF=1` the host-time profile.
- Test: `cargo test -p s3-runtime mt_pipeline` (two guest threads in the game's wait/present/signal pattern; ST and MT
  produce the same counts and guest results, the presenting thread really runs on the worker).
- Not wired into the Android frontend (no gain to ship).

### Measurements (desktop ARM64, throttling off, HUD 2316x904 zoom 10, `S3_FPS_CAP=0`)

| Run | Default mode (ST) fps | MT fps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| random map, samples 50-80 s (`tools/perf/fps-bench.ps1 -Random -Secs 80`, last 30 s), several builds of the same ST path | 307, 310, 339, 348, 363, 368 | 205, 223, 275, 278, 306, 331, 343, 369, 380, 408 |
| fixed map 384-2-Artokia, samples 30-70 s (`tools/perf/fps-bench.ps1`), big lock only | 210, 246 | 217, 185 |
| same + deferred present | 199, 231 | 190, 182 |
| same + present delay 600 µs (final) | 240 | 193, 245 |

MT is between -40 % and +17 % and much noisier (seconds with 30-60 fps). Where the time goes (summary `mt:` lines,
~70 s in game): the worker holds the big lock 0.75 ms per frame with presents on the worker (overlay compose under
the lock, so the logic thread's HLE calls wait), 0.3 ms per frame with the deferred present, but then waits ~0.5
ms per frame for the lock the main thread holds while composing; plus 0.1-0.5 ms per frame of handover latency
(the draw thread waits for "snapshot ready", the logic thread for "want next") and the renderer's guest code runs
~10-25 % slower on the worker (the snapshot it reads was just written by another core: cross-core cache traffic;
HYPOTHESIS, not measured with counters). With only ~15 % of the frame on the logic thread there is no room for these
costs.

**Conclusion**: true parallel guest execution is feasible and safe for the simulation (evidence below), but the
partition the game offers (draw vs logic) is too unbalanced for a gain while all HLE work shares one lock. To get
real gains, first do B (overlay rasterisation outside the machine / on a presenter thread: helps the default mode
by itself), then A again with the overlay out of the lock; finer-grained HLE locking (critical sections,
`Interlocked*`, events without the big lock) would remove most remaining lock waits.

## Evidence

- **Default mode unchanged**: `s3det --vms 90000` (inject of `tools/determinism-test.sh`) before (commit `e8042b2`)
  and after all changes: 91 identical hash lines, `insns=11886929367 mem=6e141c4900044d20 cpu=028473e586e3d37e`;
  also identical with `--write-trace` active.
- **Write-set trace** (`s3det --write-trace 60000-85000 --write-trace-out FILE`, new; `port/crates/s3-desktop/src/
  write_trace.rs`): one sampled scheduling turn per thread every 40 virtual ms (625 samples per thread, in game,
