## 1. What S3.EXE does with DirectPlay (static RE, GOG exe sha256 `00a925cf…`)

Sources: REA/Ghidra on `S3.EXE` plus a local `objdump -d -M intel` dump (`scratch/mp/`, gitignored). The game has
debug strings for almost every step (`NET: …`, `DPSYS_… empfangen`, `CDirectPlay::DP…`), which made the mapping easy.
Source file names leak from asserts: `E:\Siedler3\DirectX\Dplay.cpp`, `netsession.cpp`, `Dirk\LobbyManager.cpp`,
`Dirk\LobbyDialogs.cpp`.

### 1.1 Classes and interfaces

| Thing | Where | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DirectX::CDirectPlay` | methods `0x5bb000-0x5c2100` | wraps one `IDirectPlay4A` (`this+4`) and one `IDirectPlayLobby2A` (`this+8`); every call goes through `0x5bb890` (throws `CDirectPlayException` with the method name on failure) |
| COM creation | `0x5c07f0` | `CoCreateInstance(CLSID_DirectPlay, IID_IDirectPlay4A)`, sets `this+0xc = 4` (interface version) |
| Lobby creation | `0x5c0830` | `CoCreateInstance(CLSID_DirectPlayLobby, IID_IDirectPlayLobby2A)` |
| HRESULT name table | `0x7a03b4` | (code, "DPERR_…") pairs; copied verbatim into `s3_net::dplay::dperr` |
| `CNetSession` / `CGameNetSession` | game layer `0x46a000-0x472000` | setup (slots, names, GameSetup) and in-game lockstep ("TimeServer", steps, TTP) |
| `CLocalPlayer` / `CGameLocalPlayer` | vtables `0x65cd34`, `0x65ce70` | a local DirectPlay player: `+4` = CDirectPlay, `+8` = DPID; vtable slot 3 = Receive, 4 = Send, 7 = Receive+dispatch |
| `CConnectionShortcut` / `CTCPConnectionShortcut` | strings `0x79eee8`, `0x79ef48` | entries of the connection list; TCP one is labelled "Configured Internet Connection" / "Internet connection to %s" (HYPOTHESIS: built with `CreateCompoundAddress` TCP/IP SP + `DPAID_INet` at `0x5c0a40`) |
| Blue Byte lobby | `CLobbyManager`, `LobbyClient::*`, `Lobby::CSocketError` | original online lobby over **wsock32**, not DirectPlay; uses `dwUser`/LobbyId for league games. Dead server; ignore (Settlers United replaced it) |

IDirectPlay4A vtable offsets used (call sites verified): `+0x18` CreatePlayer, `+0x30` EnumPlayers, `+0x34`
EnumSessions, `+0x38` GetCaps, `+0x60` Open, `+0x64` Receive, `+0x68` Send, `+0x8c` EnumConnections (plus
InitializeConnection, Close, DestroyPlayer, Get/SetSessionDesc, Get/SetPlayerData, GetMessageCount by string).
Lobby: `+0x0c` Connect, `+0x20` GetConnectionSettings, `+0x30` SetConnectionSettings, `+0x38` CreateCompoundAddress.
No groups, no `SendEx`, no chat API, no secure sessions (no strings/calls found).

### 1.2 Startup: lobby probe (OBSERVED, `0x5bb6c0-0x5bb780`)

At startup the game creates the lobby object and calls `GetConnectionSettings(0, NULL, &size)`. If that fails
with **`DPERR_NOTLOBBIED` = 0x8877042E** (compare at `0x5bb730`; this confirms the value our stub already used) it
creates a plain DirectPlay object and continues normally. Otherwise it was **lobby-launched**: `DPLConnect`
(`0x5c0af0`: `IDirectPlayLobby::Connect(0, &dp2, NULL)` then `QueryInterface(IID_IDirectPlay4A)`) and
`EnumPlayers`. `0x4700ff` reads the connection settings again in the game layer (session/player names).

=> Two ways for our HLE to put the player into an online game: (a) let them use the in-game multiplayer menus with
our virtual service provider, or (b) **fake a lobby launch**: our native lobby UI fills a `DPLCONNECTION`
(session desc + player name + host/join), `GetConnectionSettings` returns it and `Connect` opens the relay session,
so the game skips its connection/session dialogs (HYPOTHESIS: needs a runtime test of where the game lands after a
lobby launch; Settlers United/aLobby likely use this path).

### 1.3 Connections (service providers)

`0x5bbb00`: `EnumConnections(guidApp or NULL, cb=0x5bc1a0, ctx, DPCONNECTION_DIRECTPLAY)`; the callback stores
64-byte entries (`this+0x34`, count `this+0x40`); then for each entry `0x5bb810` re-creates the DirectPlay object
and calls `InitializeConnection(entry+0x14 = connection blob, 0)` (HYPOTHESIS: to test it; the UI is
`Menus::priv::CConnectionDialog`). The game expects the usual SPs (IPX, TCP/IP, modem, serial) to be listed with
their names; it does not hard-code SP GUIDs (none found besides the CLSIDs/IIDs). Our HLE reports **one** connection,
"Internet (Settlers 3 Port)" with our own SP GUID `{6A2F4C1E-3B5D-4E8F-9A10-53335056F4E1}`
(`s3_net::dplay::SP_GUID_S3PORT`), whose connection blob is opaque to the game.

### 1.4 Sessions

**Create/join** (`0x46ff80` -> `0x5bb840`), DPSESSIONDESC2 built by the game:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `dwSize` | 0x50 |
| `dwFlags` | `DPSESSION_MIGRATEHOST|DPSESSION_KEEPALIVE` (0x44); `|DIRECTPLAYPROTOCOL` (0x2000) if interface version > 3 and the SP caps lack `DPCAPS_GUARANTEEDOPTIMIZED` (0x40) (GetCaps with `DPGETCAPS_GUARANTEED` at `0x5c0a20`); `|DPSESSION_PRIVATE` (0x200) when the 4th arg is set (password game) |
| `guidApplication` | `{0E9F8400-D9A5-11CF-8F4D-00804880B189}` (bytes at `0x6970f8`) |
| `guidInstance` | only for join (from the chosen session) |
| `dwMaxPlayers` | `0x435ac0()` (HYPOTHESIS: chosen map's player count) |
| `lpszSessionName`, `lpszPassword` | from the dialog (empty string `0x6553a0` if none) |
| `dwUser1/2` | globals `0x7a8000/0x7a8004`; runtime value `3c44fe57 3d439f21` in every run, also logged as "Siedler3 Version 1.60: (3c44fe57,3d439f21)" (OBSERVED 2026-11-05: a build/version id, not lobby ids) |
| `dwUser3` | 0xA0 (constant at `0x6970f0`; HYPOTHESIS: game/net version 1.60) |
| `dwUser4` | 1 if `0x437450()` (HYPOTHESIS: Amazons/mission CD flag, cf. "RemoteSetup with AmazonsSupport") |

`Open(&desc, join ? DPOPEN_JOIN : DPOPEN_CREATE)` then immediately `EnumPlayers(NULL, 0x5bc5f0, this, 0)`.

**Enumerate** (`0x5bbd60`, `0x5bbee0`): list = `EnumSessions(&desc, 0, cb=0x5bc310, ctx, flags)`; the callback
returns FALSE on `DPESC_TIMEDOUT` and stores 0x60-byte entries. Finding a specific session (join by instance):
loop `EnumSessions(…, flags|DPENUMSESSIONS_ASYNC)` + `Sleep(250)` for up to 20 s (`0x4e20` ms), then
`DPENUMSESSIONS_STOPASYNC`. Log: "NET: Starting find session" / "Found session" / "Stop find session %i".

### 1.5 Players, Send, Receive

* **CreatePlayer** (`0x5c12d0`): `CreatePlayer(&dpid, &DPNAME, hEvent, data, size, flags)`. **`hEvent` is a real
  Win32 event** (`lpMessageEvent`, created at `0x5c11c3`): DirectPlay must `SetEvent` it whenever a message for the
  player is queued. The HLE has to do the same (the game's network thread probably waits on it — HYPOTHESIS).
  One local player per machine.
* **Send** (`0x5c13f0`): `Send(myDpid, to (0 = all), flags, data, size)`.
  * Setup/control messages: `DPSEND_GUARANTEED` (flag 1), sizes 8, 12, 16, 315 (GameSetup), 2n+4 (to all).
  * **In-game lockstep bundles: flags 0 (not guaranteed)**. The time server sends every bundle **twice**
    (`0x46b8bd`: loop `edi = 2`), clients once; the game has its own acks/retransmits ("Requests retransmitted",
    "NoAck", TTP), so it tolerates loss and duplicates.
* **Receive** (`0x5c1380`): `Receive(&from, &to, DPRECEIVE_ALL, buf, &size)`; `DPERR_NOMESSAGES` (0x887700BE) = no
  message. Buffers: 0x400 bytes during setup (`0x470e41`), 0x9c40 = 40000 bytes in game (`0x46add3`). In-game the
  loop first calls `GetMessageCount` (vtable slot 5).
* **System messages** (`from == 0`, switch at `0x5bcde1`): `DPSYS_CREATEPLAYERORGROUP` (3), `DESTROYPLAYERORGROUP`
  (5), `SESSIONLOST` (0x31), `HOST` (0x101), `SETPLAYERORGROUPDATA` (0x102, only if `dwPlayerType == 1`),
  `SETSESSIONDESC` (0x104). Anything else logs "Unsupported DPSYS Message" (harmless).

### 1.6 Game-level protocol on top of DirectPlay (the payloads the relay forwards)

Setup layer (`CGameNetSession`, dispatcher `0x470e25`, jump table `0x471498`/`0x4714b8`, first payload byte = type):

| Type | Handler | Meaning (from log strings) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 5 | `0x471325` | KillPlayer received (kick, e.g. "wegen GameFull", "during GameStart") |
| 16 | `0x471214` | NetId request/assignment ("Requesting NetId %i") HYPOTHESIS |
| 20 | `0x470eb0` | player/slot info, then readiness check `0x471df0` HYPOTHESIS |
| 25 | `0x470f04` | Received GameSetup (315 bytes, map, races, …) |
| 26 | `0x470e85` | Slot infos HYPOTHESIS |
| 27 | `0x4712b4` | ? |
| 28 | `0x471356` | LoadGameInfo received (multiplayer save load) |

Map transfer: strings "FTP: …" belong to an **FTP download** of maps from a server (`0x465a45`), not a peer
transfer; maps are matched by checksum ("DLG: Invalid map checksum").

In-game lockstep (`CNetSession`, `0x46a000-0x46f500`): the host is the **TimeServer** ("Ich bin der TimeServer");
messages Request / Announce / Acknowledge / CurrentStep / ExecuteTo / NewHost / ping info; bundles have 4-byte
sub-message headers `type u8 (HYPOTHESIS), 0, size u8, retry u8` (byte 2 is the copy length, byte 3 is incremented on
resend; client bundle header `20 00 08 01`), bundle ≤ ~0x7d dwords.
Latency adaption: "Timings angepaßt an Spieler %i mit Ping von %u. Latency, Stepahead, TransferRate". Host migration:
on DPSYS_HOST the new host logs "Ich bin der neue TimeServer" and sends NewHost (12 bytes, guaranteed, `0x46ec3f`).
**Desync detection** is game-side: per-player checksums ("CheckSum player %u = %u - CheckBuffer[%u][%u]", "Message
ChecksumFailure" at `0x53b59a`, then "Desync!", "Desync Buildings/Settler/Pile/Trade/Economy/World!").
`-netmon` command line flag writes much net traffic to `trace.lis` — use it for runtime RE.

Implications for us:
1. The relay must deliver **per-sender FIFO**, support **host migration** with DPSYS_HOST to exactly one new host,
   and send DESTROYPLAYER for players whose client vanished. Reliability for non-guaranteed traffic is a bonus.
2. **Determinism is the real problem** (lockstep): all peers must compute bit-identical game state. x87 results
   must match across arm64/x86_64 hosts (see mobile-vision.md W5) — otherwise "Desync!" fires. The relay only carries
   bytes; it cannot fix desyncs, it can only report them (we hook the checksum-failure site and send `DesyncReport`).

## 2. Our stack

```
 S3.EXE ──IDirectPlay4A/Lobby (guest COM)──> s3-dx dplay.rs (HLE, build phase)
                                               │ sync calls + event polling, SetEvent(hEvent)
                                               ▼
                                         s3-net::client::NetClient  (background thread, tokio current_thread)
                                               │ WebSocket (binary frames), resumable link
                                               ▼
                                         s3-relay (tokio; hub actor: clients, sessions, players)
```

* **One virtual SP** "Internet (Settlers 3 Port)"; sessions come from the relay (`ListSessions` filtered by
  application GUID **and identical exe sha256**, since lockstep needs identical code).
* **Transport: WebSocket over TCP** (tokio-tungstenite, no TLS yet). Reasons: works through NAT/mobile carriers/proxies,
  trivially hostable behind any HTTPS reverse proxy (wss) later, ordered+reliable. QUIC would avoid head-of-line
  blocking but S3's traffic is tiny (bundles of a few hundred bytes every step), so TCP is fine (HYPOTHESIS to
  re-check with real games on LTE).
* **Relay = authority for sessions** (DirectPlay "client/server-ish" emulation): it assigns instance GUIDs and DPIDs,
  keeps player lists, decides the host. Peers never talk directly (no NAT punching needed).

### 2.1 Semantics (what the relay guarantees)

| DirectPlay concept | Relay behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Open CREATE | `CreateSession` → new instance GUID, creator = host, reply `Joined` |
| Open JOIN | `JoinSession` checks: exists, same exe, not `JOINDISABLED/NEWPLAYERSDISABLED`, password, `members < dwMaxPlayers` → `Joined{desc, host, players}` |
| EnumSessions | `ListSessions(appGuid)`; password never returned, `DPSESSION_PASSWORDREQUIRED` set instead; `dwCurrentPlayers` = player count |
| CreatePlayer | DPID allocated (never 0/1/0xFFFFFFFF, scrambled counter); creator gets `PlayerCreated` **before** others get `PlayerAdded` (→ DPSYS_CREATEPLAYERORGROUP) |
| DestroyPlayer / client leaves / slot expires | `PlayerRemoved` to the other members (→ DPSYS_DESTROYPLAYERORGROUP) |
| Set/GetPlayerData, SetPlayerName | owner only; broadcast `PlayerData` (→ DPSYS_SETPLAYERORGROUPDATA) / `PlayerName` |
| SetSessionDesc | host only; others get `SessionDescChanged` (→ DPSYS_SETSESSIONDESC) |
| Host leaves | with `MIGRATEHOST`: oldest remaining member becomes host, gets `BecameHost` (→ DPSYS_HOST); without: everyone gets `SessionLost` (→ DPSYS_SESSIONLOST) |
| Send(from, to, flags) | `from` must be owned by the sender (spoofing dropped). `to = 0`: one `Deliver` per other player (addressed to that player, like DirectPlay). Per-sender order preserved for every receiver |
| Send without GUARANTEED | still reliable, but dropped while the receiver has > `soft_queue_limit` (2048) unacked frames (DirectPlay may drop these too) |
| KEEPALIVE / connection loss | client pings every `keepalive` (2 s); relay drops a silent connection after 10 s; the client's slot (players, host role, queue) is kept `resume_grace` (20 s) for a resume; after that it is removed as if it left |
| Desync | `DesyncReport{step, checksum, detail}` logged and forwarded as `Desync` to the other members |

### 2.2 Resumable link

Mobile networks drop TCP connections (Wi-Fi↔LTE handover, sleep). Every non-control frame is numbered per direction
(`seq` 1, 2, …), every frame carries `ack` (highest seq received). Both sides keep unacked frames
(`s3_net::link::Link`). On reconnect the client sends `Hello{resume: token, last_seq}`; the relay answers
`Welcome{resumed: true, last_seq}` and both retransmit what the other has not seen; duplicates (`seq <= last`) are
ignored. The game sees nothing but a short stall (lockstep waits). If the relay no longer knows the token it
answers `resumed: false` and the client reports `SessionLost`. Explicit `Ack` frames are sent at most every 100 ms
when data was received but nothing was sent back. Test: `resume_after_connection_drop_loses_nothing`.

### 2.3 Wire format (protocol v1)

One WebSocket **binary** message = one frame:

```
frame   = seq:var  ack:var  tag:u8  body
var     = unsigned LEB128 (u16/u32/u64; overlong/overflow rejected)
bytes   = len:var raw[len]        (max 65536)
string  = bytes, UTF-8            (max 256 bytes)
guid    = 16 raw bytes, Windows GUID memory order (Data1..3 little-endian)
list<T> = count:var T*            (max 1024)
desc    = flags:var instance:guid application:guid max_players:var current_players:var
          name:string password:string user1..4:var
player  = dpid:var owner:var flags:var short_name:string long_name:string data:bytes
```

seq = 0 marks control frames (never retransmitted). Trailing bytes and unknown tags are errors (connection closed).

Client → relay:

| Tag | Message | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Hello (control) | proto:var(=1) exe_sha256:32 raw name:string build:string resume:(0 \| 1 token:16 raw last_seq:var) |
| 2 | Ping (control) | nonce:var |
| 3 | Ack (control) | — |
| 4 | Bye (control) | — (leave immediately, no grace) |
| 10 | ListSessions | req:var application:guid |
| 11 | CreateSession | req:var desc |
| 12 | JoinSession | req:var instance:guid password:string |
| 13 | LeaveSession | req:var |
| 14 | SetSessionDesc | req:var desc |
| 20 | CreatePlayer | req:var flags:var short:string long:string data:bytes |
| 21 | DestroyPlayer | req:var dpid:var |
| 22 | SetPlayerData | req:var dpid:var data:bytes |
| 23 | SetPlayerName | req:var dpid:var short:string long:string |
| 30 | Send | from:var to:var flags:var payload:bytes |
| 40 | DesyncReport | step:var checksum:var detail:string |

Relay → client:

| Tag | Message | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Welcome (control) | proto:var client_id:var token:16 raw resumed:u8 last_seq:var keepalive_ms:var server:string |
| 2 | Reject (control) | code:var message:string (then close) |
| 3 | Pong (control) | nonce:var |
| 4 | Ack (control) | — |
| 10 | Error | req:var code:var message:string |
| 11 | Ok | req:var |
| 12 | SessionList | req:var list\<desc\> |
| 13 | Joined | req:var desc host_client:var list\<player\> |
| 14 | PlayerCreated | req:var dpid:var |
| 20 | PlayerAdded | player |
| 21 | PlayerRemoved | dpid:var |
| 22 | PlayerData | dpid:var data:bytes |
| 23 | PlayerName | dpid:var short:string long:string |
| 24 | SessionDescChanged | desc |
| 25 | BecameHost | — |
| 26 | SessionLost | code:var |
| 30 | Deliver | from:var to:var flags:var payload:bytes |
| 40 | Desync | client_id:var step:var checksum:var detail:string |

Error codes (`ErrorCode`, mapped to HRESULTs by `s3_net::dplay::hresult_for`): 1 BadRequest (INVALIDPARAMS),
2 VersionMismatch / 3 ExeMismatch (UNKNOWNAPPLICATION), 4 ResumeFailed (SESSIONLOST), 5 ServerFull
(CANNOTCREATESERVER), 10 NoSuchSession (NOSESSIONS), 11 SessionFull / 13 JoinDisabled (NONEWPLAYERS),
12 WrongPassword (INVALIDPASSWORD), 14 NotInSession (UNINITIALIZED), 15 AlreadyInSession (ALREADYINITIALIZED),
20 NoSuchPlayer (INVALIDPLAYER), 21 NotOwner (ACCESSDENIED), 30 Timeout (TIMEOUT), 31 Disconnected (CONNECTIONLOST).

Handshake checks: protocol version must equal 1; if the relay runs with `--gog-only`/`--allow-exe`, the exe hash
must be listed. Payload limit 64 KiB per message (S3's largest buffer is 40000 bytes).

### 2.4 Code map

| File | What |
| --- | --- |
| `port/crates/s3-net/src/wire.rs` | varint/bytes/string encoder + bounded decoder |
| `port/crates/s3-net/src/protocol.rs` | `ClientMsg`, `ServerMsg`, `Frame`, `SessionDesc`, `PlayerInfo`, `ErrorCode`, `guid()` |
| `port/crates/s3-net/src/link.rs` | seq/ack/retransmit bookkeeping (both sides) |
| `port/crates/s3-net/src/client.rs` | `NetClient`: blocking requests (`create_session`, `join_session`, `create_player`, …), non-blocking `send`, `poll_event`/`wait_event`, `snapshot()` (session, host, players, rtt), auto-resume |
| `port/crates/s3-net/src/dplay.rs` | DPERR table (from the exe), DPSYS/DPSESSION/DPSEND constants, `SystemMessage::layout(guest_addr)` = DPMSG_* bytes for Receive, `hresult_for` |
| `port/crates/s3-dx/src/dplay_net.rs` | the DirectPlay HLE over `NetClient` (section 5) |
| `port/crates/s3-desktop/src/mp_hash.rs` | `s3run --mp-hash`: per-simulation-tick state hash, exec log, game-log / net debug hooks (section 6) |

| `port/crates/s3-relay/tests/two_clients.rs` | create/list/join/players/ordered data/spoofing/data+desc changes/desync/leave; host migration (3 clients) and session loss; password/full/exe rules; exe allow-list; resume after drop without loss; slot expiry |

Dependencies (all MIT/Apache-2.0, GPL-3.0-compatible): tokio, tokio-tungstenite/tungstenite (no TLS features),
futures-util, log. Randomness for GUIDs/tokens comes from std's OS-seeded hasher (HYPOTHESIS: good enough for a
hobby relay; switch to `getrandom` before public deployment).

## 3. HLE plan (original plan; what was built is in section 5)

1. `DirectPlayLobby::GetConnectionSettings`: keep `DPERR_NOTLOBBIED` unless the frontend requested a lobby launch
   (then return a DPLCONNECTION; see 1.2).
2. `EnumConnections`: one callback with `SP_GUID_S3PORT`, name "Internet (Settlers 3 Port)", a small opaque blob.
   `InitializeConnection` with that blob = `NetClient::connect` (relay URL from settings; default
   `ws://127.0.0.1:7777/` for tests). Other SPs: none.
3. `EnumSessions`: `list_sessions(guidApplication)`, call the callback per session (DPSESSIONDESC2 in guest memory),
   then once with `DPESC_TIMEDOUT`. With `DPENUMSESSIONS_ASYNC` return the cached list immediately and refresh in
   the background; `STOPASYNC` stops refreshing.
4. `Open`: CREATE → `create_session`, JOIN → `join_session(instance, password)`; map `NetError::code()` via
   `hresult_for`. `GetSessionDesc`/`SetSessionDesc` from `snapshot()` / `set_session_desc`.
5. `CreatePlayer` → `create_player`; remember the guest **event handle** per local DPID and `SetEvent` it whenever
   a message for that player is queued. `EnumPlayers` from `snapshot().players` (local + remote).
6. `Receive`/`GetMessageCount`: drain `poll_event()` into a guest-side queue: `Event::Message` → data message
   (`from`, `to`); everything else → `SystemMessage::layout(buf)` with `from = DPID_SYSMSG`; `BUFFERTOOSMALL` +
   required size if the game's buffer is short; `Event::Link(Reconnecting/Resumed)` only logged (maybe an overlay
   icon); `Event::Link(Lost)` → DPSYS_SESSIONLOST.
7. `Send` → `NetClient::send` (never blocks). `Close` → `leave_session`.
8. Desync: an `s3-mods` hook at the checksum-failure site (`0x53b59a`, "Message ChecksumFailure") calls
   `report_desync(step, checksum, …)` (HYPOTHESIS: exact hook point and arguments to be confirmed at runtime).
9. Test with two `s3run` instances on one PC against a local relay (desktop), then emulator + desktop.

## 4. PC crossplay later (design notes)

Goal: let Windows players with the real game (Settlers United / aLobby, real `dplayx.dll`) play with ours.
Options, cheapest first:

1. **Bridge client on the PC** (recommended): a small Windows helper registers a DirectPlay **service provider**
   (`dpwsockx`-style SP DLL) or simply hooks `dplayx` via the game's own `CoCreateInstance`, and speaks our relay
   protocol. Windows players then see the same "Internet (Settlers 3 Port)" connection. Requires the same exe build
   (crossplay only with GOG/SU builds whose sha256 we support) and the same determinism (PC x87 is the reference;
   our emulated x87 must match native bit-for-bit).
2. **Real DirectPlay wire protocol in the relay** ("DirectPlay 6 TCP/IP SP": enumeration on UDP/TCP 47624, then
   dynamic ports 2300-2400 (TCP + UDP), messages with the `play` signature). The relay would act as a DirectPlay
   name server/peer so unmodified PCs connect by IP (Settlers United already tunnels this over its VPN-like lobby).
   Big job (DirectPlay's peer-to-peer topology means every PC talks to every peer; the relay must impersonate all
   our mobile players with distinct addresses). Documented by Wine's `dlls/dplayx` and the MS-DPDX spec (HYPOTHESIS:
   check spec coverage).
3. **VPN/LAN emulation**: put mobile clients on a virtual LAN with PCs (e.g. a WireGuard/tun-based overlay) and run
   the real DirectPlay protocol from our HLE. Heavy on mobile (VPN permission, battery).

Our protocol keeps everything the DirectPlay wire model needs (DPIDs, session desc incl. `dwUser`, guaranteed flag,
system events), so a bridge can translate 1:1.

## 5. DirectPlay HLE (implemented 2026-11-05, `port/crates/s3-dx/src/dplay_net.rs`)

`dplay.rs` keeps the COM plumbing (vtables, factories, lobby stubs) and routes these IDirectPlay4A methods to
`dplay_net.rs`; one `NetClient` per machine (`Machine::state::<DpNet>`), shared by all DirectPlay objects the game
creates (it re-creates them per connection test).

| Method | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `EnumConnections` | one callback: SP GUID `SP_GUID_S3PORT`, connection blob `"S3PORTv1"+GUID` (24 bytes), DPNAME "Internet (Settlers 3 Port)", flags `DPCONNECTION_DIRECTPLAY` |
| `InitializeConnection` | checks the blob, connects to the relay once (`NetConfig`: `set_config(m, ..)` or env `S3_RELAY_URL`, `S3_NET_NAME`); relay down -> `DPERR_UNAVAILABLE` |
| `GetCaps` / `GetPlayerCaps` | `GUARANTEEDOPTIMIZED|GUARANTEEDSUPPORTED` (+`ISHOST`), so the game does not add `DIRECTPLAYPROTOCOL`; 65000-byte buffers, 1 local player |
| `EnumSessions` | sync: `list_sessions(app GUID)` + callbacks + `DPESC_TIMEDOUT`; `ASYNC`: cached list, refreshed by a background thread; `STOPASYNC`: no-op. Session names live in stable guest strings (the game may keep the pointer) |
| `Open` | `CREATE` -> `create_session(desc from the game)`, `JOIN` -> `join_session(instance, password)`; errors via `hresult_for` |
| `Close` | `leave_session`, clears local players and the queue |
| `EnumPlayers` | local (flag `DPENUMPLAYERS_LOCAL` 0x8) + remote (0x10) players sorted by DPID |
| `CreatePlayer` / `DestroyPlayer` | relay player; remembers the **Win32 event** per local DPID |
| `Send` | `NetClient::send` (never blocks); to a local DPID: queued locally |
| `Receive` / `GetMessageCount` | drain relay events into a host queue (data -> `from`/`to`; events -> `DPSYS_*` via `SystemMessage::layout` at the game's buffer address, `from = 0`); `BUFFERTOOSMALL` + size; `TOPLAYER`/`FROMPLAYER`/`PEEK` honoured |
| `Get/SetSessionDesc`, `Get/SetPlayerData`, `Get/SetPlayerName` | relay snapshot / requests |
| groups, `Initialize` | succeed with no entries |

Service `dplay-pump` (every scheduler slice) and every Receive/GetMessageCount drain relay events and **SetEvent the
local players' events** when messages are queued. Debug: `S3_DPLAY_TRACE=1` logs every Send/Receive with the first
24 bytes. Test: `s3-dx` `dplay_two_machines_through_relay` (two machines, real relay in-process, guest callbacks:
EnumConnections -> InitializeConnection -> Open CREATE / EnumSessions + Open JOIN -> CreatePlayer -> DPSYS
CREATEPLAYER with `BUFFERTOOSMALL` retry -> ordered data both ways -> event signalled -> GetSessionDesc ->
Close -> DESTROYPLAYER).

### 5.1 Menu flow observed at runtime (GOG exe, 800x600 menu coordinates)

- Main menu "Multi-player Game: **LAN**" (165,275) opens "LAN Game": "Type of Network" lists our connection
  (200,131); "Search for games" (175,240); "Open Games" list (first entry ~200,330); "Join Game" (610,567);
  "New Game" (730,567).
- "Multi-player Game: **Internet**" (165,315) says "Internet connection not detected." without touching DirectPlay
  (HYPOTHESIS: it is the Blue Byte lobby over wsock32, whose `WSAStartup` fails on purpose). The LAN entry is the
  DirectPlay path; a mobile UI should rename/route it.
- New Game -> Game Setup with the map picker (tabs Random 181,133 / Multi-player Map 181,180; "384-2-Artokia" =
  first MP map 165,255; OK 630,467), setup OK (730,567) -> **Open(CREATE)** + CreatePlayer -> waiting room
  ("Status: Waiting for Players"). The joiner appears after Join Game. Each player must press its ready button
  (right of the chat line: host row 723,114, second row 723,134), then the host's OK (730,567) starts. OK before
  everyone is ready shows "Not all players are ready".
- Session desc the game creates (OBSERVED): flags 0x44, `dwMaxPlayers` 2 (from the map/setup), name
  "Player's game", `dwUser1/2` = `3c44fe57 3d439f21` (constant across runs; the game logs
  "Siedler3 Version 1.60: (3c44fe57,3d439f21)" — a build/version id), `dwUser3` 0xA0, `dwUser4` 1.
- Setup traffic (OBSERVED with `S3_DPLAY_TRACE`): host -> joiner GameSetup (type 0x19, 315 B, guaranteed) and slot
  infos (0x1a, 53 B, to all); ping pairs type 0x10 (12 B, `10 00 0c 00 ...` with a `timeGetTime` value, echoed);
  joiner `SetPlayerData` (-> DPSYS 0x102 at the host); host `SetSessionDesc` at game start (-> DPSYS 0x104);
  final slot info type 0x14. "LOGIC: GameLogic random seed N" is the same on both peers (seed from GameSetup).

### 5.2 In-game lockstep protocol (OBSERVED + STATIC)

- Every in-game message is a **bundle**: dword CRC32 (table at `session+0xe78`, `0x46dbd0`, over the rest) then
  4-byte sub-message headers `type, 0, size, retry` + payload. Receive loop `0x46adaa`: GetMessageCount, Receive
  into a 40000-byte buffer, DPID -> slot (`0x434ec0`), drop unless `session+0x23d[slot]` (active) and not
  `session+0x251[slot]` (left), drop on CRC mismatch, then dispatch by type (`0x46afe8` / `0x46afb8`):
  0x06 `0x46c8b0`, 0x10 `0x45c380` (ping), 0x11 `0x46d370` (**ExecuteTo**: `session+0x224 = max(.., value)`),
  0x12 `0x46cbd0`, 0x13 `0x46d190`, 0x16 `0x46d6a0`, 0x17 `0x46d7c0`, 0x18 `0x46d820`,
  0x20 `0x46d610` (ack: `session+0x1d4[slot] = max(.., value)`), 0x21 `0x46c8d0` (player request), 0x22 `0x46db40`.
- Start: the host (TimeServer) sends `11 00 08 01 | 0x11` (ExecuteTo 17) twice per round, the joiner answers
  `20 00 08 01 | 0`, until both logic threads run; then the joiner's first request `21 fb 10 01 ...` arrives and
  normal traffic starts. While a peer is still building the map both screens show "Initiating player2player
  communication....". With a **random map** this phase took 30-100+ s in our runs ("Position gefunden nach ~30000
  Versuchen" start-position search, slow in the interpreter): runs cut at 50-80 s looked "stuck" there but were
  only slow. The test script therefore uses the fixed map 384-2-Artokia.
- Logic side: `CLogicThread` loop `0x53dxxx` increments the **frame counter** `gd+0x2d2d8` by 4 every pass
  (`0x53dda5`), executes queued logic messages (`0x535990`; switch on the class byte at `0x535a59`) and runs the
  **simulation tick** (`0x53e5a1`: `gd` tick calls `0x4e7810`, `0x4e05e0`, `0x4e9670`, then AI `0x550f80` per slot)
  only when `word [0x7ace62] == 0`. The frame counter keeps running while lockstep pauses the simulation, so it
  differs between peers; the number of simulation ticks does not.
- Logic message classes seen: `0x01` = player commands from the network (`01 cmd len 0 ...`, e.g. `0x03`
  selection, `0x09` move, `0x01` place building, `0xfb` sent by each player every ~256 ticks with a
  checksum-like value: HYPOTHESIS: the game's own sync check); `0x02` = local timing (`02 00 08 01 v`, value differs
  per peer); `0x22` (0x58 bytes, local, executed at slightly different ticks per peer, bytes 4..5 differ).
- `gd+0x2d2dc` = simulation RNG state (changes exactly on simulation ticks; equal on both peers).
- Game debug log: function `0x428720` (printf-like). `S3_GAME_LOG=1` makes s3run print it (`[game] ...`);
  `S3_EXE_ARGS=-netmon` passes the game's net-monitor switch (more `NET:` lines, e.g. "Erstelle Zufallswelt").

## 6. Local two-instance test and desync check

`port/scripts/mp-local-test.sh [OUT] [SECONDS]` starts `s3-relay` on 127.0.0.1:$PORT (7787), two
`s3run --headless` (env `S3_RELAY_URL`, `S3_NET_NAME=host|join`), injects the menu clicks of 5.1 (host creates on
Artokia, joiner searches/joins at 17-20 s, both ready, host starts at 29 s), takes screenshots every 20 s and
compares the hash files with `tools/mp_hash_compare.py`. Env: `MAP=random`, `HOST_EXTRA`/`JOIN_EXTRA` (more inject
items, e.g. in-game build/select/move clicks), `HASH_EVERY`, `PORT`, `HOST_MT`/`JOIN_MT=1` (that peer in the
multi-core mode, [multicore.md](multicore.md)), `PYTHON` (default `python3`; on Windows `PYTHON=python`). Runs on
Windows through Git Bash (`bash.exe port/scripts/mp-local-test.sh`, `S3RUN`/`RELAY` pointing at the `.exe`s).
In-game select/move clicks that hit units in the 800x600 default view on Artokia (perf-mt): host
`45000:click 300 362;46000:rclick 650 450;70000:click 480 410;71000:rclick 620 300`, joiner
`50000:click 292 368;51000:rclick 600 480;80000:click 455 425;81000:rclick 650 350` (4-8 player commands).

**Hash** (`s3run --mp-hash FILE [--mp-hash-every N]`, `port/crates/s3-desktop/src/mp_hash.rs`): a hook at the start of
every simulation tick (`0x53e5a1`) writes `step=TICK rng=.. n=settlers/buildings/piles settlers=.. buildings=..
piles=.. trade=.. econ=.. players=.. [world=.. every 64 ticks] frame=.. local=..` (FNV-1a over the tables of
game-state-units.md). World tile bytes `+0x09 +0x0b +0x0c +0x0d` are masked: they differ per peer from the first
tick (+9/+d, one region: HYPOTHESIS fog / local view) or around the local player's land in build mode (+b/+c:
HYPOTHESIS placement markers) while all simulation tables stay identical. A hook on the logic executor
(`0x535a59`) writes `exec at=TICK frame=.. msg=HEX` for every executed logic message; the compare tool checks
that both peers execute the same class-0x01 messages at the same ticks. Debug: `S3_MP_DUMP_STEP=t1,t2` writes the
raw tables before those ticks (`tools/mp_dump_diff.py DIR TICK` lists differing per-entry offsets), `S3_MP_HDR=1`
adds `gd+0x2d240..` dwords, `S3_MP_NETDBG=1` logs the receive filter and CRC failures.

Results (2026-11-05, x86_64 desktop, both peers on this PC; logs/hashes in `scratch/mp-dplay/`, local only):

| Run | Setup | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| long1 | random 384 map, 330 s, select+move by both players, 1 building placed | 3979 ticks (~4.2 min game time at 64 ms/tick), 5 player commands executed at identical ticks, all simulation tables identical at every tick; world differed only in bytes masked since (+b/+c) |
| a1 | Artokia, 60 s | 391 ticks, IDENTICAL |
| long2 | Artokia, 400 s, build/select/move by both players | 5489 ticks (~5.9 min), 8 player commands (4 building sites, 2 selections, 2 moves) at identical ticks, settlers/buildings/piles/trade/econ/players identical at **every** tick; world hash differs from tick 4992 |
| long3 | same as long2 + raw dumps | 5052 ticks, same picture; world differs from tick 3392: dump at tick 4800 = only the masked bytes plus **tile byte +0x0f on 3 tiles** ((293,345), (301,335), (301,341): 0x18 on one peer, 0 on the other) |

Conclusion: no simulation desync found in ~16 min of combined two-peer game time. The remaining world difference is
3 tiles of byte +0x0f while every settler/building/pile/economy/player record stays bit-identical for thousands of
ticks afterwards; HYPOTHESIS: another local-only marker (e.g. a move-target / selection marker drawn for the local
player), not simulation state. To confirm: watch writes to those tiles (add a write watchpoint to s3run) and check
whether the game's own sync messages (`0xfb`) still agree. The compare tool reports this case as
`RESULT: SIMULATION TABLES IDENTICAL; world tiles differ` (exit code 3).

Pitfall found on the way: hashing at the frame counter (`gd+0x2d2d8`) instead of the simulation tick reported
"desyncs" from step ~84 in about half the runs; the sequences of distinct states were identical — the peers had just
paused at different frames. Always key comparisons by simulation tick.

## 8. LAN play out of the box (embedded relay + UDP discovery)

Implemented 2026-11-08 (lan-mp) after the user report "hosting and joining over LAN does not work" (on a phone nobody
runs `s3-relay`, so InitializeConnection failed, "Type of Network" stayed empty and New/Join Game showed errors).

### 8.1 Design

- **Mode switch**: no relay URL configured (`S3_RELAY_URL` unset/empty, Android: no `relay-url.txt`) = **LAN mode**;
  `S3_LAN=0` forces the old behaviour (relay at `ws://127.0.0.1:7777/`). A configured URL = Internet/explicit relay
  mode, unchanged.
- **Every instance runs an embedded relay** (`s3_relay::spawn_background`: own thread + current-thread tokio
  runtime, listens on `0.0.0.0:7777`, else any free port; `S3_LAN_RELAY_PORT` changes the first choice). It starts in
  `InitializeConnection` (= when the game's LAN screen tests our connection), once per process, and keeps running.
  The local `NetClient` connects to it via `127.0.0.1`, so the connection entry always works. In LAN mode the entry
  is called **"Local network / Wi-Fi (Settlers 3 Port)"**.
- **Host = the device that presses New Game**: `Open(CREATE)` creates the session on its own relay and starts the
  announcement (`Discovery::set_hosting(port, session name)`); `Close` stops it.
- **Join**: `EnumSessions` merges the sessions of the own relay with those of every discovered host relay (one cached
  `NetClient` per host relay) and remembers instance GUID -> relay client. `Open(JOIN)` switches the active client to
  the relay the session came from; all later calls (players, Send/Receive, pump) use the active client. `Close`
  switches back to the local relay. No federation between relays: each game lives on exactly one relay, the host's.
- **Two hosts** on one LAN: both are announced (keyed by a per-process nonce), both games appear in "Open Games".
  Two instances on one PC: the second relay gets an ephemeral port (the beacon carries the real port).
- Why not one shared relay per LAN: electing one would need a protocol and break when that device leaves. With
  "relay = host", the game's own host-leaves behaviour is unchanged (the session ends with the host anyway: the
  relay's host migration only helps when the host's client, not its device, drops).

### 8.2 Discovery protocol (`port/crates/s3-net/src/lan.rs`)

UDP port **47777**. Packet: `"S3PLAN1"` kind:u8 (1 query, 2 beacon) nonce:u64le exe_tag:8 (first 8 bytes of the
exe sha256; other builds are ignored, lockstep needs identical code) relay_port:u16le name_len:u8 name.

- One listen socket on `0.0.0.0:47777` with `SO_REUSEADDR` (several instances on one PC; broadcasts reach all of
  them), one socket per local IPv4 interface (bound to that address, ephemeral port) and one unbound socket.
  Interfaces: Unix `getifaddrs` (real broadcast address, e.g. `192.168.1.255` on the test Wi-Fi, a /22); Windows:
  the host name's addresses (std only) with a /24 guess plus 255.255.255.255. Re-read every 10 s.
- Every second: not hosting -> **query**; hosting -> **beacon**; sent from every interface socket to
  `255.255.255.255:47777` and the interface broadcast, and to `127.0.0.1:47777`. A host answers a query with a
  unicast beacon to the query's source address.
- The receiver takes the relay address from the beacon's **source IP** + port. A host with several interfaces
  (Wi-Fi, VPN, Hyper-V switch) is heard on each; candidates are ranked by common prefix bits with a local address and
  tried in that order (2 s connect timeout each). Hosts expire after 6 s of silence.
- Firewall: the joiner's queries go out and the host's answers come back as unicast replies to a broadcast, which
  the Windows firewall allows by default ("unicast response to multicast/broadcast", 3 s window). So **a Windows PC
  can join a phone host without any firewall rule** (verified). A Windows PC as **host** needs inbound TCP 7777
  (relay) and inbound UDP 47777 (queries) for `s3run.exe`; Windows asks on first listen, or once, elevated:
  `netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="Settlers 3 Port LAN" dir=in action=allow program="<path>\s3run.exe" enable=yes profile=private`
  (HYPOTHESIS: not tested here; the PC-host case was not needed for the verification).
- Android: Wi-Fi drivers may filter broadcasts unless a `WifiManager.MulticastLock` is held. `s3-android/src/wifilock.rs`
  registers `s3_net::lan::set_start_hook`; the first discovery start acquires a non-refcounted lock (JNI, global
  ref kept forever). Manifest: `ACCESS_WIFI_STATE`, `CHANGE_WIFI_MULTICAST_STATE` (normal permissions, no prompt).
  Logcat: `WifiService: acquireMulticastLock uid=...` + `lan: Wi-Fi multicast lock acquired`.

### 8.3 Verification

- Unit tests: `cargo test -p s3-net lan` (packet round trip, address ranking, two discovery instances in one process
  find each other, other exe tag ignored).
- Desktop + desktop (Windows ARM64, two headless s3run): `LAN=1 PYTHON=python S3RUN=.../s3run.exe GAME_DIR=...
  bash port/scripts/mp-local-test.sh scratch/lan3 100` -> joiner logs `lan: host 'Player's game' relay
  192.168.1.51:7777`, `LAN: connected to host relay ...`, joined; 946 ticks **IDENTICAL (no desync)**. One run during
  a parallel APK build (`scratch/lan2`) joined fine but the game did not start before the timed clicks (timing only).
- **Phone (Galaxy Z Fold4 cover, host) <-> Windows PC (headless s3run, join) over Wi-Fi** (`scratch/lanphone/`):
  phone LAN screen lists "Local network / Wi-Fi (Settlers 3 Port)", New Game on Artokia, PC finds `relay
  192.168.1.50:7777` within a second of "Search for games", joins, both ready, phone starts; both run the map.
  PC run 240 s: 2326 simulation ticks (~2.5 min game time); the phone player's selection + 3 move orders (tapped on
  the phone, Classic Touch) were executed on the PC at ticks 1037-1063 (`exec ... msg=0103/0109` in `pc.hash`); the
  game's own periodic sync messages (`01fb`, every ~256 ticks) kept coming and the game never logged
  Desync/ChecksumFailure (`S3_GAME_LOG=1`). No firewall rule, no relay-url.txt, no typed IP. Both peers arm64
  (phone; Windows 11 ARM64 s3run). Screens: `scratch/lanphone/phone-ingame.png`, `pc-*.png` (local only).

Driving the phone (cover display 2316x904, layouts of menu-layout.md): main menu "Multi-player Game: LAN" 354,773;
LAN screen network entry 331,134, New Game 1965,596; map picker tab "Multi-player Map" 201,180, first map 154,381,
OK 2140,840; Game Setup OK 1586,813; waiting room ready (host row) 2027,259, OK 2140,847.

### 8.4 Open

- PC as host with a phone joiner needs the firewall rule above (or the user accepting Windows' prompt).
- Networks with client isolation (guest Wi-Fi, some hotspots) block both broadcast and device-to-device TCP; then only
  the Internet relay (relay-url.txt) works. Phone hotspot (host on the hotspot phone): untested.
- No manual "join by IP" field yet (would be `relay-url.txt` today).
- The beacon keeps running while the game is in progress (harmless: the relay refuses joins to a full session).

Provider auto-select (2026-11-08): `s3-mods/src/lan_autoselect.rs` clicks the only "Type of Network" entry once
when the LAN screen appears (else the game asks "Before connecting, a provider has to be selected!").

```md
# Performance (fps, interpreter speed, native fast paths)

Owner: perf-cpu (workflow `wf_a446e364-b12`, 2026-11-05). Goal: >= 60 fps on the phone (target 60-120).
Related: [cpu.md](cpu.md) (interpreter internals), [display.md](display.md) (present path, FPS counter),
[determinism.md](determinism.md) (why every change below must be bit-exact).

## Summary (desktop, x86_64, one core, 640x480 in game, random map 384)

| Version | In-game fps (uncapped, `S3_FPS_CAP=0`) | Interpreter in game | `bench_mips` | `s3det` 90 000 vms wall |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before (vblank grid pacing, old interpreter) | 28-30 (paced), ~33 uncapped | ~100-140 M instr/s | ~178 MIPS | 114.9 s |
| + frame limiter instead of 60 Hz grid | 36-47 at cap 60 (CPU bound) | same | same | same |
| + interpreter rework (pre-decoded ops, lazy flags, chaining) | 66-70 | ~225 M instr/s | ~280-290 MIPS | 66.3 s |
| + native fast paths (4 render loops) | **80-82** | ~255 M "guest-equivalent" instr/s | same | 55.9 s |

Default settings with the custom resolution mod (800x600 in game) run at 53-55 fps at the 60 cap
(`scratch/perf/def4.png`). Numbers are noisy (other agents build on the same PC, random map per s3run run); the
`s3det` wall time over a fixed deterministic workload is the most reliable comparison.

**Phone: measured 2026-11-05 (verify-fps1), see [Phone measurements](#phone-measurements)**: perf-cpu alone gave
~2.5x guest MIPS (100 -> 250) but the phone's default wide size 1536x600 needs ~6.5 M guest instructions per frame
(~10 000 snapshot tiles), so it ran 38-40 fps; three more fast paths over the per-tile loops (below) brought Classic
Touch to the 60 cap.

### Phone measurements

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold4 (SM-F936B, Snapdragon 8+ Gen 1, Android 14), cover screen 2316x904 @120 Hz, display mode
Native wide, cap 60, random map 384, readings of the detailed FPS counter (3 samples 3 s apart; "MIPS" counts a
native fast path as the guest instructions it stands for). Screenshots `scratch/vfps/phone/` (local only).

| Build | UI mode | Render size (zoom level) | fps | MIPS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before the workflow | HUD | 800x600-ish | ~26 | ~100 |
| perf-cpu | HUD | 1536x600 (6, default) | 36 | 250 |
| perf-cpu | Classic | 1536x600 (6) / ~1440x560 (5) / 1336x520 (4) | 38-40 / 40 / 44 | 250 |
| perf-cpu | Classic, Fit 4:3 | ~693x520 | 60 (cap) | 200 |
| + `snap_tiles` + `obj_empty` (v1) | Classic | 1536x600 (6) | 54-56 | 353-365 |
| + `land_clean` + `obj_empty` v2 | **Classic** | **1536x600 (6, default)** | **60 / 62 / 60** | 412-419 |
| same | Classic | 1232x480 (3) | 60 / 60 / 60 | ~320 (headroom) |
| same | Classic | 1848x720 (9) | 42 / 46 / 42 | 392-420 |
| same | HUD | 1536x600 (6, default) | 58 / 56 / 48 (48: lots of animated water) | 376-449 |
| same | HUD | 1232x480 (3) | 60 / 60 / 60 | ~322 |
| same | HUD | 1848x720 (9) | 58 / 60 / 46 | 438-509 |

Notes: the engine thread is 94-99 % of one core; simpleperf (`su`, 8 s, 4 kHz) shows it at ~2 GHz average clock
(the governor does not hold the prime core's 3.19 GHz; pinning the thread to cpu7 with `taskset` gave only ~5 %),
92 % of the process cycles in `s3-engine` (interpreter `run_with` + handlers; `to_framebuffer_into` 3.7 %, libc
5 %), 6.6 % in `s3-present`. Water and other animated landscape make triangles dirty every frame (`land_clean`
declines them), which is why the fps depends on the map view.

Desktop at the phone aspect (`s3run --headless --display native --window 2316x904 --fps full`, `S3_FPS_CAP=0`):
Classic 35 fps (perf-cpu, under the profiler) -> 43-45 (`snap_tiles`) -> **70-72** (all), HUD 62-64.
`s3det` 90 000 vms wall time 55.9 s -> 41.4 s.

## What limits fps

1. **Pacing**: the draw thread (`CDrawThread`) renders as fast as it can and calls
   `IDirectDraw2::WaitForVerticalBlank(DDWAITVB_BLOCKBEGIN)` once per frame (registry `WaitVBlank`=1). Our HLE used a
   60 Hz grid, so a frame needing 17 ms waited for the next boundary -> 30 fps (real vsync does the same).
   The game itself has no other fps cap: the logic thread is a separate 64 ms timer (`CLogicThread`), the draw
   thread only renders snapshots of it. Fixed: `WaitForVerticalBlank` is now a **frame limiter** (below).
2. **CPU**: after that the draw thread is CPU bound: ~2.5-2.9 M guest instructions per frame at 640x480 plus the
   logic thread (~20-50 M instr/s in game; during random-map generation 100% of the CPU for 10-60 s).
   All guest threads share one host core (cooperative green threads).

### Guest profile (in game, `S3_PROFILE`, functions from REA)

| Function | Thread | Share | What |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0x51f110` | logic | 18-20 % | builds the render snapshot grid (visible tiles, see resolution-zoom.md) |
| `0x4b26c0` | draw | 16-19 % | frame renderer (landscape/object pass over the snapshot tiles) |
| `0x4d3050` | draw | 12-15 % | per-tile object drawing (huge function, ~1200 lines of pseudocode) |
| `0x54cbd0` | draw | 10-12 % | landscape pass |
| `0x5fc350` | draw | 10-13 % | 16-bit RLE sprite blitter -> **fast path** for its opaque row loop |
| `0x5fd080` / `0x5fd120` / `0x5fd0c0` | draw | 8-15 % | shadow/darken sprite variants -> **fast paths** for the pixel loops, since perf-shadow the whole row loop of `0x5fd120` |
| `0x5fc160` + `0x5f48e0` | draw | 0-21 % | shadow sprite drawn as zero runs (map dependent) -> **fast path** for its row loop (perf-shadow) |
| `0x5fc860` | draw | ~5 % | 8-bit indexed sprite through a palette -> **fast path** |
| `0x5fc540` | draw | ~2 % | 4-instruction setter called ~1 M times/s |

The three big draw functions and `0x51f110` are game logic over tile structures, not pixel loops; they only get
faster through the interpreter.

## Frame limiter (s3-dx `ddraw.rs`)

`WaitForVerticalBlank` releases `1000 / cap` ms after its previous release, or at once if the frame was already
late (no catch-up bursts). Cap default **60**; env `S3_FPS_CAP=N` (0 = no wait); API
`s3_dx::ddraw::set_fps_cap(fps)` / `fps_cap()` for frontends and the display settings (refresh-rate choice,
docs/porting/display.md). Rendering only: the logic thread's timer is unaffected, so the simulation speed does
not change with the fps. Above 60 fps the game draws identical logic states more often (it has no interpolation
except camera scrolling, which uses `timeGetTime`), so 60 is the sensible default; 90/120 only make scrolling
smoother and cost battery.

## Interpreter changes (s3-cpu, details in [cpu.md](cpu.md))

1. **Pre-decoded `Op` records** (`fast.rs`): handler pointer + next EIP, register numbers, displacement, immediate
   or branch target, and the effective-address form as a const generic (`[disp]`, `[base+disp]`,
   `[base+index*s+disp]`, `[index*s+disp]`). Handlers take `(cpu, mem, op)` and return `bool`; the exit of a failing
   handler goes to `Cpu::pending_exit`. The generic path reaches its `iced_x86::Instruction` through the `Op`
   (`Op::ins` then, `Op::set_ins` since perf-interp).
2. **Fault paths out of line** (`#[cold]`): the fast paths of the handlers no longer set up a stack frame.
3. **8/16-bit fast forms**: `mov` r/m/imm, ALU (`add/or/adc/sbb/and/sub/xor/cmp/test`) for 8/16/32-bit operands —
   the blitters are full of `mov cl,[eax]`, `test bl,bl`, `mov [eax],dx`.
4. **Lazy flags** (`flags.rs`, `Cpu::lk`): add/sub/cmp/logic/inc/dec store kind, operands and result; EFLAGS are
   computed only when read (`Cpu::eflags()`), `jcc` evaluates its condition straight from the lazy state
   (`cond_fast`), CF/AF/OF have cheap accessors. Exactness: unit test `lazy_conditions_match_materialised_flags`
   (all kinds x sizes x conditions x edge values) plus the host-CPU differential tests.
5. **Run loop**: no per-instruction EIP check or `cur_ip` store (only the last instruction of a block can branch),
   instruction count added per block, **block chaining** (each block caches its last two successors).
6. `[profile.release.package.s3-cpu] codegen-units = 1`.

Remaining per-instruction cost (callgrind, benchmark): ~11 host instructions of dispatch + the handler body.

### perf-interp (2026-11-07): threaded code, pointer chaining, superinstructions

Measured first (in game, HUD 2316x904, `S3_PROFILE` + a pair profile): blocks average **6.5 instructions**; the
generic path executes ~1.1 % of the instructions (`imul m32` 0.54 %, `shr r16,imm` 0.19 %, `imul r,r` 0.10 %,
`cdq` 0.05 %, ...) but each costs several times a fast handler; instruction pairs are diffuse (`mov r,m; mov r,m`
4.3 %, `push; push` 4.1 %, everything else < 2 %), so pair superinstructions in general buy little, while the
per-instruction loop (11 host instructions + call/return + frame) and the per-block loop (~50 host instructions with
stack spills, because `exec::step` was inlined into the run loop) were the real cost. Changes, in order:

7. **Tail-call threaded dispatch inside a block**: each handler ends by calling the next `Op`'s handler (`fast::next`,
   compiled to `ldr x8, [x2, #32]!; br x8`), a `block_end` sentinel ends the chain, control transfers return to the
   loop directly. No per-instruction EIP store (EIP is set once to `Block::end`; no non-branch instruction reads
   it). Fault exits record their `Op` (`Cpu::fault_op`) through cold tail-called functions, so hot handlers are
   frameless on Android. A block the budget ends inside runs instruction by instruction through `exec::step`
   (`run_partial`), keeping budget stops exact. bench 440 -> ~780 MIPS.
8. **Lean run loop**: decode/lookup slow path and the partial-block path out of line (the run loop no longer
   spills), unchecked arena access, instruction count derived from the remaining budget, one `special` byte test
   (hooked | native) per block.
9. **Fast forms for the generic leftovers**: `imul` (2/3/1-operand), `mul`, `cdq`, `cwde`, 8/16-bit shifts by imm and
   all shifts by CL, `setcc r8`, `neg/not r32`, `inc/dec m32` (now ~0.03 % generic).
10. **32-byte `Op`** (the generic path's `Instruction` pointer lives in the unused `disp`/`imm`), Block hot fields in
    one cache line (`repr(C, align(64))`). bench ~900 MIPS.
11. **Boxed blocks + pointer chaining**: successors are cached as block pointers (no index multiply / arena reload).
    In game 98.8 % of block entries hit the 2-entry successor cache. bench ~1130 MIPS.
12. **Superinstructions** `cmp/test (r,r | r,imm | m,imm) / dec r32` + the block-ending `jcc` (12 lazy conditions):
    fused at decode time, body = both handlers (~7.8 % of in-game instructions are such pairs). ~3 % in game.

**Results** (Windows 11 ARM64 dev PC, Snapdragon X2 Elite, power throttling off, see below):

| | perf-cpu (`f0a50f7`) | perf-interp |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bench_mips` (best of 5) | 440 MIPS | **1160 MIPS** |
| `s3det` 90 000 vms: time in `Cpu::run` | 16.6-18.8 s | **9.7-9.8 s** |
| `s3det` 90 000 vms: process CPU time | 20.4-23.2 s | **13.3-13.4 s** |
| `s3run` HUD 2316x904 uncapped, samples 50-80 s (random map, noisy) | 93-102 fps, draw thread 770-780 M instr/s | **126-190 fps** (3 runs), 1040-1230 M instr/s |

Determinism: `s3det` 90 000 vms old vs new CPU: **IDENTICAL** per-second hashes and `insns=11817005518`, also with a
stronger CPU hash that adds EFLAGS, FS base, the x87 last-IP and tag word (local s3det change for the check). The
native fast paths' differential tests (`s3-mods` `fast_tests`, real exe) pass.

**Benchmarking on the Windows ARM64 PC**: processes started from an agent shell run under Windows power throttling
(EcoQoS): 2-4x slower and very noisy (`bench_mips` 125-200 instead of 440 for the same binary, once 710 by chance).
Measure with throttling off: start the process, `SetProcessInformation(ProcessPowerThrottling,
{Version 1, ControlMask EXECUTION_SPEED|IGNORE_TIMER_RESOLUTION, StateMask 0})` on its handle and High priority (a
small PowerShell P/Invoke wrapper; the agent kept it in its scratchpad), and compare process CPU time or
`Cpu::run` time, not wall time, with alternating runs.

Notes for a later arm64 JIT (done since, see "perf-jit" below; kept for the reasoning): the per-block structure (exact retired counts per block, budget stop via
the generic path, native blocks entered only at block starts, hooks at block starts) carries over unchanged; a JIT
block can reuse the `Op` decode (EA forms, register numbers) and must keep the lazy-flag state layout
(`lk/la/lb/lr/lsz/lcf`) or materialise exactly like `flags.rs`; the `cmp_jcc` fusion shows the gain of folding
conditions into fresh operands. Next interpreter ideas: a return-address cache for `ret` (most of the 1.2 % L1
lookups), fusing `mov` + `mov` chains, passing the guest memory base in a register instead of `&GuestMemory`.
iOS forbids JIT, keep the interpreter as the base.

### perf-jit (2026-11-07): optional AArch64 JIT

Design and coverage: [cpu.md](cpu.md#jit-optional-aarch64-perf-jit-2026-11-07). Off by default (`S3_JIT=1`), cargo
feature `jit` (aarch64 only; iOS builds leave it out). In short: one compiled block per decoded block (same `n`),
guest registers in host registers, lazy flags in host registers inside a block and in the interpreter's format
between blocks, NULL-guard checks with side exits into the interpreter, per-instruction fallback to the
interpreter handler for the rest (x87, `rep` strings, `adc/sbb`), direct block links, an indirect-branch table and
native-fast-path stubs, so JIT code returns to the run loop only for thunks, budget ends and hooks.

Measured (Windows 11 ARM64 PC, throttling off; this PC was ~20 % slower in the afternoon than in the morning, so
only same-session pairs are compared):

| | interpreter | JIT |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bench_mips` (same session, 3 runs) | 1074-1176 MIPS | **3976-4777 MIPS** (one earlier run 6364) |
| `s3det` 90 000 vms, time in `Cpu::run` (`S3_CPU_TIME=1`, alternating runs, native fast paths on) | 6.87 / 6.93 / 9.56 s | **2.84 / 2.84 / 2.76 s** |
| same, process CPU time | 8.84-11.9 s | **4.72 s** |
| `s3det` with `S3_FAST=0` (pure guest code), time in `Cpu::run` (morning) | 13.68 s | **3.13 s** (4.4x) |
| `s3run` HUD 2316x904 zoom 10 uncapped, samples 50-80 s, random map | 356 / 248 fps, 708 / 720 ms/s in the CPU | **443 / 328 fps**, 580 / 541 ms/s |

`s3run` is now limited by host-side work (presentation, HLE): the guest CPU uses ~55-60 % of the engine thread
with the JIT. Per presented frame the CPU time fell from ~2.0-2.9 ms to ~1.3-1.65 ms.

JIT statistics for the 90 000 vms run (`s3det` prints them with the JIT on): 14 375 compiled blocks, 7.6 M JIT
entries (exits: 4.7 M budget ends at a compiled block, 2.6 M hooked/special, 0.15 M thunks, 0.05 M uncompiled), no
side exits and no failed fallbacks, 20.2 M fallback calls: x87 `fild m64` / `fistp m64` 7.7 M each and `fxch`
3.8 M, all from one 16-byte copy loop at `0x5c3e40` (`fild [esi]; fild [esi+8]; fxch; fistp [edi]; fistp
[edi+8]; add esi,16; add edi,16; loop`), then `rep movsd` 0.78 M. Natively translating that loop (or a native
fast path for it in s3-mods: the f64 round trip per qword has to be reproduced exactly, our x87 keeps f64, so
values above 2^53 are rounded; HYPOTHESIS: the game copies pixel/struct data with it, which then is not a bit copy
under emulation either) is the next cheap step.

Before/after the native fast paths: with the JIT, `S3_FAST=0` costs 3.13 s vs 2.25 s with fast paths in
`Cpu::run` (same session), so the fast paths still pay off; switching single paths off (`S3_FAST_OFF`) changed
the time by less than the run-to-run noise (±0.3 s), so no single path is clearly slower than JIT code.

## Native fast paths (s3-cpu `NativeBlock`, s3-mods `fast*.rs`)

A **native block** replaces a guest code region *inside the CPU* (no hook exit to the host, so it pays off even for
loops entered millions of times per second):

- s3-cpu: `NativeFn = fn(&mut Cpu, &mut GuestMemory, budget) -> Option<u64>`; `NativeBlock { name, len, hash, f }`;
  `Cpu::set_native_blocks`. When a block is decoded at a registered address and `code_hash` (FNV-1a 64) of the
  next `len` bytes matches, the block gets the native function. At block entry the CPU calls it with the remaining
  instruction budget; `None` = decline (the original code runs), `Some(k)` = it did exactly what `k` guest
  instructions would have done.
- s3-runtime: `Machine::set_native_blocks` (also given to threads created later).
- s3-mods: `fast.rs` registers the GOG blocks (`gog_blocks()`) after the hooks are committed (a region containing a
  hook is skipped); env **`S3_FAST=0`** disables all. Our sources contain only addresses, lengths and hashes, never
  game bytes (`tools/perf/code_hash.py S3.EXE start end` prints them).

**Contract** (what keeps lockstep MP and `s3det` hashes intact): registers, EFLAGS (as the original's last flag
writer leaves them, via `Cpu::alu_sub` etc.), EIP, every memory byte and the retired-instruction count must equal
the original code's at the point where the native code stops. Stop only at a point the original passes through
(loop head or exit), run whole iterations within the budget (so thread switches happen at the same instruction
counts as without fast paths), and decline whenever the original could fault (NULL guard), not terminate normally,
or when its writes overlap what it reads.

| Name | Region | Original loop | Instructions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sprite_rows` | `0x5fc4c0..0x5fc536` | opaque RLE rows of the 16-bit sprite blitter `0x5fc350` (whole rows: run headers, dword copies, odd pixel, row advance, `cmp edi,[esp+0x98]`) | 15/run + 6/dword + 2 (+4 odd) + 4, + 9/row |
| `palette_row` | `0x5fc93d..0x5fc952` | 8-bit -> 16-bit through a palette (`0x5fc860`) | 8/pixel |
| `darken` | `0x5fd0ea..0x5fd0ff` | `[eax] = ([eax] >> 1) & [0x7e8dec]` per dword | 8/dword |
| `dither` | `0x5fd096..0x5fd0ae` | checkerboard shadow in `0x5fd080` | 8 or 9/pixel |
| `snap_tiles` | `0x522219..0x52303e` | logic thread, render snapshot fill (`0x51f110`): copy one map tile into its snapshot cell per iteration (`fast_snap.rs`). Common path only: tile inside the map, `[gd+0x2d284] != 1`, not the special row `[gd+0x2d2e4]`, byte +0xb != `[gd+0x2d300]`, light byte with equal 3-bit fields and bit 7 clear, no object words, no flag 0x20; else stops at the loop head before that tile | 133/tile |
| `obj_empty` | `0x4d3050..0x4d5a4f` (+ setter `0x5fc540`, hash-checked at each call) | draw thread, per-tile object drawer called by `0x4b26c0` for every tile: the whole call (prologue, four setter calls, type-compare chain, epilogue, `ret 0x18`) for object type 0 when nothing is drawn (`fast_obj.rs`) | 110-116/call |
| `land_clean` | `0x54ce53..0x54e712` | draw thread, landscape pass `0x54cbd0`: triangle loop for clean triangles (no dirty corner bit, flags `[ebp-0x68]/[ebp-0xe4]/[ebp-0xe8]` != 1) - corner heights, min y into `[ebp-0x34]`, phase flip (`fast_land.rs`) | 60-66/triangle |
| `land_rows` | `0x54e4bc..0x54e6e8` | draw thread, landscape pass `0x54cbd0`: row loop of the dirty-triangle rasteriser (edge/u/v/light stepping, per-span `idiv` steps, textured + shaded 16-bit pixels, ring-buffer row wrap, half switch); stops at the row head or the exit (`fast_land_rows.rs`, perf-landfull) | per row 35, then 12 (empty span) or 35 + 44/pixel, then 8-31; exit 3 |
| `frame_tiles` | `0x4b2e44..0x4b330e` (+ row head `0x4b2e30..0x4b2e44` and the 24 instruction ranges of `0x4d3050`'s empty case, hash-checked at entry) | draw thread, frame renderer `0x4b26c0`: the cell loop over the snapshot (x/40 sector, ambient-sound statistics `[ebx+0x5f588/0x5f5cc]`, 4x4 water-decoration grid test, `+0x508` kind checks, the object call `0x4d3050` inlined for the `obj_empty` case via `fast_obj::plan/apply`) and the row advance (`fast_tile.rs`). Stops at the loop head before a cell with weighted water/shore sound (`0x4b2f0e`), decoration (`0x4b3046`), object type != 0 (incl. 0xfe), `+0x50a`/`+0x51e` != 0, `+0x508` kind 0x800/0x1000/0x1800 or a non-empty `0x4d3050` call | ~200/cell (incl. the call) |
| `land_mark` | `0x4b277e..0x4b27a7` | draw thread, pre-pass of `0x4b26c0` over one snapshot column: landscape byte `+0x502` to 0x1c / back to 0x10 by bit 2 of `+0x509` for cells with `(+0x505 & 0x3f)*4 <= 0x48` (`fast_tile.rs`) | 8-13/cell |

**Verification**
- Differential unit test `cargo test -p s3-mods fast_tests` (needs the local S3.EXE; skipped otherwise): maps the
  exe's sections into guest memory, 120 random cases per fast path (random RLE sprites, pitches incl. odd ones,
  palettes, masks, register values, small budgets for partial stops), runs the native function, then the
  interpreter for exactly the returned instruction count, and compares registers, EFLAGS, EIP and 5 MiB of memory
  byte for byte. It caught one bug (EBX after a budget stop in `dither`).
- Whole game: `s3det` 90 000 virtual ms (menu, random map, in game, build menu, place, cancel) with `S3_FAST=0` vs
  default: identical per-second memory/CPU hashes and instruction counts (`scratch/perf/det5`).
- The interpreter rework itself: `s3det` old CPU vs new CPU on the same code: identical for 90 000 vms
  (`insns=11897551127`, `scratch/perf/det3`).

verify-fps1 (2026-11-05) added `snap_tiles`, `obj_empty`, `land_clean`: each has a differential test against the real
exe (`differential_snap_tiles`, `differential_obj_empty`, `differential_land_clean`: random cells / frames /
budgets, compare registers, EFLAGS, EIP and memory); `s3det` 90 000 vms with all fast paths vs `S3_FAST=0`:
IDENTICAL (`insns=11817005518`, `scratch/vfps/det`); live two-instance MP with zoom pinches: IDENTICAL
(`scratch/vfps/mp`). Profile after them (HUD, 2316x904): `0x4b26c0` frame renderer tile loop **46 %** (~98
instructions per tile, branchy: ambient-sound statistics, tree/decoration checks, three call sites of `0x4d3050`),
`0x5fd080`/`0x5fd120` shadow sprites 17 %, `0x4d3050` (non-empty tiles) 7 %, `0x5fc860` 4.5 %. The frame renderer
loop is the next target for the HUD default to hold 60.

perf-shadow (2026-11-07) added the run/row loops of the two shadow sprite functions (`fast_shadow.rs`), each
including the per-run call through a function pointer (callee hash-checked, emulated with every stack write of the
call and its pushes, so memory below ESP is identical too):

| Name | Region (entries) | Original loop | Instructions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shadow_zero` | `0x5fc2cd..0x5fc346` (row head `0x5fc2cd`, run head `0x5fc2d4`) | second row loop of `0x5fc160`: per run `(count, skip\|last)`, `call [0x7e8c74]` = `0x5f48e0` zeroes `count>>1` dwords + 1 word if `count&1`, source cursor skips the pixel bytes | 38/run + 5/dword + 3 (odd), 9/row end, 1/row head |
| `shadow_rows` | `0x5fd24f..0x5fd301` (`0x5fd24f`, row head `0x5fd256`, run head `0x5fd25d`) | row loop of `0x5fd120`: per run `call [0x7e8e20]` = `0x5fd080` (checkerboard, phase `[esp+0x90]`, row phase ESI) or `0x5fd0c0` (darken with masks `[0x7e8dd8]` word / `[0x7e8dec]` dword); row end: ESI = (ESI+1) C-mod 32 | 25/run + callee (`0x5fd080`: 11 empty, else 18 + 8/pixel + 1/cleared pixel; `0x5fd0c0`: 4 empty, else 17 (+6 head word, +6 tail word, +2+8/dword)), 15 or 18/row end, 1/row head |

Each native function dispatches on the entry EIP (a hash covers entry..exit; the row-head instruction that the run
head entry's hash does not cover is hashed separately before it runs), stops at a run head, row head or the exit,
and stops before a run that could fault, would not terminate (odd distance, wrap), writes into the stack frame or the
darken dword mask, or whose function pointer is not the known callee. The first loop of `0x5fc160` (`[0x7e8c70]`)
and the masked (fog) loop `0x5fc41a..0x5fc4af` of `0x5fc350` were not executed in the in-game profile and are not
covered. Tests: `differential_shadow_zero` (300 cases, 288 native), `differential_shadow_rows` (400 cases, dither
198 / darken 176 native; random/negative phases, odd destinations, wrong function pointers, budgets 1..800); a
deliberately wrong cost or pushed EBX fails them.

Profile (HUD, 2316x904, random map, from 60 s; native blocks count with their decoded length): before
`0x4b26c0` 45 %, `0x5fc160` 11.9 % + its callee `0x5f48e0` (attributed to `0x5f4830`) 9.0 %, `0x5fd120` 3.9 % +
`0x5fd080`/`0x5fd0c0` 3.7 %; after `0x4b26c0` 63 %, `0x5fc160` 1.5 %, `0x5fd120` 0.8 % (callees no longer
listed). The frame renderer `0x4b26c0` is now by far the main cost.

Ideas for more fast paths: the masked (fog) sprite loop `0x5fc41a..0x5fc4af` (when it shows up in a profile),
`0x5fc540` (could be inlined at its call sites as a superinstruction).
perf-tile (2026-11-07) added `frame_tiles` and `land_mark` (`fast_tile.rs`) for that loop. How `frame_tiles` covers
code outside its registered region: the row head `0x4b2e30..0x4b2e44` and the instructions of `0x4d3050`'s empty
case (24 ranges, 413 bytes, traced; test `obj_empty_path_hashed` checks that every executed instruction lies in
them) are FNV-hashed before the first change of each entry (`tools/perf/code_hash.py --concat`); `fast.rs`
`extra_ranges` disables it when a hook lies in that code (the hook must run). The inlined call reuses
`fast_obj::plan` (pure checks) and `fast_obj::apply` (stack writes, registers, `ret 0x18`), so both stay in step.
About 2 % of the cells end a native run (most: object type 0xfe, decoration grid, border cells with `+0x51e`);
the interpreter runs that cell and the next jump to the loop head enters the native path again.
Results (desktop ARM64, HUD, `--window 2316x904`, `S3_FPS_CAP=0`, random map, noisy shared PC):
- guest profile (`S3_PROFILE`, 60-80 s): `0x4b26c0` **41.9 % -> 6.2 %**; now on top: `0x5fd080` / `0x5fd120`
  shadow sprites 20 % each, `0x5fc860` 10 %, `0x51f110` 3 %, `0x4d3050` (non-empty) 3 %;
- fps (mean of the samples 60-80 s, two alternating runs each): before 28.9 / 35.0, after **41.0 / 46.5**
  (under the profiler 26-34 -> 47-56);
- `s3det` 90 000 vms: all fast paths vs `S3_FAST=0` and vs `S3_FAST_OFF=frame_tiles,land_mark`: IDENTICAL
  (`insns=11817005518`, `mem=4ca80f23bf398314`), wall time (two runs in parallel) 64 s -> 47 s.
Env **`S3_FAST_OFF=name,name`** leaves single fast paths out (bisecting a divergence, measuring one path).

Ideas for more fast paths: the masked (fog) sprite loop `0x5fc41a..0x5fc4af`, the run loop of `0x5fd120`
(calls through `[0x7e8e20]`), `0x5fc540` (could be inlined at its call sites as a superinstruction).

### perf-landfull (2026-11-08): dirty-triangle rasteriser rows (`land_rows`)

Pinch zoom stuttered on every step that grows the view: the next frame is a full landscape redraw (all triangles
dirty, `snap+0xc/+0x10` = 10 000 000, resolution-zoom.md). Profile while pinching out (HUD 2316x904, `S3_PROFILE`
from 64 s, 3 s, JIT off): landscape pass 428 M of 565 M guest instructions; inside it the pixel loop
`0x54e593..0x54e620` 321 M (44 instructions per pixel: two C-style `/256`, texel `tex[(u/256)*16 + v/256]`, shade
word `[[obj+0xa4] + 2*(texel*128 + light/256)]`), the rest of the row loop 74 M (edge stepping, three `idiv` per
span, row wrap), per-triangle setup `0x54d015..0x54e4bc` (texture choice, slopes) 20 M, triangle loop 12.5 M.
(REA's "Catch@0054d382" is a function start in its list only; the profiler attributes everything up to `0x54e7d0`
to it.) The average span is ~8 pixels, ~9.5 rows per triangle.

`land_rows` (`fast_land_rows.rs`) runs whole rows from the row head `0x54e4bc` to the next row head or the exit
`0x54e6e8`: frame slots are re-read per row, the row's pixels go into a buffer and are written at the row's commit.
A row whose texel/shade reads overlap its destination span or the stack frame, whose destination overlaps the frame
or `[obj+0x54]`/`[obj+0xa4]`, that could fault, is wider than 2048 pixels or exceeds the budget ends the run at
its row head. Flags at the row head: the last CF writer (`cmp esi,-1`, `neg eax` of the wrap, `cmp eax,2/3` of the
half switch) then `dec`; at the exit `test eax,eax`. Test `differential_land_rows` (600 cases, 564 native,
coverage counters for every branch: empty/pixel spans, both wraps, half switch 2/3/other, aliasing stops, budget
stops, exit); a wrong CF source fails it.
Determinism: `s3det` 90 000 vms (inject of `tools/determinism-test.sh`) all fast paths vs `S3_FAST=0` vs
`S3_FAST_OFF=land_rows`, and `S3_JIT=1` with and without fast paths: all **IDENTICAL** (91 hash lines,
`insns=12110861573`, `mem=f258db2c1e42db16`; a temporary counter confirmed that `land_rows` runs in that workload).

Results (desktop ARM64, `tools/perf/fast.ps1`, HUD `--window 2316x904`, cap 60, the pinch-out inject of the task;
time of the frame after each size switch 920x360 -> ... -> 2000x780; random map per run, so noisy):

| | JIT off | `S3_JIT=1` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before (f71f349) | 37 / 56 / 57 / 86 / 108 / 115 / 117 ms (earlier run 27-102) | 18 / 44 / 29 / 14 / 17 / 20 / 21 ms |
| after | **23 / 17 / 26 / 28 / 33 / 42 / 20 ms** | **16 / 16 / 16 / 17 / 17 / 14 / 15 ms** (at the 60 cap) |

Profile of the same 3 s after: 565 M -> 249 M guest instructions, landscape 428 M -> 37 M (pixel + row loop
395 M -> 1.4 M left in the interpreter, the per-triangle setup 22.6 M and triangle loop 12.6 M remain). Now on top:
`0x5fc860` 9.6 %, `0x5f4f20` 8.7 %, `0x54cbd0` 8.3 % (triangle loop + setup), `0x5fc160` 6.9 %. Next candidate if
the phone still stutters: the per-triangle setup `0x54d015..0x54e4bc` (~200 instructions per dirty triangle, very
branchy texture-pair selection) and the dirty-triangle path of the triangle loop head (`land_clean` declines it).

## Profiling tools

- `S3_SAMPLE=1 s3run ...`: per second `fps:N cpu:Mms` (presents, host ms inside the interpreter) and per-thread
  millions of instructions. The run summary lists per-thread `Cpu::run` time and M instr/s (perf-mt).
- `S3_HOST_PROF=1 s3run ...` (perf-mt): host time per HLE handler, hook and service plus named sections (ddraw
  blits, primary conversion, overlay compose, cursor + `Host::present`) in the run summary
  (`Stats::host_prof_start/host_prof_section` to add sections). Fps comparisons on random maps are noisy (the map
  changes per run); `tools/perf/fps-bench.ps1` (Windows, throttling off through `tools/perf/fast.ps1`) picks the fixed map Artokia.
- `S3_PROFILE=<file> [S3_PROFILE_FROM_MS=<ms>] s3run ...`: at exit writes per-thread decoded-block entry counts
  (`<file>`), the 60 hottest blocks per thread disassembled with generic-path instructions marked `*`
  (`<file>.disasm`) and the executed instruction forms weighted by count (`<file>.forms`).
  `python3 -I tools/perf_profile.py <file> scratch/perf/funcs.txt` aggregates by function (function starts
  exported from REA `list_procedures`; keep that list in `scratch/`, it is derived from the exe).
  Native blocks are counted with their decoded length per entry (approximate).
  `DecodeCache::profile_pairs()` (perf-interp) returns adjacent instruction-form pairs weighted by block entries plus
  the total block entries (`#blocks`, for the average block length); s3run does not write it yet (a local
  `.pairs` output was used for the measurements above).
- Host side: `valgrind --tool=callgrind --instr-atstart=no` on `s3det`, then `callgrind_control -i on` once the
  wanted virtual time is reached (watch the hash file); the run before that costs only ~5x.
- Deterministic benchmark: `s3det --vms 90000` wall time with the inject script of `tools/determinism-test.sh`.

## Measurements 2026-11-07 (perf review)

Phone (Fold4 cover, HUD, Native wide, **zoom level 10 = 1944x760**, cap 60): **50-56 fps**. simpleperf 8 s
(`su`, 4 kHz): `s3-engine` 86 % libs3android + 5 % libc, `s3-present` ~6 %. Inside s3-engine (share of the thread):

| Host symbol | % | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Cpu::run` (dispatch + inlined handlers) | 28.7 | interpreter core |
| `fast::mov_rm<4,1>`, `mov_mr<4,1>`, `push_r`, `generic`, ... | ~35 | handlers (`generic` = iced fallback 2.8 %) |
| `__memmove_aarch64_simd` | 5.5 | frame copies: guest surface -> `FrameBuffer` -> overlay copy -> `Shared` -> presenter local -> GL |
| `s3_dx::blit::to_framebuffer_into` | 5.2 | per-pixel `u16::from_le_bytes` loop for RGB565 (could be one memcpy per row) |
| `s3_mods::overlay::Canvas::rounded` + `fill_rect` | 5.7 | HUD bar/cards redrawn in software every frame |
| fast paths (`obj_empty`, `sprite_rows`, `snap_tiles`, `land_clean`, `darken`) | ~5.6 | native code |

So ~17 % of the engine thread is host-side presentation work, not guest code.

Desktop (Windows 11 ARM64 laptop, headless, 2316x904, HUD, `S3_FPS_CAP=0`): zoom 10: 33-35 fps, zoom 6: 40-44 fps,
`S3_FAST=0`: 13 fps (guest ~140 M instr/s: this ARM64 host's interpreter is slower than the old x86_64 desktop).
Guest profile (zoom 10, in game): `0x4b26c0` frame renderer tile loop **42.5 %**, shadow sprites `0x5fd120` 7.8 % +
`0x5fd080` 7.7 %, `0x4d3050` 5.8 %, `0x5fc860` 4.5 %, `0x5fc160` 4.2 %, `0x5f4830`/`0x5f5400` 2.8 % each; logic
thread `t5` ~20 % of the guest instructions.

Ranked ideas (estimated gain on the phone at zoom 10):
1. Fast path for the `0x4b26c0` tile loop (42 % of guest work): +20-35 %. Medium/large (branchy; differential test
   like the others).
2. Host presentation work (~17 %): RGB565 row memcpy in `to_framebuffer_into`; fewer frame copies (hand buffers
   over instead of copy_from_slice twice); HUD drawn into a cached RGBA layer that is re-rendered only when it
   changes and composited by the GPU as a second texture: +10-15 %. Small/medium, no determinism risk.
3. CPU clock: the engine thread runs at ~2 GHz avg of the prime core's 3.19 GHz. `APerformanceHint` (NDK, API 33+)
   session for the engine thread with a 16.6 ms target may let the governor boost (HYPOTHESIS, untested;
   `taskset` alone gave ~5 %). Small effort, possibly large gain.
4. Shadow sprites `0x5fd120` / `0x5fd080` outer loops (15 %): +5-10 %.
5. Interpreter: superinstructions (`cmp/test+jcc`, `mov+mov`), smaller `Op`; +10-20 %, medium.
6. arm64 JIT (Android only, iOS forbids JIT): 2-4x guest speed, large effort. **Done (perf-jit, optional,
   `S3_JIT=1`)**: 4.4x on pure guest code, 2.4x of `Cpu::run` time with fast paths, see "perf-jit" above.
7. Draw and logic threads on separate host cores: large refactor (single-threaded machine).
8. Lower default zoom (6 instead of 10 = 1536x600): immediate ~+25 %, but a UX choice.

### Done in perf-r2 (2026-11-07)

- **Item 3, CPU hint** (`s3-frontend/src/perf_hint.rs`): `APerformanceHint` session for the engine thread (dlsym,
  API 33+), reports engine-thread CPU time per presented frame against `1000 / cap` ms. On the Fold4 it does
  nothing: `adb shell dumpsys performance_hint` says `HintSessionPreferredRate: -1`, `HAL Support: false`, and
  `createSession` returns NULL (logged "perf hint: session 0x0"). Kept for devices with the HAL (Pixel etc.).
- **Item 2, host presentation**: RGB565 rows copied with one `memcpy` (`s3_dx::blit::to_framebuffer_into`);
  `Canvas::rounded` computes the distance field only in corner rows / edge columns and fills the rest as spans
  (pixel-identical, test `rounded_spans_match_per_pixel_reference`), opaque spans are plain fills; the cursor keeps
  only the pixels under it instead of a second full frame; `Machine::present_owned` takes the frame from ddraw by
  value (no "last guest frame" copy) and `present_cursor_owned` hands the overlay output to the cursor state without
  a copy; the Android presenter swaps buffers with the frame slot. Per frame: 1 conversion + 6 full copies -> 1
  memcpy + 2 copies (overlay working copy, host slot). Phone simpleperf: host presentation work ~17 % -> ~10 % of
  the engine thread.

### Phone after perf-r2 items 1-5 (2026-11-07, commit e8042b2)

Fold4 cover, HUD, Native wide, zoom 10 (1944x760), cap 60: **60 fps in all 5 samples** (before: 48-56). Engine
thread at **70 %** of one core (`top -H`; before 94-99 % while missing 60), presenter 13 %. So roughly 40 % headroom
at the cap (~85 fps worth of work), enough for higher zoom levels or a 90 Hz cap.

After the JIT + multi-core merges (135a0e6), same setup: interpreter (`jit.txt` = 0) 58-60 fps, engine thread
78.6 %; JIT (`jit.txt` = 1) 60 fps, engine thread 73.6 % (random maps, 1 sample each). At the 60 cap the JIT saves
only ~5 % of a core on the phone: guest code is no longer the main cost; host-side work (overlay/HUD compose, blits,
HLE) is (see multicore.md, option B).

## Window overlay layer (2026-11-08, overlay-window)

The mods' UI moved out of the guest frame into a window-resolution layer ([mods.md](mods.md) "Window layer"): on the
engine thread only a display list is recorded (and published when it changed); rasterizing happens on the frontend
(Android render thread). Desktop Windows ARM64, headless `--window 2316x904`, HUD + detailed FPS counter, 1536x600,
`S3_FPS_CAP=0`, EcoQoS off (`tools/perf/fast.ps1`), `S3_HOST_PROF=1`, median of 1 s samples 55-84 s (random map,
one run each, `scratch/overlay-window/fps/`):

| Build | fps | overlay per present (engine thread) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before (frame copy + compose into the frame) | 374 | 0.375 ms |
| window layer (record + compare) | **536** | 0.014 ms (+ cursor/`Host::present` 0.06 ms) |

On the phone the rasterization cost moves to the `s3-present` thread and only when the list changed (changed
rectangle only; upload of the changed rows). HYPOTHESIS: phone gain smaller than desktop (the engine thread there was
~2.9 ms/frame of which ~0.5 ms overlay), not measured yet.

## Not done / next

- Multi-core: see [multicore.md](multicore.md) (perf-mt, 2026-11-07). The draw thread on its own host thread
  (`S3_MT=1`, experimental) works but gives no reliable gain: the logic thread is only ~15 % of a frame and the HUD
  overlay compose (0.48 ms of ~2.9 ms per frame at 1944x760) runs under the one HLE lock. Next: overlay display list
  rasterised outside the machine / on a presenter thread (also +15-20 % in the default mode).
- ~~Measure on the phone~~: done (verify-fps1, table above). Phone profiling recipe: `adb shell su -c "simpleperf
  record -p PID -f 4000 --duration 8 -o /data/local/tmp/s3perf.data"`, pull, `simpleperf report --sort
  vaddr_in_file` (NDK `simpleperf/bin/linux/x86_64`) and symbolize the addresses with `llvm-symbolizer
  --obj=port/target/aarch64-linux-android/release/libs3android.so` (the .so in the APK is stripped).
- ~~Next fast path: the `0x4b26c0` tile loop~~: done (perf-tile). Next: the shadow sprite run loops `0x5fd080` /
  `0x5fd120` (40 % of the profile after perf-tile) and `0x5fc860`; measure the HUD default on the phone again.
