`docs/porting/resolution-zoom.md`:

```md
# Custom resolutions and zoom (res-zoom)

Status: implemented 2026-11-05 (agent `res-zoom`), desktop-verified (`s3run`, screenshots read), MP two-peer hash
IDENTICAL with different zoom levels per peer. Not yet tried on the phone (Verify phase).
**overlay-window (2026-11-08)**: mod UI moved to a window-resolution layer (constant size at every zoom), so the
minimum went down to **200** px high (levels 200 and 240 added; `res::MIN_H` 200); UI mode A shows its panel at a
constant scale with a matching render width ([display.md](display.md) "Classic panel at a constant size").
**res-tall (2026-11-08)**: maximum raised from 2560x780 to **3200x1200** (row stride of the snapshot grid patched, sprite
lists enlarged), see "Taller views (res-tall)" below.

Goal (user feedback 2026-11-05): use the whole phone screen like Settlers United (no 4:3 letterbox) and zoom in the
game (pinch, both UI modes, independent of the HUD). The original GOG S3.EXE only knows 640x480, 800x600 and
1024x768 (F1-F3). The port now runs the game at **any size from 480x360 up to 3200x1200** (width a multiple of 8) and
uses the render size as the zoom: a smaller size shows less map with bigger pixels, the frontend scales the frame
to the screen.

Code: `port/crates/s3-mods/src/res.rs` (game patch + switch), `zoom.rs` (levels, pinch, settings), ddraw port
extension in `port/crates/s3-dx/src/ddraw.rs` (`DDSDM_PORT_LOGICAL`), Classic menu buttons in `ui_classic.rs`,
pinch hook in `touch.rs`. RE details: [game-state-ui.md](../reverse-engineering/game-state-ui.md) section
"Resolution internals". Display modes / `Viewport`: [display.md](display.md).

## What the player gets

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Zoom levels | 18 render heights: 360, 400, 440, 480, 520, 560, 600 (default), 640, 680, 720, 760, 780, 840, 900, 960, 1040, 1120, 1200 (the last six since res-tall; phone 2316x904: up to 3072x1200). Width = height x window aspect (display mode "Native wide", "Fill", "Stretch"; 4:3 in "Fit"). Phone cover screen 2229x904: 888x360 ... 1480x600 (default) ... 1776x720 ... 1920x780. 4:3: 640x480, 800x600 = the game's own sizes |
| Pinch | both UI modes, continuous: fingers apart = zoom in (one level per factor 1.12 of finger distance), the map point under the fingers stays in place. One switch at a time (the next one when the game finished the previous one, at least 120 ms apart); the final level is saved at the end of the pinch |
| Menu | Classic Touch: Menu -> "Zoom in (n/12)" / "Zoom out (n/12)". Mobile HUD: API for the HUD menu (`zoom::zoom_in/zoom_out/label`), wiring is hud-polish's |
| Persisted | `mods-settings.json` `"res": {"enabled": true, "zoom_level": 6}`; `enabled: false` = the game's own sizes (F1-F3 work again) |
| Mode A minimum | 200 with the panel split (`NativeWide`): below 480 the frame stays 480 high (the panel art needs it) and the map part is cropped, `zoom::classic_crop` / `PanelSplit::crop_h` (2026-11-08; same map pixels as a smaller render, and instant). Without the split (Fit etc.) 480, levels 0-6 skipped |

**Start zoom (2026-11-08).** A new or loaded game no longer starts at the last game's zoom: after 3 s without a
game frame (menus), `ZoomMod` sets the in-memory zoom height to `zoom::start_height` = the height that shows the
whole start territory (`START_AREA` 1250 x 850 game px, measured border ~1130 x 800 on random 384 maps; Mobile HUD
bars ~15 % of the height, Classic panel ~12 % of the width), so the first game frame already uses it; the game
centres the camera on the castle. Pinching afterwards works as before (and is saved). Fold4 cover: 2560x1000,
inner screen: 1248x1040 (VERIFIED desktop + phone: border fully visible).

Panel at custom sizes: the panel art, minimap and panel button grid of the largest original layout whose height
fits ("variant": < 600 -> 640x480 art, < 768 -> 800x600 art, else 1024x768 art); the map view takes the rest of the
width. Below the panel art (heights between the variants) the area stays black. **UI mode A uses the 640x480
variant at every size** (`res::CLASSIC_VARIANT`, since 2026-11-08): switching the art at 600 / 768 made the panel
jump on screen while pinching ([display.md](display.md) "Classic panel at a constant size").

## Why the limits (the render snapshot grid)

The logic thread copies the visible tiles into a **render snapshot** (`[logic+0x3d0]`, allocated once by `0x51f110`
with `new(0xc7720)`, ctor `0x523480`): a grid of 130 rows x 130 columns at `snap+0x500`, 0x30 bytes per tile, index
`row + col*130` (`0x52240f`, `0x522f66`). The view needs `cols = (mapW+23)/16 + 10` and `rows = (mapH+255)/9 + 11`
(`0x51f990..0x51fab4`, stored at `snap+0x30/+0x34`), and because map rows are sheared the column index runs up to
`cols + rows/2` (+3 for neighbour reads). 1024x768 already needs 126 of the 130 columns; a wide phone frame would
write far past the grid into the fields behind it. The row stride (130) is a constant in many instructions
(displacements like `+0x1860` = one column, `+0x30` = one row), so res-zoom kept it: **height <= 780**
(`rows + 3 <= 129`). res-tall changed it to 258 (below).
The columns are cheap to extend: only the fields **behind** the grid (`snap+0xc65c0..0xc7720`: message lines, chat,
tooltip/object lists) are addressed with absolute offsets, at 51 code sites (snapshot dtor `0x405a50`, frame renderer
`0x4b3314..0x4b34a2`, panel `0x4c245e`, message lines `0x4d82fc..0x4d85b2`, fill `0x51f88c..0x51f98a`, ctor
`0x5234aa..0x523502`, unwind funclets `0x62f43c/0x62f44b`) plus the allocation size `push 0xc7720` (`0x51f16b`).
`res::patch_snapshot` adds `(256-130)*0x1860` to each (checked against the original bytes first): the grid gets
**256 columns** (2560x780 needs 237). Site list generator: `tools/res-zoom/snap_sites.py S3.EXE scratch/re-ui/s3.asm`
(objdump listing + exe bytes, reads the exe as data). The patch is applied with every GOG patch set (also when the
zoom is off) so all peers have the same heap layout.

Other fixed-size things checked: the on-screen hit list caps at 10000 entries (`0x4d8240`), the sprite lists at
4000/8000 entries with 250 row buckets (`0x4d7c90`, `0x4d7e10`; CORRECTED by res-tall: the bucket is `2*row` of the
snapshot, so 250 buckets only reach row 124 - at 780 the objects of the last row were already dropped; now 360
buckets). The frame renderer's
ambient-sound statistics only look at the left 640 px (`local_1c/0x28 < 16`, `< 0x259`), harmless. The text DIB
(`0x4a78f0`, 1 bpp) and the landscape ring buffer (`0x54bec0`) are made `MAX_W x MAX_H` (+ margins `[0x730f44]` = 32,
`[0x730f48]` = 102) by hooks, so no size ever overflows them.

## Taller views (res-tall, 2026-11-08)

Max size now **3200x1200** (`res::MAX_W/MAX_H`; zoom levels up to 1200 high). All in `res::code_patches()`, applied
by `res::patch_snapshot` with every GOG patch set (all-or-nothing check of the original bytes first):

| What | Change | Sites |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Snapshot grid row stride | 130 -> **258** (`res::SNAP_ROWS`). The index `row + col*130` is always compiled as `mov r,col; shl r,6; add r,col; lea x,[row+r*2]`; `shl r,7` makes it `col*258` with the same instruction length | 10 `shl` imm8 6 -> 7 (`STRIDE_SHL_SITES`): `0x4a99c5` (object drawer `0x4a9960`), `0x4b2e7a`, `0x4b2fa3` (frame renderer), `0x4c8603` (settler drawer `0x4c85a0`), `0x4d309a` (`0x4d3050`), `0x4d5a95` (`0x4d5a50`), `0x52240f`, `0x522f66` (fill), `0x54ce80`, `0x54cef8` (rasteriser) |
| Column steps / neighbours | `n*0x1860` -> `n*0x3060` in displacements and immediates; `3*130`, `130` -> `3*258`, `258` | 30 `STRIDE_DISP_SITES` (renderer pre-pass `add eax,0x1860` `0x4b279f`, renderer neighbours `+0x4eb2`/`+0x4e22` `0x4b2ff6`/`0x4b3003`, the 6-direction neighbour heights of `0x4c85a0` (`-0x1360`, `-0x1390`, `+0x1d60`, `+0x1d90`, three copies), 15 next-column corner reads of the rasteriser `0x54ce95..0x54d347`), 2 `STRIDE_INDEX_SITES` (`0x4b275b`, `0x4b27af`) |
| Grid columns | 256 -> **320** (`SNAP_COLS`; 3200x1200 needs 300) | tail move as before; 4 tail sites the generator had missed: `0x51f1f8` `mov eax,0xc636c` (= tail `0xc65c0` minus the logic-object offset `0x254` it is added to later) and the fill's unwind funclets `0x642cdc/0x642ceb/0x642d02` (above the generator's `0x630000` limit) |
| Sprite lists | bucket = `2*row` (+-2) of the snapshot row, the game has 250 buckets (rows >= 125 were not drawn). The six bucket arrays (heads / counts of lists 1-3 at `gfx+0x13a8c, 0x13e74, 0x4ad60, 0x4b148, 0x5edb4, 0x5f19c`) move behind the `gfx` object, **360 buckets** (`SPRITE_BUCKETS`, needs `2*rows+4`) | 62 array references, bounds `cmp ...,0xfa` (6 inserts `0x4d7c90..0x4d8184`, init `0x4b2d6c`, draw loops `0x4b34d3`, `0x4b3565`), first free node `0xfa`/`0xfb` (`0x4b2da7/b1/bb`: nodes 0..249 are the bucket tails), allocation `push 0x5f700` (`0x42c6b9`) + 6*360*4 |

How the sites were found: a temporary memory-access trace in the interpreter (effective address of every load/store
inside the three snapshot buffers, per instruction; branch commit `0956d16`, removed again) listed the 210
instructions that touch the grid in a HUD game (7 functions), then each function was reviewed completely in the
objdump listing (`tools/res-tall/x130.py` finds the `x130` idiom, `stride_scan.py` candidate constants, `sites.py` the
byte offsets). There are **three** snapshots (the logic fills one while the renderer draws another), all from the one
allocation site. Fixed-size things re-checked for big views: hit list 10000 (`0x7ade12`, full = objects not clickable),
sprite node pools 4000/8000/4000 (full = sprites dropped; `S3_RES_TRACE` prints the fill level every 300 frames:
3072x1200 HUD start scene 728/751/627 nodes, 22 hits), the snapshot's per-player arrays (`snap+0x294..0x2e4`, not
per row), text DIB and landscape buffer (hooks, follow `MAX_*`). The native fast paths (`fast_land/obj/snap/tile.rs`)
use `res::SNAP_ROWS` and hash the *patched* code (`fast_tests::fast_path_hashes_match_patched_code`; the
differential tests load the patched code via `res::apply_code_patches`).

FPS (desktop Windows ARM64, HUD, window 2316x904, `S3_RES` forced, `S3_FPS_CAP=0`, EcoQoS off via
`tools/perf/fast.ps1`, native fast paths on, no JIT, random-map start scene, median of samples 62-85 s;
`tools/res-tall/fps_sizes.ps1`):

| Render size | Pixels | fps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1536x600 (default level on the phone) | 0.92 M | 440 |
| 2000x780 (old max) | 1.56 M | 345 |
| 2304x900 | 2.07 M | 274 |
| 2664x1040 | 2.77 M | 235 |
| 3072x1200 (new max) | 3.69 M | 176 |

Cost of the patch at the same size (the display mode is now the 3072x1200 top level instead of 2000x780): within
the run-to-run noise of the random map - 1536x600 two runs each: res-tall 440 / 409, main before it 478 / 332;
2000x780 345 vs 358. The start scene is light (small explored island); a busy late game costs more per frame. HYPOTHESIS (not measured): on
the phone the top levels will be well below 60 fps (verify-fps1 measured 42-60 fps at 1848x720 there).

Memory: each snapshot grows from 1.6 MB to 4.0 MB (x3), the display mode is the largest zoom size of the aspect
(phone 3072x1200 surfaces) and the landscape buffer 3232x1302: `s3det` guest memory 64.9 MB -> 81.3 MB.

Verified (desktop, `scratch/res-tall/`, local only): HUD 3072x1200 (`S3_RES`) full landscape and objects to the
bottom rows, right and left screen edge (`c_down/c_right/c_left.png`); Classic 4:3 pinch 800x600 -> 1600x1200 and
back (`mp1/host-60.png`). `s3det` 90 000 vms: two runs IDENTICAL and `S3_FAST=0` IDENTICAL to the fast-path run
(91 hash lines, `final insns=12330027314`); the hashes differ from before the patch from the first second on (the
`mem` hash covers the patched code bytes, and the heap is laid out differently) - same for every peer of this
version, but peers of different port versions cannot play together. MP two peers (`mp-local-test.sh`, Artokia,
both pinching through 640x480 ... 1600x1200 at different times): **IDENTICAL**, 1226 ticks.

## How a size change works

The game's own F1-F3 switch (RE): the key handler (`0x525a77..`, logic thread) writes the wanted index to
`[0x7dfd44]`, stores it in the settings (`0x49ded0`) and **releases one token of the semaphore `[0x7a800c]`**
(`0x525b5b`). The frame renderer (`0x4b26c0`, render thread) calls `0x4c7490(snap)`: for `snap+0xa0` (= the copy of
`[0x7dfd44]`) in 1..3 it writes the layout table, calls `0x42ce90(w, h, 16, 0, 0)` (posts `0x804(index)` to the
window; `0x405c80` calls `IDirectDraw2::SetDisplayMode` with 640/800/1024 constants; the display setup `0x42e430` runs
again and re-creates surfaces, landscape object, text DIB from the layout globals), sets `[0x7dfd44] = 0xfa` and skips
frames while it is non-zero. The logic thread (`0x53db30`) sees `0xfa`, **waits on the semaphore** (timeout 300 s),
rebuilds the minimap image (`gd::0x4fb650`, `gd+0x1223656`), sets the previous camera `gd+0x2d254/58` to
10 000 000 (= full landscape redraw), clamps the camera, marks the panel dirty and clears `[0x7dfd44]`. While
`[0x7dfd44] != 0` the simulation step is skipped (`0x53dd5c`), exactly as in the original game.

Our switch (`res::switch_hook`, hook at `0x4c7490` entry, render thread, once per in-game frame):

1. **Mode set** (first in-game frame, or the window aspect changed): the display mode becomes the **largest zoom size
   for the aspect** (e.g. 1920x780 on the phone). The layout globals are written for that size *before*
   `0x42ce90` (the display setup sizes its render surfaces from them; with the zoom size there, later bigger steps were
   clipped to it), the `SetDisplayMode` call sites `0x405cc3` / `0x405cf2` get the custom size (pending-mode set by
   the `0x42ce90` entry hook for non-standard sizes), then the layout is set to the zoom size, the cached view
   rectangles are updated and the presented size is set (step 2). Semaphore + `0xfa` like F1-F3.
2. **Zoom step** (fast path, same mode): only the layout globals (`write_layout`, `0x730f08..0x730f40` +
   `[0x7dfd58]`), the cached view rectangles (`gfx+0x5f6e8`, landscape object `+0x58/+0x5c/+0x74..+0x80`) and the
   **presented ("logical") size** change: `IDirectDraw2::SetDisplayMode(w, h, 16, 0, DDSDM_PORT_LOGICAL)` - a flag of
   our ddraw HLE that crops the presented primary surface to `w x h` without touching surfaces (s3-dx
   `set_logical`; a real mode change clears it). The camera is moved so the pinch point keeps its world position
   (`zoom::anchor_camera`) and clamped like `0x51b4d0`; the panel is marked dirty. When the variant changes (panel
   art / minimap size) the logic acknowledgement is used (semaphore + `0xfa`) because the minimap image must be
   rebuilt. Then frames are skipped until the logic thread delivered a snapshot of the new size (`snap+0x30/+0x34`),
   and the next frames force a full landscape redraw (`snap+0xc/+0x10` = 10 000 000).
3. Every frame: the cached view rectangles are compared with the layout globals and re-synced (+ redraw on a
   matching snapshot). This also fixes the **black band with a zigzag edge after F1-F3 in HUD mode** (the HUD changes
   panel/map width after the display setup; the landscape was drawn only as wide as the cached rectangle, and the
   redraw happened on a snapshot of the old width). Verified with the zoom off: HUD + F2 now shows a complete map.

`S3_RES_TRACE=1` logs every step (`res: switch 1480x600 -> 1576x640 mode 1920x780 (fast, ...)`, view-rect syncs,
display-setup sizes, logic ticks while a switch is pending). Desktop testing without a window:
`s3run --headless --display native --window 2229x904` (the window aspect drives the size) or `S3_RES_ASPECT=WxH`;
`S3_RES=WxH` forces one size.

## Determinism (multiplayer)

Resolution is local view state: the original game lets every MP peer pick 640/800/1024 and the patch only changes
render-side memory (snapshot, layout, surfaces). Places where the view touches `gd`: the snapshot fill writes
placement-marker bytes into visible tiles (`0x5223b2`, tile `+8`, only in build mode; masked in the MP hash already)
and the minimap image `gd+0x1223656` (UI only). The ack path pauses the local step like F1-F3.

Test (2026-11-05, `scratch/res-zoom/mp1/`, local only): `PORT=7795 HOST_EXTRA="45000:pinch ...;55000:...;..."
JOIN_EXTRA="50000:pinch ...;70000:..." port/scripts/mp-local-test.sh scratch/res-zoom/mp1 110` - host went
800x600 -> 856x640 -> 1040x780 -> ... -> 1040x780, joiner 800x600 -> 744x560 -> 640x480 -> 696x520 -> 904x680 (fast
steps incl. variant changes with the ack path): **RESULT: IDENTICAL (no desync)**, 1194 ticks, executed messages in
the same order and steps.

## Performance (desktop, loaded host ~175 guest MIPS, HUD mode, `--fps full`)

| Render size | Pixels | fps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 888x360 | 0.32 M | 46 |
| 1384x560 | 0.78 M | 24 |
| 1776x720 | 1.28 M | 20 |
| 1920x780 | 1.50 M | 16 |

The frame cost grows about linearly with the pixel count (landscape blit, sprites, present conversion are per pixel);
the game's 800x600 (0.48 M) sits between the first two rows. On the phone (~100 M instructions/s measured) expect
roughly 0.55x these numbers until the perf-cpu fast paths land: the default 1480x600 is about 13 fps there, 888x360
about 25 fps. So on the phone the default level should probably be lower (e.g. level 3 = 1184x480); left at 6 until
measured in the Verify phase.

**Measured on the phone (verify-fps1, 2026-11-05)**: the window is now the full 2316x904 (cutout area used), so the
levels are 1536x600 (6, default), 1232x480 (3), 1848x720 (9). With the new fast paths Classic Touch holds 60 fps at
the default, HUD 48-60; 1848x720 42-60 depending on the view. Default kept at 6. Table:
[performance.md](performance.md#phone-measurements). A zoom step itself costs one skipped frame (fast path); a mode set (game start, aspect
change) about 1-2 s on the desktop (display re-setup).

## Camera on a size switch (2026-11-07)

`res::switch_hook` keeps a screen point over the same world point (`zoom::anchor_camera`): the pinch anchor, or
**the view centre when there is none** (game start, F1-F3). Before, the start view (castle centred by the game for
640x480) kept its top-left corner, so on a 1944x760 view the castle sat in the upper-left part. The Mobile HUD
removing / restoring the panel (`ui_hud_game::apply_layout`) moves the camera by half the panel width for the same
reason. Verified on the phone.

## Cheaper zoom steps (2026-11-07)

Pinch stuttered: after every size switch `res::switch_hook` forced a full landscape redraw for **3** frames
(`snap+0xc/+0x10` = 10 000 000); a full redraw runs the `0x54cbd0` triangle rasteriser (`0x54d382`) over the
whole view (100-280 ms per frame). Now `redraw_frames_after`: 1 frame when the view grows, 0 when it only shrinks
(zoom in; the landscape buffer already covers the smaller view). Desktop HUD 2316x904 uncapped, fps in the pinch
seconds: in 181/158 -> 311/436, out 75/181 -> 290/273. Screenshots mid/end of in and out pinches: no black bands.
(A presentation-only zoom during the pinch was tried first and reverted: the user wants the real zoom per step.)

Pinch follows the fingers continuously (2026-11-07): `zoom::pinch` asks for the render height `h_start / scale`
(8 px steps, `PinchState` overrides the level in `target_size`), one switch at a time (`res::switch_pending`, at
least 33 ms apart, so the step size adapts to how fast the game finishes a switch); the end snaps to the nearest
level and saves it. Before: 40 px level steps, at least 120 ms apart, levels skipped. Desktop JIT, 2316x904, cap 60:
no frame over 79 ms during in/out pinches, 51-61 fps.
perf-landfull (2026-11-08): the remaining full redraw after a view-growing step is now cheap: native fast path
`land_rows` for the rasteriser's row/pixel loop (performance.md, "perf-landfull"). Frame after a zoom-out step on
the desktop: JIT off 37-117 ms -> 17-42 ms, `S3_JIT=1` 14-44 ms -> 14-17 ms (holds the 60 cap).

## More zoom in, FPS counter size (2026-11-08)

- `res::MIN_H` 360 -> 280, `MIN_W` 480 -> 320; `zoom::LEVEL_HEIGHTS` gained 280 and 320 (14 levels; default level
  index 6 -> 8 = still 600 px; Classic minimum index 3 -> 5 = still 480). Tested in game with `S3_RES`: 816x320,
  720x280, 616x240, 512x200 all run (60 fps, no crash, landscape fine), but the Mobile HUD is drawn into the frame:
  below ~280 its icons vanish (top resource icons at 240, bottom bar icons at 200), so 280 is the limit until the
  HUD is drawn at window resolution (multicore.md option B). Zoom out above 780: see the res-tall work.
- FPS counter: font and padding scale with the frame height (11 px at 600), so it keeps its on-screen size at
  every zoom level, like the HUD. (Superseded by overlay-window: drawn in the window layer.)

## Zoom in to 200 (overlay-window, 2026-11-08)

The mods' UI is now drawn at window resolution ([mods.md](mods.md) "Window layer"), so the HUD no longer limits
the zoom: `res::MIN_H` 280 -> 200 (`MIN_W` stays 320), `LEVEL_HEIGHTS` gained 200 and 240 (22 levels; default index
8 -> 10 = still 600; Classic minimum 5 -> 7 = still 480). NOTE: saved `res.zoom_level` indices of older settings files
now mean a level 2 steps closer (the exact `zoom_height` of a pinch is unaffected). Verified headless 2316x904 with
`zoom_level` 0: HUD at 512x200 full size and sharp, icons harvested (the harvest raises the render size to 480 for a
moment), a building placed through the sheet (`scratch/overlay-window/vis/hudmin/`).

# Port status (after the polish night, verify1, and the mobile UX + online workflow, 2026-11-06)

One-page summary of what works, with evidence. Details: [integration-log.md](integration-log.md) (desktop),

## What works

The **unmodified GOG `S3.EXE` + the user's data** runs in our own host: iced-x86 interpreter (`s3-cpu`) + PE loader
+ HLE of KERNEL32/USER32/GDI32/ADVAPI32/WINMM/DirectX. No Wine, no game code or data in the repo or the APK.

After perf-cpu only: Classic 1536x600 38-40 fps (250 MIPS). After the verify-fps1 fast paths (`snap_tiles`, `obj_empty`, `land_clean`): **Classic Touch default zoom (1536x600) 60/62/60 fps at the 60 cap**, zoom 1232x480 60 fps (~320 MIPS-equivalent, headroom), zoom 1848x720 42-46 fps; **Mobile HUD** default 48-58 fps (48 with much animated water on screen), 1232x480 60 fps, 1848x720 46-60 fps. Engine thread ~94-99 % of one core at ~2 GHz average clock. Table: [performance.md](performance.md#phone-measurements) |

The interpreter is single-threaded (cooperative green threads), so it uses one core; the presenter is a second
thread (~10-14 %).

## Install on a phone

Full steps: [android.md](android.md#install-for-users-phone). Short version:

1. Build or take `port/target/apk/settlers3port.apk` (`cd port && scripts/build-apk.sh`); install with
   `adb install -r -g settlers3port.apk` (or copy to the phone, allow unknown sources).
2. Start the app once (status screen "Game files missing").
3. Copy the contents of your own GOG install (folder with `S3.EXE`, `regs.cmd`, `GFX`, `SND`, `MUSIC`, `Map`, `S3`)
   to `Android/data/com.settlers3port.app/files/game/` (adb push or USB/MTP; ~0.6-1.2 GB; only the
   `GFX/*.f8007e01f.dat` set is needed).
4. Reopen the app. In menus a tap is a left click. In game the touch mods are active (UI mode A by default, see
   [ui-modes.md](ui-modes.md)): tap = select / move / place, drag = pan, long press then drag = box select,
   two-finger tap = cancel/deselect, pinch = resolution; Save / Quit via the floating **Menu** button (A) or the HUD
   menu (B). Back = Esc, three-finger tap = soft keyboard (the ESC/ABC/RMB letterbox buttons were removed 2026-11-07).
   Multiplayer on the same Wi-Fi: "Multi-player Game: LAN" -> "Local network / Wi-Fi" -> New Game on one device, Search for games + Join Game on the others (embedded relay + UDP discovery, multiplayer.md section 8). Internet: put a relay URL (e.g. `ws://host:7788/`) in `<data dir>/relay-url.txt`.

## Known issues

| Issue | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Intro/mission videos skipped | MCI AVI faked (Indeo 5 decoding not implemented) |
| Esc / Back does not open an in-game menu | Esc does nothing in game on desktop either; use the panel's computer icon (Save / Quit) |
| Loading time varies on desktop | one verify1 run needed ~77 s from players OK to in game (usually 9-10 s; load average was low). HYPOTHESIS: host contention or map variance; not reproduced in 2 later runs |
| Three-finger tap (keyboard toggle) untested on a device | adb has no multi-touch; the `ABC` button works |
| Multiplayer: LAN menu entry, no lobby UI | **LAN play out of the box (2026-11-08): phone host <-> Windows PC join over Wi-Fi verified, no desync** (embedded relay + UDP discovery, multiplayer.md section 8). DirectPlay HLE over our relay works (2 desktop peers, lockstep, no simulation desync in runs of up to ~6 min, [multiplayer.md](multiplayer.md)); Android joins a desktop host (ux-verify1). Relay URL: env `S3_RELAY_URL` (desktop) or one line in `<data dir>/relay-url.txt` (Android, read at engine start); no in-app setting yet. "Multi-player Game: Internet" (Blue Byte lobby, wsock32) stays unavailable; no x86_64 <-> arm64 peer tested; no desync hash on Android |
| HUD (mode B) after an in-game switch from mode A | covers the panel ("cover mode") until the next game start, then full screen (by design, [ui-hud.md](ui-hud.md)). After B -> A the minimap showed map pixels for a few seconds, then cleared (Android, cosmetic) |
| Box select needs a long press then drag | not testable with adb (no hold-then-move); verified on desktop. Two-finger gestures and pinch: desktop inject + unit tests only |
| x87 precision | 53-bit, round-to-nearest only; unmasked FPU exceptions not delivered (see [x87-fpu.md](x87-fpu.md)) |
| Desktop real playback only with `--features audio-cpal` (not listened to yet) | WAV sink `--audio-wav` always available |
| Game files must be copied via adb/MTP | Android 11+ file managers often cannot open `Android/data`; no folder picker yet |

`docs/porting/strategy.md`:

```md
# Porting strategy

Status: **option B IMPLEMENTED (2026-11-06)**: own host, iced-x86 interpreter + HLE, code in `port/`, contract in
[architecture.md](architecture.md). What works today (details and evidence in [status.md](status.md)):

- The unmodified GOG `S3.EXE` + data runs on desktop (`s3run`) and on Android (APK, emulator `s3_api35`): main menu
  in < 1 s, Single Player scenario -> random map -> in game in ~16-25 s, building placement, map scrolling, pause/resume.
- Speed: ~100 M guest instructions/s in game, about one host core; 48 fps desktop, ~30 fps x86_64 emulator.
  Option C (static recompilation) is not needed for now. A pure interpreter also keeps the iOS path open.
- Not done yet: real arm64 phone test, cursor drawing, video, save/load check, multiplayer (DirectPlay stubs only).

Decided 2026-11-05 (option B). The original draft notes below are kept for history; the "Next steps" list is done
(wine trace: [wine-trace.md](../reverse-engineering/wine-trace.md); instruction rate measured, see status.md).

## Constraints

- Run the **user's own** `S3.EXE` + data. Nothing of the game is shipped, cached in releases or committed.
- Guest = 32-bit x86 Windows PE (MSVC 6, fixed base 0x400000, no relocs). Host = Android arm64 (later iOS arm64).
- **iOS forbids JIT** for App Store / non-debug apps → any iOS build needs an interpreter or ahead-of-time translation.
- Original HW target was a Pentium ~200 MHz; modern phones are far faster, so even an interpreter may be fast enough (to be measured).

## Options

| # | Approach | Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | Wine + Box64 container (Winlator-style) | Works soonest, good reference/baseline | Huge, slow start, bad mobile UX, impossible on iOS |
| B | **Own host: PE loader + x86-32 CPU core + HLE of Win32/DirectX** (blockheads-pc pattern) | Small, mobile-native UX (touch, lifecycle, saves), iOS possible with interpreter | We write the HLE (~219 static imports + DDraw/DSound/DPlay COM) and pick a CPU core |
| C | Static recompilation (x86 → C/LLVM) of the user's exe on device | Native speed, iOS-friendly | Indirect calls, jump tables, self-modifying code risk; complex toolchain on device |

Recommended direction: **B**, with C as a later speed path if needed. (Chosen and implemented, see status above.)

### CPU core candidates for B

| Core | License | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Own x86-32 interpreter (Rust) | ours | **Chosen.** i386 + x87 (MMX not needed: cpuid reports none). Portable incl. iOS. ~170 MIPS benchmark |
| Box64 (incl. 32-bit "box32") dynarec | MIT | ARM64 dynarec; tied to Linux/Wine-ish ABI, would need extraction |
| FEX-Emu | MIT | x86/x86-64 → ARM64 JIT, Linux-host oriented |
| Unicorn | GPL-2.0-only | Rejected in blockheads-pc for license reasons; same here if we go GPL-3.0-or-later |
| dynarmic | 0BSD | ARM guest only — not usable |

### Host layers (B)

- Loader: map PE sections at 0x400000, resolve imports to host thunks, run entry point.
- Win32 HLE: files (VFS over user's install + app data dir for Save/registry), threads/sync, time, messages/window, registry (prefilled from `regs.cmd`, see [registry](../reverse-engineering/registry.md)).
- DirectDraw → present 8/16-bit framebuffer via GLES/Vulkan texture; scale to phone screen. (Implemented without GL: RGB565 copied into the ANativeWindow buffer, the compositor scales.)
- DirectSound → Android AAudio/Oboe (later CoreAudio). MCI music → play `MUSIC/*.ogg` ourselves.
- Input: touch → mouse (tap = left click, long-press / two-finger tap = right click, pinch? = zoom n/a, drag = scroll).
- DirectPlay multiplayer: later, possibly over our own relay.
- App shell: Android app (Kotlin or Tauri like blockheads), launcher asks user to pick the GOG folder/zip (SAF).

## Next steps (DONE 2026-11-05, kept for history; current list in [status.md](status.md#next-steps))

1. Run GOG `S3.EXE` under Wine on this PC (`wine` installed) to get a working reference + API trace (`WINEDEBUG=+relay`).
2. From the trace, list the actually-used APIs and COM methods → size the HLE.
3. Benchmark: how many x86 instructions/sec the game needs in a typical match (count via trace/`perf`), to choose interpreter vs JIT.
4. Write feasibility PLAN with milestones and kill gates.

## Decision: app shell (2026-11-05, user-confirmed)

- The game is **never** rendered inside a WebView. The Rust engine draws straight to a native surface (NativeActivity / ANativeWindow) in the same APK.
- Planned after the core runs: a **Tauri 2 + Svelte 5 + SvelteKit launcher** for the GOG folder picker (SAF), file validation, settings, i18n and saves. Its "Play" button starts the native game activity.
- Tonight's Gradle-less NativeActivity shell (`port/crates/s3-android`) is the game part of that design. It will be embedded later in the Tauri Gradle project.

`docs/porting/touch.md`:

```md
# Context-aware touch (W3)

Status: implemented 2026-11-05 (agent `touch-context`). Shared by both UI modes (A "Classic Touch", B "Mobile HUD",
[mobile-vision.md](mobile-vision.md)). Framework: [mods.md](mods.md). Game facts used:
[game-state-units.md](../reverse-engineering/game-state-units.md), [game-state-ui.md](../reverse-engineering/game-state-ui.md).

Code (`port/crates/s3-mods/src/`):

| File | What |
| --- | --- |
| `touch.rs` | the `touch-context` mod: gestures -> game actions, camera pan/inertia, pinch zoom, feedback state; `install` (hook on `HandleInput` `0x524fa0` = "a game is running") |
| `touch_logic.rs` | pure decision logic + camera physics (unit tested): `Layout::region`, `find_hit`, `decide_tap`, `decide_double_tap`, `decide_two_finger_tap`, `drag_kind`, `pinch_zoom_key`, `clamp_camera`, `CameraPan` |
| `touch_game.rs` | GOG S3.EXE memory reads/writes (addresses below) -> `View` snapshot |
| `touch_fx.rs` | overlay drawing: ripple, move/attack flag, selection rings, long-press ring, selection box, ✕ cancel button |

Frontends deliver raw pointers only (`HostEvent::Pointer`): Android `s3-frontend/src/touch.rs` (MotionEvent ->
pointer events, see [android.md](android.md)) and desktop `s3run --inject` touch commands
(`s3-desktop/src/touch_inject.rs`). The gesture recognizer and everything below run in `s3-mods` on the engine
thread, so desktop tests exercise exactly the Android code path.

## Behaviour

(2026-11-08 overlay-window) Touch feedback (ripples, flags, long-press ring, box, ✕ Cancel) is drawn in the window
layer at a constant on-screen size; selection rings follow the map scale. Raw pointer events carry window pixels too
(`HostEvent::Pointer::wx/wy`); `s3run` injects with a `w` prefix (`wtap`, `wpinch`, `wdrag`, ...) take window pixels
(the viewport is frozen while injected fingers are down, like on Android).

| Gesture | In game | Outside a game (menus) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tap own unit / building (map) | select: left click at the unit (enlarged hit box, see below) | – |
| Tap ground, units selected | **move**: quick right click (down, up 60 ms later) at the point = the game's own command 9 path (incl. selection sync cmd 3, sound, minimap targets). Green flag on the map | left click |
| Tap enemy unit/building, units selected | **attack**: quick right click on the enemy. Red flag | – |
| Tap ground, nothing selected | left click (the game's default: deselect / nothing) | – |
| Tap in build placement | left click = place the site (the game checks the spot) | – |
| Tap ✕ (top right of the map, placement only) / two-finger tap | cancel placement (`[gd+0x2d28c] = 0`, panel dirty) | – |
| Tap ✕ "Deselect" (UI mode A, units or a building selected; 2026-11-08) | same as a two-finger tap: clear the unit selection / right click deselects the building (`View::deselect_button`) | – |
| Tap panel / minimap | left click (panel buttons, minimap jump; choosing another building or tab also ends placement) | left click |
| Double tap own soldier | Ctrl + left click = select the same type nearby (game rule, `0x533f21`) HYPOTHESIS: Ctrl reaches the game through our WM_KEYDOWN; not verified at runtime | – |
| Two-finger tap | placement: cancel; building selected: quick right click (deselect); units selected: clear the selection; else nothing | right click (fallback) |
| Three-finger tap | soft keyboard request (fallback) | same |
| One-finger drag on the map | **camera follows the finger** (direct camera write), inertia after a fling | left drag (fallback) |
| One-finger drag on panel / minimap | left drag | – |
| Two-finger drag | camera follows the centroid, inertia | – |
| Long press | hover only (mouse move = tooltips after ~10 logic ticks). A white ring grows from 150 ms and stays full while held | hover |
| Long press, then drag | **box selection** (left drag from the press point); green box drawn by us, the game draws its own | left drag |
| Pinch in / out | **zoom** = render resolution levels (res-zoom, [resolution-zoom.md](resolution-zoom.md)): continuous, one level per finger-distance factor 1.12, the map point under the fingers stays; levels 360..1200 px high at the window aspect. With the custom resolution off: the old F1/F2/F3 step (640x480 <-> 800x600 <-> 1024x768, threshold scale 0.75 / 1.33) | – |

**No long press is ever a right click.** The original game ignores right-ups held for 15 or more game steps
(`0x53437d`), so every synthetic right click is a quick down/up. (The `RMB` letterbox button was removed 2026-11-07; if
"next tap = right click" is armed via `s3_mods::set_right_next`, `touch-context` passes the tap to the fallback.

Hit test: the game's own single-click box is x ±10 px, feet `y-5 ..= y+32` (`0x5339a1`). We look for hit-list
entries in a larger box (x ±18, feet `y-12 ..= y+44`), prefer the local player's own entries, then the nearest to the
body, and click at `(feet.x, feet.y - 12)`, which lies inside the game's box. So taps near a unit select it.

Feedback (overlay, map effects clipped to the map view): white ripple on every in-game tap (orange for cancel,
green/red for move/attack), a flag with a pulsing ground ring at move/attack targets that stays anchored to the
map while panning (`world = screen + camera`), green rings under every selected own unit that is on screen (hit list
∩ UI selection), the long-press ring, the selection box, and the ✕ "Cancel" button in placement mode.

## Unit orders, paths, groups (unit-orders, 2026-11-08)

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/unit_orders.rs`, a mod below both UI modes plus a `HandleInput` hook. RE:
[game-state-units.md](../reverse-engineering/game-state-units.md#orders-waypoints-patrol-unit-paths).

- **Orders** = the PC's modifier + right click: **Waypoint** (Shift, stays armed for 4 taps: the first tap of an idle
  group is a plain move, then the game's 3 waypoints; tap the button again to stop), **Patrol** (Alt), **No fight**
  (Ctrl). Arming sets the fallback's "next tap = right click" plus `right_next_vk`; the tap then sends key down,
  right click, key up, so the game builds command 0x0d / 0x0e / 0x0f itself (same path as a PC, MP-safe).
  Mode B: second row of the selection card; mode A: a column below the Deselect ✕ (top right) with a hint above the
  group row ("Tap the next waypoint (3 left)"). Disarmed when the selection goes away.
- **Paths**: marching dots from each unit through target and waypoints, rings at waypoints, a green ring at the final
  target, patrol routes as an amber loop. Always for the selected units (so tapping a unit / group shows its route);
  for all own units walking on an order (job 0x35) or patrolling with **Settings `show_unit_paths`** (default off;
  Classic menu column "Paths: selected / all units", HUD Settings "Unit paths").
- **Group buttons 1..6** (**Settings `group_shortcuts`**, default off; Classic "Groups: on/off", HUD "Group buttons").
  Tap = `SelectGroup(n)` (tap again while selected = centre the camera, like pressing the digit twice), long press
  (the touch long-press time, progress bar) = `AssignGroup(n)` with the current selection. Non-empty groups show their
  count, the current group is gold. Classic: bottom of the map right of the panel; HUD: above the bottom bar right of
  the minimap card, or above the minimap card when that row would reach the selection card (tall / narrow windows).
- Deselect (✕, two-finger tap, HUD Deselect) on a group now leaves the group (slot -1) instead of emptying it.
- Desktop: `s3run --inject` has `kdown VK` / `kup VK` (hold a key, e.g. `kdown 0x12;rclick x y;kup 0x12`).

Verified desktop 2026-11-08 (`scratch/unit-orders/c3/*.png` Classic 2316x904, `h1`/`h2` HUD 2176x1812, local only):
box select -> long press 1 assigns 10 units, Waypoint + 2 taps draws the route through both waypoints, ✕ then tap
1 reselects the group, second tap centres, Patrol draws the loop; same in the HUD card.

## Game state used (GOG `00a925cf…` only)

| What | Address | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gd` (CGameData) | `[0x7e3408]`, valid when `[gd] == 0x658c18`; **in multiplayer `[0x7e3408]` stays 0**, then `[logic+0x3a0]` (ECX of `HandleInput`, recorded by `touch_game::note_logic`) | VERIFIED (0 in menus before the first game, `0x18790000` in game; MP: 0 on host and joiner, fallback works, ux-verify1) |
| Game running | hook `CLogicThread::HandleInput` `0x524fa0`: called every logic tick; "in game" = a call within 1.5 s **and** the layout globals match the presented frame size | VERIFIED in game (taps in the menus still went to the fallback, so it is not called there; HYPOTHESIS for the statistics screen) |
| Layout | `0x730f08` res index, `0x730f0c/10` screen, `0x730f18/1c` map view, `0x730f24` panel width, `0x730f2c` minimap x, `0x730f34` minimap bottom | VERIFIED (re-ui) |
| Mode | page `[gd+0x2d284]` (1 build, 4 building, 9 paused), slot `[gd+0x2d28c]`, building `[0x7dfd6c]`, UI selection slot `[0x7dfd68]` + count `word [0x7ad620+slot*2]` | VERIFIED |
| Hit list | `0x7ade08 + ([0x7dfd64] + 2i) * 10`, count `[0x7dfd5c]`; entry `u16 kind, i16 x, i16 y, u16 id` | VERIFIED (2026-11-05: kind 100 tower id 1 at (332,222); kind 3 id 0x35 at (212,316)) |
| Owner | settler `gd+0x12a5e60 + id*0x40` +0, building `gd+0x1499e64 + id*0x3a` +0, local player `[gd+0x2d2d4]` | VERIFIED (re-units) |
| Camera | write `gd+0x2d25c` / `+0x2d260`, clamp in host with the formula of `0x51b4d0` | VERIFIED (drag 100 px -> camera +100 exactly) |
| Cancel placement | `[gd+0x2d28c] = 0`, `[gd+0x2d27c] = 1` | VERIFIED (slot 1 -> 0, ✕ and two-finger tap) |
| Deselect units | count `:= 0`, dirty `[0x7ad5f8+slot*4] = 1`, page 5 -> 0, panel dirty | VERIFIED (count 10 -> 0, panel cleared, the game's own selection brackets gone). The logic-side copy is re-synced by the next right click (cmd 3 with count 0) |

Why a synthetic right click and not posting command 9 directly: the right-click path is VERIFIED end to end
(selection sync cmd 3, acknowledgement sound, minimap target, modifiers, attack on enemies) while direct
`Queue::Post` of commands is still a HYPOTHESIS (must run on the logic thread). The click is mouse input, so it also
goes through the lockstep command queue in multiplayer like any player action.

## Verified on desktop (2026-11-05, `scratch/touch-context/r*.png`, local only)

Recipe (in game after ~45-50 s on a loaded machine; random map of the first single-player game):

```sh
D=../scratch/touch-context; G=0x7e3408
I="1200:tap 165 235;3200:tap 630 467;5200:tap 730 567;7200:tap 730 567;\
50000:lpdrag 300 330 470 470 700 400;51450:shot $D/r1box.png;52500:tap 540 160;52750:shot $D/r2flag.png;\
56000:tap2 400 300;56300:peek 0x7ad620 4;57000:drag2 400 300 250 200;57320:xpeek $G@0x2d25c 8;\
59000:drag 300 300 400 300 1000;60100:xpeek $G@0x2d25c 8;61000:tap 25 167;61800:tap 23 194;62600:tap 38 230;\
63400:shot $D/r5build.png;64000:tap 612 28;64300:xpeek $G@0x2d284 12;65000:tap 38 230;66000:tap2 400 300;\
67000:longpress 400 300 1000;67700:shot $D/r7press.png;68500:pinch 400 300 0.6;71000:peek 0x730f08 4"
./target/release/s3run --headless --game-dir ../game-files/gog-s3-ultimate --data-dir $D/data --max-seconds 76 --inject "$I"
```

Results: long-press drag selected 10-11 soldiers (green rings + the game's brackets); tap on the ground made them
walk there (flag); two-finger tap cleared the selection; two-finger drag of 150 px moved the camera +159 px (then
glided ~110 px); a slow 100 px drag moved it exactly 100 px with no glide; build slot chosen by taps -> ✕ visible ->
✕ cancelled (slot 1 -> 0), and so did a two-finger tap; long-press ring drawn; pinch 0.6 switched 640x480 -> 800x600
and pinch 1.6 switched back.

Not verified at runtime: attack on an enemy (no enemy in reach on the test map; logic unit-tested), double tap = same
type selection, tap on a building with units selected.

## Known limits / notes

- **Resolution switch cool-down**: a second pinch ~3.5 s (wall time, slow host) after a switch was ignored by the
  game; 7 s later it worked. HYPOTHESIS: the game ignores F1-F3 until its display re-init finished. We fire the key
  once per gesture; the user pinches again.
- The camera clamp is the game's rectangle, so flings can reach the black corners of the diamond-shaped world, like
  the game's own scrolling.
- Fling: release speed measured over the last 80 ms; glides only above 0.25 game px/ms, time constant 300 ms,
  max 4 px/ms. Any touch-down stops a glide; the game moving the camera (minimap, keys) also stops it.
- The ✕ sits at the top right of the map view (`touch_logic::cancel_button`); UI mode A moved its Menu button to the
  bottom right for that reason. UI-mode mods are added **after** `touch-context` in `s3_mods::install`, so they are
  on top and see touches first.
- Settings: `touch.context` (default `true`) in `mods-settings.json`; `false` = legacy touch->mouse fallback only
  (which still turns long presses into right clicks if `long_press_right_click`). Unknown exes and `S3_MODS=0` also
  fall back to the legacy mapping.
- `S3_TOUCH_TRACE=1` prints camera writes and pinch decisions to stderr.
- Old Android letterbox buttons (ESC, ABC, RMB) removed 2026-11-07. Back sends Esc; three-finger tap toggles the
  keyboard.

## Tests

`cargo test -p s3-mods touch` (16): regions incl. the sheared minimap, enlarged hit box clicking inside the game box,
own-before-enemy, move/attack/select/panel taps, placement place/✕/two-finger cancel, two-finger tap per mode,
double tap, drag kinds, pinch steps, camera clamp, follow + glide + stop, two-finger equal-timestamp samples,
no glide after a resting finger or a slow drag. `s3-desktop`: `inject_touch_parsing` (lpdrag/drag2/tap3/dtap).
`s3-android`: `motion_actions_map_to_pointer_phases`, `filter_drops_unchanged_moves`.

## Tap, then press-and-drag = box select

A one-finger touch that goes down within `double_tap_ms` (300 ms) of a tap near it (2 x `double_tap_slop`) and then
drags starts the box selection at once, like a drag after a long press (`gesture.rs` `double_drag`: emits
`LongPress` + `Pan { after_long_press: true }`). A plain drag stays a camera pan; a quick second tap stays a
`DoubleTap`. Note: the first tap still does what a tap does (select / move order) (user request 2026-11-08).

## Minimap drag (UI mode A)

A one-finger drag that starts on the minimap scrolls the map, also after a long press (it used to start a box
selection). The game jumps on a left-button press on the minimap but ignores moves with the button held, so
`touch.rs` (`Drag::Minimap`) re-presses at the finger every 50 ms (`MINIMAP_REPRESS_MS`) and once more on release.
Verified desktop 2316x904: the camera rectangle follows the finger for hold-drags and quick drags (2026-11-08).

## Vibration and path modes (2026-11-08)

- `s3-mods/src/haptics.rs` queues short buzzes: 25 ms on a long press in game (box select start, also the tap-then-drag
  gesture) and on a group assign; 60 ms when a new game message appears in the foreground. The Android frontend
  drains the queue (`Shared::haptic`) and calls `Vibrator.vibrate(VibrationEffect.createOneShot)` over JNI
  (`bgservice::vibrate`, permission `VIBRATE`). Background message notifications use the channel `events_vibrate`
  (vibration on) or `events_quiet`; the first channel `events` (no vibration, cannot be changed) is deleted.
- Settings `vibrate_touch` / `vibrate_messages` (default on), one menu button cycling "Vibration: all / touch /
  messages / off" (Classic menu column, HUD settings).
- `Settings::unit_paths` = `PathMode` Selected / Units / All (old `show_unit_paths` migrated to All). Units = own
  selectable types only (`unit_orders::selectable_type`: soldiers, priest, geologist, thief, pioneer, war machines,
  ships).

Click length at game speed: taps send a button down and the up `fallback::TouchMouse::click_ms()` later = 60 ms of
game time (60 / speed on the wall clock, at least 12 ms); the game ignores long right clicks, so a fixed 60 ms wall
time broke orders at 2x..8x (2026-11-08).

```

# UI mode A "Classic Touch"

Status: implemented 2026-11-05 (agent `ui-classic`). Code: `port/crates/s3-mods/src/ui_classic.rs` (mod + hooks) and
`ui_classic_panel.rs` (pure panel model, unit tested). Vision: [mobile-vision.md](mobile-vision.md) (UI decision A).
Framework: [mods.md](mods.md). Game facts used: [game-state-ui.md](../reverse-engineering/game-state-ui.md),
[game-state-units.md](../reverse-engineering/game-state-units.md). Mode B: [ui-hud.md](ui-hud.md).

Idea: keep the original left panel, menus and screens, and make them work with fingers. Nothing is replaced and the
game is not modified on disk. Map touches (select, move, build placement, ✕ cancel, pan, pinch) belong to the
context-aware touch mod (`touch*.rs`, W3), which both UI modes share. Mode A adds only what the panel needs.

## What it does

Since 2026-11-08 (overlay-window) the floating buttons, context chip, magnifier bubble and outlines are drawn in the
window layer (window pixels, sizes as at a 600 px high window, [mods.md](mods.md) "Window layer"), and in `Native
wide` with the custom resolution the original panel itself is shown at a constant scale (the art fills the screen
height at every zoom; [display.md](display.md) "Classic panel at a constant size"). The pixel sizes below are those
reference units. Minimum zoom in Classic stays 480 px (the panel art).

| Feature | Behaviour | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Panel taps with a magnifier** | A finger on the left panel below the minimap is captured. While it is down, a bubble right of the panel shows the area under the finger enlarged 3x (64x40 px source, 192x120 px) and, below it, the button name in 18 px bold text. The chosen button gets a gold outline on the panel and in the bubble. The finger may slide to change the choice. Lifting it sends one left click to the **centre** of that button. Sliding more than 48 px right of the panel cancels without a click. | `ui_classic_panel::buttons(page, sub, category, race)` lists the known buttons in grid units. `pick()` chooses the button under the finger. In gaps, it snaps to the nearest button within 4 grid cells (12 px at 640x480), but only on pages whose buttons we know completely (0-3, and 7 sub-page 0). On other pages (4 building, 5 units, 8 messages, …) the raw point is clicked and the bubble still magnifies. |
| **Button names from the game** | The game's own strings in the game's language ("Woodcutter's Hut", "Buildings", "Save/Quit", …). English fallback when the table cannot be read. | The hook on the gfx ctor `0x42c820` records `gfx` (ECX). The string table is `[gfx+0x5f6b8]`. `panel::read_text` repeats the lookup `0x5faaa0` does, reading memory only (no guest call). Building names: text `0x80000+type`, plus the special ids for Amazon types. Results are cached. |
| **Floating Menu button** | A 76x38 "Menu" button at the bottom right of the map. It opens the in-game Save/Quit menu (panel page 7). While the menu is open it reads "Close" and returns to the previous page (build, goods, settlers; otherwise none). Replaces ESC, which S3 does not use in game. | The tap queues `Action::OpenMenu`/`CloseMenu`. The hook at `HandleInput` entry `0x524fa0` (logic thread, before input is processed) writes page 7, sub-page 0 and panel dirty, then plays the panel click sound (`0x53f560(0x3d)`, thiscall logic). |
| **Display + FPS toggles** (2026-11-05) | While the menu is open, "Screen: Fit/Fill/Stretch/Wide" and "FPS: off/on/details" buttons sit above "UI: Mobile HUD"; a tap cycles the setting (saved). The floating buttons and the touch ✕ are anchored to the visible part of the frame (Fill mode crops it; the ✕ moves below the FPS counter). Note: in Fill mode the left panel's top/bottom rows are cropped too (e.g. "Quit Game" at 640x480 on a 2.47:1 screen), so Fill suits mode B / Native wide better. | `display::cycle_mode` / `cycle_fps`, `display::visible_game_rect` (see [display.md](display.md)). |
| **Context chip** | Top left of the map: "Place: <building>" in build placement, "N selected" for a unit selection, or the selected building's name. | Read each tick: page `[gd+0x2d284]`, slot `[gd+0x2d28c]`, type `[gd+0x2d2f0]`, selection `[0x7dfd68]`/`[0x7ad620+slot*2]`, building `[0x7dfd6c]` -> building table type. |

When it is active: `settings.ui_mode == ClassicTouch` (the default) or `S3_UI_MODE=A|classic`. `S3_UI_MODE=B|hud|off`
turns it off. It also has to be in game. In-game test: `HandleInput` ran in the last 1.5 s, `gd` has the CGameData
vtable `0x658c18`, and the layout globals `0x730f0c/10` equal the presented frame size. In the 800x600 menus the
mod does nothing, because the menu buttons are already large. All hooks are installed only for the GOG exe (sha256
`00a925cf…`). With any other exe, mode A stays inactive.

Not done, and why:

- **Enlarged panel rendering** (scaling the panel region up when presenting): this needs a presenter crop/scale that
  is shared with mode B. The magnifier already makes small icons readable when needed, and keeps the map area.
  At 640x480 in game (the default), a phone shows the panel at about 2.2x its original size.
- **Own Cancel button**: `touch.rs` already draws the ✕ Cancel button for build placement (top right, for both modes).
  That is why the Menu button sits bottom right.

# UI mode B "Mobile HUD" (W4)

## How it works

**Window layer (2026-11-08 overlay-window)**: the HUD is drawn into the mods' window-resolution layer
([mods.md](mods.md) "Window layer"), not into the game frame: sizes come from the window (factor = window height /
480 x `hud_scale`, same look as a 600 px frame shown full screen before), so the bar, sheets, cards and text keep
their size and stay sharp at every zoom level (now down to 200 px render height). Touches hit-test with their window
position. Icons are still sampled from the game's frame; the icon harvest needs a frame >= 480 px high, so while it
runs the zoom keeps the render size at least 480 (`HudShared::harvesting`, hidden behind the "Preparing touch HUD"
screen). The minimap is a shared RGBA image drawn with the game's shear (`Layer::blit_map`).

### Hiding the panel: full-screen map (layout patch)

Instead of covering the panel, the game is made to draw the map over the whole screen:

| Hook | Where / thread | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0x4c6d70` return (layout setter) | display setup | if `ui_mode == MobileHud` (and full-screen not turned off): `[0x730f24]` (panel width) = 0, `[0x730f18]` (map view width) = screen width |
| `0x54bec0` entry (landscape ring buffer init, thiscall `[gfx+0x5f6cc]`, arg0 = width) | display setup | arg0 = screen width + margin when it equals map width + margin (`[0x730f44]` = 32 in our runs) |
| `0x4b4d00` entry (panel renderer) | render thread, every in-game frame | heartbeat ("in game"), records `gfx` (ecx); applies or undoes the layout; skips the panel (`return_from_function(0, 1)`) while full screen |
| `0x4ff170` entry (`gd::ScreenToMap`) | logic thread | while full screen: `sx += original panel width` (its offsets are constants for the original layout) |

Findings (VERIFIED in s3run, 2026-11-05):

- The landscape is rendered into a ring buffer (`gfx+0x5f6cc`, width at `+0x50`, height `+0x54`) of width
  `map view width + [0x730f44]`, allocated by the display setup (`0x42ef..0x42f204`, three calls to `0x54bec0`). The
  blitter `0x54c9d0` wraps at that width. With only the globals changed at runtime the map showed a wrapped black
  zigzag column at x ~ 515 (504 + margin). So the layout must be in place before the display setup; the HUD then only
  uses full screen when the buffer is wide enough (`HudShared::buffer_ok`), otherwise it covers the panel ("cover
  mode", below).
- The renderer places the map at `x = [0x730f24] - (camX & 15) - 32`; units, buildings and the on-screen hit list
  (`0x7ade08`) follow, so `gd::0x4ff0a0` (hover / placement) and the hit list need no change; only `ScreenToMap` does.
- The minimap is drawn by the frame renderer `0x4b26c0`, not the panel. Since hud-polish the HUD **skips its two
  minimap blocks** while the full-screen layout is active (hooks `ui-hud:minimap-skip`: `0x4b2b34` -> jump
  `0x4b2ce5` = incremental minimap copy; `0x4b366a` -> jump `0x4b3cf3` = minimap part right of the panel + frame art
  resources `0x40001`/`0x40003` + white camera rectangle; the selection-box drawing after `0x4b3cf3` stays). Render
  thread only, no guest-visible game state changes (lockstep safe). VERIFIED 2026-11-05 (screenshot: top left shows
  map). In cover mode / panel peek / Classic mode the blocks run as before (VERIFIED: cover mode shows the full game
  minimap again). Its hit test in HandleInput needs `x < [0x730f24] + d`, so with panel width 0 the game ignores
  taps there; the HUD widget queues `gd::CenterOn` `0x51b560` (thiscall gd, `(tx, ty)`) on the logic thread.
  Writing the camera from the host instead left stale ring-buffer columns after a big jump.
- **Custom resolutions** (res-zoom): the layout hook records `(res index, panel width, map width)` as the game's
  layout setter wrote them (`HudShared::orig_layout`) before applying the full-screen layout, and restores/compensates
  with those values (`current_original_layout`), so a patched `0x4c6d70` case for a new resolution works without a
  table entry. The landscape-buffer widening accepts screens up to 4096 px wide (was 1024).
- The panel is only redrawn when `[gd+0x2d27c]` (panel dirty) is set: after restoring the layout the HUD sets it,
  otherwise the panel area kept map pixels.
- The panel renderer does not use `[0x730f24]` (all panel art is at fixed positions), so it can draw on top of the
  full-screen map for the icon sampling (the former "panel peek" used this too); panel clicks need the original
  layout (HandleInput tests `x < [0x730f24]`).
- Runtime resolution switch (F1-F3) in HUD mode: the 800x600 frame after F2 showed a black band with a zigzag edge
  around x ~ 515..650 (screenshots `scratch/ui-hud/r9-*.png`); starting directly at 800x600 (registry
  `Resolution=1`) is correct. HYPOTHESIS: another buffer (fog of war / visibility) is sized at game start from the
  map view width. Open.
- Camera clamp: the clamp `0x51b4d0` is unchanged, so near the west map edge the void outside the (sheared) world is
  visible where the panel used to hide it. Cosmetic.

### Minimap widget and full-screen map (`ui_hud_minimap.rs`)

Source: the game's own minimap image, a square RGB565 `mw x mw` image (`mw = [0x730f28]`, 128 at 640x480) at
`[snap+0x4c]`, where `snap` is the render snapshot (the panel renderer's argument, recorded in the panel hook).
Image column `c`, row `r` = tile `(c*W/mw, r*W/mw)`; the game draws it sheared (`x = mx + (mw-r-1)/2 + c`,
`y = my + r`), we draw it the same way at any scale (`MapGeom`). Camera rectangle in image coordinates with the
game's own formula (`0x4b3a3c`): `k = (mw<<8)/[snap+0x2c]`, `x = ([snap+0x24]+11)*k/256`, `y = ([snap+0x28]+16)*k/256`,
`w = [snap+0x30]*k/256`, `h = ([snap+0x34]-40)*k/256` (VERIFIED: the rectangle follows drags and jumps; 128 px image,
384 world: `cam (58, 85, 16, 17)` at the start). Refreshed every 250 ms into a host copy (one 32 KiB read). Player
territory colours come with the image; unexplored land is black. Touch: Down on the widget captures the finger;
moving more than ~7 HUD px turns it into a drag (each new tile under the finger replaces a still queued `CenterOn`);
Up without a drag opens the overlay. Overlay tap inside the map's bounding box -> tile (clamped into the shape) ->
`CenterOn`, close. Back / Esc: new `Mod::on_key` (lib.rs, additive): the HUD consumes VK_ESCAPE while a sheet is open
(Settings -> Menu, others -> close); otherwise Esc reaches the game as before. All VERIFIED on desktop 2026-11-05.

### Settings and zoom

Display entries call `crate::display::{cycle_mode, cycle_filter, cycle_fps}` (display agent, docs/porting/display.md).
VERIFIED: "FPS counter: FPS" turned the counter on (then top right; top centre since verify-fps1) and was saved in `mods-settings.json`.
Zoom - / + is still a placeholder (open as of 2026-11-05 wrap-up; pinch already uses res-zoom's `zoom.rs`) (`ui_hud::zoom_step` / `zoom_label`): it sends F1..F3 like
the pinch in touch.rs (`touch_logic::pinch_zoom_key`) and shows the game resolution as the level. Known issue: the
runtime F1-F3 switch in HUD mode shows a black band (below) — res-zoom's zoom replaces this.

### Running game actions

UI state changes are queued (`ui_hud_game::queue`) and run in a hook at `CLogicThread::HandleInput` entry
`0x524fa0` (logic thread, the place where the game changes the same state), so no state is written mid-tick:

| HUD action | Game side | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Building card -> placement | `[gd+0x2d284]=1`, cat, slot, type, panel dirty, then `gd::0x4ff3f0` (new placement-marker generation, what the panel click does at `0x526feb`). Without `0x4ff3f0` no markers are drawn and map taps cannot place (`0x4ff0a0` picks the nearest marker from the hit list) | VERIFIED (site placed) |
| Cancel placement | slot = 0, page 0 | VERIFIED |
| Move units | `s3_mods::set_right_next` -> the next map tap is a quick right click (passes the 15-step check at `0x53437d`) | VERIFIED (unit walked) |
| Deselect | UI selection count 0 + dirty, `[0x7dfd6c]` = 0, page 0 | STATIC |
| Destroy building | command `0x06` `{0x21, 0x06, 0x08, 0, id_hi, id_lo, player, 0}` posted with `Queue::Post 0x4309c0` on `[logic+0x3c4]` (`ndwords` 2, flag 1) | VERIFIED (Guard Tower destroyed, game reported "You've Lost") |
| Minimap widget drag / full map tap | `gd::CenterOn 0x51b560` | VERIFIED (view jumped / followed the drag, 2026-11-05) |
| Save | slot list `CLogicThread::0x50b670`, save `0x50ac40(0, slot)` (multiplayer: command 0xfa), no panel page | VERIFIED (slot 1 written and listed, 2026-11-08) |
| Quit | `0x53e720` like the panel's YES | VERIFIED |
| Building sheet | commands 0x04 (stop/resume), 0xf5/0xf6 (site priority), 0x0c (garrison), work area `0x523840` + sub-page 2 | VERIFIED except work area (STATIC) |
| Recruitment (settlers sheet) | command 0x10 at the view-centre tile, then `0x542630` | VERIFIED (geologist, pioneers) |
| Pause | key `P` (0x50) down/up into `m.input` | STATIC |
| Goods tab 1 (icon harvest only) | page 2 + `[gd+0x2d290]` = 1 behind the "Preparing" cover | VERIFIED |
| UI mode switch | `settings.ui_mode` saved with `s3_mods::set_settings`; the HUD goes inactive and restores the layout + panel | VERIFIED (panel back, Classic mode's Menu button shown) |

Load game: there is no in-game load in the original panel; the menu says "load: main menu" (quit, then Load).

### Reading game state (every 200 ms, `ui_hud_game::snapshot`)

`gd = [0x7e3408]` (checked: committed memory + vtable `0x658c18`); panel page/category/slot/type; local player and
race (`gd+0x11943e0 + p*0x148`); UI selection (`0x7dfd68`, `0x7ad620`, `0x7ad634`) with settler types from the settler
table; selected building `[0x7dfd6c]` + type; settlers per type of the local player; buildings of the player; goods
summed over the pile table.

- **Goods: only piles on the player's own land** (tile `+8` owner == local player). Without this filter a game against
  the AI showed exactly twice the Storage Area numbers (both start stocks). With it the numbers matched the panel's
  Inventory page (VERIFIED, one map).
- The panel's Inventory numbers are **not** a live sum of piles: writing pile amounts (debug poke of every good-1 pile)
  changed our sum but not the panel (VERIFIED). The panel keeps its own counters (not located; re-ui also did not find
  them).
- Good ids matched to the Inventory page by unique start amounts (`ui_hud_data::GOODS`): 4 Bread, 5 Coal, 7 Iron ore,
  8 Fish, 12 Shovel, 13 Hammer, 14 Axe, 15 Pickaxe, 16 Saw, 24 Meat (VERIFIED by amounts). 1/2 = Boards/Stone and
  17/32 = Scythe/Fishing rod have equal amounts at the start: order HYPOTHESIS. 3 = Logs HYPOTHESIS.
- Settler type names: all types mapped (2026-11-08, "Settler names and icons" below).
- Names come from the game's text tables through a hook on the string lookup `0x5faaa0` (records the table object,
  `ecx`), read host-side like `tools/re-ui/strings.py` (`ui_hud_game::text`). So they follow the game's language.
  Only tables 7, 8 and 9 are loaded in game. `S3_HUD_TEXT_DUMP=1` logs every string once (game data: local logs only).

### Icons sampled from the running game (nothing shipped)

On the first in-game frames (and when the race changes) the HUD lets the original panel draw each build category once
(page 1, cat 1..4) and then the goods Inventory page, and copies pixels from the presented frame before drawing:
build slot `2k+1` / `2k+2` = grid cols 1..19 / 21..39, rows `22+12k .. 31+12k` (game-state-ui.md), goods icon
`(row, col)` at `x = 14 + 18*col`, `y = 247 + 27*row`, 16x16 at 640x480 (measured; scaled by the grid cell for other
resolutions, which worked at 800x600), and last the settlers page tab Population (page 3 tab 1, harvest step
`SETTLERS_PAGE`): 12 settler icons at grid cols `1 + 10k`, rows `41 + 18r`, 8x12 cells (`ui_hud_data::pop_icon_rect`).
It takes 6 x 3 panel frames (well under a second, inside the start-up period); a "Preparing touch HUD" cover is drawn
meanwhile. The icons live only in memory.

### Settler names and icons (hud-settlers, 2026-11-08)

`ui_hud_data::settler_info(type, race)` gives every settler type a name, icon source, sort order and whether it is
part of the game's total (RE: [game-state-units.md](../reverse-engineering/game-state-units.md) "Settler types"):
carriers, diggers, builders, soldiers with level ("Swordsman L2"; Amazons "Swordswoman", ...), priests, geologists,
thieves, pioneers and donkeys use the Population tab icons; professions (woodcutter, miner, smith, baker, ...) use the
build-menu icon of their workplace (`build_slot_of`), war machines the race's siege workshop, ships the shipyard.
Names are English (the game has no settler-name texts). The settlers sheet lists the types in the Population tab's
order with icon + count (2..4 columns by width); the title and the "Pop" pill show the game's total (without ships,
war machines, donkeys and the tower figure 0x25, which is not listed). The selection card shows "icon 3 x Swordsman L1".
`S3_HUD_DEBUG=1` logs the game's own Population numbers against the HUD's at harvest time (`log_population_check`;
VERIFIED equal, 2026-11-08). `S3_HUD_SETTLER_DUMP=1` logs every 10 s all settler types per owner with their workplace
building type. Screenshots (local): `scratch/hud-settlers/s1.png` (Amazons, 2316x904), `s3.png` (selection card),
`s4.png` (2176x1812).

### Cover mode

When the full-screen map is off (menu toggle) or not possible yet (buffer too narrow, e.g. switching to HUD mode from
Classic mid-game until the next display setup), the HUD covers the panel below the minimap with a dark sidebar and
keeps the game's minimap usable.

```md
# UI modes compared: A "Classic Touch" vs B "Mobile HUD"

For the user: the two touch UIs side by side, so you can pick one (decision request from
[mobile-vision.md](mobile-vision.md)). Details: mode A [ui-classic.md](ui-classic.md), mode B [ui-hud.md](ui-hud.md),
shared map touch [touch.md](touch.md), framework [mods.md](mods.md). State: 2026-11-06, after ux-verify1.

Screenshots are **local only** (`scratch/` is gitignored, they contain game graphics). Paths are relative to the repo
root. Both modes run the unmodified GOG `S3.EXE`; everything is done by in-memory hooks (GOG sha256 `00a925cf…`
only; with another exe both modes stay off and the plain touch-to-mouse fallback is used).

## Shared by both modes (touch-context, W3)

Map gestures are the same in A and B, so switching modes does not change how you play on the map:

| Gesture | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Tap own unit / building | select (enlarged hit box) |
| Tap ground with units selected | move / attack (a quick right click; **no long press anywhere**) |
| Tap a marker in build mode | place the construction site |
| ✕ (A) / Cancel banner (B), two-finger tap | cancel placement / deselect |
| One-finger drag, two-finger drag | pan the camera, with inertia |
| Long press, then drag | box select |
| Pinch | resolution step 640x480 <-> 800x600 <-> 1024x768 (the game's F1-F3) |

## Side by side

| | **A "Classic Touch"** | **B "Mobile HUD"** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Look | The original game screen: left panel with minimap, tabs and build icons; a floating **Menu** button bottom right; a context chip top left ("Place: Woodcutter's Hut", "14 selected") | Full-screen map (the original panel is removed by a layout patch); the game's minimap top left; resource strip top right (Boards, Stone, Logs, Food, Pop); bottom bar Basic / Food / Military / Special / Settlers / Stats / Menu |
| Building | Tap the panel tab and icon. While the finger is down a 3x **magnifier bubble** shows the icon and the game's own name; lifting snaps the click to the button centre | Bottom **sheet with large cards** (icon + name, only your race's buildings), then a banner "Tap the map to place" with Cancel |
| Selected units / building | Original panel pages (units, building page) | Native **cards**: "14 selected: 10 x Swordsmen …" with Move to / Deselect; building card with Details / Destroy (tap twice) |
| Economy pages (goods, settlers, priorities, statistics) | Original panel pages, all reachable | Native goods/settlers summary sheets; deeper pages open the original page in a temporary "panel peek" with "Back to HUD" |
| Save / Quit / Pause | Menu -> original Save/Quit page | HUD menu: Resume, Save (panel peek), Pause, Quit, UI mode, full-screen on/off, HUD size -/+ |
| Map area at 640x480 | 504 px wide (panel takes ~21 %) | full 640 px |
| Touch targets | Panel icons are small (about 2.2x on a 1080p phone); the magnifier and snapping compensate | Bar buttons ~86x46, cards ~146x56 game px (about 2.25x on a 1080p phone) |
| Text / language | Game's own strings | Game's own strings (names read from the game's tables) |
| How much depends on our RE | Little: the original panel does the work; only the build pages and menu page are modelled for snapping | More: goods ids (some HYPOTHESIS), settler type names (partly "Type N"), stock summed from piles, layout patch of the landscape buffer |
| Switch to the other mode | Menu -> "UI: Mobile HUD" | Menu -> UI mode |

Android emulator shots of both modes (taps, also in a multiplayer game): `scratch/android-shots/ux1-*.png`
(list in [integration-log.md](integration-log.md), "Mobile UX verification 1").

## Pros and cons

**A "Classic Touch"**

- + Looks and plays exactly like the original; every panel page and feature works, because the game draws and
  handles it. Lowest risk of game-logic surprises.
- + Little RE needed, so it works the same for every race, page and future content.
- − Small icons; the magnifier helps, but browsing pages is slower than with big cards.
- − The panel takes a fifth of the screen width; on a phone the map is smaller.
- − Unmapped pages (units, building, messages, save slots) have no snapping and no names in the bubble.

**B "Mobile HUD"**

- + Big targets, full-screen map, feels like a mobile game (JSettlers-like); quickest to build and read stock.
- + HUD size scales (-/+), works at 800x600 too.
- − Covers only what we reverse-engineered; deeper pages fall back to the original panel ("panel peek").
- − Some data is HYPOTHESIS (a few good ids and settler names); the panel's own goods counters are not found, so
  stock is our sum over piles on your land.
- − Known glitches: runtime F1-F3 / pinch in HUD mode leaves a black band (start at 800x600 instead); after an
  in-game switch from A it covers the panel until the next game start; west map edge shows the void.

## Recommendation

Keep **A "Classic Touch" as the default** (it matches your stated preference to play on the original panel and is
the most complete and robust), and offer **B as a switch** in the in-game menu for players on small phones who want
the full map. Decide finally after a **real phone test**: if the panel icons are too small to read at 2.2x even with
the magnifier, make B the default for screens under ~6", or add the planned "enlarged panel" rendering to A.

```
