```md
# USER32, GDI32, ADVAPI32, WINMM and the small DLLs (HLE design)

Status: implemented 2026-11-05 (task `user-gdi-misc`). Code: `port/crates/s3-win32/src/`
(`user32.rs`, `gdi32.rs`, `font.rs`, `advapi32.rs`, `registry_store.rs`, `winmm.rs`, `audio_music.rs`, `ole32.rs`,
`rpcrt4.rs`, `shell32.rs`, `wsock32.rs`, `wininet.rs`, `comctl32.rs`, `comdlg32.rs`; tests in `user_gdi_tests.rs`).
General HLE rules: [architecture.md](architecture.md).

**First results (2026-11-05, headless `s3run` against the GOG install):**

- The game reaches the **main menu**, with all GDI text drawn by our font.
- An injected click on "Single Player: Scenario" opens **Game Setup** with no serial-number prompt.
- Clicking OK through the setup and lobby screens (`--inject "25000:click 165 235;45000:click 630 467;60000:click 730
  567;90000:click 730 567"`) starts a **random 384 map in game** at 640x480. Settlers, buildings and UI are
  visible after ~220 s wall time (10.7 G instructions).
- The game then plays CD track 7 through MCI (`play tracks 7..8`, notify to the CDAUDIO window), the same track
  as in the wine reference run.

## USER32

| Area | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Classes | `RegisterClassA/ExA` (atom `0xC000+n`, also looked up as `#atomXXXX`), `UnregisterClassA` |
| Windows | `CreateWindowExA` sends `WM_GETMINMAXINFO`, `WM_NCCREATE` (FALSE = fail), `WM_NCCALCSIZE`, `WM_CREATE` (-1 = fail), `WM_SIZE`, `WM_MOVE`, all via `call_guest` on the creating thread. With `WS_VISIBLE` (or later `ShowWindow`) it sends `WM_SHOWWINDOW`. The **first visible top-level window** also gets `WM_ACTIVATEAPP(1)`, `WM_NCACTIVATE`, `WM_ACTIVATE(WA_ACTIVE)` and `WM_SETFOCUS`, and becomes active and focused. HWNDs are `0x10010 + 0x10*n`; the desktop is `0x10008` |
| Geometry | Windows sit at (0,0). The client area is the whole window rect (no caption or borders, HYPOTHESIS: harmless under exclusive full-screen DirectDraw). `CW_USEDEFAULT` means full screen. `GetSystemMetrics(SM_CX/CYSCREEN)` returns the current display mode (default 800x600) |
| Display mode | s3-dx calls `user32::set_screen_size(m, w, h, bpp)` on `SetDisplayMode`. Full-screen top-level windows are resized and get a **posted** `WM_DISPLAYCHANGE` (HYPOTHESIS: Windows sends it synchronously) |
| Window longs | `GWL_WNDPROC/HINSTANCE/HWNDPARENT/ID/STYLE/EXSTYLE/USERDATA` plus `cbWndExtra` bytes (the S3 WndProc `0x610040` keeps its object pointer there) |
| Queues | One queue per guest thread (by tid), created on demand. `PeekMessage(PM_NOREMOVE)` creates it too (S3 uses this trick). Messages go to the queue of the thread that owns the window. `PostMessage(0, …)` is a thread message, `HWND_BROADCAST` posts to all top-level windows |
| Retrieval | Order: posted messages (with hwnd and range filter), then `WM_QUIT` (from `PostQuitMessage`), then `WM_PAINT` (a visible window that needs painting; the flag is cleared when the message is taken, so a WndProc that ignores it cannot cause a loop), then `WM_TIMER` (`SetTimer`; a timer proc goes in lParam and `DispatchMessage` calls it) |
| Blocking | `GetMessageA` and `WaitMessage` return `ThunkResult::Block` when nothing is queued. `MsgWaitForMultipleObjects` takes a signaled handle first, then returns `WAIT_OBJECT_0+n` if any message is queued (no "new since last check" rule), and honours its timeout. Host quit makes `GetMessage` return `WM_QUIT` |
| Sent messages | `SendMessageA/TimeoutA` call the WndProc directly on the calling thread, also for windows owned by other threads (HYPOTHESIS: good enough for S3). No WndProc means our `DefWindowProc` |
| DefWindowProc | `WM_NCCREATE`→1, `WM_ERASEBKGND`→1, `WM_NCACTIVATE`→1, `WM_NCHITTEST`→HTCLIENT, `WM_PAINT` validates, `WM_CLOSE`→DestroyWindow, Alt+F4 posts `WM_CLOSE`, everything else 0 |
| Input | Service `user32-input`, also run at every message call. New `HostEvent`s from `m.input` become `WM_MOUSEMOVE` (coalesced), `WM_L/R/MBUTTONDOWN/UP` (plus `DBLCLK` when the class has `CS_DBLCLKS`, within 500 ms and 4 px), `WM_KEYDOWN/UP` (`WM_SYSKEY*` while Alt is held or for F10) and `WM_CHAR`. They go to the capture window, else the active window. Mouse wParam = MK_* flags, lParam = client coordinates. Key lParam = repeat 1, set-1 scan code from a VK table, extended bit, bit 29 for Alt, bits 30/31 on key-up. Events from before the first window are dropped. A tap (move + down + up in one batch, as from `--inject click` and Android touch) gives exactly MOUSEMOVE, LBUTTONDOWN, LBUTTONUP at the tap position (test `tap_gives_one_press_per_tap`) |
| Chars | `TranslateMessage` builds `WM_CHAR` from `WM_KEYDOWN` with a US layout (Shift, Caps Lock, Ctrl+letter). It stops doing this once the host has sent a `HostEvent::Char`, to avoid duplicate characters |
| Key state | `GetAsyncKeyState` and `GetKeyState` read `m.input` (0xFFFF8000 when down; toggle bit for Caps, Num and Scroll Lock). `GetKeyboardState`, `MapVirtualKeyA` |
| Cursor | Drawn (2026-11-05, see [Cursor](#cursor-drawing)). `LoadCursorA/LoadImageA(IMAGE_CURSOR)` return fake handles `0xCC0000+id` (`LoadImageA` +0x40000, `LoadIconA` +0x20000, icons not decoded) and decode the image into `s3_runtime::cursor::CursorState`. `SetCursor`/`ShowCursor`/`ClipCursor` update it. `GetCursorPos` is the host mouse position clamped to `ClipCursor`. `SetCursorPos` moves only the emulated position (the drawn cursor follows it) |
| Painting | `BeginPaint/EndPaint/GetDC/ReleaseDC` give **pixel-less** window DCs (drawing on them is a no-op; S3 draws on DirectDraw surface DCs). `InvalidateRect/ValidateRect/UpdateWindow` |
| Text | `DrawTextA`: `DT_LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT`, `DT_VCENTER/BOTTOM` (single line), `DT_WORDBREAK` (also splits words longer than the line), `DT_SINGLELINE`, `DT_CALCRECT`, `DT_NOCLIP`, `&` prefixes (`DT_NOPREFIX`). Returns the text height |
| Misc | Rect helpers (`SetRect`, `IntersectRect`, `PtInRect` with POINT by value = 3 stack args, …), `wsprintfA` (cdecl) and `wvsprintfA` (flags `-0#`, width, precision, `h/l`, `d i u x X c C s S %`, 1023-char limit). `MessageBoxA` logs at Warn level and answers IDOK/IDYES/IDIGNORE, or IDCANCEL for retry/cancel boxes. `GetSysColor`, `SystemParametersInfoA(SPI_GETWORKAREA)`, `CharUpper/LowerA` |

How S3 reads clicks (input-ok-bug, 2026-11): the main thread (t0) runs a `GetMessageA` loop; its WndProc handles
`WM_MOUSEMOVE` (0x45bec5), `WM_LBUTTONDOWN` (0x45b698) and `WM_LBUTTONUP` (0x45b89e), converts with `ClientToScreen`
and wakes the GUI thread (t2) with `SetEvent` (handle of the UI event, from 0x430b64). After every message it calls
`IDirectInputDevice::GetDeviceData(cb=16, rgdod=NULL, ...)`, i.e. it only **flushes** the DirectInput buffer in menus,
so menu clicks come from window messages only. The UI button (0x41ab10 on button-up) fires its listener at
`[this+0x38]` (0x41a9b0) and a second one at `[this-0x10]`. Single Player has **three** OK screens: the map-selection
popup over Game Setup (OK at 630,467), Game Setup (OK at 730,567; handler 0x488300 builds the game parameters,
`CoCreateGuid` in 0x431ab0, then shows the players screen) and the players screen (OK at the same 730,567; handler
0x4955b0 message 10 -> 0x496c90 -> `PostThreadMessageA(t0, 0x801)` starts loading). The old report "first OK on the
players screen is ignored" was this miscount: the "first OK" was the Game Setup OK. Verified headless: one click per
OK, 1 s apart, reaches in game.

Exposed for other crates: `user32::screen_size`, `set_screen_size`, `post_message`, `send`, `pump_input`, `def_window_proc`.

## GDI32

- **Surface DCs (the interface with s3-dx).** `s3_runtime::gdi` (`port/crates/s3-runtime/src/gdi.rs`) defines
  `DcTarget { addr, pitch, width, height, bpp, rgb565 }`. In `IDirectDrawSurface::GetDC`, s3-dx calls
  `s3_runtime::gdi::create_dc(m, target)` on the locked surface memory. In `ReleaseDC` it calls
  `s3_runtime::gdi::release_dc(m, hdc)`. `gdi32::register` installs the implementation as a process-global hook.
- **Objects.** GDI handles are `0x00C0_0000 + 4n`; stock objects are `0x00BF_0000 + index`. Supported: fonts, solid
  brushes, pens, rectangular regions, bitmaps (DIB sections, compatible bitmaps) and palettes (dummies).
  `SelectObject` returns the previous object of the same kind. New DCs hold the stock 1x1 `DEFAULT_BITMAP`
  (`0x00BF_0015`), so the first `SelectObject(memDC, bitmap)` returns non-zero (S3.EXE at `0x4a8233` throws a C++
  exception -> "abnormal program termination" if it gets 0; found by integration r1 when opening the build menu).
  Selecting a region sets the clip. `DeleteObject`
  never deletes stock objects or DCs. `SaveDC/RestoreDC`.
- **Clipping.** `CreateRectRgn` + `SelectClipRgn` (the region is copied, NULL removes clipping) and `IntersectClipRect`.
  Every drawing call clips to the target bounds ∩ clip rect.
- **Text.** `TextOutA` and `ExtTextOutA` (`ETO_OPAQUE` fills the rect with the bk colour, `ETO_CLIPPED`) honour
  `SetTextAlign` (`TA_LEFT/RIGHT/CENTER`, `TA_TOP/BOTTOM/BASELINE`, `TA_UPDATECP`), `SetBkMode` (OPAQUE fills
  the text cell), `SetTextColor/SetBkColor` and the underline flag. Glyph coverage is alpha-blended into
  RGB565/555/24/32-bit targets (8-bit: threshold). Strings are Windows-1252.
- **Metrics.** `GetTextMetricsA` (TEXTMETRICA 56 bytes), `GetTextExtentPoint32A`, `GetTextExtentExPointA`
  (fit count + partial extents), `GetTextFaceA`.
- **Drawing.** `MoveToEx/LineTo/Polyline` (Bresenham, end point excluded, pen colour, `PS_NULL`), `Rectangle`,
  `FillRect` (also registered in user32, accepts `COLOR_x+1`), `PatBlt` (PATCOPY/BLACKNESS/WHITENESS),
  `Set/GetPixel`, `BitBlt/StretchBlt` (SRCCOPY with format conversion, nearest-neighbour stretch), `Ellipse`
  (filled bounding box, HYPOTHESIS: unused).
- **DIBs.** `CreateDIBSection` allocates the bits on the guest process heap. Bottom-up DIBs use a negative pitch.
  `BI_BITFIELDS` with green mask 0x7E0 means RGB565. `CreateCompatibleDC` + `SelectObject(bitmap)` draws into the
  bitmap. **1 bpp and 4 bpp** DIBs are packed MSB first (colour table assumed black/white resp. grey ramp; 1 bpp:
  luminance >= 128 -> 1). S3.EXE draws all in-game panel text and tooltips ("Save Game", "Quit Game", "Buildings",
  the save slot list) with `DrawTextA` into one 640x480x1 top-down DIB (white on black, OPAQUE) and uses the bits
  as a mask (`0x4a8100..0x4a8bfd`); before 2026-11-05 1 bpp was written as bytes and that text was invisible.
  Test `user_gdi_tests::draw_text_into_monochrome_dib`.
- `GetDeviceCaps`: 16 bpp, 96 dpi, `NUMCOLORS` -1, no `RC_PALETTE`, HORZRES/VERTRES = target or screen size.

### Fonts (`font.rs`)

The bundled font is **Liberation Sans** Regular/Bold (`port/crates/s3-win32/assets/fonts/`, SIL OFL 1.1, license
file next to it; copied from the system `ttf-liberation`). It is metric-compatible with Arial, which is close to
MS Sans Serif. It is rasterized with **fontdue**, and glyphs are cached per (size, bold, char).

- Every face name maps to it. Weight >= 600 uses the bold face.
- `lfHeight < 0` = em size in px, `> 0` = cell height (ascent+descent), `0` = 13 px cell.
- The registry `Font`/`FontSize` = "MS Sans Serif"/15 gives tmHeight 15.
- Advances are rounded per glyph like GDI; there is no kerning.

Observed: menu buttons, "Version 1.60" and the Game Setup labels render cleanly
(`scratch/ugdi-shot.png`, `ugdi-click.png`, local only). HYPOTHESIS: the original bitmap MS Sans Serif is a little
narrower. If long labels overflow, scale `px` down (one place: `font::metrics`).

## ADVAPI32 registry (`registry_store.rs`, `advapi32.rs`)

Lazy load on the first Reg* call. Later sources override earlier ones:

1. Built-in defaults: the `regs.cmd` values from [registry.md](../reverse-engineering/registry.md) **without**
   the serial number, plus `General\Playername`, `...\1.0\Patches\Convert`, and
   `HKCR\CLSID\{0e9f8400-d9a5-11cf-8f4d00804880b189}\Seed = 0x6a0f`.
2. **`regs.cmd` from the user's game dir, parsed at runtime.** It supplies `SingleNumber`; we never embed the
   serial. `%locpath%` becomes `C:\S3`.
3. `data_dir/registry.json`: values the game wrote. The file is pretty-printed, one object per key path, with
   `{"type": "dword"|"sz"|"binary"|n, "data": ...}`.

Rules:

- Lookups are case-insensitive. `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\X` is folded to `HKLM\SOFTWARE\X`.
- Key handles are kernel handles (`KernelObject::Other("regkey")`). Predefined HKEYs are roots.
- `RegQueryValueExA` follows the size protocol: NULL buffer = size only; too small = `ERROR_MORE_DATA` (234) plus
  the needed size; missing value = 2.
- `RegSetValueExA` saves the JSON at once (atomic rename).
- A write of `General\SingleNumber` is **ignored when a value exists**. The game rewrites it encrypted and the GOG
  exe cannot decode that (see [wine-trace.md](../reverse-engineering/wine-trace.md)).
- Also implemented: `RegCreateKeyExA` (disposition), `RegOpenKeyA`, `RegCreateKeyA`, `RegQueryValueA`,
  `RegSetValueA`, `RegDeleteKeyA`, `RegDeleteValueA`, `RegQueryInfoKeyA`, `RegEnumKeyExA`, `RegEnumValueA`,
  `RegFlushKey`.
- `GetUserNameA` returns the registry `Playername` (default "Player").

Without `regs.cmd` the game asks for the serial number in single player. The rewrite is then stored encrypted, so it
would ask again next time (HYPOTHESIS). Frontends should make sure `regs.cmd` is present.

## WINMM / `_INMM` (`winmm.rs`, `audio_music.rs`)

`_inmm.dll` is a registry alias of `winmm.dll`, so the game's `_INMM` imports land here, and the GOG wrapper DLL is
never loaded.

- **Time.** `timeGetTime` = host ms. `timeBeginPeriod/EndPeriod/GetDevCaps`, `timeGetSystemTime`.
- **`timeSetEvent`** (one-shot and periodic, `TIME_CALLBACK_FUNCTION` / `EVENT_SET` / `EVENT_PULSE`).
  - The first call creates a **guest timer thread** whose entry is our thunk `winmm.dll!__s3port_timer_thread`.
  - The thunk fires the due timers: `call_guest(cb, [id, 0, user, 0, 0])` or it sets the event. Then it returns
    `Block`, so the scheduler retries it every round.
  - Periodic timers do not burst more than 4 periods to catch up.
  - S3 only uses `timeSetEvent` when `GetProcAddress("CreateWaitableTimerA")` fails
    ([static-startup.md](../reverse-engineering/static-startup.md)). `timeKillEvent` stops a timer.
- **MCI CD audio**, used by S3 through `mciSendCommandA` (code at `0x615740`–`0x615fe6`):
  - `MCI_OPEN` with flags `0x2100`, type "cdaudio".
  - `MCI_SET` time format TMSF (10).
  - `MCI_STATUS` item 3 (number of tracks).
  - `MCI_PLAY` with `FROM` = track and `TO` = track+1 (if below the track count), plus `MCI_NOTIFY` to the hidden
    "CDAUDIO CALLBACKWINDOW" (WndProc `0x615bd0`, which forwards `MM_MCINOTIFY 0x3B9`).
  - `MCI_STOP`, `MCI_CLOSE`.
- **Our side of CD audio:**
  - Track N = `MUSIC\TrackNN.ogg` through the VFS. The GOG install has Track02–14, so the number of tracks is
    14 and track 1 is "data".
  - Playback decodes with lewton and plays tracks `from..to`.
  - When playback ends, `MM_MCINOTIFY(MCI_NOTIFY_SUCCESSFUL, devid)` is posted to the callback window.
    `SUPERSEDED` is posted on a new play, `ABORTED` on stop/close.
  - Status covers: length (via the last Ogg granule; no decoding), position, mode, media present/ready,
    current track, and track type.
  - The same commands work as **MCI strings** (`open cdaudio alias x`, `set x time format tmsf`, `play x from 3 to 4
    notify`, `status x number of tracks|mode|length [track n]|position`, `stop`, `pause`, `resume`, `close`,
    `close all`).
- **Videos** (`open AVIVideo!<file> alias test`, `status test window handle`, `window test handle …`,
  `play test window notify`, `close test wait`; also the briefing videos):
  - Any non-cdaudio device type is a **fake video**: open, window, status and `close` all succeed.
  - `play … notify` posts `MM_MCINOTIFY(SUCCESSFUL)` immediately, so the game continues as if the video ended.
  - OBSERVED: if the open fails instead, S3 shows *"Error during video play, please check for DirectX Media 6.0 and
    Intel Indeo video codec 5.06 or above (Error code 266)"* over the main menu.
- **Music output.** `audio_music::MusicPlayer::mix` adds music into any interleaved i16 buffer with linear
  resampling and a volume (default 0.6, HYPOTHESIS).
  - The service `winmm-music` decodes ahead into the shared mixer stream
    `m.state::<s3_runtime::audio::AudioStreams>().streams[winmm::MUSIC_STREAM_ID]` (44100 Hz stereo), keeping
    `LEAD_MS` = 300 ms queued (more than the DirectSound mixer's 250 ms max catch-up chunk, so music never runs dry
    after a slow slice). The s3-dx DirectSound mixer mixes it with the effects and is the **only** caller of
    `Host::queue_audio` (it runs as a service even if the game never creates DirectSound). `MCI stop`, `close`
    and a new `play` flush the queued music, so an old track does not linger. Because of the decode-ahead, the
    end-of-range `MM_MCINOTIFY` is posted up to ~300 ms before the last sample is heard (harmless).
  - Fixed 2026-11-05 (audio-verify): before, `winmm-music` called `Host::queue_audio` itself while the DirectSound
    mixer also did -> two producers, music blocks interleaved between effect blocks (2x audio per wall second).
  - `set_external_music_mixer(m, true)` + `mix_music(m, buf, rate, channels)` remain for a mixer that wants to
    pull music directly (then `winmm-music` produces nothing).
  - `S3_MUSIC_VOLUME=0..1` (env) overrides the default volume (debug/test knob; 0 isolates effects in a WAV).
  - Verified with `s3run --audio-wav` in game: track 7 continuous, -31/-28 dBFS RMS L/R, no clipping, no gaps
    (details in [directx-hle.md](directx-hle.md#audio-verification-s3run---audio-wav-2026-11-05)).
  - `auxSetVolume` sets the music volume.
- Other: `waveOutGetNumDevs`=1, `auxGetNumDevs`/`joyGetNumDevs`=0, `joyGetPosEx`=JOYERR_UNPLUGGED,
  `PlaySoundA`/`sndPlaySoundA` do nothing and return TRUE.

| ole32 | `CoInitialize(Ex)`/`OleInitialize`, `CoUninitialize`, `CoCreateInstance` (CLSID factories in `m.com`), `CoCreateGuid` (random v4), `CoTaskMemAlloc/Free` (process heap) |

## Open / HYPOTHESIS

- Cross-thread `SendMessage` runs on the sender's thread.
- `MsgWaitForMultipleObjects` wakes for any queued message (not only new ones).
- No non-client area.
- `WM_SETCURSOR` is never sent (DefWindowProc returns 0). Real Windows would send it on every mouse move and
  DefWindowProc would restore the class cursor (IDC_ARROW); the game sets its cursor explicitly instead, so
  not sending it keeps the game's cursor. HYPOTHESIS: harmless for S3.
- Music output verified on desktop via `s3run --audio-wav` (2026-11-05); audible on Android through the same
  DirectSound mixer -> `queue_audio` path.

## Cursor drawing

Code: `port/crates/s3-runtime/src/cursor.rs` (decoder, built-in arrow, `CursorState`, compose), user32
`load_cursor_a`/`register_cursor_image`/`set_cursor`/`show_cursor`/`clip_cursor`, `Machine::present` and
`Machine::refresh_cursor`.

- The game runs with `GDIMouse`=1 and uses the Windows cursor. `FUN_0045c3a0` (OBSERVED, decompiled) is its
  "set cursor" method: `SetCursor(LoadCursorA(NULL, IDC_ARROW))` first, then for id `-1` `ShowCursor(FALSE)`
  (hide), else `LoadCursorA(hinst 0x400000, id)` (cached by the game) and `SetCursor`. Ids seen: `0x73` (115,
  normal arrow, `RT_CURSOR` 3, hot spot 0,0) and `0x8B` (139, `RT_CURSOR` 8, hot spot 15,10, a "busy" shape).
- S3.EXE `.rsrc`: 9 `RT_GROUP_CURSOR` (112, 113, 115, 136-141), each with one 32x32 monochrome `RT_CURSOR` (308
  bytes: hot spot + 1 bpp DIB, XOR then AND mask).
- `LoadCursorA(hinst != 0, name)`: `RT_GROUP_CURSOR` -> entry closest to 32 px (ties: more bits) -> `RT_CURSOR`
  -> `decode_cursor_resource` (1/4/8/24/32 bpp DIBs, AND/XOR semantics: AND 0 = colour, AND 1 + XOR 0 = clear,
  AND 1 + XOR colour = screen XOR colour (white = invert), 32 bpp with alpha = blend). Not found -> warning, the
  handle is still returned (the game shows an error box for NULL) and nothing is drawn.
  `LoadCursorA(NULL, IDC_*)`: our own 12x19 arrow drawn from code (`builtin_arrow`, same for all IDC_* ids).
- Visible when `ShowCursor` count >= 0 and `SetCursor` handle != 0 and its image is known.
- Present: `Machine::present` copies the guest frame (host copy, guest memory untouched) and draws the cursor
  with its hot spot at `m.input.mouse_x/y` (clamped to `ClipCursor`), so every frontend gets it. The game does
  not re-present when only the mouse moves (menus are idle), so a "cursor" service (added at the first
  `SetCursor`) calls `Machine::refresh_cursor` once per `run_slice`: when position/shape/visibility changed it
  re-presents the last guest frame with the new cursor (not counted in `stats.presents`). Frontends can set
  `CursorState::disabled` to turn drawing off. The desktop minifb window hides the OS pointer.
- Verified 2026-11-05 headless (`scratch/cursor/*.png`, local): menu cursor at an injected (300,300) while the
  menu is idle; in game at (320,240) the drawn pixels match `RT_CURSOR` 3 exactly; over the build-menu icon at
  (25,167).

```

`docs/porting/x87-fpu.md`:

```md
# x87 FPU and MMX emulation (`s3-cpu`)

Code: `port/crates/s3-cpu/src/fpu.rs` (state + dispatch), `fpu_conv.rs` (pure numeric helpers: 80-bit/BCD
conversion, bit-exact f32<->f64, rounding/precision control, `ldexp`), `fpu_math.rs` (deterministic
transcendentals, exact `fprem`, x87 NaN rules, host FP environment check), `fpu_tests.rs` (hand-assembled
snippets, no game bytes), `fpu_golden.rs` (golden-vector determinism hashes). **Determinism contract:
[determinism.md](determinism.md)** — never call host libm / `%` on floats / let the host create NaNs in fpu*.rs.
Entry point: `fpu::exec(cpu, mem, ins) -> Option<R>`, called by `exec.rs` for every mnemonic the integer core does not
handle. `None` = not an FPU instruction / not implemented -> `FaultKind::Unimplemented`.

Instruction census that drove this: [static-isa.md](../reverse-engineering/static-isa.md) (~5 000 x87 instructions,
MMX only in one optional blitter).

## Model

| Part | How it is emulated |
| --- | --- |
| Registers | 8 x `f64` (`regs`, physical order), `top`, `st(i) = regs[(top+i)&7]` |
| Tag word | only empty / in-use is stored (`tags`, 2 bits per reg, 3 = empty). Full tags (valid/zero/special/empty) are computed by `tag_word()` for `fnstenv`/`fnsave` |
| Status word | `status` without TOP; `status_word()` merges TOP. C0-C3, IE/ZE/OE/PE/SF, ES/B |
| Control word | `control`. **RC honoured** by `fist`/`fistp`/`fisttp`(always trunc)/`frndint`/`fbstp`. **PC=24 bit** rounds arithmetic results (`+ - * / sqrt`, fyl2x) to a 24-bit significand (wide exponent kept); PC=53/64 both give f64 precision. Arithmetic itself always rounds to nearest |
| Stack faults | reading an empty `st(i)` -> IE+SF, C1=0, value = indefinite NaN; pushing onto an in-use slot -> IE+SF+C1, indefinite NaN pushed (masked response) |
| Exceptions | flags are set (IE for invalid, ZE for x/0, OE on overflow to inf, PE on inexact integer conversion/frndint). **Unmasked exceptions are not delivered** (no #MF / `EXCEPTION_FLT_*` SEH); only ES/B are set. HYPOTHESIS: the game never unmasks FPU exceptions (MSVC default CW 0x027F, all masked) |
| Last IP/DP | `last_ip` = address of the last non-control x87 instruction, `last_dp` = its memory operand; opcode field stored as 0 |

## Instructions

- Loads: `fld m32/m64/m80/st(i)`, `fild m16/m32/m64`, `fbld`, `fld1/fldz/fldpi/fldl2e/fldl2t/fldlg2/fldln2` (f64-rounded constants).
- Stores: `fst/fstp m32/m64/m80/st(i)`, `fist/fistp m16/m32/m64` (out of range or NaN -> integer indefinite 0x8000.. + IE), `fisttp`, `fbstp` (BCD indefinite on overflow).
- Arithmetic incl. reverse and pop forms and integer-memory forms: `fadd/fsub/fsubr/fmul/fdiv/fdivr` (+`p`, `fi*`). Operand roles come from iced's decoded operands (op0 = destination), so the `DC/DE` reg-reg encodings are correct without special cases.
- `fchs fabs fsqrt frndint fscale fxtract fprem fprem1 fsin fcos fsincos fptan fpatan f2xm1 fyl2x fyl2xp1`.
  - `fprem/fprem1` always produce the complete remainder (C2=0) by exact integer long division (`math::fprem`); quotient bits Q2/Q1/Q0 (exact for any exponent difference) go to C0/C3/C1.
  - Transcendentals use the pinned pure-Rust `libm` crate (fdlibm port), not the host libm; `f2xm1` uses an exact x*ln2 product (<= 1 ulp). See determinism.md.
  - trig: |x| >= 2^63 -> C2=1, operand unchanged (like hardware); inf -> IE + indefinite.
- Compares: `fcom/fcomp/fcompp/ficom/ficomp/fucom/fucomp/fucompp/ftst` (C3 C2 C0: > 000, < 001, = 100, unordered 111; fucom raises IE only for SNaN), `fcomi/fcomip/fucomi/fucomip` (ZF PF CF, OF SF AF cleared), `fxam` (C1 = sign; f64 subnormals report "normal" since they are normal in 80-bit), `fcmovcc`.
- Control: `fninit/finit`, `fnclex/fclex`, `fldcw`, `fnstcw`, `fnstsw ax/m16` (also the `9B` `fstsw` form iced decodes as one instruction), `fnstenv/fldenv` (28-byte and 14-byte protected-mode formats; fnstenv then masks all exceptions), `fnsave/fsave/frstor` (108/94 bytes: env + ST(0)..ST(7) as 80-bit in stack order; fnsave then does fninit), `ffree/ffreep/fincstp/fdecstp/fxch/fnop`, 287 no-ops (`fneni/fndisi/fnsetpm`). `fwait` is handled by the integer core as a no-op.
- MMX: `movq mm,mm/m64`, `movq m64,mm`, `movd mm,r/m32`, `movd r/m32,mm`, `emms`. MMX registers are a separate `mmx[8]`
  array (not aliased with the f64 x87 registers); any MMX op sets TOP=0 and all tags valid, `emms` empties them.
  XMM forms of `movq/movd` return `None`. No other MMX instructions are implemented.

## Precision limits (known differences from real hardware)

- 64-bit significand is reduced to 53 bits on every load from m80 and on every operation. Code that depends on extended
  precision (e.g. compares of `a*b` against a stored double) can differ in the last bit. HYPOTHESIS (from static-isa.md):
  game logic is integer, floats do not feed lockstep-synced state.
- Values outside the f64 exponent range (|x| > 1.8e308 or < 4.9e-324) become inf / 0 when loaded from m80.
- `fsin/fcos/fptan` use fdlibm (exact argument reduction, < 1 ulp), not the x87's 66-bit pi approximation.
- NaN results follow x87 rules (larger significand wins; invalid -> indefinite `0xFFF8...`), never the host's.
- Arithmetic ignores RC (always round-to-nearest).

## Notes for other agents

- STALE (fixed by cpu-int): `cpuid` now reports family 5 with **no MMX** (EDX bit 23 = 0), see [cpu.md](cpu.md).
  Old note: `exec.rs` `cpuid` reported MMX = 1; static-isa.md recommends 0. With MMX reported the
  surface-copy benchmark at 0x5c3740 may pick the MMX `movq` routine (0x5c3ee0); that routine only uses `movq` and
  `emms`, which are implemented, so either choice works.
- The SEH `CONTEXT.FloatSave` (s3-runtime) can be filled with the same layout as `fnsave` (108 bytes + Cr0NpxState);
  there is no helper for that yet.

```

```md
# Progress: cpu-int (x86-32 integer interpreter, crate s3-cpu except fpu*.rs)

Goal: a complete, exact and fast integer interpreter. Doc: docs/porting/cpu.md.

## Done
- Decode cache rewritten (arena + L1 array, cache moved out of the Cpu during run, no Arc).
```

```md
  stack dump: the "ignored" click ran the Game Setup OK handler 0x488300 (CoCreateGuid in 0x431ab0); the next click
  ran the players handler 0x4955b0 -> PostThreadMessageA(0x801) -> loading. Headless
  `--inject "1000:click 165 235;2000:click 630 467;3000:click 730 567;4000:click 730 567"` reaches in game at 25 s.
- How S3 reads menu clicks: window messages on t0 (WM_MOUSEMOVE/LBUTTONDOWN/UP -> SetEvent wakes GUI thread t2);
  DirectInput GetDeviceData with rgdod=NULL only flushes. Documented in docs/porting/user32-gdi32.md.
- Added `kernel32!IsProcessorFeaturePresent` (TRUE for 2 CX8 and 8 RDTSC, matching our CPUID; else FALSE) and
  `user32!GetLastActivePopup` (returns hwnd). No more "not declared" warnings.
- Test `s3-win32 user_gdi_tests::tap_gives_one_press_per_tap` (tap -> MOUSEMOVE, LBUTTONDOWN, LBUTTONUP, twice at
  the same spot; GetProcAddress + behaviour of the two new functions).
- Docs: status.md (known issues rows removed), android.md (flow + tap coords), integration-log.md (recipe comment),
  kernel32.md, user32-gdi32.md.
- Temporary S3_STACK stack dump in s3-runtime machine.rs was removed again (not kept).
```

`docs/progress/lan-mp.md`:

```md
# lan-mp: LAN multiplayer out of the box (embedded relay + UDP discovery)

Goal: host/join over LAN without a manually started relay (user report 2026-11-08).

## Design (decided)
- No `S3_RELAY_URL` / relay-url.txt => LAN mode. InitializeConnection starts an in-process relay
  (s3-relay lib, own thread + tokio runtime, 0.0.0.0:7777, fallback ephemeral port) and a UDP discovery thread
  (s3-net `lan.rs`, port 47777). Local NetClient -> own relay, so the "Type of Network" entry always works.
- Hosting (Open CREATE on the local relay): discovery announces "relay at port P, session name" (broadcast beacon
  every 1 s + unicast reply to queries). Clients broadcast queries every 1 s from an ephemeral socket (replies are
  unicast => allowed by Windows firewall's "unicast response to broadcast" default).
- EnumSessions merges local relay + every discovered relay; remembers instance -> relay client.
  Open JOIN switches the active client to that relay's client. Close -> back to local.
- Override URL set => old single-relay Internet mode.

## Done
- s3-net/src/lan.rs (Discovery, per-interface sockets, tests), s3-relay `spawn_background`, dplay_net `LanCtx`
  (LAN mode, connection name "Local network / Wi-Fi (Settlers 3 Port)"), s3run `log` output for net crates,
  s3-android wifilock.rs (MulticastLock via JNI hook) + manifest ACCESS_WIFI_STATE / CHANGE_WIFI_MULTICAST_STATE,
  mp-local-test.sh `LAN=1`.
- Desktop+desktop LAN run: `LAN=1 ... mp-local-test.sh scratch/lan3 100` -> joiner found host via UDP, connected to
  host relay, 946 ticks IDENTICAL. (scratch/lan2 run during an APK build: game did not start, timing only.)
- APK built (port/target/apk/settlers3port.apk in this worktree, signed with main debug.keystore).

- Phone (Fold4, host) <-> PC (headless s3run, join) over Wi-Fi: found, joined, 2326 ticks, phone orders executed on
  PC, no game desync (scratch/lanphone/). Docs: multiplayer.md section 8, journal, status.md.

## Status: DONE (committed on branch worktree-agent-a444c46f316eb6eac)
```

`docs/progress/overlay-window.md`:

```md
# Progress: overlay-window (window-resolution overlay layer)

Goal: mods (Mobile HUD, touch feedback, FPS counter, Classic floating UI) draw into a separate RGBA layer at WINDOW
resolution (constant on-screen size + sharp at every zoom); frontends composite it; guest frame = game pixels only.
Classic panel drawn at a constant on-screen scale (presenter + Viewport split). Lower zoom minimum (HUD).
Branch: worktree-agent-a4fc43414e521fc52. Scratch: C:\Users\<user>\Projects\settlers-3\scratch\overlay-window\.

## Design (decided 2026-11-08)
- Mods record a display list (`s3-mods/src/layer.rs`: `Layer` recorder, `DrawList` of commands with hashes) on the
  engine thread at present/refresh time (`MachineExt::window_overlay`); unchanged list = nothing to do. The list is
  published to a `SceneSlot` sink registered by the frontend; the frontend rasterizes it (`LayerRaster`, premultiplied
  RGBA at window size, only the dirty rect of changed commands) and composites (GL 2nd texture / CPU blend).
- `HostEvent::Pointer` gets window coords `wx, wy`; mods hit-test HUD in window px (`crate::touch_window_pos`).
- `Viewport.panel: Option<PanelSplit>`: Classic + NativeWide + zoom on + in game: panel region x<pw,y<art_h shown at
  win_h/art_h, map fills the rest; zoom width computed so the map keeps its aspect.

## Status
- 2026-11-08: reading code, design done. Next: s3-runtime event + ext changes.
- 2026-11-08 ~08:30: implemented (not committed yet): s3-runtime (Pointer wx/wy, ext.window_overlay, refresh
  only re-presents for frame overlays), s3-mods layer.rs (recorder + raster + SceneSlot; Canvas shares the
  rasterizer), display.rs (PanelSplit, Viewport::new_split/for_frame_split/quads/panel_scale, frame_viewport,
  panel_split), lib.rs (draw_window, draw_viewport, touch_window_pos, set_layer_sink, last_layer), mods ported:
  fps, debug_overlay, touch/touch_fx, ui_classic, ui_hud(+minimap); zoom: levels 200/240 added (DEFAULT 10,
  CLASSIC_MIN 7), res::MIN_H 200, classic_width + anchor_camera_map; s3-desktop: window layer blend, `wshot`,
  `w`-prefixed touch injects (viewport frozen while fingers down); s3-android: present.rs layer texture + split
  quads, touch window coords, Shared.layer. `cargo test -p s3-mods` OK; android `cargo check --target
  aarch64-linux-android` OK. Determinism s3det 90000: IDENTICAL to baseline (fast + JIT).
- 2026-11-08 ~09:30: verified headless (HUD 1536x600 / pinch in 760x296 / out; HUD min 512x200 with icons via
  harvest >= 480; Classic 1232x480 .. 2952x1200 panel constant, magnifier, panel tap through split viewport, Menu
```

```md
# perf-interp (2026-11-07) — DONE

Goal: speed up the s3-cpu interpreter with bit-exact results and identical retired-instruction counts (lockstep MP).
Owner: port/crates/s3-cpu only (+ docs). Write-up: docs/porting/performance.md "perf-interp", docs/porting/cpu.md.

## Done (branch worktree-agent-a8bc815ea88c16159)
1. Tail-call threaded dispatch inside blocks (`fast::next`, `block_end` sentinel, no per-op EIP store, branch
   handlers return directly, budget-truncated blocks via `exec::step` in `Cpu::run_partial`), lean run loop.
2. Fast forms: imul/mul/cdq/cwde, 8/16-bit + CL shifts, setcc r8, neg/not r32, inc/dec m32.
3. 32-byte `Op` (generic insn pointer in disp/imm), `Block::special`, Block `repr(C, align(64))`.
4. Boxed blocks + pointer chaining.
5. `cmp/test/dec + jcc` superinstructions (`fast::cmp_jcc`, `fuse_cmp_jcc`).
6. `DecodeCache::profile_pairs()`.
7. Tests: budget_stops_are_exact, mid_block_exits_count_exactly, *_forms_fast_vs_generic, cmp_jcc_fusion_fast_vs_generic.

- bench_mips 440 -> 1160 MIPS; s3det 90000 vms Cpu::run 16.6-18.8 s -> 9.7-9.8 s; s3run HUD 2316x904 93-102 -> 126-190 fps.
- s3det old (f0a50f7 s3-cpu) vs new: IDENTICAL (insns=11817005518), also with EFLAGS/FS/x87 last-IP+tags hashed.
- s3-mods tests (incl. fast_tests vs real exe) pass.
```

`docs/reverse-engineering/directx-surface.md`:

```md
# DirectX / COM surface used by S3.EXE (GOG)

Source: static analysis with REA/Ghidra 12.1.2 on 2026-11-05 (S3.EXE sha256 `00a925cf…`).
The game wraps **every** DirectX call in a helper that takes an error-context string like
`"CSurface::DDBlt"`. Those strings give an almost complete list of the methods used. Indirect vtable
calls can still hide extra methods, so confirm with a runtime trace (Wine `+ddraw,+dsound,+dinput,+dplay`).

## How each component is created (OBSERVED)

| Component | Creation | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DirectDraw | `CoCreateInstance(CLSID_DirectDraw {D7B70EE0-4340-11CF-B063-0020AFC2CD35}, NULL, CLSCTX_ALL=7, IID_IDirectDraw2 {B3A6F3E0-2B43-11CF-A2DE-00AA00B93356})`, then vtable `+0x48` = `IDirectDraw2::Initialize(guid)` | `FUN_005bec00` |
| DirectDraw enumeration | `LoadLibraryA("ddraw.dll")` + `GetProcAddress("DirectDrawEnumerateA")` | `FUN_005beb90` |
| DirectSound | `LoadLibraryA("dsound.dll")` + `DirectSoundCreate` | `FUN_005c1d20` |
| DirectInput | `LoadLibraryA("dinput.dll")` + `DirectInputCreateA(hinst, 0x0300 /*DX3*/, …)`, then `CreateDevice` (vtable +0x0C) | `FUN_005b9ec0`, called from `0x411540`, `0x5ba230` |
| DirectPlay | COM `CoCreateInstance` at `0x5c0808` / `0x5c0847` (CLSIDs not decoded yet). Error string `"DirectPlay 6.0 nicht installiert"` → needs **DirectPlay 6** (`IDirectPlay4` + lobby `IDirectPlayLobby3`, HYPOTHESIS) | |

So the HLE must provide a **COM `CoCreateInstance`** (ole32) that hands out our own DirectDraw/DirectPlay objects,
plus fake `ddraw.dll` / `dsound.dll` / `dinput.dll` modules for `LoadLibraryA` + `GetProcAddress`.

## Methods named in error strings (OBSERVED)

| Interface | Methods |
| --- | --- |
| IDirectDraw2 | Initialize, SetCooperativeLevel, SetDisplayMode, GetDisplayMode, RestoreDisplayMode, EnumDisplayModes, CreateSurface, WaitForVerticalBlank (+ DirectDrawEnumerateA) |
| IDirectDrawSurface | Lock, Unlock, Blt, BltFast, Flip, GetAttachedSurface, GetSurfaceDesc, IsLost, Restore, GetDC, ReleaseDC |
| IDirectDrawPalette | used (RTTI `CPalette`), methods not named — check |
| IDirectSound | SetCooperativeLevel, CreateSoundBuffer, DuplicateSoundBuffer |
| IDirectSoundBuffer | Lock, Unlock, Play, GetStatus, Restore, GetVolume, SetVolume, SetPan |
| IDirectInput / Device (DX3) | CreateDevice, SetDataFormat, SetCooperativeLevel, SetProperty, SetEventNotification, Acquire, Unacquire, GetDeviceData (buffered input) |
| IDirectPlay(4?) | EnumConnections, InitializeConnection, EnumSessions, Open, Close, GetSessionDesc, SetSessionDesc, GetCaps, CreatePlayer, DestroyPlayer, EnumPlayers, GetPlayerData, SetPlayerData, Send, Receive, GetMessageCount |
| IDirectPlayLobby | Connect, CreateCompoundAddress, GetConnectionSettings, SetConnectionSettings |

`GetDC`/`ReleaseDC` on surfaces → GDI text drawing onto DirectDraw surfaces (fonts from registry `Font`/`FontSize`).
Our GDI HLE must rasterise text into the surface memory.

## Port implications

- DirectDraw part is a classic 2D software-rendered game: lock surface, write pixels, flip. HLE = surfaces in guest
  memory + upload the front buffer to a GPU texture on Flip.
- DirectInput is real (buffered mouse/keyboard via `GetDeviceData`). Touch must be translated into
  DIDEVICEOBJECTDATA events, **and** window messages (registry `GDIMouse`=1 suggests the cursor is GDI-drawn).
- DirectPlay only for multiplayer → stub with "not available" first (keep single player working), implement later.

## Static details for the HLE (2026-11-05, static RE pass; see also [static-startup.md](static-startup.md))

All addresses are VAs in GOG `S3.EXE`. Wrapper functions throw a C++ exception (`CDirectXException`-like, via
`0x5be180` + `__CxxThrowException 0x61f027`) on any failing HRESULT except `DDERR_WASSTILLDRAWING (0x8876021C)`,
which the callers retry.

### DirectDraw

- **SetCooperativeLevel** (`0x404e43`, IDirectDraw2 vtbl `+0x50`): `(hwnd, 0x13)` =
  `DDSCL_FULLSCREEN | DDSCL_ALLOWREBOOT | DDSCL_EXCLUSIVE`.
- **SetDisplayMode** (IDirectDraw2 vtbl `+0x54`, 5 args `w, h, bpp, refresh=0, flags=0`):
  - first call at startup `0x404ebd` uses the settings object `0x7a7af0`: width `+0x8C`, height `+0x90`, bpp `+0x94`;
    defaults set at `0x40d25a`: **800 × 600 × 16**. Command line `-messe` (`0x410e23`) forces **640 × 480**.
  - mode switch by index (`0x405c80`, used for the registry value **`Resolution`**, read at `0x40deb8` into settings
    `+0x70` and clamped to 0..2): **0 → 640×480×16, 1 → 800×600×16, 2 → 1024×768×16**. Always **16 bpp**.
  - `GetDisplayMode` first; if the current mode already matches it logs `"GFX: Skipping SetDisplayMode"` (`0x42cf2b`).
- **No 8-bit/palette path in the main renderer**: no `CreatePalette`/`SetPalette`/`SetColorKey` calls exist in the
  DirectDraw module (`0x5be000-0x5c0000`); vtable offsets used there are only Initialize, SetCooperativeLevel,
  SetDisplayMode, GetDisplayMode, RestoreDisplayMode, EnumDisplayModes, CreateSurface, WaitForVerticalBlank and
  surface Blt/BltFast/Flip/GetAttachedSurface/GetSurfaceDesc/Lock/Unlock/IsLost/Restore/GetDC/ReleaseDC.
  Sprites are drawn in software (the game's own blitters, incl. shadow/alpha with masks `0x7BEF/0x39E7/…`), so
  **no colour keys** are needed. (RTTI `CPalette` exists but no call site was found — HYPOTHESIS: dead or video-only.)
- **Surface creation** (`CreateSurface` IDirectDraw2 vtbl `+0x18`, wrapper `0x5bec80`; DDSURFACEDESC `dwSize=0x6C`):

  | Ctor / create | dwFlags | ddsCaps | Use |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `0x5bf800` primary | `DDSD_CAPS` (+`DDSD_PIXELFORMAT` 0x1000 if a format is given) | `DDSCAPS_PRIMARYSURFACE` (0x200) \| extra | front buffer |
  | `0x5bf9b0` flipping primary | `DDSD_CAPS\|DDSD_BACKBUFFERCOUNT` (0x21), `dwBackBufferCount=1` | `PRIMARYSURFACE\|FLIP\|COMPLEX` (0x218) | `lpFlipPrimary`; back buffer via `GetAttachedSurface` (`0x5bfa52`) |
  | `0x5bfaf0` / `0x5bfbc0` offscreen | `DDSD_CAPS\|DDSD_HEIGHT\|DDSD_WIDTH` (7) (+PIXELFORMAT) | `DDSCAPS_OFFSCREENPLAIN` (0x40) \| extra, e.g. **`DDSCAPS_SYSTEMMEMORY` (0x800)** | back buffer / work surfaces |

- **Presentation mode** (draw thread, `0x42e4f0`–`0x42e830`; log `"DRAW: Flags %i %i %i %i"`), chosen by settings bytes
  `0x7a7af0+0x5A` (getter `0x4122b0`) and `+0x5B` (getter `0x4122c0`), both default 1 (`0x40d1f4/0x40d1f8`) and
  overridden from the registry (`0x40daa2`… — HYPOTHESIS: the `NoFlip` value; string `0x695a38`):
  1. `+0x5B` set (**default**): primary surface + **offscreen back buffer in system memory (caps 0x800)**; the game
     renders into the back buffer (Lock) and copies it to the primary with **`Blt`** (`0x5bf0f8`, flags
     `|= DDBLT_ASYNC|DDBLT_WAIT` = `0x1000200`) of rect `(0,0,w,h)` (`0x730f0c` = width, `0x730f10` = height);
     before that, if `WaitVBlank` (`+0x5C`, getter `0x4122e0`) is set, `WaitForVerticalBlank(DDWAITVB_BLOCKBEGIN, 0)`
     (`0x42cddb`); if that throws, the catch block clears `+0x5C`.
  2. `+0x5B` clear, `+0x5A` set: primary + offscreen (no forced system memory), Blt.
  3. both clear: flipping chain (`0x5bf9b0`), **`Flip(NULL, 0)`** retried with `Sleep(0)` while
     `DDERR_WASSTILLDRAWING` (`0x5bf710`/`0x5bf740`).
  HLE plan: implement surfaces as plain guest memory; Blt to primary or Flip = "present" → upload the 16-bit
  front image to a GPU texture. `BltFast` (`0x5bf15d`) adds `DDBLTFAST_WAIT (0x10)`.
- **Pixel-format check → GFX file choice** (GFX loader `0x5f9ff2`): reads the R/G/B masks of the display format
  (object fields `+0x14/+0x18/+0x1C`):
  - `F800/07E0/001F` (RGB565) → shadow/blend masks `0x7BEF, 0x39E7, 0x18E3, 0x0861, 0x0020` (`0x7e8dd8…`);
  - `7C00/03E0/001F` (RGB555) → masks `0x3DEF, 0x1CE7, 0x0C63, 0x0421, 0`;
  - anything else → error path (`0x5fa106`).
  File names are `"siedler3_" + NN + "." + mask suffix + ".dat"` in `.\Gfx` (strings `0x7a2d8c/0x7a2d98/0x7a2da4`,
  wildcard `"siedler3_??."` at `0x7a2dac`); the suffix is the three masks in lowercase hex without padding:
  **`f8007e01f` = 565, `7c003e01f` = 555** (HYPOTHESIS for the exact formatting code; matches the file names on disk:
  47 `*.f8007e01f.dat` + 45 `*.7c003e01f.dat`, ≈117 MB each set). On disk the 565 set is `Siedler3_NN…` and the 555
  set `siedler3_NN…` → **the HLE file system must be case-insensitive**. The files are **memory-mapped**
  (`CreateFileMappingA` + `MapViewOfFile`, class at `0x61a5xx`) and pre-faulted with the `VirtualProtect` page-touch
  helper `0x61ab60`. Recommendation: report RGB565 (masks `F800/07E0/001F`) — it matches Android `RGB_565`.
- CPU-dependent surface copy: `0x5c3740` benchmarks 4 (5 with MMX) copy routines with QPC and keeps the fastest
  ([static-isa.md](static-isa.md) §8).

### DirectSound (`dsound.dll` via `LoadLibraryA`, `DirectSoundCreate` at `0x5c1d4e`)

- `SetCooperativeLevel(hwnd, DSSCL_PRIORITY = 2)` (`0x5fe96d`, IDirectSound vtbl `+0x18`).
- **Primary buffer** (`0x5c21c0`): `DSBUFFERDESC{dwSize=0x14, dwFlags=0x81 = DSBCAPS_PRIMARYBUFFER|DSBCAPS_CTRLVOLUME,
  dwBufferBytes=0, lpwfxFormat=NULL}`. **No `SetFormat` call** (no wrapper/error string, no vtbl `+0x38` call) →
  the primary format is whatever the device default is; the game only uses it for master volume.
- **Secondary buffers** (`0x5c2220`): `dwFlags=0xE0 = CTRLFREQUENCY|CTRLPAN|CTRLVOLUME`, size and `WAVEFORMATEX`
  from the sound data; `DuplicateSoundBuffer` (vtbl `+0x14`) for repeated effects. Methods: Lock/Unlock/Play/
  GetStatus/Restore/GetVolume/SetVolume/SetPan. A down-conversion mode exists (`0x5c26d8`: when the `SoundFormat`
  mode is 4 and the sample is ≥ 22050 Hz 16-bit, it halves rate and converts to 8-bit — HYPOTHESIS on the registry link).

### DirectInput (DirectX 3, `dinput.dll`)

- One device: **`GUID_SysMouse` {6F1D2B60-D5A0-11CF-BFC7-444553540000}** (`0x65b388`, created at `0x5ba233`).
  No keyboard device (keys come from `WM_KEYDOWN/UP/CHAR`).
- `SetDataFormat` with the in-exe copy of **`c_dfDIMouse`** (`0x62ef60`: `dwSize 0x18, dwObjSize 0x10,
  dwFlags DIDF_RELAXIS (2), dwDataSize 16`, 7 objects: X/Y/Z axes at 0/4/8, buttons 0–3 at 12–15).
- `SetCooperativeLevel(hwnd, 6 = DISCL_NONEXCLUSIVE | DISCL_FOREGROUND)` (`0x404f81`).
- `SetEventNotification(hEvent)` and `SetProperty(DIPROP_BUFFERSIZE (1), DIPROPDWORD{0x14,0x10,0,DIPH_DEVICE,
  dwData = 128})` (`0x404f18`–`0x404f9a`) → **buffered, 128 events**.
- Main thread reads with `GetDeviceData(sizeof(DIDEVICEOBJECTDATA)=16, buf, &n /*2*/, 0)` (`0x5ba290`) whenever
  the event is signalled (§3 of static-startup). Touch → relative X/Y axis events + button 0/1 events, *and*
  `WM_MOUSEMOVE/WM_LBUTTON*` window messages (cursor position).

### DirectPlay (multiplayer only)

| Site | rclsid | riid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0x5c0808` | `{D1EB6D20-8923-11D0-9D97-00A0C90A43CB}` = **CLSID_DirectPlay** | `{0AB1C531-4745-11D1-A7A1-0000F803ABFC}` = **IID_IDirectPlay4A** |
| `0x5c0847` | `{2FE8F810-B2A5-11D0-A787-0000F803ABFC}` = **CLSID_DirectPlayLobby** | `{1BB4AF80-A303-11D0-9C4F-00A0C905425E}` = **IID_IDirectPlayLobby2A** |
| `0x5bec16` | `{D7B70EE0-4340-11CF-B063-0020AFC2CD35}` = CLSID_DirectDraw | `{B3A6F3E0-2B43-11CF-A2DE-00AA00B93356}` = IID_IDirectDraw2 |

All with `CLSCTX_ALL (7)`. Names from `dplay.h`/`dplobby.h`/`ddraw.h` (memory; GUID values decoded from the exe with
`python3 -I` + `pefile` + `uuid.UUID(bytes_le=…)`). HLE: `CoCreateInstance` for the DirectPlay CLSIDs can return
`REGDB_E_CLASSNOTREG`; the game then shows "DirectPlay 6.0 nicht installiert" only when entering multiplayer
(HYPOTHESIS: confirm that single player does not create it at startup).

```

`docs/reverse-engineering/game-state-ui.md`:

```md
# Game state RE part 2: camera, screen layout, left panel, cursor modes, menus, resources, text (W2)

Target: GOG `S3.EXE` sha256 `00a925cfdcfc3349b5d0f3b8a4c312f01b813e363b4464f6f3d6de17804d950b` (all addresses for this
exe only). Workstream W2 of [mobile-vision.md](../porting/mobile-vision.md). Part 1 (units, buildings, selection,
commands, click dispatch, settler/building/pile tables): [game-state-units.md](game-state-units.md).

Status words: **VERIFIED** = seen at runtime in s3run (2026-11-05, re-ui task); **STATIC** = read from code, not
exercised; **HYPOTHESIS** = a guess. No decompiled code is reproduced here, only addresses, layouts and behaviour.

Names used below:

- `gd` = `CGameData` = `[logic+0x3a0]` (part 1). Also `*(0x7e3408)` (= `*(0x7e7b60)`). `0x18790000` in every s3run run
  so far (deterministic in our emulator; mods should take it from the ctor hook `0x4fc990` instead of hard-coding).
  **In a multiplayer game `*(0x7e3408)` stays 0** (VERIFIED 2026-11-05 ux-verify1, host and joiner); `[logic+0x3a0]` is
  valid there, so mods use it as the fallback (`touch_game::gd`).
- `logic` = `CLogicThread` (part 1). `HandleInput` = `0x524fa0` (thiscall logic), runs on the logic thread.
- `gfx` = the render-side screen object (`new 0x5f700` at `0x42c6b9`, ctor `0x42c820`, vtable `0x656aec`; `0x1011def8`
  in s3run). Owns the string table `[gfx+0x5f6b8]` and the text renderer `[gfx+0x5f6e0]`. Runs on the render thread.
- `snap` = the per-frame UI snapshot that the logic thread fills for the renderer (`[logic+0x3d0]`, function `0x51f110`).

## Summary for hook / HUD authors

| Need | How | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Camera position | `[gd+0x2d25c]` x, `[gd+0x2d260]` y (world pixels, top-left of the map view). Write, then the clamp `0x51b4d0` (thiscall gd) | VERIFIED (poke moves the view) |
| Center camera on a tile | `0x51b560` thiscall gd, `(x, y)` stdcall (`ret 8`); clamps itself | STATIC (used by minimap click, hotkeys) |
| Scroll step | arrow keys: +-40 px (`0x525977..`) | VERIFIED (Up: y `0x5e7 -> 0x5bf`) |
| Screen layout per resolution | globals `0x730f08..0x730f40`, set by `0x4c6d70(resIndex)` (table below) | VERIFIED (all three) |
| Bigger map view ("zoom out") | switch to 800x600 / 1024x768 at runtime: F2 / F3 (F1 = 640x480), or registry `Resolution` 1 / 2; the port runs any size up to 3200x1200 ([resolution-zoom.md](../porting/resolution-zoom.md), section "Resolution internals" below) | VERIFIED |
| Panel page | `[gd+0x2d284]`: 1 build, 2 goods, 3 settlers, 4 building selected, 5 units selected, 7 Save/Quit menu, 8 messages, 9 paused | VERIFIED (1, 2, 3, 7, 9; 4/5 from part 1) |
| Build category / slot / type | `[gd+0x2d288]` cat 1..4, `[gd+0x2d28c]` list slot (0 = none), `[gd+0x2d2f0]` building type | VERIFIED |
| Start build placement for type T | write page 1, cat, slot, type T, then `[gd+0x2d27c] = 1`; the next map left-click places a site | VERIFIED (site count 6 -> 7) |
| Open the in-game menu | page 7, `[gd+0x2d298] = 0`, `[gd+0x2d27c] = 1` (ESC is not a hotkey) | VERIFIED |
| Redraw panel | `[gd+0x2d27c] = 1` ("panel dirty") | VERIFIED |
| Tooltip text id | `[logic+0x54]` (set by the hover pass of HandleInput) -> `snap+0x270` -> drawn by `0x4b3de1..` | STATIC + VERIFIED text ids |
| Text id -> string | `0x5faaa0` thiscall `[gfx+0x5f6b8]`, `(id, lang = -1)`, returns `char*`; id = `table<<16 | index` | VERIFIED (resolver `tools/re-ui/strings.py`) |
| Building names | text `0x80000 + type` (table 8) | VERIFIED |
| Goods in stock | sum of `amount` over the pile table (part 1) by good | VERIFIED (one map, panel = sum) |
| Panel renderer | `0x4b4d00` thiscall gfx, `(snap)`; called from the frame renderer at `0x4b2dc5` | STATIC |
| In-game message lines (tutorial text, chat, notices) | ring `logic+0x414` (5 x 0x1c, UTF-16); drawn by `0x4d82b0` + `0x4d8400` (skip both to hide); tutorial arrow = `[gd+0x2d304] = 1`; section 7 | VERIFIED |
| Safe place to change UI state | a hook at `HandleInput` entry `0x524fa0` (logic thread, before input is processed) | STATIC (s3run pokes between slices also worked) |

## 1. Camera and viewport

### Camera

| Field | Meaning | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gd+0x2d25c` | camera x, world pixels (left edge of the map view) | VERIFIED (poke moves the view) |
| `gd+0x2d260` | camera y, world pixels (top edge) | VERIFIED |
| `gd+0x2d254`, `gd+0x2d258` | second copy (equal to the above when idle; HYPOTHESIS: the value of the previous frame / scroll origin) | VERIFIED values |
| `gd+0x2d264` | cleared by arrow-key scrolling (HYPOTHESIS: "follow"/scroll-to target active) | STATIC |
| `gd+0x2d2d0` | world size `W` in tiles (384 on a 384 map) | VERIFIED |

- **Clamp** `0x51b4d0` (thiscall gd, no args): `x` into `[0, 24*W + 0x167 - mapW]`, `y` into `[0, 9*W + 0x176 - mapW]`
  where `mapW = [0x730f18]` (yes, the y limit also uses the view width in this build). Call it after writing the camera.
  **Patched 2026-11-07** (gog-base, `0x51b528` `mov edi,[0x730f18]` -> `[0x730f1c]`): with our wide custom
  resolutions (mapW ~1400-2500) the y limit collapsed; on the small tutorial map the camera could not go below
  the upper half (user report). Now `y` into `[0, 9*W + 0x176 - mapH]` (VERIFIED on the phone: tutorial pans to
  the south coast). The host clamp `touch_logic::clamp_camera` uses `map_h` the same way.
- **Center on tile** `0x51b560` (thiscall gd, `(tx, ty)`, `ret 8`): `x = (W + 2*tx + 24 - ty)*8 - mapW/2`,
  `y = 9*ty + 200 - mapH/2 - height(tx,ty)` with `height` = byte `gd+0x67448 + (tx*768+ty)*0x18` (tile +4) and
  `mapH = [0x730f1c]`; then calls the clamp. Callers: minimap click (`0x525438`), `0x4fef2d`, `0x51b6d4`, `0x526a90`,
  `0x52e1ef` (HYPOTHESIS: "go to event" from a message).
- Tile geometry implied by these formulas: a tile is 16 px wide (x step 8 per half tile), rows are 9 px high, rows are
  sheared (x shifts by 8 px per row). The renderer converts camera pixels to a first tile column with `/16` and row
  with `/18` in `0x51f9xx` (STATIC). Exact map -> screen formula for HUD markers: still open (see part 1).
- **Scrolling**: arrow keys (VK 0x25..0x28) change the camera by 40 px and clamp (`0x525977`, `0x5259b1`, `0x5259ea`,
  `0x525a0a`); right-drag scroll is in HandleInput (part 1, `[0x7dfd80]`). Edge scrolling: not looked at.
- Two-finger pan for touch: write `x/y` (`+0x2d25c/+0x2d260`) on the logic thread and call `0x51b4d0`, or keep
  `delta` in host and write absolute values each frame. Centering: call `0x51b560`.

### Screen layout per resolution (`0x4c6d70(resIndex)`, stdcall, `ret 4`)

Panel grid: the left panel is a grid of `cell x cell` pixel cells; `col = (x - [0x730f3c]) / cell`,
`row = (y - [0x730f40]) / cell`, 40 columns (0..0x27) x 106 rows (0..0x69). All panel buttons are defined in grid
units, so **the same (col,row) works at every resolution**.

| Global | Meaning | 640x480 | 800x600 | 1024x768 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0x730f08` | resolution index + 1 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
| `0x730f0c` / `0x730f10` | screen width / height | 640 / 480 | 800 / 600 | 1024 / 768 |
| `0x730f24` | panel width (x < this = panel or minimap) | 136 | 176 | 216 |
| `0x730f18` / `0x730f1c` | map view width / height (`= screen - panel`, full height) | 504 / 480 | 624 / 600 | 808 / 768 |
| `0x730f2c` / `0x730f30` | minimap origin x / y | 5 / 10 | 8 / 5 | 6 / 8 |
| `0x730f28` | minimap width (in pixels; the map is drawn as a sheared parallelogram) | 128 | 160 | 208 |
| `0x730f34` | minimap bottom y | 142 | 170 | 224 |
| `0x730f38` | panel grid cell size (px) | 3 | 4 | 5 |
| `0x730f3c` / `0x730f40` | panel grid origin x / y | 8 / 152 | 8 / 171 | 8 / 228 |
| `0x730f14` | 16 (HYPOTHESIS: tile width) | 16 | 16 | 16 |
| `0x730f20` | 437 / 540 / 697 (HYPOTHESIS: top of the bottom button bar region) | 437 | 540 | 697 |

Values VERIFIED with `peek 0x730f08` at 640x480, 800x600 (`Resolution=1`) and 1024x768 (F3). `[0x7dfd58]` is cleared
by the same function.

- **Minimap hit test** (HandleInput `0x52537b..`): `y < [0x730f34]` and
  `[0x730f2c] + d < x < [0x730f24] + d` with `d = ([0x730f34] - y)/2` (sheared). Tile:
  `ty = W*(y - [0x730f30]) / [0x730f28]`, `tx = W*((y - [0x730f30])/2 - [0x730f28]/2 - [0x730f2c] + x) / [0x730f28]`,
  then `0x51b560(tx, ty)` (STATIC).
- **Minimap image and drawing** (REA static + VERIFIED in s3run 2026-11-05, hud-polish): the minimap is a square
  RGB565 image of `mw x mw` pixels (`mw = [0x730f28]`) at `[snap+0x4c]` (`snap` = render snapshot, arg of the frame
  renderer `0x4b26c0` and of the panel renderer `0x4b4d00`); column `c` / row `r` = tile `(c*W/mw, r*W/mw)`. The
  frame renderer copies it into the back buffer `[gfx+0xec]` (pitch `[gfx+0x90]` bytes) sheared:
  `x = mx + (mw - r - 1)/2 + c`, `y = my + r`. Block `0x4b2b34..0x4b2ce5`: incremental copy in 64 interleaved chunks
  (per-chunk counters `0x7ad4f8[64]`, "dissolve"; full copy when `[snap+0x3c] == 1`). Block `0x4b366a..0x4b3cf3`:
  copies the minimap part at `x >= [0x730f24]` (over the map) every frame, draws the frame art (gfx resources
  `0x40001` at `(panelW, 0)`, `0x40003` at `(panelW, [0x730f34])`), then erases the previous camera rectangle
  (`gfx+0x5f6a4..b0`, from the image) and draws the new one in white (`0xffff`) and stores it (`gfx+0x5f694..a0`).
  Camera rectangle in image coordinates (`0x4b3a3c`): `k = (mw << 8) / [snap+0x2c]`,
  `x = ([snap+0x24] + 11)*k >> 8`, `y = ([snap+0x28] + 16)*k >> 8`, `w = [snap+0x30]*k >> 8`,
  `h = ([snap+0x34] - 40)*k >> 8` (signed, truncating). At `0x4b3aba` the results are in x `[ebp-0x1c]`, y `esi`,
  w `[ebp-0x2c]`, h `[ebp-0x44]` (`ebp+8` = snap); the port's `res:minimap-rect` hook rescales them there. After `0x4b3cf3`: the drag-selection box (`0x7dfd34`,
  `0x7dfb98..`). Skipping both blocks (jump) hides the minimap without side effects (Mobile HUD, ui-hud.md).
- **Map rect**: `x >= [0x730f24]` (the minimap's sheared right edge overlaps the map at the top). The map is rendered
  under the panel frame; the view origin is the camera.
- **Other resolutions**: `0x4c6d70` only knows indexes 0..2 (other values leave the table unchanged) and the panel art
  exists in three variants (resource `0x40000`, variant `[0x730f08]-1`, `0x4b4dfb`). Registry `Resolution` (part of
  `HKLM\Software\BlueByte\Siedler3\1.0\General`, see [registry.md](registry.md)) selects 0/1/2 at start; values 1 and 2
  VERIFIED. A custom resolution (e.g. 1280x720) would need: our DirectDraw mode, a patched `0x4c6d70` case (map view
  sizes are used generically via `0x730f18/0x730f1c`) and reuse of variant 2 panel art. HYPOTHESIS, untested.
- **Runtime switch** (VERIFIED in s3run): F1/F2/F3 (VK 0x70..0x72, handlers `0x525a77`, `0x525b36`, `0x525bfb`) write
  the wanted index to `[0x7a7af0+0x70]` (setter `0x49ded0`) and signal the render thread; the game re-runs
  `SetDisplayMode` and the layout. Ignored when `[0x7dfd44] != 0` (HYPOTHESIS: multiplayer/replay) or already active.
  This is the cheapest "zoom out / more map" for mobile: switch to 1024x768 and let our presenter scale the frame.

## 2. The left panel

### Page state (all in `gd`, copied every frame to the render snapshot by `0x51f110` at `0x51f5ff..`)

| Field | snap | Meaning | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `+0x2d284` | `+0x60` | page: 0 none, 1 build, 2 goods, 3 settlers, 4 building selected, 5 units selected, 6 (TAB key; HYPOTHESIS: next unit group), 7 Save/Quit menu, 8 messages, 9 game paused, 0xb (`G` key, unknown) | VERIFIED 1,2,3,7,9; 4,5 part 1 |
| `+0x2d288` | `+0x64` | build category 1..4 (page 1) | VERIFIED |
| `+0x2d28c` | `+0x68` | build list slot 1..12, 0 = nothing selected (cleared after a site is placed and by right-click) | VERIFIED |
| `+0x2d290` | `+0x6c` | goods page tab 1..4 | VERIFIED (1) |
| `+0x2d294` | `+0x70` | goods page sub-selection (cleared when tab 2 is chosen) | STATIC |
| `+0x2d298` | `+0x74` | menu sub-page (page 7: 0 main, 1 quit confirmation, 2 save slot list) / building page action (page 4, part 1) | STATIC (0 VERIFIED) |
| `+0x2d29c`, `+0x2d2a4`, `+0x2d2a8` | `+0x78`, `+0x80`, `+0x84` | further page state (not analysed) | |
| `+0x2d2a0` | `+0x7c` | settlers page tab 1..4 | VERIFIED (1) |
| `+0x2d27c` | – | panel dirty: set to 1 after every change | VERIFIED (needed after a poke) |
| `+0x2d280` | – | set together with settlers tab 4 (HYPOTHESIS: statistics refresh) | STATIC |
| `+0x2d2f0` | – | building type to place | VERIFIED |
| `+0x2d320 + n*0x4b0` (n = 0..3) | `+0x88` bits | message categories (battle, general, resources, trade): a bottom button works only when its slot is non-zero; bit n of `snap+0x88` = "has messages", blinking with bit 5 of the step counter | STATIC |

Each click handler also plays the click sound (`0x53f560(0x3d)`, thiscall logic) and calls `0x542630` (thiscall logic;
HYPOTHESIS: refresh/notify). After choosing a building type it calls `0x4ff3f0` (thiscall gd; HYPOTHESIS: recompute the
placement ghost map). Poking without these calls still showed the placement ghosts and placed the site (VERIFIED), so
a HUD may poke + set the dirty flag; calling the same functions from a logic-thread hook is the cleaner option.

### Click handling

All panel clicks are handled inside `HandleInput` (`0x524fa0`), left-down branch at `0x526aaa`: if `x < [0x730f24]`
the grid cell is computed and a long chain of `(col range, row range)` tests follows (`0x526aaa..0x532fa2`). Page
specific blocks start with `cmp [gd+0x2d284], page`: build list `0x526f8a..0x528a37`, goods `0x528a38`, settlers
`0x52c237`, building selected (4) `0x52xxxx/0x53xxxx` (part 1), units (5) `0x52ec5a`, menu (7) `0x52e21a`,
messages (8) `0x52e1b0`, `0xb` `0x532f4f`. `tools/re-ui/panelmap.py` lists every state write with the preceding
column/row tests (heuristic, linear).

The **same code is also the tooltip query**: `HandleInput` counts calls without input in `[logic+0x74]`; on the 10th
idle call it sets `[logic+0x78] = 3` and copies the mouse to `[logic+0x7c]/[logic+0x80]`; with `[logic+0x78] != 0`
every button block stores its tooltip text id in `[logic+0x54]` instead of acting (STATIC). `[logic+0x78]`: 0 = an
input event is being handled, 2 = queue empty, 3 = tooltip pass (idle count == 10), 1 = idle count > 10. So a tooltip appears
when the pointer rests ~10 logic ticks on a button. For touch, a host "hover" (mouse move without button) shows the
same tooltip.

Grid map of the common buttons (all VERIFIED by tooltip text ids and clicks at 640x480; pixel = origin + grid*cell):

| Button | cols | rows | Action | Tooltip id |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Build tab | 2..13 | 1..8 | page 1, slot 0 | `0x8004a` "Buildings" |
| Goods tab | 15..26 | 1..8 | page 2 | `0x8004b` "Goods" |
| Settlers tab | 28..39 | 1..8 | page 3 | `0x8004c` "Settlers" |
| Category 1..4 (page 1) | 0..9, 10..19, 20..29, 30..39 | 11..18 | cat = 1..4, slot 0 | `0x8004d..0x80050` Resource / Food / Military / Misc. Buildings |
| Goods tabs 1..4 (page 2) | 0..9, 10..19, 20..29, 30..39 | 11..18 | `+0x2d290` = 1..4 | `0x80051` Inventory, `0x80052` Tools and Weapons, `0x80081` Priority of Buildings, `0x80082` Priority of Goods |
| Settlers tabs 1..4 (page 3) | same | 11..18 | `+0x2d2a0` = 1..4 | `0x8005a` Population, `0x8005b` Occupations, `0x8005c` Recruitment, `0x80155` Production statistics |
| Build list slot `2k+1` / `2k+2` (k = 0..5) | 1..19 / 21..39 | `22+12k .. 31+12k` | slot, type (table below) | `0x80000 + type` |
| Menu (computer icon) | 0..7 | 97..103 | page 7, sub-page 0 | `0x8008f` "Save/Quit" |
| Messages 1..4 | 8..15, 16..23, 24..31, 32..39 | 97..103 | page 8, `0x4fee90(n)` (thiscall gd) | `0x800ad` Battle, `0x800ae` General, `0x800af` Resources, `0x800b0` Trade Messages |
| Menu: "Save Game" (page 7, sub 0) | 3..37 | 22..29 | opens the save slot list (`0x50b670` enumerates `slot%2i.sav`; HYPOTHESIS: sub-page 2) | – |
| Menu: "Quit Game" (page 7, sub 0) | 3..37 | 87..91 | sub-page 1 (confirmation) | – |

Recipe from [integration-log.md](../porting/integration-log.md) (640x480 pixels): menu icon `21 452`, "Save Game"
`68 225`, slot 1 `40 244` (slots 21 px apart), "Quit Game" `68 420`, YES `38 420`.

part 1).

### Programmatic tab switch / building selection (for the Mobile HUD)

VERIFIED sequence (s3run pokes, `scratch/re-ui/t1`): `[gd+0x2d284]=1, [gd+0x2d288]=cat, [gd+0x2d28c]=slot,
[gd+0x2d2f0]=type, [gd+0x2d27c]=1` -> the panel shows the build list with the slot highlighted and the map shows the
placement ghosts; the next left-click on the map places the construction site (building count `[gd+0x1499e60]` 6 -> 7)
and resets the slot to 0 (page and category stay). Alternatives:

- Send command 1 directly (part 1) after checking `AddBuilding(x,y,type,player,0)`; no UI state needed.
- **Hotkeys** (key events through our USER32 input; table `0x534cbc`/`0x534c00`, dispatch `0x5254a7`):
  Q/W/E/R = page 1 category 1..4 (VERIFIED: W -> page 1 cat 2), A/S/D/F = goods tabs (STATIC), Y(Z)/X/C/V = settlers
  tabs (STATIC), Space = page 8 messages, P = pause toggle (page 9 "Game Paused", VERIFIED; other hotkeys are ignored
  while paused), TAB = page 6 / selection cycling (`[0x7dfd68]`, HYPOTHESIS), G = page 0xb, arrows = scroll 40 px,
  Home (0x24) = `0x51b6b0` (HYPOTHESIS: center on castle), F1..F3 = resolution, F5/F6/F12, `+`/`-` (0x6b/0x6d),
  Enter (chat, `0x5254ae`), 1..9 (`0x542820`, HYPOTHESIS: unit groups or speed), T/B/O/I/U/J/K toggle globals
  `0x7deb54`, `0x7deb49`, `0x7dfdac`, `0x7dfda8` (debug/display options, HYPOTHESIS). Hotkeys are skipped while
  `[0x7dfda8] != 0` (`0x52548d`, chat input HYPOTHESIS).

### Where the panel is drawn (for UI mode B)

- Frame render (render thread) `0x4b2900..`: the text DIB / landscape / then `0x4b4d00` (call at `0x4b2dc5`) draws the
  panel: background art from gfx resource `0x40000` variant by resolution (`0x5faaf0` lookup at `0x4b4df6`), then a
  per-page block (`[snap+0x60]` checks at `0x4b53b5` (7), `0x4b5449` (2), ...), sprites via `0x5faca0`/`0x5fdab0`/
  `0x5f64c0` (HYPOTHESIS: get sprite / blit / blit transparent).
- Hiding the panel: skip `0x4b4d00` (hook + `return_from_function(0, 1)`) and crop the presented frame to
  `x >= [0x730f24]` in our presenter. The map is not rendered under the panel (HYPOTHESIS), so skipping the panel alone
  leaves stale pixels; cropping is the safe option. The minimap is part of the same top-left art (drawn in the frame
  render, `0x4b2b58..` uses `0x730f28/2c/30`).
- Input: with the panel hidden, HUD buttons must change state by pokes/commands/hotkeys (above); map clicks keep working
  with the original coordinates (map x starts at `[0x730f24]`).

## 3. Cursor / interaction mode

There is no separate cursor-mode variable; the mode is derived from the panel page and selections:

| Mode | Condition | Effect of left click on the map | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Normal | page 0/2/3/7/8 or page 1 with slot 0 | select (drag box / single) | VERIFIED |
| Build placement of type T | page 1, `[gd+0x2d28c] != 0`, `[gd+0x2d2f0] = T` | place a site (command 1), slot -> 0; right-click cancels (`[gd+0x2d28c]=0`) | VERIFIED |
| Building selected | page 4, `[0x7dfd6c]` = building id | building panel actions; right-click deselects | part 1 |
| Building target / work area | page 4, `[gd+0x2d298] = 3` | the next click sets the target tile (command 5) | STATIC (part 1) |
| Units selected | page 5, UI selection list non-empty | right-click (quick!) = move/attack (command 9, modifiers 0xd..0xf) | VERIFIED (part 1) |
| Paused | page 9 | input ignored | VERIFIED |
| Hover/tooltip pass | `[logic+0x78] != 0` | none; tooltip id set | STATIC |

Attack is not a mode: a move command onto an enemy target attacks (part 1). The mouse cursor image is chosen by our
cursor composer (see [user32-gdi32.md](../porting/user32-gdi32.md)); the game calls `SetCursor` with resources.

## 4. Dialogs and menus

- In game there are no Windows dialogs: Save/Quit is panel page 7 (`0x52e21a`), drawn by `0x4b4d00`.
  Sub-pages (`[gd+0x2d298]`): 0 = "Save Game" / "Quit Game" (VERIFIED, `scratch/re-ui/m1.png`), 1 = quit
  confirmation YES/NO, 2 = save slot list (8 slots, render loop at `0x51f1dd..`; STATIC). The save itself is a system
  command (0xf1..0xff family, part 1); a save writes `Save/slotNN.sav` without a name prompt.
- **Open the menu programmatically** (ESC is not in the hotkey table): page 7 + sub-page 0 + dirty (VERIFIED).
  Then "Save Game"/"Quit Game" are grid clicks (table above) or the integration-log pixel recipe.
- **Quit confirmation YES** (page 7 sub-page 1, grid x 3..16, y 87..91; handler `0x52e978..0x52e9b7`, STATIC):
  `0x53e720(logic)` (thiscall `CLogicThread`, ends the game: computes the statistics, sets `[logic+0x234]`), then the
  UI sound `0x53f560(logic, 0x33)`, sub-page := 0, panel dirty. NO (grid x 23..36) plays 0x3d and sets sub-page 0.
  The Mobile HUD's own "Quit this game?" calls the same (`LogicAction::QuitGame`; VERIFIED 2026-11-08: statistics
  screen follows).
- After "Quit Game -> YES" the game shows the statistics screen and then the 800x600 main menu (main menu, load list,
  options are full-screen 800x600 screens of the app's menu system, not the panel; not analysed here).
- Pause: P toggles page 9 (`0x52571b`).
- Message pages: page 8 with category `0x4fee90(n)`, n = 1..4.

## 5. Player resources and statistics (HUD)

- **Goods in stock**: the pile table (`gd+0x123885c`, 0xe bytes, count `[gd+0x1238858]`, part 1). Layout seen:
  `+0 u8 good`, `+1 u8 amount (<= 8)`, `+2/+3 u8` (HYPOTHESIS: reserved/incoming), `+4 u8 0xfe` (stored pile) or `0xfd`
  (HYPOTHESIS: free/transport pile), `+6 u16 x`, `+8 u16 y`, `+0xa/+0xc u16 next/prev pile of the same good`.
  The "Storage Area" inventory equals the sum of `amount` per good over the player's piles (VERIFIED on one map: planks
  8+8+8+1 = 25, stone 25, good 0xc 8+2 = 10, 0xd 8+7 = 15, ...). Which piles belong to which player: by tile ownership
  / economy sector (HYPOTHESIS; the panel probably sums piles of the local player's sectors). Good id -> name: text
  table not mapped yet (HYPOTHESIS: another table of the same string file; use `strings.py all:<t>`).
- **Settlers**: count settler table entries (part 1) by owner and type; the Population page shows the same split
  (carriers 32 at start = type 0 count, VERIFIED in part 1).
- **Economy sectors** `gd+0xe145e8` (0x2e0 bytes, count `[gd+0xe115dc]`): distribution/priority settings, not stock
  counts (VERIFIED: no inventory numbers there).
- **End-of-game statistics** (STATIC + VERIFIED 2026-11-08 by `xpeek`): 20 records `0x7acfac + id*0x44` (id = player
  id 0..19, the owner byte of settlers/buildings). `+0` rank (1 = best, set at game end), `+0x1c` score, then
  cumulative counters `+0x20` settlers, `+0x24` buildings, `+0x28` food, `+0x2c` mines, `+0x30` gold, `+0x34` manna,
  `+0x38` soldiers, `+0x3c` battles (incremented during the game, e.g. `0x4eca5f` buildings, `0x4eef16`
  settlers). `+8..+0x18` other per-player values (not mapped). `0x53e720` (end of game): score = 2*settlers +
  buildings + food + mines + gold + manna + 2*soldiers + 5*battles, then gold halved in place, then ranks by score
  (existing players: `[[logic+0x3a0] + id*0x148 + 0x11943dc] != 0`; ties -> the higher id first). Seen: vs one
  computer, 225 s game time: computer (id 1) buildings 22, score 22, rank 1; human id 0 rank 2. The screen is an
  800x600 menu: one 20 px row per player by rank (y 102 + 20*i), each cell a bar (light blue = share of the
  column's best). Any click leaves it. Used by `s3-mods/src/end_stats.rs`.
- Settlers tab 4 "Production statistics": not analysed.

## 6. Text and tooltip rendering

- **Strings**: `0x5faaa0` thiscall `strtab = [gfx+0x5f6b8]`, `(id, lang)`; `lang = -1` -> `[strtab+0xc40]` (1 in our
  runs = English). `table = id >> 16`, header `[strtab+0x37c + table*4]` with `u16 count` at +8 and offsets at
  `+0xc + (count*lang + index)*4`, base `[strtab+0x264 + table*4]`. The tables live in memory-mapped text files.
  Table 8 = UI texts (building names `0x80000+type`, tooltips `0x8004a..`, messages). A hook here translates or
  replaces any UI text (localisation, larger HUD labels).
- **Panel text drawing**: `0x4a87d0` (cdecl, printf-style; args `(textObj=[gfx+0x5f6e0], out, 1, RECT*, flags, fmt,
  ...)`, uses `_vsnprintf` `0x621408`) renders into a 640x480 1-bpp DIB (`CreateDIBSection` at `0x4a7b42`) with
  `DrawTextA` (`0x4a8725`); the DIB is then composed onto the frame. Font: `CreateFontIndirectA` `0x4a8028`.
  Host-side alternative: our `DrawTextA` HLE (`s3-win32/src/gdi32.rs`) sees every string with its rectangle.
- **Tooltip**: `[logic+0x54]` (text id, `-1` = none) and the mouse position `[logic+0x7c]/[logic+0x80]` are copied to
  `snap+0x270/+0x27c/+0x280` by `0x51f110` and cleared; the renderer (`0x4b3de1..0x4b3f4b`) builds a box of
  180x20 px around the pointer (`x-90..x+90`, `y-15..y+5`, clamped to the screen), saves the background (`0x4d65e0`),
  draws the string with `0x4a87d0` (flags 9) and restores (`0x4d6740`). Hook `0x4b3de1` region or read `snap+0x270` to
  draw our own tooltip.
- **Text DIB composite (panel-text, 2026-11-08; STATIC unless marked).** Every in-game text goes the same way:
  `0x4d65e0(x, y, w, h)` (thiscall gfx, `ret 0x10`) clears a DIB rectangle, `0x4a87d0` / `0x4a8090` draws into the
  DIB (the only `DrawTextA` call is `0x4a8725` in `0x4a8090`: `[esp]` hdc, `+4` string, `+8` count, `+0xc` RECT*,
  `+0x10` format; DIB pixel = frame pixel), then `0x4d6740(x, y, w, h)` (thiscall gfx, `ret 0x10`) walks the DIB
  bytes of the rectangle and calls `0x4d6950(byte x, y, bits)` per non-zero byte, which writes colour
  `0x4c7b00(0xe6, 0xe6, 0xe6)` = RGB(230, 230, 230) for each set bit straight into the locked frame surface
  `[gfx+0xec]` (pitch in bytes `[gfx+0x90]`) and a black pixel at (x+1, y+1) (shadow; not on the last screen row).
  Call triples clear/draw/composite: tooltip `0x4b3ef4/0x4b3f20/0x4b3f46`, clock `0x4b40e5/0x4b4104/0x4b4122`, end
  banner `0x4b4167/0x4b41eb/0x4b4227`, panel renderer helpers `0x4d6a30`, `0x4d6b10` (font 0 / 1, rect from
  `[0x730f38]`, `[0x730f3c]`, `[0x730f40]`, text id via `0x5faaa0`, flags 9) and further ones up to `0x4d79a6`,
  `0x4b56e4..0x4b588e`, map labels `0x4bffe3..0x4c0111`, `0x4c2841..0x4c2d20`, `0x4c8bad..0x4c8c08`,
  `0x4c9058..0x4c90b3`. The panel info text (`0x4b2838..0x4b2b13`) is only drawn into the DIB there (when
  `snap+0x274 != -1`); its composite is elsewhere. The panel renderer `0x4b4d00` is called once per frame at
  `0x4b2dc5` (frame renderer `0x4b26c0`, the only caller is `0x42c73d`); its texts stay on the frame until it
  redraws, the map part (tooltip, clock, map labels) is redrawn every frame. Skipping `0x4d6740` (`ret 0x10`) keeps
  the text out of the frame without other effects (VERIFIED with `s3-mods/src/panel_text.rs`).
- Other text users: `0x41xxxx..0x42xxxx` (TextOutA/DrawTextA; main menu screens, HYPOTHESIS), `0x5a1970..` (TextOutA +
  `CreateFontA`; HYPOTHESIS: debug/statistics overlay).

## Tools (re-ui)

- `s3run --inject` debug commands (`port/crates/s3-desktop/src/debug.rs`): `dump/peek/poke/regs/watch/dumpall DIR
  [mapped]` (`mapped` also writes memory-mapped file views, needed for the string tables; output is game data, keep it
  in `scratch/`). Plus re-units' `xpeek/xdump/scan`.
- `tools/re-ui/run.sh MAXSEC "inject"` starts a random single-player map (in game after ~17-45 s).
- `tools/re-ui/panelmap.py ASM START END` (panel button table), `tools/re-ui/strings.py DUMPDIR GFXOBJ ID...|all:T`
  (text ids; find `GFXOBJ` with `scan 0x656aec`), `tools/re-ui/scan.py`, `diff.py`, `peek.py` (snapshot diffs),
  `findstock*.py` (counter search), `dis.sh ADDR [N]` (objdump listing `scratch/re-ui/s3.asm`, local only).
```
