```md
## Additions from the Mobile HUD work (ui-hud, 2026-11-05)

Details and evidence: [ui-hud.md](../porting/ui-hud.md).

- Programmatic building selection also needs `gd::0x4ff3f0` (thiscall gd, no args; bumps the placement-marker
  generation `gd+0x2d300`) after the pokes, else no placement markers are drawn and map clicks do not place (VERIFIED;
  the earlier poke test had markers from a previous real click).
- The panel is only redrawn when `[gd+0x2d27c]` is set (VERIFIED). The panel renderer `0x4b4d00` does not read
  `[0x730f24]`; it draws at fixed positions.
- Landscape ring buffer: object `[gfx+0x5f6cc]` (vtable `0x65a520`), width `+0x50` = map view width + `[0x730f44]`
  (32 in s3run), set by `0x54bec0` from the display setup `0x42ef..`; blitter `0x54c9d0` wraps at that width. A wider
  map view therefore needs the layout change before the display setup.
- Full-screen map works with `[0x730f24] = 0`, `[0x730f18] = screen width` set at `0x4c6d70` return plus a
  `ScreenToMap` x correction (VERIFIED at 640x480 and 800x600 from start; runtime F1-F3 switch leaves a black band, open).
- Goods: the panel's Inventory numbers are separate counters, not a live sum of piles (VERIFIED by poking piles).
  Piles of the local player = piles on tiles owned by the player (tile +8). Good ids, see ui-hud.md.
- Command `0x06` (destroy building) VERIFIED through `Queue::Post 0x4309c0` from a HandleInput-entry hook.

## Resolution internals (res-zoom, 2026-11-05)

Details and how the port uses them: [resolution-zoom.md](../porting/resolution-zoom.md). All VERIFIED in s3run
unless marked STATIC.

- `[0x7dfd44]` = resolution request: F1-F3 handlers (`0x525a77`, `0x525b36`, `0x525bfb`) write 1..3, call the setter
  `0x49ded0` and `ReleaseSemaphore([[0x7a800c]+8], 1, 0)` (`0x525b5b`). Copied to `snap+0xa0` by the snapshot fill
  (`0x51f4f5`). `0x4c7490(snap)` (render thread, from `0x4b26c0`) switches for 1..3 (inline layout table, the 640 case
  uses minimap x 4 instead of 5), calls `gfx::0x42ce90(w, h, 16, 0, 0)`, sets `0xfa`; returns al=1 (frame skipped)
  for 1..3 / `0xfa`. The logic thread (`0x53db30`) on `0xfa`: waits on the semaphore `[0x7a800c]` (`0x53db80`,
  timeout `0x40d0e0(7)`), rebuilds the minimap image (`gd::0x4fb650` -> `gd+0x1223656`, `[0x730f28]^2` pixels),
  `gd+0x2d264 = 0`, `gd+0x2d254/58 = 10 000 000` (full landscape redraw), `gd+0x2d278 = gd+0x2d27c = 1`, clamp
  `0x51b4d0`, `[0x7dfd44] = 0`. While `[0x7dfd44] != 0` the simulation step is skipped (`0x53dd5c`). Without the
  semaphore token the logic thread blocks forever (VERIFIED by calling the switch without it).
- `0x42ce90` (thiscall gfx): index = 2 for w 1024, 1 for 800, else 0; if the current mode differs,
  `SendMessage(hwnd, 0x804, index)`; window proc `0x45cc9c` -> `0x405c80(index)` -> `IDirectDraw2::SetDisplayMode`
  with constants (calls at `0x405cc3` index 1, `0x405cf2` index 0/2). The display setup `0x42e430` (vtable, no direct
  callers) then runs again: map rect `gfx+0x5f6e8..+0x5f6f4` from the layout, new landscape surface via `0x54bec0(mapW
  + [0x730f44], mapH + [0x730f48], surf, rect)` (`[0x730f44]` = 32, `[0x730f48]` = 102; the object stores the rect
  at `+0x58/+0x5c` size and `+0x74..+0x80`), text DIB `0x4a78f0(screenW, screenH)` (1 bpp, `CreateDIBSection`).
- Initial layout: `0x4c6d40` (from the gfx ctor `0x42c990`) -> `0x4c6d70(registry index)`; game start sets the mode
  through `0x42ca70` -> `0x42ce90([0x730f0c], [0x730f10])`.
- **Render snapshot** `[logic+0x3d0]`: `new(0xc7720)` + ctor `0x523480` (lazy, in `0x51f110`); grid of 130 x 130
  tiles at `+0x500` (0x30 bytes each, index `row + col*130`, filled at `0x522410..`, out-of-map tiles `0x522f60`),
  view size `+0x30` cols = `(mapW+23)/16 + 10`, `+0x34` rows = `(mapH+255)/9 + 11`, camera `+4/+8`, previous camera
  `+0xc/+0x10`; behind the grid: 16 x 16-byte array `+0xc65c0`, strings `+0xc66c0..`, 20 x 0x1c `+0xc66d8`, 100 x
  0x24 `+0xc690c`, count `+0xc771c`. Rows are sheared: column index up to `cols + rows/2`; 1024x768 uses 126 of 130
  columns (with neighbour reads). In placement mode the fill also writes marker bytes into visible `gd` tiles
  (`0x5223b2`, tile `+8`).
- Fixed caps that do not limit bigger views: hit list 10000 entries (`0x4d8240`), sprite lists 4000 / 8000 entries
  in 250 row buckets (`0x4d7c90`, `0x4d7e10`).
- `0x5158f0` (thiscall gd): tile at the view centre from camera and `0x730f18/1c` (STATIC, callers not checked).
- `0x4d82b0`: bottom-left message lines, positioned from `[0x730f38]` and `[0x730f10]`; details in section 7.

## 7. In-game messages (re-messages, 2026-11-08)

Goal: draw the game's text messages at a constant on-screen size in a window-resolution overlay (the port changes the
render size for zoom, so everything drawn into the game frame grows and shrinks). VERIFIED = seen in s3run on
2026-11-08 (tutorial at 800x600; recipe and evidence at the end), STATIC = read from code only.

### What is drawn as text over the map

| Text | Source | Drawn by (render thread, inside the frame renderer `0x4b26c0`) | Clickable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Message lines** bottom-left (tutorial text, chat, desync / CD / ladder notices, "game already saved", ...) | ring in `logic` (below) | text into the text DIB: `0x4d82b0` (call `0x4b2833`); icons + composite: `0x4d8400` (call `0x4b422f`) | only the tutorial "arrow" corner |
| **Chat input line** (multiplayer, Enter) | `logic+0x3f8` | the same two functions | no (keyboard) |
| Tooltip | `logic+0x54` -> `snap+0x270` | `0x4b3de1..0x4b3f4b` (section 6) | no |
| Game clock `hh:mm:ss` while `[0x7deb54]` is set (T key) | `[0x7dfd48]` (logic ticks of 64 ms; VERIFIED 2026-11-08: 838 -> `00:00:53`) | `0x4b3f95..0x4b412d`, rect `(W-80, H-20, W, H)`, font 1 | no |
| End banner "You've Lost." `0x80113` / "You've won." `0x80115` / "The game ends as a draw." `0x8015c` | `[0x730f64]` = 0 / 1 / 2 (`-1` = game running) | `0x4b412d..0x4b422c`, rect `(W-[0x730f20], 20, W, 47)` | no |
| Panel info text (`snap+0x274` text id, printf args `+0x284..+0x290`, from `logic+0x50..0x64`) | panel rect `gfx+0x5f654..0x5f660` (set at `0x4c73da`) | `0x4b2838..0x4b2b13` | panel |

All of them use the game's text renderer `[gfx+0x5f6e0]`: GDI `DrawTextA` into a 1-bpp DIB the size of the screen
(created by `0x4a78f0`). `0x4d65e0(x, y, w, h)` clears a rectangle of that DIB, `0x4d6740(x, y, w, h)` copies the set
pixels of a rectangle onto the frame (per-run blitter `0x4d6950`); both thiscall `gfx`, `ret 0x10` (STATIC). Fonts are
created per resolution in `0x4c6fd0..0x4c73b6` (`0x4a7df0`); font 0 has height `5 * cell` (STATIC).

### Message ring (logic thread)

All in `logic` (`CLogicThread`, `[0x700ffee0]` in s3run; part 1). VERIFIED by `xdump 0x700ffee0@0x414 0x8c` +
`tools/re-messages/slots.py`, matching the screenshots.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `logic+0x414 + i*0x1c`, i = 0..19 | entries; only `i < [logic+0x644]` are used, and `[logic+0x644] = 5` (set once at `0x53cade`) |
| entry `+0x00` (16 B) | string object: `+4` pointer to **UTF-16** text, `+8` length in chars, `+0xc` capacity (reference count byte at `ptr-1`; the game's wide string class) |
| entry `+0x10` | timer in logic ticks; the line is shown while it is `!= 0`. 800 for normal lines, 1 000 000 for icon `>= 0xfa` (tutorial: "forever") |
| entry `+0x14` | icon: `< 0x14` = player colour mark (locally generated lines pass `word [0x7ace64 + player*2]`, = 1 for player 0), `0xfd` = info "i" (gfx `0x10088`), `0xfe` = second icon (gfx `0x10089`), `0xfc` = tutorial **arrow** (gfx `0x1008b`), `0xff` = none |
| entry `+0x18` | dirty byte (text must be redrawn into the DIB) |
| `logic+0x648` | next write index; it **decreases** (`(idx + n - 1) % n`): a new line goes one slot up until it wraps |
| `logic+0x3f8` (16 B) | chat input line (UTF-16; starts with the player name and ": ", prefix length `logic+0x40c`), `+0x400` length (max 0x50), `+0x408` chat open, `+0x410` dirty |

Functions (all thiscall `logic`, logic thread; STATIC unless marked):

- `0x51e440` **AddMessage(string by value (16 B), icon)**, `ret 0x14`: assigns the text to slot `[logic+0x648]`, timer
  800 (1 000 000 if icon `>= 0xfa`), icon, dirty; moves the index down; for icon `< 0x14` it also clears the timer of
  the next slot (one free line between chat lines). Plays sound `0x3d`. 40 call sites: chat echo `0x5256e5`,
  "[Server]: " `0x541051`, text ids `0x8012c` "Ladder games cannot be saved.", `0x8012d` "The game has already been
  saved within the last minute.", `0x80152` "This is the last tower", `0x80174` "You cannot steal goods from an ally.",
  hard-coded desync / CD / ladder / lobby strings (`0x53a2f6..0x53b7ec`, `0x53d8a5..0x53d99a`, `0x540801..0x541333`).
- `0x51e650` ClearMessages: all timers 0, all dirty, index = n-1 (top slot).
- `0x51e680` Tick: every timer `> 0` is decremented and marked dirty; called once per logic loop at `0x53e6d5`
  (VERIFIED rate: ~74 per second in s3run, so a normal line lives ~11 s).
- `0x51e2e0` chat editor (adds a key to `logic+0x3f8`). The Enter handler `0x5254ae` opens the chat **only in a
  network game** (`0x4318d0` on `0x7a7a18`; VERIFIED: Enter + typing in single player leaves the ring and the chat
  line empty).

**Tutorial text** (VERIFIED): the tutorial (`[0x7dfdb0] == 0x63`) is a state machine in `gd`: step `[gd+0x2d308]`,
wait counter `[gd+0x2d304]`. `0x53fbb0` (called every logic loop at `0x53e629` in the tutorial) checks the condition
of the current step; for "press the arrow" steps it is `0x515b00` (decrement `gd+0x2d304`, true at 0). On success
`0x53f950` looks the step up in the table `0x72faf0` (16-byte entries `{step, next step, icon, text id}`, first entry
`{0, 1, 0xfd, 0x70090}`), sets the next step, resets the wait counter to 100 000 (`0x515af0`), loads the text
(`0x5faaa0` on `[0x7a8010]`, table 7) and calls `0x540400(text, icon)`: **ClearMessages**, then split the text into
chunks of at most 75 chars at a space (no pixel measuring), at most 4 lines, each through `AddMessage` from the top
slot down. Icons: first chunk = the step icon, middle chunks `0xff`; if the step icon is `0xfd` the **last** chunk
gets `0xfc` (the arrow; a one-line text gets only the arrow, no "i"). Step icon `0xfe` = no arrow (the step waits for
a game action). At 800x600 the first line is clipped at the right edge ("...boot camp. Pl" / "the arrow button to
continue.") because 75 chars do not fit the 580 px line rectangle.

### Per-frame copy and drawing

The snapshot fill `0x51f110` (logic thread) copies every frame: chat line `logic+0x3f8 -> snap+0xc66c0` (`0x523a40`),
chat dirty `logic+0x410 -> snap+0xc66d4` (then clears it), `snap+0xc66d0` = chat icon choice (0/1; HYPOTHESIS: team vs
all), and the 20 entries `logic+0x414.. -> snap+0xc66d8 + i*0x1c` (`0x523330` copies string, timer, icon, dirty),
clearing each `logic` dirty byte. **In the port the snapshot tail is moved** by the res patch (`s3-mods/src/res.rs`
`snap_delta()`, `SNAP_TAIL_SITES`): use `snap + 0xc66d8 + snap_delta()` etc., or read `logic` directly.

Render thread (`ecx` = `gfx`, the only stack argument = `snap`; both functions `ret 4`):

1. `0x4d82b0` (from `0x4b2833`, early in the frame): if the chat line is dirty, clear its rectangle and draw it into
   the DIB; for each entry with the dirty byte set: clear its rectangle and, if the timer is `!= 0`, draw the text
   (`0x4a8a20`: UTF-16 -> ANSI, then `0x4a8090` -> `DrawTextA`; font 0, flags 0x40) clipped to the line rectangle.
2. `0x4d8400` (from `0x4b422f`, the last drawing before the flip): composite the chat rectangle (if dirty or non-empty)
   and its icon (`0x4000a` / `0x40009`); for each entry with dirty or timer `!= 0`: draw the icon sprite (timer `!= 0`)
   and composite the line rectangle from the DIB onto the frame.

Geometry (game pixels; `c = [0x730f38]` = 3 / 4 / 5 for heights < 600 / < 768 / >= 768, `H = [0x730f10]`; the
constants are the table `0x658ab8..0x658ad4` times `c`; not shifted by the panel width). VERIFIED at 800x600.

| Item | Rectangle |
| --- | --- |
| line slot i (0..4, 0 = bottom) | `x 50c .. 195c`, `y H - (21 + 6i)c .. H - (15 + 6i)c` (800x600: slot 0 = 200..780 x 516..540, slot 4 = y 420..444) |
| icon of slot i | anchor `x 48c` (`0xfc` arrow: `48c + 8`), `y H - (18 + 6i)c`; the sprites carry their own offset (at 800x600 the arrow of slot 4 is seen around (197, 487), of slot 2 around (197, 535)) |
| chat line | `x 50c .. 195c`, `y H - 10c .. H - 5c`; icon anchor `(48c, H - 7c)` |

### Clicks

- **Tutorial arrow** (VERIFIED): the map branch of HandleInput's left-down (`0x532fa2`, `x >= [0x730f24]`): if
  `[0x7dfdb0] == 0x63` and `x - [0x730f24] < 50` and `H - y < 210` (fixed game pixels, not scaled) then
  `[gd+0x2d304] = 1` and the click ends there; the next logic loops advance the step if it is an arrow step. The area
  is the whole bottom-left corner of the map (no test whether the arrow is shown). Clicks at (196, 570) and (196, 395)
  advanced, (300, 570) did not. **Poking `[gd+0x2d304] = 1` advances the same way** (VERIFIED, step 1 -> 2), so an
  overlay button can do that (or inject a game click at `([0x730f24] + 10, H - 10)`). HYPOTHESIS: with the Mobile HUD
  layout (`[0x730f24] = 0`) the area is `x < 50`, left of where the arrow is drawn: tapping the original arrow may not
  work there.
- **Message lines are not clickable.** "Go to the event" lives in the panel messages page (page 8): the buttons
  Messages 1..4 call `0x4fee90(n)` (thiscall gd), which stores the event position in `gd+0x2d314/0x2d318`; the "go to"
  button (cols 0x11..0x16, rows 0x54..0x59 on page 8) centres the camera with `0x51b560(x, y)` (`0x52e1ef`) and closes
  the page. STATIC.

### Suppressing the game's drawing (VERIFIED)

Patching `0x4d8400` to `ret 4` (s3run `poke 0x4d8400 c20400`, restore `83ec4c`) removes all message lines, icons and
the chat line from the frame with no stale pixels (the landscape is redrawn every frame); restoring brings them back at
once (`scratch/re-messages/r3`). The text still goes into the DIB through `0x4d82b0`; skipping that too keeps the DIB
clean for the other composites (tooltip, clock) and saves the GDI work. The logic side (ring, timers, tutorial) is not
affected.

### Implemented (2026-11-08): `s3-mods/src/messages.rs`

Hooks `0x4d82b0` (skip) and `0x4d8400` (read the 5 entries + chat line from the snapshot, skip); the `messages` mod
draws them in the window layer (14 px at a 600 px high window, bottom-left right of the HUD minimap / Classic panel,
slot positions kept), info icon as a blue "i", the tutorial arrow as a "Next >" button that writes
`[gd+0x2d304] = 1` (VERIFIED: tutorial step 1 -> 2 in s3run). Same on-screen size at 1536x600 and 616x240.

### Hook plan for the constant-size overlay

1. Mods hook at `0x4d82b0` entry: `return_from_function(0, 1)` (render thread; no DrawText into the DIB).
2. Mods hook at `0x4d8400` entry: `snap = [esp+4]`; copy the 5 used entries (`snap + 0xc66d8 + snap_delta() + i*0x1c`:
   text pointer / length at `+4` / `+8`, UTF-16; timer `+0x10`; icon `+0x14`) and the chat line (`+0xc66c0 +
   snap_delta()`, shown when non-empty) into the overlay state, then `return_from_function(0, 1)`. Reading the snapshot
   here gives exactly what the game would have drawn (the logic thread writes the ring concurrently).
3. Overlay (window resolution): draw slot i from the bottom up at a fixed size and keep the game's slot order
   (slot 4 = top); hide lines with timer 0. Icon `0xfd` = info, `0xfc` = arrow button, `0xfe` = second icon,
   `< 0x14` = player colour mark. The 75-char tutorial chunks can be re-joined (consecutive slots from the `0xfd`/`0xfe`
   line down to the `0xfc`/`0xff` line) and re-wrapped by pixel width.
4. Arrow tap: write `[gd+0x2d304] = 1` (from a logic-thread hook such as `HandleInput` entry `0x524fa0`, or from the
   host between slices) or inject a game left click at `([0x730f24] + 10, H - 10)`, only while `[0x7dfdb0] == 0x63`.
5. Tooltip, clock and end banner can stay in the frame or be hooked the same way later (table above).

### Recipe and evidence

`sh tools/re-messages/run.sh OUT SECS "inject"` starts the tutorial (main menu 165 35; in game after ~3 s at 800x600;
`START=scen` = random map). Example inject: `12000:xdump 0x700ffee0@0x414 0x8c OUT/s.bin;18000:click 196 570;21000:shot
OUT/c.png`, then `python -I tools/re-messages/slots.py OUT/s.bin`. `tools/re-messages/lst.py ADDR N` prints the local
objdump listing. s3run `poke` now also invalidates decoded code, so code patches take effect at once. Evidence (local,
not committed): `scratch/re-messages/r1..r6`.

Open: the chat line, its icons and the colour mark (icon `< 0x14`, drawn via `0x5fab50(0x40000)` / `0x5fac10(icon +
0x10000)`) are STATIC only (need a two-instance MP run); the exact sprite offsets of the icons; whether other missions
use `0x540400` (`[0x7dfdb0]` values other than 0x63).

### Recruitment (page 3 tab 3, `0x52cbf7..0x52d5ff`)

Command 0x10, 12 bytes `{0x21, 0x10, 0x0c, 0, kind, player, x_hi, x_lo, y_hi, y_lo, count, 0}`, posted with 3 dwords,
then `CLogicThread::0x542630()`; sound 0x2f. kind 1 geologist, 2 thief, 3 pioneer, 4 pioneer -> carrier; count 1 or 5
(buttons "1 New Geologist" `0x8007a`, "5 New Geologists" `0x80079`, ... `0x8007f`/`0x80080`; Amazons use the texts
`0x80177..0x8017e`). x, y = tile at the centre of the map view, computed from the camera (`0x52ccbc..`):
`q = (camY + 1600) / 18`, `x = (camX - 208) / 16 - (W - (2q - 200)) / 2 + ((H + 255) / 9 + 11) / 4 + ((mapW + 23) / 16
+ 10) / 2`, `y = 2q - 200 + ((H + 255) / 9 + 11) / 2` (camX/camY `gd+0x2d25c/0x2d260`, W world size, H `[0x730f1c]`,
mapW `[0x730f18]`; `ui_hud_game::view_centre_tile`). VERIFIED: "1 New Geologist" + "5 New Pioneers" turned 6 carriers
into settler types 22 (geologist) and 40 (pioneer). Not done natively: soldier recruitment (`0x8006a..0x8006f`) and
the carrier / digger / builder limits (`0x80067..0x80069`).

### Save (page 7)

- "Save Game" (sub-page 0, `0x52e29a`): `0x4318d0` (thiscall `0x7a7a18`) = multiplayer session. Single player: for
  slot 1..8 `CLogicThread::0x50b670(slot, 0, &line1, &b, &a)` (three MSVC 6 `std::string`s: 16 bytes, +4 data, +8
  length; ctor `0x523540`, dtor `0x401b60`) returns al = slot used; line 1 = map path (`\Random`), line 2 = `a + " " +
  b` = date/time + race ("11/08/2026 01:28:54" "Egyptians"); the panel keeps them at `logic+0x250 + 0x20*i`; sub-page 2.
- Slot click (sub-page 2, rows `0x1c + 7*i`): `CLogicThread::0x50ac40(0, slot)` (arg0 = multiplayer flag; it formats
  `Save\slot%2i.sav`) -> al 1 = sub-page 3 "saved" (then `[0x7deb50] = 0`, `[0x7dfd50] = [0x7dfd48]`: the "not saved
  for N min" reminder), else sub-page 4. VERIFIED from a HUD logic-thread hook: `slot 1.sav` written (4.6 MB) and
  listed by the reader.
- Multiplayer (`0x52e438`): refuses within 0x3a9 time units of the last save (message `0x8012d`), checks
  `0x435aa0`, then sound 0x30, command 0xfa `{player}`, `0x542630()`, sub-page 5. STATIC (the HUD sends the same).
```

```md
## Object model

- `app` (main window/application object, vtable `0x6553fc`, ctor `0x4043d0`) is a local of the WinMain-level function
  `0x45a0xx` (call at `0x45a183`); its `Run` loop is `0x404860` on thread t0. `app+0x90` = logic thread object, created at
  `0x4058cc..0x4058fe` (`new 0x678`, ctor `0x53c5e0`).
- `CLogicThread` (`0x53c5e0` ctor; second vptr at +4 = `0x65a140`; `Init/Run` virtual `0x53c9e0` creates `CGameData`
  with `new 0x153a128` at `0x53cb31` and stores it at `+0x3a0`). Relevant members:
  - `+0x3a0` gd; `+0x3c0` input event queue (read by HandleInput); `+0x3c4` outgoing request queue (player commands).
  - `+0x44/+0x48` last mouse x/y (screen, from events); `+0x78` input state (0..3, HYPOTHESIS: idle/drag/hold);
    `+0x220` non-zero blocks map input (HYPOTHESIS: modal dialog/menu open).
- The logic thread in s3run is the one whose EIP is mostly in `0x4dxxxx..0x54xxxx` (t4 in a normal single-player run).

How to find the pointers at runtime (for the W1 mod framework): hook the `CGameData` ctor `0x4fc990` (ecx = gd) or the
store `0x53cb63` (`mov [ebp+0x3a0], eax`, ebp = logic, eax = gd). Both are executed once per game start / load.

## Building table (`gd+0x1499e64`, 0x3a bytes)

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| +0x00 | u8 | owner (0xff = free; entry 0 unused) | VERIFIED |
| +0x02, +0x04 | u16 | x, y (tile of the building origin; = the clicked placement tile) | VERIFIED |
| +0x06 | u8 | building type. 15 = Guard Tower (start building of random maps); 2 = first entry of the first build category ("Woodcutter"? HYPOTHESIS); 3, 4 seen for AI sites | VERIFIED (15, 2) |
| +0x07 | u8 | race of the owner (= player record +0) | VERIFIED |
| +0x08 | u16 | 2 / 0x3c on finished towers (HYPOTHESIS: occupants/strength) | |
| +0x0a, +0x0c | u16 | door / flag tile x, y | VERIFIED (next to x,y) |
| +0x10, +0x12 | u16 | settler ids working on a construction site (builder/digger) | VERIFIED (sites only) |
| +0x18 | u8 | bit 0 = working / building active (toggled by command 4 "Stop/Resume Working/Building"), bits 1..4 = construction priority (commands 0xf5/0xf6); game-state-ui.md section 8 | VERIFIED (site) |
| +0x18..+0x21 | u8 | construction progress bytes on sites (`01 03 01 05 04 00 00 04 00 01` on a fresh site, `01 00 01 ...` on finished) | HYPOTHESIS: build phase ("Baubauphase") |
| +0x21 | u8 | non-zero = construction site (building page tooltips; VERIFIED 0 on a finished tower, non-zero on a fresh site); also excludes the building from some command checks (`0x535b51`, `0x537307`) | VERIFIED |
| +0x30, +0x32 | u16 | x, y again (or a sign/target position) | VERIFIED values |
| +0x38 | u16 | 0xfa (250) on finished buildings | ? |

Tile `+0x0a` bit `0x20` marks a building tile; tile `+0x02` holds the building id (VERIFIED for the tower's origin).
`gd::DestroyBuildingAt(x, y)` (`0x4d97b0`, thiscall gd, ret 8) searches the building that covers a tile through the
building shape tables (`0x6aa174`, indexed by race and type) and calls `gd::CrushBuilding(id)` `0x4d9250`
(thiscall gd, ret 4, logs `Start crushing nr. %u art %u`). STATIC.

`gd::AddBuilding` `0x4d99e0`, thiscall gd, `(x, y, type, player, mode)`, ret 0x14: mode 0 = only test whether the site
is valid (used by the click handler before sending the command), mode 1 = place a construction site (used by the
command executor). Returns non-zero on success. STATIC + VERIFIED effect (placement created building 7 at the tile
`[gd+0x2d2e4/e8]`).

## Map tiles (`gd+0x67444`, 0x18 bytes, 768 tiles per x column)

`tile(x, y) = gd + 0x67444 + (x*768 + y) * 0x18`, valid for `0 <= x, y < [gd+0x2d2d0]`. Note the layout: **x is the
major index**. VERIFIED: 57 of 58 settlers have their id at `tile(x,y)+0` (the 58th was inside the tower).

| Off | Type | Meaning | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| +0x00 | u16 | settler id standing on the tile (0 = none) | VERIFIED |
| +0x02 | u16 | building id (with flag below) | VERIFIED |
| +0x04 | u8 | terrain height (ScreenToMap uses it) | STATIC + plausible values 0..50 |
| +0x06 | u8 | terrain type ("worldart" in a log; bits 0xf0 tested by the move command) | STATIC |
| +0x07 | u8 | economy sector ("ecosec" in a log) | STATIC |
| +0x08 | u8 | owner of the land (0xff = nobody) | VERIFIED values (mostly 0xff, 0 near the player) |
| +0x0a | u8 | flags; 0x20 = building on tile | VERIFIED |
| +0x10 | u8 | sector (0 = not walkable/water, 1 = land seen) | STATIC (`Siedler steht auf sector 0` log) |
| +0x14 | u16 | map object (tree, stone, ...; "object" in a log) | STATIC |

## Selection

Local (UI) selection, written by the left-button-up handler, VERIFIED with a box drag over 8 and 14 soldiers:

- `[0x7dfd68]` current group slot (0 after a normal selection, -1 when a building is selected or nothing).
- `word [0x7ad620 + slot*2]` count; `word [0x7ad634 + slot*200 + i*2]` settler ids (max 100, check at `0x533b89`).
- `dword [0x7ad5f8 + slot*4]` dirty flag: 1 after the selection changed; the next right-click first sends
  command 3 (selection sync) and clears it.
- `[0x7dfd6c]` selected building id (single click on a building, kind 100 in the hit list). Clicking our tower set it to 1,
  `[0x7dfd68] = -1` and `[gd+0x2d284] = 4` (building panel). Selecting soldiers set `[gd+0x2d284] = 5`.
- Drag state: `[0x7dfd34]` drag active, start `[0x7dfb9c]` x / `[0x7dfb98]` y, current `[0x7dfd38]` x / `[0x7dfd3c]` y
  (VERIFIED: 200,270 -> 560,400).

Selection rectangle logic (left button up, `0x5339a1..0x534100`, STATIC, effect VERIFIED):

1. Normalise the rectangle. If width < 5 and height < 5 it is a **single click**: the rectangle becomes the point
   ±10 px horizontally and -5..+32 px vertically (units are hit at their feet).
2. Without Shift the old selection is replaced; with Shift (`flags & 1`) ids are appended to the current slot.
3. A box first finds the "best" class present (soldier kinds 1..9 and 40 first, then 50/51, 11, 21, 20, 10; HYPOTHESIS:
   soldiers before ships before specialists) and then selects only entries of that class.
4. For every hit-list entry inside the rectangle: append its id, call `CLogicThread::0x5428e0(id, slot)`
   (HYPOTHESIS: marks the settler selected / plays the voice), and remember a building (kind 100) in `[0x7dfd6c]`.
5. With Ctrl or Alt (`flags & 4` / `& 2`) on a single unit: select units of the same type around it (loop over
   the neighbourhood table `gd+0x110a588` and tile `+0` owners, `0x533f21..`).

Logic-side copy (what commands act on; VERIFIED: count 0 -> 14 after the right-click that sent command 3):
`dword [gd+0x11940bc + (player*10 + slot)*4]` count, `word [gd+0x118a47c + (player*10 + slot)*200 + i*2]` ids.

## What is under a screen point (hit list)

The renderer fills a list of **selectable things currently drawn**: base `0x7ade08`, entry stride 20 bytes (two 10-byte
copies; the reader uses `0x7ade08 + ([0x7dfd64] + 2*i) * 10`), count `[0x7dfd5c]` (`[0x7dfd60]` = count of the other
buffer). Entry (10 bytes): `u16 kind, i16 screen_x, i16 screen_y, u16 id, u16 0`. VERIFIED values:

- kind 100 = building (several entries per building, one per hot spot of its footprint), id = building id.
- kind 1 = swordsman, 2 = bowman, 3 = third soldier kind (ids 41..54 matched the selected settlers). Carriers are not in
  the list (not selectable).
- Screen coordinates are 640x480 game-screen pixels at the unit's feet.

So a touch frontend can find the unit/building under a finger without calling game code: nearest entry to the tap,
within the same ±10 / -5..+32 box the game uses. Ground tiles: `gd::ScreenToMap`.

## Screen -> map transform

`gd::ScreenToMap` `0x4ff170`, thiscall(gd), args `(int sx, int sy)` in 640x480 screen pixels, ret 8, no return value:
writes the tile to `[gd+0x2d2e4]` (x) and `[gd+0x2d2e8]` (y), clamped to `0..ws-1`. Returns without writing when
`sx < [0x730f24]` (left of the map view, i.e. in the panel). VERIFIED: right-click at (500,150) -> (127,231), and
soldiers' targets (+0x24/+0x26) were around that tile.

Algorithm (STATIC, our description): add the camera (`[gd+0x2d254]`, `[gd+0x2d258]`) and fixed offsets (x: -0x118,
-0x20 per resolution step `[0x730f08]` 1..3; y: -0xc8); x is quantised to 8-pixel half-columns and y to 18-pixel rows;
odd half-columns shift by 9 px. This gives a first tile on the screen column; the function then walks down the column
(`x+1, y+2` per 18 px) comparing the tile heights (`tile+4`) to find the tile whose raised position matches the pixel.
So heights matter; calling the game function (W1 `call_guest`) is the safest way. Map -> screen (for drawing HUD
markers) is the inverse: about `x_px = 16*x - 8*y`, `y_px = 9*y - height` plus camera (HYPOTHESIS, not verified).

`gd::0x4ff0a0(sx, sy)` (thiscall gd, ret 8) is the variant used on mouse move and for building placement; in build
mode it fills the same `[gd+0x2d2e4/e8]` with the snapped construction tile (VERIFIED: hover at (470,110) gave
(0xb3, 0xe2), the site was then created exactly there).

## Input path: from a mouse button to a game action

1. Window messages (thread t0). The WndProc object's vtable is `0x6572b0`; the message switch `0x45c860` calls:
   `WM_LBUTTONDOWN/DBLCLK -> +0x38 0x45b630`, `WM_LBUTTONUP -> +0x3c 0x45b850`, `WM_RBUTTONDOWN/DBLCLK -> +0x40
   0x45ba50`, `WM_RBUTTONUP -> +0x44 0x45bc70`, `WM_MOUSEMOVE -> +0x48 0x45be80`, keys -> `0x45b370` (also keeps the
   modifier bits). DirectInput mouse data (`0x45ce10 -> 0x45cea0`) only produces **relative move** events; DI buttons
   are ignored.
2. Each handler converts to an **input event** (20 bytes = 5 dwords) and posts it with `Queue::Post` `0x4309c0`
   (thiscall queue, `(buf, ndwords, flag)`, ret 0xc). Event layout: `+0 u8 type`, `+1 u8 modifiers`, `+8 i16 x`,
   `+0xa i16 y` (screen). Types: `0x10` left down, `0x11` left double click, `0x12` left up, `0x13` right down,
   `0x14` right double click, `0x15` right up, `0x16` mouse move (window message), `0x17` relative DI move;
   `0x01` key (`+4` = VK, e.g. ESC 0x1b), `0x03`, `0x20` other. Modifiers (`obj+0x14`): Shift = 1, Alt = 2, Ctrl = 4.
3. **Logic thread** `CLogicThread::HandleInput` `0x524fa0` pops events from `[logic+0x3c0]` (`0x430980`) and does all
   click logic (64 KB function, mostly if-chains):
   - `0x10/0x11` (left down): panel/minimap areas first (geometry globals `0x730f0c..0x730f38`, see game-state-ui.md);
     map area: build mode places a building (below), otherwise starts the selection drag.
   - `0x12` (left up, `0x5339a1`): selection rectangle / single-click selection (above).
   - `0x13` (right down, `0x534aa5`): stores the current game step `[gd+0x2d2d8]` in `[0x7dfd70]`; if
     `[0x7dfd80] == 1` it handles right-drag scrolling (HYPOTHESIS).
   - `0x15` (right up, `0x53431f`): **the right-click is ignored if the button was held for 15 or more game steps**
     (`[gd+0x2d2d8] - [0x7dfd70] >= 15`, check at `0x53437d`; with `[0x7dfd80] == 1` the limit is 50). This is why a
     long-press right-click does nothing in the original game (relevant for touch: a synthetic right-click must be a
     quick down+up, or the check can be patched). Then: in build mode (`[gd+0x2d284] == 1`) it cancels the placement
     (`[gd+0x2d28c] = 0`); in building mode (`== 4`) it deselects the building (`[0x7dfd6c] = 0`, mode 0). If units
     are selected: plays an acknowledgement (sound 0x39/0x3a/0x3b for <=5 / <=20 / more units, `0x53f560`), computes the
     target (minimap if the point is inside it, else `gd::ScreenToMap`), sends command 3 if the selection is dirty,
     then the move command (9 / 0xd / 0xe / 0xf by modifier, below).
   - `0x16` (move, `0x5348fa`): stores the mouse in `logic+0x44/0x48`, calls `gd::0x4ff0a0`, updates the drag end.
4. Commands are **not executed directly**: HandleInput builds a request and posts it to `[logic+0x3c4]`
   (`Queue::Post(buf, 3 or 2, 1)`), but only if `[0x730f64] != 0` (it is `0xffffffff` in single player, VERIFIED).
   The network layer (lockstep, `NET:` logs) returns it at the execution step; the executor at `0x535a5b` (in the
   logic message handler) switches on the request's command byte (`0x535a9d`, table `0x53b898`/`0x53b934`). Single
   player uses the same path, so **commands are the natural injection point for HUD actions and for multiplayer**.

## Player commands (requests)

Common header: `+0 u8 0x21` (request class), `+1 u8 cmd`, `+2 u8 length in bytes` (0x0c or 0x08), `+3 u8 0`.
Multi-byte numbers in the payload are **big-endian** (high byte first). Executor addresses are the case targets of the
switch at `0x535a9d`.

| cmd | Payload (from +4) | Built at | Executor | Meaning | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0x01 | x(2), y(2), type(2), player(1) | `0x533065` (left click in build mode after `AddBuilding(...,0)` succeeded, sound 0x2e) | `0x535aa4` -> `gd::AddBuilding(x,y,type,player,1)` | place construction site | VERIFIED |
| 0x03 | player(1), slot(1), count(2), ids (2 each, high byte first) ... ; byte +2 = `((count+1)/2 + 2) * 4` | `0x534541` (right-click, if dirty) and `0x52ece7`, `0x52f90d`.. | `0x535cb0` | copy the UI selection to the logic copy | VERIFIED (logic copy filled) |
| 0x09 | player(1), slot(1), x(2), y(2) | `0x53487e` (right-click, no modifier) | `0x536045` (mode 0) | move selected units to tile; on an enemy building/unit this is the attack order (HYPOTHESIS: target classification inside the executor) | VERIFIED (units walked to the tile) |
| 0x0d | same | `0x5345fc` (Shift + right-click) | `0x536045` (mode 1) | add a waypoint (see [Orders](#orders-waypoints-patrol-unit-paths)) | VERIFIED |
| 0x0e | same | `0x534787` (Alt + right-click; a special case with a thief (settler type 0x17) on land of an allied player shows a text message `0x80174` instead) | `0x536045` (mode 2) | patrol between the current position and the target | VERIFIED |
| 0x0f | same | `0x534814` (Ctrl + right-click) | `0x536045` (mode 3) | move ignoring enemies on the way (manual); not inspected further | STATIC + manual |
| 0x06 | building id(2), player(1); length 8 | `0x52fee7` (destroy button in the building panel, mode 4, `[gd+0x2d298] == 1`) | `0x53729c` -> `gd::CrushBuilding` `0x4d9250` | destroy building | STATIC |
| 0x04 | building id(2), new flag(1) = bit 0 of building +0x18 toggled, player(1); length 8 | `0x531d65` (building panel, sounds 0x35/0x36) | `0x536fbf` | Stop / Resume Working (Stop / Resume Building on sites) | VERIFIED (site, 2026-11-08) |
| 0x0c | building id(2), player(1), action(1): 1 max garrison, 2/3/4 add sword/bow/spear, 5 min garrison, 6/7/8 remove | `0x531499..0x531ab6` (towers / castle) | | garrison wishes (game-state-ui.md section 8) | VERIFIED (1) |
| 0x10 | kind(1), player(1), x(2), y(2), count(1), 0; length 12 | `0x52cbf7..0x52d5ff` (settlers page Recruitment) | | 1 geologist, 2 thief, 3 pioneer, 4 pioneer -> carrier, at the view-centre tile | VERIFIED (1, 3) |
| 0xf5 / 0xf6 | building id(2), owner(1); length 8 | `0x531eb3` / `0x531f2c` (building page) | | construction site highest priority on / off | VERIFIED |
| 0xfa | player(1); length 8 | `0x52e510` (multiplayer "Save Game") | | network save | STATIC |
| 0x05 | x(2), y(2), ..., building id | `0x53330e` (building panel, `[gd+0x2d298] = 3`) | `0x5370b4` | set a building's work area / target to a tile (HYPOTHESIS) | STATIC |
| 0x07, 0x08, 0x0a, 0x0b, 0x11 | economy sector / goods index / value | panel code `0x528c65..0x52e040` | `0x5375c7`, `0x53767d`, `0x53919d`, `0x5395b5`, `0x537728` (0x10 = recruitment, below; executor `0x539f30` HYPOTHESIS) | economy settings in the economy sector table `gd+0xe145e8` (0x2e0 bytes each): goods distribution / transport priorities / tool and weapon production (HYPOTHESIS for which is which) | STATIC |
| 0x12, 0x14, 0x15, 0x17 | player, building id, tile x/y, panel action | `0x533439`, `0x5335c9`, `0x5338f4`, `0x533729`, `0x530b43` | `0x5377cf`, `0x538e45`, `0x53888e`, `0x538f19` | building-panel actions with a target tile (0x14/0x17 only for building types 0x20/0x21: HYPOTHESIS harbour/shipyard) | STATIC |
| 0x13, 0x16, 0x18, 0x19, 0x1a, 0x1b, 0x1c | 8-byte requests | `0x52d68b`, `0x52f5ff`, `0x5300bc`.. | see table | unknown | STATIC |
| 0xf1..0xff | | `0x52e510` (0xfa), `0x531eb3` (0xf5), `0x531f2c` (0xf6) | `0x53a1af..0x53b34e` | system: save/load (`slot%2i.sav`), quit, game status, multiplayer save | STATIC |

Executor callee hints (STATIC): 0x02 -> `0x51b4d0`, 0x11 -> `0x51bc20`, 0x12 -> `0x5236b0`, 0x13 -> `0x4dda10`,
0x14/0x17 -> `0x4dbb90`/`0x4db710`, 0x16 -> `0x50ce80`, 0x18 -> `0x508450`, 0x19 -> `0x5194e0`, 0x1c -> `0x4dfb40`.

How a mod issues a command (HYPOTHESIS until W1 tries it): build the bytes as above and call `Queue::Post`
`0x4309c0` with `ecx = [logic+0x3c4]`, args `(ptr, ndwords = len/4, 1)` on the logic thread (where HandleInput runs).
For a move, first write the UI selection and send command 3, exactly like the right-click path. Alternative without
calling game code: post synthetic **input events** (type 0x10..0x16, 20 bytes) to `[logic+0x3c0]` and let HandleInput
do the work (this is what our window-message injection already does indirectly).

## Orders, waypoints, patrol, unit paths

Sources: the game's own manual (`MANUAL/in_keyb/keyb.htm`, `military/military.htm` in the GOG install, read as data)
plus static RE and s3run runs (2026-11-08, `scratch/unit-orders/r2..r4`, local only).

| PC input (units selected) | Command | Executor mode | Effect | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RMB | 0x09 | 0 | move / attack | VERIFIED |
| Shift + RMB | 0x0d | 1 | add a waypoint: written to the first free slot of the settler's queue `+0x30/+0x34/+0x38`; a settler that is not walking (job not one of the walking states) moves there directly (`0x503610`). Manual: "in addition to the normal move three waypoints"; any other move order cancels them | VERIFIED (target 278,248, queue (293,253), (298,276) after a move + 2 Shift clicks) |
| Alt + RMB | 0x0e | 2 | patrol: `0x503610` move to the target, queue = (start = current position, target, `0xfffe` marker), job `0x35` | VERIFIED (queue (223,182), (237,159), (fffe,fffe)) |
| Ctrl + RMB | 0x0f | 3 | move ignoring the enemy on the way (manual) | STATIC + manual |
| Shift + LMB | | | add units to the current selection / group slot | STATIC (`0x533ae2`) |
| Alt + LMB / Ctrl + LMB on a unit | | | select the same kind nearby / all nearby (manual; code `0x533f21..`) | STATIC |
| Tab | | | keep only the wounded soldiers in the selection (`0x525788`) | STATIC + manual |

Ships (types 0x16, 0x28) take a different branch (`+0x1c`, a table at `0x4a97a << 6`); not covered.

Paths for a HUD: per settler, position `+4/+6` -> target `+0x24/+0x26` (when walking on an order, job `0x35`) ->
waypoint queue. Map tile -> 640x480-style screen pixel (the unit's feet), the inverse of `gd::ScreenToMap`:

    sx = 16 x - 8 y - [gd+0x2d254] + 8 W + 280 + 32 res        (W = [gd+0x2d2d0], res = [0x730f08] 1..3)
    sy =  9 y - h  - [gd+0x2d258] + 182                         (h = byte tile(x, y) + 4)

VERIFIED against the hit list for 14 of 14 units (dx 0, dy + h = 182 exactly). With the Mobile HUD's full-screen
layout the shown map is shifted by the original panel width (calibrate against the hit list).

## Control groups

Key handler in `HandleInput`: `vk - 9` indexes the byte table `0x534cbc`, which selects a case of the jump table
`0x534c00`. Digits 1..9 (`0x525ce1..`): with Alt (modifier bit 2) `CLogicThread::AssignGroup(n)` `0x542820`, else
`CLogicThread::SelectGroup(n)` `0x542660` (both thiscall logic, ret 4). VERIFIED in s3run (Alt+1 -> slot 1 count 9;
key 1 -> slot 1; key 1 again -> camera moved).

- Groups are the UI selection slots 1..9 (`word [0x7ad620 + n*2]` count, ids at `0x7ad634 + n*200`); slot 0 is the
  plain selection a click / box creates (`0x533b0d`, without Shift).
- AssignGroup copies the current slot's ids to slot n, sets dirty `[0x7ad5f8 + n*4]`, calls `0x5428e0(id, n)` per
  unit, makes n current and calls `0x542990(n)`.
- SelectGroup(n): nothing if the group is empty. If n is not current: slot = n, building selection 0, panel page 5,
  `0x542990(n)`. If n is already current (second press): average position of the group's own units ->
  `gd::CenterOn` `0x51b560`, i.e. "press twice to centre" (manual).
- The game's deselect click only sets slot -1 (`0x534178`), keeping the group. (Our touch deselect used to zero the
  current slot's count, which emptied a group; fixed 2026-11-08.)
- UI-local: groups are not commands (only the next move syncs the slot with command 3 via the dirty flag).

## Other game-state words seen in `gd+0x2d250..0x2d304`

| Address | Meaning | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gd+0x2d254/+0x2d258` | camera pixel x/y (`0xc04/0x7d4` in one run) | VERIFIED values |
| `gd+0x2d27c` | "refresh panel" flag (set to 1 after many UI actions) | HYPOTHESIS |
| `gd+0x2d284` | panel page: 0 none, 1 build, 2 goods, 3 settlers, 4 building selected, 5 units selected, 7 menu, 8 messages, 9 paused (game-state-ui.md) | VERIFIED |
| `gd+0x2d288/0x2d28c` | build category (1..4) / build list slot (0 = none; right-click clears it). Corrected by re-ui, see game-state-ui.md | VERIFIED |
| `gd+0x2d298` | building panel page/action | STATIC |
| `gd+0x2d2d0` | world size | VERIFIED |
| `gd+0x2d2d4` | local player | VERIFIED |
| `gd+0x2d2d8` | game step counter (used for the right-click time limit) | VERIFIED (increases) |
| `gd+0x2d2e4/0x2d2e8` | last computed target tile (ScreenToMap / placement) | VERIFIED |
| `gd+0x2d2f0` | building type selected for placement (2 after choosing the first building) | VERIFIED |

Global `[0x7dfdb0]` = mission/campaign id (0x42 and 0x63 have special cases). Header-level desync check (`0x53a2xx`)
compares checksums of the building, settler, pile (`gd+0x123885c`, 0xe bytes, count `gd+0x1238858`), trade
(`gd+0x10f45e8`, 0x5a bytes, count `gd+0x110a578`), economy (`gd+0xe145e8`, 0x2e0 bytes, count `gd+0xe115dc`), player
(0x148 bytes) and world tables; the dump helper `0x4ff6d0` writes them to `d:\*.dmp` (debug only).

## Consequences for touch (W3) and the HUD (W4)

- Right-click on touch: send right down + up within the same few frames (or move-command directly). A long press
  cannot be a right-click in the original logic (`0x53437d`).
- Tap on a unit/building: hit list at `0x7ade08`; tap on ground with units selected: command 9 to
  `ScreenToMap(tap)`; box select: synthetic left down/move/up, or write the UI selection + dirty flag.
- Build menu in the HUD: set `[gd+0x2d2f0]` type and mode (`[gd+0x2d284] = 1`, re-ui), or send command 1 directly
  after checking `AddBuilding(x,y,type,player,0)`.
- Selected-unit card: counts per kind from the hit list / settler types; building card: `[0x7dfd6c]` + building table.

## Tools

`s3run --inject` read-only commands added for this work (`port/crates/s3-desktop/src/debug_units.rs`):

- `t:xpeek EXPR LEN` / `t:xdump EXPR LEN FILE`: `EXPR` = address with `@OFF` pointer steps and `+` sums, e.g.
  `GD=0x700ffee0@0x3a0` then `$GD@0x2d280` (game state words), `$GD@0x12a5e5c` (settler count + table),
  `$GD@0x67444+0x4800` (tile column x=1).
- `t:scan VALUE [MAX]`: find dwords in all committed memory (e.g. a vtable to find heap objects).
- re-ui's `dump/peek/poke/regs` (`debug.rs`) for fixed addresses.

Recipe (in game after ~35-50 s on a loaded machine; check with a `shot`): see the runs in
`docs/progress/re-units.md`. Example box select + move:
`51000:move 180 260;51100:down 180 260;51300:move 300 330;51500:move 500 420;51700:move 620 470;51900:up 620 470;54000:rclick 520 140`.
Random maps differ per run (positions, races), so read positions from the dumps or a screenshot first.

## Open questions

- Settler types: done (section "Settler types"); open: 0x14, 0x25, 0x2a.
- Commands 0x05, 0x12..0x1c; Ctrl move (0x0f) effect not traced in the executor.
- Construction state bytes in the building entry.

```

```md
# S3.EXE structure (GOG, sha256 00a925cf…)

## PE header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Machine | i386, PE32, GUI subsystem 4.0 |
| ImageBase | `0x00400000`, **no relocation table** (must load at fixed base — easy for our loader, guest address space must keep 0x400000-0x7ED000 free) |
| EntryPoint | RVA `0x221BC6` |
| SizeOfImage | `0x3ED000` |
| Linker | 6.0 (MSVC 6 / Visual Studio 98) |
| TLS | none |
| Timestamp | 2000-03-31 17:09:52 |

| Section | RVA | VSize | RawSize | Flags |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.text` | `0x1000` | `0x2537F6` (2.3 MB code) | `0x254000` | RX |
| `.rdata` | `0x255000` | `0x3CB36` | `0x3D000` | R |
| `.data` | `0x292000` | `0x158AC8` | `0x116000` | RW (≈270 KB BSS) |
| `.rsrc` | `0x3EB000` | `0x1840` | `0x2000` | R |

Code mentions source paths `E:\Siedler3\DirectX\Ddraw.cpp`, `Dplay.cpp`, `Dsound.cpp`; RTTI names
`CDirectDrawDevice`, `CSurface`, `CPalette`, `CSoundEffect`, `CGameThread`, `CGameNetSession` in namespace `DirectX`,
`CMCIException` in `Win32`, `Lobby::CLMAddPlayerToGroup`. Containers are Watcom-style `WC*` templates.
Debug/log strings are German ("Konnte keine Kreisposition finden"). Banner: "another finest directx game by volker und dirk".

## Static imports — 219 functions

Full list: [s3-exe-imports.md](s3-exe-imports.md). Counts: KERNEL32 130, USER32 41, GDI32 23, ADVAPI32 10 (registry),
`_INMM` 8 (winmm: `timeGetTime`, `timeSetEvent`, `mciSendCommandA/StringA` …), ole32 4 (`CoCreateInstance`, `CoCreateGuid` …),
RPCRT4 2, SHELL32 1. Threads: `CreateThread` + events/semaphores/`WaitForMultipleObjects`. `VirtualProtect` is imported (check why).

## Dynamically loaded (LoadLibraryA / GetProcAddress / CoCreateInstance)

Strings found: `ddraw.dll`, `dsound.dll` (`DirectSoundCreate`), `dinput.dll`, DirectPlay (via COM, `DPLAY:` / `DPERR_*` logs),
`wsock32.dll`, `wininet.dll`, `COMCTL32.dll`, `comdlg32.dll`, `ProtectCD.dll` (copy protection — check if still called in GOG build).
Video: MCI `open AVIVideo!%s alias %s` → Indeo 5 AVI via MCI; `GetCDVideoDirectory`. Music: MCI CD audio (GOG `_inmm.dll` redirects to ogg).

Port implication: the HLE surface is small. Needed families: Win32 kernel (files, threads, sync, time, memory),
a window + message loop, GDI subset (fonts/text? — check which GDI calls are used in game vs. setup paths),
registry (fake, preloaded from `regs.cmd` values), DirectDraw (8/16-bit surfaces, palette, blit, flip),
DirectSound (buffers, mixing), DirectInput (maybe unused — mouse comes via window messages; `GDIMouse` registry),
MCI (music/video), DirectPlay (multiplayer; later).

## Details

- DirectX creation paths and full method list: [directx-surface.md](directx-surface.md).
- `ProtectCD.dll` string has no code references (dead, static view).
- `VirtualProtect` is only used by a page-touch helper (`FUN_0061ab60`), not for self-modifying code.
- Address of the statically linked CRT and helpers: roughly `0x610000-0x630000` (HYPOTHESIS from function addresses).
```

`docs/reverse-engineering/static-isa.md`:

```md
# S3.EXE instruction-set census (static)

Date: 2026-11-05. Target: GOG `S3.EXE` (sha256 `00a925cf…`). Audience: the CPU-interpreter agents.
Question answered: which x86 instructions must the interpreter implement, and which must be bit-exact.

## Method

- Tool: [`tools/isa-census`](../../tools/isa-census) (our Rust code, iced-x86 decoder, prints statistics only).
  Build/run: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=port/target cargo build --release -j 4 --manifest-path tools/isa-census/Cargo.toml`,
  then `port/target/release/isa-census game-files/gog-s3-ultimate/S3.EXE --data-seeds --list-rare`.
- **Recursive descent**, not linear sweep. Seeds: entry point, every 32-bit immediate that points into `.text`
  (callbacks, thread procs, `atexit` funcs), every dword in `.rdata`/`.data` that points into `.text` (vtables,
  jump tables, static-init tables). `jmp [idx*4+table]` tables are followed. Result: **663 233 instructions,
  2 268 855 of 2 439 158 `.text` bytes (93 %)**, 186 jump tables, 355 overlap conflicts and 103 invalid stops
  (these come from data dwords that only look like code pointers; a handful of the "rare" instructions below come
  from them).
- Linear sweep (`objdump -d`) over-counts badly: `.text` has 118 501 bytes of `0x90` padding between game
  functions and 17 609 bytes of `0xCC` padding between CRT functions, plus switch jump tables and byte index
  tables (MSVC `mov dl,[esi+table]; jmp [edx*4+table2]`) inside `.text`. That is where objdump's `in`, `out`,
  `bound`, `retf`, `(bad)` come from. They are **data, not code**.
- Seeding only from the entry point reaches just 11 042 instructions: almost all game code is reached through
  vtables and function pointers, so a decoder must decode lazily at whatever EIP it lands on.
- Helper scripts: [`tools/iat_xrefs.py`](../../tools/iat_xrefs.py) lists every instruction that references an
  IAT slot. [`tools/dis.py`](../../tools/dis.py) disassembles a VA range and shows API names in place of IAT slots.

## CPUID feature classes (recursive descent, data seeds)

| Class (iced `CpuidFeature`) | Count | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| INTEL386 | 594 658 | plain 386 integer code |
| INTEL8086 | 63 397 | 8086-era encodings (string ops, `cdq`, `xchg`, …) |
| FPU (8087) | 4 993 | x87 |
| INTEL186 | 93 | `enter`/`leave`/`push imm`/`imul r,rm,imm`… |
| FPU287 | 84 | `fnstsw ax` etc. |
| MMX | 4 | `movq` ×2, `emms` ×2 (see below) |
| CPUID | 2 | CPU detection (see below) |
| FPU387 | 2 | `fsin`/`fcos`/`fprem1`-class (CRT math) |
| INTEL486 (`bswap`/`xadd`/`cmpxchg`) | **0** | |
| SSE / 3DNow! / CMOV / RDTSC | **0** | |

So: **i386 + x87 is enough.** No SSE, no 3DNow!, no `cmov`, no `rdtsc`, no `bswap`/`cmpxchg`.

## Ranked mnemonics (top part, recursive descent)

`mov` 206 102 · `push` 108 423 · `lea` 58 086 · `call` 57 364 · `jmp` 29 293 · `cmp` 24 448 · `pop` 21 890 ·
`je` 18 786 · `add` 18 176 · `xor` 17 731 · `test` 17 151 · `ret` 13 632 · `sub` 12 597 · `jne` 11 799 ·
`and` 5 660 · `dec` 4 876 · `shl` 3 683 · `inc` 3 477 · `or` 2 716 · `jbe` 2 672 · `jl` 2 066 · `jae` 1 921 ·
`fstp` 1 551 · `shr` 1 489 · `not` 1 429 · `fild` 1 426 · **`repne scasb` 1 373** (inlined `strlen`) ·
`fidiv` 1 361 · `jle` 1 354 · `jge` 1 156 · `jb` 1 130 · `jg` 827 · `imul` 721 · `nop` 705 · `ja` 642 · `sar` 518 ·
**`rep movsd` 511** · `cdq` 489 · `movzx` 347 · `movsx` 333 · `fld` 287 · **`rep movsb` 263** · `neg` 241 ·
`sbb` 227 · `sete` 225 · `idiv` 217 · `setne` 171 · `leave` 167 · **`rep stosd` 159** · `div` 155 · `xchg` 151 ·
`fmul` 86 · `fnstsw` 86 · `jns` 72 · `fcomp` 67 · `mul` 46 · **`repe cmpsb` 45** · `setge` 42 · `setl` 36 ·
`fadd` 35 · `adc` 31 · `js` 29 · `sahf` 26 · `fabs`/`movsd`/`movsw`/`wait` 19 · `fsub` 17 · `fdivr` 16 ·
`movsb` 16 · **`repe cmpsd` 16** · `fst` 15 · `stosb` 14 · `fchs` 13 · `fiadd` 12 · `setg` 11 · `fdiv` 10 ·
`rep stosb` 10 · `setle` 10.
Tail (≤ 9 each): `cld`, `fcom`, `stosd`, `fldcw` 8, `jcxz` 8, `fcompp`, `fldz`, `rcr`, `setb`, `stosw`, `fxch`, `std` 5,
`fistp`, `fld1`, `fnstcw`, `frndint`, `fsqrt`, `lock dec` 4, `xlatb` 4, `faddp`, `fscale`, `ror`, `sal`, `scasb`, `sets`,
`aam`, `bt`/`bts` 2, `cpuid` 2, `emms` 2, `enter` 2, `fist`, `fnclex`, `fnop`, `fsubr`, `jp`, `lock inc` 2, `loop` 2,
`movq` 2, `pushfd` 2, `scasd`, `seta`, `shld` 2, `stc`, `cwde`, `f2xm1`, `fdivp`, `fdivrp`, `fimul`, `fldpi`,
`fnsave`/`frstor` 1, `fyl2x` 1, `jecxz`, `lahf`, `lodsb`, `loope`, `pushad`, `rep stosw`, `setae`, `setns`.
(`in`/`out`/`iretd`/`int1`/`into`/`bound`/`arpl`/`retf`/`salc`/`insb`/`sti`/`cli`, 1–4 each, and the 5 `gs:` and 4 `es:`/`cs:`
overrides are decodes of misidentified data; they do not appear in real functions. Treat them as "raise #UD".)

## What must be exact (priority list for the interpreter)

1. **Integer core + EFLAGS**: `add/sub/adc/sbb/cmp/test/and/or/xor/inc/dec/neg/not`, shifts (`shl/shr/sar/rol/ror/rcr`,
   `shld` 2×), `imul` (1-, 2-, 3-operand), `mul`, `div`, `idiv`, `cdq`, `cwde`, `setcc`, `jcc`, `movzx/movsx`, `xchg`,
   `lea`, `leave`, `enter` (2×). `sahf`/`lahf` are used after `fnstsw ax` for float compares → PF/ZF/CF from AH matter.
   `jp`/`jnp` exist (float compare unordered checks).
2. **String ops with prefixes**: `repne scasb` (strlen, 1 373×), `rep movsd`/`rep movsb` (memcpy), `rep stosd`/`stosb`/
   `stosw` (memset), `repe cmpsb`/`cmpsd` (memcmp/strcmp), single `movs*`/`stos*`/`lods*`/`scas*`. **DF**: `std` appears
   5× (backwards `memmove` in the CRT); `cld` 9×. Respect DF.
3. **Address-size prefix `0x67` on `jcxz`**: the hand-written blitters at `0x5c3e27`, `0x5c3e2f`, `0x5c3e57`,
   `0x5c3fc5`, `0x5c3fcd`, `0x5c3fe1`… use `67 E3 xx` = **`jcxz` (tests CX, not ECX)**. iced decodes it as `Jcxz`
   (8×) vs `Jecxz` (1×). Implement both. `loop` (ECX) is used right after (`0x5c3fdc`).
4. **x87** (≈5 000 instrs). Most are static initialisers of float constants (`fild/fidiv/fstp` in ~1 360 tiny functions,
   `0x54f2xx`–`0x58xxxx`) and game math (`fmul/fadd/fcomp/fnstsw/sahf`). CRT `_ftol` = **`0x61fe98`**
   (`fnstcw`, `or ah,0x0c`, `fldcw`, `fistp qword`, `fldcw`), called 44×: **rounding control must be honoured**
   (truncate inside `_ftol`, round-to-nearest otherwise). CRT math uses `fyl2x`, `f2xm1`, `fscale`, `frndint`, `fprem`,
   `fsqrt`, `fxam`, `fldpi/fldln2/fldl2e/fldlg2`, `fnsave/frstor`, `fnstenv/fldenv`, `fnclex`. A 64-bit-double
   implementation of the x87 stack is very likely good enough (HYPOTHESIS: no code relies on 80-bit precision; game
   logic is integer — Settlers sync is lockstep, check that float results do not feed network-synced state).
5. **`fs:` segment** (5 489 uses): every C++/SEH function does `mov eax,fs:[0]; push eax; mov fs:[0],esp`
   (1 661 frames). Only `fs:[0]` (SEH chain head) and `fs:[4]` (stack base, 1 site) are read; no `fs:[0x18]`/
   `fs:[0x2c]` (TLS goes through `TlsGetValue`). FS base must point to a per-thread TIB.
6. **`lock` prefix**: `lock dec` 4×, `lock inc` 2× (plus `InterlockedIncrement/Decrement/Exchange` imports).
   With a single-threaded interpreter (one guest thread at a time) atomicity is free.
7. **CPUID**: only in the CPU detector `0x5c3900` / `0x5c3970` (leaf 1). Both run inside an SEH `__try`
   (`_except_handler3`): if `cpuid` faults, the `__except` path returns 0 ("no CPUID"). If implemented, return
   a Pentium-class family 5/6 and **EDX bit 23 (MMX) = 0** – see next point.
8. **MMX**: only one routine, `0x5c3ee0`→`0x5c3f00` (an 8-byte `movq` memcpy-to-surface loop, `emms` at `0x5c405a`),
   plus a probe `emms` at `0x5c39f0`. `0x5c3740` benchmarks five surface-copy routines (`0x5c3a40`, `0x5c3d40`,
   `0x5c4070`, `0x5c40f0`, and the MMX one **only if** CPUID says MMX) with `QueryPerformanceCounter` and keeps the
   fastest. **Report no MMX and no MMX code ever runs.** The timing loop at `0x5c4280`-`0x5c4300` calls each
   routine repeatedly and adds `(QPC delta)/QPF` until the total passes a constant: **`QueryPerformanceCounter` must
   advance between calls** or the loop never ends. If `QueryPerformanceFrequency` returns FALSE the benchmark is
   skipped (`je 0x5c4310`).
9. **No self-modifying code**: no instruction writes to an absolute `.text` address (census "store to .text" = 0).
   `VirtualProtect` is only used by the page-touch helper `0x61ab60` on memory-mapped GFX files. A decode cache per
   EIP is safe. `.text` contains jump tables and byte tables, so never pre-decode linearly.
10. **Calls**: 57 k direct `call rel32`, 1 679 indirect `call [reg+off]` (vtables), imports via `call [IAT]` **and**
    `mov reg,[IAT]; call reg` (e.g. `PeekMessageA` at `0x60d6d5`, `GetProcAddress` at `0x60ceb5`). 6 import thunks
    `jmp [IAT]` (e.g. `RtlUnwind` at `0x62ef78`). So HLE must trap on *executing* the IAT target address, not on
    the call instruction pattern.

## Not present

`rdtsc`, SSE (the 7 `movups/movlps/divps/orps/movmskps` hits in linear sweep are data), 3DNow!, `cmov`, `bswap`,
`cmpxchg`, `xadd`, `int 0x2e`/`sysenter` (no direct syscalls), `int 3` in reached code (9 hits are padding at the
end of functions after no-return calls).

```

`docs/reverse-engineering/static-startup.md`:

```md
# S3.EXE startup, window, message loop, threads, frame pacing (static)

Date: 2026-11-05. Source: REA/Ghidra 12.1.2 + objdump on GOG `S3.EXE` (sha256 `00a925cf…`). All addresses are VAs.
Everything here is **static** (not observed at runtime) unless marked otherwise. Helper: `tools/dis.py` (disassembly
with API names), `tools/iat_xrefs.py` (all IAT references).

## 1. Entry → WinMain (standard MSVC6 `WinMainCRTStartup`)

`entry` `0x621bc6`, SEH frame with `_except_handler3` = **`0x622230`**, scope table `0x65de38`:

| Step | Address | MSVC6 CRT name (by shape) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GetVersion` → `_osver/_winver/_winmajor/_winminor` at `0x7e9350..5c` | | |
| `FUN_00628496(1)` | `0x628496` | `_heap_init` (`HeapCreate`; small-block heap uses `VirtualAlloc` at `0x628be5/0x628c71`) |
| `FUN_006228d3` | `0x6228d3` | `_mtinit` (`TlsAlloc`, per-thread data `_ptd`, 0x74 bytes) |
| `FUN_006232b1` | `0x6232b1` | `_ioinit` (`GetStartupInfoA`, `GetStdHandle`, `GetFileType`, `SetHandleCount`) |
| `GetCommandLineA`, `FUN_00629f98` | | `__crtGetEnvironmentStringsA` |
| `FUN_00629d4b`, `FUN_00629c92` | | `_setargv`, `_setenvp` |
| `FUN_0061f06a` | `0x61f06a` | `_cinit` → runs C++ static constructors (thousands; e.g. global `CString`s and float constants) |
| `GetStartupInfoA`, `FUN_00629c3a` | | `_wincmdln` |
| **`FUN_0045a120(GetModuleHandleA(0), 0, cmdline, nShow)`** | `0x45a120` | **WinMain** |
| `FUN_0061f097(ret)` | `0x61f097` | `exit` (atexit table, then `ExitProcess`) |

WinMain `0x45a120`:
1. `GetSystemTime`; **if `wYear > 2037` → MessageBox "The Settlers III cannot be started…" and exit**
   (HLE: return a sane date).
2. `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")` (`0x620001`).
3. Construct the application object (`0x4043d0`, `this` = global; virtual inheritance, `CThread` base).
4. `FUN_0060f000` → `0x60e2d0` = `CThread::Execute` on the **main thread**: state=5, `vtbl+0x10` **Init**
   (`0x40b3f0` via thunk `0x40a790`), `vtbl+0x14` **Run** (`0x404860`), `vtbl+0x18` **Exit** (`0x404b10`).
5. Destructors (`0x60bfe0`×3, `0x5b59d0`, `0x610330`, `0x60dff0`), return exit code.

Init `0x40b3f0` (main thread): version banner (`"Siedler3 Version %i.%i: (%x,%x)"`, `0x7a8000/4` from `0x60eff0`),
`0x60ca30`, settings (`0x40d700`, registry, see §6), `GetModuleFileNameA`, command line (`0x410da0`: options
`-messe` = 640x480 trade-show mode, `-mouse`, …), `SetThreadPriority(main, 2 = HIGHEST)` (`0x60e9d0` called at
`0x40b9cf`), window + DirectX setup (`0x405b00`/`0x404d..`), `0x49d8f0`, `0x5b5a30`.

## 2. Window

Generic window class code (namespace "DirectX"/`Win32` library, `0x60ff00`, called from `0x45ae40` and `0x5b5db1`):

- `RegisterClassA` with WNDCLASS from virtual `GetWndClass` (default `0x60ffa0`): `style=0`, **`lpfnWndProc =
  0x610040`**, `cbClsExtra=0`, `cbWndExtra=0` (the S3 subclass sets extra bytes, `DAT_007e9170` = window-long index),
  `hIcon=LoadIconA(0, IDI_APPLICATION)`, `hCursor=LoadCursorA(0, IDC_ARROW)`, `hbrBackground=6`,
  **class name `"CWindow"`** (`0x7a4598`).
- `CreateWindowExA` from a CREATESTRUCT filled by virtual `Create`:
  - S3 window (`0x45ade0`, vtable `0x657238`): **exStyle `WS_EX_TOPMOST` (8)**, **style `0x90C80000` =
    `WS_POPUP|WS_VISIBLE|WS_CAPTION|WS_SYSMENU`** (set at `0x45ace7`), x=y=0,
    **cx=`GetSystemMetrics(SM_CXSCREEN)`, cy=`GetSystemMetrics(SM_CYSCREEN)`**, no parent/menu, title from the object
    (default `""`). `ShowCursor(FALSE)` if `0x7a8018` set.
  - Base DirectX window (`0x5b5d50`, vtable `0x65c9c8`): same but style `0x90080000` (`WS_POPUP|WS_VISIBLE|WS_SYSMENU`).
  - `ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_SHOW)` at `0x60fe46`.
- **WndProc `0x610040`**: `GetWindowLongA(hwnd, idx)`; on the first message (`WM_GETMINMAXINFO`/`WM_NCCREATE`, object
  not yet attached) it stores the creating object (`0x7e9174`) with `SetWindowLongA` and sets `obj->hwnd`; then calls
  virtual `obj->vtbl[+0xC](hwnd, msg, wParam, lParam)`. S3: `0x45c820` → `vtbl[+0x78]` = message switch **`0x45c860`**.
- Messages handled by `0x45c860` (everything else → `DefWindowProcA`):
  `WM_ACTIVATEAPP 0x1C`, `WM_SETCURSOR 0x20`, `WM_DISPLAYCHANGE 0x7E`, `WM_NCPAINT 0x85`, `WM_NCACTIVATE 0x86`,
  `WM_NCMOUSEMOVE 0xA0`, `WM_NCLBUTTON*/NCRBUTTON* 0xA1–0xA6`, `WM_KEYDOWN 0x100`, `WM_KEYUP 0x101`, `WM_CHAR 0x102`,
  `WM_SYSKEYDOWN 0x104`, `WM_SYSKEYUP 0x105`, `WM_MOUSEMOVE 0x200`, `WM_LBUTTONDOWN/UP/DBLCLK 0x201–0x203`,
  `WM_RBUTTONDOWN/UP/DBLCLK 0x204–0x206`, `MM_MCINOTIFY 0x3B9` (music/video end), `WM_APP+2..+4 0x802–0x804`
  (internal). **So keyboard comes only via window messages; mouse comes via window messages and DirectInput.**
- Second window class: `RegisterClassExA` `0x615831` + `CreateWindowExA` `0x6159e4` (module `0x615xxx`; HYPOTHESIS:
  hidden helper window of the lobby/network code — not on the main menu path).

## 3. Main-thread loop (input + message pump)

Run `0x404860` (main thread, priority HIGHEST):
```
loop:
  while game_active (0x4120d0):
      vtbl call (… +8)(-1, 0xFF)                       ; HYPOTHESIS: signal/refresh
      while DI mouse has data (0x5ba260):              ; DirectInput event handle signalled
          n = GetDeviceData(buf, 2, 0) (0x5ba290)      ; DIDEVICEOBJECTDATA, 16 bytes each, 2 per call
          for each: 0x45ce10(obj)                      ; mouse event → game
          0x45ce90()
      0x45ce90()
      while PeekMessageA(&m,0,0,0,PM_NOREMOVE) (0x60d9e0 → 0x60d9f0):
          if GetMessage-step (0x60d740) == WM_QUIT: 0x45d2a0(); PostQuitMessage(code)
  if 0x5b8c40(): drain DI buffer
  if 0x60d740() == WM_QUIT: return wParam               ; blocking GetMessageA
```
`0x60d740` = one `GetMessageA(&m, this->hwndFilter, 0, 0)` + `TranslateMessage` + (thread messages with `hwnd==0` go
to `vtbl+8`) + `DispatchMessageA`. Returns 1 on `WM_QUIT`.

The four `PeekMessageA` sites:

| Site | Function | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0x60d6d5` | `0x60d6d0` | idle loop: `while(!PeekMessage(NOREMOVE)) vtbl[+4]()` (OnIdle); then `0x60d740` |
| `0x60d9f0` | `0x60d9e0` | "message waiting?" test used by Run above |
| `0x60f452` | `0x60f430` | `PeekMessage(NOREMOVE)` at the start of a new thread → **creates the thread message queue** (classic trick), then signals the creator (`0x42cf80` = `SetEvent`) |
| `0x60f893` | `0x60f880` | same, other thread class |

HLE consequence: each guest thread needs its own message queue (`PostThreadMessageA` is imported, 1 site);
`PeekMessage` with `PM_NOREMOVE` must create it.

## 4. Threads

All threads go through CRT **`_beginthreadex` = `0x62279a`** (the only `CreateThread` caller, `0x6227db`);
`_threadstartex` = `0x622805` (sets TLS `_ptd`, installs SEH, calls `[ptd+0x48](arg)`, then `_endthreadex`).
`_beginthreadex` has exactly one caller: **`CThread::Start` `0x60e060`**:
`_beginthreadex(NULL, 0x1000 /*stack commit hint*/, 0x60ec20, this, CREATE_SUSPENDED, &this->tid)`, then
`ResumeThread`. Thread proc **`0x60ec20`**: log `"Thread gestartet"`, `this->vtbl[+0x1C]()` (thread body), log
`"Thread beendet"`, return. Priorities via `SetThreadPriority` wrapper `0x60e9d0`.

`CGameThread::Start` = `0x5b6130` (passes the app's message thread as parent); per-thread init `0x5b6160`
(`CoInitialize`, see `"CGameThread::~CGameThread:: iCoInitOpen != 0"`).

| Thread (RTTI) | Created at | Object size / ctor | Pacing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Main (app, `CConsoleThread`?) | process main thread | `0x4043d0` | blocking `GetMessageA` / DirectInput event |
| `CLogicThread` (`lpLogicThread`) | `0x4058cc`, started `0x405954` | 0x678 B, `0x53c5e0` | **periodic timer 64 ms** (`0x53d761`: `SetPeriodic(0x40)`), priority +1 (`0x53d743`) |
| `CDrawThread` / `DirectX::CGameDrawThread` (`lpDrawThread`) | `0x40583f` | 0x74 B, `0x42c2d0` | draw as fast as possible; `WaitForVerticalBlank(DDWAITVB_BLOCKBEGIN)` if `WaitVBlank` (§DirectDraw); `Flip` retry `Sleep(0)` |
| `CNetThread` (`lpNetThread`) | `0x4057c0`, started `0x40582c` | `0x46f4e0` | periodic 500 ms? (`0x493617`: `SetPeriodic(0x1F4)`) |
| `Menus::CNetThread` (`lpMenuNetThread`) | `0x4055a6` area, started `0x4055b6` | | periodic **500 ms** (`0x45f3b7`) |
| `Menus::CDrawThread` (`lpMenuDrawThread`) | `0x40553f` area | | menu rendering |
| `Menus::priv::CFTPThread`, `CNetBounceThread`, `LobbyClient::priv::CHelperThread` | network/lobby only | | |

HYPOTHESIS: in the main menu the running threads are main + `Menus::CDrawThread` + `Menus::CNetThread`; in a game
main + `CLogicThread` + `CDrawThread` + `CNetThread`. Threads talk through events (`SetEvent`/`PulseEvent` 11 sites/
`ResetEvent`), semaphores, critical sections and `PostThreadMessageA`.

### Waiting / timers (`Win32::CWin32Waitable`, `CWin32WaitableBag`)

- Generic thread loop `0x60da30` (`CMessagedThread`): builds a handle array from its waitable bag and loops on
  **`MsgWaitForMultipleObjects(n, handles, FALSE, timeout, wakeMask)`** (`0x60db22`); index `n` = message → `0x60d740`;
  `WAIT_TIMEOUT (0x102)` → throws (`"CWin32Waitable::WaitForXYZ"`); otherwise dispatches signalled object `0x463db0`.
  Same with no message queue: `0x60dcd0` (`MsgWaitFor…` at `0x60ddaf`) and `WaitForMultipleObjects` at `0x4631db`.
- Timer object (`0x60ce..`): at construction it does `GetProcAddress(kernel32, "CreateWaitableTimerA" /
  "OpenWaitableTimerA" / "SetWaitableTimer" / "CancelWaitableTimer")` (`0x60ceb5`–`0x60cee8`).
  - **If `CreateWaitableTimerA` is found**: waitable-timer path. `SetPeriodic(ms)` `0x60d3a0` →
    `0x60d0a0`: `SetWaitableTimer(h, &due, period=ms, NULL, NULL, resume)` with **`due = +ms*10000`** (positive =
    absolute time in 1601 → already past → fires immediately, then every `ms`).
  - **Else (Win95 path)**: `timeBeginPeriod(res)` (`0x60cef5`), event object, and
    `timeSetEvent(ms, 0, 0x60d640, this, TIME_PERIODIC)` (`0x60d34c`); callback `0x60d640` → `SetEvent` (`0x42cf80`).
  - HLE choice: returning NULL from `GetProcAddress("CreateWaitableTimerA")` selects the `timeSetEvent` path
    (needs a host timer thread that sets an event). Providing waitable timers is equally simple. Either way the
    logic tick is **64 ms (15.6 ticks/s)** — HYPOTHESIS: game speed setting changes this period.
- `timeGetTime` is called from 31 sites (animation, scrolling, network timing): needs millisecond resolution.
  `QueryPerformanceCounter/Frequency` only in the blit benchmark `0x5c4280`. `GetTickCount` 2 sites.

### Android lifecycle (pause/resume) — HYPOTHESIS

Pausing = stop scheduling all guest threads and stop the host timer thread; on resume, the 64 ms timer simply
continues. Because `due` is relative to "now" only at arm time, no catch-up burst happens with `timeSetEvent`.

## 5. Exceptions (SEH + C++ EH) — how much emulation is needed

- **C++ exceptions are used for normal error handling** (DirectX failures, waits, file errors):
  `__CxxThrowException@8` = **`0x61f027`** (149 call sites, 69 of them rethrow `throw;`), which calls
  `RaiseException(0xE06D7363, EXCEPTION_NONCONTINUABLE, 3, {magic, pObj, pThrowInfo})` (`0x61f055`).
  `__CxxFrameHandler` = **`0x61ec26`**; 1 653 per-function stubs `mov eax, FuncInfo; jmp 0x61ec26`;
  1 661 functions push an SEH record on `fs:[0]`. Example: `WaitForVerticalBlank` failure is caught in the draw
  thread (`0x42cddb`) and the catch block turns the option off.
- Plain SEH `__try/__except` with **`_except_handler3` `0x622230`** (24 frames): CRT startup, thread start
  `0x622805`, CPUID/MMX probes `0x5c3900`/`0x5c3970`, others.
- `RtlUnwind` (thunk `0x62ef78`) is used by both handlers; `RaiseException` also at `0x62e3bf` (CRT);
  `SetUnhandledExceptionFilter` `0x624b7f/0x624b91`, `UnhandledExceptionFilter` `0x629bf6`.
- **Needed in the HLE**: a real Win32 SEH dispatcher — `RaiseException` builds `EXCEPTION_RECORD` + `CONTEXT` on the
  guest stack, walks the `fs:[0]` chain calling each guest handler (`handler(rec, frame, ctx, dispctx)`),
  honours `ExceptionContinueSearch/ContinueExecution`; `RtlUnwind(targetFrame, targetIp, rec, retval)` calls handlers
  with `EH_UNWINDING` (flag 2) and pops `fs:[0]`. The CRT's `__CxxFrameHandler` then does all C++ work (catch
  matching, destructors, `_JumpToContinuation`) in guest code — no C++ knowledge needed in the host.
  Hardware faults (#DE, access violation) only need to be turned into SEH exceptions if we want the game's own
  error dialogs; for bring-up, abort with a host log.

## 6. Kernel32 hot path vs rare (static call-site counts, `call [IAT]` only; `mov reg,[IAT]` sites come on top)

Hot (per frame / per tick / per allocation): `timeGetTime` (31), `EnterCriticalSection`/`LeaveCriticalSection`
(game + CRT locks), `SetEvent`/`PulseEvent`/`ResetEvent`, `WaitForSingleObject`, `WaitForMultipleObjects`,
`MsgWaitForMultipleObjects`, `PeekMessageA`/`GetMessageA`/`DispatchMessageA`, `InterlockedIncrement/Decrement/
Exchange`, `HeapAlloc`/`HeapFree`/`HeapReAlloc` (via CRT `malloc`; MSVC6 small-block heap sits on top),
`TlsGetValue` (CRT `_getptd`, every `errno`/`rand`/`strtok`), `GetLastError`/`SetLastError` (146 sites, error checks
after every API), `Sleep(0)` (Flip retry), `OutputDebugStringA` (35 sites, debug log `0x428720`).
File I/O during loading: `CreateFileA`, `ReadFile`, `SetFilePointer`, `GetFileSize`, `CloseHandle`, `FindFirstFileA/
FindNextFileA/FindClose`, **`CreateFileMappingA` + `MapViewOfFile`** (GFX `.dat` files are memory-mapped by the
`CMappedFile` class `0x61a5xx`/`0x61a80c` and pre-faulted with `VirtualProtect`/`VirtualQuery` page-touch helper
`0x61ab60`, called from the GFX loader `0x5fa833`, `0x5ff2a6` and `0x61b358`, `0x61b4e1`; one more mapping at
`0x5a9d17`).
Rare (startup/shutdown/locale): everything else (`GetVersion`, `GetStartupInfoA`, locale/codepage functions,
environment, `CreateProcessA` (patch converter `565to555`, `ShellExecuteExA`), `GetTempPathA`, `CopyFileA`, …).

```
