`port/crates/s3-android/src/present.rs`:

```rs
//! Render thread: presents the newest frame on the ANativeWindow with EGL + GLES 2 (docs/porting/display.md).
//!
//! - The engine thread only copies its frame into `Shared::frame` and signals `Shared::frame_cv`; it never waits
//!   for the display.
//! - This thread uploads the RGB565 frame (`glTexSubImage2D`, no CPU conversion or scaling) and draws one textured
//!   quad placed by [`Viewport`] (Fit / Fill / Stretch / Native wide) with the selected filter (nearest, linear,
//!   sharp bilinear shader); `eglSwapBuffers` with swap interval 1
//!   paces it to the display (60/90/120 Hz). It requests the panel's high refresh rate with
//!   `ANativeWindow_setFrameRate[WithChangeStrategy]` (looked up with dlsym: API 30/31).
//! - The mods' window layer (`s3_mods::layer`: HUD, FPS counter, touch feedback, Classic floating UI at window
//!   resolution) is rasterized here ([`LayerRaster`], only the changed rectangle), uploaded as a second RGBA texture
//!   (only the changed rows) and blended over the game quad (premultiplied alpha). In UI mode A the scene's panel
//!   split draws the panel part of the frame at its own scale ([`Viewport::quads`]).
//! - If EGL / GLES fails, it falls back to the old CPU path (`ANativeWindow_lock`, letterbox, compositor scaling).
//! - Window changes come from the activity thread through [`Presenter::set_window`]; losing the window waits until
//!   the EGL surface is destroyed (Android requires that before `onNativeWindowDestroyed` returns).

use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Condvar, Mutex};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use ndk::hardware_buffer_format::HardwareBufferFormat;
use ndk::native_window::NativeWindow;
use s3_mods::display::{DisplayMode, Viewport};

use crate::frontend::Shared;
use crate::gl::*;
use crate::glrender::{Composer, GlRenderer};
use crate::layout::{blit_letterboxed, Letterbox};

struct CtlState {
    window: Option<NativeWindow>,
    gen: u64,
    acked: u64,
    quit: bool,
}

struct Ctl {
    m: Mutex<CtlState>,
    cv: Condvar,
    /// Mirror of `CtlState::gen` readable without the lock.
    gen: AtomicU64,
}

pub struct Presenter {
    ctl: Arc<Ctl>,
    shared: Arc<Shared>,
    thread: Option<std::thread::JoinHandle<()>>,
}

impl Presenter {
    pub fn start(shared: Arc<Shared>) -> Presenter {
        let ctl = Arc::new(Ctl { m: Mutex::new(CtlState { window: None, gen: 0, acked: 0, quit: false }), cv: Condvar::new(), gen: AtomicU64::new(0) });
        let (c2, s2) = (ctl.clone(), shared.clone());
        let thread = std::thread::Builder::new()
            .name("s3-present".into())
            .spawn(move || render_thread(c2, s2))
            .expect("spawn render thread");
        Presenter { ctl, shared, thread: Some(thread) }
    }

    /// New window (or `None` when it goes away). Waits (up to 2 s) until the render thread switched.
    pub fn set_window(&self, w: Option<NativeWindow>) {
        let mut c = self.ctl.m.lock().unwrap();
        c.window = w;
        c.gen += 1;
        let gen = c.gen;
        self.ctl.gen.store(gen, Ordering::Release);
        drop(c);
        self.shared.notify_render();
        let c = self.ctl.m.lock().unwrap();
        let _ = self.ctl.cv.wait_timeout_while(c, Duration::from_secs(2), |c| c.acked < gen && !c.quit).unwrap();
    }

    /// Redraw the current image (RedrawNeeded / resume).
    pub fn invalidate(&self) {
        self.shared.display_seq.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
        self.shared.notify_render();
    }
}

impl Drop for Presenter {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.ctl.m.lock().unwrap().quit = true;
        self.ctl.gen.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
        self.shared.notify_render();
        if let Some(t) = self.thread.take() {
            let _ = t.join();
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- frame rate request (dlsym, API 30+)

extern "C" {
    fn dlopen(name: *const std::ffi::c_char, flags: i32) -> *mut c_void;
    fn dlsym(h: *mut c_void, name: *const std::ffi::c_char) -> *mut c_void;
}

type SetFrameRate = unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, f32, i8) -> i32;
type SetFrameRateStrategy = unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, f32, i8, i8) -> i32;

fn request_frame_rate(win: &NativeWindow, hz: f32) {
    unsafe {
        let h = dlopen(c"libandroid.so".as_ptr(), 0);
        let h = if h.is_null() { dlopen(c"libnativewindow.so".as_ptr(), 0) } else { h };
        if h.is_null() {
            log::warn!("present: dlopen libandroid failed; no frame rate request");
            return;
        }
        let p = win.ptr().as_ptr() as *mut c_void;
        let f = dlsym(h, c"ANativeWindow_setFrameRateWithChangeStrategy".as_ptr());
        if !f.is_null() {
            let f: SetFrameRateStrategy = std::mem::transmute(f);
            // COMPATIBILITY_DEFAULT (0), CHANGE_FRAME_RATE_ALWAYS (1).
            let r = f(p, hz, 0, 1);
            log::info!("present: ANativeWindow_setFrameRateWithChangeStrategy({hz}) -> {r}");
            return;
        }
        let f = dlsym(h, c"ANativeWindow_setFrameRate".as_ptr());
        if !f.is_null() {
            let f: SetFrameRate = std::mem::transmute(f);
            let r = f(p, hz, 0);
            log::info!("present: ANativeWindow_setFrameRate({hz}) -> {r}");
        } else {
            log::info!("present: ANativeWindow_setFrameRate unavailable (API < 30)");
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- GL state

struct Gles {
    display: EGLDisplay,
    config: EGLConfig,
    context: EGLContext,
    surface: EGLSurface,
    /// The context is GLES 3 (needed by the AI filter).
    es3: bool,
    /// Programs and textures (`crate::glrender`), created on the first attach.
    r: Option<GlRenderer>,
}

impl Gles {
    unsafe fn new() -> Result<Gles, String> {
        let display = eglGetDisplay(EGL_DEFAULT_DISPLAY);
        if display == EGL_NO_DISPLAY || eglInitialize(display, std::ptr::null_mut(), std::ptr::null_mut()) == 0 {
            return Err(format!("eglInitialize: {:#x}", eglGetError()));
        }
        // GLES 3 capable configs first (the AI filter needs a GLES 3 context), else GLES 2.
        let mut configs = [std::ptr::null_mut(); 32];
        let mut n = 0;
        let mut es3 = false;
        for bits in [EGL_OPENGL_ES2_BIT | EGL_OPENGL_ES3_BIT_KHR, EGL_OPENGL_ES2_BIT] {
            let attribs = [
                EGL_SURFACE_TYPE, EGL_WINDOW_BIT, EGL_RENDERABLE_TYPE, bits,
                EGL_RED_SIZE, 5, EGL_GREEN_SIZE, 6, EGL_BLUE_SIZE, 5, EGL_DEPTH_SIZE, 0, EGL_NONE,
            ];
            if eglChooseConfig(display, attribs.as_ptr(), configs.as_mut_ptr(), 32, &mut n) != 0 && n > 0 {
                es3 = bits & EGL_OPENGL_ES3_BIT_KHR != 0;
                break;
            }
        }
        if n == 0 {
            return Err(format!("eglChooseConfig: {:#x}", eglGetError()));
        }
        // Prefer an exact RGB565 / no-alpha config (cheapest scan-out), else the first one.
        let mut config = configs[0];
        for &c in &configs[..n as usize] {
            let (mut r, mut g, mut b, mut a) = (0, 0, 0, 0);
            eglGetConfigAttrib(display, c, EGL_RED_SIZE, &mut r);
            eglGetConfigAttrib(display, c, EGL_GREEN_SIZE, &mut g);
            eglGetConfigAttrib(display, c, EGL_BLUE_SIZE, &mut b);
            eglGetConfigAttrib(display, c, EGL_ALPHA_SIZE, &mut a);
            if (r, g, b, a) == (8, 8, 8, 0) || (r, g, b, a) == (5, 6, 5, 0) {
                config = c;
                if r == 8 {
                    break; // RGBX8888 avoids 565 dithering of the sharp-bilinear edges.
                }
            }
        }
        let mut context = EGL_NO_CONTEXT;
        if es3 {
            let ctx3 = [EGL_CONTEXT_CLIENT_VERSION, 3, EGL_NONE];
            context = eglCreateContext(display, config, EGL_NO_CONTEXT, ctx3.as_ptr());
            es3 = context != EGL_NO_CONTEXT;
        }
        if context == EGL_NO_CONTEXT {
            let ctx_attribs = [EGL_CONTEXT_CLIENT_VERSION, 2, EGL_NONE];
            context = eglCreateContext(display, config, EGL_NO_CONTEXT, ctx_attribs.as_ptr());
        }
        if context == EGL_NO_CONTEXT {
            return Err(format!("eglCreateContext: {:#x}", eglGetError()));
        }
        log::info!("present: GLES {} context", if es3 { 3 } else { 2 });
        Ok(Gles { display, config, context, surface: EGL_NO_SURFACE, es3, r: None })
    }

    /// Create the window surface (and on first use the GL objects). Returns the surface size.
    unsafe fn attach(&mut self, win: &NativeWindow) -> Result<(u32, u32), String> {
        self.detach();
        let mut visual = 0;
        eglGetConfigAttrib(self.display, self.config, EGL_NATIVE_VISUAL_ID, &mut visual);
        let fmt = HardwareBufferFormat::from(visual);
        let _ = win.set_buffers_geometry(0, 0, Some(fmt));
        let s = eglCreateWindowSurface(self.display, self.config, win.ptr().as_ptr() as *mut c_void, [EGL_NONE].as_ptr());
        if s == EGL_NO_SURFACE {
            return Err(format!("eglCreateWindowSurface: {:#x}", eglGetError()));
        }
        if eglMakeCurrent(self.display, s, s, self.context) == 0 {
            eglDestroySurface(self.display, s);
            return Err(format!("eglMakeCurrent: {:#x}", eglGetError()));
        }
        self.surface = s;
        eglSwapInterval(self.display, 1);
        if self.r.is_none() {
            self.r = Some(GlRenderer::new(self.es3)?);
        }
        Ok(self.size())
    }

    unsafe fn size(&self) -> (u32, u32) {
        let (mut w, mut h) = (0, 0);
        eglQuerySurface(self.display, self.surface, EGL_WIDTH, &mut w);
        eglQuerySurface(self.display, self.surface, EGL_HEIGHT, &mut h);
        (w.max(1) as u32, h.max(1) as u32)
    }

    unsafe fn detach(&mut self) {
        if self.surface != EGL_NO_SURFACE {
            eglMakeCurrent(self.display, EGL_NO_SURFACE, EGL_NO_SURFACE, self.context);
            eglDestroySurface(self.display, self.surface);
            self.surface = EGL_NO_SURFACE;
        }
    }

    /// Swap; `false` if the surface is gone (re-attach needed).
    unsafe fn swap(&mut self) -> bool {
        if eglSwapBuffers(self.display, self.surface) == 0 {
            let e = eglGetError();
            log::warn!("present: eglSwapBuffers failed {e:#x}");
            return false;
        }
        true
    }
}

impl Drop for Gles {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        unsafe {
            self.detach();
            eglDestroyContext(self.display, self.context);
            eglTerminate(self.display);
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the thread

fn render_thread(ctl: Arc<Ctl>, shared: Arc<Shared>) {
    let mut gles: Option<Gles> = None;
    let mut gl_failed = false;
    let mut window: Option<NativeWindow> = None;
    let mut my_gen = 0u64;
    let mut win_size = (1u32, 1u32);
    let mut comp = Composer::new();
    let mut cpu_geometry: Option<(u32, u32)> = None;
    let mut fps_t0 = Instant::now();
    let mut fps_n = 0u32;
    let mut requested_hz: Option<u32> = None;
    log::info!("present: render thread started");
    loop {
        // 1. Window changes.
        if ctl.gen.load(Ordering::Acquire) != my_gen {
            let mut c = ctl.m.lock().unwrap();
            if c.quit {
                c.acked = c.gen;
                ctl.cv.notify_all();
                break;
            }
            my_gen = c.gen;
            let w = c.window.clone();
            if let Some(g) = gles.as_mut() {
                unsafe { g.detach() };
            }
            window = w;
            cpu_geometry = None;
            // New surface: re-upload the whole layer texture.
            comp.reset();
            if let Some(r) = gles.as_mut().and_then(|g| g.r.as_mut()) {
                r.ltex_size = (0, 0);
            }
            requested_hz = None;
            if let Some(w) = &window {
                if gles.is_none() && !gl_failed {
                    match unsafe { Gles::new() } {
                        Ok(g) => gles = Some(g),
                        Err(e) => {
                            log::error!("present: EGL init failed ({e}); using the CPU path");
                            gl_failed = true;
                        }
                    }
                }
                if let Some(g) = gles.as_mut() {
                    match unsafe { g.attach(w) } {
                        Ok(sz) => {
                            win_size = sz;
                            log::info!("present: GLES surface {}x{} (window {}x{})", sz.0, sz.1, w.width(), w.height());
                        }
                        Err(e) => {
                            log::error!("present: surface failed ({e}); using the CPU path");
                            gles = None;
                            gl_failed = true;
                        }
                    }
                }
                if gles.is_none() {
                    let _ = w.set_buffers_geometry(0, 0, None);
                    win_size = (w.width().max(1) as u32, w.height().max(1) as u32);
                }
            }
            c.acked = my_gen;
            ctl.cv.notify_all();
        }
        let Some(win) = window.clone() else {
            let g = shared.frame.lock().unwrap();
            let _ = shared.frame_cv.wait_timeout(g, Duration::from_millis(200)).unwrap();
            continue;
        };
        // 2. Wait for something new.
        if !comp.wait_news(&shared, Duration::from_millis(250)) {
            // Keep the display rate current while nothing new arrives (paused game, menus).
            let el = fps_t0.elapsed();
            if el >= Duration::from_secs(1) {
                shared.host_fps.store((fps_n as f32 / el.as_secs_f32()).to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
                fps_n = 0;
                fps_t0 = Instant::now();
            }
            continue;
        }
        let display = *shared.display.lock().unwrap();
        let want_hz = if display.refresh_hz == 0 { 120 } else { display.refresh_hz };
        if requested_hz != Some(want_hz) {
            request_frame_rate(&win, want_hz as f32);
            requested_hz = Some(want_hz);
        }
        let picked = comp.pick(&shared);

        if let Some(g) = gles.as_mut() {
            // GPU path.
            let sz = unsafe { g.size() };
            win_size = sz;
            unsafe { comp.draw_gl(&shared, g.r.as_mut().unwrap(), sz, &picked) };
            if !unsafe { g.swap() } {
                // Surface lost: wait for the activity to give us a window again.
                unsafe { g.detach() };
                window = None;
                continue;
            }
        } else {
            // CPU fallback: letterbox into the window buffer, the compositor scales (Fit only).
            let fb = comp.local.as_ref().unwrap();
            let lb = Letterbox::new(fb.width, fb.height, win_size.0, win_size.1);
            if cpu_geometry != Some((lb.buf_w, lb.buf_h)) {
                if let Err(e) = win.set_buffers_geometry(lb.buf_w as i32, lb.buf_h as i32, Some(HardwareBufferFormat::R5G6B5_UNORM)) {
                    log::error!("set_buffers_geometry: {e}");
                }
                cpu_geometry = Some((lb.buf_w, lb.buf_h));
            }
            match win.lock(None) {
                Ok(mut guard) => {
                    let (bw, bh, stride) = (guard.width(), guard.height(), guard.stride());
                    let mut l = lb;
                    l.off_x = (bw as u32).saturating_sub(lb.game_w) / 2;
                    l.off_y = (bh as u32).saturating_sub(lb.game_h) / 2;
                    let dst = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(guard.bits() as *mut u16, stride * bh) };
                    blit_letterboxed(&l, &fb.pixels, dst, stride, bh);
                    // Window layer, sampled down to the buffer the compositor scales to the window.
                    if picked.layer_on && (picked.scene.list.width, picked.scene.list.height) == win_size {
                        comp.raster.update(&picked.scene.list);
                        comp.raster.blend_onto_rgb565_scaled(dst, stride, bw as u32, bh as u32);
                    }
                }
                Err(e) => log::error!("ANativeWindow_lock: {e}"),
            }
            *shared.letterbox.lock().unwrap() = Some(lb);
            shared.set_viewport(if picked.game_frame { Some(Viewport::new(DisplayMode::Fit, fb.width, fb.height, win_size.0, win_size.1)) } else { None });
        }
        // 3. Display rate.
        fps_n += 1;
        let el = fps_t0.elapsed();
        if el >= Duration::from_secs(1) {
            let f = fps_n as f32 / el.as_secs_f32();
            shared.host_fps.store(f.to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
            fps_n = 0;
            fps_t0 = Instant::now();
        }
    }
    drop(gles);
    log::info!("present: render thread stopped");
}
```

`port/crates/s3-android/src/uithread.rs`:

```rs
//! Run small JNI jobs on the Java main (UI) thread without any Java code of our own.
//!
//! android-activity runs `android_main` on its own thread, but View calls (system bar visibility, IME) must run
//! on the UI thread. We register one end of a socket pair on the Java main looper (`ALooper_addFd` with a
//! callback); writing a byte to the other end makes the looper call us on the UI thread, where the queued jobs
//! run with a JNI env and the activity object.

use std::io::{Read, Write};
use std::os::fd::{AsRawFd, BorrowedFd};
use std::os::unix::net::UnixStream;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

use android_activity::AndroidApp;
use jni::objects::{JObject, JValue};
use jni::{jni_sig, jni_str, Env, JavaVM};
use ndk::looper::FdEvent;

type Job = Box<dyn for<'a> FnOnce(&mut Env<'a>, &JObject<'a>) -> jni::errors::Result<()> + Send>;

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct UiThread {
    tx: Arc<Mutex<UnixStream>>,
    jobs: Arc<Mutex<Vec<(&'static str, Job)>>>,
}

impl UiThread {
    pub fn new(app: &AndroidApp) -> Option<UiThread> {
        let (tx, mut rx) = UnixStream::pair().ok()?;
        rx.set_nonblocking(true).ok()?;
        tx.set_nonblocking(true).ok()?;
        let jobs: Arc<Mutex<Vec<(&'static str, Job)>>> = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
        let vm = unsafe { JavaVM::from_raw(app.vm_as_ptr() as *mut _) };
        let activity = app.activity_as_ptr() as usize;
        let j2 = jobs.clone();
        let fd = rx.as_raw_fd();
        let res = app.java_main_looper().add_fd_with_callback(
            unsafe { BorrowedFd::borrow_raw(fd) },
            FdEvent::INPUT,
            move |_fd, _ev| {
                let mut buf = [0u8; 64];
                while matches!(rx.read(&mut buf), Ok(n) if n > 0) {}
                let list = std::mem::take(&mut *j2.lock().unwrap());
                for (name, job) in list {
                    let r = vm.attach_current_thread(|env: &mut Env| -> jni::errors::Result<()> {
                        let act = unsafe { JObject::from_raw(env, activity as jni::sys::jobject) };
                        let r = job(env, &act);
                        if env.exception_check() {
                            env.exception_clear();
                        }
                        r
                    });
                    match r {
                        Ok(()) => log::debug!("ui thread: {name} ok"),
                        Err(e) => log::warn!("ui thread: {name} failed: {e:?}"),
                    }
                }
                true
            },
        );
        if let Err(e) = res {
            log::warn!("ui thread: ALooper_addFd failed: {e:?}");
            return None;
        }
        Some(UiThread { tx: Arc::new(Mutex::new(tx)), jobs })
    }

    pub fn run(&self, name: &'static str, job: Job) {
        self.jobs.lock().unwrap().push((name, job));
        let _ = self.tx.lock().unwrap().write(&[1]);
    }

    /// `Activity.finish()` (the game exited).
    pub fn finish(&self) {
        self.run("finish", Box::new(|env, act| {
            env.call_method(act, jni_str!("finish"), jni_sig!("()V"), &[])?;
            Ok(())
        }));
    }

    /// Hide status and navigation bars (sticky immersive: a swipe shows them briefly).
    pub fn immersive(&self) {
        self.run("immersive", Box::new(|env, act| {
            let win = env.call_method(act, jni_str!("getWindow"), jni_sig!("()Landroid/view/Window;"), &[])?.l()?;
            // API 30+: WindowInsetsController.
            let r = (|| -> jni::errors::Result<()> {
                let ctrl = env
                    .call_method(&win, jni_str!("getInsetsController"), jni_sig!("()Landroid/view/WindowInsetsController;"), &[])?
                    .l()?;
                let bars = env
                    .call_static_method(jni_str!("android/view/WindowInsets$Type"), jni_str!("systemBars"), jni_sig!("()I"), &[])?
                    .i()?;
                // BEHAVIOR_SHOW_TRANSIENT_BARS_BY_SWIPE = 2
                env.call_method(&ctrl, jni_str!("setSystemBarsBehavior"), jni_sig!("(I)V"), &[JValue::Int(2)])?;
                env.call_method(&ctrl, jni_str!("hide"), jni_sig!("(I)V"), &[JValue::Int(bars)])?;
                Ok(())
            })();
            if r.is_ok() {
                return Ok(());
            }
            env.exception_clear();
            // API 26-29: IMMERSIVE_STICKY | FULLSCREEN | HIDE_NAVIGATION | LAYOUT_* flags.
            let decor = env.call_method(&win, jni_str!("getDecorView"), jni_sig!("()Landroid/view/View;"), &[])?.l()?;
            env.call_method(&decor, jni_str!("setSystemUiVisibility"), jni_sig!("(I)V"), &[JValue::Int(0x1706)])?;
            Ok(())
        }));
    }

    /// Update `state` with the real IME visibility (the user can close the keyboard with Back or its own button).
    pub fn refresh_keyboard(&self, state: Arc<Mutex<bool>>) {
        self.run("keyboard state", Box::new(move |env, act| {
            let win = env.call_method(act, jni_str!("getWindow"), jni_sig!("()Landroid/view/Window;"), &[])?.l()?;
            let decor = env.call_method(&win, jni_str!("getDecorView"), jni_sig!("()Landroid/view/View;"), &[])?.l()?;
            if let Some(v) = ime_visible(env, &decor) {
                *state.lock().unwrap() = v;
            }
            Ok(())
        }));
    }

    /// Show (`Some(true)`), hide (`Some(false)`) or toggle (`None`) the soft keyboard. Uses the focused view (the
    /// NativeActivity content view), like `ANativeActivity_showSoftInput`.
    pub fn soft_keyboard(&self, want: Option<bool>, state: Arc<Mutex<bool>>) {
        self.run("soft keyboard", Box::new(move |env, act| {
            let win = env.call_method(act, jni_str!("getWindow"), jni_sig!("()Landroid/view/Window;"), &[])?.l()?;
            let decor = env.call_method(&win, jni_str!("getDecorView"), jni_sig!("()Landroid/view/View;"), &[])?.l()?;
            let focus = env.call_method(act, jni_str!("getCurrentFocus"), jni_sig!("()Landroid/view/View;"), &[])?.l()?;
            let view = if focus.is_null() { decor } else { focus };
            let name = env.new_string("input_method")?;
            let imm = env
                .call_method(act, jni_str!("getSystemService"), jni_sig!("(Ljava/lang/String;)Ljava/lang/Object;"), &[JValue::Object(&name)])?
                .l()?;
            // Current visibility (API 30+); fall back to our own flag.
            let mut visible = *state.lock().unwrap();
            if let Some(v) = ime_visible(env, &view) {
                visible = v;
            }
            let show = want.unwrap_or(!visible);
            if show {
                env.call_method(&view, jni_str!("requestFocus"), jni_sig!("()Z"), &[])?;
                let ok = env
                    .call_method(&imm, jni_str!("showSoftInput"), jni_sig!("(Landroid/view/View;I)Z"), &[JValue::Object(&view), JValue::Int(0)])?
                    .z()?;
                log::info!("soft keyboard: show -> {ok} (was visible: {visible})");
            } else {
                let token = env.call_method(&view, jni_str!("getWindowToken"), jni_sig!("()Landroid/os/IBinder;"), &[])?.l()?;
                let ok = env
                    .call_method(
                        &imm,
                        jni_str!("hideSoftInputFromWindow"),
                        jni_sig!("(Landroid/os/IBinder;I)Z"),
                        &[JValue::Object(&token), JValue::Int(0)],
                    )?
                    .z()?;
                log::info!("soft keyboard: hide -> {ok}");
            }
            *state.lock().unwrap() = show;
            Ok(())
        }));
    }
}

impl UiThread {
    /// Use the whole screen and the fastest display mode (docs/porting/display.md):
    /// `layoutInDisplayCutoutMode = ALWAYS` (API 30, SHORT_EDGES on 28-29) so the game also covers the camera
    /// cutout strip, and `preferredDisplayModeId` / `preferredRefreshRate` = the mode with the current resolution
    /// and the refresh rate closest to `hz` (0 = highest). Stores the chosen rate in `shared.refresh_hz`.
    pub fn display_prefs(&self, hz: u32, shared: std::sync::Arc<crate::frontend::Shared>) {
        self.run("display prefs", Box::new(move |env, act| {
            let sdk = env.get_static_field(jni_str!("android/os/Build$VERSION"), jni_str!("SDK_INT"), jni_sig!("I"))?.i()?;
            let win = env.call_method(act, jni_str!("getWindow"), jni_sig!("()Landroid/view/Window;"), &[])?.l()?;
            let lp = env.call_method(&win, jni_str!("getAttributes"), jni_sig!("()Landroid/view/WindowManager$LayoutParams;"), &[])?.l()?;
            if sdk >= 28 {
                let mode = if sdk >= 30 { 3 } else { 1 };
                env.set_field(&lp, jni_str!("layoutInDisplayCutoutMode"), jni_sig!("I"), JValue::Int(mode))?;
            }
            let wm = env.call_method(act, jni_str!("getWindowManager"), jni_sig!("()Landroid/view/WindowManager;"), &[])?.l()?;
            let disp = env.call_method(&wm, jni_str!("getDefaultDisplay"), jni_sig!("()Landroid/view/Display;"), &[])?.l()?;
            let cur = env.call_method(&disp, jni_str!("getMode"), jni_sig!("()Landroid/view/Display$Mode;"), &[])?.l()?;
            let cw = env.call_method(&cur, jni_str!("getPhysicalWidth"), jni_sig!("()I"), &[])?.i()?;
            let ch = env.call_method(&cur, jni_str!("getPhysicalHeight"), jni_sig!("()I"), &[])?.i()?;
            let modes = env.call_method(&disp, jni_str!("getSupportedModes"), jni_sig!("()[Landroid/view/Display$Mode;"), &[])?.l()?;
            let n = env
                .call_static_method(jni_str!("java/lang/reflect/Array"), jni_str!("getLength"), jni_sig!("(Ljava/lang/Object;)I"), &[JValue::Object(&modes)])?
                .i()?;
            let mut best: Option<(i32, f32)> = None;
            let mut all = Vec::new();
            for i in 0..n {
                let md = env
                    .call_static_method(
                        jni_str!("java/lang/reflect/Array"),
                        jni_str!("get"),
                        jni_sig!("(Ljava/lang/Object;I)Ljava/lang/Object;"),
                        &[JValue::Object(&modes), JValue::Int(i)],
                    )?
                    .l()?;
                let w = env.call_method(&md, jni_str!("getPhysicalWidth"), jni_sig!("()I"), &[])?.i()?;
                let h = env.call_method(&md, jni_str!("getPhysicalHeight"), jni_sig!("()I"), &[])?.i()?;
                let id = env.call_method(&md, jni_str!("getModeId"), jni_sig!("()I"), &[])?.i()?;
                let r = env.call_method(&md, jni_str!("getRefreshRate"), jni_sig!("()F"), &[])?.f()?;
                all.push(format!("{id}:{w}x{h}@{r:.0}"));
                if (w, h) != (cw, ch) {
                    continue;
                }
                let better = match best {
                    None => true,
                    Some((_, br)) if hz == 0 => r > br,
                    Some((_, br)) => (r - hz as f32).abs() < (br - hz as f32).abs(),
                };
                if better {
                    best = Some((id, r));
                }
            }
            log::info!("display: modes [{}], current {cw}x{ch}, want {hz} Hz -> {best:?}", all.join(" "));
            if let Some((id, r)) = best {
                env.set_field(&lp, jni_str!("preferredDisplayModeId"), jni_sig!("I"), JValue::Int(id))?;
                env.set_field(&lp, jni_str!("preferredRefreshRate"), jni_sig!("F"), JValue::Float(r))?;
                shared.refresh_hz.store(r.to_bits(), std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
            }
            env.call_method(&win, jni_str!("setAttributes"), jni_sig!("(Landroid/view/WindowManager$LayoutParams;)V"), &[JValue::Object(&lp)])?;
            Ok(())
        }));
    }
}

/// `view.getRootWindowInsets().isVisible(WindowInsets.Type.ime())` (API 30+); `None` if unavailable.
fn ime_visible<'a>(env: &mut Env<'a>, view: &JObject<'a>) -> Option<bool> {
    let q = (|| -> jni::errors::Result<bool> {
        let ins = env.call_method(view, jni_str!("getRootWindowInsets"), jni_sig!("()Landroid/view/WindowInsets;"), &[])?.l()?;
        if ins.is_null() {
            return Err(jni::errors::Error::NullPtr("insets"));
        }
        let ime = env.call_static_method(jni_str!("android/view/WindowInsets$Type"), jni_str!("ime"), jni_sig!("()I"), &[])?.i()?;
        env.call_method(&ins, jni_str!("isVisible"), jni_sig!("(I)Z"), &[JValue::Int(ime)])?.z()
    })();
    match q {
        Ok(v) => Some(v),
        Err(_) => {
            env.exception_clear();
            None
        }
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-android/src/wifilock.rs`:

```rs
//! Wi-Fi multicast lock for LAN game discovery (docs/porting/multiplayer.md section 8).
//!
//! Many Wi-Fi drivers drop broadcast/multicast frames to save power unless an app holds a
//! `WifiManager.MulticastLock` (permission `CHANGE_WIFI_MULTICAST_STATE`). [`install`] registers a hook with
//! `s3_net::lan` that acquires the lock the first time the LAN discovery starts (the game's LAN menu) and keeps it
//! for the rest of the process.

use std::sync::OnceLock;

use android_activity::AndroidApp;
use jni::objects::{JObject, JValue};
use jni::{jni_sig, jni_str, Env, JavaVM};

static APP: OnceLock<AndroidApp> = OnceLock::new();

pub fn install(app: &AndroidApp) {
    let _ = APP.set(app.clone());
    s3_net::lan::set_start_hook(acquire);
}

fn acquire() {
    let Some(app) = APP.get() else { return };
    let vm = unsafe { JavaVM::from_raw(app.vm_as_ptr() as *mut _) };
    let activity = app.activity_as_ptr() as usize;
    let r = vm.attach_current_thread(|env: &mut Env| -> jni::errors::Result<()> {
        let act = unsafe { JObject::from_raw(env, activity as jni::sys::jobject) };
        let r = (|| -> jni::errors::Result<()> {
            let name = env.new_string("wifi")?;
            let wm = env
                .call_method(&act, jni_str!("getSystemService"), jni_sig!("(Ljava/lang/String;)Ljava/lang/Object;"), &[JValue::Object(&name)])?
                .l()?;
            if wm.is_null() {
                return Ok(());
            }
            let tag = env.new_string("s3port-lan")?;
            let lock = env
                .call_method(
                    &wm,
                    jni_str!("createMulticastLock"),
                    jni_sig!("(Ljava/lang/String;)Landroid/net/wifi/WifiManager$MulticastLock;"),
                    &[JValue::Object(&tag)],
                )?
                .l()?;
            env.call_method(&lock, jni_str!("setReferenceCounted"), jni_sig!("(Z)V"), &[JValue::Bool(false)])?;
            env.call_method(&lock, jni_str!("acquire"), jni_sig!("()V"), &[])?;
            // MulticastLock releases itself when garbage-collected: keep a global reference forever.
            let g = env.new_global_ref(&lock)?;
            std::mem::forget(g);
            Ok(())
        })();
        if env.exception_check() {
            env.exception_describe();
            env.exception_clear();
        }
        r
    });
    match r {
        Ok(()) => log::info!("lan: Wi-Fi multicast lock acquired"),
        Err(e) => log::warn!("lan: Wi-Fi multicast lock failed: {e:?}"),
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-cpu/src/diff_tests.rs`:

```rs
//! Differential tests: every integer ALU / shift / multiply / divide / bit instruction is executed natively on
//! the x86_64 host (inline asm; these instructions behave the same in 64-bit mode for 8/16/32-bit operands)
//! and in the interpreter, over edge-case and pseudo-random operands and incoming flag states. Results and
//! EFLAGS must match, except for flags Intel documents as *undefined* for that instruction.
//! Both the specialised fast handlers and the generic path are checked.
//! Only compiled on x86_64 hosts.

#![allow(clippy::type_complexity)]

use core::arch::asm;

use iced_x86::code_asm::*;

use crate::*;

const CODE: u32 = 0x0040_1000;
const STACK_TOP: u32 = 0x0090_0000;
#[allow(dead_code)]
const DATA: u32 = 0x0060_0000;

const CF: u32 = fl::CF;
const PF: u32 = fl::PF;
const AF: u32 = fl::AF;
const ZF: u32 = fl::ZF;
const SF: u32 = fl::SF;
const OF: u32 = fl::OF;
const ALL: u32 = fl::STATUS;

/// Interpreter harness: one assembled snippet (`op` + `ret`), run many times with different inputs.
struct Harness {
    cpu: Cpu,
    mem: GuestMemory,
}

impl Harness {
    fn new(generic: bool, build: &dyn Fn(&mut CodeAssembler)) -> Self {
        let mut a = CodeAssembler::new(32).unwrap();
        build(&mut a);
        a.ret().unwrap();
        let bytes = a.assemble(CODE as u64).unwrap();
        let mut mem = GuestMemory::new().unwrap();
        mem.write_bytes(CODE, &bytes);
        let mut cpu = Cpu::new();
        cpu.set_generic_only(generic);
        Harness { cpu, mem }
    }

    /// Run with EAX, ECX, EDX, EBX and incoming flags. Returns (exit, regs, eflags).
    fn run(&mut self, v_eax: u32, v_ecx: u32, v_edx: u32, v_ebx: u32, fin: u32) -> (CpuExit, [u32; 8], u32) {
        let c = &mut self.cpu;
        c.regs = [v_eax, v_ecx, v_edx, v_ebx, STACK_TOP, 0x1111, 0x2222, 0x3333];
        c.push32(&mut self.mem, layout::MAGIC_RETURN);
        c.eip = CODE;
        c.set_eflags(fin | 0x202);
        let e = c.run(&mut self.mem, 100);
        (e, c.regs, c.eflags())
    }
}

fn values() -> Vec<u32> {
    let mut v = vec![
        0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 9, 15, 16, 17, 31, 32, 33, 0x7F, 0x80, 0x81, 0xFE, 0xFF, 0x100, 0x7FFF, 0x8000, 0x8001,
        0xFFFE, 0xFFFF, 0x1_0000, 0x7FFF_FFFF, 0x8000_0000, 0x8000_0001, 0xFFFF_FFFE, 0xFFFF_FFFF, 0x1234_5678,
        0xDEAD_BEEF, 0x0000_FF80, 0x00FF_FF7F,
    ];
    let mut x: u32 = 0x9E37_79B9;
    for _ in 0..30 {
        x ^= x << 13;
        x ^= x >> 17;
        x ^= x << 5;
        v.push(x);
    }
    v
}

/// Incoming flag states (CF matters for adc/sbb/rcl/rcr and must survive inc/dec).
const FLAG_INS: [u32; 3] = [0, CF, ALL];

fn sz_mask(size: u32) -> u32 {
    match size {
        1 => 0xFF,
        2 => 0xFFFF,
        _ => 0xFFFF_FFFF,
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Native helpers. `fin` = incoming flags (loaded with popfq), returns (rax/eax, flags) etc.

macro_rules! nat_rr {
    ($tmpl:literal) => {{
        fn f(a: u32, b: u32, fin: u32) -> (u32, u32) {
            let mut a = a as u64;
            let fo: u64;
            unsafe {
                asm!("push {fi}", "popfq", $tmpl, "pushfq", "pop {fo}",
                    a = inout(reg) a, b = in(reg) b as u64, fi = in(reg) fin as u64, fo = lateout(reg) fo);
            }
            (a as u32, fo as u32)
        }
        f as fn(u32, u32, u32) -> (u32, u32)
    }};
}

macro_rules! nat_r {
    ($tmpl:literal) => {{
        fn f(a: u32, _b: u32, fin: u32) -> (u32, u32) {
            let mut a = a as u64;
            let fo: u64;
            unsafe {
                asm!("push {fi}", "popfq", $tmpl, "pushfq", "pop {fo}",
                    a = inout(reg) a, fi = in(reg) fin as u64, fo = lateout(reg) fo);
            }
            (a as u32, fo as u32)
        }
        f as fn(u32, u32, u32) -> (u32, u32)
    }};
}

/// `op a, cl` (b = count).
macro_rules! nat_cl {
    ($tmpl:literal) => {{
        fn f(a: u32, b: u32, fin: u32) -> (u32, u32) {
            let mut a = a as u64;
            let fo: u64;
            unsafe {
                asm!("push {fi}", "popfq", $tmpl, "pushfq", "pop {fo}",
                    a = inout(reg) a, in("ecx") b, fi = in(reg) fin as u64, fo = lateout(reg) fo);
            }
            (a as u32, fo as u32)
        }
        f as fn(u32, u32, u32) -> (u32, u32)
    }};
}

/// `shld/shrd a, b, cl` (c = count).
macro_rules! nat_rrcl {
    ($tmpl:literal) => {{
        fn f(a: u32, b: u32, c: u32, fin: u32) -> (u32, u32) {
            let mut a = a as u64;
            let fo: u64;
            unsafe {
                asm!("push {fi}", "popfq", $tmpl, "pushfq", "pop {fo}",
                    a = inout(reg) a, b = in(reg) b as u64, in("ecx") c, fi = in(reg) fin as u64,
                    fo = lateout(reg) fo);
            }
            (a as u32, fo as u32)
        }
        f as fn(u32, u32, u32, u32) -> (u32, u32)
    }};
}

/// One-operand mul/imul/div/idiv with EAX/EDX implicit; operand in EBX-like register `b`.
macro_rules! nat_md {
    ($tmpl:literal) => {{
        fn f(v_eax: u32, v_edx: u32, b: u32, fin: u32) -> (u32, u32, u32) {
            let mut va = v_eax as u64;
            let mut vd = v_edx as u64;
            let fo: u64;
            unsafe {
                asm!("push {fi}", "popfq", $tmpl, "pushfq", "pop {fo}",
                    inout("rax") va, inout("rdx") vd, b = in(reg) b as u64, fi = in(reg) fin as u64,
                    fo = lateout(reg) fo);
            }
            (va as u32, vd as u32, fo as u32)
        }
        f as fn(u32, u32, u32, u32) -> (u32, u32, u32)
    }};
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Checkers

type Nat2 = fn(u32, u32, u32) -> (u32, u32);

/// Binary op `op eax-ish, ebx-ish` (or unary / `op eax, cl` when `cl` is set, then b goes to ECX).
fn check_bin(
    name: &str,
    size: u32,
    build: &dyn Fn(&mut CodeAssembler),
    native: Nat2,
    by_cl: bool,
    undef: &dyn Fn(u32, u32) -> u32,
) {
    let vals = values();
    let counts: Vec<u32> = (0..=40).chain([63, 64, 255, 0x101]).collect();
    let bs: &[u32] = if by_cl { &counts } else { &vals };
    for generic in [false, true] {
        let mut h = Harness::new(generic, build);
        for &a in &vals {
            for &b in bs {
                for &fin in &FLAG_INS {
                    let (na, nf) = native(a, b, fin);
                    let (exit, regs, f) =
                        if by_cl { h.run(a, b, 0, 0, fin) } else { h.run(a, 0, 0, b, fin) };
                    assert_eq!(exit, CpuExit::ReturnMagic, "{name}/{size} a={a:#x} b={b:#x}");
                    let u = undef(a, b);
                    let res_undef = u & 0x8000_0000 != 0;
                    let fm = ALL & !u;
                    let ctx = format!(
                        "{name} size={size} generic={generic} a={a:#x} b={b:#x} fin={fin:#x}: \
                         interp eax={:#x} fl={:#x}, native eax={na:#x} fl={nf:#x} (compared flags {fm:#x})",
                        regs[EAX], f
                    );
                    if !res_undef {
                        assert_eq!(regs[EAX], na, "result: {ctx}");
                    }
                    assert_eq!(f & fm, nf & fm, "flags: {ctx}");
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Bit for "result undefined" in the undef mask.
const RES: u32 = 0x8000_0000;

macro_rules! bin3 {
    ($name:literal, $m:ident, $t8:literal, $t16:literal, $t32:literal, $undef:expr) => {{
        check_bin($name, 1, &|a| { a.$m(al, bl).unwrap(); }, nat_rr!($t8), false, &$undef);
        check_bin($name, 2, &|a| { a.$m(ax, bx).unwrap(); }, nat_rr!($t16), false, &$undef);
        check_bin($name, 4, &|a| { a.$m(eax, ebx).unwrap(); }, nat_rr!($t32), false, &$undef);
    }};
}

#[test]
fn diff_alu_rr() {
    let none = |_: u32, _: u32| 0;
    let logic = |_: u32, _: u32| AF;
    bin3!("add", add, "add {a:l}, {b:l}", "add {a:x}, {b:x}", "add {a:e}, {b:e}", none);
    bin3!("adc", adc, "adc {a:l}, {b:l}", "adc {a:x}, {b:x}", "adc {a:e}, {b:e}", none);
    bin3!("sub", sub, "sub {a:l}, {b:l}", "sub {a:x}, {b:x}", "sub {a:e}, {b:e}", none);
    bin3!("sbb", sbb, "sbb {a:l}, {b:l}", "sbb {a:x}, {b:x}", "sbb {a:e}, {b:e}", none);
    bin3!("cmp", cmp, "cmp {a:l}, {b:l}", "cmp {a:x}, {b:x}", "cmp {a:e}, {b:e}", none);
    bin3!("and", and, "and {a:l}, {b:l}", "and {a:x}, {b:x}", "and {a:e}, {b:e}", logic);
    bin3!("or", or, "or {a:l}, {b:l}", "or {a:x}, {b:x}", "or {a:e}, {b:e}", logic);
    bin3!("xor", xor, "xor {a:l}, {b:l}", "xor {a:x}, {b:x}", "xor {a:e}, {b:e}", logic);
    bin3!("test", test, "test {a:l}, {b:l}", "test {a:x}, {b:x}", "test {a:e}, {b:e}", logic);
}

/// Undefined flags of shifts by `count` for operand `size`.
fn shift_undef(size: u32, kind: &'static str) -> impl Fn(u32, u32) -> u32 {
    move |_a, count| {
        let c = count & 31;
        if c == 0 {
            return 0;
        }
        let bits = size * 8;
        let mut u = 0;
        match kind {
            "shift" => {
                u |= AF;
                if c != 1 {
                    u |= OF;
                }
            }
            "shlr" => {
                u |= AF;
                if c != 1 {
                    u |= OF;
                }
                if c >= bits {
                    u |= CF;
                }
            }
            _ => {
                // rotates
                if c != 1 {
                    u |= OF;
                }
            }
        }
        u
    }
}

#[test]
fn diff_shifts() {
    macro_rules! sh3 {
        ($name:literal, $m:ident, $kind:literal, $t8:literal, $t16:literal, $t32:literal) => {{
            check_bin($name, 1, &|a| { a.$m(al, cl).unwrap(); }, nat_cl!($t8), true, &shift_undef(1, $kind));
            check_bin($name, 2, &|a| { a.$m(ax, cl).unwrap(); }, nat_cl!($t16), true, &shift_undef(2, $kind));
            check_bin($name, 4, &|a| { a.$m(eax, cl).unwrap(); }, nat_cl!($t32), true, &shift_undef(4, $kind));
        }};
    }
    sh3!("shl", shl, "shlr", "shl {a:l}, cl", "shl {a:x}, cl", "shl {a:e}, cl");
    sh3!("shr", shr, "shlr", "shr {a:l}, cl", "shr {a:x}, cl", "shr {a:e}, cl");
    sh3!("sar", sar, "shift", "sar {a:l}, cl", "sar {a:x}, cl", "sar {a:e}, cl");
    sh3!("rol", rol, "rot", "rol {a:l}, cl", "rol {a:x}, cl", "rol {a:e}, cl");
    sh3!("ror", ror, "rot", "ror {a:l}, cl", "ror {a:x}, cl", "ror {a:e}, cl");
    sh3!("rcl", rcl, "rot", "rcl {a:l}, cl", "rcl {a:x}, cl", "rcl {a:e}, cl");
    sh3!("rcr", rcr, "rot", "rcr {a:l}, cl", "rcr {a:x}, cl", "rcr {a:e}, cl");
}

#[test]
fn diff_shifts_by_immediate() {
    // `shl eax, 1` (D1 /4) and `shl eax, imm8` (C1 /4) encodings.
    for n in [1u32, 3, 31] {
        for (name, kind) in [("shl", "shlr"), ("shr", "shlr"), ("sar", "shift"), ("rol", "rot"), ("ror", "rot")] {
            let build = move |a: &mut CodeAssembler| {
                match name {
                    "shl" => a.shl(eax, n).unwrap(),
                    "shr" => a.shr(eax, n).unwrap(),
                    "sar" => a.sar(eax, n).unwrap(),
                    "rol" => a.rol(eax, n).unwrap(),
                    _ => a.ror(eax, n).unwrap(),
                }
            };
            let native: Nat2 = match name {
                "shl" => nat_cl!("shl {a:e}, cl"),
                "shr" => nat_cl!("shr {a:e}, cl"),
                "sar" => nat_cl!("sar {a:e}, cl"),
                "rol" => nat_cl!("rol {a:e}, cl"),
                _ => nat_cl!("ror {a:e}, cl"),
            };
            let u = shift_undef(4, kind);
            for generic in [false, true] {
                let mut h = Harness::new(generic, &build);
                for &a in &values() {
                    for &fin in &FLAG_INS {
                        let (na, nf) = native(a, n, fin);
                        let (_, regs, f) = h.run(a, 0, 0, 0, fin);
                        let fm = ALL & !u(a, n);
                        assert_eq!(regs[EAX], na, "{name} {n} a={a:#x}");
                        assert_eq!(f & fm, nf & fm, "{name} {n} a={a:#x} fin={fin:#x}");
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn diff_shld_shrd() {
    type Nat3 = fn(u32, u32, u32, u32) -> (u32, u32);
    let cases: [(&str, u32, &dyn Fn(&mut CodeAssembler), Nat3); 4] = [
        ("shld32", 4, &|a| a.shld(eax, ebx, cl).unwrap(), nat_rrcl!("shld {a:e}, {b:e}, cl")),
        ("shrd32", 4, &|a| a.shrd(eax, ebx, cl).unwrap(), nat_rrcl!("shrd {a:e}, {b:e}, cl")),
        ("shld16", 2, &|a| a.shld(ax, bx, cl).unwrap(), nat_rrcl!("shld {a:x}, {b:x}, cl")),
        ("shrd16", 2, &|a| a.shrd(ax, bx, cl).unwrap(), nat_rrcl!("shrd {a:x}, {b:x}, cl")),
    ];
    let vals = values();
    for (name, size, build, native) in cases {
        for generic in [false, true] {
            let mut h = Harness::new(generic, build);
            for &a in vals.iter().step_by(3) {
                for &b in vals.iter().step_by(2) {
                    for c in 0..=33u32 {
                        let mc = c & 31;
                        if mc > size * 8 {
                            continue; // result undefined
                        }
                        let fin = CF;
                        let (na, nf) = native(a, b, c, fin);
                        let (_, regs, f) = h.run(a, c, 0, b, fin);
                        let mut u = 0;
                        if mc != 0 {
                            u |= AF;
                            if mc != 1 {
                                u |= OF;
                            }
                            if mc == size * 8 {
                                u |= CF | OF; // count == size (16-bit): CF/OF undefined in practice
                            }
                        }
                        let fm = ALL & !u;
                        assert_eq!(regs[EAX], na, "{name} a={a:#x} b={b:#x} c={c}");
                        assert_eq!(f & fm, nf & fm, "{name} flags a={a:#x} b={b:#x} c={c}");
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn diff_imul2_bsf_bsr_bt() {
    let mul_undef = |_: u32, _: u32| SF | ZF | AF | PF;
    check_bin("imul16", 2, &|a| { a.imul_2(ax, bx).unwrap(); }, nat_rr!("imul {a:x}, {b:x}"), false, &mul_undef);
    check_bin("imul32", 4, &|a| { a.imul_2(eax, ebx).unwrap(); }, nat_rr!("imul {a:e}, {b:e}"), false, &mul_undef);
    let bs_undef = |_: u32, b: u32| (ALL & !ZF) | if b == 0 { RES } else { 0 };
    let bs16_undef = |_: u32, b: u32| (ALL & !ZF) | if b & 0xFFFF == 0 { RES } else { 0 };
    check_bin("bsf32", 4, &|a| { a.bsf(eax, ebx).unwrap(); }, nat_rr!("bsf {a:e}, {b:e}"), false, &bs_undef);
    check_bin("bsr32", 4, &|a| { a.bsr(eax, ebx).unwrap(); }, nat_rr!("bsr {a:e}, {b:e}"), false, &bs_undef);
    check_bin("bsf16", 2, &|a| { a.bsf(ax, bx).unwrap(); }, nat_rr!("bsf {a:x}, {b:x}"), false, &bs16_undef);
    check_bin("bsr16", 2, &|a| { a.bsr(ax, bx).unwrap(); }, nat_rr!("bsr {a:x}, {b:x}"), false, &bs16_undef);
    let bt_undef = |_: u32, _: u32| OF | SF | AF | PF | ZF;
    check_bin("bt32", 4, &|a| { a.bt(eax, ebx).unwrap(); }, nat_rr!("bt {a:e}, {b:e}"), false, &bt_undef);
    check_bin("bts32", 4, &|a| { a.bts(eax, ebx).unwrap(); }, nat_rr!("bts {a:e}, {b:e}"), false, &bt_undef);
    check_bin("btr32", 4, &|a| { a.btr(eax, ebx).unwrap(); }, nat_rr!("btr {a:e}, {b:e}"), false, &bt_undef);
    check_bin("btc32", 4, &|a| { a.btc(eax, ebx).unwrap(); }, nat_rr!("btc {a:e}, {b:e}"), false, &bt_undef);
    check_bin("bt16", 2, &|a| { a.bt(ax, bx).unwrap(); }, nat_rr!("bt {a:x}, {b:x}"), false, &bt_undef);
    check_bin("bts16", 2, &|a| { a.bts(ax, bx).unwrap(); }, nat_rr!("bts {a:x}, {b:x}"), false, &bt_undef);
}

#[test]
fn diff_mul_div() {
    type NatMD = fn(u32, u32, u32, u32) -> (u32, u32, u32);
    let vals = values();
    let cases: [(&str, u32, &dyn Fn(&mut CodeAssembler), NatMD); 12] = [
        ("mul8", 1, &|a| a.mul(bl).unwrap(), nat_md!("mul {b:l}")),
        ("mul16", 2, &|a| a.mul(bx).unwrap(), nat_md!("mul {b:x}")),
        ("mul32", 4, &|a| a.mul(ebx).unwrap(), nat_md!("mul {b:e}")),
        ("imul8", 1, &|a| a.imul(bl).unwrap(), nat_md!("imul {b:l}")),
        ("imul16", 2, &|a| a.imul(bx).unwrap(), nat_md!("imul {b:x}")),
        ("imul32", 4, &|a| a.imul(ebx).unwrap(), nat_md!("imul {b:e}")),
        ("div8", 1, &|a| a.div(bl).unwrap(), nat_md!("div {b:l}")),
        ("div16", 2, &|a| a.div(bx).unwrap(), nat_md!("div {b:x}")),
        ("div32", 4, &|a| a.div(ebx).unwrap(), nat_md!("div {b:e}")),
        ("idiv8", 1, &|a| a.idiv(bl).unwrap(), nat_md!("idiv {b:l}")),
        ("idiv16", 2, &|a| a.idiv(bx).unwrap(), nat_md!("idiv {b:x}")),
        ("idiv32", 4, &|a| a.idiv(ebx).unwrap(), nat_md!("idiv {b:e}")),
    ];
    for (name, size, build, native) in cases {
        let is_div = name.contains("div");
        let signed = name.starts_with('i');
        for generic in [false, true] {
            let mut h = Harness::new(generic, build);
            for &a in &vals {
                for &d in vals.iter().step_by(4) {
                    for &b in &vals {
                        // Would the native division fault? Then the interpreter must raise #DE.
                        if is_div {
                            let m = sz_mask(size);
                            let bad = if b & m == 0 {
                                true
                            } else if !signed {
                                let n: u64 = match size {
                                    1 => (a & 0xFFFF) as u64,
                                    2 => (((d & 0xFFFF) << 16) | (a & 0xFFFF)) as u64,
                                    _ => ((d as u64) << 32) | a as u64,
                                };
                                n / (b & m) as u64 > m as u64
                            } else {
                                let n: i64 = match size {
                                    1 => a as u16 as i16 as i64,
                                    2 => ((((d & 0xFFFF) << 16) | (a & 0xFFFF)) as i32) as i64,
                                    _ => (((d as u64) << 32) | a as u64) as i64,
                                };
                                let dv: i64 = match size {
                                    1 => b as u8 as i8 as i64,
                                    2 => b as u16 as i16 as i64,
                                    _ => b as i32 as i64,
                                };
                                let q = n.checked_div(dv);
                                let (lo, hi) = match size {
                                    1 => (-128i64, 127i64),
                                    2 => (-32768, 32767),
                                    _ => (i32::MIN as i64, i32::MAX as i64),
                                };
                                !matches!(q, Some(q) if q >= lo && q <= hi)
                            };
                            if bad {
                                let (exit, _, _) = h.run(a, 0, d, b, 0);
                                assert!(
                                    matches!(exit, CpuExit::Fault { kind: FaultKind::DivideError, .. }),
                                    "{name} a={a:#x} d={d:#x} b={b:#x}: {exit:?}"
                                );
                                continue;
                            }
                        }
                        let (na, nd, nf) = native(a, d, b, 0);
                        let (exit, regs, f) = h.run(a, 0, d, b, 0);
                        assert_eq!(exit, CpuExit::ReturnMagic);
                        let ctx = format!("{name} generic={generic} a={a:#x} d={d:#x} b={b:#x}");
                        assert_eq!(regs[EAX], na, "eax {ctx}");
                        assert_eq!(regs[EDX], nd, "edx {ctx}");
                        if !is_div {
                            let fm = CF | OF;
                            assert_eq!(f & fm, nf & fm, "flags {ctx}");
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

```

`port/crates/s3-cpu/src/exec.rs`:

```rs
//! Integer instruction semantics. One `match` on the mnemonic; anything not handled here goes to `fpu::exec`.
//!
//! Conventions for adding instructions:
//! - `self.eip` already points to the next instruction when `step` runs; branches overwrite it.
//! - Use `read_op`/`write_op` with the operand size from `op_size` (bytes) unless the instruction has its own.
//! - Return `Err(self.fault(..))` for CPU exceptions; `run` rewinds EIP to the faulting instruction.

use std::sync::OnceLock;
use std::time::Instant;

use iced_x86::{Code, Instruction, Mnemonic, OpKind, Register};

use crate::flags::{mask, sext, sign_bit};
use crate::{fl, fpu, layout, Cpu, CpuExit, FaultKind, GuestMemory, EAX, EBP, EBX, ECX, EDI, EDX, ESI, ESP};

/// Result of executing one instruction.
pub type R = Result<(), CpuExit>;

const R_AL: u32 = Register::AL as u32;
const R_BL: u32 = Register::BL as u32;
const R_AH: u32 = Register::AH as u32;
const R_BH: u32 = Register::BH as u32;
const R_AX: u32 = Register::AX as u32;
const R_DI: u32 = Register::DI as u32;
const R_EAX: u32 = Register::EAX as u32;
const R_EDI: u32 = Register::EDI as u32;

/// EFLAGS bits writable by popf/popfd in user mode: CF PF AF ZF SF DF OF, AC (bit 18, 486 probe) and ID
/// (bit 21, CPUID probe). TF/IOPL/NT/RF/VM are not modelled; IF stays set.
const POPF_MASK: u32 = fl::STATUS | fl::DF | (1 << 18) | fl::ID;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum StrOp {
    Movs,
    Stos,
    Lods,
    Scas,
    Cmps,
}

impl Cpu {
    /// Read a register by iced name (8/16/32-bit GPRs; segment registers return fixed flat selectors).
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn get_reg(&self, r: Register) -> u32 {
        let n = r as u32;
        if (R_EAX..=R_EDI).contains(&n) {
            return self.regs[(n - R_EAX) as usize];
        }
        if (R_AL..=R_BL).contains(&n) {
            return self.regs[(n - R_AL) as usize] & 0xFF;
        }
        if (R_AH..=R_BH).contains(&n) {
            return (self.regs[(n - R_AH) as usize] >> 8) & 0xFF;
        }
        if (R_AX..=R_DI).contains(&n) {
            return self.regs[(n - R_AX) as usize] & 0xFFFF;
        }
        match r {
            Register::CS => 0x1B,
            Register::DS | Register::ES | Register::SS => 0x23,
            Register::FS => 0x3B,
            _ => 0,
        }
    }

    /// Write a register by iced name (partial registers merge). Writes to segment registers are ignored.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn set_reg(&mut self, r: Register, v: u32) {
        let n = r as u32;
        if (R_EAX..=R_EDI).contains(&n) {
            self.regs[(n - R_EAX) as usize] = v;
        } else if (R_AL..=R_BL).contains(&n) {
            let x = &mut self.regs[(n - R_AL) as usize];
            *x = (*x & !0xFF) | (v & 0xFF);
        } else if (R_AH..=R_BH).contains(&n) {
            let x = &mut self.regs[(n - R_AH) as usize];
            *x = (*x & !0xFF00) | ((v & 0xFF) << 8);
        } else if (R_AX..=R_DI).contains(&n) {
            let x = &mut self.regs[(n - R_AX) as usize];
            *x = (*x & !0xFFFF) | (v & 0xFFFF);
        }
    }

    /// Build a fault exit for the current instruction.
    pub fn fault(&self, kind: FaultKind, detail: impl Into<String>) -> CpuExit {
        CpuExit::Fault { eip: self.cur_ip, kind, detail: detail.into() }
    }

    /// Access-violation exit (out of line: keeps the callers' fast paths small).
    #[cold]
    #[inline(never)]
    pub(crate) fn av_exit(&self, addr: u32, write: bool) -> CpuExit {
        let what = if write { "write" } else { "read" };
        self.fault(FaultKind::AccessViolation { addr, write }, format!("{what} {addr:#x}"))
    }

    fn unimplemented(&self, ins: &Instruction) -> CpuExit {
        self.fault(FaultKind::Unimplemented, format!("{:?}: {}", ins.mnemonic(), ins))
    }

    /// Segment base for a memory operand (only FS/GS are non-zero).
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn seg_base(&self, seg: Register) -> u32 {
        match seg {
            Register::FS => self.fs_base,
            Register::GS => self.gs_base,
            _ => 0,
        }
    }

    /// Effective address of the memory operand without segment base (LEA).
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn ea_noseg(&self, ins: &Instruction) -> u32 {
        let mut a = ins.memory_displacement32();
        let b = ins.memory_base();
        if b != Register::None {
            a = a.wrapping_add(self.get_reg(b));
        }
        let i = ins.memory_index();
        if i != Register::None {
            a = a.wrapping_add(self.get_reg(i).wrapping_mul(ins.memory_index_scale()));
        }
        // 16-bit addressing (0x67 prefix, e.g. `[bx+si]`) wraps at 64 KiB.
        if b.is_gpr16() || i.is_gpr16() {
            a &= 0xFFFF;
        }
        a
    }

    /// Linear address of the memory operand.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn ea(&self, ins: &Instruction) -> u32 {
        self.ea_noseg(ins).wrapping_add(self.seg_base(ins.memory_segment()))
    }

    /// Guest load of `size` bytes (1/2/4) with the NULL-guard check.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn rd(&self, mem: &GuestMemory, addr: u32, size: u32) -> Result<u32, CpuExit> {
        if addr < layout::NULL_GUARD_END {
            return Err(self.av_exit(addr, false));
        }
        Ok(match size {
            1 => mem.read_u8(addr) as u32,
            2 => mem.read_u16(addr) as u32,
            _ => mem.read_u32(addr),
        })
    }

    /// Guest store of `size` bytes (1/2/4) with the NULL-guard check.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn wr(&self, mem: &mut GuestMemory, addr: u32, size: u32, v: u32) -> R {
        if addr < layout::NULL_GUARD_END {
            return Err(self.av_exit(addr, true));
        }
        match size {
            1 => mem.write_u8(addr, v as u8),
            2 => mem.write_u16(addr, v as u16),
            _ => mem.write_u32(addr, v),
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Check an address for the NULL guard (for multi-byte helpers that access memory directly).
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn check_addr(&self, addr: u32, write: bool) -> R {
        if addr < layout::NULL_GUARD_END {
            return Err(self.fault(FaultKind::AccessViolation { addr, write }, format!("access {addr:#x}")));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Operand size in bytes of operand 0 (register size or memory size), 4 otherwise.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn op_size(ins: &Instruction) -> u32 {
        Self::op_size_n(ins, 0)
    }

    /// Operand size in bytes of operand `i`.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn op_size_n(ins: &Instruction, i: u32) -> u32 {
        match ins.op_kind(i) {
            OpKind::Register => ins.op_register(i).size() as u32,
            OpKind::Memory => ins.memory_size().size() as u32,
            OpKind::Immediate8 => 1,
            OpKind::Immediate16 | OpKind::Immediate8to16 => 2,
            _ => 4,
        }
    }

    /// Read operand `i` (register, memory, immediate, near branch).
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn read_op(&self, mem: &GuestMemory, ins: &Instruction, i: u32, size: u32) -> Result<u32, CpuExit> {
        match ins.op_kind(i) {
            OpKind::Register => Ok(self.get_reg(ins.op_register(i))),
            OpKind::Memory => self.rd(mem, self.ea(ins), size),
            OpKind::NearBranch32 | OpKind::NearBranch16 => Ok(ins.near_branch_target() as u32),
            OpKind::Immediate8
            | OpKind::Immediate16
            | OpKind::Immediate32
            | OpKind::Immediate8to16
            | OpKind::Immediate8to32
            | OpKind::Immediate8_2nd => Ok(ins.immediate(i) as u32 & mask(size)),
            _ => Err(self.unimplemented(ins)),
        }
    }

    /// Write operand `i` (register or memory).
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn write_op(&mut self, mem: &mut GuestMemory, ins: &Instruction, i: u32, size: u32, v: u32) -> R {
        match ins.op_kind(i) {
            OpKind::Register => {
                self.set_reg(ins.op_register(i), v);
                Ok(())
            }
            OpKind::Memory => {
                let a = self.ea(ins);
                self.wr(mem, a, size, v)
            }
            _ => Err(self.unimplemented(ins)),
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn push(&mut self, mem: &mut GuestMemory, size: u32, v: u32) -> R {
        let sp = self.regs[ESP].wrapping_sub(size);
        self.wr(mem, sp, size, v)?;
        self.regs[ESP] = sp;
        Ok(())
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn pop(&mut self, mem: &GuestMemory, size: u32) -> Result<u32, CpuExit> {
        let v = self.rd(mem, self.regs[ESP], size)?;
        self.regs[ESP] = self.regs[ESP].wrapping_add(size);
        Ok(v)
    }

    fn acc(&self, size: u32) -> u32 {
        self.regs[EAX] & mask(size)
    }

    fn set_acc(&mut self, size: u32, v: u32) {
        match size {
            1 => self.set_reg(Register::AL, v),
            2 => self.set_reg(Register::AX, v),
            _ => self.regs[EAX] = v,
        }
    }

    /// Shift/rotate. Returns None when the masked count is zero (no change at all).
    pub(crate) fn shift(&mut self, m: Mnemonic, a: u32, count: u32, size: u32) -> Option<u32> {
        let bits = size * 8;
        let msk = mask(size);
        let sb = sign_bit(size);
        let a = a & msk;
        let c = count & 0x1F;
        if c == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let cf_in = self.flag(fl::CF) as u32;
        let r;
        match m {
            Mnemonic::Shl | Mnemonic::Sal => {
                r = if c >= 32 { 0 } else { ((a as u64) << c) as u32 & msk };
                let cf = if c <= bits { (a as u64 >> (bits - c)) & 1 != 0 } else { false };
                self.set_szp(r, size);
                self.set_flag(fl::CF, cf);
                self.set_flag(fl::OF, ((r & sb) != 0) != cf);
            }
            Mnemonic::Shr => {
                r = if c >= bits { 0 } else { a >> c };
                let cf = if c <= bits { (a as u64 >> (c - 1)) & 1 != 0 } else { false };
                self.set_szp(r, size);
                self.set_flag(fl::CF, cf);
                self.set_flag(fl::OF, a & sb != 0);
            }
            Mnemonic::Sar => {
                let s = sext(a, size);
                let cc = c.min(31);
                r = (s >> cc) as u32 & msk;
                let cf = (s >> (c.min(bits) - 1).min(31)) & 1 != 0;
                self.set_szp(r, size);
                self.set_flag(fl::CF, cf);
                self.set_flag(fl::OF, false);
            }
            Mnemonic::Rol => {
                let k = c % bits;
                r = if k == 0 { a } else { ((a << k) | (a >> (bits - k))) & msk };
                let cf = r & 1 != 0;
                self.set_flag(fl::CF, cf);
                self.set_flag(fl::OF, ((r & sb) != 0) != cf);
            }
            Mnemonic::Ror => {
                let k = c % bits;
                r = if k == 0 { a } else { ((a >> k) | (a << (bits - k))) & msk };
                let msb = r & sb != 0;
                self.set_flag(fl::CF, msb);
                self.set_flag(fl::OF, msb != ((r & (sb >> 1)) != 0));
            }
            Mnemonic::Rcl => {
                let k = c % (bits + 1);
                let (mut v, mut cf) = (a, cf_in);
                for _ in 0..k {
                    let msb = (v >> (bits - 1)) & 1;
                    v = ((v << 1) | cf) & msk;
                    cf = msb;
                }
                r = v;
                self.set_flag(fl::CF, cf != 0);
                self.set_flag(fl::OF, ((r & sb) != 0) != (cf != 0));
            }
            Mnemonic::Rcr => {
                let k = c % (bits + 1);
                let (mut v, mut cf) = (a, cf_in);
                for _ in 0..k {
                    let lsb = v & 1;
                    v = (v >> 1) | (cf << (bits - 1));
                    cf = lsb;
                }
                r = v & msk;
                self.set_flag(fl::CF, cf != 0);
                self.set_flag(fl::OF, ((r & sb) != 0) != ((r & (sb >> 1)) != 0));
            }
            _ => unreachable!(),
        }
        Some(r)
    }

    fn string_op(&mut self, mem: &mut GuestMemory, ins: &Instruction, op: StrOp, size: u32) -> R {
        // 16-bit address size (SI/DI/CX) never occurs in S3.EXE; refuse loudly instead of running it wrong.
        if (0..ins.op_count()).any(|i| matches!(ins.op_kind(i), OpKind::MemorySegSI | OpKind::MemorySegDI | OpKind::MemoryESDI)) {
            return Err(self.unimplemented(ins));
        }
        let step = if self.flag(fl::DF) { (size as i32).wrapping_neg() as u32 } else { size };
        let rep = ins.has_rep_prefix() || ins.has_repne_prefix();
        let repne = ins.has_repne_prefix();
        let sbase = match op {
            StrOp::Movs | StrOp::Lods | StrOp::Cmps => self.seg_base(ins.memory_segment()),
            _ => 0,
        };
        let mut n = if rep { self.regs[ECX] } else { 1 };
        if n == 0 {
            return Ok(());
        }
        // Fast paths (forward, no overlap hazards).
        if rep && !self.flag(fl::DF) && n > 4 {
            let bytes = n as u64 * size as u64;
            let src = self.regs[ESI].wrapping_add(sbase);
            let dst = self.regs[EDI];
            if bytes < 0x4000_0000 && dst as u64 + bytes <= 1 << 32 && src as u64 + bytes <= 1 << 32 {
                match op {
                    StrOp::Movs if (dst as u64 >= src as u64 + bytes) || (src as u64 >= dst as u64 + bytes) || dst <= src => {
                        // dst <= src overlapping forward copy behaves like memmove for element-wise copies.
                        self.check_addr(src, false)?;
                        self.check_addr(dst, true)?;
                        mem.copy_within(src, dst, bytes as usize);
                        self.regs[ESI] = self.regs[ESI].wrapping_add(bytes as u32);
                        self.regs[EDI] = self.regs[EDI].wrapping_add(bytes as u32);
                        self.regs[ECX] = 0;
                        return Ok(());
                    }
                    StrOp::Stos => {
                        self.check_addr(dst, true)?;
                        let v = self.acc(size);
                        match size {
                            1 => mem.fill(dst, bytes as usize, v as u8),
                            _ => {
                                let mut a = dst;
                                for _ in 0..n {
                                    if size == 2 {
                                        mem.write_u16(a, v as u16)
                                    } else {
                                        mem.write_u32(a, v)
                                    }
                                    a = a.wrapping_add(size);
                                }
                            }
                        }
                        self.regs[EDI] = self.regs[EDI].wrapping_add(bytes as u32);
                        self.regs[ECX] = 0;
                        return Ok(());
                    }
                    _ => {}
                }
            }
        }
        while n > 0 {
            match op {
                StrOp::Movs => {
                    let v = self.rd(mem, self.regs[ESI].wrapping_add(sbase), size)?;
                    self.wr(mem, self.regs[EDI], size, v)?;
                    self.regs[ESI] = self.regs[ESI].wrapping_add(step);
                    self.regs[EDI] = self.regs[EDI].wrapping_add(step);
                }
                StrOp::Stos => {
                    self.wr(mem, self.regs[EDI], size, self.acc(size))?;
                    self.regs[EDI] = self.regs[EDI].wrapping_add(step);
                }
                StrOp::Lods => {
                    let v = self.rd(mem, self.regs[ESI].wrapping_add(sbase), size)?;
                    self.set_acc(size, v);
                    self.regs[ESI] = self.regs[ESI].wrapping_add(step);
                }
                StrOp::Scas => {
                    let v = self.rd(mem, self.regs[EDI], size)?;
                    self.alu_sub(self.acc(size), v, 0, size);
                    self.regs[EDI] = self.regs[EDI].wrapping_add(step);
                }
                StrOp::Cmps => {
                    let a = self.rd(mem, self.regs[ESI].wrapping_add(sbase), size)?;
                    let b = self.rd(mem, self.regs[EDI], size)?;
                    self.alu_sub(a, b, 0, size);
                    self.regs[ESI] = self.regs[ESI].wrapping_add(step);
                    self.regs[EDI] = self.regs[EDI].wrapping_add(step);
                }
            }
            n -= 1;
            if rep {
                self.regs[ECX] = n;
                if matches!(op, StrOp::Scas | StrOp::Cmps) {
                    let zf = self.flag(fl::ZF);
                    if (repne && zf) || (!repne && !zf) {
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn rdtsc_value() -> u64 {
        static START: OnceLock<Instant> = OnceLock::new();
        let ns = START.get_or_init(Instant::now).elapsed().as_nanos() as u64;
        ns / 5 // pretend 200 MHz
    }
}

/// Execute one decoded instruction.
#[inline(always)]
pub(crate) fn step(cpu: &mut Cpu, mem: &mut GuestMemory, ins: &Instruction) -> R {
    use Mnemonic as M;
    let m = ins.mnemonic();
    match m {
        M::Mov => {
            let s = Cpu::op_size(ins);
            let v = cpu.read_op(mem, ins, 1, s)?;
            cpu.write_op(mem, ins, 0, s, v)
        }
        M::Movzx | M::Movsx => {
            let ds = Cpu::op_size(ins);
            let ss = Cpu::op_size_n(ins, 1);
            let v = cpu.read_op(mem, ins, 1, ss)?;
            let v = if m == M::Movsx { sext(v, ss) as u32 & mask(ds) } else { v };
            cpu.write_op(mem, ins, 0, ds, v)
        }
        M::Lea => {
            let s = Cpu::op_size(ins);
            let a = cpu.ea_noseg(ins);
            cpu.write_op(mem, ins, 0, s, a & mask(s))
        }
        M::Xchg => {
            let s = Cpu::op_size(ins);
            let a = cpu.read_op(mem, ins, 0, s)?;
            let b = cpu.read_op(mem, ins, 1, s)?;
            cpu.write_op(mem, ins, 0, s, b)?;
            cpu.write_op(mem, ins, 1, s, a)
        }
        M::Push => {
            let s = (-ins.stack_pointer_increment()) as u32;
            let v = cpu.read_op(mem, ins, 0, s)?;
            cpu.push(mem, s, v)
        }
        M::Pop => {
            let s = ins.stack_pointer_increment() as u32;
            let v = cpu.pop(mem, s)?;
            cpu.write_op(mem, ins, 0, s, v)
        }
        M::Pushad => {
            let sp = cpu.regs[ESP];
            for r in [EAX, ECX, EDX, EBX] {
                cpu.push(mem, 4, cpu.regs[r])?;
            }
            cpu.push(mem, 4, sp)?;
            for r in [EBP, ESI, EDI] {
                cpu.push(mem, 4, cpu.regs[r])?;
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        M::Popad => {
            for r in [EDI, ESI, EBP] {
                cpu.regs[r] = cpu.pop(mem, 4)?;
            }
            cpu.pop(mem, 4)?;
            for r in [EBX, EDX, ECX, EAX] {
                cpu.regs[r] = cpu.pop(mem, 4)?;
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        M::Pushfd => cpu.push(mem, 4, (cpu.eflags() & 0x00FC_FFFF) | 2),
        M::Pushf => cpu.push(mem, 2, cpu.eflags() & 0xFFFF),
        M::Popfd => {
            let v = cpu.pop(mem, 4)?;
            cpu.set_eflags((v & POPF_MASK) | fl::IF | 2);
            Ok(())
        }
        M::Popf => {
            let v = cpu.pop(mem, 2)?;
            cpu.set_eflags((cpu.eflags() & 0xFFFF_0000) | (v & POPF_MASK & 0xFFFF) | fl::IF | 2);
            Ok(())
        }
        M::Call => {
            let target = match ins.op0_kind() {
                OpKind::NearBranch32 | OpKind::NearBranch16 => ins.near_branch_target() as u32,
                OpKind::Register | OpKind::Memory => cpu.read_op(mem, ins, 0, 4)?,
                _ => return Err(cpu.fault(FaultKind::GeneralProtection, format!("far call: {ins}"))),
            };
            cpu.push(mem, 4, cpu.eip)?;
            cpu.eip = target;
            Ok(())
        }
        M::Ret => {
            let ret = cpu.pop(mem, 4)?;
            if ins.op_count() == 1 {
                cpu.regs[ESP] = cpu.regs[ESP].wrapping_add(ins.immediate16() as u32);
            }
            cpu.eip = ret;
            Ok(())
        }
        M::Jmp => {
            cpu.eip = match ins.op0_kind() {
                OpKind::NearBranch32 | OpKind::NearBranch16 => ins.near_branch_target() as u32,
                OpKind::Register | OpKind::Memory => cpu.read_op(mem, ins, 0, 4)?,
                _ => return Err(cpu.fault(FaultKind::GeneralProtection, format!("far jmp: {ins}"))),
            };
            Ok(())
        }
        M::Jo | M::Jno | M::Jb | M::Jae | M::Je | M::Jne | M::Jbe | M::Ja | M::Js | M::Jns | M::Jp | M::Jnp
        | M::Jl | M::Jge | M::Jle | M::Jg => {
            if cpu.cond(ins.condition_code()) {
                cpu.eip = ins.near_branch_target() as u32;
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        M::Loop | M::Loope | M::Loopne => {
            // Address-size prefix 0x67 selects CX as the counter.
            let cx = matches!(
                ins.code(),
                Code::Loop_rel8_16_CX | Code::Loop_rel8_32_CX | Code::Loope_rel8_16_CX | Code::Loope_rel8_32_CX
                    | Code::Loopne_rel8_16_CX | Code::Loopne_rel8_32_CX
            );
            let c = if cx {
                let c = cpu.regs[ECX].wrapping_sub(1) & 0xFFFF;
                cpu.set_reg(Register::CX, c);
                c
            } else {
                let c = cpu.regs[ECX].wrapping_sub(1);
                cpu.regs[ECX] = c;
                c
            };
            let zf = cpu.flag(fl::ZF);
            let take = c != 0
                && match m {
                    M::Loope => zf,
                    M::Loopne => !zf,
                    _ => true,
                };
            if take {
                cpu.eip = ins.near_branch_target() as u32;
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        M::Jecxz => {
            if cpu.regs[ECX] == 0 {
                cpu.eip = ins.near_branch_target() as u32;
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        // `67 E3 rel8`: tests CX only (used by the game's blitters, see static-isa.md).
        M::Jcxz => {
            if cpu.regs[ECX] & 0xFFFF == 0 {
                cpu.eip = ins.near_branch_target() as u32;
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        M::Add | M::Adc | M::Sub | M::Sbb | M::Cmp | M::And | M::Or | M::Xor | M::Test => {
            let s = Cpu::op_size(ins);
            let a = cpu.read_op(mem, ins, 0, s)?;
            let b = cpu.read_op(mem, ins, 1, s)?;
            let cf = cpu.flag(fl::CF) as u32;
            let r = match m {
                M::Add => cpu.alu_add(a, b, 0, s),
                M::Adc => cpu.alu_add(a, b, cf, s),
                M::Sub | M::Cmp => cpu.alu_sub(a, b, 0, s),
                M::Sbb => cpu.alu_sub(a, b, cf, s),
                M::And | M::Test => cpu.alu_logic(a & b, s),
                M::Or => cpu.alu_logic(a | b, s),
                _ => cpu.alu_logic(a ^ b, s),
            };
            if m != M::Cmp && m != M::Test {
                cpu.write_op(mem, ins, 0, s, r)?;
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        M::Inc | M::Dec => {
            let s = Cpu::op_size(ins);
            let a = cpu.read_op(mem, ins, 0, s)?;
            let r = if m == M::Inc { cpu.alu_inc(a, s) } else { cpu.alu_dec(a, s) };
            cpu.write_op(mem, ins, 0, s, r)
        }
        M::Neg => {
            let s = Cpu::op_size(ins);
            let a = cpu.read_op(mem, ins, 0, s)?;
            let r = cpu.alu_sub(0, a, 0, s);
            cpu.write_op(mem, ins, 0, s, r)
        }
        M::Not => {
            let s = Cpu::op_size(ins);
            let a = cpu.read_op(mem, ins, 0, s)?;
            cpu.write_op(mem, ins, 0, s, !a & mask(s))
        }
        M::Shl | M::Sal | M::Shr | M::Sar | M::Rol | M::Ror | M::Rcl | M::Rcr => {
            let s = Cpu::op_size(ins);
            let a = cpu.read_op(mem, ins, 0, s)?;
            let c = cpu.read_op(mem, ins, 1, 1)?;
            if let Some(r) = cpu.shift(m, a, c, s) {
                cpu.write_op(mem, ins, 0, s, r)?;
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        M::Shld | M::Shrd => {
            let s = Cpu::op_size(ins);
            let d = cpu.read_op(mem, ins, 0, s)?;
            let src = cpu.read_op(mem, ins, 1, s)?;
            let c = cpu.read_op(mem, ins, 2, 1)? & 0x1F;
            if c == 0 {
                return Ok(());
            }
            let bits = s * 8;
            let (r, cf) = if s == 4 {
                if m == M::Shld {
                    let w = ((d as u64) << 32) | src as u64;
                    (((w << c) >> 32) as u32, (d >> (32 - c)) & 1 != 0)
                } else {
                    let w = ((src as u64) << 32) | d as u64;
                    ((w >> c) as u32, (d >> (c - 1)) & 1 != 0)
                }
            } else {
                // 16-bit: concatenate to 32 bits (count > 16 is undefined on real hardware).
                if m == M::Shld {
                    let w = (d << 16) | src;
                    (((w as u64) << c >> 16) as u32 & 0xFFFF, ((w as u64) << c >> 32) & 1 != 0)
                } else {
                    let w = ((src as u64) << 16) | d as u64;
                    ((w >> c) as u32 & 0xFFFF, (w >> (c - 1)) & 1 != 0)
                }
            };
            cpu.set_szp(r, s);
            cpu.set_flag(fl::CF, cf);
            cpu.set_flag(fl::OF, ((r ^ d) & sign_bit(s)) != 0);
            let _ = bits;
            cpu.write_op(mem, ins, 0, s, r)
        }
        M::Mul | M::Imul if ins.op_count() == 1 => {
            let s = Cpu::op_size(ins);
            let b = cpu.read_op(mem, ins, 0, s)?;
            let a = cpu.acc(s);
            let (lo, hi, of) = if m == M::Mul {
                let r = a as u64 * b as u64;
                match s {
                    1 => ((r & 0xFFFF) as u32, 0, r > 0xFF),
                    2 => ((r & 0xFFFF) as u32, (r >> 16) as u32, r > 0xFFFF),
                    _ => (r as u32, (r >> 32) as u32, r > 0xFFFF_FFFF),
                }
            } else {
                let r = sext(a, s) as i64 * sext(b, s) as i64;
                let fits = match s {
                    1 => r == r as i8 as i64,
                    2 => r == r as i16 as i64,
                    _ => r == r as i32 as i64,
                };
                match s {
                    1 => ((r as u32) & 0xFFFF, 0, !fits),
                    2 => ((r as u32) & 0xFFFF, ((r >> 16) as u32) & 0xFFFF, !fits),
                    _ => (r as u32, (r >> 32) as u32, !fits),
                }
            };
            match s {
                1 => cpu.set_reg(Register::AX, lo),
                2 => {
                    cpu.set_reg(Register::AX, lo);
                    cpu.set_reg(Register::DX, hi);
                }
                _ => {
                    cpu.regs[EAX] = lo;
                    cpu.regs[EDX] = hi;
                }
            }
            cpu.set_szp(lo, s);
            cpu.set_flag(fl::CF, of);
            cpu.set_flag(fl::OF, of);
            Ok(())
        }
        M::Imul => {
            let s = Cpu::op_size(ins);
            let (a, b) = if ins.op_count() == 2 {
                (cpu.read_op(mem, ins, 0, s)?, cpu.read_op(mem, ins, 1, s)?)
            } else {
```
