`port/crates/s3-cpu/src/fpu.rs`:

```rs
//! x87 FPU (and the small MMX subset the game can use) state and instruction semantics.
//!
//! See `docs/porting/x87-fpu.md` for the design and precision limits. Summary:
//! - Registers are `f64` (80-bit precision is not modelled; `m80` loads/stores convert exactly / round to nearest).
//!   `st(i)` = `regs[(top + i) & 7]`.
//! - Control word: rounding control is honoured by `fist`/`fistp`/`fisttp`/`frndint`/`fbstp`
//!   (MSVC6 `_ftol` sets RC=truncate via `fldcw` before `fistp`); precision control PC=24 bits rounds
//!   arithmetic results to a 24-bit significand, PC=53/64 both give f64 precision. Arithmetic itself always
//!   rounds to nearest. Exception masks are stored but unmasked exceptions are not delivered (only the
//!   status-word flags and ES are set).
//! - Status word: C0/C1/C2/C3 from `fcom*`/`fucom*`/`ftst`/`fxam`/`fprem*`/trig, IE/ZE/SF flags, TOP.
//! - Tag word: only "empty / not empty" is tracked; the full 2-bit tags are computed for `fnstenv`/`fnsave`.
//! - MMX (`movd`/`movq`/`emms`) uses a separate `mmx` array (aliasing with the x87 registers is not modelled).

use iced_x86::{Instruction, MemorySize, Mnemonic, OpKind, Register};

#[path = "fpu_conv.rs"]
pub mod conv;
#[path = "fpu_math.rs"]
pub mod math;
#[cfg(test)]
#[path = "fpu_tests.rs"]
mod tests;
#[cfg(test)]
#[path = "fpu_golden.rs"]
mod golden;

use conv::INDEFINITE;

/// 2^63 (range limit for `fistp m64` and the trig instructions).
const TWO63: f64 = (1u64 << 63) as f64;

use crate::exec::R;
use crate::{fl, Cpu, CpuExit, GuestMemory};

/// Status-word bits.
pub mod sw {
    pub const IE: u16 = 1 << 0;
    pub const DE: u16 = 1 << 1;
    pub const ZE: u16 = 1 << 2;
    pub const OE: u16 = 1 << 3;
    pub const UE: u16 = 1 << 4;
    pub const PE: u16 = 1 << 5;
    pub const SF: u16 = 1 << 6;
    pub const ES: u16 = 1 << 7;
    pub const C0: u16 = 1 << 8;
    pub const C1: u16 = 1 << 9;
    pub const C2: u16 = 1 << 10;
    pub const TOP: u16 = 7 << 11;
    pub const C3: u16 = 1 << 14;
    pub const B: u16 = 1 << 15;
    /// All condition codes.
    pub const CC: u16 = C0 | C1 | C2 | C3;
    /// Exception flags (IE..PE).
    pub const EXC: u16 = 0x3F;
}

/// x87 state.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Fpu {
    /// Physical registers R0..R7.
    pub regs: [f64; 8],
    /// Top-of-stack index (0..7).
    pub top: u8,
    /// Control word (default 0x037F after `fninit`).
    pub control: u16,
    /// Status word without TOP (TOP is merged in from `top` when stored).
    pub status: u16,
    /// Tag word (2 bits per physical register; 3 = empty, anything else = in use).
    pub tags: u16,
    /// MMX registers (aliasing is not modelled exactly).
    pub mmx: [u64; 8],
    /// Last instruction / operand pointers (for fnstenv/fnsave).
    pub last_ip: u32,
    pub last_dp: u32,
}

impl Default for Fpu {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl Fpu {
    /// State after `fninit`.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Fpu { regs: [0.0; 8], top: 0, control: 0x037F, status: 0, tags: 0xFFFF, mmx: [0; 8], last_ip: 0, last_dp: 0 }
    }

    /// `fninit` (MMX registers are left alone).
    pub fn reset(&mut self) {
        let mmx = self.mmx;
        *self = Fpu::new();
        self.mmx = mmx;
    }

    /// Status word including TOP.
    pub fn status_word(&self) -> u16 {
        (self.status & !sw::TOP) | ((self.top as u16 & 7) << 11)
    }

    /// Set the status word (including TOP).
    pub fn set_status_word(&mut self, v: u16) {
        self.status = v & !sw::TOP;
        self.top = ((v >> 11) & 7) as u8;
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn phys(&self, i: u8) -> usize {
        ((self.top + i) & 7) as usize
    }

    /// Is physical register `p` empty?
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn is_empty_phys(&self, p: usize) -> bool {
        (self.tags >> (p * 2)) & 3 == 3
    }

    /// Is `st(i)` empty?
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn is_empty(&self, i: u8) -> bool {
        self.is_empty_phys(self.phys(i))
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn set_tag_phys(&mut self, p: usize, empty: bool) {
        if empty {
            self.tags |= 3 << (p * 2);
        } else {
            self.tags &= !(3 << (p * 2));
        }
    }

    /// `st(i)` without stack checks.
    pub fn st(&self, i: u8) -> f64 {
        self.regs[self.phys(i)]
    }

    /// Set `st(i)` (marks it in use).
    pub fn set_st(&mut self, i: u8, v: f64) {
        let p = self.phys(i);
        self.regs[p] = v;
        self.set_tag_phys(p, false);
    }

    /// Push a value (marks the new top valid). No overflow check (see [`Fpu::push_checked`]).
    pub fn push(&mut self, v: f64) {
        self.top = (self.top + 7) & 7;
        self.regs[self.top as usize] = v;
        self.set_tag_phys(self.top as usize, false);
    }

    /// Pop (marks the old top empty) and return it.
    pub fn pop(&mut self) -> f64 {
        let v = self.regs[self.top as usize];
        self.set_tag_phys(self.top as usize, true);
        self.top = (self.top + 1) & 7;
        v
    }

    /// Record exception flags; sets ES/B if any of them is unmasked.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn raise(&mut self, flags: u16) {
        self.status |= flags;
        if flags & !self.control & sw::EXC != 0 {
            self.status |= sw::ES | sw::B;
        }
    }

    /// `st(i)` with the stack-underflow check (empty => IE|SF, C1=0, returns the indefinite NaN).
    pub fn get(&mut self, i: u8) -> f64 {
        if self.is_empty(i) {
            self.status &= !sw::C1;
            self.raise(sw::IE | sw::SF);
            return INDEFINITE;
        }
        self.st(i)
    }

    /// Push with the stack-overflow check (target in use => IE|SF|C1 and the indefinite NaN is pushed).
    pub fn push_checked(&mut self, v: f64) {
        let p = ((self.top + 7) & 7) as usize;
        if !self.is_empty_phys(p) {
            self.raise(sw::IE | sw::SF);
            self.status |= sw::C1;
            self.push(INDEFINITE);
        } else {
            self.status &= !sw::C1;
            self.push(v);
        }
    }

    /// Full 2-bit tag word as stored by `fnstenv`/`fnsave` (00 valid, 01 zero, 10 special, 11 empty).
    pub fn tag_word(&self) -> u16 {
        let mut t = 0u16;
        for p in 0..8 {
            let tag = if self.is_empty_phys(p) {
                3
            } else {
                let v = self.regs[p];
                if v == 0.0 {
                    1
                } else if !v.is_normal() {
                    2
                } else {
                    0
                }
            };
            t |= tag << (p * 2);
        }
        t
    }

    /// Load a tag word (only empty / non-empty is kept).
    pub fn set_tag_word(&mut self, t: u16) {
        self.tags = 0;
        for p in 0..8 {
            if (t >> (p * 2)) & 3 == 3 {
                self.tags |= 3 << (p * 2);
            }
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn set_cc(&mut self, c3: bool, c2: bool, c1: bool, c0: bool) {
        self.status &= !sw::CC;
        if c3 {
            self.status |= sw::C3;
        }
        if c2 {
            self.status |= sw::C2;
        }
        if c1 {
            self.status |= sw::C1;
        }
        if c0 {
            self.status |= sw::C0;
        }
    }

    /// Rounding control (0 nearest, 1 down, 2 up, 3 truncate).
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn rc(&self) -> u16 {
        (self.control >> 10) & 3
    }

    /// Finish an arithmetic result: NaN from non-NaN inputs => IE + indefinite; precision control.
    /// NaN results never come from the host (its NaN sign/payload/propagation rules differ between x86 and
    /// aarch64): NaN operands go through [`math::propagate_nan`] (IE for SNaN), new NaNs become the indefinite.
    fn finish(&mut self, r: f64, a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
        if a.is_nan() || b.is_nan() {
            if math::is_snan(a) || math::is_snan(b) {
                self.raise(sw::IE);
            }
            return math::propagate_nan(a, b);
        }
        if r.is_nan() {
            self.raise(sw::IE);
            return INDEFINITE;
        }
        if r.is_infinite() && a.is_finite() && b.is_finite() {
            self.raise(sw::OE | sw::PE);
        }
        conv::apply_pc(r, self.control)
    }

    fn arith(&mut self, op: Mnemonic, d: f64, s: f64) -> f64 {
        use Mnemonic as M;
        self.status &= !sw::C1;
        let (a, b) = match op {
            M::Fsubr | M::Fsubrp | M::Fisubr | M::Fdivr | M::Fdivrp | M::Fidivr => (s, d),
            _ => (d, s),
        };
        let r = match op {
            M::Fadd | M::Faddp | M::Fiadd => a + b,
            M::Fsub | M::Fsubp | M::Fisub | M::Fsubr | M::Fsubrp | M::Fisubr => a - b,
            M::Fmul | M::Fmulp | M::Fimul => a * b,
            _ => {
                if b == 0.0 && a.is_finite() && a != 0.0 {
                    self.raise(sw::ZE);
                }
                a / b
            }
        };
        self.finish(r, a, b)
    }

    /// Compare `a` with `b`, set C3/C2/C0 (C1 = 0). `quiet` = fucom semantics (only SNaN raises IE).
    fn compare(&mut self, a: f64, b: f64, quiet: bool) -> std::cmp::Ordering {
        use std::cmp::Ordering;
        match a.partial_cmp(&b) {
            None => {
                let snan = |x: f64| x.is_nan() && (x.to_bits() >> 51) & 1 == 0;
                if !quiet || snan(a) || snan(b) {
                    self.raise(sw::IE);
                }
                self.set_cc(true, true, false, true);
                Ordering::Equal // unused for unordered
            }
            Some(o) => {
                self.set_cc(o == Ordering::Equal, false, false, o == Ordering::Less);
                o
            }
        }
    }

    /// `fxam` classification into C3/C2/C1/C0.
    fn fxam(&mut self) {
        let v = self.st(0);
        let neg = v.is_sign_negative();
        if self.is_empty(0) {
            self.set_cc(true, false, neg, true);
        } else if v.is_nan() {
            self.set_cc(false, false, neg, true);
        } else if v.is_infinite() {
            self.set_cc(false, true, neg, true);
        } else if v == 0.0 {
            self.set_cc(true, false, neg, false);
        } else if v.is_subnormal() {
            // NOTE: f64 subnormals are normal numbers in 80-bit format; report "normal" like real hardware would
            // for the same value loaded from an f64.
            self.set_cc(false, true, neg, false);
        } else {
            self.set_cc(false, true, neg, false);
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Memory helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn ld_u16(cpu: &Cpu, mem: &GuestMemory, a: u32) -> Result<u16, CpuExit> {
    cpu.check_addr(a, false)?;
    Ok(mem.read_u16(a))
}
fn ld_u32(cpu: &Cpu, mem: &GuestMemory, a: u32) -> Result<u32, CpuExit> {
    cpu.check_addr(a, false)?;
    Ok(mem.read_u32(a))
}
fn ld_u64(cpu: &Cpu, mem: &GuestMemory, a: u32) -> Result<u64, CpuExit> {
    cpu.check_addr(a, false)?;
    Ok(mem.read_u64(a))
}
fn st_u16(cpu: &Cpu, mem: &mut GuestMemory, a: u32, v: u16) -> R {
    cpu.check_addr(a, true)?;
    mem.write_u16(a, v);
    Ok(())
}
fn st_u32(cpu: &Cpu, mem: &mut GuestMemory, a: u32, v: u32) -> R {
    cpu.check_addr(a, true)?;
    mem.write_u32(a, v);
    Ok(())
}
fn st_u64(cpu: &Cpu, mem: &mut GuestMemory, a: u32, v: u64) -> R {
    cpu.check_addr(a, true)?;
    mem.write_u64(a, v);
    Ok(())
}
fn ld_f80(cpu: &Cpu, mem: &GuestMemory, a: u32) -> Result<f64, CpuExit> {
    let m = ld_u64(cpu, mem, a)?;
    let se = ld_u16(cpu, mem, a.wrapping_add(8))?;
    Ok(conv::f80_to_f64(m, se))
}
fn st_f80(cpu: &Cpu, mem: &mut GuestMemory, a: u32, v: f64) -> R {
    let (m, se) = conv::f64_to_f80(v);
    st_u64(cpu, mem, a, m)?;
    st_u16(cpu, mem, a.wrapping_add(8), se)
}

/// Load a floating/integer memory operand as f64 according to its iced memory size.
fn load_mem(cpu: &Cpu, mem: &GuestMemory, ins: &Instruction, a: u32) -> Result<Option<f64>, CpuExit> {
    Ok(Some(match ins.memory_size() {
        MemorySize::Float32 => conv::f32_to_f64(f32::from_bits(ld_u32(cpu, mem, a)?)),
        MemorySize::Float64 => f64::from_bits(ld_u64(cpu, mem, a)?),
        MemorySize::Float80 => ld_f80(cpu, mem, a)?,
        MemorySize::Int16 => ld_u16(cpu, mem, a)? as i16 as f64,
        MemorySize::Int32 => ld_u32(cpu, mem, a)? as i32 as f64,
        MemorySize::Int64 => ld_u64(cpu, mem, a)? as i64 as f64,
        MemorySize::Bcd => {
            cpu.check_addr(a, false)?;
            let mut b = [0u8; 10];
            b.copy_from_slice(mem.slice(a, 10));
            conv::bcd_to_f64(&b)
        }
        _ => return Ok(None),
    }))
}

#[inline(always)]
fn st_index(r: Register) -> Option<u8> {
    let n = r as u32;
    let b = Register::ST0 as u32;
    if (b..b + 8).contains(&n) {
        Some((n - b) as u8)
    } else {
        None
    }
}

#[inline(always)]
fn mm_index(r: Register) -> Option<usize> {
    let n = r as u32;
    let b = Register::MM0 as u32;
    if (b..b + 8).contains(&n) {
        Some((n - b) as usize)
    } else {
        None
    }
}

/// Store `v` as an integer of `bytes` bytes with the current rounding mode (indefinite + IE on overflow/NaN).
fn store_int(cpu: &mut Cpu, mem: &mut GuestMemory, a: u32, bytes: u32, v: f64, rc: u16) -> R {
    let r = conv::round_rc(v, rc);
    if r != v && !v.is_nan() {
        cpu.fpu.raise(sw::PE);
    }
    match bytes {
        2 => {
            let x = if r.is_nan() || !(-32768.0..=32767.0).contains(&r) {
                cpu.fpu.raise(sw::IE);
                0x8000u16
            } else {
                r as i16 as u16
            };
            st_u16(cpu, mem, a, x)
        }
        4 => {
            let x = if r.is_nan() || !(-2147483648.0..=2147483647.0).contains(&r) {
                cpu.fpu.raise(sw::IE);
                0x8000_0000u32
            } else {
                r as i32 as u32
            };
            st_u32(cpu, mem, a, x)
        }
        _ => {
            let x = if r.is_nan() || !(-TWO63..TWO63).contains(&r) {
                cpu.fpu.raise(sw::IE);
                0x8000_0000_0000_0000u64
            } else {
                r as i64 as u64
            };
            st_u64(cpu, mem, a, x)
        }
    }
}

/// Source operand of a compare: 0 operands => st(1); otherwise the last operand (memory or st(i)).
fn compare_src(cpu: &mut Cpu, mem: &GuestMemory, ins: &Instruction) -> Result<f64, CpuExit> {
    let n = ins.op_count();
    if n == 0 {
        return Ok(cpu.fpu.get(1));
    }
    let k = n - 1;
    match ins.op_kind(k) {
        OpKind::Memory => {
            let a = cpu.ea(ins);
            cpu.fpu.last_dp = a;
            Ok(load_mem(cpu, mem, ins, a)?.unwrap_or(INDEFINITE))
        }
        _ => {
            let i = st_index(ins.op_register(k)).unwrap_or(1);
            Ok(cpu.fpu.get(i))
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Environment / state save
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Store the FPU environment (14- or 28-byte protected-mode format) at `a`. Returns the env size.
fn store_env(cpu: &Cpu, mem: &mut GuestMemory, a: u32, small: bool) -> Result<u32, CpuExit> {
    let f = &cpu.fpu;
    let fields: [u32; 7] =
        [f.control as u32, f.status_word() as u32, f.tag_word() as u32, f.last_ip, 0x1B, f.last_dp, 0x23];
    if small {
        for (k, v) in fields.iter().enumerate() {
            st_u16(cpu, mem, a + 2 * k as u32, *v as u16)?;
        }
        Ok(14)
    } else {
        for (k, v) in fields.iter().enumerate() {
            // Reserved upper halves of CW/SW/TW read as 0xFFFF on real hardware.
            let hi = if k < 3 || k == 6 { 0xFFFF_0000 } else { 0 };
            st_u32(cpu, mem, a + 4 * k as u32, *v | hi)?;
        }
        Ok(28)
    }
}

fn load_env(cpu: &mut Cpu, mem: &GuestMemory, a: u32, small: bool) -> Result<u32, CpuExit> {
    let mut fields = [0u32; 7];
    for (k, f) in fields.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        *f = if small { ld_u16(cpu, mem, a + 2 * k as u32)? as u32 } else { ld_u32(cpu, mem, a + 4 * k as u32)? };
    }
    let f = &mut cpu.fpu;
    f.control = fields[0] as u16;
    f.set_status_word(fields[1] as u16);
    f.set_tag_word(fields[2] as u16);
    f.last_ip = fields[3];
    f.last_dp = fields[5];
    // Re-evaluate ES/B against the new masks.
    if f.status & !f.control & sw::EXC != 0 {
        f.status |= sw::ES | sw::B;
    } else {
        f.status &= !(sw::ES | sw::B);
    }
    Ok(if small { 14 } else { 28 })
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Dispatch
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Execute an x87/MMX instruction. Returns `None` if the instruction is not an FPU instruction or is not
/// implemented (the caller then raises `FaultKind::Unimplemented`).
pub fn exec(cpu: &mut Cpu, mem: &mut GuestMemory, ins: &Instruction) -> Option<R> {
    use Mnemonic as M;
    let m = ins.mnemonic();
    match m {
        M::Movq | M::Movd | M::Emms => return exec_mmx(cpu, mem, ins),
        _ => {}
    }
    // Control instructions do not update the last-instruction pointers.
    let control = matches!(
        m,
        M::Fninit
            | M::Finit
            | M::Fnclex
            | M::Fclex
            | M::Fldcw
            | M::Fnstcw
            | M::Fstcw
            | M::Fnstsw
            | M::Fstsw
            | M::Fnstenv
            | M::Fstenv
            | M::Fldenv
            | M::Fnsave
            | M::Fsave
            | M::Frstor
    );
    let ip = cpu.fpu.last_ip;
    if !control {
        cpu.fpu.last_ip = cpu.cur_ip;
    }
    match exec_x87(cpu, mem, ins, m) {
        Err(CpuExit::Halt) => {
            cpu.fpu.last_ip = ip;
            None
        }
        r => Some(r),
    }
}

/// Marker used internally: `Err(Halt)` from `exec_x87` means "not handled" (mapped to `None`).
const NOT_HANDLED: R = Err(CpuExit::Halt);

fn exec_x87(cpu: &mut Cpu, mem: &mut GuestMemory, ins: &Instruction, m: Mnemonic) -> R {
    use Mnemonic as M;
    let has_mem = ins.op_count() > 0 && (0..ins.op_count()).any(|k| ins.op_kind(k) == OpKind::Memory);
    let ea = if has_mem { cpu.ea(ins) } else { 0 };
    if has_mem
        && !matches!(m, M::Fldcw | M::Fnstcw | M::Fstcw | M::Fnstsw | M::Fstsw)
        && !matches!(m, M::Fnstenv | M::Fstenv | M::Fldenv | M::Fnsave | M::Fsave | M::Frstor)
    {
        cpu.fpu.last_dp = ea;
    }
    match m {
        // ---- loads ----
        M::Fld | M::Fild | M::Fbld => {
            let v = if has_mem {
                match load_mem(cpu, mem, ins, ea)? {
                    Some(v) => v,
                    None => return NOT_HANDLED,
                }
            } else {
                let i = st_index(ins.op_register(ins.op_count() - 1)).unwrap_or(0);
                cpu.fpu.get(i)
            };
            cpu.fpu.push_checked(v);
        }
        M::Fld1 | M::Fldz | M::Fldpi | M::Fldl2e | M::Fldl2t | M::Fldlg2 | M::Fldln2 => {
            use std::f64::consts as c;
            let v = match m {
                M::Fld1 => 1.0,
                M::Fldz => 0.0,
                M::Fldpi => c::PI,
                M::Fldl2e => c::LOG2_E,
                M::Fldl2t => c::LOG2_10,
                M::Fldlg2 => c::LOG10_2,
                _ => c::LN_2,
            };
            cpu.fpu.push_checked(v);
        }

        // ---- stores ----
        M::Fst | M::Fstp => {
            let v = cpu.fpu.get(0);
            cpu.fpu.status &= !sw::C1;
            if has_mem {
                match ins.memory_size() {
                    MemorySize::Float32 => {
                        let f = conv::f64_to_f32(v);
                        if f.is_infinite() && v.is_finite() {
                            cpu.fpu.raise(sw::OE | sw::PE);
                        }
                        st_u32(cpu, mem, ea, f.to_bits())?
                    }
                    MemorySize::Float64 => st_u64(cpu, mem, ea, v.to_bits())?,
                    MemorySize::Float80 => st_f80(cpu, mem, ea, v)?,
                    _ => return NOT_HANDLED,
                }
            } else {
                let i = st_index(ins.op_register(0)).unwrap_or(0);
                cpu.fpu.set_st(i, v);
            }
            if m == M::Fstp {
                cpu.fpu.pop();
            }
        }
        M::Fist | M::Fistp | M::Fisttp => {
            let v = cpu.fpu.get(0);
            cpu.fpu.status &= !sw::C1;
            let rc = if m == M::Fisttp { 3 } else { cpu.fpu.rc() };
            let bytes = ins.memory_size().size() as u32;
            store_int(cpu, mem, ea, bytes, v, rc)?;
            if m != M::Fist {
                cpu.fpu.pop();
            }
        }
        M::Fbstp => {
            let v = cpu.fpu.get(0);
            let r = conv::round_rc(v, cpu.fpu.rc());
            let b = match conv::f64_to_bcd(r) {
                Some(b) => b,
                None => {
                    cpu.fpu.raise(sw::IE);
                    conv::BCD_INDEFINITE
                }
            };
            cpu.check_addr(ea, true)?;
            mem.write_bytes(ea, &b);
            cpu.fpu.pop();
        }

        // ---- register moves ----
        M::Fxch => {
            let n = ins.op_count();
            let i = if n == 0 { 1 } else { st_index(ins.op_register(n - 1)).unwrap_or(1) };
            let i = if i == 0 && n == 2 { st_index(ins.op_register(0)).unwrap_or(1) } else { i };
            let a = cpu.fpu.get(0);
            let b = cpu.fpu.get(i);
            cpu.fpu.set_st(0, b);
            cpu.fpu.set_st(i, a);
            cpu.fpu.status &= !sw::C1;
        }
        M::Ffree | M::Ffreep => {
            let i = st_index(ins.op_register(0)).unwrap_or(0);
            let p = cpu.fpu.phys(i);
            cpu.fpu.set_tag_phys(p, true);
            if m == M::Ffreep {
                cpu.fpu.pop();
            }
        }
        M::Fincstp => {
            cpu.fpu.top = (cpu.fpu.top + 1) & 7;
            cpu.fpu.status &= !sw::C1;
        }
        M::Fdecstp => {
            cpu.fpu.top = (cpu.fpu.top + 7) & 7;
            cpu.fpu.status &= !sw::C1;
        }
        M::Fcmovb | M::Fcmove | M::Fcmovbe | M::Fcmovu | M::Fcmovnb | M::Fcmovne | M::Fcmovnbe | M::Fcmovnu => {
            let (cf, zf, pf) = (cpu.flag(fl::CF), cpu.flag(fl::ZF), cpu.flag(fl::PF));
            let cond = match m {
                M::Fcmovb => cf,
                M::Fcmove => zf,
                M::Fcmovbe => cf || zf,
                M::Fcmovu => pf,
                M::Fcmovnb => !cf,
                M::Fcmovne => !zf,
                M::Fcmovnbe => !cf && !zf,
                _ => !pf,
            };
            if cond {
                let i = st_index(ins.op_register(ins.op_count() - 1)).unwrap_or(1);
                let v = cpu.fpu.get(i);
                cpu.fpu.set_st(0, v);
            }
        }

        // ---- arithmetic ----
        M::Fadd | M::Faddp | M::Fiadd | M::Fsub | M::Fsubp | M::Fisub | M::Fsubr | M::Fsubrp | M::Fisubr | M::Fmul
        | M::Fmulp | M::Fimul | M::Fdiv | M::Fdivp | M::Fidiv | M::Fdivr | M::Fdivrp | M::Fidivr => {
            let n = ins.op_count();
            let (di, s) = if has_mem {
                match load_mem(cpu, mem, ins, ea)? {
                    Some(v) => (0u8, v),
                    None => return NOT_HANDLED,
                }
            } else if n == 2 {
                let d = st_index(ins.op_register(0)).unwrap_or(0);
                let s = st_index(ins.op_register(1)).unwrap_or(0);
                (d, cpu.fpu.get(s))
            } else if n == 1 {
                let s = st_index(ins.op_register(0)).unwrap_or(1);
                (0, cpu.fpu.get(s))
            } else {
                (1, cpu.fpu.get(0))
            };
            let d = cpu.fpu.get(di);
            let r = cpu.fpu.arith(m, d, s);
            cpu.fpu.set_st(di, r);
            if matches!(m, M::Faddp | M::Fsubp | M::Fsubrp | M::Fmulp | M::Fdivp | M::Fdivrp) {
                cpu.fpu.pop();
            }
        }
        M::Fchs => {
            let v = cpu.fpu.get(0);
            cpu.fpu.set_st(0, -v);
            cpu.fpu.status &= !sw::C1;
        }
        M::Fabs => {
            let v = cpu.fpu.get(0);
            cpu.fpu.set_st(0, v.abs());
            cpu.fpu.status &= !sw::C1;
        }
        M::Fsqrt => {
            let v = cpu.fpu.get(0);
            let r = math::sqrt(v);
            let r = cpu.fpu.finish(r, v, 0.0);
            cpu.fpu.set_st(0, r);
        }
        M::Frndint => {
            let v = cpu.fpu.get(0);
            let r = conv::round_rc(v, cpu.fpu.rc());
            if r != v && !v.is_nan() {
                cpu.fpu.raise(sw::PE);
            }
            cpu.fpu.set_st(0, r);
        }
        M::Fscale => {
            let a = cpu.fpu.get(0);
            let b = cpu.fpu.get(1);
            let r = if a.is_nan() || b.is_nan() {
                if math::is_snan(a) || math::is_snan(b) {
                    cpu.fpu.raise(sw::IE);
                }
                math::propagate_nan(a, b)
            } else if b.is_infinite() {
                if b > 0.0 {
                    if a == 0.0 {
                        cpu.fpu.raise(sw::IE);
                        INDEFINITE
                    } else {
                        a * f64::INFINITY
                    }
                } else if a.is_infinite() {
                    cpu.fpu.raise(sw::IE);
                    INDEFINITE
                } else {
                    a * 0.0
                }
            } else {
                conv::ldexp(a, b.trunc().clamp(-1e5, 1e5) as i64)
            };
            cpu.fpu.status &= !sw::C1;
            cpu.fpu.set_st(0, r);
        }
        M::Fxtract => {
            let v = cpu.fpu.get(0);
            if v == 0.0 {
                cpu.fpu.raise(sw::ZE);
                cpu.fpu.set_st(0, f64::NEG_INFINITY);
                cpu.fpu.push_checked(v);
            } else if v.is_infinite() {
                cpu.fpu.set_st(0, f64::INFINITY);
                cpu.fpu.push_checked(v);
            } else if v.is_nan() {
                cpu.fpu.push_checked(v);
            } else {
                let e = conv::exponent_of(v);
                cpu.fpu.set_st(0, e as f64);
                cpu.fpu.push_checked(conv::ldexp(v, -e));
            }
        }
        M::Fprem | M::Fprem1 => {
            let a = cpu.fpu.get(0);
            let b = cpu.fpu.get(1);
            if a.is_nan() || b.is_nan() || a.is_infinite() || b == 0.0 {
                if !(a.is_nan() || b.is_nan()) || math::is_snan(a) || math::is_snan(b) {
                    cpu.fpu.raise(sw::IE);
                }
                cpu.fpu.set_st(0, if a.is_nan() || b.is_nan() { math::propagate_nan(a, b) } else { INDEFINITE });
                cpu.fpu.set_cc(false, false, false, false);
            } else if b.is_infinite() {
                cpu.fpu.set_cc(false, false, false, false);
            } else {
                // Exact integer long division (no host fmod); q = low 3 bits of the quotient.
                let math::Rem { r, q } = math::fprem(a, b, m == M::Fprem1);
                cpu.fpu.set_st(0, r);
                cpu.fpu.set_cc((q >> 1) & 1 == 1, false, q & 1 == 1, (q >> 2) & 1 == 1);
            }
        }
        M::Fsin | M::Fcos | M::Fptan | M::Fsincos => {
            let v = cpu.fpu.get(0);
            if v.is_finite() && v.abs() >= TWO63 {
                // Out of range: C2=1, operand unchanged.
                cpu.fpu.set_cc(false, true, false, false);
                return Ok(());
            }
            if v.is_infinite() || math::is_snan(v) {
                cpu.fpu.raise(sw::IE);
            }
            cpu.fpu.status &= !(sw::C2 | sw::C1);
            match m {
                // Deterministic (pure-Rust fdlibm) — never the host libm. See fpu_math.rs.
                M::Fsin => cpu.fpu.set_st(0, math::sin(v)),
                M::Fcos => cpu.fpu.set_st(0, math::cos(v)),
                M::Fptan => {
                    cpu.fpu.set_st(0, math::tan(v));
                    cpu.fpu.push_checked(1.0);
                }
                _ => {
                    let (s, c) = (math::sin(v), math::cos(v));
                    cpu.fpu.set_st(0, s);
                    cpu.fpu.push_checked(c);
                }
            }
        }
        M::Fpatan => {
            let x = cpu.fpu.get(0);
            let y = cpu.fpu.get(1);
            cpu.fpu.status &= !sw::C1;
            if math::is_snan(x) || math::is_snan(y) {
                cpu.fpu.raise(sw::IE);
            }
            cpu.fpu.set_st(1, math::atan2(y, x));
            cpu.fpu.pop();
        }
        M::F2xm1 => {
            let x = cpu.fpu.get(0);
            cpu.fpu.status &= !sw::C1;
            if math::is_snan(x) {
                cpu.fpu.raise(sw::IE);
            }
            cpu.fpu.set_st(0, math::exp2m1(x));
        }
        M::Fyl2x | M::Fyl2xp1 => {
            let x = cpu.fpu.get(0);
            let y = cpu.fpu.get(1);
            cpu.fpu.status &= !sw::C1;
            let r = if m == M::Fyl2x {
                if x == 0.0 && y.is_finite() && y != 0.0 {
                    cpu.fpu.raise(sw::ZE);
                }
                y * math::log2(x)
            } else {
                y * math::log2_1p(x)
            };
            let r = cpu.fpu.finish(r, x, y);
            cpu.fpu.set_st(1, r);
            cpu.fpu.pop();
        }

        // ---- compares ----
        M::Fcom | M::Fcomp | M::Fcompp | M::Fucom | M::Fucomp | M::Fucompp | M::Ficom | M::Ficomp => {
            let a = cpu.fpu.get(0);
            let b = compare_src(cpu, mem, ins)?;
            let quiet = matches!(m, M::Fucom | M::Fucomp | M::Fucompp);
            cpu.fpu.compare(a, b, quiet);
            match m {
                M::Fcomp | M::Fucomp | M::Ficomp => {
                    cpu.fpu.pop();
                }
                M::Fcompp | M::Fucompp => {
                    cpu.fpu.pop();
                    cpu.fpu.pop();
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        M::Fcomi | M::Fcomip | M::Fucomi | M::Fucomip => {
            let a = cpu.fpu.get(0);
            let b = compare_src(cpu, mem, ins)?;
            let quiet = matches!(m, M::Fucomi | M::Fucomip);
            let saved = cpu.fpu.status & sw::CC;
            cpu.fpu.compare(a, b, quiet);
            let c = cpu.fpu.status;
            cpu.fpu.status = (cpu.fpu.status & !sw::CC) | (saved & !sw::C1);
            cpu.set_eflags(cpu.eflags() & !(fl::OF | fl::SF | fl::AF | fl::ZF | fl::PF | fl::CF));
            cpu.set_flag(fl::ZF, c & sw::C3 != 0);
            cpu.set_flag(fl::PF, c & sw::C2 != 0);
            cpu.set_flag(fl::CF, c & sw::C0 != 0);
            if matches!(m, M::Fcomip | M::Fucomip) {
                cpu.fpu.pop();
            }
        }
        M::Ftst | M::Ftstp => {
            let a = cpu.fpu.get(0);
            cpu.fpu.compare(a, 0.0, false);
            if m == M::Ftstp {
                cpu.fpu.pop();
            }
        }
        M::Fxam => cpu.fpu.fxam(),

        // ---- control ----
        M::Fninit | M::Finit => cpu.fpu.reset(),
        M::Fnclex | M::Fclex => cpu.fpu.status &= !(sw::EXC | sw::SF | sw::ES | sw::B),
        M::Fldcw => {
            cpu.fpu.control = ld_u16(cpu, mem, ea)? | 0x0040;
            let f = &mut cpu.fpu;
            if f.status & !f.control & sw::EXC != 0 {
                f.status |= sw::ES | sw::B;
            } else {
                f.status &= !(sw::ES | sw::B);
            }
        }
        M::Fnstcw | M::Fstcw => st_u16(cpu, mem, ea, cpu.fpu.control)?,
        M::Fnstsw | M::Fstsw => {
            let v = cpu.fpu.status_word();
            if has_mem {
                st_u16(cpu, mem, ea, v)?;
            } else {
                cpu.set_reg(Register::AX, v as u32);
            }
        }
        M::Fnstenv | M::Fstenv => {
            store_env(cpu, mem, ea, ins.memory_size() == MemorySize::FpuEnv14)?;
            // fnstenv masks all exceptions after storing.
            cpu.fpu.control |= sw::EXC;
        }
        M::Fldenv => {
            load_env(cpu, mem, ea, ins.memory_size() == MemorySize::FpuEnv14)?;
        }
        M::Fnsave | M::Fsave => {
            let small = ins.memory_size() == MemorySize::FpuState94;
            let off = store_env(cpu, mem, ea, small)?;
            for i in 0..8u8 {
                let v = cpu.fpu.st(i);
                st_f80(cpu, mem, ea + off + 10 * i as u32, v)?;
            }
            cpu.fpu.reset();
        }
        M::Frstor => {
            let small = ins.memory_size() == MemorySize::FpuState94;
            let off = load_env(cpu, mem, ea, small)?;
            for i in 0..8u8 {
                let v = ld_f80(cpu, mem, ea + off + 10 * i as u32)?;
                let p = cpu.fpu.phys(i);
                cpu.fpu.regs[p] = v;
            }
        }
        M::Fnop | M::Fneni | M::Feni | M::Fndisi | M::Fdisi | M::Fnsetpm | M::Fsetpm | M::Frstpm => {}
        _ => return NOT_HANDLED,
    }
    Ok(())
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MMX subset
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn exec_mmx(cpu: &mut Cpu, mem: &mut GuestMemory, ins: &Instruction) -> Option<R> {
    if ins.mnemonic() == Mnemonic::Emms {
        cpu.fpu.tags = 0xFFFF;
        return Some(Ok(()));
    }
    let n = ins.op_count();
    if n != 2 {
        return None;
    }
    let dst_mm = (ins.op_kind(0) == OpKind::Register).then(|| mm_index(ins.op_register(0))).flatten();
    let src_mm = (ins.op_kind(1) == OpKind::Register).then(|| mm_index(ins.op_register(1))).flatten();
    if dst_mm.is_none() && src_mm.is_none() {
        return None; // SSE/XMM forms are not supported.
    }
    let is_q = ins.mnemonic() == Mnemonic::Movq;
    let r = (|| -> R {
        // Read the source.
        let v: u64 = if let Some(s) = src_mm {
            cpu.fpu.mmx[s]
        } else if ins.op_kind(1) == OpKind::Memory {
            let a = cpu.ea(ins);
            if is_q {
                ld_u64(cpu, mem, a)?
            } else {
                ld_u32(cpu, mem, a)? as u64
            }
        } else if ins.op_kind(1) == OpKind::Register {
            cpu.get_reg(ins.op_register(1)) as u64
        } else {
            return NOT_HANDLED;
        };
        if let Some(d) = dst_mm {
            cpu.fpu.mmx[d] = if is_q { v } else { v & 0xFFFF_FFFF };
        } else if ins.op_kind(0) == OpKind::Memory {
            let a = cpu.ea(ins);
            if is_q {
                st_u64(cpu, mem, a, v)?;
            } else {
                st_u32(cpu, mem, a, v as u32)?;
            }
        } else if ins.op_kind(0) == OpKind::Register {
            cpu.set_reg(ins.op_register(0), v as u32);
        } else {
            return NOT_HANDLED;
        }
        // Any MMX instruction: TOP=0, all tags valid.
        cpu.fpu.top = 0;
        cpu.fpu.tags = 0;
        Ok(())
    })();
    match r {
        Err(CpuExit::Halt) => None,
        r => Some(r),
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-cpu/src/fpu_conv.rs`:

```rs
//! Pure numeric helpers for the x87 emulation: 80-bit extended <-> f64, packed BCD, rounding control,
//! precision control, `ldexp`/`frexp`-style helpers. No CPU state here.

/// The x87 "real indefinite" (negative quiet NaN) as f64.
pub const INDEFINITE: f64 = f64::from_bits(0xFFF8_0000_0000_0000);

/// Round `m / 2^s` to nearest, ties to even (s may be 0..=127).
fn shr_round_ne(m: u64, s: u32) -> u64 {
    if s == 0 {
        return m;
    }
    if s >= 128 {
        return 0;
    }
    let m = m as u128;
    let q = m >> s;
    let rem = m & ((1u128 << s) - 1);
    let half = 1u128 << (s - 1);
    let q = if rem > half || (rem == half && (q & 1) == 1) { q + 1 } else { q };
    q as u64
}

/// f64 -> 80-bit extended `(significand with explicit integer bit, sign|exponent)`. Exact.
pub fn f64_to_f80(v: f64) -> (u64, u16) {
    let bits = v.to_bits();
    let sign = ((bits >> 63) as u16) << 15;
    let e = ((bits >> 52) & 0x7FF) as i32;
    let f = bits & ((1u64 << 52) - 1);
    if e == 0 {
        if f == 0 {
            return (0, sign);
        }
        // Denormal: normalise (80-bit has the exponent range to represent it as a normal).
        let p = 63 - f.leading_zeros() as i32; // MSB position (< 52)
        let mant = f << (63 - p);
        let exp = p - 1074 + 16383;
        return (mant, sign | exp as u16);
    }
    if e == 0x7FF {
        if f == 0 {
            return (1u64 << 63, sign | 0x7FFF);
        }
        return ((1u64 << 63) | (f << 11), sign | 0x7FFF);
    }
    ((1u64 << 63) | (f << 11), sign | (e - 1023 + 16383) as u16)
}

/// 80-bit extended -> f64, rounding to nearest-even (overflow -> inf, underflow -> denormal/0).
pub fn f80_to_f64(mant: u64, se: u16) -> f64 {
    let sign = ((se >> 15) as u64) << 63;
    let e = (se & 0x7FFF) as i32;
    if e == 0x7FFF {
        let frac = (mant << 1) >> 12;
        if mant << 1 == 0 {
            return f64::from_bits(sign | 0x7FF0_0000_0000_0000);
        }
        // NaN: keep the top fraction bits, force quiet.
        return f64::from_bits(sign | 0x7FF8_0000_0000_0000 | frac);
    }
    if mant == 0 {
        return f64::from_bits(sign);
    }
    let lz = mant.leading_zeros() as i32;
    let m = mant << lz;
    // value = m / 2^63 * 2^unb
    let unb = if e == 0 { 1 } else { e } - 16383 - lz;
    let mut ef = unb + 1023;
    if ef >= 1 {
        let mut r = shr_round_ne(m, 11);
        if r == 1u64 << 53 {
            r >>= 1;
            ef += 1;
        }
        if ef >= 0x7FF {
            return f64::from_bits(sign | 0x7FF0_0000_0000_0000);
        }
        f64::from_bits(sign | ((ef as u64) << 52) | (r & ((1u64 << 52) - 1)))
    } else {
        let s = (11 + (1 - ef)) as u32;
        let r = shr_round_ne(m, s);
        f64::from_bits(sign | r)
    }
}

/// f32 -> f64 as `fld m32` does it. Non-NaN values convert exactly; NaNs are quieted with the payload kept
/// (bit-level, so the host's NaN conversion rules never matter).
pub fn f32_to_f64(x: f32) -> f64 {
    if x.is_nan() {
        let b = x.to_bits() as u64;
        let sign = (b >> 31) << 63;
        let payload = (b & 0x003F_FFFF) << 29;
        return f64::from_bits(sign | 0x7FF8_0000_0000_0000 | payload);
    }
    x as f64
}

/// f64 -> f32 as `fst m32` does it: round to nearest even (IEEE conversion, identical on all hosts);
/// NaNs are quieted and the payload truncated (bit-level).
pub fn f64_to_f32(x: f64) -> f32 {
    if x.is_nan() {
        let b = x.to_bits();
        let sign = ((b >> 63) as u32) << 31;
        let payload = ((b >> 29) & 0x003F_FFFF) as u32;
        return f32::from_bits(sign | 0x7FC0_0000 | payload);
    }
    x as f32
}

/// Round to an integral value using x87 rounding control (0 nearest-even, 1 down, 2 up, 3 truncate).
/// NaN is returned quieted (never through the host's rounding functions, which may be libm calls).
pub fn round_rc(v: f64, rc: u16) -> f64 {
    if v.is_nan() {
        return f64::from_bits(v.to_bits() | (1u64 << 51));
    }
    match rc & 3 {
        0 => v.round_ties_even(),
        1 => v.floor(),
        2 => v.ceil(),
        _ => v.trunc(),
    }
}

/// Apply x87 precision control to an arithmetic result: PC=0 (24-bit significand) rounds the significand to
/// 24 bits (keeping the wide exponent range); PC=2/3 are left at f64's 53 bits.
pub fn apply_pc(v: f64, control: u16) -> f64 {
    if (control >> 8) & 3 != 0 || !v.is_finite() || v == 0.0 {
        return v;
    }
    // Round the 52-bit fraction to 23 bits (drop 29) with ties-to-even. The carry may ripple into the exponent,
    // which is the correct behaviour (including overflow to infinity).
    let bits = v.to_bits();
    let keep_lsb = (bits >> 29) & 1;
    let r = bits.wrapping_add((1u64 << 28) - 1 + keep_lsb) & !((1u64 << 29) - 1);
    f64::from_bits(r)
}

/// `x * 2^n` without intermediate overflow/underflow for large `n`.
pub fn ldexp(mut x: f64, mut n: i64) -> f64 {
    if x == 0.0 || !x.is_finite() {
        return x;
    }
    n = n.clamp(-5000, 5000);
    let p1000 = f64::from_bits(((1023 + 1000) as u64) << 52);
    let m1000 = f64::from_bits(((1023 - 1000) as u64) << 52);
    while n > 1000 {
        x *= p1000;
        n -= 1000;
        if x.is_infinite() {
            return x;
        }
    }
    while n < -1000 {
        x *= m1000;
        n += 1000;
        if x == 0.0 {
            return x;
        }
    }
    // Now |n| <= 1000: split so that each factor is a normal f64.
    let a = n / 2;
    let b = n - a;
    x * f64::from_bits(((1023 + a) as u64) << 52) * f64::from_bits(((1023 + b) as u64) << 52)
}

/// Unbiased binary exponent of a finite non-zero `x` (floor(log2|x|)), as `fxtract` reports it.
pub fn exponent_of(x: f64) -> i64 {
    let bits = x.to_bits();
    let e = ((bits >> 52) & 0x7FF) as i64;
    if e == 0 {
        let f = bits & ((1u64 << 52) - 1);
        let p = 63 - f.leading_zeros() as i64;
        p - 1074
    } else {
        e - 1023
    }
}

/// Decode 10-byte packed BCD (18 digits + sign byte).
pub fn bcd_to_f64(b: &[u8; 10]) -> f64 {
    let mut v: u64 = 0;
    for i in (0..9).rev() {
        let hi = (b[i] >> 4) as u64;
        let lo = (b[i] & 0xF) as u64;
        v = v * 100 + hi * 10 + lo;
    }
    let f = v as f64;
    if b[9] & 0x80 != 0 {
        -f
    } else {
        f
    }
}

/// Encode an integral value as 10-byte packed BCD. Returns `None` if out of range (|v| >= 10^18) or NaN.
pub fn f64_to_bcd(v: f64) -> Option<[u8; 10]> {
    if v.is_nan() || v.abs() >= 1e18 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut out = [0u8; 10];
    let mut n = v.abs() as u64;
    for byte in out.iter_mut().take(9) {
        let lo = (n % 10) as u8;
        n /= 10;
        let hi = (n % 10) as u8;
        n /= 10;
        *byte = (hi << 4) | lo;
    }
    if v.is_sign_negative() {
        out[9] = 0x80;
    }
    Some(out)
}

/// The BCD indefinite encoding stored by `fbstp` on invalid operation.
pub const BCD_INDEFINITE: [u8; 10] = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0xC0, 0xFF, 0xFF];

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn f80_roundtrip_and_known_values() {
        for &v in &[0.0, -0.0, 1.0, -2.5, std::f64::consts::PI, 1e300, -1e-300, 5e-324, f64::MAX, f64::MIN_POSITIVE] {
            let (m, se) = f64_to_f80(v);
            assert_eq!(f80_to_f64(m, se).to_bits(), v.to_bits(), "{v}");
        }
        // 1.0 = 3FFF 8000000000000000
        assert_eq!(f64_to_f80(1.0), (0x8000_0000_0000_0000, 0x3FFF));
        // pi as stored by fldpi (rounded to 64 bits): C90FDAA22168C235 -> nearest f64 pi
        assert_eq!(f80_to_f64(0xC90F_DAA2_2168_C235, 0x4000), std::f64::consts::PI);
        // Overflow / underflow
        assert!(f80_to_f64(0x8000_0000_0000_0000, 0x7000).is_infinite());
        assert_eq!(f80_to_f64(0x8000_0000_0000_0000, 0x0001), 0.0);
        // Infinity, NaN
        assert_eq!(f80_to_f64(0x8000_0000_0000_0000, 0xFFFF), f64::NEG_INFINITY);
        assert!(f80_to_f64(0xC000_0000_0000_0000, 0x7FFF).is_nan());
        // Ties-to-even on the 11 dropped bits: 1 + 2^-53 -> 1.0, 1 + 3*2^-53 -> 1 + 2^-51
        assert_eq!(f80_to_f64(0x8000_0000_0000_0400, 0x3FFF), 1.0);
        assert_eq!(f80_to_f64(0x8000_0000_0000_0C00, 0x3FFF), 1.0 + 2f64.powi(-51));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rounding_and_bcd() {
        assert_eq!(round_rc(2.5, 0), 2.0);
        assert_eq!(round_rc(-2.5, 1), -3.0);
        assert_eq!(round_rc(2.1, 2), 3.0);
        assert_eq!(round_rc(-2.9, 3), -2.0);
        assert_eq!(apply_pc(1.0 + 2f64.powi(-30), 0x007F), 1.0);
        assert_eq!(apply_pc(1.0 + 2f64.powi(-30), 0x027F), 1.0 + 2f64.powi(-30));
        let b = f64_to_bcd(-1234567.0).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(&b[..4], &[0x67, 0x45, 0x23, 0x01]);
        assert_eq!(bcd_to_f64(&b), -1234567.0);
        assert_eq!(ldexp(1.0, -1074), 5e-324);
        assert_eq!(ldexp(3.0, 4), 48.0);
        assert_eq!(exponent_of(48.0), 5);
    }

    #[test]
    fn f32_nan_conversion_is_bit_exact() {
        // SNaN f32 0x7F800001 -> quiet f64 with payload << 29
        assert_eq!(f32_to_f64(f32::from_bits(0x7F80_0001)).to_bits(), 0x7FF8_0000_2000_0000);
        assert_eq!(f32_to_f64(f32::from_bits(0xFFC0_0000)).to_bits(), 0xFFF8_0000_0000_0000);
        assert_eq!(f64_to_f32(f64::from_bits(0xFFF8_0000_0000_0000)).to_bits(), 0xFFC0_0000);
        assert_eq!(f64_to_f32(f64::from_bits(0x7FF0_0000_2000_0000)).to_bits(), 0x7FC0_0001);
        assert_eq!(f64_to_f32(0.1), 0.1f32);
        assert_eq!(f32_to_f64(0.1f32), 0.1f32 as f64);
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-cpu/src/fpu_golden.rs`:

```rs
//! Golden-vector determinism test for the x87 emulation.
//!
//! Runs every non-trivial x87 operation over a fixed pseudo-random input set (normal values in several ranges,
//! plus random bit patterns that hit NaN/SNaN/inf/subnormal/zero), through the real instruction path
//! (assembled snippets executed by the interpreter), and hashes the result bits + status words. The hashes are
//! stored below. They must be identical on every host (x86_64, aarch64, i686-SSE2, ...): lockstep multiplayer
//! peers compute the same game state only if this holds. See `docs/porting/determinism.md`.
//!
//! If a hash changes:
//! - on a new host only -> a real cross-platform determinism bug (do NOT just update the constant);
//! - after an intended semantic change in fpu*.rs (or a `libm` bump) -> update the constant in the same commit and
//!   note it in determinism.md (it changes multiplayer compatibility between app versions).
//!
//! Print the current values with `cargo test -p s3-cpu golden -- --nocapture`.

use iced_x86::code_asm::*;

use crate::*;

const CODE: u32 = 0x0040_1000;
const STACK_TOP: u32 = 0x0090_0000;
const IN_A: u32 = 0x0060_0000;
const IN_B: u32 = 0x0068_0000;
const OUT: u32 = 0x0070_0000;
const OUT_SW: u32 = 0x0078_0000;
const N: usize = 2048;

/// xorshift64* (fixed seed): deterministic input generator.
struct Rng(u64);
impl Rng {
    fn next(&mut self) -> u64 {
        self.0 ^= self.0 >> 12;
        self.0 ^= self.0 << 25;
        self.0 ^= self.0 >> 27;
        self.0.wrapping_mul(0x2545_F491_4F6C_DD1D)
    }
    fn unit(&mut self) -> f64 {
        (self.next() >> 11) as f64 / (1u64 << 53) as f64
    }
}

/// Input class mix: 0..4 = uniform in [-r, r] for r = 1, 10, 1e4, 1e15; 5 = raw bits; 6 = special values.
fn gen(rng: &mut Rng) -> f64 {
    const SPECIAL: [u64; 12] = [
        0,
        0x8000_0000_0000_0000,
        0x7FF0_0000_0000_0000,
        0xFFF0_0000_0000_0000,
        0x7FF8_0000_0000_0000,
        0xFFF8_0000_0000_0000,
        0x7FF0_0000_0000_0001, // SNaN
        0x7FF8_0000_DEAD_BEEF,
        0x0000_0000_0000_0001, // min subnormal
        0x000F_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF, // max subnormal
        0x0010_0000_0000_0000, // min normal
        0x7FEF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF, // max
    ];
    let c = rng.next() % 8;
    let s = rng.unit() * 2.0 - 1.0;
    match c {
        0 => s,
        1 => s * 10.0,
        2 => s * 1e4,
        3 => s * 1e15,
        4 => s * std::f64::consts::PI * 2.0,
        5 | 6 => f64::from_bits(rng.next()),
        _ => f64::from_bits(SPECIAL[(rng.next() % SPECIAL.len() as u64) as usize]),
    }
}

fn inputs(seed: u64) -> (Vec<f64>, Vec<f64>) {
    let mut r = Rng(seed);
    let a = (0..N).map(|_| gen(&mut r)).collect();
    let b = (0..N).map(|_| gen(&mut r)).collect();
    (a, b)
}

/// Run `body` once per input pair: ST0 = a[i], ST1 = b[i] on entry; `body` must leave exactly `pops` values,
/// ST0 is stored as a qword (or, if `store32`, as a dword), the status word recorded, then the stack emptied.
fn run_op(
    a_in: &[f64],
    b_in: &[f64],
    control: u16,
    store32: bool,
    body: impl Fn(&mut CodeAssembler),
    left: usize,
) -> u64 {
    let mut a = CodeAssembler::new(32).unwrap();
    let mut lp = a.create_label();
    let cw_slot = OUT_SW - 4;
    a.mov(dword_ptr(cw_slot as u64), control as u32).unwrap();
    a.fldcw(word_ptr(cw_slot as u64)).unwrap();
    a.mov(esi, 0u32).unwrap();
    a.set_label(&mut lp).unwrap();
    a.fld(qword_ptr(esi * 8 + IN_B as i32)).unwrap();
    a.fld(qword_ptr(esi * 8 + IN_A as i32)).unwrap();
    body(&mut a);
    if store32 {
        a.fst(dword_ptr(esi * 8 + OUT as i32)).unwrap();
    } else {
        a.fst(qword_ptr(esi * 8 + OUT as i32)).unwrap();
    }
    a.fnstsw(ax).unwrap();
    a.mov(word_ptr(esi * 2 + OUT_SW as i32), ax).unwrap();
    for _ in 0..left {
        a.fstp(st0).unwrap();
    }
    a.fnclex().unwrap();
    a.inc(esi).unwrap();
    a.cmp(esi, N as u32).unwrap();
    a.jne(lp).unwrap();
    a.ret().unwrap();
    let bytes = a.assemble(CODE as u64).unwrap();

    let mut mem = GuestMemory::new().unwrap();
    mem.write_bytes(CODE, &bytes);
    for i in 0..N {
        mem.write_u64(IN_A + 8 * i as u32, a_in[i].to_bits());
        mem.write_u64(IN_B + 8 * i as u32, b_in[i].to_bits());
    }
    let mut cpu = Cpu::new();
    cpu.regs[ESP] = STACK_TOP;
    cpu.push32(&mut mem, layout::MAGIC_RETURN);
    cpu.eip = CODE;
    let exit = cpu.run(&mut mem, 100_000_000);
    assert_eq!(exit, CpuExit::ReturnMagic, "eip={:#x}", cpu.eip);

    // FNV-1a over result bits and status words.
    let mut h: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;
    let mut eat = |x: u64, n: usize| {
        for k in 0..n {
            h ^= (x >> (8 * k)) & 0xFF;
            h = h.wrapping_mul(0x0100_0000_01b3);
        }
    };
    for i in 0..N {
        eat(mem.read_u64(OUT + 8 * i as u32), 8);
        eat(mem.read_u16(OUT_SW + 2 * i as u32) as u64, 2);
    }
    h
}

type Body = fn(&mut CodeAssembler);

// Needs the 4 GiB guest window, so 64-bit hosts only; `golden_pure_functions` covers 32-bit hosts.
#[cfg(target_pointer_width = "64")]
#[test]
fn golden_x87_vectors() {
    let (a, b) = inputs(0x5E77_1E55_3000_0001);
    let mut got = Vec::new();
    for (name, cw, f32s, body, left) in cases() {
        got.push((name, run_op(&a, &b, cw, f32s, body, left)));
    }
    for (n, h) in &got {
        println!("        (\"{n}\", {h:#018x}),");
    }
    if EXPECTED.is_empty() {
        panic!("EXPECTED is empty: paste the lines printed above into fpu_golden.rs");
    }
    let mut bad = Vec::new();
    for ((n, h), (en, eh)) in got.iter().zip(EXPECTED) {
        assert_eq!(n, en, "case list changed: update EXPECTED");
        if h != eh {
            bad.push(*n);
        }
    }
    assert_eq!(got.len(), EXPECTED.len(), "case list changed: update EXPECTED");
    assert!(bad.is_empty(), "x87 results differ from the golden vectors for: {bad:?} (host determinism bug?)");
}
```

`port/crates/s3-cpu/src/fpu_math.rs`:

```rs
//! Deterministic x87 math: every result here is a pure function of the input bits and is bit-identical on every
//! host (x86_64, aarch64, i686 with SSE2, wasm32). Needed for lockstep multiplayer (see
//! `docs/porting/determinism.md`).
//!
//! Rules:
//! - Never call the host libm (`f64::sin`, `f64::ln_1p`, `%`, ...): its results differ between glibc, Bionic,
//!   musl and macOS. Transcendentals use the pinned pure-Rust `libm` crate (a port of musl/FreeBSD fdlibm,
//!   built with `default-features = false`, i.e. no arch intrinsics). fdlibm is not correctly rounded (< 1 ulp),
//!   but it is a fixed algorithm made of IEEE basic operations only, so its output is reproducible.
//! - Only IEEE-754 basic operations (`+ - * /`, `sqrt`, conversions) are used directly: they are correctly
//!   rounded on all hosts. Rust never contracts `a*b+c` into an FMA, so no fusion differences.
//! - NaNs are never produced by the host: x86 SSE creates `0xFFF8..` (negative), aarch64 creates `0x7FF8..`
//!   (positive), and two-NaN propagation depends on operand order (which LLVM may commute). We decide every NaN
//!   result ourselves with the x87 rules (see [`propagate_nan`]).
//! - `fmod` is done in integer arithmetic ([`fprem`]), which also gives the exact quotient bits.

use super::conv::INDEFINITE;

/// Is `x` a signalling NaN (quiet bit clear)?
#[inline]
pub fn is_snan(x: f64) -> bool {
    x.is_nan() && (x.to_bits() >> 51) & 1 == 0
}

/// Quiet a NaN (set the quiet bit), keeping sign and payload.
#[inline]
pub fn quiet(x: f64) -> f64 {
    f64::from_bits(x.to_bits() | (1u64 << 51))
}

/// x87 NaN propagation for a two-operand instruction where at least one operand is a NaN:
/// one NaN -> that NaN (quieted); two NaNs -> the one with the larger significand (quieted); equal significands
/// -> `a` (the destination operand). The caller raises IE when [`is_snan`] is true for either operand.
/// Deterministic: does not depend on host NaN rules or operand order chosen by the compiler.
pub fn propagate_nan(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    match (a.is_nan(), b.is_nan()) {
        (true, false) => quiet(a),
        (false, true) => quiet(b),
        _ => {
            let sig = |x: f64| x.to_bits() & ((1u64 << 51) - 1);
            if sig(b) > sig(a) {
                quiet(b)
            } else {
                quiet(a)
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Canonicalise a host result of a one-operand operation: NaN input -> quieted input; NaN output from a
/// non-NaN input -> x87 indefinite. Returns (value, invalid).
#[inline]
pub fn canon1(input: f64, r: f64) -> (f64, bool) {
    if input.is_nan() {
        (quiet(input), is_snan(input))
    } else if r.is_nan() {
        (INDEFINITE, true)
    } else {
        (r, false)
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- transcendentals

/// `fsin` for |x| < 2^63 (caller handles the out-of-range case). Infinity -> indefinite.
pub fn sin(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x.is_nan() {
        return quiet(x);
    }
    if x.is_infinite() {
        return INDEFINITE;
    }
    libm::sin(x)
}

/// `fcos`.
pub fn cos(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x.is_nan() {
        return quiet(x);
    }
    if x.is_infinite() {
        return INDEFINITE;
    }
    libm::cos(x)
}

/// `fptan` (the pushed 1.0 is the caller's job).
pub fn tan(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x.is_nan() {
        return quiet(x);
    }
    if x.is_infinite() {
        return INDEFINITE;
    }
    libm::tan(x)
}

/// `fpatan`: atan2(y, x) with x87 NaN propagation (ST(1)=y is the "first" operand).
pub fn atan2(y: f64, x: f64) -> f64 {
    if y.is_nan() || x.is_nan() {
        return propagate_nan(y, x);
    }
    libm::atan2(y, x)
}

/// `f2xm1`: 2^x - 1 (x87 domain -1 <= x <= 1; other finite inputs are still computed).
/// Computed as expm1(x * ln2) — the product is rounded once, so the result is within ~1 ulp of the true value.
pub fn exp2m1(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x.is_nan() {
        return quiet(x);
    }
    if x == f64::NEG_INFINITY {
        return -1.0;
    }
    if x == f64::INFINITY {
        return x;
    }
    if x == 0.0 {
        return x; // keeps the sign of zero
    }
    // t = x*ln2 as a double-double (p + e): Dekker's exact product (no FMA, so identical everywhere) plus the
    // low part of ln2. Then 2^x - 1 = expm1(p + e) ~= expm1(p) + e * (1 + expm1(p)).
    let p = x * LN2_HI_D;
    let e = two_prod_err(x, LN2_HI_D, p) + x * LN2_LO_D;
    let m = libm::expm1(p);
    m + e * (1.0 + m)
}

/// ln 2 = LN2_HI_D + LN2_LO_D (LN2_HI_D = the f64 nearest ln 2).
const LN2_HI_D: f64 = std::f64::consts::LN_2;
const LN2_LO_D: f64 = f64::from_bits(0x3C7A_BC9E_3B39_803F); // 2.3190468138462996e-17

/// Exact error of the product `a*b` rounded to `p` (Dekker/Veltkamp split; valid for |a|,|b| well inside the
/// f64 range, which holds for the f2xm1 domain).
fn two_prod_err(a: f64, b: f64, p: f64) -> f64 {
    fn split(x: f64) -> (f64, f64) {
        let c = 134_217_729.0 * x; // 2^27 + 1
        let hi = c - (c - x);
        (hi, x - hi)
    }
    if !a.is_finite() || a.abs() > 1e300 {
        return 0.0;
    }
    let (ah, al) = split(a);
    let (bh, bl) = split(b);
    ((ah * bh - p) + ah * bl + al * bh) + al * bl
}

/// log2(x) for `fyl2x` (x <= 0 handled by the caller's invalid/zero-divide logic via the returned value:
/// log2(0) = -inf, log2(<0) = NaN which the caller turns into indefinite).
pub fn log2(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x.is_nan() {
        return quiet(x);
    }
    if x < 0.0 {
        return INDEFINITE;
    }
    libm::log2(x)
}

/// log2(1 + x) for `fyl2xp1`.
pub fn log2_1p(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x.is_nan() {
        return quiet(x);
    }
    if x < -1.0 {
        return INDEFINITE;
    }
    if x == 0.0 {
        return x;
    }
    // log1p(x) / ln2: two roundings, deterministic.
    libm::log1p(x) / std::f64::consts::LN_2
}

/// `fsqrt` core: IEEE sqrt is correctly rounded on all hosts; only the NaN result needs canonicalising.
pub fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x.is_nan() {
        return quiet(x);
    }
    if x < 0.0 {
        return INDEFINITE;
    }
    x.sqrt()
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ remainder

/// Decompose a finite non-zero f64 into (integer significand < 2^53, exponent) with |x| = m * 2^e.
fn decompose(x: f64) -> (u64, i32) {
    let bits = x.to_bits();
    let e = ((bits >> 52) & 0x7FF) as i32;
    let f = bits & ((1u64 << 52) - 1);
    if e == 0 {
        (f, -1074)
    } else {
        (f | (1u64 << 52), e - 1075)
    }
}

/// `m * 2^e` for m < 2^53 and a result known to be representable exactly (used for remainders: they are
/// multiples of 2^e(b) and smaller than |b|).
fn compose(m: u64, e: i32) -> f64 {
    if m == 0 {
        return 0.0;
    }
    // Normalise m to 53 bits, then build the bits directly (handles subnormal results too).
    let lz = m.leading_zeros() as i32 - 11; // shift that puts the MSB at bit 52
    let (mut mm, mut ee) = (m << lz, e - lz);
    // value = mm * 2^ee, mm in [2^52, 2^53)
    let biased = ee + 1075;
    if biased >= 1 {
        f64::from_bits(((biased as u64) << 52) | (mm & ((1u64 << 52) - 1)))
    } else {
        // Subnormal: shift right; exact by construction (the low bits are zero).
        let s = (1 - biased) as u32;
        mm >>= s.min(63);
        ee += s as i32;
        let _ = ee;
        f64::from_bits(mm)
    }
}

/// Result of [`fprem`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub struct Rem {
    /// Remainder (sign of the dividend; zero keeps the dividend's sign).
    pub r: f64,
    /// Low 3 bits of the integer quotient |a/b| (for C0/C3/C1).
    pub q: u8,
}

/// Exact `fprem` (truncating quotient, `ieee = false`) or `fprem1` (round-to-nearest-even quotient,
/// `ieee = true`) for finite `a` and finite non-zero `b`. Always the complete remainder (C2 = 0): real hardware
/// may need several iterations for exponent differences >= 64, which the CRT loops over anyway.
pub fn fprem(a: f64, b: f64, ieee: bool) -> Rem {
    debug_assert!(a.is_finite() && b.is_finite() && b != 0.0);
    if a == 0.0 {
        return Rem { r: a, q: 0 };
    }
    let (ma, ea) = decompose(a);
    let (mb, eb) = decompose(b);
    // |a| = ma*2^ea, |b| = mb*2^eb. Long division of ma*2^(ea-eb) by mb, keeping the remainder and q mod 8.
    let (mut r, mut q): (u64, u64);
    if ea >= eb {
        r = ma % mb;
        q = ma / mb;
        let mut d = ea - eb;
        // Shift in chunks of up to 10 bits: r < mb < 2^53, so r << 10 < 2^63 fits.
        while d > 0 {
            let k = d.min(10) as u32;
            let x = r << k;
            q = (q << k) | (x / mb); // only the low bits of q matter (wrapping shift is fine)
            r = x % mb;
            d -= k as i32;
        }
        // remainder value = r * 2^eb
    } else {
        // ea < eb only happens for a normal b (eb > -1074, mb >= 2^52); then |a| < 2^53 * 2^ea <= 2^52 * 2^eb
        // <= |b|, so the truncated quotient is 0 and the remainder is a itself.
        if !ieee {
            return Rem { r: a, q: 0 };
        }
        // fprem1 still needs the rounding step: compare |a| with |b|/2 exactly at exponent ea.
        let d = (eb - ea) as u32;
        if d >= 2 {
            // |a| < 2^53*2^ea <= 2^51*2^eb <= |b|/2: no rounding.
            return Rem { r: a, q: 0 };
        }
        // d == 1: |b| = (2*mb) * 2^ea, 2*mb < 2^54 fits in u64.
        return finish_rem(a, b, ma, ea, 0, ieee, Some((mb << 1, ea)));
    }
    finish_rem(a, b, r, eb, q, ieee, Some((mb, eb)))
}

/// Shared tail of [`fprem`]: r (at exponent `e`) is the truncating remainder, q the truncated quotient.
/// `div` = (divisor significand, exponent) at the same exponent `e`.
fn finish_rem(a: f64, _b: f64, mut r: u64, e: i32, mut q: u64, ieee: bool, div: Option<(u64, i32)>) -> Rem {
    let neg = a.is_sign_negative();
    let mut flip = false;
    if ieee {
        if let Some((mb, _)) = div {
            // Round the quotient to nearest even: if 2r > mb, or 2r == mb and q odd -> q+1, r = mb - r (sign flips).
            let two_r = (r as u128) * 2;
            let mb128 = mb as u128;
            if two_r > mb128 || (two_r == mb128 && q & 1 == 1) {
                q = q.wrapping_add(1);
                r = mb - r;
                flip = true;
            }
        }
    }
    let mag = compose(r, e);
    let rv = if r == 0 {
        0.0f64.copysign(a)
    } else if neg != flip {
        -mag
    } else {
        mag
    };
    Rem { r: rv, q: (q & 7) as u8 }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- host environment check

/// Verify that the host FPU is in the IEEE mode determinism relies on: subnormals are neither flushed to zero
/// (FTZ) nor treated as zero on input (DAZ), round-to-nearest is active, and basic ops are correctly rounded.
/// Some Android audio/graphics libraries are known to set FTZ on their own threads (HYPOTHESIS for ours); call
/// this on the emulation thread at startup. Values go through `black_box` so the checks run at runtime.
pub fn host_float_env_check() -> Result<(), &'static str> {
    use std::hint::black_box as bb;
    let tiny = bb(f64::from_bits(1)); // smallest subnormal
    if bb(tiny * 1.0) != tiny || bb(tiny + tiny).to_bits() != 2 {
        return Err("subnormal results flushed to zero (FTZ)");
    }
    if bb(f64::MIN_POSITIVE) / bb(2.0) == 0.0 {
        return Err("subnormal results flushed to zero (FTZ)");
    }
    if bb(tiny) == 0.0 {
        return Err("subnormal inputs treated as zero (DAZ)");
    }
    // Round to nearest even: 1 + 2^-53 -> 1, 1 + 3*2^-53 -> 1 + 2^-51.
    let e53 = f64::from_bits(0x3CA0_0000_0000_0000);
    if bb(1.0f64) + bb(e53) != 1.0 || bb(1.0f64) + bb(3.0 * e53) != 1.0 + 4.0 * e53 {
        return Err("rounding mode is not round-to-nearest-even");
    }
    if bb(-1.0f64) - bb(e53) != -1.0 {
        return Err("rounding mode is not round-to-nearest-even");
    }
    // Correctly rounded division and sqrt.
    if bb(1.0f64) / bb(3.0) != f64::from_bits(0x3FD5_5555_5555_5555) || bb(2.0f64).sqrt() != std::f64::consts::SQRT_2 {
        return Err("division/sqrt not correctly rounded");
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn host_fmod(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
        a % b
    }

    #[test]
    fn fprem_matches_exact_fmod() {
        let vals = [
            1.0, -1.0, 3.5, -7.25, 1e10, -1e-10, 123456789.123, 2.0f64.powi(60), 5e-324, 1e-310, 1e300, -1e308,
            std::f64::consts::PI, 0.1, 6.0, 7.0,
        ];
        for &a in &vals {
            for &b in &vals {
                let r = fprem(a, b, false);
                // fmod is exact in every conforming libm; compare against it here (test only).
                assert_eq!(r.r.to_bits(), host_fmod(a, b).to_bits(), "fprem({a:e}, {b:e})");
            }
        }
        // Quotient bits: 7 / 2 = 3 rem 1 -> q = 3
        assert_eq!(fprem(7.0, 2.0, false), Rem { r: 1.0, q: 3 });
        assert_eq!(fprem(-7.0, 2.0, false), Rem { r: -1.0, q: 3 });
        assert_eq!(fprem(13.0, 1.0, false), Rem { r: 0.0, q: 5 });
        assert_eq!(fprem(1.0, 2.0, false), Rem { r: 1.0, q: 0 });
        // Large quotient: 2^60 / 3 -> q mod 8 exact.
        let q = (1u64 << 60) / 3;
        assert_eq!(fprem(2.0f64.powi(60), 3.0, false).q, (q & 7) as u8);
    }

    #[test]
    fn fprem1_is_ieee_remainder() {
        assert_eq!(fprem(7.0, 2.0, true), Rem { r: -1.0, q: 4 });
        assert_eq!(fprem(5.0, 2.0, true), Rem { r: 1.0, q: 2 }); // 2.5 -> 2 (even)
        assert_eq!(fprem(3.0, 2.0, true), Rem { r: -1.0, q: 2 }); // 1.5 -> 2
        assert_eq!(fprem(1.0, 4.0, true), Rem { r: 1.0, q: 0 });
        assert_eq!(fprem(3.0, 4.0, true), Rem { r: -1.0, q: 1 });
        for &(a, b) in &[(10.3, 3.0), (-10.3, 3.0), (1e20, 7.0), (5.5, -2.0)] {
            assert_eq!(fprem(a, b, true).r, libm::remainder(a, b), "{a} {b}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn nan_rules_are_host_independent() {
        let qa = f64::from_bits(0x7FF8_0000_0000_0005);
        let qb = f64::from_bits(0xFFF8_0000_0000_0009);
        let sa = f64::from_bits(0x7FF0_0000_0000_0007);
        assert_eq!(propagate_nan(qa, 1.0).to_bits(), qa.to_bits());
        assert_eq!(propagate_nan(1.0, qb).to_bits(), qb.to_bits());
        assert_eq!(propagate_nan(qa, qb).to_bits(), qb.to_bits()); // larger significand
        assert_eq!(propagate_nan(qb, qa).to_bits(), qb.to_bits());
        assert_eq!(propagate_nan(sa, 1.0).to_bits(), 0x7FF8_0000_0000_0007);
        assert_eq!(sqrt(-1.0).to_bits(), INDEFINITE.to_bits());
        assert_eq!(sin(f64::INFINITY).to_bits(), INDEFINITE.to_bits());
        assert_eq!(log2(-1.0).to_bits(), INDEFINITE.to_bits());
        assert_eq!(sin(qa).to_bits(), qa.to_bits());
    }

    #[test]
    fn host_env_is_ieee() {
        host_float_env_check().unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn accuracy_against_known_values() {
        // fdlibm is < 1 ulp; these are exact or correctly rounded reference values.
        assert_eq!(sin(0.0).to_bits(), 0);
        assert_eq!(cos(0.0), 1.0);
        assert_eq!(atan2(1.0, 1.0), std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_4);
        assert_eq!(log2(8.0), 3.0);
        assert_eq!(exp2m1(1.0), 1.0);
        assert_eq!(exp2m1(-1.0), -0.5);
        assert_eq!(log2_1p(1.0), 1.0);
        let ulp = |a: f64, b: f64| (a.to_bits() as i64 - b.to_bits() as i64).abs();
        // The f64 constants are rounded, so the exact results are themselves up to ~1 ulp away from 0.5.
        assert!(ulp(sin(std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_6), 0.5) <= 2);
        assert!(ulp(cos(std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_3), 0.5) <= 2);
        assert!(ulp(tan(std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_4), 1.0) <= 1);
        // sqrt(2) - 1 correctly rounded (the f64 expression SQRT_2 - 1.0 is 2 ulp off).
        assert!(ulp(exp2m1(0.5), f64::from_bits(0x3FDA_8279_99FC_EF32)) <= 1);
        assert!(ulp(exp2m1(-0.25), f64::from_bits(0xBFC4_5D81_9A94_B14B)) <= 1);
    }
}
```

```rs
//! x87 tests: hand-assembled snippets (iced-x86 `code_asm`), no game bytes.

use iced_x86::code_asm::*;

use crate::fpu::sw;
use crate::*;

const CODE: u32 = 0x0040_1000;
const STACK_TOP: u32 = 0x0090_0000;
const D: u32 = 0x0060_0000;

fn run_with(init: impl FnOnce(&mut GuestMemory), build: impl FnOnce(&mut CodeAssembler)) -> (Cpu, GuestMemory) {
    let mut a = CodeAssembler::new(32).unwrap();
    build(&mut a);
    a.ret().unwrap();
    let bytes = a.assemble(CODE as u64).unwrap();
    let mut mem = GuestMemory::new().unwrap();
    mem.write_bytes(CODE, &bytes);
    init(&mut mem);
    let mut cpu = Cpu::new();
    cpu.regs[ESP] = STACK_TOP;
    cpu.push32(&mut mem, layout::MAGIC_RETURN);
    cpu.eip = CODE;
    let exit = cpu.run(&mut mem, 1_000_000);
    assert_eq!(exit, CpuExit::ReturnMagic, "eip={:#x}", cpu.eip);
    (cpu, mem)
}

fn d(off: u32) -> AsmMemoryOperand {
    ptr(D as u64 + off as u64)
}

fn put_f64(m: &mut GuestMemory, off: u32, v: f64) {
    m.write_u64(D + off, v.to_bits());
}

#[test]
fn load_add_store_and_stack() {
    let (cpu, mem) = run_with(
        |m| {
            put_f64(m, 0, 1.5);
            m.write_u32(D + 8, 2.25f32.to_bits());
            m.write_u32(D + 12, (-7i32) as u32);
        },
        |a| {
            a.fld(qword_ptr(d(0))).unwrap(); // 1.5
            a.fadd(dword_ptr(d(8))).unwrap(); // 3.75
            a.fild(dword_ptr(d(12))).unwrap(); // -7, 3.75
            a.fmulp(st1, st0).unwrap(); // -26.25
            a.fld1().unwrap();
            a.fsubrp(st1, st0).unwrap(); // st1 = st0 - st1 -> 1 - (-26.25) = 27.25
            a.fst(qword_ptr(d(16))).unwrap();
            a.fstp(tword_ptr(d(32))).unwrap();
        },
    );
    assert_eq!(f64::from_bits(mem.read_u64(D + 16)), 27.25);
    assert_eq!(mem.read_u16(D + 40), 0x4003);
    assert_eq!(mem.read_u64(D + 32), 0xDA00_0000_0000_0000);
    assert_eq!(cpu.fpu.top, 0);
    assert_eq!(cpu.fpu.tags, 0xFFFF);
}

#[test]
fn ftol_truncation_and_rounding_modes() {
    // MSVC6 _ftol: fnstcw; or ah,0x0c; fldcw; fistp qword; fldcw
    let (_, mem) = run_with(
        |m| {
            put_f64(m, 0, -2.7);
            put_f64(m, 8, 2.5);
        },
        |a| {
            a.fld(qword_ptr(d(0))).unwrap();
            a.fnstcw(word_ptr(d(0x40))).unwrap();
            a.mov(ax, word_ptr(d(0x40))).unwrap();
            a.or(ah, 0x0c).unwrap();
            a.mov(word_ptr(d(0x42)), ax).unwrap();
            a.fldcw(word_ptr(d(0x42))).unwrap();
            a.fistp(qword_ptr(d(0x50))).unwrap();
            a.fldcw(word_ptr(d(0x40))).unwrap();
            // Default round-to-nearest-even: 2.5 -> 2
            a.fld(qword_ptr(d(8))).unwrap();
            a.fist(dword_ptr(d(0x60))).unwrap();
            a.frndint().unwrap();
            a.fistp(word_ptr(d(0x64))).unwrap();
            // Overflow -> integer indefinite
            a.fld(qword_ptr(d(0x70))).unwrap();
            a.fistp(word_ptr(d(0x66))).unwrap();
        },
    );
    assert_eq!(mem.read_u64(D + 0x50) as i64, -2);
    assert_eq!(mem.read_u32(D + 0x60), 2);
    assert_eq!(mem.read_u16(D + 0x64), 2);
    // d(0x70) is 0.0 (fresh memory) -> 0, not overflow; check a real overflow separately below.
    assert_eq!(mem.read_u16(D + 0x66), 0);
    let (cpu, mem) = run_with(
        |m| put_f64(m, 0, 70000.0),
        |a| {
            a.fld(qword_ptr(d(0))).unwrap();
            a.fistp(word_ptr(d(8))).unwrap();
        },
    );
    assert_eq!(mem.read_u16(D + 8), 0x8000);
    assert!(cpu.fpu.status & sw::IE != 0);
}

#[test]
fn fcomp_fnstsw_sahf_pattern() {
    // if (a < b) ebx = 1 ; if (a == a) ecx = 1 ; unordered -> PF
    let (cpu, _) = run_with(
        |m| {
            put_f64(m, 0, 1.0);
            put_f64(m, 8, 2.0);
            put_f64(m, 16, f64::NAN);
        },
        |a| {
            let mut l1 = a.create_label();
            let mut l2 = a.create_label();
            a.xor(ebx, ebx).unwrap();
            a.xor(ecx, ecx).unwrap();
            a.xor(edx, edx).unwrap();
            a.fld(qword_ptr(d(0))).unwrap();
            a.fcomp(qword_ptr(d(8))).unwrap();
            a.fnstsw(ax).unwrap();
            a.sahf().unwrap();
            a.jae(l1).unwrap();
            a.mov(ebx, 1).unwrap();
            a.set_label(&mut l1).unwrap();
            a.fld(qword_ptr(d(8))).unwrap();
            a.fld(qword_ptr(d(8))).unwrap();
            a.fcompp().unwrap();
            a.fnstsw(ax).unwrap();
            a.test(ah, 0x40).unwrap();
            a.jz(l2).unwrap();
            a.mov(ecx, 1).unwrap();
            a.set_label(&mut l2).unwrap();
            a.fld(qword_ptr(d(16))).unwrap();
            a.fld(qword_ptr(d(0))).unwrap();
            a.fxch(st0, st1).unwrap();
            a.fucompp().unwrap();
            a.fnstsw(ax).unwrap();
            a.sahf().unwrap();
            a.setp(dl).unwrap();
        },
    );
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EBX], 1);
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[ECX], 1);
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EDX], 1);
    assert_eq!(cpu.fpu.top, 0);
    assert_eq!(cpu.fpu.status & sw::IE, 0, "fucom with QNaN must not raise IE");
}

#[test]
fn constants_and_transcendentals() {
    let (_, mem) = run_with(
        |m| {
            put_f64(m, 0, 0.5);
            put_f64(m, 8, 8.0);
        },
        |a| {
            a.fldpi().unwrap();
            a.fstp(qword_ptr(d(0x20))).unwrap();
            a.fld(qword_ptr(d(0))).unwrap();
            a.fsin().unwrap();
            a.fstp(qword_ptr(d(0x28))).unwrap();
            // log2(8) * 1 via fyl2x
            a.fld1().unwrap();
            a.fld(qword_ptr(d(8))).unwrap();
            a.fyl2x().unwrap();
            a.fstp(qword_ptr(d(0x30))).unwrap();
            // 2^0.5 - 1 via f2xm1
            a.fld(qword_ptr(d(0))).unwrap();
            a.f2xm1().unwrap();
            a.fstp(qword_ptr(d(0x38))).unwrap();
            // fscale: 3 * 2^4
            a.fld(qword_ptr(d(8))).unwrap();
            a.fsqrt().unwrap(); // sqrt(8)
            a.fstp(qword_ptr(d(0x40))).unwrap();
            a.mov(dword_ptr(d(0x48)), 4).unwrap();
            a.fild(dword_ptr(d(0x48))).unwrap();
            a.mov(dword_ptr(d(0x48)), 3).unwrap();
            a.fild(dword_ptr(d(0x48))).unwrap();
            a.fscale().unwrap();
            a.fstp(qword_ptr(d(0x50))).unwrap();
            a.fstp(st0).unwrap();
            // fpatan: atan2(1, 1)
            a.fld1().unwrap();
            a.fld1().unwrap();
            a.fpatan().unwrap();
            a.fstp(qword_ptr(d(0x58))).unwrap();
        },
    );
    let f = |o: u32| f64::from_bits(mem.read_u64(D + o));
    assert_eq!(f(0x20), std::f64::consts::PI);
    assert_eq!(f(0x28), 0.5f64.sin());
    assert_eq!(f(0x30), 3.0);
    assert!((f(0x38) - (2f64.sqrt() - 1.0)).abs() < 1e-15);
    assert_eq!(f(0x40), 8f64.sqrt());
    assert_eq!(f(0x50), 48.0);
    assert_eq!(f(0x58), std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_4);
}

#[test]
fn fprem_loop_and_fxam() {
    // CRT fmod pattern: loop fprem until C2 clear.
    let (cpu, mem) = run_with(
        |m| {
            put_f64(m, 0, 3.0);
            put_f64(m, 8, 17.5);
        },
        |a| {
            let mut again = a.create_label();
            a.fld(qword_ptr(d(0))).unwrap(); // divisor
            a.fld(qword_ptr(d(8))).unwrap(); // dividend
            a.set_label(&mut again).unwrap();
            a.fprem().unwrap();
            a.fnstsw(ax).unwrap();
            a.sahf().unwrap();
            a.jp(again).unwrap();
            a.fstp(qword_ptr(d(0x10))).unwrap();
            a.fstp(st0).unwrap();
            a.fldz().unwrap();
            a.fchs().unwrap();
            a.fxam().unwrap();
            a.fnstsw(ax).unwrap();
            a.mov(ebx, eax).unwrap();
            a.fstp(st0).unwrap();
            a.fxam().unwrap(); // empty
            a.fnstsw(ax).unwrap();
        },
    );
    assert_eq!(f64::from_bits(mem.read_u64(D + 0x10)), 2.5);
    // -0: C3=1, C1=1 (sign), C2=0, C0=0
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EBX] as u16 & (sw::CC), sw::C3 | sw::C1);
    // empty: C3=1, C0=1
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EAX] as u16 & (sw::C3 | sw::C2 | sw::C0), sw::C3 | sw::C0);
    // 17.5 / 3 -> q = 5 = 0b101: C0=Q2=1, C3=Q1=0, C1=Q0=1 checked via fprem1 below.
    let (cpu, mem) = run_with(
        |m| {
            put_f64(m, 0, 3.0);
            put_f64(m, 8, 17.5);
        },
        |a| {
            a.fld(qword_ptr(d(0))).unwrap();
            a.fld(qword_ptr(d(8))).unwrap();
            a.fprem1().unwrap(); // 17.5 - 6*3 = -0.5, q = 6 = 0b110
            a.fnstsw(ax).unwrap();
            a.fstp(qword_ptr(d(0x10))).unwrap();
            a.fstp(st0).unwrap();
        },
    );
    assert_eq!(f64::from_bits(mem.read_u64(D + 0x10)), -0.5);
    let s = cpu.regs[EAX] as u16;
    assert_eq!(s & (sw::C0 | sw::C3 | sw::C1 | sw::C2), sw::C0 | sw::C3);
}

#[test]
fn fnsave_frstor_and_fnstenv() {
    let (cpu, mem) = run_with(
        |m| put_f64(m, 0, 6.5),
        |a| {
            a.fld(qword_ptr(d(0))).unwrap();
            a.fld1().unwrap();
            a.fnsave(ptr(d(0x100))).unwrap();
            // After fnsave: fninit state
            a.fnstsw(ax).unwrap();
            a.mov(ebx, eax).unwrap();
            a.frstor(ptr(d(0x100))).unwrap();
            a.faddp(st1, st0).unwrap(); // 7.5
            a.fnstenv(ptr(d(0x200))).unwrap();
            a.fstp(qword_ptr(d(8))).unwrap();
        },
    );
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EBX] & 0xFFFF, 0);
    assert_eq!(f64::from_bits(mem.read_u64(D + 8)), 7.5);
    // Saved image: CW 0x37F, TOP=6, st0 = 1.0 in 80-bit at +28.
    assert_eq!(mem.read_u16(D + 0x100), 0x037F);
    assert_eq!((mem.read_u16(D + 0x104) >> 11) & 7, 6);
    assert_eq!(mem.read_u64(D + 0x100 + 28), 0x8000_0000_0000_0000);
    assert_eq!(mem.read_u16(D + 0x100 + 36), 0x3FFF);
    // Tag word in the save image: R6 = valid (1.0), R7 = valid (6.5), others empty.
    assert_eq!(mem.read_u16(D + 0x108), 0x0FFF);
    // fnstenv: TOP = 7, one valid reg (R7), then exceptions masked.
    assert_eq!((mem.read_u16(D + 0x204) >> 11) & 7, 7);
    assert_eq!(mem.read_u16(D + 0x208), 0x3FFF);
    assert_eq!(cpu.fpu.control & 0x3F, 0x3F);
}
```

`port/crates/s3-cpu/src/jit/a64.rs`:

```rs
//! Minimal AArch64 encoder for the JIT (hand-encoded; only what `compile.rs` needs).
//!
//! Registers are numbers 0..=31; 31 means `wzr/xzr` or `sp` depending on the instruction (as in the ISA).
//! `w*` methods are 32-bit (sf = 0), `x*` methods 64-bit. Branches to labels are fixed up in [`Asm::finish`].

#![allow(dead_code)]

pub type R = u32;
pub const ZR: R = 31;
pub const SP: R = 31;

/// Condition codes.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u32)]
pub enum Cond {
    Eq = 0,
    Ne = 1,
    Hs = 2,
    Lo = 3,
    Mi = 4,
    Pl = 5,
    Vs = 6,
    Vc = 7,
    Hi = 8,
    Ls = 9,
    Ge = 10,
    Lt = 11,
    Gt = 12,
    Le = 13,
    Al = 14,
}

impl Cond {
    pub fn invert(self) -> Cond {
        // SAFETY: flipping bit 0 of 0..=13 stays inside the enum.
        unsafe { std::mem::transmute(self as u32 ^ 1) }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Label(pub u32);

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum Fix {
    /// imm26 (b / bl).
    B26,
    /// imm19 at bit 5 (b.cond, cbz, cbnz, ldr literal).
    B19,
    /// imm14 at bit 5 (tbz / tbnz).
    B14,
}

/// Code buffer with labels.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Asm {
    /// Address the code will run at (for branches to absolute addresses).
    pub base: usize,
    pub code: Vec<u32>,
    labels: Vec<Option<u32>>,
    fixups: Vec<(usize, Label, Fix)>,
}

/// N:immr:imms field (bits 22..10) of a 32-bit logical immediate, or `None` if `v` is not encodable.
pub fn logic_imm32(v: u32) -> Option<u32> {
    if v == 0 || v == u32::MAX {
        return None;
    }
    let mut size = 32u32;
    while size > 2 {
        let h = size / 2;
        let m = (1u64 << h) - 1;
        if (v as u64 & m) != ((v as u64 >> h) & m) {
            break;
        }
        size = h;
    }
    let m = if size == 32 { u32::MAX } else { (1u32 << size) - 1 };
    let elt = v & m;
    let k = elt.count_ones();
    let ones = if k == 32 { u32::MAX } else { (1u32 << k) - 1 };
    for r in 0..size {
        let rol = if r == 0 { elt } else { ((elt << r) | (elt >> (size - r))) & m };
        if rol == ones {
            let imms = ((!((size << 1) - 1)) & 0x3f) | (k - 1);
            return Some((r << 16) | (imms << 10));
        }
    }
    None
}

impl Asm {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Asm::default()
    }

    pub fn new_at(base: usize) -> Self {
        Asm { base, ..Asm::default() }
    }

    /// `b <addr>` (absolute target inside +-128 MiB).
    pub fn b_abs(&mut self, addr: usize) {
        let pc = self.base + self.code.len() * 4;
        let d = (addr as i64 - pc as i64) / 4;
        assert!((-(1 << 25)..(1 << 25)).contains(&d), "b_abs out of range");
        self.emit(0x1400_0000 | ((d as u32) & 0x03FF_FFFF));
    }

    #[inline]
```
