`port/crates/s3-cpu/src/jit_tests.rs`:

```rs
//! JIT differential tests (perf-jit): random guest programs run through the interpreter and through the JIT;
//! registers, EFLAGS, lazy-flag state, EIP, exits, retired counts and memory must be identical after every
//! budget slice. Only built on aarch64 with the `jit` feature.

use iced_x86::code_asm::*;

use crate::*;

const CODE: u32 = 0x0040_1000;
const SUBS: u32 = 0x0048_0000;
const STACK_TOP: u32 = 0x0090_0000;
const STACK_LO: u32 = 0x008F_0000;
const DATA: u32 = 0x0100_0000;
const DATA_LEN: u32 = 0x10_0000;
const MID: u32 = DATA + DATA_LEN / 2;
const CNT: u32 = DATA + DATA_LEN + 0x10;

struct Rng(u64);

impl Rng {
    fn next(&mut self) -> u64 {
        self.0 ^= self.0 << 13;
        self.0 ^= self.0 >> 7;
        self.0 ^= self.0 << 17;
        self.0
    }
    fn n(&mut self, k: u64) -> u64 {
        self.next() % k
    }
    fn u32(&mut self) -> u32 {
        // Edge values often.
        const E: [u32; 12] = [0, 1, 2, 0x7F, 0x80, 0xFF, 0x7FFF, 0x8000, 0xFFFF, 0x7FFF_FFFF, 0x8000_0000, 0xFFFF_FFFF];
        if self.n(3) == 0 {
            E[self.n(E.len() as u64) as usize]
        } else {
            self.next() as u32
        }
    }
    fn small(&mut self) -> i32 {
        self.n(256) as i32 - 128
    }
}

const DREG: [AsmRegister32; 3] = [eax, ecx, edx];
const PREG: [AsmRegister32; 4] = [ebx, esi, edi, ebp];
const AREG: [AsmRegister32; 7] = [eax, ecx, edx, ebx, esi, edi, ebp];
const R8W: [AsmRegister8; 7] = [al, cl, dl, ah, ch, dh, bl];
const R8R: [AsmRegister8; 8] = [al, cl, dl, ah, ch, dh, bl, bh];
const R16: [AsmRegister16; 3] = [ax, cx, dx];

fn pick<T: Copy>(r: &mut Rng, v: &[T]) -> T {
    v[r.n(v.len() as u64) as usize]
}

/// A memory operand that stays inside the DATA region (pointer registers stay near MID).
fn mem(r: &mut Rng) -> AsmMemoryOperand {
    let p = pick(r, &PREG);
    match r.n(10) {
        0..=5 => p + r.small(),
        6 => {
            let q = pick(r, &PREG);
            let s = [1u32, 2, 4, 8][r.n(4) as usize];
            let d = (s.wrapping_mul(MID)).wrapping_neg().wrapping_add(r.small() as u32) as i32;
            p + q * s + d
        }
        7 => {
            let q = pick(r, &PREG);
            let s = [1u32, 2, 4, 8][r.n(4) as usize];
            let d = MID.wrapping_sub(s.wrapping_mul(MID)).wrapping_add(r.small() as u32) as i32;
            q * s + d
        }
        _ => ptr((MID as i64 + r.small() as i64) as u64),
    }
    .into()
}

struct Gen {
    r: Rng,
    pushes: u32,
    subs: Vec<CodeLabel>,
    ops: u32,
}

macro_rules! alu_all {
    ($a:expr, $g:expr, $op:ident) => {{
        let g: &mut Gen = $g;
        let a: &mut CodeAssembler = $a;
        match g.r.n(13) {
            0 => a.$op(pick(&mut g.r, &DREG), pick(&mut g.r, &AREG)).unwrap(),
            1 => a.$op(pick(&mut g.r, &DREG), g.r.u32() as i32).unwrap(),
            2 => a.$op(pick(&mut g.r, &DREG), dword_ptr(mem(&mut g.r))).unwrap(),
            3 => a.$op(dword_ptr(mem(&mut g.r)), pick(&mut g.r, &AREG)).unwrap(),
            4 => a.$op(dword_ptr(mem(&mut g.r)), g.r.u32() as i32).unwrap(),
            5 => a.$op(pick(&mut g.r, &R8W), pick(&mut g.r, &R8R)).unwrap(),
            6 => a.$op(pick(&mut g.r, &R8W), g.r.u32() as i32 & 0xFF).unwrap(),
            7 => a.$op(pick(&mut g.r, &R8W), byte_ptr(mem(&mut g.r))).unwrap(),
            8 => a.$op(byte_ptr(mem(&mut g.r)), pick(&mut g.r, &R8R)).unwrap(),
            9 => a.$op(byte_ptr(mem(&mut g.r)), g.r.u32() as i32 & 0xFF).unwrap(),
            10 => a.$op(pick(&mut g.r, &R16), pick(&mut g.r, &R16)).unwrap(),
            11 => a.$op(pick(&mut g.r, &R16), g.r.u32() as i32 & 0xFFFF).unwrap(),
            _ => a.$op(word_ptr(mem(&mut g.r)), pick(&mut g.r, &R16)).unwrap(),
        }
    }};
}

macro_rules! cmp_all {
    ($a:expr, $g:expr, $op:ident) => {{
        let g: &mut Gen = $g;
        let a: &mut CodeAssembler = $a;
        match g.r.n(8) {
            0 => a.$op(pick(&mut g.r, &AREG), pick(&mut g.r, &AREG)).unwrap(),
            1 => a.$op(pick(&mut g.r, &AREG), g.r.u32() as i32).unwrap(),
            2 => a.$op(dword_ptr(mem(&mut g.r)), pick(&mut g.r, &AREG)).unwrap(),
            3 => a.$op(dword_ptr(mem(&mut g.r)), g.r.u32() as i32).unwrap(),
            4 => a.$op(pick(&mut g.r, &R8R), pick(&mut g.r, &R8R)).unwrap(),
            5 => a.$op(byte_ptr(mem(&mut g.r)), g.r.u32() as i32 & 0xFF).unwrap(),
            6 => a.$op(pick(&mut g.r, &R16), g.r.u32() as i32 & 0xFFFF).unwrap(),
            _ => a.$op(pick(&mut g.r, &R8R), g.r.u32() as i32 & 0xFF).unwrap(),
        }
    }};
}

impl Gen {
    /// One random instruction (or a small group that keeps the invariants).
    fn insn(&mut self, a: &mut CodeAssembler, depth: u32) {
        self.ops += 1;
        let r = &mut self.r;
        match r.n(60) {
            0..=3 => alu_all!(a, self, add),
            4..=6 => alu_all!(a, self, sub),
            7 => alu_all!(a, self, and),
            8 => alu_all!(a, self, or),
            9 => alu_all!(a, self, xor),
            10 => alu_all!(a, self, adc),
            11 => alu_all!(a, self, sbb),
            12..=15 => cmp_all!(a, self, cmp),
            16..=17 => cmp_all!(a, self, test),
            18..=23 => match r.n(9) {
                0 => a.mov(pick(r, &DREG), pick(r, &AREG)).unwrap(),
                1 => a.mov(pick(r, &DREG), r.u32()).unwrap(),
                2 => a.mov(pick(r, &DREG), dword_ptr(mem(r))).unwrap(),
                3 => a.mov(dword_ptr(mem(r)), pick(r, &AREG)).unwrap(),
                4 => a.mov(dword_ptr(mem(r)), r.u32()).unwrap(),
                5 => a.mov(pick(r, &R8W), byte_ptr(mem(r))).unwrap(),
                6 => a.mov(byte_ptr(mem(r)), pick(r, &R8R)).unwrap(),
                7 => a.mov(word_ptr(mem(r)), pick(r, &R16)).unwrap(),
                _ => a.mov(pick(r, &R16), word_ptr(mem(r))).unwrap(),
            },
            24 => match r.n(6) {
                0 => a.movzx(pick(r, &DREG), byte_ptr(mem(r))).unwrap(),
                1 => a.movsx(pick(r, &DREG), word_ptr(mem(r))).unwrap(),
                2 => a.movzx(pick(r, &DREG), pick(r, &R8R)).unwrap(),
                3 => a.movsx(pick(r, &DREG), pick(r, &R8R)).unwrap(),
                4 => a.movzx(pick(r, &DREG), pick(r, &R16)).unwrap(),
                _ => a.movsx(pick(r, &DREG), byte_ptr(mem(r))).unwrap(),
            },
            25 => match r.n(3) {
                0 => a.lea(pick(r, &DREG), mem(r)).unwrap(),
                1 => {
                    let p = pick(r, &PREG);
                    a.lea(p, p + r.small()).unwrap()
                }
                _ => {
                    let p = pick(r, &PREG);
                    a.lea(pick(r, &DREG), p + pick(r, &DREG) * 4 + r.small()).unwrap()
                }
            },
            26..=27 => match r.n(6) {
                0 => a.inc(pick(r, &DREG)).unwrap(),
                1 => a.dec(pick(r, &DREG)).unwrap(),
                2 => a.inc(dword_ptr(mem(r))).unwrap(),
                3 => a.dec(dword_ptr(mem(r))).unwrap(),
                4 => a.dec(pick(r, &PREG)).unwrap(),
                _ => a.inc(byte_ptr(mem(r))).unwrap(),
            },
            28 => match r.n(3) {
                0 => a.neg(pick(r, &DREG)).unwrap(),
                1 => a.not(pick(r, &DREG)).unwrap(),
                _ => a.neg(byte_ptr(mem(r))).unwrap(),
            },
            29..=31 => {
                let d = pick(r, &DREG);
                let c = [0u32, 1, 2, 7, 8, 15, 16, 24, 31, 32, 33][r.n(11) as usize];
                match r.n(9) {
                    0 => a.shl(d, c).unwrap(),
                    1 => a.shr(d, c).unwrap(),
                    2 => a.sar(d, c).unwrap(),
                    3 => a.shl(d, cl).unwrap(),
                    4 => a.shr(pick(r, &R8W), c).unwrap(),
                    5 => a.rol(d, c).unwrap(),
                    6 => a.rcr(d, 1).unwrap(),
                    7 => a.sar(pick(r, &R16), cl).unwrap(),
                    _ => a.shl(d, 1).unwrap(),
                }
            }
            32..=33 => match r.n(6) {
                0 => a.imul_2(pick(r, &DREG), pick(r, &AREG)).unwrap(),
                1 => a.imul_2(pick(r, &DREG), dword_ptr(mem(r))).unwrap(),
                2 => a.imul_3(pick(r, &DREG), pick(r, &AREG), r.u32() as i32).unwrap(),
                3 => a.imul_3(pick(r, &DREG), dword_ptr(mem(r)), r.small()).unwrap(),
                4 => a.mul(pick(r, &AREG)).unwrap(),
                _ => a.imul(dword_ptr(mem(r))).unwrap(),
            },
            34 => match r.n(3) {
                0 => a.cdq().unwrap(),
                1 => a.cwde().unwrap(),
                _ => a.nop().unwrap(),
            },
            35..=36 => {
                let d = pick(r, &R8W);
                match r.n(16) {
                    0 => a.seto(d),
                    1 => a.setno(d),
                    2 => a.setb(d),
                    3 => a.setae(d),
                    4 => a.sete(d),
                    5 => a.setne(d),
                    6 => a.setbe(d),
                    7 => a.seta(d),
                    8 => a.sets(d),
                    9 => a.setns(d),
                    10 => a.setp(d),
                    11 => a.setnp(d),
                    12 => a.setl(d),
                    13 => a.setge(d),
                    14 => a.setle(d),
                    _ => a.setg(d),
                }
                .unwrap()
            }
            37..=39 if depth == 0 => {
                // push (balanced by later pops)
                match r.n(3) {
                    0 => a.push(pick(r, &AREG)).unwrap(),
                    1 => a.push(r.u32() as i32).unwrap(),
                    _ => a.push(dword_ptr(mem(r))).unwrap(),
                }
                self.pushes += 1;
            }
            40..=41 if depth == 0 => {
                if self.pushes > 0 {
                    a.pop(pick(r, &DREG)).unwrap();
                    self.pushes -= 1;
                } else {
                    a.cmc().unwrap();
                }
            }
            42 => match r.n(8) {
                0 => {
                    a.pushfd().unwrap();
                    a.pop(eax).unwrap()
                }
                1 => a.lahf().unwrap(),
                2 => a.clc().unwrap(),
                3 => a.stc().unwrap(),
                4 => a.bt(pick(r, &DREG), r.n(32) as i32).unwrap(),
                5 => a.bswap(pick(r, &DREG)).unwrap(),
                6 => a.xchg(pick(r, &DREG), pick(r, &DREG)).unwrap(),
                _ => a.cmove(pick(r, &DREG), pick(r, &AREG)).unwrap(),
            },
            43 => {
                // Possible #DE.
                if r.n(4) == 0 {
                    a.div(ecx).unwrap();
                } else {
                    a.xor(edx, edx).unwrap();
                    a.or(ecx, 1).unwrap();
                    a.div(ecx).unwrap();
                }
            }
            44 => {
                if r.n(8) == 0 {
                    // Possible NULL fault (memory access below 64 KiB).
                    a.mov(eax, (r.n(0xF000) as u32) & !3).unwrap();
                    match r.n(3) {
                        0 => a.mov(ecx, dword_ptr(eax + 4)).unwrap(),
                        1 => a.add(dword_ptr(eax), ecx).unwrap(),
                        _ => a.push(dword_ptr(eax)).unwrap(),
                    }
                    if r.n(2) == 0 {
                        self.pushes += 0;
                    }
                } else {
                    a.cld().unwrap();
                    a.and(ecx, 7).unwrap();
                    a.rep().movsb().unwrap();
                }
            }
            45..=48 if depth < 2 => {
                // Forward conditional jump over a few instructions (new blocks, flags across blocks).
                let mut l = a.create_label();
                match r.n(10) {
                    0 => a.je(l),
                    1 => a.jne(l),
                    2 => a.jl(l),
                    3 => a.jge(l),
                    4 => a.jb(l),
                    5 => a.ja(l),
                    6 => a.jbe(l),
                    7 => a.js(l),
                    8 => a.jo(l),
                    _ => a.jmp(l),
                }
                .unwrap();
                let k = 1 + r.n(4);
                for _ in 0..k {
                    self.insn(a, depth + 1);
                }
                a.set_label(&mut l).unwrap();
                a.nop().unwrap();
            }
            49 if !self.subs.is_empty() && depth < 2 => {
                let l = self.subs[self.r.n(self.subs.len() as u64) as usize];
                a.call(l).unwrap();
            }
            // Forms the interpreter runs through its generic path (native in the JIT since perf-jit).
            50 if depth < 2 => {
                // loop / jecxz / jcxz with a bounded counter.
                let guard = r.n(3);
                let k = r.n(5) as u32 + (guard == 2) as u32;
                a.mov(ecx, k).unwrap();
                let mut top = a.create_label();
                let mut out = a.create_label();
                match guard {
                    0 => a.jecxz(out).unwrap(),
                    // `67 E3 06`: jcxz over the 6-byte loop below (iced would add a 0x66 prefix, i.e. 16-bit IP).
                    1 => a.db(&[0x67, 0xE3, 0x06]).unwrap(),
                    _ => a.nop().unwrap(),
                }
                a.set_label(&mut top).unwrap();
                a.add(eax, ebx).unwrap();
                a.xor(edx, eax).unwrap();
                a.loop_(top).unwrap();
                a.set_label(&mut out).unwrap();
                a.nop().unwrap();
            }
            51 => match r.n(4) {
                0 => a.idiv(pick(r, &AREG)).unwrap(),
                1 => a.idiv(dword_ptr(mem(r))).unwrap(),
                2 => a.div(dword_ptr(mem(r))).unwrap(),
                _ => {
                    a.cdq().unwrap();
                    a.or(ecx, 0x100).unwrap();
                    a.idiv(ecx).unwrap()
                }
            },
            52 => match r.n(5) {
                0 => a.movzx(pick(r, &R16), byte_ptr(mem(r))).unwrap(),
                1 => a.movzx(pick(r, &R16), pick(r, &R8R)).unwrap(),
                2 => a.inc(pick(r, &R8W)).unwrap(),
                3 => a.dec(pick(r, &R8W)).unwrap(),
                _ => a.neg(pick(r, &R8W)).unwrap(),
            },
            53 => match r.n(5) {
                0 => {
                    a.push(ebp).unwrap();
                    a.mov(ebp, esp).unwrap();
                    a.push(eax).unwrap();
                    a.push(ecx).unwrap();
                    a.leave().unwrap();
                }
                1 => {
                    if r.n(2) == 0 {
                        a.std().unwrap();
                    }
                    a.movsd().unwrap();
                    a.cld().unwrap();
                }
                2 => {
                    if r.n(2) == 0 {
                        a.std().unwrap();
                    }
                    match r.n(3) {
                        0 => a.movsb().unwrap(),
                        1 => a.stosd().unwrap(),
                        _ => a.stosb().unwrap(),
                    }
                    a.cld().unwrap();
                }
                3 => a.mov(pick(r, &DREG), dword_ptr(mem(r)).fs()).unwrap(),
                _ => a.mov(dword_ptr(mem(r)).fs(), pick(r, &AREG)).unwrap(),
            },
            54 => {
                let c = [0u32, 1, 2, 7, 8, 9, 15, 16, 17, 24, 31][r.n(11) as usize];
                match r.n(7) {
                    0 => a.shr(pick(r, &R16), c).unwrap(),
                    1 => a.shl(pick(r, &R16), c).unwrap(),
                    2 => a.sar(pick(r, &R16), c).unwrap(),
                    3 => a.sar(pick(r, &R8W), c).unwrap(),
                    4 => a.shl(pick(r, &R8W), c).unwrap(),
                    5 => a.shr(pick(r, &DREG), cl).unwrap(),
                    _ => a.sar(pick(r, &DREG), cl).unwrap(),
                }
            }
            _ => alu_all!(a, self, add),
        }
    }
}

struct Prog {
    bytes: Vec<u8>,
    sub_bytes: Vec<u8>,
}

fn gen_prog(seed: u64) -> Prog {
    let mut g = Gen { r: Rng(seed.wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15) | 1), pushes: 0, subs: Vec::new(), ops: 0 };
    // Subroutines (own assembler at SUBS): random body + ret, no pushes left.
    let mut sa = CodeAssembler::new(32).unwrap();
    let nsub = g.r.n(3) as usize;
    let mut starts = Vec::new();
    for _ in 0..nsub {
        let mut l = sa.create_label();
        sa.set_label(&mut l).unwrap();
        starts.push(l);
        let saved = g.pushes;
        g.pushes = 0;
        for _ in 0..(1 + g.r.n(12)) {
            g.insn(&mut sa, 1);
        }
        for _ in 0..g.pushes {
            sa.pop(edx).unwrap();
        }
        g.pushes = saved;
        if g.r.n(2) == 0 {
            sa.ret().unwrap();
        } else {
            sa.ret_1(0).unwrap();
        }
    }
    let sub_res = if nsub > 0 {
        sa.assemble_options(SUBS as u64, iced_x86::BlockEncoderOptions::RETURN_NEW_INSTRUCTION_OFFSETS).unwrap()
    } else {
        sa.nop().unwrap();
        sa.assemble_options(SUBS as u64, iced_x86::BlockEncoderOptions::RETURN_NEW_INSTRUCTION_OFFSETS).unwrap()
    };
    let sub_addrs: Vec<u64> = starts.iter().map(|l| sub_res.label_ip(l).unwrap()).collect();
    let sub_bytes = sub_res.inner.code_buffer.clone();

    let mut a = CodeAssembler::new(32).unwrap();
    // Calls to the subroutines use their absolute addresses (`call rel32`).
    let iters = 1 + g.r.n(12) as u32;
    a.mov(dword_ptr(CNT as u64), iters).unwrap();
    let mut top = a.create_label();
    a.set_label(&mut top).unwrap();
    let body = 1 + g.r.n(48);
    for _ in 0..body {
        if !sub_addrs.is_empty() && g.r.n(16) == 0 {
            let t = sub_addrs[g.r.n(sub_addrs.len() as u64) as usize];
            a.call(t).unwrap();
        } else {
            g.insn(&mut a, 0);
        }
    }
    for _ in 0..g.pushes {
        a.pop(edx).unwrap();
    }
    g.pushes = 0;
    match g.r.n(3) {
        0 => {
            a.dec(dword_ptr(CNT as u64)).unwrap();
            a.jne(top).unwrap();
        }
        1 => {
            a.sub(dword_ptr(CNT as u64), 1).unwrap();
            a.jg(top).unwrap();
        }
        _ => {
            a.mov(eax, dword_ptr(CNT as u64)).unwrap();
            a.dec(eax).unwrap();
            a.mov(dword_ptr(CNT as u64), eax).unwrap();
            a.test(eax, eax).unwrap();
            a.jne(top).unwrap();
        }
    }
    a.ret().unwrap();
    let bytes = a.assemble(CODE as u64).unwrap();
    Prog { bytes, sub_bytes }
}

fn machine(p: &Prog, seed: u64) -> (Cpu, GuestMemory) {
    let mut mem = GuestMemory::new().unwrap();
    mem.write_bytes(CODE, &p.bytes);
    mem.write_bytes(SUBS, &p.sub_bytes);
    let mut r = Rng(seed ^ 0x5555_AAAA_1234_5678);
    let mut fill = vec![0u8; DATA_LEN as usize];
    for c in fill.chunks_mut(8) {
        let v = r.next().to_le_bytes();
        c.copy_from_slice(&v[..c.len()]);
    }
    mem.write_bytes(DATA, &fill);
    let mut cpu = Cpu::new();
    for (i, reg) in cpu.regs.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        *reg = match i {
            EBX | ESI | EDI | EBP => MID.wrapping_add(r.n(512) as u32).wrapping_sub(256),
            _ => r.u32(),
        };
    }
    cpu.regs[ESP] = STACK_TOP;
    cpu.push32(&mut mem, layout::MAGIC_RETURN);
    cpu.eip = CODE;
    cpu.set_eflags(0x202 | (r.next() as u32 & fl::STATUS));
    cpu.fs_base = r.n(64) as u32 * 4;
    (cpu, mem)
}

/// Observable CPU state (lazy fields only where they are observable).
fn state(c: &Cpu) -> String {
    let lazy = if c.lk == flags::lk::NONE || c.lk == flags::lk::LOGIC {
        String::new()
    } else {
        format!(
            " lk={} lsz={} la={:#x} lb={:#x} lr={:#x} lcf={}",
            c.lk,
            c.lsz,
            c.la,
            c.lb,
            c.lr,
            if c.lk >= 4 { c.lcf } else { 0 }
        )
    };
    format!(
        "regs={:08x?} eip={:#x} eflags={:#x} insns={} fs={:#x}{lazy}",
        c.regs,
        c.eip,
        c.eflags(),
        c.instructions,
        c.fs_base
    )
}

fn compare_mem(a: &GuestMemory, b: &GuestMemory) -> Option<String> {
    for (lo, len) in [(DATA, DATA_LEN + 0x100), (STACK_LO, STACK_TOP - STACK_LO)] {
        let x = a.slice(lo, len as usize);
        let y = b.slice(lo, len as usize);
        if x != y {
            let i = x.iter().zip(y).position(|(p, q)| p != q).unwrap();
            return Some(format!("memory differs at {:#x}: {:#x} vs {:#x}", lo as usize + i, x[i], y[i]));
        }
    }
    None
}

/// Run program `seed` on the interpreter and on the JIT with the same budget slices; panic on any difference.
fn diff_one(seed: u64, thr: u64, slices: bool) -> (u64, usize) {
    let p = gen_prog(seed);
    let (mut ci, mut mi) = machine(&p, seed);
    let (mut cj, mut mj) = machine(&p, seed);
    ci.set_jit(Some(false));
    cj.set_jit(Some(true));
    cj.set_jit_threshold(Some(thr));
    let mut r = Rng(seed ^ 0xABCD);
    for step in 0..100_000 {
        let big = r.n(4) == 0;
        let mut budget = if slices { 1 + r.n(if big { 400 } else { 40 }) } else { 5_000_000 };
        if std::env::var_os("JIT_STEP1").is_some() {
            budget = 1;
        }
        if std::env::var_os("JIT_VERBOSE").is_some_and(|v| v == "2") {
            eprintln!("  step {step} budget {budget} eip {:#x} {}", ci.eip, state(&ci));
        }
        let ei = ci.run(&mut mi, budget);
        if std::env::var_os("JIT_VERBOSE").is_some_and(|v| v == "2") {
            eprintln!("  interp done: {ei:?}");
        }
        let ej = cj.run(&mut mj, budget);
        let (s_i, s_j) = (state(&ci), state(&cj));
        if ei != ej || s_i != s_j {
            panic!("seed {seed} thr {thr} step {step} budget {budget}:\n interp {ei:?} {s_i}\n jit    {ej:?} {s_j}");
        }
        if let Some(d) = compare_mem(&mi, &mj) {
            panic!("seed {seed} thr {thr} step {step}: {d}");
        }
        // Generator slips (e.g. a jump into zero-filled memory) can run forever; both sides agreed so far.
        if ei != CpuExit::Budget || ci.instructions > 30_000_000 {
            break;
        }
    }
    (ci.instructions, cj.cache.jit_blocks())
}

#[test]
fn jit_matches_interpreter_on_random_programs() {
    let mut insns = 0;
    let mut compiled = 0;
    // `JIT_SEEDS=a-b` picks the seed range (debugging), `JIT_VERBOSE=1` prints each seed first.
    let (lo, hi) = std::env::var("JIT_SEEDS")
        .ok()
        .and_then(|v| v.split_once('-').map(|(a, b)| (a.parse().unwrap(), b.parse().unwrap())))
        .unwrap_or((1u64, 1000u64));
    let verbose = std::env::var_os("JIT_VERBOSE").is_some();
    for seed in lo..=hi {
        for (thr, slices) in [(0, false), (0, true), (2, true)] {
            if verbose {
                eprintln!("seed {seed} thr {thr} slices {slices}");
            }
            let (n, c) = diff_one(seed, thr, slices);
            insns += n;
            compiled += c;
        }
    }
    assert!(compiled > 1000, "too few compiled blocks: {compiled}");
    eprintln!("jit diff: {insns} instructions, {compiled} compiled blocks");
}

/// Hooks and native blocks are still entered at their addresses (never inside JIT-linked code).
#[test]
fn jit_respects_hooks_natives_and_invalidation() {
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
    static CALLS: [AtomicU64; 2] = [AtomicU64::new(0), AtomicU64::new(0)];
    fn decline0(_: &mut Cpu, _: &mut GuestMemory, _: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        CALLS[0].fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        None
    }
    fn decline1(_: &mut Cpu, _: &mut GuestMemory, _: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        CALLS[1].fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        None
    }
    // Loop: top: add eax, ecx ; [mid:] xor edx, eax ; dec ecx ; jnz top ; ret
    let mut a = CodeAssembler::new(32).unwrap();
    let mut top = a.create_label();
    let mut mid = a.create_label();
    a.mov(ecx, 1000).unwrap();
    a.set_label(&mut top).unwrap();
    a.add(eax, ecx).unwrap();
    a.set_label(&mut mid).unwrap();
    a.xor(edx, eax).unwrap();
    a.dec(ecx).unwrap();
    a.jne(top).unwrap();
    a.ret().unwrap();
    let res = a.assemble_options(CODE as u64, iced_x86::BlockEncoderOptions::RETURN_NEW_INSTRUCTION_OFFSETS).unwrap();
    let mid_ip = res.label_ip(&mid).unwrap() as u32;
    let top_ip = res.label_ip(&top).unwrap() as u32;
    let bytes = res.inner.code_buffer.clone();
    let p = Prog { bytes, sub_bytes: vec![0x90] };
    for (k, jit) in [false, true].into_iter().enumerate() {
        let (mut c, mut m) = machine(&p, 7);
        c.set_jit(Some(jit));
        c.set_jit_threshold(Some(0));
        let mut nb = NativeBlocks::new();
        let f: NativeFn = if k == 0 { decline0 } else { decline1 };
        nb.insert(top_ip, NativeBlock { name: "t", len: 2, hash: code_hash(m.slice(top_ip, 2)), f });
        c.set_native_blocks(Some(std::sync::Arc::new(nb)));
        let mut hooks = HookAddrs::new();
        hooks.insert(mid_ip);
        c.set_hooks(Some(std::sync::Arc::new(hooks)));
        let run_all = |c: &mut Cpu, m: &mut GuestMemory| {
            let mut hits = 0;
            loop {
                match c.run(m, 1_000_000) {
                    CpuExit::Hook(e) => {
                        assert_eq!(e, mid_ip);
                        hits += 1;
                        c.skip_hook_once(e);
                    }
                    CpuExit::ReturnMagic => break hits,
                    e => panic!("{e:?}"),
                }
            }
        };
        assert_eq!(run_all(&mut c, &mut m), 1000, "jit={jit}");
        assert_eq!(CALLS[k].load(Ordering::Relaxed), 999, "jit={jit}"); // the first pass enters `top` mid-block
                                                                        // Self-modifying code: patch `add eax, ecx` (01 c8) into `sub eax, ecx` (29 c8), invalidate, rerun.
        let before = c.regs[EAX];
        m.write_bytes(top_ip, &[0x29]);
        c.invalidate_range(top_ip, 1);
        c.eip = CODE;
        c.regs[ESP] = STACK_TOP - 4;
        m.write_u32(STACK_TOP - 4, layout::MAGIC_RETURN);
        assert_eq!(run_all(&mut c, &mut m), 1000, "jit={jit}");
        if jit {
            assert!(c.cache.jit_blocks() > 0);
        }
        let mut expect = before;
        for i in (1..=1000u32).rev() {
            expect = expect.wrapping_sub(i);
        }
        assert_eq!(c.regs[EAX], expect, "jit={jit}");
    }
}

/// A native fast path that sometimes accepts: JIT (native stub at the block entry) and interpreter agree after
/// every budget slice, including slices that end right before the native block.
#[test]
fn jit_native_stub_matches_interpreter() {
    fn add_native(cpu: &mut Cpu, _: &mut GuestMemory, budget: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        if std::env::var_os("JIT_VERBOSE").is_some() {
            eprintln!(
                "  native jit={} insns={} budget={budget} ecx={:#x}",
                cpu.cache.jit_mode, cpu.instructions, cpu.regs[ECX]
            );
        }
        if cpu.regs[ECX] % 3 != 0 {
            return None;
        }
        cpu.regs[EAX] = cpu.alu_add(cpu.regs[EAX], cpu.regs[ECX], 0, 4);
        cpu.eip += 2;
        Some(1)
    }
    let mut a = CodeAssembler::new(32).unwrap();
    let mut top = a.create_label();
    a.mov(ecx, 3000).unwrap();
    a.set_label(&mut top).unwrap();
    a.add(eax, ecx).unwrap();
    a.xor(edx, eax).unwrap();
    a.dec(ecx).unwrap();
    a.jne(top).unwrap();
    a.ret().unwrap();
    let res = a.assemble_options(CODE as u64, iced_x86::BlockEncoderOptions::RETURN_NEW_INSTRUCTION_OFFSETS).unwrap();
    let top_ip = res.label_ip(&top).unwrap() as u32;
    let p = Prog { bytes: res.inner.code_buffer.clone(), sub_bytes: vec![0x90] };
    let mut cpus = Vec::new();
    for jit in [false, true] {
        let (mut c, m) = machine(&p, 11);
        c.set_jit(Some(jit));
        c.set_jit_threshold(Some(0));
        let mut nb = NativeBlocks::new();
        nb.insert(top_ip, NativeBlock { name: "add", len: 2, hash: code_hash(m.slice(top_ip, 2)), f: add_native });
        c.set_native_blocks(Some(std::sync::Arc::new(nb)));
        cpus.push((c, m));
    }
    let mut r = Rng(99);
    loop {
        let budget = 1 + r.n(30);
        let (a, b) = cpus.split_at_mut(1);
        let e0 = a[0].0.run(&mut a[0].1, budget);
        let e1 = b[0].0.run(&mut b[0].1, budget);
        if std::env::var_os("JIT_VERBOSE").is_some() {
            eprintln!("budget {budget}: {e0:?} {}\n           {e1:?} {}", state(&a[0].0), state(&b[0].0));
        }
        assert_eq!(e0, e1);
        assert_eq!(state(&a[0].0), state(&b[0].0));
        if e0 != CpuExit::Budget {
            break;
        }
    }
    assert!(cpus[1].0.cache.jit_blocks() > 0);
}

```

`port/crates/s3-cpu/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! x86-32 interpreter for the Settlers III port.
//!
//! - Decoding: `iced-x86` (32-bit mode). Decoded instructions are cached per *basic block* keyed by the start
//!   EIP ([`DecodeCache`]); a block ends at the first control-flow instruction or after
//!   [`MAX_BLOCK_INSNS`] instructions. [`Cpu::invalidate_range`] drops blocks overlapping written code.
//! - Execution: [`Cpu::run`] executes until the instruction budget is exhausted or something needs the host
//!   (EIP enters the thunk page, the magic return address is reached, a fault, `int n`, `hlt`). Inside a block
//!   the handlers of `fast.rs` tail-call each other (threaded code); see `docs/porting/cpu.md`.
//! - Flags are lazy (`flags.rs`): read them with [`Cpu::eflags`], write with [`Cpu::set_eflags`].
//! - Memory is flat; only FS/GS segment overrides add a base (`fs_base` = TEB).
//! - Accesses to guest addresses below `layout::NULL_GUARD_END` (64 KiB) raise
//!   `FaultKind::AccessViolation`, like a NULL dereference on Windows.
//! - x87 FPU lives in [`fpu`]; anything not handled by the integer core is offered to `fpu::exec`.

pub mod fpu;

mod exec;
mod fast;
mod flags;
#[cfg(all(feature = "jit", target_arch = "aarch64"))]
mod jit;

#[cfg(all(test, target_arch = "x86_64"))]
mod diff_tests;
#[cfg(all(test, feature = "jit", target_arch = "aarch64"))]
mod jit_tests;
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::hash::{BuildHasherDefault, Hasher};

use iced_x86::{Code, Decoder, DecoderOptions, FlowControl, Instruction};
pub use s3_mem::{layout, GuestMemory};

pub use fpu::Fpu;

/// Register indices into [`Cpu::regs`] (x86 encoding order).
pub const EAX: usize = 0;
pub const ECX: usize = 1;
pub const EDX: usize = 2;
pub const EBX: usize = 3;
pub const ESP: usize = 4;
pub const EBP: usize = 5;
pub const ESI: usize = 6;
pub const EDI: usize = 7;

/// EFLAGS bits.
pub mod fl {
    pub const CF: u32 = 1 << 0;
    pub const PF: u32 = 1 << 2;
    pub const AF: u32 = 1 << 4;
    pub const ZF: u32 = 1 << 6;
    pub const SF: u32 = 1 << 7;
    pub const TF: u32 = 1 << 8;
    pub const IF: u32 = 1 << 9;
    pub const DF: u32 = 1 << 10;
    pub const OF: u32 = 1 << 11;
    pub const ID: u32 = 1 << 21;
    /// Arithmetic status flags.
    pub const STATUS: u32 = CF | PF | AF | ZF | SF | OF;
}

/// Maximum instructions per decoded block.
pub const MAX_BLOCK_INSNS: usize = 64;

/// Why the CPU faulted.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FaultKind {
    /// Undecodable bytes or `ud2`.
    InvalidOpcode,
    /// Valid instruction the interpreter does not implement yet (`detail` names it).
    Unimplemented,
    /// `div`/`idiv` by zero or quotient overflow (#DE).
    DivideError,
    /// Access to an address in the NULL guard (`addr`, `write`).
    AccessViolation { addr: u32, write: bool },
    /// Privileged / unsupported system instruction.
    GeneralProtection,
}

/// Why [`Cpu::run`] returned.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum CpuExit {
    /// EIP is inside the thunk page; the value is EIP (the HLE function's address). ESP points at the
    /// guest return address, arguments follow.
    Thunk(u32),
    /// EIP reached [`layout::MAGIC_RETURN`] (a host->guest call returned).
    ReturnMagic,
    /// The instruction budget ran out.
    Budget,
    /// `hlt` executed.
    Halt,
    /// CPU exception. EIP still points at the faulting instruction.
    Fault { eip: u32, kind: FaultKind, detail: String },
    /// `int n` (`int3` => 3). EIP points after the instruction.
    Interrupt(u8),
    /// EIP reached a registered hook address ([`Cpu::set_hooks`]); nothing at that address has executed yet.
    /// The host runs its hook, then either resumes at the same EIP after [`Cpu::skip_hook_once`] (run the
    /// original code) or redirects EIP itself.
    Hook(u32),
}

/// Guest addresses that stop execution with [`CpuExit::Hook`] (shared by all CPUs of a machine).
///
/// Decoded blocks end *before* any hooked address, so a hooked address is always a block start and the check
/// costs one byte compare per executed block (`Block::hooked`). Changing the set requires clearing the decode
/// caches ([`Cpu::set_hooks`] does that).
pub type HookAddrs = std::collections::HashSet<u32>;

/// Native replacement of a guest code region ("fast path"), see [`NativeBlock`].
///
/// Called at the start of the block at the registered address with the remaining instruction budget. It either
/// declines (`None`: nothing changed, the interpreter runs the original code) or runs the region natively and
/// returns `Some(k)`: the number of guest instructions the original code would have retired (`k <= budget`),
/// with registers, EFLAGS, memory and EIP exactly as the original code leaves them at that point. It must stop at
/// a point the original code passes through (e.g. a loop head) and must decline instead of faulting.
pub type NativeFn = fn(&mut Cpu, &mut GuestMemory, u64) -> Option<u64>;

/// A native fast path for the guest code at a fixed address (registered per exe by the host, e.g. s3-mods).
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct NativeBlock {
    pub name: &'static str,
    /// Length of the guest code region the fast path replaces (from the start address).
    pub len: u32,
    /// [`code_hash`] of those bytes; the fast path is used only if it matches when the block is decoded (so no
    /// game code needs to be stored in our sources).
    pub hash: u64,
    pub f: NativeFn,
}

/// FNV-1a 64-bit hash of guest code bytes (for [`NativeBlock::hash`]).
pub fn code_hash(b: &[u8]) -> u64 {
    let mut h: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;
    for &x in b {
        h ^= x as u64;
        h = h.wrapping_mul(0x0000_0100_0000_01B3);
    }
    h
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for NativeBlock {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "NativeBlock({})", self.name)
    }
}

/// Native fast paths by guest start address.
pub type NativeBlocks = HashMap<u32, NativeBlock>;

/// Register snapshot (for host->guest calls, thread switches and SEH `CONTEXT`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct Context {
    pub regs: [u32; 8],
    pub eip: u32,
    pub eflags: u32,
}

/// A decoded basic block.
///
/// `repr(C)` + 64-byte alignment: the fields the run loop reads at every block entry (`succ_eip` ..
/// `special`) share one cache line. Blocks are boxed (stable addresses) so chaining can use pointers.
#[derive(Debug)]
#[repr(C, align(64))]
pub struct Block {
    /// Block chaining: the last two successors seen after this block, start EIP (`u32::MAX` = empty; it was 0
    /// before 2026-11-07, so a jump to EIP 0 matched an empty slot and dereferenced a null block pointer) and
    /// block (pointer into the owning cache's arena). Cleared whenever blocks are dropped (`invalidate_range`).
    succ_eip: [u32; 2],
    succ_blk: [*mut Block; 2],
    /// Times this block was entered (profiling; see [`DecodeCache::profile`]).
    pub entries: u64,
    /// Native fast path for this block's start address (see [`NativeFn`]).
    native: Option<NativeFn>,
    /// `ops.as_ptr()`.
    op0: *const fast::Op,
    /// Address after the last instruction.
    pub end: u32,
    /// Number of instructions (`insns.len()`).
    n: u32,
    /// `hooked || native.is_some()` (one test per block entry on the common path).
    special: bool,
    /// `start` is a hook address (see [`HookAddrs`]).
    pub hooked: bool,
    /// Handler + pre-decoded operands per instruction (threaded dispatch, see `fast.rs`), plus a final
    /// `fast::block_end` sentinel (so `ops.len() == insns.len() + 1`).
    ops: Box<[fast::Op]>,
    pub start: u32,
    pub insns: Vec<Instruction>,
    /// End of the guest code covered by `native` (for invalidation; 0 = none).
    native_end: u32,
    /// JIT code address (0 = not compiled yet, 1 = never compile; see `jit/mod.rs`).
    jit: usize,
}

// SAFETY: the raw pointers (`succ_blk`, `op0`) only point into the cache that owns this block (its arena and its
// own `ops`); a cache and its CPU move between host threads as a whole and are never shared.
unsafe impl Send for Block {}
unsafe impl Sync for Block {}

#[derive(Default)]
struct AddrHasher(u64);

impl Hasher for AddrHasher {
    fn finish(&self) -> u64 {
        self.0
    }
    fn write(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) {
        for &b in bytes {
            self.0 = (self.0 << 8) | b as u64;
        }
    }
    fn write_u32(&mut self, v: u32) {
        self.0 = (v as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
    }
}

/// Entries in the direct-mapped first-level lookup (power of two).
const L1_SIZE: usize = 8192;

/// Decoded-block cache keyed by start EIP.
///
/// Blocks live in an arena (`Vec<Block>`); a `HashMap` maps start EIP -> arena index and a direct-mapped
/// array (`l1`, indexed by low EIP bits) short-cuts the common lookups. `Cpu::run` moves the cache out of the
/// `Cpu` while executing, so instructions are borrowed straight from the arena (no refcounting per block).
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct DecodeCache {
    blocks: Vec<Box<Block>>,
    map: HashMap<u32, u32, BuildHasherDefault<AddrHasher>>,
    /// `(eip, arena index + 1)`; index 0 = empty. Allocated lazily (so `Default` is allocation-free).
    l1: Vec<(u32, u32)>,
    /// Use only the generic `exec::step` handler (tests / debugging; see `Cpu::set_generic_only`).
    generic_only: bool,
    /// Hook addresses (blocks are split before them and flagged).
    hooks: Option<std::sync::Arc<HookAddrs>>,
    /// Native fast paths (looked up when a block is decoded).
    natives: Option<std::sync::Arc<NativeBlocks>>,
    /// JIT state (code arena, links), created on the first compile.
    #[cfg(all(feature = "jit", target_arch = "aarch64"))]
    jit: Option<Box<jit::Jit>>,
    /// Per-CPU JIT switch: 0 = global setting (`S3_JIT` / [`set_jit_enabled`]), 1 = off, 2 = on.
    jit_mode: u8,
    /// Block entries before compiling (`None` = default `jit::THRESHOLD`).
    jit_thr: Option<u64>,
}

impl DecodeCache {
    /// Number of cached blocks.
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.blocks.len()
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.blocks.is_empty()
    }

    /// Drop everything.
    pub fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.blocks.clear();
        self.map.clear();
        self.l1.clear();
        #[cfg(all(feature = "jit", target_arch = "aarch64"))]
        if let Some(j) = &mut self.jit {
            j.reset();
        }
    }

    /// Drop blocks overlapping `[start, start+len)`.
    pub fn invalidate_range(&mut self, start: u32, len: u32) {
        let end = start as u64 + len as u64;
        let before = self.blocks.len();
        self.blocks.retain(|b| !((b.start as u64) < end && (b.end.max(b.native_end) as u64) > start as u64));
        if self.blocks.len() != before {
            self.map.clear();
            for (i, b) in self.blocks.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                self.map.insert(b.start, i as u32);
                b.succ_eip = [u32::MAX; 2];
                b.succ_blk = [std::ptr::null_mut(); 2];
            }
            self.l1.clear();
            // JIT: compiled blocks branch to each other directly, so drop all JIT code (rare: S3.EXE has no
            // self-modifying code).
            #[cfg(all(feature = "jit", target_arch = "aarch64"))]
            if let Some(j) = &mut self.jit {
                for b in self.blocks.iter_mut() {
                    b.jit = 0;
                }
                j.reset();
            }
        }
    }

    /// Number of blocks with JIT code (statistics).
    pub fn jit_blocks(&self) -> usize {
        self.blocks.iter().filter(|b| b.jit > 1).count()
    }

    /// Arena index of the block starting at `eip`, decoding it if needed.
    #[inline(always)]
    fn lookup(&mut self, eip: u32, mem: &GuestMemory) -> Result<usize, CpuExit> {
        if self.l1.is_empty() {
            self.l1 = vec![(0, 0); L1_SIZE];
        }
        let slot = (eip as usize ^ (eip as usize >> 13)) & (L1_SIZE - 1);
        let (tag, idx) = self.l1[slot];
        if tag == eip && idx != 0 {
            return Ok(idx as usize - 1);
        }
        self.lookup_slow(eip, slot, mem)
    }

    /// [`DecodeCache::lookup`] after an L1 miss: hash map, else decode the block.
    #[inline(never)]
    fn lookup_slow(&mut self, eip: u32, slot: usize, mem: &GuestMemory) -> Result<usize, CpuExit> {
        let idx = match self.map.get(&eip) {
            Some(&i) => i as usize,
            None => {
                let mut b = decode_block(eip, mem, self.generic_only, self.hooks.as_deref())?;
                if let Some(nb) = self.natives.as_ref().and_then(|n| n.get(&eip)) {
                    if code_hash(mem.slice(eip, nb.len as usize)) == nb.hash {
                        b.native = Some(nb.f);
                        b.native_end = eip.wrapping_add(nb.len);
                        b.special = true;
                    }
                }
                self.blocks.push(Box::new(b));
                let i = self.blocks.len() - 1;
                self.map.insert(eip, i as u32);
                i
            }
        };
        self.l1[slot] = (eip, idx as u32 + 1);
        Ok(idx)
    }

    /// Profile: `(start, instruction count, entries)` of every cached block (entries since decode).
    pub fn profile(&self) -> Vec<(u32, u32, u64)> {
        self.blocks.iter().map(|b| (b.start, b.insns.len() as u32, b.entries)).collect()
    }

    /// Disassembly of the `top` blocks with most executed instructions; instructions that use the generic
    /// (slow) handler are marked `*` (profiling aid).
    pub fn profile_disasm(&self, top: usize) -> String {
        use iced_x86::Formatter;
        let mut v: Vec<&Block> = self.blocks.iter().map(|b| &**b).filter(|b| b.entries > 0).collect();
        v.sort_by_key(|b| std::cmp::Reverse(b.entries * b.insns.len() as u64));
        let mut f = iced_x86::IntelFormatter::new();
        let mut out = String::new();
        for b in v.into_iter().take(top) {
            out.push_str(&format!("block {:#x} entries {} len {}\n", b.start, b.entries, b.insns.len()));
            for (ins, op) in b.insns.iter().zip(&b.ops) {
                let mut t = String::new();
                f.format(ins, &mut t);
                let g = if op.h as usize == fast::generic as fast::Handler as usize { '*' } else { ' ' };
                out.push_str(&format!("  {g} {:#x} {t}\n", ins.ip32()));
            }
        }
        out
    }

    /// Executed instruction forms (mnemonic + operand kinds, `*` = generic handler), weighted by block entries.
    pub fn profile_forms(&self) -> Vec<(String, u64)> {
        let mut m: HashMap<String, u64> = HashMap::new();
        for b in self.blocks.iter().filter(|b| b.entries > 0) {
            for (ins, op) in b.insns.iter().zip(&b.ops) {
                *m.entry(form_key(ins, op)).or_default() += b.entries;
            }
        }
        let mut v: Vec<_> = m.into_iter().collect();
        v.sort_by_key(|e| std::cmp::Reverse(e.1));
        v
    }

    /// Adjacent instruction pairs inside blocks (`"form ; form"`, same keys as [`DecodeCache::profile_forms`]),
    /// weighted by block entries: candidates for superinstructions. The first entry is `"#blocks"` with the total
    /// block entries (average executed block length = total instructions / that).
    pub fn profile_pairs(&self) -> Vec<(String, u64)> {
        let mut m: HashMap<String, u64> = HashMap::new();
        let mut blocks = 0u64;
        for b in self.blocks.iter().filter(|b| b.entries > 0) {
            blocks += b.entries;
            let keys: Vec<String> = b.insns.iter().zip(&b.ops).map(|(i, o)| form_key(i, o)).collect();
            for w in keys.windows(2) {
                *m.entry(format!("{} ; {}", w[0], w[1])).or_default() += b.entries;
            }
        }
        let mut v: Vec<_> = m.into_iter().collect();
        v.sort_by_key(|e| std::cmp::Reverse(e.1));
        v.insert(0, ("#blocks".into(), blocks));
        v
    }

    /// Zero all block entry counters.
    pub fn reset_profile(&mut self) {
        for b in &mut self.blocks {
            b.entries = 0;
        }
    }

    /// The block starting at `eip`, if it is cached.
    pub fn get(&self, eip: u32) -> Option<&Block> {
        self.map.get(&eip).map(|&i| &*self.blocks[i as usize])
    }
}

/// Profile key of one instruction form: `*` (generic handler) or ` `, mnemonic, operand kinds.
pub(crate) fn form_key(ins: &Instruction, op: &fast::Op) -> String {
    let g = if op.h as usize == fast::generic as fast::Handler as usize { "*" } else { " " };
    let mut k = format!("{g}{:?}", ins.mnemonic());
    for i in 0..ins.op_count() {
        let kind = ins.op_kind(i);
        let d = match kind {
            iced_x86::OpKind::Register => format!("r{}", ins.op_register(i).size() * 8),
            iced_x86::OpKind::Memory => format!("m{}", ins.memory_size().size() * 8),
            _ => format!("{kind:?}"),
        };
        k.push(' ');
        k.push_str(&d);
    }
    k
}

fn decode_block(eip: u32, mem: &GuestMemory, generic_only: bool, hooks: Option<&HookAddrs>) -> Result<Block, CpuExit> {
    let avail = (layout::THUNK_BASE as u64).saturating_sub(eip as u64).min(16 * MAX_BLOCK_INSNS as u64) as usize;
    let bytes = mem.slice(eip, avail.max(1));
    let mut dec = Decoder::with_ip(32, bytes, eip as u64, DecoderOptions::NONE);
    let mut insns = Vec::with_capacity(8);
    let mut ops = Vec::with_capacity(8);
    let mut end = eip;
    while dec.can_decode() && insns.len() < MAX_BLOCK_INSNS {
        let ins = dec.decode();
        if ins.code() == Code::INVALID {
            if insns.is_empty() {
                return Err(CpuExit::Fault {
                    eip,
                    kind: FaultKind::InvalidOpcode,
                    detail: format!("bytes {:02x?}", &bytes[..bytes.len().min(8)]),
                });
            }
            break;
        }
        end = ins.next_ip() as u32;
        let flow = ins.flow_control();
        ops.push(if generic_only { fast::select_generic(&ins) } else { fast::select(&ins) });
        insns.push(ins);
        if flow != FlowControl::Next {
            break;
        }
        // Never let a block run into the thunk page.
        if end >= layout::THUNK_BASE {
            break;
        }
        // A hooked address must start its own block.
        if let Some(h) = hooks {
            if h.contains(&end) {
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    if insns.is_empty() {
        return Err(CpuExit::Fault { eip, kind: FaultKind::InvalidOpcode, detail: "truncated".into() });
    }
    insns.shrink_to_fit();
    for (op, ins) in ops.iter_mut().zip(&insns) {
        if op.h as usize == fast::generic as fast::Handler as usize {
            op.set_ins(ins);
        }
    }
    // Superinstruction: a compare right before the block-ending `jcc` (see `fast::cmp_jcc`).
    let k = insns.len();
    if !generic_only && k >= 2 && fast::is_fast_jcc(&insns[k - 1]) {
        let g = fast::generic as fast::Handler as usize;
        if ops[k - 2].h as usize != g {
            if let Some(h) = fast::fuse_cmp_jcc(&insns[k - 2], insns[k - 1].condition_code()) {
                ops[k - 2].h = h;
            }
        }
    }
    // Sentinel: the handlers dispatch to `op + 1` after each instruction (see `fast::next`).
    let mut sentinel = fast::select_generic(&insns[insns.len() - 1]);
    sentinel.h = fast::block_end;
    ops.push(sentinel);
    let hooked = hooks.is_some_and(|h| h.contains(&eip));
    let n = insns.len() as u32;
    let ops = ops.into_boxed_slice();
    Ok(Block {
        start: eip,
        end,
        n,
        insns,
        op0: ops.as_ptr(),
        ops,
        hooked,
        special: hooked,
        entries: 0,
        native: None,
        native_end: 0,
        jit: 0,
        succ_eip: [u32::MAX; 2],
        succ_blk: [std::ptr::null_mut(); 2],
    })
}

/// Compile the block `bp` (JIT); its code address, or 0 if it will not be compiled.
///
/// # Safety
/// `bp` must be a block of `cache`.
#[cfg(all(feature = "jit", target_arch = "aarch64"))]
#[cold]
#[inline(never)]
unsafe fn jit_compile(cache: &mut DecodeCache, bp: *mut Block) -> usize {
    // SAFETY: see the function contract.
    let blk = unsafe { &mut *bp };
    if cache.jit.is_none() {
        cache.jit = jit::Jit::new();
    }
    let Some(j) = cache.jit.as_mut() else {
        blk.jit = 1;
        return 0;
    };
    let (entry, body) = match j.compile(blk) {
        Some(c) => c,
        None => {
            // Arena full: drop all JIT code (no JIT code is running now) and start over.
            for b in cache.blocks.iter_mut() {
                b.jit = 0;
            }
            j.reset();
            match j.compile(blk) {
                Some(c) => c,
                None => {
                    blk.jit = 1;
                    return 0;
                }
            }
        }
    };
    blk.jit = body;
    j.register(blk.start, entry);
    body
}

/// Switch the JIT on or off for all CPUs (overrides env `S3_JIT`; takes effect at the next `Cpu::run`). Does
/// nothing in builds without JIT ([`jit_available`]).
pub fn set_jit_enabled(on: bool) {
    #[cfg(all(feature = "jit", target_arch = "aarch64"))]
    jit::set_enabled(on);
    #[cfg(not(all(feature = "jit", target_arch = "aarch64")))]
    let _ = on;
}

/// `S3_CPU_TIME=1`: measure the host time spent in [`Cpu::run`] (see [`cpu_run_seconds`]).
fn run_timing() -> bool {
    static ON: std::sync::OnceLock<bool> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    *ON.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("S3_CPU_TIME").is_some())
}

static RUN_NS: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0);

/// Host seconds spent in [`Cpu::run`] by all CPUs (only measured with env `S3_CPU_TIME=1`, else 0).
pub fn cpu_run_seconds() -> f64 {
    RUN_NS.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) as f64 / 1e9
}

/// JIT counters of this process (one line of text; empty without JIT).
pub fn jit_stats() -> String {
    #[cfg(all(feature = "jit", target_arch = "aarch64"))]
    return jit::stats();
    #[cfg(not(all(feature = "jit", target_arch = "aarch64")))]
    String::new()
}

/// Whether this build has the JIT (cargo feature `jit` on aarch64).
pub fn jit_available() -> bool {
    cfg!(all(feature = "jit", target_arch = "aarch64"))
}

/// Whether the JIT is currently switched on (env `S3_JIT=1` or [`set_jit_enabled`]).
pub fn jit_enabled() -> bool {
    #[cfg(all(feature = "jit", target_arch = "aarch64"))]
    return jit::enabled();
    #[cfg(not(all(feature = "jit", target_arch = "aarch64")))]
    false
}

/// One guest CPU (one per guest thread).
///
/// `repr(C)`: the JIT's generated code addresses the first fields (registers, EIP, flag state, JIT exchange
/// fields) by their offsets (`jit/mod.rs`).
#[repr(C)]
pub struct Cpu {
    /// General registers, see [`EAX`]..[`EDI`].
    pub regs: [u32; 8],
    pub eip: u32,
    /// EFLAGS storage: all bits when `lk == NONE`, else only the non-status bits are valid. Read with
    /// [`Cpu::eflags`], write with [`Cpu::set_eflags`] (lazy flags, see `flags.rs`).
    pub(crate) ef: u32,
    /// Lazy-flag state: operands, result, saved CF (inc/dec), kind (`flags::lk`), operand size.
    pub(crate) la: u32,
    pub(crate) lb: u32,
    pub(crate) lr: u32,
    pub(crate) lcf: u32,
    pub(crate) lk: u8,
    pub(crate) lsz: u8,
    /// Linear base of FS (the thread's TEB).
    pub fs_base: u32,
    pub gs_base: u32,
    /// Instructions retired by this CPU.
    pub instructions: u64,
    /// JIT exchange fields (remaining budget, block + instruction index of a side exit, guest memory).
    pub(crate) jit_left: u64,
    pub(crate) jit_blk: usize,
    pub(crate) jit_mem: usize,
    /// `instructions` = `jit_total - left` while JIT code runs (for native fast paths).
    pub(crate) jit_total: u64,
    pub(crate) jit_idx: u32,
    /// Address of the instruction currently executing (valid during `run`).
    pub cur_ip: u32,
    /// Hook address whose next block entry must not exit with [`CpuExit::Hook`] (0 = none).
    hook_skip: u32,
    /// Address of the `fast::Op` whose handler failed (set together with `pending_exit`).
    fault_op: usize,
    /// Exit produced by a handler that returned `false` (see `fast.rs`).
    pending_exit: Option<CpuExit>,
    /// x87 (and MMX) state.
    pub fpu: Fpu,
    /// Decoded-block cache. Threads may share code, but each CPU keeps its own cache (simple, no locking).
    pub cache: DecodeCache,
}

impl Default for Cpu {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl Cpu {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Cpu {
            regs: [0; 8],
            eip: 0,
            ef: 0x202,
            lk: 0,
            lsz: 4,
            la: 0,
            lb: 0,
            lr: 0,
            lcf: 0,
            fs_base: 0,
            gs_base: 0,
            fpu: Fpu::new(),
            instructions: 0,
            cache: DecodeCache::default(),
            cur_ip: 0,
            hook_skip: 0,
            pending_exit: None,
            fault_op: 0,
            jit_left: 0,
            jit_blk: 0,
            jit_mem: 0,
            jit_total: 0,
            jit_idx: 0,
        }
    }

    #[inline]
    pub fn esp(&self) -> u32 {
        self.regs[ESP]
    }

    /// Snapshot of registers, EIP and EFLAGS.
    pub fn context(&self) -> Context {
        Context { regs: self.regs, eip: self.eip, eflags: self.eflags() }
    }

    /// Restore a snapshot.
    pub fn set_context(&mut self, c: &Context) {
        self.regs = c.regs;
        self.eip = c.eip;
        self.set_eflags(c.eflags);
    }

    /// Push a dword on the guest stack.
    pub fn push32(&mut self, mem: &mut GuestMemory, v: u32) {
        self.regs[ESP] = self.regs[ESP].wrapping_sub(4);
        mem.write_u32(self.regs[ESP], v);
    }

    /// Pop a dword from the guest stack.
    pub fn pop32(&mut self, mem: &GuestMemory) -> u32 {
        let v = mem.read_u32(self.regs[ESP]);
        self.regs[ESP] = self.regs[ESP].wrapping_add(4);
        v
    }

    /// Route every instruction through the generic interpreter instead of the specialised fast handlers
    /// (debugging aid; also used by the tests to cross-check both paths). Clears the decode cache.
    pub fn set_generic_only(&mut self, on: bool) {
        self.cache.clear();
        self.cache.generic_only = on;
    }

    /// Install the hook address set (`None` = no hooks). Clears the decode cache so blocks are re-split.
    pub fn set_hooks(&mut self, hooks: Option<std::sync::Arc<HookAddrs>>) {
        self.cache.clear();
        self.cache.hooks = hooks.filter(|h| !h.is_empty());
        self.hook_skip = 0;
    }

    /// Install native fast paths (`None` = none). Clears the decode cache.
    pub fn set_native_blocks(&mut self, natives: Option<std::sync::Arc<NativeBlocks>>) {
        self.cache.clear();
        self.cache.natives = natives.filter(|n| !n.is_empty());
    }

    /// Per-CPU JIT switch (`None` = follow the global setting, see [`set_jit_enabled`]). No effect without JIT.
    pub fn set_jit(&mut self, on: Option<bool>) {
        self.cache.jit_mode = match on {
            None => 0,
            Some(false) => 1,
            Some(true) => 2,
        };
    }

    /// Block entries (through the run loop) before a block is compiled (tests; `None` = default).
    pub fn set_jit_threshold(&mut self, n: Option<u64>) {
        self.cache.jit_thr = n;
    }

    /// The installed hook address set.
    pub fn hooks(&self) -> Option<&std::sync::Arc<HookAddrs>> {
        self.cache.hooks.as_ref()
    }

    /// After a [`CpuExit::Hook`] at `eip`: execute the original code at `eip` once without exiting again.
    pub fn skip_hook_once(&mut self, eip: u32) {
        self.hook_skip = eip;
    }

    /// Invalidate decoded code in `[start, start+len)` (call after the guest or host writes code).
    pub fn invalidate_range(&mut self, start: u32, len: u32) {
        self.cache.invalidate_range(start, len);
    }

    /// Execute up to `max_instructions` instructions.
    pub fn run(&mut self, mem: &mut GuestMemory, max_instructions: u64) -> CpuExit {
        // Move the cache out so instructions can be borrowed from it while `self` is mutated.
        let mut cache = std::mem::take(&mut self.cache);
        let t = run_timing().then(std::time::Instant::now);
        let exit = self.run_with(&mut cache, mem, max_instructions);
        if let Some(t) = t {
            RUN_NS.fetch_add(t.elapsed().as_nanos() as u64, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
        }
        self.cache = cache;
        exit
    }

    fn run_with(&mut self, cache: &mut DecodeCache, mem: &mut GuestMemory, max_instructions: u64) -> CpuExit {
        // Retired instructions are counted through `left` only and stored into `self.instructions` (= base +
        // max_instructions - left) before anything that may read it (native blocks, exits).
        let base = self.instructions;
        let mut left = max_instructions;
        // Previous block (for chaining), null = none.
        let mut prev: *mut Block = std::ptr::null_mut();
        #[cfg(all(feature = "jit", target_arch = "aarch64"))]
        let jit_on = match cache.jit_mode {
            2 => true,
            1 => false,
            _ => jit::enabled(),
        } && !cache.generic_only;
        #[cfg(all(feature = "jit", target_arch = "aarch64"))]
        let jit_thr = cache.jit_thr.unwrap_or(jit::THRESHOLD);
        let exit = 'run: loop {
            let eip = self.eip;
            if eip >= layout::THUNK_BASE {
                break if eip == layout::MAGIC_RETURN { CpuExit::ReturnMagic } else { CpuExit::Thunk(eip) };
            }
            if left == 0 {
                break CpuExit::Budget;
            }
            // Block pointers stay valid while this loop runs: blocks are boxed and only appended while the cache
            // is out of the `Cpu` (`invalidate_range`, which drops blocks, also clears every `succ_blk`).
            let bp: *mut Block = 'find: {
                if !prev.is_null() {
                    // SAFETY: see above.
                    let p = unsafe { &mut *prev };
                    if p.succ_eip[0] == eip {
                        break 'find p.succ_blk[0];
                    }
                    if p.succ_eip[1] == eip {
                        break 'find p.succ_blk[1];
                    }
                }
                let i = match cache.lookup(eip, mem) {
                    Ok(i) => i,
                    Err(e) => break 'run e,
                };
                let b: *mut Block = &mut *cache.blocks[i];
                if !prev.is_null() {
                    // SAFETY: see above.
                    let p = unsafe { &mut *prev };
                    p.succ_eip[1] = p.succ_eip[0];
                    p.succ_blk[1] = p.succ_blk[0];
                    p.succ_eip[0] = eip;
                    p.succ_blk[0] = b;
                }
                b
            };
            prev = bp;
            // SAFETY: see above.
            let blk = unsafe { &mut *bp };
            blk.entries += 1;
            let blk = &*blk;
            if blk.special {
                if blk.hooked {
                    if self.hook_skip == eip {
                        self.hook_skip = 0;
                    } else {
                        break CpuExit::Hook(eip);
                    }
                }
                if let Some(f) = blk.native {
                    self.instructions = base + (max_instructions - left);
                    if let Some(k) = f(self, mem, left) {
                        debug_assert!(k <= left);
                        left -= k.min(left);
                        continue;
                    }
                }
            }
            let n = blk.n as u64;
            if n <= left {
                #[cfg(all(feature = "jit", target_arch = "aarch64"))]
                if jit_on && blk.jit != 1 && !blk.hooked {
                    let code = if blk.jit != 0 {
                        blk.jit
                    } else if blk.entries >= jit_thr {
                        // SAFETY: `bp` is a live block of `cache` (see above).
                        unsafe { jit_compile(cache, bp) }
                    } else {
                        0
                    };
                    if code != 0 {
                        match self.run_jit(cache, code, mem, &mut left, base, max_instructions) {
                            None => {
                                prev = std::ptr::null_mut();
                                continue;
                            }
                            Some(e) => return e,
                        }
                    }
                }
                // Threaded code: the first handler runs the whole block (each handler tail-calls the next one,
                // see `fast::next`). Inside a block only the last instruction can change EIP (blocks end at the
                // first control-flow instruction) and no other instruction reads it, so EIP is set once to the
                // last instruction's next address before the block runs.
                self.eip = blk.end;
                // SAFETY: `ops` holds at least one instruction plus the sentinel.
                let op0 = unsafe { &*blk.op0 };
                if (op0.h)(self, mem, op0) {
                    left -= n;
                    continue;
                }
                let i = (self.fault_op - blk.ops.as_ptr() as usize) / std::mem::size_of::<fast::Op>();
                self.instructions = base + (max_instructions - left);
                return self.block_exit(blk, i);
            }
            // The budget ends inside this block.
            self.instructions = base + (max_instructions - left);
            if let Some(e) = self.run_partial(blk, mem, left as usize) {
                return e;
            }
            left = 0;
        };
        self.instructions = base + (max_instructions - left);
        exit
    }

    /// Enter JIT code at `code` (a compiled block whose instruction count fits `left`) and run until it exits.
    /// `None` = continue the run loop at `self.eip`; `Some(exit)` = a failing instruction ended the run.
    #[cfg(all(feature = "jit", target_arch = "aarch64"))]
    #[inline(never)]
    fn run_jit(
        &mut self,
        cache: &mut DecodeCache,
        code: usize,
        mem: &mut GuestMemory,
        left: &mut u64,
        base: u64,
        max_instructions: u64,
    ) -> Option<CpuExit> {
        let enter = cache.jit.as_ref().map(|j| j.enter).unwrap_or(0);
        self.jit_left = *left;
        self.jit_total = base + max_instructions;
        self.jit_mem = mem as *mut GuestMemory as usize;
        // SAFETY: `enter` is the trampoline emitted by `Jit::new` (`jit::EnterFn` ABI); the code it jumps to only
        // touches this `Cpu`, guest memory and the JIT's own tables, all alive for the call.
        let r = unsafe {
            let f: jit::EnterFn = std::mem::transmute(enter);
            f(self, mem.base_ptr(), code)
        };
        *left = self.jit_left;
        jit::count(jit::ST_ENTER);
        jit::count(jit::ST_ENTER + 1 + r as usize);
        if r == jit::EXIT_EIP {
            if jit::fallback_profile() {
                jit::exit_reason(cache, self.eip);
            }
            return None;
        }
        // SAFETY: the JIT code stored a pointer to its (live) block.
        let b = unsafe { &*(self.jit_blk as *const Block) };
        let i = self.jit_idx as usize;
        if r == jit::EXIT_SIDE {
            // Continue the block from instruction `i` with the interpreter (e.g. a memory access that faults).
            self.eip = b.end;
            let op = &b.ops[i];
            if (op.h)(self, mem, op) {
                *left -= b.n as u64;
                return None;
            }
            let k = (self.fault_op - b.ops.as_ptr() as usize) / std::mem::size_of::<fast::Op>();
            self.instructions = base + (max_instructions - *left);
            return Some(self.block_exit(b, k));
        }
        // EXIT_FAIL: a fallback instruction (interpreter handler called from JIT code) failed.
        self.instructions = base + (max_instructions - *left);
        Some(self.block_exit(b, i))
    }

    /// Execute the first `n` (< `blk.n`) instructions of `blk` one by one with the generic interpreter (same
    /// results as the fast handlers by their contract), so the CPU stops at exactly the same instruction as a
    /// complete block run would pass. `Some(exit)` if one of them failed (`self.instructions` updated).
    #[cold]
    #[inline(never)]
    fn run_partial(&mut self, blk: &Block, mem: &mut GuestMemory, n: usize) -> Option<CpuExit> {
        for (i, ins) in blk.insns[..n].iter().enumerate() {
            self.eip = ins.next_ip32();
            self.cur_ip = ins.ip32();
            if let Err(e) = exec::step(self, mem, ins) {
                self.pending_exit = Some(e);
                return Some(self.block_exit(blk, i));
            }
        }
        None
    }

    /// Exit after instruction `i` of `blk` failed (its exit is in `pending_exit`): a fault rewinds EIP to the
    /// faulting instruction (as Windows reports it); `Interrupt`/`Halt` complete the instruction.
    #[cold]
    #[inline(never)]
    fn block_exit(&mut self, blk: &Block, i: usize) -> CpuExit {
        let mut exit = self.pending_exit.take().unwrap_or(CpuExit::Halt);
        let ins = &blk.insns[i];
        if let CpuExit::Fault { eip, .. } = &mut exit {
            let ip = ins.ip32();
            *eip = ip;
            self.eip = ip;
            self.cur_ip = ip;
            self.instructions += i as u64;
        } else {
            // EIP after the instruction, unless it is a control transfer that set it already (e.g. `int n` via
            // the generic path leaves EIP after the instruction too).
            if ins.flow_control() == FlowControl::Next {
                self.eip = ins.next_ip32();
            }
            self.instructions += i as u64 + 1;
        }
        exit
    }

    /// Execute exactly one instruction (debugging / tests). Thunk/magic EIPs return their exits.
    pub fn step(&mut self, mem: &mut GuestMemory) -> CpuExit {
        self.run(mem, 1)
    }
}

```

`port/crates/s3-cpu/src/tests.rs`:

```rs
//! CPU tests: hand-assembled snippets (iced-x86 `code_asm`), no game bytes.

use iced_x86::code_asm::*;

use crate::*;

const CODE: u32 = 0x0040_1000;
const STACK_TOP: u32 = 0x0090_0000;
const DATA: u32 = 0x0060_0000;

fn setup(build: impl FnOnce(&mut CodeAssembler)) -> (Cpu, GuestMemory) {
    let mut a = CodeAssembler::new(32).unwrap();
    build(&mut a);
    a.ret().unwrap();
    let bytes = a.assemble(CODE as u64).unwrap();
    let mut mem = GuestMemory::new().unwrap();
    mem.write_bytes(CODE, &bytes);
    let mut cpu = Cpu::new();
    cpu.regs[ESP] = STACK_TOP;
    cpu.push32(&mut mem, layout::MAGIC_RETURN);
    cpu.eip = CODE;
    (cpu, mem)
}

fn run(build: impl FnOnce(&mut CodeAssembler)) -> (Cpu, GuestMemory) {
    let (mut cpu, mut mem) = setup(build);
    let exit = cpu.run(&mut mem, 1_000_000);
    assert_eq!(exit, CpuExit::ReturnMagic, "eip={:#x}", cpu.eip);
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[ESP], STACK_TOP);
    (cpu, mem)
}

#[test]
fn mov_add_sub_flags() {
    let (cpu, _) = run(|a| {
        a.mov(eax, 0xFFFF_FFFFu32).unwrap();
        a.add(eax, 1).unwrap(); // CF=1 ZF=1
        a.mov(ebx, 5).unwrap();
        a.sub(ebx, 7).unwrap(); // -2, CF=1 SF=1
        a.mov(ecx, 0x7FFF_FFFF).unwrap();
        a.inc(ecx).unwrap(); // OF=1, CF preserved (1 from sub)
    });
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EAX], 0);
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EBX], (-2i32) as u32);
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[ECX], 0x8000_0000);
    assert!(cpu.flag(fl::OF));
    assert!(cpu.flag(fl::CF));
    assert!(cpu.flag(fl::SF));
    assert!(!cpu.flag(fl::ZF));
}

#[test]
fn partial_registers_and_extend() {
    let (cpu, _) = run(|a| {
        a.mov(eax, 0x1234_5678).unwrap();
        a.mov(ah, 0xAB).unwrap();
        a.mov(al, 0xCD).unwrap();
        a.mov(bx, 0xFFFF).unwrap();
        a.movsx(ecx, bx).unwrap();
        a.movzx(edx, ah).unwrap();
        a.mov(esi, 0x80).unwrap();
        a.movsx(edi, si).unwrap(); // 0x80 as i16 is positive
    });
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EAX], 0x1234_ABCD);
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EBX] & 0xFFFF, 0xFFFF);
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[ECX], 0xFFFF_FFFF);
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EDX], 0xAB);
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EDI], 0x80);
}

#[test]
fn memory_lea_push_pop_call() {
    let (cpu, mem) = run(|a| {
        let mut func = a.create_label();
        let mut done = a.create_label();
        a.mov(ebx, DATA).unwrap();
        a.mov(dword_ptr(ebx + 8), 41).unwrap();
        a.lea(esi, ptr(ebx + ecx * 4 + 8)).unwrap(); // ecx = 0
        a.push(dword_ptr(esi)).unwrap();
        a.call(func).unwrap();
        a.add(esp, 4).unwrap();
        a.jmp(done).unwrap();
        a.set_label(&mut func).unwrap();
        a.mov(eax, dword_ptr(esp + 4)).unwrap();
        a.inc(eax).unwrap();
        a.mov(dword_ptr(ebx + 12), eax).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
        a.set_label(&mut done).unwrap();
        a.nop().unwrap();
    });
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[ESI], DATA + 8);
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EAX], 42);
    assert_eq!(mem.read_u32(DATA + 12), 42);
}

#[test]
fn loop_with_jcc_sum() {
    // sum 1..=100 with cmp/jle
    let (cpu, _) = run(|a| {
        let mut top = a.create_label();
        a.xor(eax, eax).unwrap();
        a.mov(ecx, 1).unwrap();
        a.set_label(&mut top).unwrap();
        a.add(eax, ecx).unwrap();
        a.inc(ecx).unwrap();
        a.cmp(ecx, 100).unwrap();
        a.jle(top).unwrap();
    });
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EAX], 5050);
}

#[test]
fn logic_and_test_and_signed_conditions() {
    let (cpu, _) = run(|a| {
        a.mov(eax, 0xF0F0).unwrap();
        a.and(eax, 0x0FF0).unwrap();
        a.or(eax, 1).unwrap();
        a.xor(eax, 0x10).unwrap();
        a.mov(ebx, -5i32).unwrap();
        a.cmp(ebx, 3).unwrap();
        a.setl(cl).unwrap(); // -5 < 3 signed
        a.setb(dl).unwrap(); // unsigned 0xFFFFFFFB < 3 false
        a.test(eax, eax).unwrap();
        a.setne(dh).unwrap();
    });
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EAX], 0x00E1);
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[ECX] & 0xFF, 1);
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EDX] & 0xFF, 0);
    assert_eq!((cpu.regs[EDX] >> 8) & 0xFF, 1);
}

#[test]
fn shifts_mul_div() {
    let (cpu, _) = run(|a| {
        a.mov(eax, 1).unwrap();
        a.shl(eax, 4).unwrap(); // 16
        a.mov(ebx, -64i32).unwrap();
        a.sar(ebx, 2).unwrap(); // -16
        a.mov(ecx, 0x8000_0001u32).unwrap();
        a.rol(ecx, 1).unwrap(); // 3, CF=1
        a.mov(esi, 7).unwrap();
        a.imul_3(edi, esi, 6).unwrap(); // 42
        a.mul(esi).unwrap(); // edx:eax = 16*7 = 112
        a.mov(esi, 10).unwrap();
        a.xor(edx, edx).unwrap();
        a.div(esi).unwrap(); // eax = 11, edx = 2
    });
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EAX], 11);
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EDX], 2);
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EBX], (-16i32) as u32);
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[ECX], 3);
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EDI], 42);
}

        a.idiv(ecx).unwrap();
    });
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EAX] as i32, -3);
    assert_eq!(cpu.regs[EDX] as i32, -1);
}

        e => panic!("unexpected {e:?}"),
    }
}
```
