`port/crates/s3-frontend/src/touch.rs`:

```rs
//! Touch input: Android MotionEvents -> raw [`HostEvent::Pointer`] events (docs/porting/android.md "Controls",
//! docs/porting/touch.md).
//!
//! The frontend only reports fingers. Gesture recognition (tap, long press, pans, pinch, multi-finger taps) and
//! what a gesture does in the game (context-aware touch, UI modes, touch->mouse fallback) live in `s3-mods`,
//! shared with the desktop `s3run --inject` touch commands, so both behave the same.

use s3_runtime::{HostEvent, PointerPhase};

/// MotionEvent action kinds we care about (android-activity `MotionAction`, platform independent for tests).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Action {
    /// First finger down (ACTION_DOWN).
    Down,
    /// Another finger down (ACTION_POINTER_DOWN).
    PointerDown,
    /// One or more fingers moved (ACTION_MOVE): every pointer of the event is reported.
    Move,
    /// A finger other than the last lifted (ACTION_POINTER_UP).
    PointerUp,
    /// Last finger lifted (ACTION_UP).
    Up,
    /// The system took the gesture (ACTION_CANCEL): every pointer is cancelled.
    Cancel,
}

/// Position of a pointer: game pixels (x, y) and window pixels (wx, wy).
pub type Pos = (i32, i32, i32, i32);

/// Raw pointer events for one MotionEvent. `acting` = (pointer id, position) of the pointer the action is
/// about (`pointer_index()`); `all` = every pointer of the event.
pub fn pointer_events(action: Action, acting: (i32, Pos), all: &[(i32, Pos)]) -> Vec<HostEvent> {
    let ev = |id: i32, phase, p: Pos| HostEvent::Pointer { id: id as u32, phase, x: p.0, y: p.1, wx: p.2, wy: p.3 };
    match action {
        Action::Down | Action::PointerDown => vec![ev(acting.0, PointerPhase::Down, acting.1)],
        Action::PointerUp | Action::Up => vec![ev(acting.0, PointerPhase::Up, acting.1)],
        Action::Move => all.iter().map(|&(id, p)| ev(id, PointerPhase::Move, p)).collect(),
        Action::Cancel => all.iter().map(|&(id, p)| ev(id, PointerPhase::Cancel, p)).collect(),
    }
}

/// Drops Move events that do not change a finger's (window) position (MotionEvents batch all pointers).
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct PointerFilter {
    last: Vec<(u32, i32, i32)>,
}

impl PointerFilter {
    pub fn keep(&mut self, e: &HostEvent) -> bool {
        let HostEvent::Pointer { id, phase, wx: x, wy: y, .. } = *e else { return true };
        let i = self.last.iter().position(|l| l.0 == id);
        match phase {
            PointerPhase::Move => {
                if let Some(i) = i {
                    if (self.last[i].1, self.last[i].2) == (x, y) {
                        return false;
                    }
                    self.last[i] = (id, x, y);
                }
                true
            }
            PointerPhase::Down => {
                match i {
                    Some(i) => self.last[i] = (id, x, y),
                    None => self.last.push((id, x, y)),
                }
                true
            }
            PointerPhase::Up | PointerPhase::Cancel => {
                if let Some(i) = i {
                    self.last.swap_remove(i);
                }
                true
            }
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use PointerPhase::*;

    fn p(id: u32, phase: PointerPhase, x: i32, y: i32) -> HostEvent {
        HostEvent::Pointer { id, phase, x, y, wx: x * 2, wy: y * 2 }
    }

    fn q(x: i32, y: i32) -> Pos {
        (x, y, x * 2, y * 2)
    }

    #[test]
    fn motion_actions_map_to_pointer_phases() {
        assert_eq!(pointer_events(Action::Down, (0, q(10, 20)), &[(0, q(10, 20))]), vec![p(0, Down, 10, 20)]);
        let all = [(0, q(10, 20)), (1, q(50, 60))];
        assert_eq!(pointer_events(Action::PointerDown, (1, q(50, 60)), &all), vec![p(1, Down, 50, 60)]);
        assert_eq!(pointer_events(Action::Move, (0, q(10, 20)), &all), vec![p(0, Move, 10, 20), p(1, Move, 50, 60)]);
        assert_eq!(pointer_events(Action::PointerUp, (0, q(11, 21)), &all), vec![p(0, Up, 11, 21)]);
        assert_eq!(pointer_events(Action::Up, (1, q(50, 61)), &[(1, q(50, 61))]), vec![p(1, Up, 50, 61)]);
        assert_eq!(pointer_events(Action::Cancel, (0, q(0, 0)), &all), vec![p(0, Cancel, 10, 20), p(1, Cancel, 50, 60)]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn filter_drops_unchanged_moves() {
        let mut f = PointerFilter::default();
        assert!(f.keep(&p(0, Down, 1, 1)));
        assert!(f.keep(&p(1, Down, 5, 5)));
        assert!(!f.keep(&p(0, Move, 1, 1)));
        assert!(f.keep(&p(1, Move, 6, 5)));
        assert!(!f.keep(&p(1, Move, 6, 5)));
        assert!(f.keep(&p(1, Up, 6, 5)));
        assert!(f.keep(&HostEvent::MouseMove { x: 0, y: 0 }));
    }
}

```

`port/crates/s3-frontend/src/upload.rs`:

```rs
//! Built-in web upload server for the game files (launcher "Game files" page, docs/porting/android.md
//! "Launcher"). A minimal HTTP/1.1 server on std::net: the user opens `http://<phone ip>:<port>/?k=<token>` in a
//! PC browser on the same network, picks the Settlers III folder (`<input webkitdirectory>` or drag and drop) and
//! the page uploads every file with one `POST /upload` per file. Files go below the game dir only (path
//! sanitizing, size limit); the server runs only while the user has it switched on.
//!
//! Routes (all need `k=<token>`, otherwise 403):
//! - `GET /` the upload page (HTML + JS, no external resources);
//! - `GET /status` JSON: missing required parts, files/bytes received;
//! - `GET /stat?path=P` JSON `{"size":N}` (-1 = not there), so the page can skip files already on the phone;
//! - `POST /upload?path=P` body = file contents (Content-Length required), written to `<root>/P` via a
//!   `.upload-part` temp file + rename.

use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader, Read, Write};
use std::net::{Ipv4Addr, TcpListener, TcpStream};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::thread::JoinHandle;
use std::time::Duration;

/// First port tried (then the next ones, then any free port).
pub const DEFAULT_PORT: u16 = 8080;
/// Largest single file accepted (the biggest Settlers III files are a few hundred MB).
pub const MAX_FILE_BYTES: u64 = 4 << 30;
/// Deepest accepted path (components).
const MAX_DEPTH: usize = 12;
const MAX_HEAD: usize = 16 * 1024;

/// What the launcher shows while the server runs.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct UploadStatus {
    /// Files completely written, and their bytes.
    pub files: u64,
    pub bytes: u64,
    /// File being received now (relative path), bytes so far and its size.
    pub current: Option<(String, u64, u64)>,
    /// Last error (bad path, write failed, ...).
    pub error: Option<String>,
    /// Address of the last client.
    pub client: Option<String>,
    /// Bumped on every change.
    pub seq: u64,
}

pub struct UploadServer {
    pub port: u16,
    pub token: String,
    pub root: PathBuf,
    pub status: Arc<Mutex<UploadStatus>>,
    stop: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    thread: Option<JoinHandle<()>>,
}

/// Returns the required parts still missing below a root (the launcher passes `frontend::missing_parts`).
pub type MissingFn = fn(&Path) -> Vec<&'static str>;

impl UploadServer {
    /// Listen on all interfaces, port [`DEFAULT_PORT`] (or the next free one), writing below `root`.
    pub fn start(root: PathBuf, missing: MissingFn) -> std::io::Result<UploadServer> {
        let listener = (DEFAULT_PORT..DEFAULT_PORT + 10)
            .find_map(|p| TcpListener::bind((Ipv4Addr::UNSPECIFIED, p)).ok())
            .map_or_else(|| TcpListener::bind((Ipv4Addr::UNSPECIFIED, 0)), Ok)?;
        let port = listener.local_addr()?.port();
        listener.set_nonblocking(true)?;
        let token = new_token();
        let status = Arc::new(Mutex::new(UploadStatus::default()));
        let stop = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
        let ctx = Arc::new(Ctx { root: root.clone(), token: token.clone(), status: status.clone(), missing });
        let st = stop.clone();
        let thread = std::thread::Builder::new().name("s3-upload".into()).spawn(move || {
            while !st.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
                match listener.accept() {
                    Ok((s, addr)) => {
                        let c = ctx.clone();
                        let _ = std::thread::Builder::new().name("s3-upload-conn".into()).spawn(move || {
                            let _ = s.set_nonblocking(false);
                            let _ = s.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(60)));
                            c.status.lock().unwrap().client = Some(addr.ip().to_string());
                            if let Err(e) = handle(&c, s) {
                                log::warn!("upload: connection from {addr}: {e}");
                            }
                        });
                    }
                    Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)),
                    Err(e) => {
                        log::warn!("upload: accept: {e}");
                        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500));
                    }
                }
            }
            log::info!("upload: server stopped");
        })?;
        log::info!("upload: server on port {port}, writing into {}", root.display());
        Ok(UploadServer { port, token, root, status, stop, thread: Some(thread) })
    }

    /// The address to open, for the given phone IP.
    pub fn url(&self, ip: &str) -> String {
        format!("http://{ip}:{}/?k={}", self.port, self.token)
    }

    pub fn snapshot(&self) -> UploadStatus {
        self.status.lock().unwrap().clone()
    }
}

impl Drop for UploadServer {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.stop.store(true, Ordering::Release);
        if let Some(t) = self.thread.take() {
            let _ = t.join();
        }
    }
}

/// The phone's address in the local network: a private IPv4 address (Wi-Fi / hotspot) if there is one.
pub fn local_ip() -> Option<Ipv4Addr> {
    let private = |ip: &Ipv4Addr| ip.is_private();
    let primary = s3_net::lan::primary_ipv4();
    if let Some(p) = primary.filter(private) {
        return Some(p);
    }
    s3_net::lan::interfaces().into_iter().map(|(ip, _)| ip).find(private).or(primary)
}

/// 6 lowercase letters / digits from the clock and address-space randomness (only keeps other devices in the
/// network from writing files by accident or by guessing the port).
fn new_token() -> String {
    use std::hash::{BuildHasher, Hasher};
    let mut h = std::collections::hash_map::RandomState::new().build_hasher();
    h.write_u128(std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).map(|d| d.as_nanos()).unwrap_or(0));
    let mut v = h.finish();
    const A: &[u8] = b"abcdefghjkmnpqrstuvwxyz23456789";
    (0..6)
        .map(|_| {
            let c = A[(v % A.len() as u64) as usize] as char;
            v /= A.len() as u64;
            c
        })
        .collect()
}

struct Ctx {
    root: PathBuf,
    token: String,
    status: Arc<Mutex<UploadStatus>>,
    missing: MissingFn,
}

impl Ctx {
    fn update(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut UploadStatus)) {
        let mut s = self.status.lock().unwrap();
        f(&mut s);
        s.seq += 1;
    }
}

struct Request {
    method: String,
    path: String,
    query: Vec<(String, String)>,
    content_length: Option<u64>,
    expect_continue: bool,
}

impl Request {
    fn q(&self, k: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        self.query.iter().find(|(a, _)| a == k).map(|(_, v)| v.as_str())
    }
}

fn read_head(r: &mut BufReader<TcpStream>) -> std::io::Result<Option<Request>> {
    let mut line = String::new();
    if r.read_line(&mut line)? == 0 {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    let mut it = line.split_whitespace();
    let (method, target) = (it.next().unwrap_or("").to_string(), it.next().unwrap_or("/").to_string());
    let (mut content_length, mut expect_continue, mut total) = (None, false, line.len());
    loop {
        let mut h = String::new();
        let n = r.read_line(&mut h)?;
        total += n;
        if n == 0 || total > MAX_HEAD {
            return Err(std::io::Error::other("bad request head"));
        }
        let h = h.trim_end();
        if h.is_empty() {
            break;
        }
        if let Some((k, v)) = h.split_once(':') {
            let (k, v) = (k.trim().to_ascii_lowercase(), v.trim());
            if k == "content-length" {
                content_length = v.parse().ok();
            } else if k == "expect" && v.eq_ignore_ascii_case("100-continue") {
                expect_continue = true;
            }
        }
    }
    let (path, qs) = target.split_once('?').unwrap_or((&target, ""));
    let query = qs
        .split('&')
        .filter(|p| !p.is_empty())
        .map(|p| {
            let (k, v) = p.split_once('=').unwrap_or((p, ""));
            (percent_decode(k), percent_decode(v))
        })
        .collect();
    Ok(Some(Request { method, path: path.to_string(), query, content_length, expect_continue }))
}

/// `%XX` decoding (UTF-8; `+` stays `+`, `encodeURIComponent` encodes spaces as `%20`).
pub fn percent_decode(s: &str) -> String {
    let b = s.as_bytes();
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(b.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < b.len() {
        if b[i] == b'%' && i + 2 < b.len() {
            if let Some(v) = std::str::from_utf8(&b[i + 1..i + 3]).ok().and_then(|h| u8::from_str_radix(h, 16).ok()) {
                out.push(v);
                i += 3;
                continue;
            }
        }
        out.push(b[i]);
        i += 1;
    }
    String::from_utf8_lossy(&out).into_owned()
}

/// Checks an uploaded relative path (`/` or `\` separated): no `..`, `.`, empty parts, drive letters, control
/// characters or reserved names; at most [`MAX_DEPTH`] parts. Returns the parts.
pub fn sanitize(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
    let parts: Vec<&str> = path.split(['/', '\\']).filter(|p| !p.is_empty()).collect();
    if parts.is_empty() {
        return Err("empty path".into());
    }
    if parts.len() > MAX_DEPTH {
        return Err(format!("path too deep: {path}"));
    }
    for p in &parts {
        if *p == "." || *p == ".." || p.contains(':') || p.chars().any(|c| c.is_control()) || p.len() > 200 {
            return Err(format!("bad path: {path}"));
        }
        if p.ends_with(".upload-part") {
            return Err(format!("bad name: {path}"));
        }
    }
    Ok(parts.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect())
}

/// `root` joined with `parts`, reusing existing entries whose names differ only in case (the game looks files
/// up case-insensitively too, so `gfx/` and `GFX/` must not end up as two folders).
pub fn resolve_ci(root: &Path, parts: &[String]) -> PathBuf {
    let mut cur = root.to_path_buf();
    for p in parts {
        let exact = cur.join(p);
        if exact.exists() {
            cur = exact;
            continue;
        }
        let found = std::fs::read_dir(&cur).ok().and_then(|rd| {
            rd.flatten().find(|e| e.file_name().to_string_lossy().eq_ignore_ascii_case(p)).map(|e| e.path())
        });
        cur = found.unwrap_or(exact);
    }
    cur
}

fn respond(s: &mut TcpStream, code: u16, ctype: &str, body: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let reason = match code {
        200 => "OK",
        400 => "Bad Request",
        403 => "Forbidden",
        404 => "Not Found",
        413 => "Payload Too Large",
        _ => "Error",
    };
    write!(
        s,
        "HTTP/1.1 {code} {reason}\r\nContent-Type: {ctype}\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\nCache-Control: no-store\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n",
        body.len()
    )?;
    s.write_all(body)?;
    s.flush()
}

fn json_str(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut o = String::from("\"");
    for c in s.chars() {
        match c {
            '"' => o.push_str("\\\""),
            '\\' => o.push_str("\\\\"),
            c if (c as u32) < 0x20 => o.push_str(&format!("\\u{:04x}", c as u32)),
            c => o.push(c),
        }
    }
    o.push('"');
    o
}

fn status_json(c: &Ctx) -> String {
    let missing = (c.missing)(&c.root);
    let s = c.status.lock().unwrap().clone();
    format!(
        "{{\"missing\":[{}],\"files\":{},\"bytes\":{},\"error\":{}}}",
        missing.iter().map(|m| json_str(m)).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(","),
        s.files,
        s.bytes,
        s.error.as_deref().map_or("null".into(), json_str)
    )
}

fn handle(c: &Ctx, stream: TcpStream) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let mut w = stream.try_clone()?;
    let mut r = BufReader::with_capacity(256 * 1024, stream);
    let Some(req) = read_head(&mut r)? else { return Ok(()) };
    if req.path == "/favicon.ico" {
        return respond(&mut w, 404, "text/plain", b"");
    }
    if req.q("k") != Some(c.token.as_str()) {
        let msg = "<!doctype html><meta charset=utf-8><title>S3 Mobile</title><body style=\"font:18px sans-serif\">\
                   Please open the full address shown on the phone (it ends with <b>?k=...</b>).</body>";
        return respond(&mut w, 403, "text/html; charset=utf-8", msg.as_bytes());
    }
    match (req.method.as_str(), req.path.as_str()) {
        ("GET", "/") => respond(&mut w, 200, "text/html; charset=utf-8", PAGE.as_bytes()),
        ("GET", "/status") => respond(&mut w, 200, "application/json", status_json(c).as_bytes()),
        ("GET", "/stat") => {
            let size = sanitize(req.q("path").unwrap_or(""))
                .ok()
                .and_then(|p| std::fs::metadata(resolve_ci(&c.root, &p)).ok())
                .filter(|m| m.is_file())
                .map_or(-1, |m| m.len() as i64);
            respond(&mut w, 200, "application/json", format!("{{\"size\":{size}}}").as_bytes())
        }
        ("POST", "/upload") => {
            let rel = req.q("path").unwrap_or("").to_string();
            let parts = match sanitize(&rel) {
                Ok(p) => p,
                Err(e) => {
                    c.update(|s| s.error = Some(e.clone()));
                    return respond(&mut w, 400, "text/plain", e.as_bytes());
                }
            };
            let Some(len) = req.content_length else {
                return respond(&mut w, 400, "text/plain", b"Content-Length required");
            };
            if len > MAX_FILE_BYTES {
                let e = format!("{rel}: file too large ({len} bytes)");
                c.update(|s| s.error = Some(e.clone()));
                return respond(&mut w, 413, "text/plain", e.as_bytes());
            }
            if req.expect_continue {
                w.write_all(b"HTTP/1.1 100 Continue\r\n\r\n")?;
            }
            match receive(c, &mut r, &parts, &rel, len) {
                Ok(()) => {
                    c.update(|s| {
                        s.files += 1;
                        s.bytes += len;
                        s.current = None;
                    });
                    respond(&mut w, 200, "application/json", status_json(c).as_bytes())
                }
                Err(e) => {
                    let e = format!("{rel}: {e}");
                    log::warn!("upload: {e}");
                    c.update(|s| {
                        s.error = Some(e.clone());
                        s.current = None;
                    });
                    respond(&mut w, 400, "text/plain", e.as_bytes())
                }
            }
        }
        _ => respond(&mut w, 404, "text/plain", b"not found"),
    }
}

fn receive(c: &Ctx, r: &mut impl Read, parts: &[String], rel: &str, len: u64) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let dest = resolve_ci(&c.root, parts);
    if !dest.starts_with(&c.root) {
        return Err(std::io::Error::other("outside the game folder"));
    }
    if dest.is_dir() {
        return Err(std::io::Error::other("a folder with this name exists"));
    }
    if let Some(parent) = dest.parent() {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
    }
    let tmp = dest.with_file_name(format!("{}.upload-part", dest.file_name().unwrap_or_default().to_string_lossy()));
    c.update(|s| s.current = Some((rel.to_string(), 0, len)));
    let res = (|| {
        let mut f = std::io::BufWriter::with_capacity(1 << 20, std::fs::File::create(&tmp)?);
        let mut buf = vec![0u8; 256 * 1024];
        let mut left = len;
        let mut since = 0u64;
        while left > 0 {
            let want = left.min(buf.len() as u64) as usize;
            let n = r.read(&mut buf[..want])?;
            if n == 0 {
                return Err(std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof, "connection closed during upload"));
            }
            f.write_all(&buf[..n])?;
            left -= n as u64;
            since += n as u64;
            if since >= 4 << 20 {
                since = 0;
                c.update(|s| s.current = Some((rel.to_string(), len - left, len)));
            }
        }
        f.flush()?;
        drop(f);
        std::fs::rename(&tmp, &dest)
    })();
    if res.is_err() {
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&tmp);
    }
    res
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn sanitize_rejects_escapes() {
        assert_eq!(sanitize("GFX/a.gfx").unwrap(), vec!["GFX", "a.gfx"]);
        assert_eq!(sanitize("\\Map\\x.map").unwrap(), vec!["Map", "x.map"]);
        assert!(sanitize("../x").is_err());
        assert!(sanitize("a/./b").is_err());
        assert!(sanitize("C:/x").is_err());
        assert!(sanitize("").is_err());
        assert!(sanitize("a\u{0}b").is_err());
        assert!(sanitize(&"a/".repeat(20)).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn percent_decoding() {
        assert_eq!(percent_decode("GFX%2F1%20a.gfx"), "GFX/1 a.gfx");
        assert_eq!(percent_decode("a+b%"), "a+b%");
        assert_eq!(percent_decode("%C3%BC"), "ü");
    }

    fn no_missing(_: &Path) -> Vec<&'static str> {
        vec!["GFX"]
    }

    #[test]
    fn upload_roundtrip() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("s3upload-test-{}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join("gfx")).unwrap();
        let srv = UploadServer::start(dir.clone(), no_missing).unwrap();
        let send = |req: String, body: &[u8]| {
            let mut s = TcpStream::connect(("127.0.0.1", srv.port)).unwrap();
            s.write_all(req.as_bytes()).unwrap();
            s.write_all(body).unwrap();
            let mut out = String::new();
            s.read_to_string(&mut out).unwrap();
            out
        };
        let k = srv.token.clone();
        let r = send(format!("POST /upload?k={k}&path=GFX%2F1.gfx HTTP/1.1\r\nContent-Length: 5\r\n\r\n"), b"hello");
        assert!(r.starts_with("HTTP/1.1 200"), "{r}");
        // Existing `gfx/` is reused (case-insensitive).
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(dir.join("gfx/1.gfx")).unwrap(), b"hello");
        let r = send(format!("POST /upload?k={k}&path=..%2Fx HTTP/1.1\r\nContent-Length: 1\r\n\r\n"), b"x");
        assert!(r.starts_with("HTTP/1.1 400"), "{r}");
        let r = send("GET /?k=wrong HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n".into(), b"");
        assert!(r.starts_with("HTTP/1.1 403"), "{r}");
        let r = send(format!("GET /stat?k={k}&path=GFX/1.gfx HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n"), b"");
        assert!(r.ends_with("{\"size\":5}"), "{r}");
        let r = send(format!("GET /status?k={k} HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n"), b"");
        assert!(r.contains("\"missing\":[\"GFX\"],\"files\":1,\"bytes\":5"), "{r}");
        let st = srv.snapshot();
        assert_eq!((st.files, st.bytes), (1, 5));
        drop(srv);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-frontend/src/upscale_ai.rs`:

```rs
//! "AI" display filter: Anime4K's small CNN x2 upscaler (`crate::anime4k`, MIT) run on the GPU per new game frame
//! (docs/porting/display.md "AI upscaling filter").
//!
//! Needs a GLES 3 context and renderable half-float textures. Four convolution passes at the game frame's size
//! (RGBA16F, ping-pong `a` / `b`), then depth-to-space into an RGBA8 texture twice the frame size = bilinear frame
//! + the network's residual. The presenter then draws that texture instead of the game frame (same normalized
//! texture coordinates, so menu layouts / the Classic panel split quads work unchanged).

use crate::anime4k;
use crate::gl::*;

struct Pass {
    id: GLuint,
    u_tex: GLint,
    u_pt: GLint,
}

pub struct AiUpscaler {
    conv: Vec<Pass>,
    d2s: GLuint,
    d2s_last: GLint,
    d2s_main: GLint,
    d2s_size: GLint,
    fbo: GLuint,
    a: GLuint,
    b: GLuint,
    out: GLuint,
    size: (u32, u32),
}

unsafe fn tex(w: u32, h: u32, half: bool) -> GLuint {
    let mut t = 0;
    glGenTextures(1, &mut t);
    glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, t);
    if half {
        glTexImage2D(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0, GL_RGBA16F as GLint, w as i32, h as i32, 0, GL_RGBA, GL_HALF_FLOAT, std::ptr::null());
    } else {
        glTexImage2D(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0, GL_RGBA8 as GLint, w as i32, h as i32, 0, GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, std::ptr::null());
    }
    let f = if half { GL_NEAREST } else { GL_LINEAR };
    glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, f);
    glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, f);
    glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_WRAP_S, GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE);
    glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_WRAP_T, GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE);
    t
}

impl AiUpscaler {
    /// Compile the passes (GLES 3 context required).
    pub unsafe fn new() -> Result<AiUpscaler, String> {
        let mut conv = Vec::new();
        for fs in anime4k::CONV {
            let id = program_es3(fs)?;
            conv.push(Pass { id, u_tex: uniform(id, c"u_tex"), u_pt: uniform(id, c"u_pt") });
        }
        let d2s = program_es3(anime4k::DEPTH_TO_SPACE)?;
        let mut fbo = 0;
        glGenFramebuffers(1, &mut fbo);
        Ok(AiUpscaler {
            conv,
            d2s,
            d2s_last: uniform(d2s, c"u_last"),
            d2s_main: uniform(d2s, c"u_main"),
            d2s_size: uniform(d2s, c"u_last_size"),
            fbo,
            a: 0,
            b: 0,
            out: 0,
            size: (0, 0),
        })
    }

    unsafe fn ensure(&mut self, w: u32, h: u32) -> Result<(), String> {
        if self.size == (w, h) {
            return Ok(());
        }
        for t in [self.a, self.b, self.out] {
            if t != 0 {
                glDeleteTextures(1, &t);
            }
        }
        self.a = tex(w, h, true);
        self.b = tex(w, h, true);
        self.out = tex(2 * w, 2 * h, false);
        self.size = (w, h);
        glBindFramebuffer(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, self.fbo);
        for t in [self.a, self.out] {
            glFramebufferTexture2D(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0, GL_TEXTURE_2D, t, 0);
            let st = glCheckFramebufferStatus(GL_FRAMEBUFFER);
            if st != GL_FRAMEBUFFER_COMPLETE {
                glBindFramebuffer(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, 0);
                self.size = (0, 0);
                return Err(format!("framebuffer incomplete: {st:#x}"));
            }
        }
        glBindFramebuffer(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, 0);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Run the network on the game frame texture `main` (`w` x `h`); returns the 2x output texture (RGBA8,
    /// linear filtering). Leaves the default framebuffer bound; the caller sets its viewport / program again.
    pub unsafe fn run(&mut self, main: GLuint, w: u32, h: u32) -> Result<GLuint, String> {
        self.ensure(w, h)?;
        glBindFramebuffer(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, self.fbo);
        glDisable(GL_BLEND);
        glActiveTexture(GL_TEXTURE0);
        let (pw, ph) = (1.0 / w as f32, 1.0 / h as f32);
        glViewport(0, 0, w as i32, h as i32);
        // main -> a -> b -> a -> b
        let mut src = main;
        for (k, p) in self.conv.iter().enumerate() {
            let dst = if k % 2 == 0 { self.a } else { self.b };
            glFramebufferTexture2D(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0, GL_TEXTURE_2D, dst, 0);
            glUseProgram(p.id);
            glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, src);
            if k == 0 {
                glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, GL_NEAREST);
                glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, GL_NEAREST);
            }
            glUniform1i(p.u_tex, 0);
            glUniform2f(p.u_pt, pw, ph);
            glDrawArrays(GL_TRIANGLE_STRIP, 0, 4);
            src = dst;
        }
        // Depth to space at 2x: residual (last pass, nearest) + bilinear game frame.
        glFramebufferTexture2D(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0, GL_TEXTURE_2D, self.out, 0);
        glViewport(0, 0, 2 * w as i32, 2 * h as i32);
        glUseProgram(self.d2s);
        glActiveTexture(GL_TEXTURE1);
        glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, main);
        glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, GL_LINEAR);
        glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, GL_LINEAR);
        glActiveTexture(GL_TEXTURE0);
        glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, src);
        glUniform1i(self.d2s_last, 0);
        glUniform1i(self.d2s_main, 1);
        glUniform2f(self.d2s_size, w as f32, h as f32);
        glDrawArrays(GL_TRIANGLE_STRIP, 0, 4);
        glBindFramebuffer(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, 0);
        Ok(self.out)
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-ios/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! iOS frontend core: `libs3ios.a`, driven by the Swift shell in `port/ios` through the C API in
//! `port/ios/Sources/CS3iOS/include/s3ios.h` (docs/porting/ios.md).
//!
//! The Swift side owns UIKit: the window, a GLKView with an OpenGL ES context, CADisplayLink, touches, the soft
//! keyboard, haptics and the audio unit. Everything else is shared with the Android frontend (`s3_frontend`): the
//! launcher, the engine thread ([`run_engine`]), the GLES renderer ([`GlRenderer`] / [`Composer`]), touch ->
//! pointer events, the audio ring.
//!
//! Threads: every `s3ios_*` call except [`s3ios_audio_pull`] comes from the main thread. The engine runs on its own
//! thread (started by Play); the audio unit's render thread only reads the [`AudioRing`].

use std::ffi::{c_char, CStr};
use std::io::Write;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use s3_frontend::audio::AudioRing;
use s3_frontend::frontend::{run_engine, EngineEnd, Phase, Shared};
use s3_frontend::glrender::{Composer, GlRenderer};
use s3_frontend::launcher::{Launcher, Request, Touch};
use s3_frontend::touch::{pointer_events, Action, PointerFilter, Pos};
use s3_mods::display::Viewport;
use s3_runtime::HostEvent;

/// What the shell should do after [`s3ios_tick`] (`S3Out` in s3ios.h).
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct S3Out {
    /// Something new to show: call `display()` on the GL view (it calls [`s3ios_draw`]).
    pub redraw: u8,
    /// Soft keyboard: 0 = no change, 1 = show, 2 = hide, 3 = toggle.
    pub keyboard: u8,
    /// The app asked to close (launcher Quit).
    pub quit: u8,
    /// A game is running (not the launcher): the shell may keep the screen awake.
    pub in_game: u8,
    /// Vibrate this long (ms, 0 = no).
    pub haptic_ms: u32,
    /// Game folder: 1 = show the folder picker, 2 = forget the picked folder (use the app's own folder); the shell
    /// answers with [`s3ios_set_game_dir`].
    pub pick_folder: u8,
}

/// Frontend state owned by the shell (one per process).
pub struct App {
    shared: Arc<Shared>,
    woken: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    data_dir: PathBuf,
    launcher: Launcher,
    in_launcher: bool,
    launcher_drawn: Option<(u32, u32, u64)>,
    launcher_dirty: bool,
    engine_thread: Option<std::thread::JoinHandle<()>>,
    reqs: Vec<Request>,
    size: (u32, u32),
    dpi: u32,
    pointers: PointerFilter,
    /// Viewport frozen while two or more fingers are down (see the Android frontend: pinch zoom switches the
    /// render size every few frames).
    pinch_vp: Option<Viewport>,
    renderer: Option<GlRenderer>,
    gl_failed: bool,
    comp: Composer,
    keyboard: u8,
    pick_folder: u8,
    quit: bool,
    fps_t0: Instant,
    fps_n: u32,
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- logging

struct Logger {
    file: Mutex<Option<std::fs::File>>,
    t0: Instant,
}

impl log::Log for Logger {
    fn enabled(&self, m: &log::Metadata) -> bool {
        m.level() <= log::Level::Info
    }
    fn log(&self, r: &log::Record) {
        if !self.enabled(r.metadata()) {
            return;
        }
        let line = format!("{:8.3} {:5} {}\n", self.t0.elapsed().as_secs_f32(), r.level(), r.args());
        let _ = std::io::stderr().write_all(line.as_bytes());
        if let Some(f) = self.file.lock().unwrap().as_mut() {
            let _ = f.write_all(line.as_bytes());
        }
    }
    fn flush(&self) {
        if let Some(f) = self.file.lock().unwrap().as_mut() {
            let _ = f.flush();
        }
    }
}

static LOGGER: std::sync::OnceLock<Logger> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();

/// Log to stderr (Xcode / `idevicesyslog`) and to `<data dir>/log.txt` (last run; visible in the Files app when
/// the data dir is under Documents).
fn init_log(data_dir: &std::path::Path) {
    let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(data_dir);
    let file = std::fs::File::create(data_dir.join("log.txt")).ok();
    let l = LOGGER.get_or_init(|| Logger { file: Mutex::new(file), t0: Instant::now() });
    if log::set_logger(l).is_ok() {
        log::set_max_level(log::LevelFilter::Info);
    }
    std::panic::set_hook(Box::new(|info| {
        log::error!("PANIC: {info}");
        log::logger().flush();
    }));
}

unsafe fn path_arg(p: *const c_char) -> PathBuf {
    if p.is_null() {
        return PathBuf::new();
    }
    PathBuf::from(CStr::from_ptr(p).to_string_lossy().into_owned())
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- app logic

impl App {
    fn new(game_dir: PathBuf, data_dir: PathBuf) -> App {
        let woken = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(true));
        let w2 = woken.clone();
        let shared = Shared::new(Box::new(move || w2.store(true, Ordering::Release)));
        let game_dir = s3_frontend::launcher::game_dir_override(&data_dir, game_dir);
        let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(&game_dir);
        log::info!("S3 Mobile {} (iOS) starting; game dir {}, data dir {}", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"), game_dir.display(), data_dir.display());
        // The audio unit pulls from the ring from the start (silence until the engine plays something).
        shared.audio.running.store(true, Ordering::Release);
        let mut launcher = Launcher::new(game_dir, data_dir.clone());
        launcher.folder_picker = Some(false);
        App {
            launcher,
            shared,
            woken,
            data_dir,
            in_launcher: true,
            launcher_drawn: None,
            launcher_dirty: true,
            engine_thread: None,
            reqs: Vec::new(),
            size: (1, 1),
            dpi: 0,
            pointers: PointerFilter::default(),
            pinch_vp: None,
            renderer: None,
            gl_failed: false,
            comp: Composer::new(),
            keyboard: 0,
            pick_folder: 0,
            quit: false,
            fps_t0: Instant::now(),
            fps_n: 0,
        }
    }

    fn start_engine(&mut self) {
        self.shared.engine_end.lock().unwrap().take();
        self.shared.guest_exited.store(false, Ordering::Release);
        self.shared.events.lock().unwrap().clear();
        self.shared.frame.lock().unwrap().fb = None;
        self.shared.set_status(Phase::Starting, "Starting", "Loading the game ...");
        self.keyboard = 2;
        let sh = self.shared.clone();
        let (g, d) = (self.launcher.game_dir().to_path_buf(), self.data_dir.clone());
        self.engine_thread = Some(
            std::thread::Builder::new()
                .name("s3-engine".into())
                .stack_size(16 << 20)
                .spawn(move || {
                    let end = run_engine(sh.clone(), g, d).unwrap_or(EngineEnd { title: "Stopped".into(), body: String::new(), exited: false });
                    *sh.engine_end.lock().unwrap() = Some(end);
                    (sh.wake)();
                })
                .expect("spawn engine thread"),
        );
        self.in_launcher = false;
        self.shared.set_launcher(None);
    }

    fn tick(&mut self) -> S3Out {
        let mut out = S3Out::default();
        // The engine run ended (Exit Game, error): back to the launcher.
        if self.engine_thread.is_some() {
            if let Some(end) = self.shared.engine_end.lock().unwrap().take() {
                if let Some(t) = self.engine_thread.take() {
                    let _ = t.join();
                }
                log::info!("launcher: engine ended ({}{})", end.title, if end.exited { ", game exited" } else { "" });
                self.shared.in_game.store(false, Ordering::Release);
                self.shared.frame.lock().unwrap().fb = None;
                self.launcher.message = Some(if end.exited {
                    ("The game was closed. Tap Play to start it again.".to_string(), false)
                } else {
                    let first = end.body.lines().next().unwrap_or("").to_string();
                    (format!("{}: {first}", end.title), true)
                });
                self.launcher.reload_settings();
                self.launcher.recheck();
                self.in_launcher = true;
                self.launcher_drawn = None;
                self.launcher_dirty = true;
            }
        }
        if self.in_launcher {
            for r in std::mem::take(&mut self.reqs) {
                log::info!("launcher: {r:?}");
                match r {
                    Request::Play if self.engine_thread.is_none() => self.start_engine(),
                    Request::Play => {}
                    Request::Keyboard(show) => self.keyboard = if show { 1 } else { 2 },
                    Request::PickFolder => self.pick_folder = 1,
                    Request::UseAppFolder => self.pick_folder = 2,
                    Request::Quit => {
                        self.launcher.stop_upload();
                        self.quit = true;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        if self.in_launcher {
            self.launcher_dirty |= self.launcher.tick();
            let hz = f32::from_bits(self.shared.refresh_hz.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
            self.launcher.refresh_hz = if hz > 0.0 { hz.round() as u32 } else { 0 };
            let (w, h) = self.size;
            if self.launcher_dirty || self.launcher_drawn.map(|d| (d.0, d.1)) != Some((w, h)) {
                self.launcher_dirty = false;
                let list = self.launcher.draw(w, h, self.dpi);
                if self.launcher_drawn != Some((w, h, list.hash)) {
                    self.launcher_drawn = Some((w, h, list.hash));
                    self.shared.set_launcher(Some(Arc::new(list)));
                }
            }
        }
        if self.shared.keyboard_req.swap(false, Ordering::AcqRel) {
            self.keyboard = 3;
        }
        let buzz = std::mem::take(&mut *self.shared.haptic.lock().unwrap());
        out.haptic_ms = buzz.iter().copied().max().unwrap_or(0);
        out.keyboard = std::mem::take(&mut self.keyboard);
        out.pick_folder = std::mem::take(&mut self.pick_folder);
        out.quit = self.quit as u8;
        out.in_game = !self.in_launcher as u8;
        self.woken.store(false, Ordering::Release);
        out.redraw = self.comp.has_news(&self.shared) as u8;
        // Display rate (FPS counter) while nothing is drawn.
        let el = self.fps_t0.elapsed();
        if el >= Duration::from_secs(1) {
            self.shared.host_fps.store((self.fps_n as f32 / el.as_secs_f32()).to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
            self.fps_n = 0;
            self.fps_t0 = Instant::now();
        }
        out
    }

    /// Draw into the GL view's framebuffer (bound by GLKit) of `w` x `h` pixels.
    unsafe fn draw(&mut self, w: u32, h: u32) {
        if self.gl_failed {
            return;
        }
        if self.renderer.is_none() {
            match GlRenderer::new(false) {
                Ok(r) => {
                    log::info!("present: GLES renderer ready ({w}x{h})");
                    self.renderer = Some(r);
                }
                Err(e) => {
                    log::error!("present: GL setup failed: {e}");
                    self.gl_failed = true;
                    return;
                }
            }
        }
        let r = self.renderer.as_mut().unwrap();
        r.bind_state();
        let picked = self.comp.pick(&self.shared);
        self.comp.draw_gl(&self.shared, r, (w.max(1), h.max(1)), &picked);
        self.fps_n += 1;
    }

    fn resize(&mut self, w: u32, h: u32, dpi: u32) {
        let (w, h) = (w.max(1), h.max(1));
        if (w, h) != self.size || dpi != self.dpi {
            log::info!("window {w}x{h} px, {dpi} dpi");
            self.size = (w, h);
            self.dpi = dpi;
            self.shared.density_dpi.store(dpi, Ordering::Relaxed);
            self.comp.reset();
            if let Some(r) = self.renderer.as_mut() {
                r.ltex_size = (0, 0);
            }
            self.launcher_dirty = true;
            self.shared.display_seq.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
            self.shared.notify_render();
        }
    }

    fn touch(&mut self, action: Action, id: i32, x: f32, y: f32, all: &[(i32, f32, f32)]) {
        if self.in_launcher {
            // Launcher: the first finger only, in window pixels.
            let first = all.first().map(|a| a.0).unwrap_or(id);
            if id != first && !matches!(action, Action::Cancel) {
                return;
            }
            let t = match action {
                Action::Down => Touch::Down,
                Action::Move => Touch::Move,
                Action::Up => Touch::Up,
                Action::Cancel => Touch::Cancel,
                _ => return,
            };
            if t == Touch::Down {
                log::info!("launcher: touch at ({x:.0},{y:.0})");
            }
            if let Some(r) = self.launcher.touch(t, x as i32, y as i32) {
                self.reqs.push(r);
            }
            self.launcher_dirty = true;
            return;
        }
        let Some(cur_vp) = *self.shared.viewport.lock().unwrap() else { return };
        let vp = match action {
            Action::PointerDown => *self.pinch_vp.get_or_insert(cur_vp),
            Action::Up | Action::Cancel => self.pinch_vp.take().unwrap_or(cur_vp),
            _ => self.pinch_vp.unwrap_or(cur_vp),
        };
        let pos = |x: f32, y: f32| -> Pos {
            let g = vp.window_to_game(x, y);
            (g.0, g.1, x.max(0.0) as i32, y.max(0.0) as i32)
        };
        let all: Vec<(i32, Pos)> = all.iter().map(|&(i, ax, ay)| (i, pos(ax, ay))).collect();
        for ev in pointer_events(action, (id, pos(x, y)), &all) {
            if self.pointers.keep(&ev) {
                self.shared.push_event(ev);
            }
        }
    }

    fn pause(&mut self) {
        log::info!("lifecycle: background (paused)");
        self.shared.set_paused(true);
    }

    fn resume(&mut self) {
        log::info!("lifecycle: foreground");
        self.shared.set_paused(false);
        // Drop sound queued before the pause (it would play late).
        self.shared.audio.clear();
        self.shared.display_seq.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
        self.shared.notify_render();
    }

    fn text(&mut self, c: u32) {
        if self.in_launcher {
            if let Some(r) = self.launcher.char(c) {
                self.reqs.push(r);
            }
            self.launcher_dirty = true;
            return;
        }
        // Backspace / Enter also as keys (the game's text fields read WM_KEYDOWN for them).
        let vk = match c {
            8 => Some(0x08),
            13 | 10 => Some(0x0d),
            _ => char::from_u32(c).and_then(s3_frontend::keys::vk_for_char),
        };
        if let Some(vk) = vk {
            self.shared.push_event(HostEvent::Key { vk, down: true });
        }
        self.shared.push_event(HostEvent::Char(if c == 10 { 13 } else { c }));
        if let Some(vk) = vk {
            self.shared.push_event(HostEvent::Key { vk, down: false });
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for App {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        log::info!("shutting down");
        self.launcher.stop_upload();
        self.shared.request_quit();
        if let Some(t) = self.engine_thread.take() {
            let _ = t.join();
        }
        log::logger().flush();
    }
}

/// Create the app. `game_dir`: where the user's Settlers III files go (Documents/..., visible in Files);
/// `data_dir`: settings, saves of our own, logs.
///
/// # Safety
/// Both arguments are NUL-terminated UTF-8 paths (or null).
#[no_mangle]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn s3ios_create(game_dir: *const c_char, data_dir: *const c_char) -> *mut App {
    let (g, d) = (path_arg(game_dir), path_arg(data_dir));
    init_log(&d);
    Box::into_raw(Box::new(App::new(g, d)))
}

/// # Safety
/// `app` comes from [`s3ios_create`] and is not used afterwards.
#[no_mangle]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn s3ios_destroy(app: *mut App) {
    if !app.is_null() {
        drop(Box::from_raw(app));
    }
}

/// View size in pixels (points * contentScaleFactor) and the screen density.
///
/// # Safety
/// `app` comes from [`s3ios_create`].
#[no_mangle]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn s3ios_resize(app: *mut App, w: u32, h: u32, dpi: u32) {
    (*app).resize(w, h, dpi);
}

/// The screen's maximum refresh rate (`UIScreen.maximumFramesPerSecond`, 120 on ProMotion iPhones): shown by the
/// FPS counter and offered by the FPS limit setting.
///
/// # Safety
/// `app` comes from [`s3ios_create`].
#[no_mangle]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn s3ios_set_refresh(app: *mut App, hz: u32) {
    let app = &*app;
    app.shared.refresh_hz.store((hz as f32).to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
}

/// Once per display refresh (CADisplayLink), before drawing.
///
/// # Safety
/// `app` comes from [`s3ios_create`].
#[no_mangle]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn s3ios_tick(app: *mut App) -> S3Out {
    (*app).tick()
}

/// Draw the current image into the bound framebuffer (GLKView `draw(in:)`, its EAGLContext current).
///
/// # Safety
/// `app` comes from [`s3ios_create`]; a GLES context is current on this thread.
#[no_mangle]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn s3ios_draw(app: *mut App, w: u32, h: u32) {
    (*app).draw(w, h);
}

/// Touch event. `action`: 0 down (first finger), 1 pointer down (another finger), 2 move, 3 pointer up (not the
/// last finger), 4 up (last finger), 5 cancel. `id`, `x`, `y`: the finger the action is about (window pixels);
/// `ids` / `xs` / `ys` (`n` entries): every finger currently down, including the acting one.
///
/// # Safety
/// `app` comes from [`s3ios_create`]; the arrays hold `n` elements (or `n` is 0).
#[no_mangle]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn s3ios_touch(app: *mut App, action: i32, id: i32, x: f32, y: f32, n: i32, ids: *const i32, xs: *const f32, ys: *const f32) {
    let action = match action {
        0 => Action::Down,
        1 => Action::PointerDown,
        2 => Action::Move,
        3 => Action::PointerUp,
        4 => Action::Up,
        _ => Action::Cancel,
    };
    let n = n.max(0) as usize;
    let all: Vec<(i32, f32, f32)> = if n == 0 || ids.is_null() || xs.is_null() || ys.is_null() {
        vec![(id, x, y)]
    } else {
        let (ids, xs, ys) = (std::slice::from_raw_parts(ids, n), std::slice::from_raw_parts(xs, n), std::slice::from_raw_parts(ys, n));
        (0..n).map(|i| (ids[i], xs[i], ys[i])).collect()
    };
    (*app).touch(action, id, x, y, &all);
}

/// Typed character from the soft / hardware keyboard (Unicode scalar; 8 = backspace, 10/13 = return).
///
/// # Safety
/// `app` comes from [`s3ios_create`].
#[no_mangle]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn s3ios_text(app: *mut App, c: u32) {
    (*app).text(c);
}

/// Hardware key (Windows virtual key code) down / up (UIPress from a hardware keyboard).
///
/// # Safety
/// `app` comes from [`s3ios_create`].
#[no_mangle]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn s3ios_key(app: *mut App, vk: u32, down: u8) {
    if !(*app).in_launcher {
        (*app).shared.push_event(HostEvent::Key { vk, down: down != 0 });
    }
}

/// Character typed on a hardware keyboard (its key went through [`s3ios_key`] already): only the WM_CHAR part in
/// the game; the launcher gets it like typed text.
///
/// # Safety
/// `app` comes from [`s3ios_create`].
#[no_mangle]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn s3ios_char(app: *mut App, c: u32) {
    let app = &mut *app;
    if app.in_launcher {
        app.text(c);
    } else {
        app.shared.push_event(HostEvent::Char(if c == 10 { 13 } else { c }));
    }
}

/// Use `dir` as the game folder: a folder the user picked (`external` = 1, security-scoped access already started by
/// the shell) or the app's own one (0). Ignored while a game runs.
///
/// # Safety
/// `app` comes from [`s3ios_create`]; `dir` is a NUL-terminated UTF-8 path.
#[no_mangle]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn s3ios_set_game_dir(app: *mut App, dir: *const c_char, external: u8) {
    let app = &mut *app;
    if !app.in_launcher {
        log::warn!("set_game_dir while a game runs: ignored");
        return;
    }
    let d = path_arg(dir);
    if external == 0 {
        let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(&d);
    }
    app.launcher.set_game_dir(d, external != 0);
    app.launcher_dirty = true;
}

/// App goes to the background (`background` = 1) or comes back (0).
///
/// # Safety
/// `app` comes from [`s3ios_create`].
#[no_mangle]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn s3ios_set_background(app: *mut App, background: u8) {
    if background != 0 {
        (*app).pause();
    } else {
        (*app).resume();
    }
}

/// Audio source for the audio unit's render thread (stays valid until [`s3ios_audio_release`]).
///
/// # Safety
/// `app` comes from [`s3ios_create`].
#[no_mangle]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn s3ios_audio_handle(app: *mut App) -> *const AudioRing {
    let app = &*app;
    Arc::into_raw(app.shared.audio.clone())
}

/// Fill `frames` interleaved stereo i16 frames at 44100 Hz (silence when nothing is queued).
///
/// # Safety
/// `ring` comes from [`s3ios_audio_handle`]; `out` holds `frames * 2` samples.
#[no_mangle]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn s3ios_audio_pull(ring: *const AudioRing, out: *mut i16, frames: u32) {
    let out = std::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(out, frames as usize * 2);
    (*ring).pop_into(out);
}

/// # Safety
/// `ring` comes from [`s3ios_audio_handle`] and is not used afterwards.
#[no_mangle]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn s3ios_audio_release(ring: *const AudioRing) {
    if !ring.is_null() {
        drop(Arc::from_raw(ring));
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-mem/src/heap.rs`:

```rs
//! Guest heaps (`HeapCreate`/`HeapAlloc`/...). Metadata lives on the host side.
//!
//! Each heap owns one or more segments (VirtualAlloc'd, committed). Free space is tracked in two maps
//! (by address for coalescing, by (size, address) for best-fit). Blocks are 8-byte aligned (like Windows).

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet, HashMap};

use crate::layout::{ALLOC_ARENA_END, ALLOC_ARENA_START, ALLOC_GRANULARITY};
use crate::regions::{RegionKind, Regions, PAGE_READWRITE};
use crate::{align_up, MemError};

pub const HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY: u32 = 0x08;
pub const HEAP_REALLOC_IN_PLACE_ONLY: u32 = 0x10;

const MIN_SEGMENT: u32 = 0x10_0000; // 1 MiB
const ALIGN: u32 = 8;

/// One guest heap.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct GuestHeap {
    /// (base, size) of each segment; the first segment's base is the heap handle.
    pub segments: Vec<(u32, u32)>,
    free_by_addr: BTreeMap<u32, u32>,
    free_by_size: BTreeSet<(u32, u32)>,
    /// ptr -> (block size, requested size)
    used: HashMap<u32, (u32, u32)>,
    /// Bytes currently handed out (block sizes).
    pub used_bytes: u64,
}

impl GuestHeap {
    fn insert_free(&mut self, mut addr: u32, mut size: u32) {
        // Coalesce with predecessor.
        if let Some((&pa, &ps)) = self.free_by_addr.range(..addr).next_back() {
            if pa as u64 + ps as u64 == addr as u64 {
                self.free_by_addr.remove(&pa);
                self.free_by_size.remove(&(ps, pa));
                addr = pa;
                size += ps;
            }
        }
        // Coalesce with successor.
        let end = addr as u64 + size as u64;
        if end <= u32::MAX as u64 {
            if let Some(&ns) = self.free_by_addr.get(&(end as u32)) {
                self.free_by_addr.remove(&(end as u32));
                self.free_by_size.remove(&(ns, end as u32));
                size += ns;
            }
        }
        self.free_by_addr.insert(addr, size);
        self.free_by_size.insert((size, addr));
    }

    fn take_free(&mut self, size: u32) -> Option<u32> {
        let &(fs, fa) = self.free_by_size.range((size, 0)..).next()?;
        self.free_by_size.remove(&(fs, fa));
        self.free_by_addr.remove(&fa);
        if fs > size {
            let rest = fa + size;
            let rs = fs - size;
            self.free_by_addr.insert(rest, rs);
            self.free_by_size.insert((rs, rest));
        }
        Some(fa)
    }

    /// Number of live blocks.
    pub fn live_blocks(&self) -> usize {
        self.used.len()
    }

    /// Total free bytes in all segments.
    pub fn free_bytes(&self) -> u64 {
        self.free_by_addr.values().map(|&s| s as u64).sum()
    }
}

/// All guest heaps by handle.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct Heaps {
    heaps: BTreeMap<u32, GuestHeap>,
}

fn block_size(size: u32) -> u32 {
    align_up(size.max(1), ALIGN)
}

impl Heaps {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    /// Heap by handle.
    pub fn get(&self, heap: u32) -> Option<&GuestHeap> {
        self.heaps.get(&heap)
    }

    /// All heap handles.
    pub fn handles(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = u32> + '_ {
        self.heaps.keys().copied()
    }

    fn add_segment(regions: &mut Regions, min: u32) -> Result<(u32, u32), MemError> {
        let size = align_up(min.max(MIN_SEGMENT), ALLOC_GRANULARITY);
        let base = regions.reserve_in(None, size, RegionKind::Private, PAGE_READWRITE, (ALLOC_ARENA_START, ALLOC_ARENA_END))?;
        regions.commit(base, size, PAGE_READWRITE)?;
        Ok((base, size))
    }

    /// Create a heap. `max` is ignored (heaps are growable).
    pub fn create(&mut self, regions: &mut Regions, initial: u32, _max: u32) -> Result<u32, MemError> {
        let (base, size) = Self::add_segment(regions, initial)?;
        let mut h = GuestHeap::default();
        h.segments.push((base, size));
        h.insert_free(base, size);
        self.heaps.insert(base, h);
        Ok(base)
    }

    /// Destroy a heap; returns its segments so the caller can release them.
    pub fn destroy(&mut self, heap: u32) -> Result<Vec<(u32, u32)>, MemError> {
        let h = self.heaps.remove(&heap).ok_or(MemError::BadHeap(heap))?;
        Ok(h.segments)
    }

    /// Allocate `size` bytes. The memory is NOT zeroed here (see `GuestMemory::heap_alloc`).
    pub fn alloc(&mut self, regions: &mut Regions, heap: u32, size: u32) -> Result<u32, MemError> {
        let bs = block_size(size);
        let h = self.heaps.get_mut(&heap).ok_or(MemError::BadHeap(heap))?;
        let p = match h.take_free(bs) {
            Some(p) => p,
            None => {
                let (base, ssize) = Self::add_segment(regions, bs)?;
                h.segments.push((base, ssize));
                h.insert_free(base, ssize);
                h.take_free(bs).ok_or(MemError::OutOfSpace)?
            }
        };
        h.used.insert(p, (bs, size));
        h.used_bytes += bs as u64;
        Ok(p)
    }

    /// Free a block.
    pub fn free(&mut self, heap: u32, ptr: u32) -> Result<(), MemError> {
        let h = self.heaps.get_mut(&heap).ok_or(MemError::BadHeap(heap))?;
        let (bs, _) = h.used.remove(&ptr).ok_or(MemError::NotAllocated { addr: ptr, len: 0 })?;
        h.used_bytes -= bs as u64;
        h.insert_free(ptr, bs);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Requested size of a live block.
    pub fn size(&self, heap: u32, ptr: u32) -> Option<u32> {
        self.heaps.get(&heap)?.used.get(&ptr).map(|&(_, s)| s)
    }

    /// Which heap owns `ptr` (any heap), if it is a live block.
    pub fn owner_of(&self, ptr: u32) -> Option<u32> {
        self.heaps.iter().find(|(_, h)| h.used.contains_key(&ptr)).map(|(k, _)| *k)
    }

    /// Shrink or grow a block without moving it. Returns false if it cannot grow in place.
    pub fn try_resize_in_place(&mut self, heap: u32, ptr: u32, size: u32) -> bool {
        let Some(h) = self.heaps.get_mut(&heap) else { return false };
        let Some(&(bs, _)) = h.used.get(&ptr) else { return false };
        let nbs = block_size(size);
        if nbs <= bs {
            if nbs < bs {
                h.insert_free(ptr + nbs, bs - nbs);
                h.used_bytes -= (bs - nbs) as u64;
            }
            h.used.insert(ptr, (nbs, size));
            return true;
        }
        let next = ptr + bs;
        let need = nbs - bs;
        match h.free_by_addr.get(&next).copied() {
            Some(fs) if fs >= need => {
                h.free_by_addr.remove(&next);
                h.free_by_size.remove(&(fs, next));
                if fs > need {
                    h.free_by_addr.insert(next + need, fs - need);
                    h.free_by_size.insert((fs - need, next + need));
                }
                h.used.insert(ptr, (nbs, size));
                h.used_bytes += need as u64;
                true
            }
            _ => false,
        }
    }
}

```

`port/crates/s3-mem/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! Guest 32-bit address space for the Settlers III port.
//!
//! One 4 GiB (+ guard) host reservation backs the whole guest address space: guest address `g` lives at host
//! address `base + g`. The reservation is `PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE`, `MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS|MAP_NORESERVE`,
//! so untouched pages cost nothing and every guest access is a plain host load/store (no fault handling).
//!
//! On top of the raw window this crate keeps *bookkeeping* for Win32 semantics:
//! - [`Regions`]: VirtualAlloc/VirtualFree/VirtualProtect/VirtualQuery (64 KiB allocation granularity).
//! - [`Heaps`]: HeapCreate/HeapAlloc/HeapFree/HeapReAlloc/HeapSize with metadata kept on the host side
//!   (guest buffer overruns cannot corrupt the allocator).
//!
//! The address map is in [`layout`]; see `docs/porting/architecture.md`.

mod heap;
mod regions;
mod sys;

pub use heap::{GuestHeap, Heaps, HEAP_REALLOC_IN_PLACE_ONLY, HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY};
pub use regions::{
    Allocation, MemoryInfo, RegionKind, Regions, MEM_COMMIT, MEM_DECOMMIT, MEM_FREE, MEM_IMAGE, MEM_MAPPED,
    MEM_PRIVATE, MEM_RELEASE, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_EXECUTE, PAGE_EXECUTE_READ, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE, PAGE_NOACCESS,
    PAGE_READONLY, PAGE_READWRITE,
};

use std::fmt;

/// Guest address map. All values are guest virtual addresses.
pub mod layout {
    /// Size of the guest window.
    pub const WINDOW_SIZE: u64 = 1 << 32;
    /// Extra host bytes mapped after the window so that `addr + 16` never leaves the mapping.
    pub const GUARD_SIZE: u64 = 1 << 16;
    /// Page size.
    pub const PAGE_SIZE: u32 = 0x1000;
    /// VirtualAlloc allocation granularity.
    pub const ALLOC_GRANULARITY: u32 = 0x1_0000;
    /// Accesses below this address are treated as NULL-pointer faults by the CPU.
    pub const NULL_GUARD_END: u32 = 0x0001_0000;
    /// Low arena: process parameters, environment block, misc runtime data.
    pub const LOW_ARENA_START: u32 = 0x0001_0000;
    pub const LOW_ARENA_END: u32 = 0x0040_0000;
    /// S3.EXE image (fixed base, no relocations).
    pub const IMAGE_BASE: u32 = 0x0040_0000;
    pub const IMAGE_END: u32 = 0x007E_D000;
    /// VirtualAlloc / heap arena (anything without a fixed address).
    pub const ALLOC_ARENA_START: u32 = 0x1000_0000;
    pub const ALLOC_ARENA_END: u32 = 0x7000_0000;
    /// Thread stacks.
    pub const STACK_ARENA_START: u32 = 0x7000_0000;
    pub const STACK_ARENA_END: u32 = 0x7F00_0000;
    /// System area: TEBs (one page each, growing down from `TEB_TOP`) and the PEB.
    pub const SYSTEM_AREA_START: u32 = 0x7F00_0000;
    pub const SYSTEM_AREA_END: u32 = 0x7FFF_0000;
    /// PEB address (Windows-like).
    pub const PEB_ADDR: u32 = 0x7FFD_F000;
    /// TEB of thread slot 0; slot `i` is at `TEB_TOP - i * PAGE_SIZE`.
    pub const TEB_TOP: u32 = 0x7FFD_E000;
    /// Fake module handles for HLE DLLs (`ddraw.dll`, `kernel32.dll`, ...): `FAKE_MODULE_BASE + i * 0x10000`.
    pub const FAKE_MODULE_BASE: u32 = 0x7800_0000;
    /// Every HLE function is one address in `[THUNK_BASE, THUNK_END)`. The CPU exits when EIP enters it.
    pub const THUNK_BASE: u32 = 0xFFF0_0000;
    pub const THUNK_END: u32 = 0xFFFF_F000;
    /// Return address pushed by host->guest calls; the CPU exits with `ReturnMagic` when EIP reaches it.
    pub const MAGIC_RETURN: u32 = 0xFFFF_F000;
}

/// Errors from guest memory operations.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MemError {
    /// Range overlaps an existing allocation.
    Overlap { addr: u32, len: u32 },
    /// Range is not (fully) inside an allocation / not committed.
    NotAllocated { addr: u32, len: u32 },
    /// Bad parameters (zero size, wrap-around, misaligned base for release, ...).
    BadRange { addr: u32, len: u32 },
    /// No free address space left in the arena.
    OutOfSpace,
    /// Unknown heap handle.
    BadHeap(u32),
    /// Host OS error (errno).
    Os(i32),
}

impl fmt::Display for MemError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            MemError::Overlap { addr, len } => write!(f, "guest range {addr:#x}+{len:#x} overlaps an allocation"),
            MemError::NotAllocated { addr, len } => write!(f, "guest range {addr:#x}+{len:#x} is not allocated"),
            MemError::BadRange { addr, len } => write!(f, "invalid guest range {addr:#x}+{len:#x}"),
            MemError::OutOfSpace => write!(f, "guest address space exhausted"),
            MemError::BadHeap(h) => write!(f, "unknown heap handle {h:#x}"),
            MemError::Os(e) => write!(f, "host error {e}"),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for MemError {}

/// Round `v` up to a multiple of `align` (power of two). Saturates at `u32::MAX & !(align-1)`.
#[inline]
pub fn align_up(v: u32, align: u32) -> u32 {
    let a = align - 1;
    match v.checked_add(a) {
        Some(x) => x & !a,
        None => u32::MAX & !a,
    }
}

/// Round `v` down to a multiple of `align` (power of two).
#[inline]
pub fn align_down(v: u32, align: u32) -> u32 {
    v & !(align - 1)
}

/// The guest address space.
///
/// Reads take `&self`, writes take `&mut self`. All accessors accept any `u32` address: the whole window is
/// mapped, so there is no failure path (unallocated memory reads as zero). Wrap-around (`addr + len > 2^32`)
/// panics for slices.
pub struct GuestMemory {
    base: *mut u8,
    /// VirtualAlloc bookkeeping.
    pub regions: Regions,
    /// Guest heaps (HeapCreate & co).
    pub heaps: Heaps,
    process_heap: u32,
    /// False for an alias view ([`GuestMemory::alias_view`]): it does not release the window on drop.
    owns_window: bool,
}

// The raw pointer is only an address; `GuestMemory` owns its mapping exclusively.
unsafe impl Send for GuestMemory {}

impl fmt::Debug for GuestMemory {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("GuestMemory").field("base", &self.base).finish()
    }
}

macro_rules! rw_num {
    ($read:ident, $write:ident, $t:ty) => {
        #[inline(always)]
        pub fn $read(&self, addr: u32) -> $t {
            // SAFETY: the window is 4 GiB + guard and addr < 2^32, so addr + size_of::<$t>() is in bounds.
            unsafe { <$t>::from_le_bytes(std::ptr::read_unaligned(self.base.add(addr as usize) as *const _)) }
        }
        #[inline(always)]
        pub fn $write(&mut self, addr: u32, v: $t) {
            // SAFETY: see read.
            unsafe { std::ptr::write_unaligned(self.base.add(addr as usize) as *mut _, v.to_le_bytes()) }
        }
    };
}

impl GuestMemory {
    /// Reserve the 4 GiB window and create the process heap.
    pub fn new() -> Result<Self, MemError> {
        let base = sys::reserve_window((layout::WINDOW_SIZE + layout::GUARD_SIZE) as usize)?;
        let mut m =
            GuestMemory { base, regions: Regions::new(), heaps: Heaps::new(), process_heap: 0, owns_window: true };
        m.process_heap = m.heap_create(0x10_0000, 0)?;
        Ok(m)
    }

    /// A second handle on the same guest window for a CPU running on another host thread (multi-core mode,
    /// docs/porting/multicore.md): same base pointer, **empty** `regions`/`heaps` (the bookkeeping stays with the
    /// owner), and it never unmaps the window.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    /// The view must not outlive `self`, and it may only be used for plain guest loads/stores (what `Cpu::run`
    /// does). Concurrent accesses through both handles race exactly like guest threads on a real multi-core PC.
    pub unsafe fn alias_view(&self) -> GuestMemory {
        GuestMemory { base: self.base, regions: Regions::new(), heaps: Heaps::new(), process_heap: 0, owns_window: false }
    }

    /// Host pointer of guest address 0.
    pub fn base_ptr(&self) -> *mut u8 {
        self.base
    }

    /// Host pointer for a guest address.
    #[inline]
    pub fn host_ptr(&self, addr: u32) -> *mut u8 {
        // SAFETY: in bounds of the window.
        unsafe { self.base.add(addr as usize) }
    }

    rw_num!(read_u8, write_u8, u8);
    rw_num!(read_u16, write_u16, u16);
    rw_num!(read_u32, write_u32, u32);
    rw_num!(read_u64, write_u64, u64);
    rw_num!(read_i8, write_i8, i8);
    rw_num!(read_i16, write_i16, i16);
    rw_num!(read_i32, write_i32, i32);
    rw_num!(read_f32, write_f32, f32);
    rw_num!(read_f64, write_f64, f64);

    #[inline]
    fn check(addr: u32, len: usize) {
        assert!(
            addr as u64 + len as u64 <= layout::WINDOW_SIZE,
            "guest slice {addr:#x}+{len:#x} wraps the 4 GiB window"
        );
    }

    /// Borrow guest bytes.
    pub fn slice(&self, addr: u32, len: usize) -> &[u8] {
        Self::check(addr, len);
        // SAFETY: bounds checked; the mapping lives as long as self.
        unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(self.base.add(addr as usize), len) }
    }

    /// Mutably borrow guest bytes.
    pub fn slice_mut(&mut self, addr: u32, len: usize) -> &mut [u8] {
        Self::check(addr, len);
        // SAFETY: bounds checked; &mut self guarantees exclusivity.
        unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(self.base.add(addr as usize), len) }
    }

    /// Copy bytes out of guest memory.
    pub fn read_bytes(&self, addr: u32, len: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
        self.slice(addr, len).to_vec()
    }

    /// Copy bytes into guest memory.
    pub fn write_bytes(&mut self, addr: u32, data: &[u8]) {
        self.slice_mut(addr, data.len()).copy_from_slice(data);
    }

    /// Fill guest memory with a byte.
    pub fn fill(&mut self, addr: u32, len: usize, value: u8) {
        self.slice_mut(addr, len).fill(value);
    }

    /// Copy within guest memory (memmove semantics).
    pub fn copy_within(&mut self, src: u32, dst: u32, len: usize) {
        Self::check(src, len);
        Self::check(dst, len);
        // SAFETY: both ranges in bounds; ptr::copy handles overlap.
        unsafe { std::ptr::copy(self.base.add(src as usize), self.base.add(dst as usize), len) }
    }

    /// Length of the NUL-terminated byte string at `addr` (scans at most `max` bytes).
    pub fn strlen(&self, addr: u32, max: usize) -> usize {
        let max = max.min((layout::WINDOW_SIZE - addr as u64) as usize);
        let s = self.slice(addr, max);
        s.iter().position(|&b| b == 0).unwrap_or(max)
    }

    /// NUL-terminated ANSI string bytes (without the NUL), at most 64 KiB.
    pub fn read_cstr_bytes(&self, addr: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
        let n = self.strlen(addr, 0x1_0000);
        self.read_bytes(addr, n)
    }

    /// NUL-terminated ANSI string decoded as Windows-1252/Latin-1 (each byte -> one char).
    pub fn read_cstr(&self, addr: u32) -> String {
        self.read_cstr_bytes(addr).iter().map(|&b| b as char).collect()
    }

    /// Write `s` (chars > 0xFF become '?') plus a NUL. Returns bytes written including the NUL.
    pub fn write_cstr(&mut self, addr: u32, s: &str) -> usize {
        let bytes: Vec<u8> = s.chars().map(|c| if (c as u32) < 0x100 { c as u8 } else { b'?' }).collect();
        self.write_bytes(addr, &bytes);
        self.write_u8(addr + bytes.len() as u32, 0);
        bytes.len() + 1
    }

    /// Write raw bytes plus a NUL.
    pub fn write_cstr_bytes(&mut self, addr: u32, s: &[u8]) -> usize {
        self.write_bytes(addr, s);
        self.write_u8(addr + s.len() as u32, 0);
        s.len() + 1
    }

    /// NUL-terminated UTF-16LE string (at most 32 Ki units).
    pub fn read_wstr(&self, addr: u32) -> String {
        let mut units = Vec::new();
        let mut a = addr;
        while units.len() < 0x8000 {
            let u = self.read_u16(a);
            if u == 0 {
                break;
            }
            units.push(u);
            a = a.wrapping_add(2);
        }
        String::from_utf16_lossy(&units)
    }

    /// Write `s` as UTF-16LE plus a NUL unit. Returns units written including the NUL.
    pub fn write_wstr(&mut self, addr: u32, s: &str) -> usize {
        let mut a = addr;
        let mut n = 0;
        for u in s.encode_utf16() {
            self.write_u16(a, u);
            a += 2;
            n += 1;
        }
        self.write_u16(a, 0);
        n + 1
    }

    /// Zero a range and give whole host pages back to the kernel (used on release/decommit).
    pub fn discard(&mut self, addr: u32, len: u32) {
        if len == 0 {
            return;
        }
        Self::check(addr, len as usize);
        // Errors already fell back to zeroing by hand.
        let _ = sys::discard(self.host_ptr(addr), len as usize);
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- VirtualAlloc family

    /// Win32 `VirtualAlloc` semantics (`alloc_type` = MEM_COMMIT/MEM_RESERVE bits). Returns the base address.
    pub fn virtual_alloc(&mut self, addr: u32, size: u32, alloc_type: u32, protect: u32) -> Result<u32, MemError> {
        self.regions.virtual_alloc(addr, size, alloc_type, protect)
    }

    /// Win32 `VirtualFree` semantics. Freed / decommitted memory reads back as zero.
    pub fn virtual_free(&mut self, addr: u32, size: u32, free_type: u32) -> Result<(), MemError> {
        let (a, len) = self.regions.virtual_free(addr, size, free_type)?;
        self.discard(a, len);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Win32 `VirtualProtect`; returns the old protection of the first page. Protection is bookkeeping only.
    pub fn virtual_protect(&mut self, addr: u32, size: u32, protect: u32) -> Result<u32, MemError> {
        self.regions.protect(addr, size, protect)
    }

    /// Win32 `VirtualQuery`.
    pub fn virtual_query(&self, addr: u32) -> MemoryInfo {
        self.regions.query(addr)
    }

    /// Reserve + commit a range for runtime use. `addr = None` picks a free spot in `[lo, hi)`.
    pub fn alloc_region(
        &mut self,
        addr: Option<u32>,
        size: u32,
        kind: RegionKind,
        arena: (u32, u32),
    ) -> Result<u32, MemError> {
        let base = self.regions.reserve_in(addr, size, kind, PAGE_READWRITE, arena)?;
        self.regions.commit(base, size, PAGE_READWRITE)?;
        Ok(base)
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- heaps

    /// The default process heap (`GetProcessHeap`).
    pub fn process_heap(&self) -> u32 {
        self.process_heap
    }

    /// `HeapCreate`. Returns the heap handle (= guest address of its first segment).
    pub fn heap_create(&mut self, initial: u32, max: u32) -> Result<u32, MemError> {
        self.heaps.create(&mut self.regions, initial, max)
    }

    /// `HeapDestroy`.
    pub fn heap_destroy(&mut self, heap: u32) -> Result<(), MemError> {
        let segs = self.heaps.destroy(heap)?;
        for (base, size) in segs {
            let _ = self.regions.virtual_free(base, 0, MEM_RELEASE);
            self.discard(base, size);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// `HeapAlloc`. `flags & HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY` zeroes the block.
    pub fn heap_alloc(&mut self, heap: u32, size: u32, flags: u32) -> Option<u32> {
        let p = self.heaps.alloc(&mut self.regions, heap, size).ok()?;
        if flags & HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY != 0 {
            self.fill(p, size as usize, 0);
        }
        Some(p)
    }

    /// `HeapFree`.
    pub fn heap_free(&mut self, heap: u32, ptr: u32) -> bool {
        self.heaps.free(heap, ptr).is_ok()
    }

    /// `HeapSize` (the size requested by the guest).
    pub fn heap_size(&self, heap: u32, ptr: u32) -> Option<u32> {
        self.heaps.size(heap, ptr)
    }

    /// `HeapReAlloc`. Keeps contents; zeroes the grown part when `HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY` is set.
    pub fn heap_realloc(&mut self, heap: u32, ptr: u32, size: u32, flags: u32) -> Option<u32> {
        let old = self.heaps.size(heap, ptr)?;
        if self.heaps.try_resize_in_place(heap, ptr, size) {
            if flags & HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY != 0 && size > old {
                self.fill(ptr + old, (size - old) as usize, 0);
            }
            return Some(ptr);
        }
        if flags & HEAP_REALLOC_IN_PLACE_ONLY != 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let new = self.heaps.alloc(&mut self.regions, heap, size).ok()?;
        self.copy_within(ptr, new, old.min(size) as usize);
        if flags & HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY != 0 && size > old {
            self.fill(new + old, (size - old) as usize, 0);
        }
        self.heaps.free(heap, ptr).ok()?;
        Some(new)
    }

    /// Convenience: allocate from the process heap (runtime-internal strings, COM objects, ...). Zeroed.
    pub fn alloc(&mut self, size: u32) -> u32 {
        let h = self.process_heap;
        self.heap_alloc(h, size.max(1), HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY).expect("process heap exhausted")
    }

    /// Convenience: free a block from [`GuestMemory::alloc`].
    pub fn free(&mut self, ptr: u32) -> bool {
        let h = self.process_heap;
        self.heap_free(h, ptr)
    }
}

impl Drop for GuestMemory {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if !self.owns_window {
            return;
        }
        sys::release_window(self.base, (layout::WINDOW_SIZE + layout::GUARD_SIZE) as usize);
    }
}

mod tests;
```
