`port/crates/s3-mem/src/regions.rs`:

```rs
//! VirtualAlloc-style bookkeeping: allocations (reservations) with per-page commit state and protection.
//!
//! Memory itself is always accessible in the host window; this only answers the questions Win32 code asks
//! (`VirtualQuery`, "is this already reserved?", "where is free space?").

use std::collections::BTreeMap;

use crate::layout::{ALLOC_ARENA_END, ALLOC_ARENA_START, ALLOC_GRANULARITY, PAGE_SIZE};
use crate::{align_down, align_up, MemError};

pub const MEM_COMMIT: u32 = 0x1000;
pub const MEM_RESERVE: u32 = 0x2000;
pub const MEM_DECOMMIT: u32 = 0x4000;
pub const MEM_RELEASE: u32 = 0x8000;
pub const MEM_FREE: u32 = 0x1_0000;
pub const MEM_PRIVATE: u32 = 0x2_0000;
pub const MEM_MAPPED: u32 = 0x4_0000;
pub const MEM_IMAGE: u32 = 0x100_0000;

pub const PAGE_NOACCESS: u32 = 0x01;
pub const PAGE_READONLY: u32 = 0x02;
pub const PAGE_READWRITE: u32 = 0x04;
pub const PAGE_EXECUTE: u32 = 0x10;
pub const PAGE_EXECUTE_READ: u32 = 0x20;
pub const PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE: u32 = 0x40;

/// What an allocation is (the `Type` field of `MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RegionKind {
    Private,
    Image,
    Mapped,
}

impl RegionKind {
    fn mem_type(self) -> u32 {
        match self {
            RegionKind::Private => MEM_PRIVATE,
            RegionKind::Image => MEM_IMAGE,
            RegionKind::Mapped => MEM_MAPPED,
        }
    }
}

/// One reservation.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Allocation {
    pub base: u32,
    /// Size in bytes, multiple of the page size.
    pub size: u32,
    pub alloc_protect: u32,
    pub kind: RegionKind,
    /// Per page: 0 = reserved only, otherwise the committed page's protection.
    pub pages: Vec<u32>,
}

impl Allocation {
    fn end(&self) -> u64 {
        self.base as u64 + self.size as u64
    }
}

/// `MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION` contents.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MemoryInfo {
    pub base_address: u32,
    pub allocation_base: u32,
    pub allocation_protect: u32,
    pub region_size: u32,
    /// MEM_COMMIT / MEM_RESERVE / MEM_FREE.
    pub state: u32,
    pub protect: u32,
    /// MEM_PRIVATE / MEM_IMAGE / MEM_MAPPED (0 for free).
    pub type_: u32,
}

impl MemoryInfo {
    /// Serialize as the 28-byte Win32 `MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION`.
    pub fn to_bytes(&self) -> [u8; 28] {
        let mut b = [0u8; 28];
        let f = [
            self.base_address,
            self.allocation_base,
            self.allocation_protect,
            self.region_size,
            self.state,
            self.protect,
            self.type_,
        ];
        for (i, v) in f.iter().enumerate() {
            b[i * 4..i * 4 + 4].copy_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
        }
        b
    }
}

/// All reservations, keyed by base address.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct Regions {
    allocs: BTreeMap<u32, Allocation>,
}

impl Regions {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    /// Iterate allocations in address order.
    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Allocation> {
        self.allocs.values()
    }

    /// The allocation containing `addr`, if any.
    pub fn find(&self, addr: u32) -> Option<&Allocation> {
        let (_, a) = self.allocs.range(..=addr).next_back()?;
        if (addr as u64) < a.end() {
            Some(a)
        } else {
            None
        }
    }

    fn find_mut(&mut self, addr: u32) -> Option<&mut Allocation> {
        let (_, a) = self.allocs.range_mut(..=addr).next_back()?;
        if (addr as u64) < a.end() {
            Some(a)
        } else {
            None
        }
    }

    fn overlaps(&self, addr: u32, size: u32) -> bool {
        let end = addr as u64 + size as u64;
        if let Some((_, a)) = self.allocs.range(..end.min(u32::MAX as u64 + 1) as u32).next_back() {
            if a.end() > addr as u64 && (a.base as u64) < end {
                return true;
            }
        }
        // The range query above uses `..end` which excludes an allocation starting exactly at `end` (fine) but
        // when end == 2^32 the cast saturates; double check the last allocation.
        if end > u32::MAX as u64 {
            if let Some((_, a)) = self.allocs.iter().next_back() {
                return a.end() > addr as u64;
            }
        }
        false
    }

    /// Lowest 64 KiB aligned free gap of `size` bytes inside `[lo, hi)`.
    fn find_free(&self, size: u32, lo: u32, hi: u32) -> Option<u32> {
        let mut cand = align_up(lo, ALLOC_GRANULARITY) as u64;
        let size = size as u64;
        for a in self.allocs.values() {
            if a.end() <= cand {
                continue;
            }
            if a.base as u64 >= hi as u64 {
                break;
            }
            if cand + size <= a.base as u64 {
                break;
            }
            cand = align_up(a.end().min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32, ALLOC_GRANULARITY) as u64;
            if a.end() > u32::MAX as u64 {
                return None;
            }
        }
        if cand + size <= hi as u64 {
            Some(cand as u32)
        } else {
            None
        }
    }

    /// Reserve `size` bytes at `addr` (rounded down to 64 KiB) or anywhere in the default arena.
    pub fn reserve(&mut self, addr: Option<u32>, size: u32, kind: RegionKind, protect: u32) -> Result<u32, MemError> {
        self.reserve_in(addr, size, kind, protect, (ALLOC_ARENA_START, ALLOC_ARENA_END))
    }

    /// Like [`Regions::reserve`] but searching `arena = [lo, hi)` when `addr` is `None`.
    /// A fixed `addr` is only rounded down to the page size (runtime-internal fixed placements like TEBs);
    /// Win32 `VirtualAlloc` rounds to 64 KiB itself.
    pub fn reserve_in(
        &mut self,
        addr: Option<u32>,
        size: u32,
        kind: RegionKind,
        protect: u32,
        arena: (u32, u32),
    ) -> Result<u32, MemError> {
        if size == 0 {
            return Err(MemError::BadRange { addr: addr.unwrap_or(0), len: size });
        }
        let (base, size) = match addr {
            Some(a) => {
                let base = align_down(a, PAGE_SIZE);
                let end = a as u64 + size as u64;
                let end = (end + PAGE_SIZE as u64 - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE as u64 - 1);
                if end > 1u64 << 32 {
                    return Err(MemError::BadRange { addr: a, len: size });
                }
                (base, (end - base as u64) as u32)
            }
            None => {
                let size = align_up(size, PAGE_SIZE);
                (self.find_free(size, arena.0, arena.1).ok_or(MemError::OutOfSpace)?, size)
            }
        };
        if self.overlaps(base, size) {
            return Err(MemError::Overlap { addr: base, len: size });
        }
        let pages = vec![0u32; (size / PAGE_SIZE) as usize];
        self.allocs.insert(base, Allocation { base, size, alloc_protect: protect, kind, pages });
        Ok(base)
    }

    /// Commit pages of an existing allocation.
    pub fn commit(&mut self, addr: u32, size: u32, protect: u32) -> Result<(), MemError> {
        let start = align_down(addr, PAGE_SIZE);
        let end = addr as u64 + size.max(1) as u64;
        let a = self.find_mut(start).ok_or(MemError::NotAllocated { addr, len: size })?;
        if end > a.end() {
            return Err(MemError::NotAllocated { addr, len: size });
        }
        let p0 = ((start - a.base) / PAGE_SIZE) as usize;
        let p1 = ((end - a.base as u64).div_ceil(PAGE_SIZE as u64)) as usize;
        for p in &mut a.pages[p0..p1] {
            *p = if protect == 0 { PAGE_READWRITE } else { protect };
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// `VirtualAlloc` semantics.
    pub fn virtual_alloc(&mut self, addr: u32, size: u32, alloc_type: u32, protect: u32) -> Result<u32, MemError> {
        if size == 0 {
            return Err(MemError::BadRange { addr, len: size });
        }
        let reserve = alloc_type & MEM_RESERVE != 0;
        let commit = alloc_type & MEM_COMMIT != 0;
        if addr == 0 || reserve {
            let fixed = if addr == 0 { None } else { Some(align_down(addr, ALLOC_GRANULARITY)) };
            let size = match fixed {
                Some(b) => (addr - b) + size,
                None => size,
            };
            let base = self.reserve(fixed, size, RegionKind::Private, protect)?;
            if commit {
                let sz = self.find(base).map(|a| a.size).unwrap_or(size);
                self.commit(base, sz, protect)?;
            }
            return Ok(base);
        }
        if commit {
            self.commit(addr, size, protect)?;
            return Ok(align_down(addr, PAGE_SIZE));
        }
        Err(MemError::BadRange { addr, len: size })
    }

    /// `VirtualFree` semantics. Returns the guest range whose contents must be discarded.
    pub fn virtual_free(&mut self, addr: u32, size: u32, free_type: u32) -> Result<(u32, u32), MemError> {
        if free_type & MEM_RELEASE != 0 {
            if size != 0 {
                return Err(MemError::BadRange { addr, len: size });
            }
            let a = self.allocs.remove(&addr).ok_or(MemError::NotAllocated { addr, len: 0 })?;
            return Ok((a.base, a.size));
        }
        if free_type & MEM_DECOMMIT != 0 {
            let a = self.find_mut(addr).ok_or(MemError::NotAllocated { addr, len: size })?;
            let (start, end) = if size == 0 {
                // size 0 with DECOMMIT: from addr to end of the allocation.
                (align_down(addr, PAGE_SIZE), a.end())
            } else {
                let s = align_down(addr, PAGE_SIZE);
                let e = (addr as u64 + size as u64 + PAGE_SIZE as u64 - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE as u64 - 1);
                (s, e)
            };
            if end > a.end() {
                return Err(MemError::NotAllocated { addr, len: size });
            }
            let p0 = ((start - a.base) / PAGE_SIZE) as usize;
            let p1 = ((end - a.base as u64) / PAGE_SIZE as u64) as usize;
            for p in &mut a.pages[p0..p1] {
                *p = 0;
            }
            return Ok((start, (end - start as u64) as u32));
        }
        Err(MemError::BadRange { addr, len: size })
    }

    /// `VirtualProtect` bookkeeping. Returns the previous protection of the first page.
    pub fn protect(&mut self, addr: u32, size: u32, protect: u32) -> Result<u32, MemError> {
        let start = align_down(addr, PAGE_SIZE);
        let end = addr as u64 + size.max(1) as u64;
        let a = self.find_mut(start).ok_or(MemError::NotAllocated { addr, len: size })?;
        if end > a.end() {
            return Err(MemError::NotAllocated { addr, len: size });
        }
        let p0 = ((start - a.base) / PAGE_SIZE) as usize;
        let p1 = ((end - a.base as u64).div_ceil(PAGE_SIZE as u64)) as usize;
        if a.pages[p0..p1].iter().any(|&p| p == 0) {
            return Err(MemError::NotAllocated { addr, len: size });
        }
        let old = a.pages[p0];
        for p in &mut a.pages[p0..p1] {
            *p = protect;
        }
        Ok(old)
    }

    /// `VirtualQuery` semantics.
    pub fn query(&self, addr: u32) -> MemoryInfo {
        let page = align_down(addr, PAGE_SIZE);
        if let Some(a) = self.find(page) {
            let idx = ((page - a.base) / PAGE_SIZE) as usize;
            let st = a.pages[idx];
            let mut n = 1;
            while idx + n < a.pages.len() && a.pages[idx + n] == st {
                n += 1;
            }
            return MemoryInfo {
                base_address: page,
                allocation_base: a.base,
                allocation_protect: a.alloc_protect,
                region_size: n as u32 * PAGE_SIZE,
                state: if st == 0 { MEM_RESERVE } else { MEM_COMMIT },
                protect: st,
                type_: a.kind.mem_type(),
            };
        }
        // Free: extend up to the next allocation.
        let next = self.allocs.range(page..).next().map(|(b, _)| *b as u64).unwrap_or(1u64 << 32);
        MemoryInfo {
            base_address: page,
            allocation_base: 0,
            allocation_protect: 0,
            region_size: (next - page as u64).min(u32::MAX as u64 & !(PAGE_SIZE as u64 - 1)) as u32,
            state: MEM_FREE,
            protect: PAGE_NOACCESS,
            type_: 0,
        }
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-mem/src/sys.rs`:

```rs
//! Host mapping primitives.
//!
//! - Unix (Linux / Android; any Unix with MAP_NORESERVE semantics): anonymous private `mmap`.
//! - Windows: `VirtualAlloc`. Windows has no MAP_NORESERVE, so the whole window is committed up front. Pages are still
//!   demand-zero (no physical memory until touched), but the full size counts against the system commit limit
//!   (RAM + page file).

pub(crate) use imp::{discard, release_window, reserve_window};

/// Zero `[p, p+len)`: whole host pages in the interior go through `give_back` (returns them to the OS and leaves them
/// zero), the unaligned edges are zeroed by hand. Shared by both platforms.
fn discard_with(
    p: *mut u8,
    len: usize,
    hp: usize,
    give_back: impl FnOnce(usize, usize) -> Result<(), crate::MemError>,
) -> Result<(), crate::MemError> {
    let start = p as usize;
    let end = start + len;
    let a = (start + hp - 1) & !(hp - 1);
    let b = end & !(hp - 1);
    if a >= b {
        // SAFETY: inside our mapping.
        unsafe { std::ptr::write_bytes(p, 0, len) };
        return Ok(());
    }
    // SAFETY: all ranges are inside our private anonymous mapping.
    unsafe {
        std::ptr::write_bytes(p, 0, a - start);
        std::ptr::write_bytes(b as *mut u8, 0, end - b);
    }
    give_back(a, b - a).inspect_err(|_| {
        // SAFETY: inside our mapping; fall back to zeroing by hand.
        unsafe { std::ptr::write_bytes(a as *mut u8, 0, b - a) };
    })
}

fn errno() -> i32 {
    std::io::Error::last_os_error().raw_os_error().unwrap_or(0)
}

#[cfg(unix)]
mod imp {
    use super::errno;
    use crate::MemError;

    /// Reserve `len` bytes readable/writable, lazily backed, not counted against commit limits.
    pub(crate) fn reserve_window(len: usize) -> Result<*mut u8, MemError> {
        // SAFETY: anonymous private mapping at a kernel-chosen address.
        let p = unsafe {
            libc::mmap(
                std::ptr::null_mut(),
                len,
                libc::PROT_READ | libc::PROT_WRITE,
                libc::MAP_PRIVATE | libc::MAP_ANONYMOUS | libc::MAP_NORESERVE,
                -1,
                0,
            )
        };
        if p == libc::MAP_FAILED {
            return Err(MemError::Os(errno()));
        }
        Ok(p as *mut u8)
    }

    pub(crate) fn release_window(p: *mut u8, len: usize) {
        // SAFETY: p/len come from reserve_window.
        unsafe {
            libc::munmap(p as *mut libc::c_void, len);
        }
    }

    fn host_page_size() -> usize {
        // SAFETY: sysconf is always safe to call.
        let v = unsafe { libc::sysconf(libc::_SC_PAGESIZE) };
        if v <= 0 {
            4096
        } else {
            v as usize
        }
    }

    /// Zero a range, giving whole host pages back to the kernel (host pages may be 16 KiB on Android, so only the
    /// host-page-aligned interior is madvised; the edges are zeroed by hand).
    pub(crate) fn discard(p: *mut u8, len: usize) -> Result<(), MemError> {
        super::discard_with(p, len, host_page_size(), |a, n| {
            // SAFETY: page-aligned range inside our private anonymous mapping.
            if unsafe { libc::madvise(a as *mut libc::c_void, n, libc::MADV_DONTNEED) } != 0 {
                return Err(MemError::Os(errno()));
            }
            Ok(())
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(windows)]
mod imp {
    use super::errno;
    use crate::MemError;
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
        VirtualAlloc, VirtualFree, MEM_COMMIT, MEM_DECOMMIT, MEM_RELEASE, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_READWRITE,
    };
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::SystemInformation::{GetSystemInfo, SYSTEM_INFO};

    /// Reserve and commit `len` bytes readable/writable. Pages are demand-zero, but (unlike MAP_NORESERVE on Unix)
    /// the full size is charged against the commit limit.
    pub(crate) fn reserve_window(len: usize) -> Result<*mut u8, MemError> {
        // SAFETY: new private allocation at a system-chosen address.
        let p = unsafe { VirtualAlloc(std::ptr::null(), len, MEM_RESERVE | MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE) };
        if p.is_null() {
            return Err(MemError::Os(errno()));
        }
        Ok(p as *mut u8)
    }

    pub(crate) fn release_window(p: *mut u8, _len: usize) {
        // SAFETY: p comes from reserve_window; MEM_RELEASE requires size 0 and frees the whole allocation.
        unsafe {
            VirtualFree(p as *mut core::ffi::c_void, 0, MEM_RELEASE);
        }
    }

    fn host_page_size() -> usize {
        // SAFETY: GetSystemInfo only writes the struct we pass.
        let mut si: SYSTEM_INFO = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        unsafe { GetSystemInfo(&mut si) };
        if si.dwPageSize == 0 {
            4096
        } else {
            si.dwPageSize as usize
        }
    }

    /// Zero a range. The page-aligned interior is decommitted (physical pages go back to the OS) and committed again,
    /// which leaves it demand-zero, the same effect as `madvise(MADV_DONTNEED)` on a private anonymous mapping.
    pub(crate) fn discard(p: *mut u8, len: usize) -> Result<(), MemError> {
        super::discard_with(p, len, host_page_size(), |a, n| {
            // SAFETY: page-aligned range inside our committed allocation.
            unsafe {
                if VirtualFree(a as *mut core::ffi::c_void, n, MEM_DECOMMIT) == 0 {
                    return Err(MemError::Os(errno()));
                }
                if VirtualAlloc(a as *const core::ffi::c_void, n, MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE).is_null() {
                    // The range is decommitted now; this must not be left that way. Commit failure here means the
                    // system ran out of commit, which the caller cannot recover from either.
                    panic!("s3-mem: re-commit after discard failed (os error {})", errno());
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        })
    }
}
```

```rs
use super::*;

#[test]
fn read_write_numbers_and_strings() {
    let mut m = GuestMemory::new().unwrap();
    m.write_u32(0x40_0000, 0xDEAD_BEEF);
    assert_eq!(m.read_u32(0x40_0000), 0xDEAD_BEEF);
    assert_eq!(m.read_u8(0x40_0000), 0xEF);
    assert_eq!(m.read_u16(0x40_0002), 0xDEAD);
    m.write_u64(0x40_0011, 0x0102_0304_0506_0708); // unaligned
    assert_eq!(m.read_u64(0x40_0011), 0x0102_0304_0506_0708);
    m.write_f64(0x40_0100, 1.5);
    assert_eq!(m.read_f64(0x40_0100), 1.5);
    m.write_f32(0x40_0108, -2.25);
    assert_eq!(m.read_f32(0x40_0108), -2.25);
    // Top of the window: reading 8 bytes at the last address must not crash (guard).
    m.write_u8(0xFFFF_FFFF, 7);
    assert_eq!(m.read_u8(0xFFFF_FFFF), 7);
    let _ = m.read_u64(0xFFFF_FFFF);

    assert_eq!(m.write_cstr(0x50_0000, "S3.EXE\u{e9}"), 8);
    assert_eq!(m.read_cstr(0x50_0000), "S3.EXE\u{e9}");
    assert_eq!(m.strlen(0x50_0000, 100), 7);
    assert_eq!(m.write_wstr(0x50_1000, "Grüße"), 6);
    assert_eq!(m.read_wstr(0x50_1000), "Grüße");
    m.write_bytes(0x50_2000, b"abcdef");
    m.copy_within(0x50_2000, 0x50_2002, 4);
    assert_eq!(m.slice(0x50_2000, 6), b"ababcd");
}

#[test]
fn virtual_alloc_reserve_commit_query_free() {
    let mut m = GuestMemory::new().unwrap();
    let a = m.virtual_alloc(0, 0x3000, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_READWRITE).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(a % layout::ALLOC_GRANULARITY, 0);
    assert!(a >= layout::ALLOC_ARENA_START);
    let q = m.virtual_query(a + 0x10);
    assert_eq!(q.state, MEM_RESERVE);
    assert_eq!(q.allocation_base, a);
    assert_eq!(q.base_address, a);
    assert_eq!(q.region_size, 0x3000);

    let c = m.virtual_alloc(a + 0x1004, 0x10, MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(c, a + 0x1000);
    let q = m.virtual_query(a + 0x1000);
    assert_eq!((q.state, q.protect, q.region_size, q.type_), (MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE, 0x1000, MEM_PRIVATE));
    assert_eq!(m.virtual_query(a).state, MEM_RESERVE);
    assert_eq!(m.virtual_query(a + 0x2000).state, MEM_RESERVE);

    assert_eq!(m.virtual_protect(a + 0x1000, 0x1000, PAGE_READONLY).unwrap(), PAGE_READWRITE);
    assert!(m.virtual_protect(a, 0x1000, PAGE_READONLY).is_err()); // not committed

    m.write_u32(a + 0x1000, 42);
    m.virtual_free(a + 0x1000, 0x1000, MEM_DECOMMIT).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(m.read_u32(a + 0x1000), 0);
    assert_eq!(m.virtual_query(a + 0x1000).state, MEM_RESERVE);

    // Second allocation does not overlap.
    let b = m.virtual_alloc(0, 0x1_0000, MEM_RESERVE | MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE).unwrap();
    assert!(b >= a + 0x1_0000);
    // Fixed reserve over an existing allocation fails.
    assert!(m.virtual_alloc(a, 0x1000, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_READWRITE).is_err());

    assert!(m.virtual_free(a + 0x1000, 0, MEM_RELEASE).is_err());
    m.virtual_free(a, 0, MEM_RELEASE).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(m.virtual_query(a).state, MEM_FREE);
    // Freed space is reused.
    let c = m.virtual_alloc(0, 0x1000, MEM_RESERVE | MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(c, a);

    // Fixed address reservation.
    let f = m.virtual_alloc(0x2000_1234, 0x100, MEM_RESERVE | MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(f, 0x2000_0000);
    assert_eq!(m.virtual_query(0x2000_1000).state, MEM_COMMIT);
}

#[test]
fn query_free_space_and_bytes() {
    let m = GuestMemory::new().unwrap();
    let q = m.virtual_query(0x0050_0000);
    assert_eq!(q.state, MEM_FREE);
    let b = q.to_bytes();
    assert_eq!(&b[0..4], &0x0050_0000u32.to_le_bytes());
    assert_eq!(&b[16..20], &MEM_FREE.to_le_bytes());
}

#[test]
fn heap_alloc_free_realloc() {
    let mut m = GuestMemory::new().unwrap();
    let h = m.process_heap();
    let a = m.heap_alloc(h, 10, 0).unwrap();
    let b = m.heap_alloc(h, 100, HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(a % 8, 0);
    assert_eq!(b % 8, 0);
    assert!(b >= a + 16 || a >= b + 100);
    assert_eq!(m.heap_size(h, a), Some(10));
    assert!(m.slice(b, 100).iter().all(|&x| x == 0));

    m.write_bytes(a, b"0123456789");
    // Grow: must keep contents.
    let a2 = m.heap_realloc(h, a, 5000, HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(m.slice(a2, 10), b"0123456789");
    assert!(m.slice(a2 + 10, 4990).iter().all(|&x| x == 0));
    assert_eq!(m.heap_size(h, a2), Some(5000));
    // Shrink in place.
    assert_eq!(m.heap_realloc(h, a2, 4, 0), Some(a2));
    assert_eq!(m.heap_size(h, a2), Some(4));

    assert!(m.heap_free(h, b));
    assert!(!m.heap_free(h, b)); // double free detected
    assert!(m.heap_free(h, a2));
    assert_eq!(m.heaps.get(h).unwrap().live_blocks(), 0);
    // All free space coalesced back into the single segment.
    let seg = m.heaps.get(h).unwrap().segments[0];
    assert_eq!(m.heaps.get(h).unwrap().free_bytes(), seg.1 as u64);
}

#[test]
fn heap_grows_and_destroys() {
    let mut m = GuestMemory::new().unwrap();
    let h = m.heap_create(0, 0).unwrap();
    // Bigger than one segment.
    let big = m.heap_alloc(h, 3 * 1024 * 1024, 0).unwrap();
    m.write_u32(big + 3 * 1024 * 1024 - 4, 1);
    let mut v = Vec::new();
    for i in 0..2000u32 {
        v.push(m.heap_alloc(h, 1 + i % 300, 0).unwrap());
    }
    for p in v {
        assert!(m.heap_free(h, p));
    }
    m.heap_destroy(h).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(m.virtual_query(h).state, MEM_FREE);
    assert!(m.heap_alloc(h, 4, 0).is_none());
}
```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/call.rs`:

```rs
//! Calling guest functions from host code with the usual MSVC conventions. All wrap
//! [`Machine::call_guest`], which runs the call on the current guest thread and restores every register
//! (including ESP) afterwards, so stdcall and cdecl differ only in documentation here.
//!
//! Where to call from: inside a hook (the thread is stopped at a clean instruction boundary) or from a
//! deferred closure ([`crate::defer`]) that runs at a safe point of the main thread. Calling from input or
//! overlay callbacks runs on whatever thread is current and is not recommended.

use s3_cpu::{ECX, EDX};
use s3_runtime::Machine;

/// `__stdcall f(args...)` (callee pops the arguments).
pub fn call_stdcall(m: &mut Machine, addr: u32, args: &[u32]) -> u32 {
    m.call_guest(addr, args)
}

/// `__cdecl f(args...)` (caller pops; `call_guest` restores ESP).
pub fn call_cdecl(m: &mut Machine, addr: u32, args: &[u32]) -> u32 {
    m.call_guest(addr, args)
}

/// `__thiscall this->f(args...)` (MSVC: `this` in ECX, callee pops the arguments).
pub fn call_thiscall(m: &mut Machine, addr: u32, this: u32, args: &[u32]) -> u32 {
    with_regs(m, &[(ECX, this)], |m| m.call_guest(addr, args))
}

/// `__fastcall f(a, b, rest...)` (first two dword arguments in ECX, EDX).
pub fn call_fastcall(m: &mut Machine, addr: u32, args: &[u32]) -> u32 {
    let a = args.first().copied().unwrap_or(0);
    let b = args.get(1).copied().unwrap_or(0);
    let rest = if args.len() > 2 { &args[2..] } else { &[] };
    with_regs(m, &[(ECX, a), (EDX, b)], |m| m.call_guest(addr, rest))
}

/// Call a virtual method: `this->vtbl[index](args...)` with thiscall.
pub fn call_virtual(m: &mut Machine, this: u32, index: u32, args: &[u32]) -> u32 {
    let vtbl = m.mem.read_u32(this);
    let f = m.mem.read_u32(vtbl.wrapping_add(4 * index));
    call_thiscall(m, f, this, args)
}

/// Set registers for the duration of `f`, restoring them afterwards (the interrupted guest code must not
/// see our ECX/EDX).
fn with_regs(m: &mut Machine, regs: &[(usize, u32)], f: impl FnOnce(&mut Machine) -> u32) -> u32 {
    let saved: Vec<(usize, u32)> = regs.iter().map(|&(r, _)| (r, m.cpu().regs[r])).collect();
    for &(r, v) in regs {
        m.cpu().regs[r] = v;
    }
    let ret = f(m);
    for (r, v) in saved {
        m.cpu().regs[r] = v;
    }
    ret
}
```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/cursor_layer.rs`:

```rs
//! The game's mouse cursor in the window layer (docs/porting/display.md "Cursor in the window layer").
//!
//! `s3_runtime::cursor` draws the Windows cursor the game set into the presented frame, so with the zoom
//! (= render size) it grew, shrank and moved on screen together with the map. When a frontend shows the window
//! layer, this mod turns that off (`CursorState::disabled`) and draws the same image here: at the window position
//! of the emulated mouse (through the shown viewport, so it stays where the finger / mouse is) and at a constant
//! size (the cursor's size in a 600 px high frame shown full height, `Layer::ui`).

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::Arc;

use s3_runtime::cursor::{CursorImage, CursorPixel, CursorState};
use s3_runtime::Machine;

use crate::layer::{ImageRef, Layer};
use crate::overlay::Image;
use crate::{FrameBuffer, Mod};

/// What the cursor looks like now: window-independent part (game position, HCURSOR).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Shown {
    x: i32,
    y: i32,
    handle: u32,
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct CursorMod {
    /// RGBA images by HCURSOR.
    images: HashMap<u32, (ImageRef, i32, i32)>,
    /// Cursor to draw (from the last tick), `None` = hidden.
    want: Option<Shown>,
    /// Cursor in the last recorded layer.
    drawn: Option<Shown>,
    /// Window position the cursor was drawn at, for its game position: kept while the game position does not
    /// change, so a zoom (other game px under the same screen point) does not move the cursor on screen.
    win_pos: Option<((i32, i32), (f32, f32))>,
    /// The frontend shows the window layer (the frame cursor is turned off).
    active: bool,
}

fn rgb565_to_rgba(c: u16) -> [u8; 4] {
    let r = ((c >> 11) & 31) as u32 * 255 / 31;
    let g = ((c >> 5) & 63) as u32 * 255 / 63;
    let b = (c & 31) as u32 * 255 / 31;
    [r as u8, g as u8, b as u8, 255]
}

/// RGBA copy of a cursor (XOR pixels: their colour, usually white = the inverted outline on dark ground).
fn to_rgba(img: &CursorImage) -> Image {
    let mut out = Image::new(img.width, img.height);
    for (i, p) in img.pixels.iter().enumerate() {
        let px = match *p {
            CursorPixel::Clear => [0, 0, 0, 0],
            CursorPixel::Color(c) | CursorPixel::Xor(c) => rgb565_to_rgba(c),
            CursorPixel::Blend(c, a) => {
                let [r, g, b, _] = rgb565_to_rgba(c);
                [r, g, b, a]
            }
        };
        out.rgba[i * 4..i * 4 + 4].copy_from_slice(&px);
    }
    out
}

impl CursorMod {
    /// Read the cursor state; turn the frame cursor off while the window layer is shown.
    fn update(&mut self, m: &mut Machine) {
        self.active = m.state::<crate::ModsState>().borrow_mut().layer_sink.is_some();
        let (mx, my) = (m.input.mouse_x, m.input.mouse_y);
        let cs = m.state::<CursorState>();
        let mut c = cs.borrow_mut();
        c.disabled = self.active;
        if !self.active || c.show_count < 0 || c.current == 0 {
            self.want = None;
            return;
        }
        let Some(img) = c.images.get(&c.current).cloned() else {
            self.want = None;
            return;
        };
        let (x, y) = match c.clip {
            Some((l, t, r, b)) => (mx.clamp(l, (r - 1).max(l)), my.clamp(t, (b - 1).max(t))),
            None => (mx, my),
        };
        let handle = c.current;
        drop(c);
        self.images.entry(handle).or_insert_with(|| (Arc::new(to_rgba(&img)), img.hot_x, img.hot_y));
        self.want = Some(Shown { x, y, handle });
    }
}

impl Mod for CursorMod {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        "cursor"
    }

    fn wants_draw(&self) -> bool {
        self.want.is_some()
    }

    fn needs_redraw(&self) -> bool {
        self.want != self.drawn
    }

    fn tick(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, _now: u64) {
        self.update(m);
    }

    fn draw_window(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, l: &mut Layer, _frame: &FrameBuffer) {
        self.update(m);
        let Some(s) = self.want else { return };
        let Some((img, hx, hy)) = self.images.get(&s.handle).cloned() else { return };
        let (wx, wy) = match self.win_pos {
            Some((g, w)) if g == (s.x, s.y) => w,
            _ => {
                let w = crate::draw_viewport(m).game_to_window(s.x as f32, s.y as f32);
                self.win_pos = Some(((s.x, s.y), w));
                w
            }
        };
        let k = l.ui();
        let (w, h) = ((img.width as f32 * k).round() as i32, (img.height as f32 * k).round() as i32);
        let (x, y) = ((wx - hx as f32 * k).round() as i32, (wy - hy as f32 * k).round() as i32);
        l.blit_scaled(&img, x, y, w, h, 1.0);
        self.drawn = Some(s);
    }
}

/// Add the mod (last, so the cursor is drawn on top of every other window-layer UI).
pub fn install(m: &mut Machine) {
    crate::add_mod(m, Box::new(CursorMod::default()));
}
```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/debug_overlay.rs`:

```rs
//! Built-in debug overlay (settings `debug_overlay` or `S3_MODS_DEBUG=1`): fingers as circles, the last
//! recognized gesture as a label (window layer, window pixels). Never consumes events.

use s3_runtime::{FrameBuffer, Machine};

use crate::gesture::TouchEvent;
use crate::layer::Layer;
use crate::overlay::{Rgba, Weight};
use crate::{Mod, ModsState};

#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct DebugTouch {
    enabled: Option<bool>,
    fingers: Vec<(u32, f32, f32)>,
    label: String,
    label_at: (f32, f32),
    last_event_ms: u64,
    now: u64,
    dirty: bool,
}

const SHOW_MS: u64 = 1500;

impl Mod for DebugTouch {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        "debug-touch"
    }

    fn observe(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, ev: &TouchEvent) {
        if self.enabled.is_none() {
            self.enabled = Some(m.state::<ModsState>().borrow_mut().settings.debug_overlay);
        }
        if self.enabled != Some(true) {
            return;
        }
        self.last_event_ms = m.real_ms();
        self.dirty = true;
        // Window position of the event (the layer draws in window pixels).
        let (x, y) = crate::touch_window_pos(m, ev);
        let ev = &match *ev {
            TouchEvent::Down { id, .. } => TouchEvent::Down { id, x, y },
            TouchEvent::Move { id, .. } => TouchEvent::Move { id, x, y },
            TouchEvent::Tap { .. } => TouchEvent::Tap { x, y },
            TouchEvent::DoubleTap { .. } => TouchEvent::DoubleTap { x, y },
            TouchEvent::LongPress { .. } => TouchEvent::LongPress { x, y },
            TouchEvent::TwoFingerTap { .. } => TouchEvent::TwoFingerTap { x, y },
            TouchEvent::ThreeFingerTap { .. } => TouchEvent::ThreeFingerTap { x, y },
            TouchEvent::Pan { phase, fingers, dx, dy, start_x, start_y, after_long_press, .. } => {
                TouchEvent::Pan { phase, fingers, x, y, dx, dy, start_x, start_y, after_long_press }
            }
            TouchEvent::Pinch { phase, scale, .. } => TouchEvent::Pinch { phase, cx: x, cy: y, scale },
            e => e,
        };
        match *ev {
            TouchEvent::Down { id, x, y } | TouchEvent::Move { id, x, y } => {
                match self.fingers.iter_mut().find(|f| f.0 == id) {
                    Some(f) => *f = (id, x, y),
                    None => self.fingers.push((id, x, y)),
                }
            }
            TouchEvent::Up { id, .. } | TouchEvent::Cancel { id } => self.fingers.retain(|f| f.0 != id),
            TouchEvent::Tap { x, y } => self.set_label("Tap", x, y),
            TouchEvent::DoubleTap { x, y } => self.set_label("DoubleTap", x, y),
            TouchEvent::LongPress { x, y } => self.set_label("LongPress", x, y),
            TouchEvent::TwoFingerTap { x, y } => self.set_label("TwoFingerTap", x, y),
            TouchEvent::ThreeFingerTap { x, y } => self.set_label("ThreeFingerTap", x, y),
            // Two-finger pans come with a Pinch; show the pinch label.
            TouchEvent::Pan { fingers: 2, .. } => {}
            TouchEvent::Pan { phase, fingers, x, y, after_long_press, .. } => {
                let l = format!("Pan{fingers} {phase:?}{}", if after_long_press { " (held)" } else { "" });
                self.set_label(&l, x, y)
            }
            TouchEvent::Pinch { phase, cx, cy, scale } => self.set_label(&format!("Pinch {phase:?} x{scale:.2}"), cx, cy),
        }
    }

    fn wants_draw(&self) -> bool {
        self.enabled == Some(true) && (!self.fingers.is_empty() || self.now.saturating_sub(self.last_event_ms) < SHOW_MS)
    }

    fn needs_redraw(&self) -> bool {
        self.dirty || (self.enabled == Some(true) && self.now.saturating_sub(self.last_event_ms) < SHOW_MS + 100)
    }

    fn tick(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, now: u64) {
        self.now = now;
        self.enabled = Some(m.state::<ModsState>().borrow_mut().settings.debug_overlay);
    }

    fn draw_window(&mut self, _m: &mut Machine, c: &mut Layer, _frame: &FrameBuffer) {
        self.dirty = false;
        let u = c.ui();
        for &(_, x, y) in &self.fingers {
            c.fill_circle(x, y, 14.0 * u, Rgba::rgba(255, 220, 0, 110));
            c.fill_circle(x, y, 3.0 * u, Rgba::rgba(255, 60, 0, 230));
        }
        if !self.label.is_empty() {
            let k = 1.0 - (self.now.saturating_sub(self.last_event_ms) as f32 / SHOW_MS as f32).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
            let k = if self.fingers.is_empty() { k } else { 1.0 };
            let px = 14.0 * u;
            let (tw, th) = crate::overlay::measure_text(px, Weight::Bold, &self.label);
            let p = |v: f32| (v * u).round() as i32;
            let x = (self.label_at.0 as i32 + p(16.0)).min(c.width() as i32 - tw - p(12.0)).max(0);
            let y = (self.label_at.1 as i32 - th - p(16.0)).max(0);
            c.fill_rounded_rect(x, y, tw + p(12.0), th + p(8.0), 6.0 * u, Rgba::rgba(0, 0, 0, 170).fade(k));
            c.text(x + p(6.0), y + p(4.0), px, Weight::Bold, Rgba::WHITE.fade(k), &self.label);
        }
    }
}

impl DebugTouch {
    fn set_label(&mut self, l: &str, x: f32, y: f32) {
        self.label = l.to_string();
        self.label_at = (x, y);
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/display.rs`:

```rs
//! Display modes and the one shared screen <-> game transform (docs/porting/display.md).
//!
//! Every frontend (Android GPU / CPU presenter, desktop `s3run` window) scales the game frame into its window with a
//! [`Viewport`] and maps touches / mouse positions back with [`Viewport::window_to_game`]. Mods read the active
//! viewport (window size, visible part of the game frame in `Fill` mode) with [`viewport`]; the frontend publishes
//! it with [`set_viewport`]. Settings ([`DisplaySettings`]) live in `mods-settings.json` under `display` and are read
//! by the frontends once per engine slice ([`display_settings`]); menus change them with [`set_display`] /
//! [`cycle_mode`] / [`cycle_filter`] / [`cycle_fps`].
//!
//! Pure presentation: nothing here changes guest-visible state, so lockstep multiplayer is unaffected.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use s3_runtime::Machine;

use crate::menu_layout::{self, MenuLayout};

/// How the game frame is placed in the window.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
pub enum DisplayMode {
    /// Keep the aspect ratio, whole frame visible, black bars (letterbox / pillarbox).
    Fit,
    /// Keep the aspect ratio, fill the whole window, crop the overflow (centred).
    Fill,
    /// Fill the whole window, distort the aspect ratio.
    Stretch,
    /// The game renders at a custom resolution with the window's aspect ratio (res-zoom, docs/porting/
    /// resolution-zoom.md), shown like `Fit` (so no bars once the resolution matches). Frames of another aspect
    /// (menus at 800x600) are shown like `Fit`.
    #[default]
    NativeWide,
}

impl DisplayMode {
    pub const ALL: [DisplayMode; 4] = [DisplayMode::Fit, DisplayMode::Fill, DisplayMode::Stretch, DisplayMode::NativeWide];
    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            DisplayMode::Fit => "Fit",
            DisplayMode::Fill => "Fill",
            DisplayMode::Stretch => "Stretch",
            DisplayMode::NativeWide => "Native wide",
        }
    }
    pub fn next(self) -> DisplayMode {
        let i = Self::ALL.iter().position(|&m| m == self).unwrap_or(0);
        Self::ALL[(i + 1) % Self::ALL.len()]
    }
    /// Parse a CLI / settings name (`fit`, `fill`, `stretch`, `native`/`native-wide`).
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<DisplayMode> {
        match s.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
            "fit" | "letterbox" => Some(DisplayMode::Fit),
            "fill" | "crop" => Some(DisplayMode::Fill),
            "stretch" => Some(DisplayMode::Stretch),
            "native" | "native-wide" | "nativewide" | "wide" => Some(DisplayMode::NativeWide),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// Texture filter used when scaling.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
pub enum ScaleFilter {
    /// Blocky pixels (uneven pixel sizes at non-integer scales).
    Nearest,
    /// Bilinear (soft).
    Linear,
    /// Sharp bilinear: nearest inside each source pixel, linear only across the edge band (crisp and even).
    #[default]
    SharpBilinear,
    /// Pixel-art edge upscaler (xBR level 2, Hyllian's algorithm; GPU shader in the Android presenter): smooth
    /// diagonal and curved edges at any zoom. The desktop CPU scaler uses sharp bilinear for it.
    Xbr,
    /// Neural x2 upscaler (Anime4K CNN S, MIT; GLES 3 passes in the Android presenter, `upscale_ai.rs`) when the
    /// frame is shown at >= 1.2x; sharp bilinear otherwise and on the desktop.
    Ai,
}

impl ScaleFilter {
    pub const ALL: [ScaleFilter; 5] = [ScaleFilter::Nearest, ScaleFilter::Linear, ScaleFilter::SharpBilinear, ScaleFilter::Xbr, ScaleFilter::Ai];
    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            ScaleFilter::Nearest => "Pixel",
            ScaleFilter::Linear => "Smooth",
            ScaleFilter::SharpBilinear => "Sharp",
            ScaleFilter::Xbr => "xBR (HD edges)",
            ScaleFilter::Ai => "AI (Anime4K)",
        }
    }
    pub fn next(self) -> ScaleFilter {
        let i = Self::ALL.iter().position(|&m| m == self).unwrap_or(0);
        Self::ALL[(i + 1) % Self::ALL.len()]
    }
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<ScaleFilter> {
        match s.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
            "nearest" | "pixel" => Some(ScaleFilter::Nearest),
            "linear" | "bilinear" | "smooth" => Some(ScaleFilter::Linear),
            "sharp" | "sharp-bilinear" => Some(ScaleFilter::SharpBilinear),
            "xbr" | "hd" => Some(ScaleFilter::Xbr),
            "ai" | "anime4k" => Some(ScaleFilter::Ai),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// Where the FPS counter sits (cycled from the menus).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
pub enum FpsPos {
    /// Top right in UI mode A, top center in the Mobile HUD.
    #[default]
    Auto,
    TopLeft,
    TopCenter,
    TopRight,
    BottomRight,
    BottomCenter,
    BottomLeft,
}

impl FpsPos {
    pub const ALL: [FpsPos; 7] =
        [FpsPos::Auto, FpsPos::TopLeft, FpsPos::TopCenter, FpsPos::TopRight, FpsPos::BottomRight, FpsPos::BottomCenter, FpsPos::BottomLeft];
    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            FpsPos::Auto => "auto",
            FpsPos::TopLeft => "top left",
            FpsPos::TopCenter => "top center",
            FpsPos::TopRight => "top right",
            FpsPos::BottomRight => "bottom right",
            FpsPos::BottomCenter => "bottom center",
            FpsPos::BottomLeft => "bottom left",
        }
    }
    pub fn next(self) -> FpsPos {
        let i = Self::ALL.iter().position(|&p| p == self).unwrap_or(0);
        Self::ALL[(i + 1) % Self::ALL.len()]
    }
}

/// FPS counter (drawn by [`crate::fps`] in the top-right corner of the visible game area).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
pub enum FpsCounter {
    #[default]
    Off,
    /// Game frames per second.
    Fps,
    /// FPS + frame time (avg / worst) + guest MIPS (+ display refresh rate when the frontend reports it).
    Detailed,
}

impl FpsCounter {
    pub const ALL: [FpsCounter; 3] = [FpsCounter::Off, FpsCounter::Fps, FpsCounter::Detailed];
    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            FpsCounter::Off => "Off",
            FpsCounter::Fps => "FPS",
            FpsCounter::Detailed => "FPS + details",
        }
    }
    pub fn next(self) -> FpsCounter {
        let i = Self::ALL.iter().position(|&m| m == self).unwrap_or(0);
        Self::ALL[(i + 1) % Self::ALL.len()]
    }
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<FpsCounter> {
        match s.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
            "off" | "0" | "none" => Some(FpsCounter::Off),
            "fps" | "on" | "1" => Some(FpsCounter::Fps),
            "full" | "detailed" | "details" | "2" => Some(FpsCounter::Detailed),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// `display` section of `mods-settings.json`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct DisplaySettings {
    pub mode: DisplayMode,
    pub filter: ScaleFilter,

    /// offers.
    pub refresh_hz: u32,
    /// Game frame limit (fps) applied by the DirectDraw frame limiter (`s3_dx::ddraw::set_fps_cap`): one of
    /// [`fps_limit_options`] (30, 60, 120, 144, or the display's refresh rate when it is higher).

            fps_limit: DEFAULT_FPS_LIMIT,
            fps_pos: FpsPos::Auto,
        }
    }
}

/// Default game frame limit (the original game's 60 Hz pacing).
pub const DEFAULT_FPS_LIMIT: u32 = 60;
/// Fixed frame limit choices; the display's refresh rate is added when it is higher ([`fps_limit_options`]).
pub const FPS_LIMITS: [u32; 4] = [30, 60, 120, 144];

/// UI mode A in `NativeWide` with the custom resolution (docs/porting/display.md "Classic panel"): the original
/// panel (frame `x < w`, `y < h` = the panel art of the current layout variant) is shown at a constant scale
/// (`window height / h`, the art fills the screen height at every zoom level) on the left; the map part of the frame
/// (`x >= w`) fills the rest of the window. The zoom picks render widths that keep the map's aspect
/// (`crate::zoom::classic_width`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PanelSplit {
    pub w: u32,
    pub h: u32,
    /// UI mode A zoomed in below the panel art (`zoom::classic_crop`): only this many rows of the map part are
    /// shown (centred, with the matching width); 0 = the whole map part.
    pub crop_h: u32,
}

/// Parts of the 640x480 panel art (`res::CLASSIC_VARIANT`) that reach past the panel width into the map view:
/// the minimap frame's diagonal edge and leaves (`y0, y1, x_end` in game px; runs of rows with the same `x_end` =
/// the rightmost art pixel + 1, measured from a game frame with a black map behind, 2026-11-08). Exact per row:
/// 4-row bands also carried map pixels right of the art, which then moved during zoom (phone report). Only the
/// minimap frame (rows < 156): the leaves further down reach at most to x 144; they are cut at the panel edge
/// instead, and the map part starts right of them ([`PanelSplit::map_x0`]), else the frame showed them a second
/// time in the map part at the map's scale, at other heights than the panel's ("the effect at the panel's right
/// edge moves while zooming", 2026-11-08). With a
/// [`PanelSplit`] they are drawn at the panel's scale on top of the map part, else they scaled with the zoom
/// like the map (user report: "the diagonal edge still moves"). Numbers only, no game art.
const OVERHANG_136X480: [(u16, u16, u16); 84] = [
    (0, 6, 207), (6, 8, 206), (8, 10, 205), (10, 12, 204), (12, 14, 203), (14, 16, 202), (16, 18, 201), (18, 19, 199),
    (19, 20, 200), (20, 22, 199), (22, 24, 198), (24, 25, 196), (25, 26, 197), (26, 28, 196), (28, 30, 195), (30, 31, 193),
    (31, 32, 194), (32, 34, 193), (34, 36, 192), (36, 38, 191), (38, 40, 190), (40, 42, 189), (42, 44, 188), (44, 46, 187),
    (46, 48, 186), (48, 50, 185), (50, 52, 184), (52, 54, 183), (54, 56, 182), (56, 58, 181), (58, 60, 180), (60, 62, 179),
    (62, 64, 178), (64, 66, 177), (66, 68, 176), (68, 70, 175), (70, 72, 174), (72, 74, 173), (74, 76, 172), (76, 81, 171),
    (81, 82, 170), (82, 83, 169), (83, 84, 168), (84, 85, 167), (85, 86, 174), (86, 88, 175), (88, 89, 174), (89, 93, 175),
    (93, 94, 163), (94, 96, 162), (96, 98, 161), (98, 100, 160), (100, 102, 159), (102, 104, 158), (104, 106, 157), (106, 107, 156),
    (107, 108, 157), (108, 109, 158), (109, 110, 159), (110, 113, 160), (113, 114, 157), (114, 118, 158), (118, 119, 151), (119, 120, 152),
    (120, 121, 154), (121, 124, 155), (124, 125, 153), (125, 126, 151), (126, 127, 148), (127, 128, 149), (128, 130, 150), (130, 131, 149),
    (131, 132, 148), (132, 134, 147), (134, 135, 146), (135, 136, 145), (136, 138, 144), (138, 140, 143), (140, 143, 142), (143, 145, 141),
    (145, 148, 140), (148, 151, 139), (151, 152, 138), (152, 155, 137),
];

/// Frame columns right of the panel width that are not shown in the map part (panel leaves, see
/// `OVERHANG_136X480`): 9 for the 640x480 panel.
pub const fn map_skip(w: u32, h: u32) -> u32 {
    if w == 136 && h == 480 {
        9
    } else {
        0
    }
}

impl PanelSplit {
    /// The crop height, if any.
    pub fn crop(&self) -> Option<u32> {
        (self.crop_h > 0).then_some(self.crop_h)
    }

    /// Bands of the panel art past `w` (see `OVERHANG_136X480`; none for the other variants).
    pub fn overhang(&self) -> &'static [(u16, u16, u16)] {
        if (self.w, self.h) == (136, 480) {
            &OVERHANG_136X480
        } else {
            &[]
        }
    }

    /// Frame x where the shown map part starts: right of the panel art's leaves (`w + 9` for the 640x480 panel).
    pub fn map_x0(&self) -> u32 {
        self.w + map_skip(self.w, self.h)
    }

    /// Right edge (game x) of the panel art in row `y`: `w`, or further in an overhang band.
    pub fn art_right(&self, y: f32) -> f32 {
        let yi = y.max(0.0) as u16;
        self.overhang().iter().find(|b| yi >= b.0 && yi < b.1).map_or(self.w as f32, |b| b.2 as f32)
    }
}

/// Placement of a `game_w` x `game_h` frame in a `win_w` x `win_h` window (physical pixels). The destination
/// rectangle may extend past the window (`Fill`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub struct Viewport {
    pub mode: DisplayMode,
    pub game_w: u32,
    pub game_h: u32,
    pub win_w: u32,
    pub win_h: u32,
    /// Destination rectangle of the whole game frame in window pixels.
    pub dst_x: f32,
    pub dst_y: f32,
    pub dst_w: f32,
    pub dst_h: f32,
    /// Full-screen menu layout ([`crate::menu_layout`]): the frame is shown re-arranged on a canvas. Then
    /// `dst_*` describe the canvas placement (origin, frame size times the canvas scale) and the window is fully
    /// covered (no bars).
    pub layout: Option<&'static MenuLayout>,
    /// Classic panel shown at its own scale ([`PanelSplit`]); then `dst_*` = the whole window.
    pub panel: Option<PanelSplit>,
}

impl Viewport {
    pub fn new(mode: DisplayMode, game_w: u32, game_h: u32, win_w: u32, win_h: u32) -> Viewport {
        let (gw, gh) = (game_w.max(1), game_h.max(1));
        let (ww, wh) = (win_w.max(1), win_h.max(1));
        let (sx, sy) = (ww as f64 / gw as f64, wh as f64 / gh as f64);
        let (dw, dh) = match mode {
            // Native wide: the render size has the window's aspect up to the width rounding (multiple of 8), which
            // left 1-4 px bars whose width changed with every zoom step; the whole UI anchored to the shown frame
            // then shifted by a few px per step (Mobile HUD "jitter", 2026-11-08). Within 2 % fill the window.
            DisplayMode::NativeWide
                if ((gw as f64 * sy) - ww as f64).abs() <= ww as f64 * 0.02
                    && ((gh as f64 * sx) - wh as f64).abs() <= wh as f64 * 0.02 =>
            {
                (ww as f64, wh as f64)
            }
            DisplayMode::Fit | DisplayMode::NativeWide => {
                let s = sx.min(sy);
                // Snap to the window edge when within half a pixel (avoid 1 px bars from rounding).
                let dw = if (gw as f64 * s - ww as f64).abs() < 1.0 { ww as f64 } else { (gw as f64 * s).round() };
                let dh = if (gh as f64 * s - wh as f64).abs() < 1.0 { wh as f64 } else { (gh as f64 * s).round() };
                (dw, dh)
            }
            DisplayMode::Fill => {
                let s = sx.max(sy);
                ((gw as f64 * s).round().max(ww as f64), (gh as f64 * s).round().max(wh as f64))
            }
            DisplayMode::Stretch => (ww as f64, wh as f64),
        };
        let dx = ((ww as f64 - dw) / 2.0).round();
        let dy = ((wh as f64 - dh) / 2.0).round();
        Viewport { mode, game_w: gw, game_h: gh, win_w: ww, win_h: wh, dst_x: dx as f32, dst_y: dy as f32, dst_w: dw as f32, dst_h: dh as f32, layout: None, panel: None }
    }

    /// Viewport for this frame: a full-screen menu layout when the frame is a known menu screen and the mode
    /// fills the screen (`NativeWide`, `Fill`), else [`Viewport::new`].
    pub fn for_frame(mode: DisplayMode, pixels: &[u16], game_w: u32, game_h: u32, win_w: u32, win_h: u32) -> Viewport {
        Viewport::for_frame_split(mode, pixels, game_w, game_h, win_w, win_h, None)
    }

    /// [`Viewport::for_frame`] with the Classic panel split the mods published for this frame
    /// ([`crate::layer::Scene::panel`]); a menu layout wins over it.
    pub fn for_frame_split(mode: DisplayMode, pixels: &[u16], game_w: u32, game_h: u32, win_w: u32, win_h: u32, panel: Option<PanelSplit>) -> Viewport {
        if matches!(mode, DisplayMode::NativeWide | DisplayMode::Fill) {
            if let Some(l) = menu_layout::detect(pixels, game_w, game_h) {
                return Viewport::with_layout(mode, menu_layout::choose(l, win_w, win_h), win_w, win_h);
            }
        }
        Viewport::new_split(mode, game_w, game_h, win_w, win_h, panel)
    }

    /// [`Viewport::new`], with the Classic panel at its own scale when `panel` is given, the mode is `NativeWide`
    /// and the split fits (panel narrower than the frame and the window, art not taller than the frame).
    pub fn new_split(mode: DisplayMode, game_w: u32, game_h: u32, win_w: u32, win_h: u32, panel: Option<PanelSplit>) -> Viewport {
        let mut v = Viewport::new(mode, game_w, game_h, win_w, win_h);
        if let Some(p) = panel {
            let ok = mode == DisplayMode::NativeWide && p.w > 0 && p.h > 0 && p.w < v.game_w && p.h <= v.game_h;
            let pw_win = (p.w as f64 * v.win_h as f64 / p.h.max(1) as f64).round();
            if ok && pw_win + 16.0 < v.win_w as f64 {
                v.panel = Some(p);
                v.dst_x = 0.0;
                v.dst_y = 0.0;
                v.dst_w = v.win_w as f32;
                v.dst_h = v.win_h as f32;
            }
        }
        v
    }

    /// With a panel split: (panel width in window px, window px per game px of the panel).
    fn split(&self) -> Option<(PanelSplit, f32, f32)> {
        let p = self.panel?;
        let ps = self.win_h as f32 / p.h.max(1) as f32;
        Some((p, (p.w as f32 * ps).round(), ps))
    }

    /// With a panel split: the source rectangle of the map part (game px: x, y, w, h); a centred crop when
    /// [`PanelSplit::crop_h`] is set.
    fn map_src(&self, p: PanelSplit) -> (f32, f32, f32, f32) {
        let x0 = p.map_x0().min(self.game_w.saturating_sub(1));
        let (mw, gh) = ((self.game_w - x0) as f32, self.game_h as f32);
        match p.crop().filter(|&c| c < self.game_h) {
            Some(c) => {
                let (ch, cw) = (c as f32, mw * c as f32 / gh);
                (x0 as f32 + (mw - cw) / 2.0, (gh - ch) / 2.0, cw, ch)
            }
            None => (x0 as f32, 0.0, mw, gh),
        }
    }

    /// Source rectangles (game px: x, y, w, h) and where they are drawn (window px: x, y, w, h) for a frame without
    /// a menu layout: the whole frame, or the panel and the map part with a [`PanelSplit`].
    pub fn quads(&self) -> Vec<([f32; 4], [f32; 4])> {
        let (gw, gh) = (self.game_w as f32, self.game_h as f32);
        match self.split() {
            Some((p, pww, ps)) => {
                let mut q = vec![
                    ([0.0, 0.0, p.w as f32, p.h as f32], [0.0, 0.0, pww, p.h as f32 * ps]),
                    ({
                        let (x, y, w, h) = self.map_src(p);
                        [x, y, w, h]
                    }, [pww, 0.0, self.win_w as f32 - pww, self.win_h as f32]),
                ];
                // Panel art past the panel width, at the panel's scale on top of the map part.
                for &(y0, y1, xe) in p.overhang() {
                    let (y0, y1, xe) = (y0 as f32, y1 as f32, (xe as f32).min(gw));
                    if xe > p.w as f32 && y1 <= gh {
                        q.push(([p.w as f32, y0, xe - p.w as f32, y1 - y0], [pww, y0 * ps, (xe - p.w as f32) * ps, (y1 - y0) * ps]));
                    }
                }
                q
            }
            None => vec![([0.0, 0.0, gw, gh], [self.dst_x, self.dst_y, self.dst_w, self.dst_h])],
        }
    }

    /// Window px per game px of the panel part (`None` without a split).
    pub fn panel_scale(&self) -> Option<f32> {
        self.split().map(|s| s.2)
    }

    /// Viewport showing the frame through a menu layout.
    pub fn with_layout(mode: DisplayMode, l: &'static MenuLayout, win_w: u32, win_h: u32) -> Viewport {
        let (ww, wh) = (win_w.max(1), win_h.max(1));
        let (ox, oy, sc) = menu_layout::canvas_placement(l, ww, wh);
        let (gw, gh) = (l.frame[0] as u32, l.frame[1] as u32);
        Viewport { mode, game_w: gw, game_h: gh, win_w: ww, win_h: wh, dst_x: ox, dst_y: oy, dst_w: gw as f32 * sc, dst_h: gh as f32 * sc, layout: Some(l), panel: None }
    }

    /// Window pixel -> game pixel, clamped to the frame.
    pub fn window_to_game(&self, x: f32, y: f32) -> (i32, i32) {
        let (gx, gy) = self.window_to_game_f(x, y);
        (
            (gx.floor() as i64).clamp(0, self.game_w as i64 - 1) as i32,
            (gy.floor() as i64).clamp(0, self.game_h as i64 - 1) as i32,
        )
    }

    /// Window pixel -> game coordinates (unclamped, fractional).
    pub fn window_to_game_f(&self, x: f32, y: f32) -> (f32, f32) {
        if let Some((p, pww, ps)) = self.split() {
            if x < pww || (y < p.h as f32 * ps && x < p.art_right(y / ps) * ps) {
                return (x / ps, y / ps);
            }
            let mw = (self.win_w as f32 - pww).max(1.0);
            let (sx, sy, sw, sh) = self.map_src(p);
            return (sx + (x - pww) * sw / mw, sy + y * sh / self.win_h as f32);
        }
        if let Some(l) = self.layout {
            let (sx, sy) = self.scale();
            return l.canvas_to_game((x - self.dst_x) / sx, (y - self.dst_y) / sy);
        }
        (
            ((x as f64 - self.dst_x as f64) * self.game_w as f64 / self.dst_w as f64) as f32,
            ((y as f64 - self.dst_y as f64) * self.game_h as f64 / self.dst_h as f64) as f32,
        )
    }

    /// Game pixel -> window pixel (top-left corner of that game pixel).
    pub fn game_to_window(&self, gx: f32, gy: f32) -> (f32, f32) {
        if let Some((p, pww, ps)) = self.split() {
            if gx < p.art_right(gy) {
                return (gx * ps, gy * ps);
            }
            let mw = self.win_w as f32 - pww;
            let (sx, sy, sw, sh) = self.map_src(p);
            return (pww + (gx - sx) * mw / sw.max(1.0), (gy - sy) * self.win_h as f32 / sh.max(1.0));
        }
        if let Some(l) = self.layout {
            // Game pixels not shown by any piece go far off screen.
            let (u, v) = l.game_to_canvas(gx, gy).unwrap_or((-1.0e6, -1.0e6));
            let (sx, sy) = self.scale();
            return (self.dst_x + u * sx, self.dst_y + v * sy);
        }
        (self.dst_x + gx * self.dst_w / self.game_w as f32, self.dst_y + gy * self.dst_h / self.game_h as f32)
    }

    /// Window pixels per game pixel (x, y); with a panel split: of the map part.
    pub fn scale(&self) -> (f32, f32) {
        if let Some((p, pww, _)) = self.split() {
            let (_, _, sw, sh) = self.map_src(p);
            return ((self.win_w as f32 - pww) / sw.max(1.0), self.win_h as f32 / sh.max(1.0));
        }
        (self.dst_w / self.game_w as f32, self.dst_h / self.game_h as f32)
    }

    /// Part of the game frame that is on screen, in game pixels (x, y, w, h). The whole frame except in `Fill`.
    pub fn visible_game_rect(&self) -> (i32, i32, i32, i32) {
        if self.layout.is_some() || self.panel.is_some() {
            return (0, 0, self.game_w as i32, self.game_h as i32);
        }
        let (x0, y0) = self.window_to_game_f(0.0, 0.0);
        let (x1, y1) = self.window_to_game_f(self.win_w as f32, self.win_h as f32);
        let x0 = (x0.max(0.0).ceil() as i32).min(self.game_w as i32);
        let y0 = (y0.max(0.0).ceil() as i32).min(self.game_h as i32);
        let x1 = (x1.min(self.game_w as f32).floor() as i32).max(x0);
        let y1 = (y1.min(self.game_h as f32).floor() as i32).max(y0);
        (x0, y0, x1 - x0, y1 - y0)
    }

    /// Destination rectangle clipped to the window: (x, y, w, h) in whole window pixels.
    pub fn dst_rect_clipped(&self) -> (i32, i32, i32, i32) {
        if self.layout.is_some() || self.panel.is_some() {
            return (0, 0, self.win_w as i32, self.win_h as i32);
        }
        let x0 = self.dst_x.max(0.0).round() as i32;
        let y0 = self.dst_y.max(0.0).round() as i32;
        let x1 = (self.dst_x + self.dst_w).min(self.win_w as f32).round() as i32;
        let y1 = (self.dst_y + self.dst_h).min(self.win_h as f32).round() as i32;
        (x0, y0, (x1 - x0).max(0), (y1 - y0).max(0))
    }

    /// Black bar sizes in window pixels: (left, right, top, bottom).
    pub fn bars(&self) -> (u32, u32, u32, u32) {
        let (x, y, w, h) = self.dst_rect_clipped();
        (x as u32, (self.win_w as i32 - x - w).max(0) as u32, y as u32, (self.win_h as i32 - y - h).max(0) as u32)
    }

    /// Aspect-matched game resolution for `NativeWide`: the window's aspect ratio with height `game_h`
    /// (width rounded to a multiple of 8, as DirectDraw surfaces of the game like).
    pub fn native_wide_size(win_w: u32, win_h: u32, game_h: u32) -> (u32, u32) {
        let w = (game_h as u64 * win_w.max(1) as u64 + win_h.max(1) as u64 / 2) / win_h.max(1) as u64;
        ((((w + 4) / 8) * 8).max(8) as u32, game_h)
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- CPU scaler (desktop window, CPU fallback)

/// One axis of a scaling: for each destination pixel the two source taps and the weight of the second (0..=256).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct AxisTaps {
    pub i0: Vec<u32>,
    pub i1: Vec<u32>,
    pub w1: Vec<u16>,
}

/// Taps for `dst_n` destination pixels starting at window coordinate `dst_from`, for a source of `src_n` pixels
/// drawn at `dst_off` with size `dst_size` (window pixels).
pub fn axis_taps(filter: ScaleFilter, src_n: u32, dst_from: i32, dst_n: u32, dst_off: f32, dst_size: f32) -> AxisTaps {
    let mut t = AxisTaps { i0: Vec::with_capacity(dst_n as usize), i1: Vec::with_capacity(dst_n as usize), w1: Vec::with_capacity(dst_n as usize) };
    let n = src_n.max(1) as f64;
    let scale = dst_size as f64 / n; // window px per source px
    let last = src_n.saturating_sub(1);
    for d in 0..dst_n {
        // Source coordinate of the destination pixel centre.
        let s = ((dst_from + d as i32) as f64 + 0.5 - dst_off as f64) / scale;
        let (i0, i1, w) = match filter {
            ScaleFilter::Nearest => {
                let i = (s.floor().max(0.0) as u32).min(last);
                (i, i, 0.0)
            }
            ScaleFilter::Linear => {
                let c = s - 0.5;
                let f = c.floor();
                (f.max(0.0) as u32, ((f + 1.0).max(0.0) as u32), c - f)
            }
            ScaleFilter::SharpBilinear | ScaleFilter::Xbr | ScaleFilter::Ai => {
                // Same as the GLES shader: linear only across a 1-window-pixel band around texel edges.
                let fl = s.floor();
                let fr = s - fl - 0.5;
                let range = 0.5 - 0.5 / scale.max(1.0);
                let f = (fr - fr.clamp(-range, range)) * scale.max(1.0) + 0.5;
                let c = fl + f - 0.5;
                let cf = c.floor();
                (cf.max(0.0) as u32, ((cf + 1.0).max(0.0) as u32), c - cf)
            }
        };
        t.i0.push(i0.min(last));
        t.i1.push(i1.min(last));
        t.w1.push((w.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * 256.0).round() as u16);
    }
    t
}

#[inline]
fn rgb565_to_888(p: u16) -> (u32, u32, u32) {
    let r = ((p >> 11) & 31) as u32;
    let g = ((p >> 5) & 63) as u32;
    let b = (p & 31) as u32;
    ((r << 3) | (r >> 2), (g << 2) | (g >> 4), (b << 3) | (b >> 2))
}

/// Scale an RGB565 frame into an XRGB8888 window buffer (`dst` = `win_w * win_h`) with black bars.
pub fn scale_to_xrgb(vp: &Viewport, filter: ScaleFilter, src: &[u16], dst: &mut [u32]) {
    let (ww, wh) = (vp.win_w as usize, vp.win_h as usize);
    let (gw, gh) = (vp.game_w as usize, vp.game_h as usize);
    if dst.len() < ww * wh || src.len() < gw * gh {
        return;
    }
    if let Some(l) = vp.layout {
        menu_layout::render_xrgb(l, src, gw, gh, dst, ww, wh);
        return;
    }
    dst[..ww * wh].fill(0);
    for (s, d) in vp.quads() {
        scale_region(filter, src, gw, s, d, ww, wh, dst);
    }
}

/// Draw the layer's frame insets ([`crate::layer::Cmd::FrameInset`]) into an XRGB window buffer (CPU frontends).
pub fn draw_insets_xrgb(insets: &[([f32; 4], [f32; 4])], filter: ScaleFilter, src: &[u16], gw: usize, gh: usize, dst: &mut [u32], ww: usize, wh: usize) {
    for &(s, d) in insets {
        if s[0] >= 0.0 && s[1] >= 0.0 && (s[0] + s[2]) as usize <= gw && (s[1] + s[3]) as usize <= gh {
            scale_region(filter, src, gw, s, d, ww, wh, dst);
        }
    }
}

/// Scale the source rectangle `s` (game px x, y, w, h) of an RGB565 frame (`gw` wide) to the window rectangle `d`
/// (clipped to the `ww` x `wh` window buffer).
fn scale_region(filter: ScaleFilter, src: &[u16], gw: usize, s: [f32; 4], d: [f32; 4], ww: usize, wh: usize, dst: &mut [u32]) {
    let (sx, sy, sw, sh) = (s[0] as usize, s[1] as usize, s[2] as u32, s[3] as u32);
    let rx = d[0].max(0.0).round() as i32;
    let ry = d[1].max(0.0).round() as i32;
    let rw = ((d[0] + d[2]).min(ww as f32).round() as i32 - rx).max(0);
    let rh = ((d[1] + d[3]).min(wh as f32).round() as i32 - ry).max(0);
    if rw == 0 || rh == 0 || sw == 0 || sh == 0 {
        return;
    }
    let tx = axis_taps(filter, sw, rx, rw as u32, d[0], d[2]);
    let ty = axis_taps(filter, sh, ry, rh as u32, d[1], d[3]);
    let plain = filter == ScaleFilter::Nearest;
    for (yi, y) in (ry as usize..ry as usize + rh as usize).enumerate() {
        let r0 = (sy + ty.i0[yi] as usize) * gw + sx;
        let r1 = (sy + ty.i1[yi] as usize) * gw + sx;
        let row0 = &src[r0..r0 + sw as usize];
        let row1 = &src[r1..r1 + sw as usize];
        let wy = ty.w1[yi] as u32;
        let out = &mut dst[y * ww + rx as usize..y * ww + rx as usize + rw as usize];
        if plain || (wy == 0 && tx.w1.iter().all(|&w| w == 0)) {
            for (xi, o) in out.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                let (r, g, b) = rgb565_to_888(row0[tx.i0[xi] as usize]);
                *o = (r << 16) | (g << 8) | b;
            }
            continue;
        }
        for (xi, o) in out.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            let wx = tx.w1[xi] as u32;
            let (a, b_) = (tx.i0[xi] as usize, tx.i1[xi] as usize);
            let p00 = rgb565_to_888(row0[a]);
            let p01 = rgb565_to_888(row0[b_]);
            let p10 = rgb565_to_888(row1[a]);
            let p11 = rgb565_to_888(row1[b_]);
            let lerp = |c00: u32, c01: u32, c10: u32, c11: u32| {
                let top = c00 * (256 - wx) + c01 * wx;
                let bot = c10 * (256 - wx) + c11 * wx;
                (top * (256 - wy) + bot * wy + 32768) >> 16
            };
            let r = lerp(p00.0, p01.0, p10.0, p11.0);
            let g = lerp(p00.1, p01.1, p10.1, p11.1);
            let b = lerp(p00.2, p01.2, p10.2, p11.2);
            *o = (r << 16) | (g << 8) | b;
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- machine state (frontend <-> mods)

/// Display info published by the frontend.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct DisplayState {
    /// Viewport used for the last shown frame (`None` headless / before the first frame).
    pub viewport: Option<Viewport>,
    /// Display (host) presents per second, if the frontend measures them (Android render thread).
    pub host_fps: Option<f32>,
    /// Display refresh rate the frontend runs at, if known.
    pub refresh_hz: Option<f32>,
    /// Screen density in dpi (frontend; 0 = unknown).
    pub density_dpi: u32,
    /// Bumped whenever [`DisplaySettings`] change through this module (frontends may poll it).
    pub settings_seq: u64,
}

/// Frontend: publish the viewport of the shown frame.
pub fn set_viewport(m: &mut Machine, vp: Option<Viewport>) {
    m.state::<DisplayState>().borrow_mut().viewport = vp;
}

/// Viewport of the shown frame (`None` headless).
pub fn viewport(m: &mut Machine) -> Option<Viewport> {
    m.state::<DisplayState>().borrow_mut().viewport
}

/// Window size of the frontend (`None` headless).
pub fn window_size(m: &mut Machine) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
    viewport(m).map(|v| (v.win_w, v.win_h))
}

/// Visible part of the game frame (game pixels); the whole last frame when no viewport is known.
pub fn visible_game_rect(m: &mut Machine) -> (i32, i32, i32, i32) {
    let size = m.last_frame_size();
    match viewport(m) {
        Some(v) if (v.game_w, v.game_h) == size || size == (0, 0) => v.visible_game_rect(),
        Some(v) => Viewport::new(v.mode, size.0, size.1, v.win_w, v.win_h).visible_game_rect(),
        None => (0, 0, size.0 as i32, size.1 as i32),
    }
}

/// Classic panel split for the last frame (see [`PanelSplit`]): UI mode A, display mode `NativeWide`, custom
/// resolution on, in game and the layout globals match the frame. `S3_PANEL_SPLIT=0` turns it off.
pub fn panel_split(m: &mut Machine) -> Option<PanelSplit> {
    let (fw, fh) = m.last_frame_size();
    let (mode, ui) = {
        let st = m.state::<crate::ModsState>();
        let s = st.borrow_mut();
        (s.settings.display.mode, s.settings.ui_mode)
    };
    if mode != DisplayMode::NativeWide || ui != crate::settings::UiMode::ClassicTouch || std::env::var("S3_PANEL_SPLIT").is_ok_and(|v| v == "0") {
        return None;
    }
    if !crate::zoom::enabled(m) || !crate::res::in_game_frame(m) {
        if std::env::var_os("S3_PANEL_TRACE").is_some() {
            let (fw, fh) = m.last_frame_size();
            eprintln!(
                "panel_split: none: zoom {} in_game {} t {} frame {fw}x{fh} glob {}x{} last {}",
                crate::zoom::enabled(m),
                crate::res::in_game_frame(m),
                m.real_ms(),
                m.mem.read_u32(crate::res::L_SCREEN_W),
                m.mem.read_u32(crate::res::L_SCREEN_H),
                m.state::<crate::res::ResState>().borrow_mut().last_frame_ms
            );
        }
        return None;
    }
    let pw = m.mem.read_u32(crate::res::L_PANEL_W);
    // The layout globals may already be for the next size while this frame has the old one (zoom in progress);
    // UI mode A uses one panel variant at every size (`res::CLASSIC_VARIANT`), so only the fit is checked.
    let v = crate::res::variant(m.mem.read_u32(crate::res::L_RES))?;
    let r = (pw > 0 && pw == v.panel_w && pw < fw && v.h <= fh).then_some(PanelSplit { w: pw, h: v.h, crop_h: 0 });
    let crop = crate::zoom::classic_crop(m).filter(|&c| c < fh).unwrap_or(0);
    let r = r.map(|p| PanelSplit { crop_h: crop, ..p });
    if r.is_none() && std::env::var_os("S3_PANEL_TRACE").is_some() {
        eprintln!("panel_split: none: frame {fw}x{fh} pw {pw} variant {} ({}x{})", v.index, v.panel_w, v.h);
    }
    r
}

/// Frontends: the panel split for a frame of size `frame`, given the latest published scene (its split and the
/// frame size it was made for). During a zoom the frame of a new size can reach the presenter before the scene
/// made for it; showing it without the split made the Classic panel jump to the frame's scale for one frame
/// (flicker, 2026-11-08). The panel variant does not change with the size in UI mode A, so the split carries over.
pub fn panel_for_frame(scene_panel: Option<PanelSplit>, scene_frame: (u32, u32), frame: (u32, u32)) -> Option<PanelSplit> {
    let p = scene_panel?;
    if scene_frame == frame {
        return Some(p);
    }
    // UI mode A uses one panel variant at every size (`res::CLASSIC_VARIANT`): the split carries over (a crop
    // only to a frame of the same height).
    let crop_h = if scene_frame.1 == frame.1 && p.crop_h < frame.1 { p.crop_h } else { 0 };
    (p.w < frame.0 && p.h <= frame.1).then_some(PanelSplit { crop_h, ..p })
}

/// Viewport of the last game frame as the frontend will show it: published window size, display mode, the panel
/// split of this frame (the published menu layout when it is for a frame of this size). Headless without a window
/// size: the frame itself (1:1).
pub fn frame_viewport(m: &mut Machine) -> Viewport {
    let (fw, fh) = m.last_frame_size();
    let (fw, fh) = (fw.max(1), fh.max(1));
    let panel = panel_split(m);
    match viewport(m) {
        Some(v) if v.layout.is_some() && (v.game_w, v.game_h) == (fw, fh) => v,
        Some(v) => Viewport::new_split(v.mode, fw, fh, v.win_w, v.win_h, panel),
        None => Viewport::new(DisplayMode::Stretch, fw, fh, fw, fh),
    }
}

/// Frontend: report display-side rates (shown by the detailed FPS counter).
/// Frontend: screen density in dpi (0 = unknown, e.g. desktop).
pub fn set_density(m: &mut Machine, dpi: u32) {
    m.state::<DisplayState>().borrow_mut().density_dpi = dpi;
}

/// Window pixels per Android dp (density / 160), if the frontend reported a density. UI that should keep a
/// constant physical size on every screen (phone cover / foldable inner screen / tablet) uses it.
pub fn dp(m: &mut Machine) -> Option<f32> {
    let d = m.state::<DisplayState>().borrow_mut().density_dpi;
    (d >= 80).then(|| d as f32 / 160.0)
}

pub fn set_host_rates(m: &mut Machine, host_fps: Option<f32>, refresh_hz: Option<f32>) {
    let st = m.state::<DisplayState>();
    let mut s = st.borrow_mut();
    s.host_fps = host_fps;
    s.refresh_hz = refresh_hz;
}

/// Current display settings (cheap copy; frontends call it once per slice).
pub fn display_settings(m: &mut Machine) -> DisplaySettings {
    m.state::<crate::ModsState>().borrow_mut().settings.display
}

/// Change and persist the display settings.
pub fn set_display(m: &mut Machine, d: DisplaySettings) {
    let mut s = crate::settings(m);
    if s.display == d {
        return;
    }
    s.display = d;
    if let Err(e) = crate::set_settings(m, s) {
        m.log(s3_runtime::LogLevel::Warn, &format!("display: saving settings failed: {e}"));
    }
    m.state::<DisplayState>().borrow_mut().settings_seq += 1;
    m.log(s3_runtime::LogLevel::Info, &format!("display: {:?} / {:?} / fps {:?}", d.mode, d.filter, d.fps_counter));
}

/// Set the display settings for this run only (not saved; e.g. `s3run --display/--fps`).
pub fn override_display(m: &mut Machine, d: DisplaySettings) {
    m.state::<crate::ModsState>().borrow_mut().settings.display = d;
    m.state::<DisplayState>().borrow_mut().settings_seq += 1;
}

/// Menu helpers: next value, persisted. They return the new value (for the button label).
pub fn cycle_mode(m: &mut Machine) -> DisplayMode {
    let mut d = display_settings(m);
    d.mode = d.mode.next();
    set_display(m, d);
    d.mode
}

pub fn cycle_filter(m: &mut Machine) -> ScaleFilter {
    let mut d = display_settings(m);
    d.filter = d.filter.next();
    set_display(m, d);
    d.filter
}

/// Frame limit choices: [`FPS_LIMITS`] plus the display's refresh rate (published by the frontend) when higher.
pub fn fps_limit_options(m: &mut Machine) -> Vec<u32> {
    let mut v = FPS_LIMITS.to_vec();
    let hz = m.state::<DisplayState>().borrow_mut().refresh_hz.map(|r| r.round() as u32).unwrap_or(0);
    if hz > *FPS_LIMITS.last().unwrap() {
        v.push(hz);
    }
    v
}

/// Next frame limit (saved and applied).
pub fn cycle_fps_limit(m: &mut Machine) -> u32 {
    let opts = fps_limit_options(m);
    let mut d = display_settings(m);
    let i = opts.iter().position(|&o| o == d.fps_limit);
    d.fps_limit = opts[i.map_or(0, |i| (i + 1) % opts.len())];
    set_display(m, d);
    apply_fps_limit(m);
    d.fps_limit
}

/// Apply the frame limit setting to the frame limiter, unless a developer override is set (env `S3_FPS_CAP`,
/// Android `fps-cap.txt` sets that env too).
pub fn apply_fps_limit(m: &mut Machine) {
    if std::env::var_os("S3_FPS_CAP").is_some() {
        return;
    }
    let l = display_settings(m).fps_limit;
    let l = if l == 0 { DEFAULT_FPS_LIMIT } else { l };
    s3_dx::ddraw::set_fps_cap(l);
}

/// Label for menus, e.g. "FPS limit: 60".
pub fn fps_limit_label(m: &mut Machine) -> String {
    format!("FPS limit: {}", display_settings(m).fps_limit)
}

/// Next FPS counter position (saved).
pub fn cycle_fps_pos(m: &mut Machine) -> FpsPos {
    let mut d = display_settings(m);
    d.fps_pos = d.fps_pos.next();
    set_display(m, d);
    d.fps_pos
}

pub fn cycle_fps(m: &mut Machine) -> FpsCounter {
    let mut d = display_settings(m);
    d.fps_counter = d.fps_counter.next();
    set_display(m, d);
    d.fps_counter
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
```
