```rs
    }

    #[test]
    fn cpu_scaler_nearest_and_sharp() {
        // 2x1 source: red, blue; scaled 2x into 4x2 window with Fit.
        let src = [0xF800u16, 0x001F];
        let v = Viewport::new(DisplayMode::Stretch, 2, 1, 4, 2);
        let mut dst = vec![0u32; 8];
        scale_to_xrgb(&v, ScaleFilter::Nearest, &src, &mut dst);
        assert_eq!(&dst[..4], &[0xFF0000, 0xFF0000, 0x0000FF, 0x0000FF]);
        assert_eq!(&dst[4..], &dst[..4].to_vec()[..]);
        // Sharp bilinear at an integer scale equals nearest.
        scale_to_xrgb(&v, ScaleFilter::SharpBilinear, &src, &mut dst);
        assert_eq!(&dst[..4], &[0xFF0000, 0xFF0000, 0x0000FF, 0x0000FF]);
        // Linear mixes in the middle.
        scale_to_xrgb(&v, ScaleFilter::Linear, &src, &mut dst);
        assert_eq!(dst[0], 0xFF0000);
        assert!(dst[1] >> 16 > 0 && dst[1] & 0xFF > 0, "{:x}", dst[1]);
        // Fit with bars: 2x1 in 4x4 -> rows 1..3 drawn, others black.
        let v = Viewport::new(DisplayMode::Fit, 2, 1, 4, 4);
        let mut dst = vec![7u32; 16];
        scale_to_xrgb(&v, ScaleFilter::Nearest, &src, &mut dst);
        assert_eq!(&dst[..4], &[0, 0, 0, 0]);
        assert_eq!(dst[4], 0xFF0000);
        assert_eq!(&dst[12..], &[0, 0, 0, 0]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn sharp_taps_are_monotonic_and_mostly_nearest() {
        let t = axis_taps(ScaleFilter::SharpBilinear, 800, 0, 2229, 0.0, 2229.0);
        let mut prev = 0.0f64;
        let mut blended = 0;
        for i in 0..t.i0.len() {
            let pos = t.i0[i] as f64 + t.w1[i] as f64 / 256.0;
            assert!(pos + 1e-9 >= prev, "not monotonic at {i}");
            prev = pos;
            if t.w1[i] != 0 && t.w1[i] != 256 {
                blended += 1;
            }
        }
        // ~2.8x scale: at most about one blended pixel per source pixel.
        assert!(blended <= 800, "{blended}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn panel_split_maps_both_parts() {
        // Fold4 cover 2316x904, Classic at 600 high: 800x600 art (panel 176), frame 1480x600.
        let p = PanelSplit { w: 176, h: 600, crop_h: 0 };
        let v = Viewport::new_split(DisplayMode::NativeWide, 1480, 600, 2316, 904, Some(p));
        assert_eq!(v.panel, Some(p));
        assert_eq!(v.bars(), (0, 0, 0, 0));
        let ps = v.panel_scale().unwrap();
        assert!((ps - 904.0 / 600.0).abs() < 1e-4);
        // Panel point.
        let (wx, wy) = v.game_to_window(100.0, 300.0);
        assert!((wx - 100.0 * ps).abs() < 0.01 && (wy - 452.0).abs() < 0.01);
        assert_eq!(v.window_to_game(wx + 0.1, wy + 0.1), (100, 300));
        // Map point round trip and the right edge.
        let (wx, wy) = v.game_to_window(1000.0, 450.0);
        assert_eq!(v.window_to_game(wx + 0.01, wy + 0.01), (1000, 450));
        assert_eq!(v.window_to_game(2315.0, 903.0), (1479, 599));
        // A taller frame (780 high, 1024x768 art): the panel keeps (almost) the same on-screen width.
        let v2 = Viewport::new_split(DisplayMode::NativeWide, 1880, 780, 2316, 904, Some(PanelSplit { w: 216, h: 768, crop_h: 0 }));
        let w1 = v.game_to_window(176.0, 0.0).0;
        let w2 = v2.game_to_window(216.0, 0.0).0;
        assert!((w1 - w2).abs() < 20.0, "{w1} {w2}");
        // Two quads (no overhang table for this variant); the CPU scaler fills the whole window.
        assert_eq!(v.quads().len(), 2);
        // The 640x480 panel: the minimap frame's diagonal edge stays at the panel scale.
        let v3 = Viewport::new_split(DisplayMode::NativeWide, 1600, 640, 2316, 904, Some(PanelSplit { w: 136, h: 480, crop_h: 0 }));
        assert_eq!(v3.quads().len(), 2 + 84);
        let ps3 = 904.0 / 480.0;
        let (wx, wy) = v3.game_to_window(200.0, 2.0);
        assert!((wx - 200.0 * ps3).abs() < 0.01 && (wy - 2.0 * ps3).abs() < 0.01);
        assert_eq!(v3.window_to_game(200.0 * ps3 + 0.5, 2.0 * ps3 + 0.5), (200, 2));
        // Below the overhang: map scale.
        let (wx, _) = v3.game_to_window(200.0, 300.0);
        assert!((wx - 200.0 * ps3).abs() > 1.0);
        // Crop (Classic zoomed below 480): 240 rows of a 480 high frame fill the window height.
        let v4 = Viewport::new_split(DisplayMode::NativeWide, 1240, 480, 2316, 904, Some(PanelSplit { w: 136, h: 480, crop_h: 240 }));
        let (sx, sy) = v4.scale();
        assert!((sy - 904.0 / 240.0).abs() < 0.01 && (sx / sy - 1.0).abs() < 0.02, "{sx} {sy}");
        // The map centre stays the window's map-part centre; round trip.
        let mid = (145.0 + (1240.0 - 145.0) / 2.0, 240.0);
        let (wx, wy) = v4.game_to_window(mid.0, mid.1);
        let pww = (136.0f32 * 904.0 / 480.0).round();
        assert!((wx - (pww + (2316.0 - pww) / 2.0)).abs() < 1.0 && (wy - 452.0).abs() < 1.0, "{wx} {wy}");
        assert_eq!(v4.window_to_game(wx + 0.01, wy + 0.01), (mid.0 as i32, mid.1 as i32));
        // The panel keeps its scale.
        assert_eq!(v4.window_to_game(100.0 * ps3 + 0.5, 300.0 * ps3 + 0.5), (100, 300));
        let src: Vec<u16> = (0..1480 * 600).map(|i| if i % 1480 < 176 { 0xF800 } else { 0x001F }).collect();
        let mut dst = vec![0u32; 2316 * 904];
        scale_to_xrgb(&v, ScaleFilter::Nearest, &src, &mut dst);
        assert_eq!(dst[0], 0xFF0000);
        assert_eq!(dst[903 * 2316 + 260], 0xFF0000);
        assert_eq!(dst[903 * 2316 + 2315], 0x0000FF);
        assert!(dst.iter().all(|&p| p != 0));
        // Not in Fit / without a panel.
        assert_eq!(Viewport::new_split(DisplayMode::Fit, 1480, 600, 2316, 904, Some(p)).panel, None);
        assert_eq!(Viewport::new_split(DisplayMode::NativeWide, 1480, 600, 2316, 904, None).panel, None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn enum_parsing_and_cycles() {
        assert_eq!(DisplayMode::parse("fill"), Some(DisplayMode::Fill));
        assert_eq!(DisplayMode::parse("native"), Some(DisplayMode::NativeWide));
        assert_eq!(DisplayMode::NativeWide.next(), DisplayMode::Fit);
        assert_eq!(FpsCounter::parse("full"), Some(FpsCounter::Detailed));
        assert_eq!(FpsCounter::Detailed.next(), FpsCounter::Off);
        assert_eq!(ScaleFilter::parse("sharp"), Some(ScaleFilter::SharpBilinear));
        let s: DisplaySettings = serde_json_roundtrip(&DisplaySettings { mode: DisplayMode::Fill, ..Default::default() });
        assert_eq!(s.mode, DisplayMode::Fill);
    }

    fn serde_json_roundtrip(d: &DisplaySettings) -> DisplaySettings {
        serde_json::from_str(&serde_json::to_string(d).unwrap()).unwrap()
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/end_stats.rs`:

```rs
//! Statistics over game time on the end-of-game "Game Statistics" screen (user request 2026-11-08: "make that
//! scoreboard like Settlers United made it"). Settlers United adds a "View Extended Game Stats" button there that
//! opens charts of Points / Settlers / Buildings / Food / Mines / Gold / Mana / Soldiers / Battles against game
//! time (docs/settlers-united/README.md). This is our own version of that idea, drawn in the window layer:
//!
//! - While a game runs, every [`SAMPLE_TICKS`] of game time, the game's own per-player statistics counters are
//!   read (`STATS_BASE`, one 0x44-byte record per player id 0..19; docs/reverse-engineering/game-state-ui.md
//!   "End-of-game statistics"). Read only: guest memory is never written (lockstep MP unaffected).
//! - On the statistics screen (detected menu layout `statistics*`), a button "Statistics over time" opens a
//!   full-window sheet: one tab per column of the game's table, a line per player, the game's own player rows
//!   (rank, team, name; copied from the frame) as the legend. Any other tap still leaves the screen as before.
//!
//! The history starts when the game (or the loaded save) starts in this session; it is not saved.

use s3_runtime::{FrameBuffer, Machine};

use crate::gesture::TouchEvent;
use crate::layer::Layer;
use crate::overlay::{measure_text, Rgba, Weight};
use crate::{Mod, ModEvent};

/// Per-player statistics records: `STATS_BASE + id * STATS_STRIDE`, 20 players.
pub const STATS_BASE: u32 = 0x007a_cfac;
pub const STATS_STRIDE: u32 = 0x44;
pub const PLAYERS: usize = 20;
/// Game clock (logic ticks of 64 ms), see `game_time.rs`.
const GAME_CLOCK_TICKS: u32 = 0x007d_fd48;
/// Sample every 10 s of game time (156 ticks of 64 ms).
pub const SAMPLE_TICKS: u32 = 156;
/// At most this many samples per game (older ones thinned out: every second one dropped).
const MAX_SAMPLES: usize = 720;
/// Out of the game for longer than this, a new game (or a loaded save) starts a new history.
const NEW_GAME_GAP_MS: u64 = 5_000;

/// Columns of the game's table (same order). Record offsets: rank `+0`, score `+0x1c`, counters `+0x20..+0x3c`.
pub const COLUMNS: [&str; 9] = ["Score", "Settlers", "Buildings", "Food", "Mines", "Gold", "Manna", "Soldiers", "Battles"];

/// One sample: game ticks and per player the 9 column values.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct Sample {
    pub tick: u32,
    pub v: [[u32; 9]; PLAYERS],
}

/// The 9 values of one record as the game's table shows them. `final_` = after the game computed its statistics
/// (`0x53e720`: score stored at `+0x1c`, gold halved in place); during the game the score is computed with the
/// same formula: 2 x settlers + buildings + food + mines + gold + manna + 2 x soldiers + 5 x battles.
pub fn values(rec: &[u32; 17], final_: bool) -> [u32; 9] {
    let c = |i: usize| rec[8 + i];
    let (settlers, buildings, food, mines, gold, manna, soldiers, battles) = (c(0), c(1), c(2), c(3), c(4), c(5), c(6), c(7));
    let w = u32::wrapping_add;
    if final_ {
        [rec[7], settlers, buildings, food, mines, gold, manna, soldiers, battles]
    } else {
        let score = [settlers, settlers, buildings, food, mines, gold, manna, soldiers, soldiers, battles.wrapping_mul(5)]
            .into_iter()
            .fold(0, w);
        [score, settlers, buildings, food, mines, gold >> 1, manna, soldiers, battles]
    }
}

fn read_record(m: &mut Machine, id: usize) -> [u32; 17] {
    let base = STATS_BASE + id as u32 * STATS_STRIDE;
    std::array::from_fn(|i| m.mem.read_u32(base + 4 * i as u32))
}

/// Sample history of one game.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
pub struct History {
    pub samples: Vec<Sample>,
    /// Current sampling interval (doubles when the history is thinned out).
    pub every: u32,
}

impl History {
    /// Add a sample if `every` ticks passed since the last one (or it is the first / the final one).
    pub fn push(&mut self, s: Sample, force: bool) {
        if self.every == 0 {
            self.every = SAMPLE_TICKS;
        }
        if let Some(last) = self.samples.last_mut() {
            if s.tick < last.tick {
                return;
            }
            if s.tick == last.tick {
                *last = s;
                return;
            }
            if !force && s.tick < last.tick + self.every {
                return;
            }
        }
        self.samples.push(s);
        if self.samples.len() > MAX_SAMPLES {
            // Keep the first and every second one after it.
            let mut i = 0;
            self.samples.retain(|_| {
                i += 1;
                i % 2 == 1
            });
            self.every *= 2;
        }
    }
}

/// Players shown on the statistics screen: (player id, rank 1..), by rank (the game's row order).
pub fn ranked(rec_rank: &[u32; PLAYERS]) -> Vec<(usize, u32)> {
    let mut v: Vec<(usize, u32)> = rec_rank.iter().enumerate().filter(|(_, &r)| (1..=PLAYERS as u32).contains(&r)).map(|(i, &r)| (i, r)).collect();
    v.sort_by_key(|&(_, r)| r);
    v.dedup_by_key(|p| p.1);
    v
}

/// "Nice" axis maximum >= v (1, 2, 5 x 10^k).
pub fn nice_max(v: u32) -> u32 {
    let v = v.max(1) as u64;
    let mut p = 1u64;
    loop {
        for k in [1, 2, 5] {
            if k * p >= v {
                return (k * p).min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32;
            }
        }
        p *= 10;
    }
}

const SHEET: Rgba = Rgba::rgba(16, 20, 28, 244);
const PLOT_BG: Rgba = Rgba::rgba(30, 36, 48, 255);
const GRID: Rgba = Rgba::rgba(90, 100, 120, 120);
const TEXT: Rgba = Rgba::rgb(240, 236, 226);
const TEXT_DIM: Rgba = Rgba::rgb(168, 174, 188);
const BTN: Rgba = Rgba::rgba(52, 61, 80, 255);
const BTN_ON: Rgba = Rgba::rgba(196, 138, 36, 255);
const OPEN_BG: Rgba = Rgba::rgba(20, 16, 10, 215);
const GOLD: Rgba = Rgba::rgb(236, 196, 92);

/// Line colours by rank (distinct, readable on the dark plot).
const COLOURS: [Rgba; PLAYERS] = [
    Rgba::rgb(236, 72, 60),
    Rgba::rgb(76, 140, 255),
    Rgba::rgb(80, 200, 90),
    Rgba::rgb(245, 208, 50),
    Rgba::rgb(190, 110, 240),
    Rgba::rgb(250, 150, 50),
    Rgba::rgb(70, 214, 220),
    Rgba::rgb(240, 240, 240),
    Rgba::rgb(250, 120, 190),
    Rgba::rgb(170, 125, 80),
    Rgba::rgb(160, 230, 70),
    Rgba::rgb(120, 120, 255),
    Rgba::rgb(255, 90, 120),
    Rgba::rgb(40, 170, 140),
    Rgba::rgb(210, 180, 140),
    Rgba::rgb(150, 150, 150),
    Rgba::rgb(255, 180, 120),
    Rgba::rgb(130, 200, 255),
    Rgba::rgb(200, 90, 160),
    Rgba::rgb(110, 160, 60),
];

type Rect = (i32, i32, i32, i32);

fn hit(r: Rect, x: f32, y: f32) -> bool {
    x >= r.0 as f32 && y >= r.1 as f32 && x < (r.0 + r.2) as f32 && y < (r.1 + r.3) as f32
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
enum Target {
    Open,
    Close,
    Tab(usize),
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct EndStatsMod {
    hist: History,
    /// Final sample taken for the current game (statistics screen seen).
    final_taken: bool,
    /// Ranks of the final sample (by player id).
    ranks: [u32; PLAYERS],
    in_game: bool,
    /// Real ms when the game was last seen running.
    last_game_ms: u64,
    /// The statistics screen is shown (menu layout `statistics*`).
    on_screen: bool,
    open: bool,
    tab: usize,
    /// Hit targets of the last drawn layer (window px).
    targets: Vec<(Rect, Target)>,
    /// Pointer captured by us, and the target it went down on.
    pressed: Option<(u32, Option<Target>)>,
    dirty: bool,
}

impl EndStatsMod {
    fn sample(m: &mut Machine, final_: bool) -> (Sample, [u32; PLAYERS]) {
        let tick = m.mem.read_u32(GAME_CLOCK_TICKS);
        let mut v = [[0u32; 9]; PLAYERS];
        let mut ranks = [0u32; PLAYERS];
        for (id, row) in v.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            let r = read_record(m, id);
            *row = values(&r, final_);
            ranks[id] = r[0];
        }
        (Sample { tick, v }, ranks)
    }

    fn shown_players(&self) -> Vec<(usize, u32)> {
        ranked(&self.ranks)
    }

    fn usable(&self) -> bool {
        self.final_taken && self.hist.samples.len() >= 2 && !self.shown_players().is_empty()
    }

    fn target_at(&self, x: f32, y: f32) -> Option<Target> {
        self.targets.iter().rev().find(|(r, _)| hit(*r, x, y)).map(|&(_, t)| t)
    }

    fn act(&mut self, t: Target) {
        match t {
            Target::Open => self.open = true,
            Target::Close => self.open = false,
            Target::Tab(i) => self.tab = i,
        }
        self.dirty = true;
    }

    fn draw_open_button(&mut self, c: &mut Layer, sk: f32) {
        let label = "Statistics over time";
        let px = 17.0 * sk;
        let (tw, th) = measure_text(px, Weight::Bold, label);
        let pad = (12.0 * sk) as i32;
        let (w, h) = (tw + 2 * pad, th + pad * 3 / 2);
        let mrg = (14.0 * sk) as i32;
        let (x, y) = (c.width() as i32 - w - mrg, c.height() as i32 - h - mrg);
        c.fill_rounded_rect(x, y, w, h, 8.0 * sk, OPEN_BG);
        c.stroke_rounded_rect(x, y, w, h, 8.0 * sk, 2.0 * sk, GOLD);
        c.text_centered(x, y, w, h, px, Weight::Bold, GOLD, label);
        self.targets.push(((x, y, w, h), Target::Open));
        let hint = "Tap anywhere else to continue";
        let hpx = 13.0 * sk;
        let (hw, hh) = measure_text(hpx, Weight::Regular, hint);
        c.fill_rounded_rect(mrg, y + h - hh - pad, hw + pad, hh + pad / 2, 6.0 * sk, Rgba::rgba(0, 0, 0, 120));
        c.text(mrg + pad / 2, y + h - hh - pad * 3 / 4, hpx, Weight::Regular, TEXT_DIM, hint);
    }

    fn draw_sheet(&mut self, c: &mut Layer, sk: f32) {
        let (ww, wh) = (c.width() as i32, c.height() as i32);
        c.fill_rect(0, 0, ww, wh, SHEET);
        let mrg = (12.0 * sk) as i32;
        // Header: title + Close.
        let hh = (40.0 * sk) as i32;
        c.text(mrg, mrg + (6.0 * sk) as i32, 20.0 * sk, Weight::Bold, GOLD, "Statistics over game time");
        let cw = (110.0 * sk) as i32;
        let close = (ww - cw - mrg, mrg, cw, hh);
        c.fill_rounded_rect(close.0, close.1, close.2, close.3, 8.0 * sk, BTN);
        c.text_centered(close.0, close.1, close.2, close.3, 17.0 * sk, Weight::Bold, TEXT, "Close");
        self.targets.push((close, Target::Close));
        // Tabs: the game's columns.
        let ty = mrg * 2 + hh;
        let th = (38.0 * sk) as i32;
        let gap = (6.0 * sk) as i32;
        let n = COLUMNS.len() as i32;
        let tw = (ww - 2 * mrg - gap * (n - 1)) / n;
        for (i, name) in COLUMNS.iter().enumerate() {
            let r = (mrg + i as i32 * (tw + gap), ty, tw, th);
            c.fill_rounded_rect(r.0, r.1, r.2, r.3, 7.0 * sk, if i == self.tab { BTN_ON } else { BTN });
            c.text_centered(r.0, r.1, r.2, r.3, 16.0 * sk, Weight::Bold, TEXT, name);
            self.targets.push((r, Target::Tab(i)));
        }
        // Body: plot left, legend right (below the plot on a narrow window).
        let by = ty + th + mrg;
        let (bw, bh) = (ww - 2 * mrg, wh - by - mrg);
        let players = self.shown_players();
        let row_h = (26.0 * sk) as i32;
        let legend_w = ((330.0 * sk) as i32).min(bw * 2 / 5);
        let side = bw > bh;
        let (plot, legend) = if side {
            ((mrg, by, bw - legend_w - mrg, bh), (mrg + bw - legend_w, by, legend_w, bh))
        } else {
            let lh = (row_h * players.len() as i32 + mrg).min(bh / 2);
            ((mrg, by, bw, bh - lh - mrg), (mrg, by + bh - lh, bw, lh))
        };
        self.draw_plot(c, sk, plot, &players);
        self.draw_legend(c, sk, legend, &players, row_h);
    }

    fn draw_plot(&self, c: &mut Layer, sk: f32, r: Rect, players: &[(usize, u32)]) {
        let s = &self.hist.samples;
        let (Some(first), Some(last)) = (s.first(), s.last()) else { return };
        let col = self.tab;
        let max = players.iter().flat_map(|&(id, _)| s.iter().map(move |x| x.v[id][col])).max().unwrap_or(0);
        let top = nice_max(max);
        let lpx = 14.0 * sk;
        let (lw, lh) = measure_text(lpx, Weight::Regular, &top.to_string());
        let left = r.0 + lw + (10.0 * sk) as i32;
        let bottom = r.1 + r.3 - lh - (10.0 * sk) as i32;
        let (px0, py0, pw, ph) = (left, r.1 + lh / 2, r.0 + r.2 - left, bottom - r.1 - lh / 2);
        if pw < 20 || ph < 20 {
            return;
        }
        c.fill_rect(px0, py0, pw, ph, PLOT_BG);
        // Grid + y labels (whole numbers: 0 .. top in `div` steps), "Count".
        let div = [4u32, 5, 2, 1].into_iter().find(|d| top % d == 0).unwrap_or(1);
        for k in 0..=div {
            let y = py0 + ph - (ph as i64 * k as i64 / div as i64) as i32;
            c.line(px0 as f32, y as f32, (px0 + pw) as f32, y as f32, 1.0, GRID);
            let label = (top as u64 * k as u64 / div as u64).to_string();
            let (w, h) = measure_text(lpx, Weight::Regular, &label);
            c.text(left - w - (6.0 * sk) as i32, y - h / 2, lpx, Weight::Regular, TEXT_DIM, &label);
        }
        c.text(px0 + (6.0 * sk) as i32, py0 + (4.0 * sk) as i32, lpx, Weight::Regular, TEXT_DIM, "Count");
        // x labels: game time.
        let (t0, t1) = (first.tick, last.tick.max(first.tick + 1));
        for k in 0..=4u32 {
            let t = t0 as u64 + (t1 - t0) as u64 * k as u64 / 4;
            let label = crate::game_time::format(t * 64);
            let (w, _) = measure_text(lpx, Weight::Regular, &label);
            let x = px0 + (pw as i64 * k as i64 / 4) as i32;
            let x = (x - w / 2).clamp(px0, px0 + pw - w);
            c.text(x, bottom + (6.0 * sk) as i32, lpx, Weight::Regular, TEXT_DIM, &label);
            c.line(x as f32 + w as f32 / 2.0, py0 as f32, x as f32 + w as f32 / 2.0, (py0 + ph) as f32, 1.0, GRID.fade(0.5));
        }
        let gt = "Game time";
        let (gw, _) = measure_text(lpx, Weight::Regular, gt);
        c.text(px0 + pw - gw - (6.0 * sk) as i32, py0 + ph - lh - (6.0 * sk) as i32, lpx, Weight::Regular, TEXT_DIM, gt);
        // Lines (at most ~1 point per 4 px), lowest rank drawn last = on top.
        let step = (s.len() / (pw as usize / 4).max(2)).max(1);
        let pts = |id: usize| {
            let mut v: Vec<(f32, f32)> = s
                .iter()
                .enumerate()
                .filter(|(i, _)| i % step == 0 || *i == s.len() - 1)
                .map(|(_, x)| {
                    let fx = px0 as f32 + pw as f32 * (x.tick - t0) as f32 / (t1 - t0) as f32;
                    let fy = (py0 + ph) as f32 - ph as f32 * x.v[id][col] as f32 / top as f32;
                    (fx, fy)
                })
                .collect();
            v.dedup();
            v
        };
        for &(id, rank) in players.iter().rev() {
            let colr = COLOURS[(rank as usize - 1) % PLAYERS];
            let p = pts(id);
            for w in p.windows(2) {
                c.line(w[0].0, w[0].1, w[1].0, w[1].1, 2.5 * sk, colr);
            }
            if let Some(&(x, y)) = p.last() {
                c.fill_circle(x, y, 4.0 * sk, colr);
            }
        }
    }

    fn draw_legend(&self, c: &mut Layer, sk: f32, r: Rect, players: &[(usize, u32)], row_h: i32) {
        let Some(last) = self.hist.samples.last() else { return };
        let col = self.tab;
        let pad = (8.0 * sk) as i32;
        c.fill_rounded_rect(r.0, r.1, r.2, r.3, 8.0 * sk, PLOT_BG);
        let cols = if r.2 > r.3 * 2 { 2 } else { 1 };
        let cw = (r.2 - pad) / cols;
        let per_col = ((r.3 - pad) / row_h.max(1)).max(1);
        for (n, &(id, rank)) in players.iter().enumerate() {
            let (ci, ri) = (n as i32 / per_col, n as i32 % per_col);
            if ci >= cols {
                break;
            }
            let (x, y) = (r.0 + pad + ci * cw, r.1 + pad / 2 + ri * row_h);
            let sw = (14.0 * sk) as i32;
            c.fill_rect(x, y + (row_h - sw) / 2, sw, sw, COLOURS[(rank as usize - 1) % PLAYERS]);
            // The game's own row: rank, team, name (frame px 14..186 of row `rank`).
            let value = last.v[id][col].to_string();
            let vpx = 16.0 * sk;
            let (vw, vh) = measure_text(vpx, Weight::Bold, &value);
            let name_h = row_h - (2.0 * sk) as i32;
            let name_w = (name_h * 172 / 20).min(cw - sw - vw - 3 * pad);
            let src_w = (name_w as f32 * 20.0 / name_h.max(1) as f32).min(172.0);
            let gy = 102.0 + 20.0 * (rank as f32 - 1.0);
            c.frame_inset([14.0, gy, src_w, 20.0], x + sw + pad / 2, y + 1, name_w, name_h);
            c.text(x + cw - vw - pad, y + (row_h - vh) / 2, vpx, Weight::Bold, TEXT, &value);
        }
    }
}

impl Mod for EndStatsMod {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        "end-stats"
    }

    fn tick(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, _now: u64) {
        let now = m.real_ms();
        if crate::res::in_game_frame(m) {
            if !self.in_game && now.saturating_sub(self.last_game_ms) > NEW_GAME_GAP_MS {
                // A new game or a loaded save.
                self.hist = History::default();
                self.final_taken = false;
                self.ranks = [0; PLAYERS];
            }
            self.in_game = true;
            self.last_game_ms = now;
            let (s, _) = Self::sample(m, false);
            if s.tick < self.hist.samples.last().map_or(0, |l| l.tick) {
                self.hist = History::default(); // clock went back: another game
            }
            self.hist.push(s, false);
        } else {
            self.in_game = false;
        }
        let on = crate::display::frame_viewport(m).layout.is_some_and(|l| l.name.starts_with("statistics"));
        if on && !self.final_taken && !self.hist.samples.is_empty() {
            let (s, ranks) = Self::sample(m, true);
            let tick = s.tick.max(self.hist.samples.last().map_or(0, |l| l.tick));
            self.hist.push(Sample { tick, ..s }, true);
            self.ranks = ranks;
            self.final_taken = true;
            self.dirty = true;
        }
        if on != self.on_screen {
            self.on_screen = on;
            if !on {
                self.open = false;
                self.pressed = None;
            }
            self.dirty = true;
        }
    }

    fn wants_draw(&self) -> bool {
        self.on_screen && self.usable()
    }

    fn needs_redraw(&self) -> bool {
        self.dirty
    }

    fn draw_window(&mut self, _m: &mut Machine, c: &mut Layer, _frame: &FrameBuffer) {
        self.dirty = false;
        self.targets.clear();
        // Window height / 600, but not wider than the window allows (tall inner screens).
        let sk = c.ui().min(c.width() as f32 / 900.0).clamp(0.5, 4.0);
        if self.open {
            self.draw_sheet(c, sk);
        } else {
            self.draw_open_button(c, sk);
        }
    }

    fn on_touch(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, ev: &TouchEvent) -> ModEvent {
        if !self.on_screen || !self.usable() {
            return ModEvent::Pass;
        }
        match *ev {
            TouchEvent::Down { id, .. } => {
                let (wx, wy) = crate::touch_window_pos(m, ev);
                let t = self.target_at(wx, wy);
                if t.is_some() || self.open {
                    self.pressed = Some((id, t));
                    return ModEvent::Consumed;
                }
                ModEvent::Pass
            }
            TouchEvent::Move { id, .. } | TouchEvent::Cancel { id } if self.pressed.is_some_and(|p| p.0 == id) => {
                if matches!(ev, TouchEvent::Cancel { .. }) {
                    self.pressed = None;
                }
                ModEvent::Consumed
            }
            TouchEvent::Up { id, .. } if self.pressed.is_some_and(|p| p.0 == id) => {
                let (wx, wy) = crate::touch_window_pos(m, ev);
                if let Some((_, Some(t))) = self.pressed.take() {
                    if self.target_at(wx, wy) == Some(t) {
                        self.act(t);
                    }
                }
                ModEvent::Consumed
            }
            // While the sheet is open, nothing reaches the game (its click would leave the screen).
            _ if self.open => ModEvent::Consumed,
            _ => ModEvent::Pass,
        }
    }

    fn on_key(&mut self, _m: &mut Machine, vk: u32, down: bool) -> ModEvent {
        if self.open && vk == 0x1b {
            if !down {
                self.open = false;
                self.dirty = true;
            }
            return ModEvent::Consumed;
        }
        ModEvent::Pass
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn score_formula_matches_the_game() {
        // rank, ..., score at [7], counters at [8..16].
        let mut r = [0u32; 17];
        r[8..16].copy_from_slice(&[10, 4, 3, 2, 8, 1, 6, 1]);
        let v = values(&r, false);
        assert_eq!(v[0], 2 * 10 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 8 + 1 + 2 * 6 + 5);
        assert_eq!(v[5], 4, "gold is shown halved");
        // Final: the game's own stored score and (already halved) gold.
        r[7] = 77;
        r[12] = 4;
        let f = values(&r, true);
        assert_eq!((f[0], f[5]), (77, 4));
    }

    #[test]
    fn history_samples_and_thins_out() {
        let mut h = History::default();
        let s = |tick| Sample { tick, v: [[tick; 9]; PLAYERS] };
        h.push(s(0), false);
        h.push(s(10), false); // too early
        h.push(s(SAMPLE_TICKS), false);
        assert_eq!(h.samples.len(), 2);
        h.push(s(SAMPLE_TICKS + 3), true); // final
        assert_eq!(h.samples.len(), 3);
        for i in 3..2000 {
            h.push(s(i * SAMPLE_TICKS * 2), false);
        }
        assert!(h.samples.len() <= MAX_SAMPLES);
        assert_eq!(h.samples[0].tick, 0);
        assert!(h.every > SAMPLE_TICKS);
    }

    #[test]
    fn ranks_and_axis() {
        let mut r = [0u32; PLAYERS];
        r[0] = 2;
        r[1] = 1;
        assert_eq!(ranked(&r), vec![(1, 1), (0, 2)]);
        assert_eq!(nice_max(0), 1);
        assert_eq!(nice_max(7), 10);
        assert_eq!(nice_max(130), 200);
        assert_eq!(nice_max(500), 500);
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/fallback.rs`:

```rs
//! Fallback touch->mouse mapping for touch events no mod consumed. Mirrors the legacy Android mapping
//! (`s3-frontend/src/touch.rs`) so behaviour stays the same until W3's context-aware input replaces it:
//! - Tap: left click (right click when "right-click next" is armed);
//! - LongPress: right click (if `long_press_right_click`), TwoFingerTap: right click;
//! - ThreeFingerTap: keyboard request flag for the frontend;
//! - one-finger Pan: drag with the left button, or in game on the map with the right button (S3 scrolls
//!   the map with a right drag; mirrored and halved so the map follows the finger);
//! - long-press drags, two-finger pans and pinches: nothing (yet).
//!
//! Button-up events are delayed by [`CLICK_MS`] so games polling the button state see the press.

use s3_runtime::{HostEvent, MouseButton};

use crate::gesture::{Phase, TouchEvent};

pub const CLICK_MS: u64 = 60;
/// Width of the in-game left panel (640x480 game pixels), as in s3-android.
pub const PANEL_W: i32 = 170;

/// Drag button for a one-finger drag starting at `p` (menus are 800x600, see s3-android `drag_button_for`).
pub fn drag_button_for(frame: (u32, u32), p: (i32, i32)) -> MouseButton {
    let in_menu = frame == (800, 600);
    if !in_menu && p.0 >= PANEL_W {
        MouseButton::Right
    } else {
        MouseButton::Left
    }
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct TouchMouse {
    queue: Vec<(u64, HostEvent)>,
    last_due: u64,
    drag: Option<(MouseButton, (i32, i32))>,
    pub right_next: bool,
    /// Key (VK) held around the armed right click: a modifier order (Shift waypoint / Alt patrol / Ctrl no fight,
    /// `crate::unit_orders`). 0 = a plain right click.
    pub right_next_vk: u32,
    pub keyboard_request: bool,
    pub long_press_right_click: bool,
    /// Game speed (`Machine::time_scale`, set by the scheduler service): button-ups are scheduled on the wall
    /// clock, but the game measures click length on its (faster) guest clock and ignores long right clicks, so
    /// at 2x..8x the orders (quick right clicks) were dropped (user report 2026-11-08). 0 = 1x.
    pub time_scale: f64,
}

impl TouchMouse {
    pub(crate) fn push(&mut self, t: u64, e: HostEvent) {
        let t = t.max(self.last_due);
        self.last_due = t;
        self.queue.push((t, e));
    }

    /// Button / key hold time on the wall clock: [`CLICK_MS`] of game time at the current game speed (at least
    /// 12 ms so the game still sees the press).
    pub fn click_ms(&self) -> u64 {
        if self.time_scale > 1.0 {
            ((CLICK_MS as f64 / self.time_scale).round() as u64).max(12)
        } else {
            CLICK_MS
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn click(&mut self, t: u64, p: (i32, i32), button: MouseButton) {
        let c = self.click_ms();
        self.push(t, HostEvent::MouseMove { x: p.0, y: p.1 });
        self.push(t, HostEvent::MouseButton { button, down: true });
        self.push(t + c, HostEvent::MouseButton { button, down: false });
    }

    /// Map one unconsumed touch event. `frame` = current game frame size.
    pub fn handle(&mut self, ev: &TouchEvent, now: u64, frame: (u32, u32)) {
        let pt = |x: f32, y: f32| (x.round() as i32, y.round() as i32);
        match *ev {
            TouchEvent::Tap { x, y } => {
                let vk = std::mem::take(&mut self.right_next_vk);
                if std::mem::take(&mut self.right_next) {
                    if vk != 0 {
                        // Modifier down before the click, up after its button-up (the game reads the modifier
                        // byte of the button events, `0x45b370`).
                        self.push(now, HostEvent::Key { vk, down: true });
                        self.click(now + 10, pt(x, y), MouseButton::Right);
                        let c = self.click_ms();
                        self.push(now + 10 + c + 10, HostEvent::Key { vk, down: false });
                    } else {
                        self.click(now, pt(x, y), MouseButton::Right);
                    }
                } else {
                    self.click(now, pt(x, y), MouseButton::Left);
                }
            }
            TouchEvent::LongPress { x, y } if self.long_press_right_click => self.click(now, pt(x, y), MouseButton::Right),
            TouchEvent::TwoFingerTap { x, y } => self.click(now, pt(x, y), MouseButton::Right),
            TouchEvent::ThreeFingerTap { .. } => self.keyboard_request = true,
            TouchEvent::Pan { phase, fingers: 1, x, y, start_x, start_y, after_long_press: false, .. } => match phase {
                Phase::Begin => {
                    let o = pt(start_x, start_y);
                    let b = drag_button_for(frame, o);
                    self.drag = Some((b, o));
                    self.push(now, HostEvent::MouseMove { x: o.0, y: o.1 });
                    self.push(now, HostEvent::MouseButton { button: b, down: true });
                    let p = drag_pos(b, o, pt(x, y), frame);
                    self.push(now, HostEvent::MouseMove { x: p.0, y: p.1 });
                }
                Phase::Update => {
                    if let Some((b, o)) = self.drag {
                        let p = drag_pos(b, o, pt(x, y), frame);
                        self.push(now, HostEvent::MouseMove { x: p.0, y: p.1 });
                    }
                }
                Phase::End => {
                    if let Some((b, _)) = self.drag.take() {
                        self.push(now, HostEvent::MouseButton { button: b, down: false });
                    }
                }
            },
            TouchEvent::Cancel { .. } => {
                if let Some((b, _)) = self.drag.take() {
                    self.push(now, HostEvent::MouseButton { button: b, down: false });
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    /// Events due at `now`, in order.
    pub fn drain_due(&mut self, now: u64) -> Vec<HostEvent> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        self.queue.retain(|&(t, e)| {
            if t <= now {
                out.push(e);
                false
            } else {
                true
            }
        });
        out
    }

    pub fn pending(&self) -> bool {
        !self.queue.is_empty()
    }
}

/// Mouse position while dragging (right drag mirrored around the origin and halved = grab scrolling).
fn drag_pos(b: MouseButton, o: (i32, i32), cur: (i32, i32), frame: (u32, u32)) -> (i32, i32) {
    let p = match b {
        MouseButton::Right => (o.0 - (cur.0 - o.0) / 2, o.1 - (cur.1 - o.1) / 2),
        _ => cur,
    };
    let (w, h) = (frame.0.max(1) as i32, frame.1.max(1) as i32);
    (p.0.clamp(0, w - 1), p.1.clamp(0, h - 1))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn tap_click_and_right_next() {
        let mut t = TouchMouse::default();
        t.handle(&TouchEvent::Tap { x: 10.4, y: 20.6 }, 100, (640, 480));
        let ev = t.drain_due(100);
        assert_eq!(ev, vec![
            HostEvent::MouseMove { x: 10, y: 21 },
            HostEvent::MouseButton { button: MouseButton::Left, down: true }
        ]);
        assert_eq!(t.drain_due(160), vec![HostEvent::MouseButton { button: MouseButton::Left, down: false }]);
        t.right_next = true;
        t.handle(&TouchEvent::Tap { x: 1.0, y: 1.0 }, 200, (640, 480));
        assert!(t.drain_due(300).contains(&HostEvent::MouseButton { button: MouseButton::Right, down: true }));
        assert!(!t.right_next);
        // Modifier order: Shift down, right click, Shift up.
        t.right_next = true;
        t.right_next_vk = 0x10;
        t.handle(&TouchEvent::Tap { x: 5.0, y: 6.0 }, 400, (640, 480));
        let ev = t.drain_due(1000);
        assert_eq!(ev.first(), Some(&HostEvent::Key { vk: 0x10, down: true }));
        assert_eq!(ev.last(), Some(&HostEvent::Key { vk: 0x10, down: false }));
        assert!(ev.contains(&HostEvent::MouseButton { button: MouseButton::Right, down: true }));
        assert!(!t.right_next && t.right_next_vk == 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn map_drag_uses_right_button_mirrored() {
        let mut t = TouchMouse::default();
        let pan = |phase, x| TouchEvent::Pan { phase, fingers: 1, x, y: 200.0, dx: 0.0, dy: 0.0, start_x: 300.0, start_y: 200.0, after_long_press: false };
        t.handle(&pan(Phase::Begin, 320.0), 0, (640, 480));
        t.handle(&pan(Phase::Update, 340.0), 10, (640, 480));
        t.handle(&pan(Phase::End, 340.0), 20, (640, 480));
        let ev = t.drain_due(100);
        assert_eq!(ev[1], HostEvent::MouseButton { button: MouseButton::Right, down: true });
        assert_eq!(ev[2], HostEvent::MouseMove { x: 290, y: 200 });
        assert_eq!(ev[3], HostEvent::MouseMove { x: 280, y: 200 });
        assert_eq!(ev[4], HostEvent::MouseButton { button: MouseButton::Right, down: false });
        // Menus (800x600): left drag, not mirrored.
        t.handle(&pan(Phase::Begin, 320.0), 200, (800, 600));
        let ev = t.drain_due(300);
        assert_eq!(ev[1], HostEvent::MouseButton { button: MouseButton::Left, down: true });
        assert_eq!(ev[2], HostEvent::MouseMove { x: 320, y: 200 });
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/fast.rs`:

```rs
//! Native fast paths for hot guest loops (perf-cpu, docs/porting/performance.md).
//!
//! Each fast path replaces a fixed region of the GOG S3.EXE code with Rust that leaves *exactly* the same guest
//! state (registers, EFLAGS, memory, EIP, retired-instruction count) as the original code, so it is safe for
//! lockstep multiplayer and invisible to the `s3det` state hashes. The CPU runs it at the start of the region
//! (`s3_cpu::NativeBlock`, matched by a hash of the code bytes) instead of exiting to the host like a hook, so it
//! costs nothing per call. Disable with `S3_FAST=0`.

use s3_cpu::{NativeBlock, NativeBlocks};
use s3_runtime::{LogLevel, Machine};

use crate::{fast_blit, fast_land, fast_land_rows, fast_obj, fast_shadow, fast_snap, fast_sprite, fast_tile};

/// All fast paths for the GOG exe: (start, end, block).
pub fn gog_blocks() -> Vec<(u32, u32, NativeBlock)> {
    fn nb(name: &'static str, start: u32, end: u32, hash: u64, f: s3_cpu::NativeFn) -> (u32, u32, NativeBlock) {
        (start, end, NativeBlock { name, len: end - start, hash, f })
    }
    vec![
        nb("sprite_rows", fast_sprite::START, fast_sprite::EXIT, fast_sprite::HASH, fast_sprite::sprite_rows),
        nb("palette_row", fast_blit::PAL_START, fast_blit::PAL_EXIT, fast_blit::PAL_HASH, fast_blit::palette_row),
        nb("darken", fast_blit::DARK_START, fast_blit::DARK_EXIT, fast_blit::DARK_HASH, fast_blit::darken),
        nb("dither", fast_blit::DITHER_START, fast_blit::DITHER_EXIT, fast_blit::DITHER_HASH, fast_blit::dither),
        nb("obj_empty", fast_obj::START, fast_obj::END, fast_obj::HASH, fast_obj::obj_empty),
        nb("land_clean", fast_land::START, fast_land::END, fast_land::HASH, fast_land::land_clean),
        nb("land_rows", fast_land_rows::START, fast_land_rows::EXIT, fast_land_rows::HASH, fast_land_rows::land_rows),
        // shadow sprites (fast_shadow.rs): one function per loop, several entries (each hash covers entry..exit)
        nb("shadow_zero", fast_shadow::ZERO_ROW, fast_shadow::ZERO_EXIT, fast_shadow::ZERO_ROW_HASH, fast_shadow::shadow_zero),
        nb("shadow_zero_run", fast_shadow::ZERO_RUN, fast_shadow::ZERO_EXIT, fast_shadow::ZERO_RUN_HASH, fast_shadow::shadow_zero),
        nb("shadow_rows", fast_shadow::ROWS_FIRST, fast_shadow::ROWS_EXIT, fast_shadow::ROWS_FIRST_HASH, fast_shadow::shadow_rows),
        nb("shadow_rows_row", fast_shadow::ROWS_ROW, fast_shadow::ROWS_EXIT, fast_shadow::ROWS_ROW_HASH, fast_shadow::shadow_rows),
        nb("shadow_rows_run", fast_shadow::ROWS_RUN, fast_shadow::ROWS_EXIT, fast_shadow::ROWS_RUN_HASH, fast_shadow::shadow_rows),
        nb("snap_tiles", fast_snap::START, fast_snap::EXIT, fast_snap::HASH, fast_snap::snap_tiles),
        nb("frame_tiles", fast_tile::START, fast_tile::END, fast_tile::HASH, fast_tile::frame_tiles),
        nb("land_mark", fast_tile::MARK_START, fast_tile::MARK_EXIT, fast_tile::MARK_HASH, fast_tile::land_mark),
    ]
}

/// Code outside its registered region that a fast path also stands for (inlined calls, a loop head before the
/// region): a hook anywhere in these ranges (start included) disables it.
fn extra_ranges(name: &str) -> Vec<(u32, u32)> {
    match name {
        "frame_tiles" => vec![fast_tile::HEAD, (fast_obj::START, fast_obj::END), (0x005f_c540, 0x005f_c54b)],
        _ => Vec::new(),
    }
}

/// Install the fast paths for the GOG exe (after the hooks are committed: a region containing a hook address
/// is skipped, the hook must run).
pub fn install(m: &mut Machine, exe_sha256: &str) {
    if std::env::var("S3_FAST").map(|v| v == "0").unwrap_or(false) {
        m.log(LogLevel::Info, "mods: native fast paths disabled (S3_FAST=0)");
        return;
    }
    if exe_sha256 != crate::patchset::GOG_SHA256 {
        return;
    }
    let hooks: Vec<u32> = m.hook_addrs().map(|h| h.iter().copied().collect()).unwrap_or_default();
    let mut map = NativeBlocks::new();
    let mut names = Vec::new();
    // `S3_FAST_OFF=name,name`: leave single fast paths out (bisecting a divergence, measuring one path).
    let off = std::env::var("S3_FAST_OFF").unwrap_or_default();
    for (start, end, b) in gog_blocks() {
        if off.split(',').any(|n| n.trim() == b.name) {
            m.log(LogLevel::Info, &format!("mods: fast path {} disabled (S3_FAST_OFF)", b.name));
            continue;
        }
        let extra = extra_ranges(b.name);
        if let Some(h) = hooks.iter().find(|&&h| (h > start && h < end) || extra.iter().any(|&(a, e)| h >= a && h < e)) {
            m.log(LogLevel::Warn, &format!("mods: fast path {} skipped: hook at {h:#x} inside it", b.name));
            continue;
        }
        names.push(b.name);
        map.insert(start, b);
    }
    m.log(LogLevel::Info, &format!("mods: native fast paths: {}", names.join(", ")));
    m.set_native_blocks(Some(map));
}
```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/fast_blit.rs`:

```rs
//! Native fast paths: three small pixel loops of the GOG S3.EXE renderer (see `fast.rs` for the contract).
//!
//! Each runs whole loop iterations from its loop head, stops at the loop head when the instruction budget is
//! used up (the state there is exactly the interpreter's) or at the loop exit, and declines when the loop would
//! not terminate normally (odd distance, wrap), could fault (NULL guard) or when its writes overlap what it
//! reads.
//!
//! | Region | Loop | Guest instructions per iteration |
//! | --- | --- | --- |
//! | `0x5fc93d..0x5fc952` (in `0x5fc860`) | 8-bit indexed -> 16-bit pixels through a 256-entry palette at EBP | 8 |
//! | `0x5fd0ea..0x5fd0ff` (in `0x5fd0c0`) | darken dwords in place: `[eax] = ([eax] >> 1) & [0x7e8dec]` | 8 |
//! | `0x5fd096..0x5fd0ae` (in `0x5fd080`) | checkerboard shadow: zero every pixel where `(phase + ebp)` is odd, phase = `(phase+1) & 31` | 8, +1 when it writes |

use s3_cpu::{layout, Cpu, GuestMemory, EAX, EBX, ECX, EDI, ESI};

/// Largest iteration count handled natively (a longer loop is surely a wrapped/garbage range: decline).
const MAX_ITERS: u32 = 1 << 22;

/// `[a, a+len)` lies inside the guest window above the NULL guard without wrapping.
#[inline]
fn range_ok(a: u32, len: u64) -> bool {
    a >= layout::NULL_GUARD_END && a as u64 + len <= u32::MAX as u64
}

#[inline]
fn disjoint(a: u32, alen: u64, b: u32, blen: u64) -> bool {
    let (a, b) = (a as u64, b as u64);
    a + alen <= b || b + blen <= a
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ palette loop 0x5fc93d

pub const PAL_START: u32 = 0x005f_c93d;
pub const PAL_EXIT: u32 = 0x005f_c952;
pub const PAL_HASH: u64 = 0x4c41_6f63_4446_80ce;

/// `xor ebx,ebx; add eax,2; mov bl,[ecx]; inc ecx; cmp eax,esi; mov di,[ebp+ebx*2]; mov [eax-2],di; jne`.
pub fn palette_row(cpu: &mut Cpu, mem: &mut GuestMemory, budget: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    const PER: u64 = 8;
    let [mut eax, mut ecx, _, mut ebx, _, ebp, esi, mut edi] = cpu.regs;
    let dist = esi.wrapping_sub(eax);
    if dist == 0 || dist & 1 != 0 || dist / 2 > MAX_ITERS {
        return None;
    }
    let n = (dist / 2).min((budget / PER).min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32);
    if n == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let (dlen, slen) = (2 * n as u64, n as u64);
    if !range_ok(eax, dlen) || !range_ok(ecx, slen) || !range_ok(ebp, 512) {
        return None;
    }
    if !disjoint(eax, dlen, ecx, slen) || !disjoint(eax, dlen, ebp, 512) {
        return None;
    }
    for _ in 0..n {
        ebx = mem.read_u8(ecx) as u32;
        eax = eax.wrapping_add(2);
        ecx = ecx.wrapping_add(1);
        let px = mem.read_u16(ebp.wrapping_add(ebx * 2));
        edi = (edi & 0xFFFF_0000) | px as u32;
        mem.write_u16(eax.wrapping_sub(2), px);
    }
    cpu.regs[EAX] = eax;
    cpu.regs[ECX] = ecx;
    cpu.regs[EBX] = ebx;
    cpu.regs[EDI] = edi;
    cpu.alu_sub(eax, esi, 0, 4);
    cpu.eip = if eax == esi { PAL_EXIT } else { PAL_START };
    Some(n as u64 * PER)
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ darken loop 0x5fd0ea

pub const DARK_START: u32 = 0x005f_d0ea;
pub const DARK_EXIT: u32 = 0x005f_d0ff;
pub const DARK_HASH: u64 = 0x50e3_c0c6_7165_21a4;
/// The mask global read every iteration.
const DARK_MASK: u32 = 0x007e_8dec;

/// `mov edi,[eax]; mov ebx,[0x7e8dec]; shr edi,1; and edi,ebx; mov [eax],edi; add eax,4; cmp eax,esi; jne`.
pub fn darken(cpu: &mut Cpu, mem: &mut GuestMemory, budget: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    const PER: u64 = 8;
    let [mut eax, _, _, _, _, _, esi, _] = cpu.regs;
    let dist = esi.wrapping_sub(eax);
    if dist == 0 || dist & 3 != 0 || dist / 4 > MAX_ITERS {
        return None;
    }
    let n = (dist / 4).min((budget / PER).min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32);
    if n == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let len = 4 * n as u64;
    if !range_ok(eax, len) || !disjoint(eax, len, DARK_MASK, 4) {
        return None;
    }
    let mask = mem.read_u32(DARK_MASK);
    let mut edi = 0;
    for _ in 0..n {
        edi = (mem.read_u32(eax) >> 1) & mask;
        mem.write_u32(eax, edi);
        eax = eax.wrapping_add(4);
    }
    cpu.regs[EAX] = eax;
    cpu.regs[EBX] = mask;
    cpu.regs[EDI] = edi;
    cpu.alu_sub(eax, esi, 0, 4);
    cpu.eip = if eax == esi { DARK_EXIT } else { DARK_START };
    Some(n as u64 * PER)
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ checkerboard shadow 0x5fd096

pub const DITHER_START: u32 = 0x005f_d096;
pub const DITHER_EXIT: u32 = 0x005f_d0ae;
pub const DITHER_HASH: u64 = 0xa260_2e8f_9197_8473;

/// `lea ebx,[esi+ebp]; test bl,1; jz +; mov word [eax],0; +: add eax,2; inc esi; and esi,1f; cmp eax,edx; jnz`.
pub fn dither(cpu: &mut Cpu, mem: &mut GuestMemory, budget: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    let [mut eax, _, edx, mut ebx, _, ebp, mut esi, _] = cpu.regs;
    let dist = edx.wrapping_sub(eax);
    if dist == 0 || dist & 1 != 0 || dist / 2 > MAX_ITERS || !range_ok(eax, dist as u64) {
        return None;
    }
    let mut done = 0u64;
    while eax != edx {
        let b = esi.wrapping_add(ebp);
        let odd = b & 1;
        let per = 8 + odd as u64;
        if done + per > budget {
            break;
        }
        ebx = b;
        if odd != 0 {
            mem.write_u16(eax, 0);
        }
        eax = eax.wrapping_add(2);
        esi = esi.wrapping_add(1) & 0x1f;
        done += per;
    }
    if done == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    cpu.regs[EAX] = eax;
    cpu.regs[EBX] = ebx;
    cpu.regs[ESI] = esi;
    cpu.alu_sub(eax, edx, 0, 4);
    cpu.eip = if eax == edx { DITHER_EXIT } else { DITHER_START };
    Some(done)
}

```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/fast_land.rs`:

```rs
//! Native fast path: the triangle loop of the landscape pass `0x54cbd0` (draw thread) for triangles that need no
//! redraw (see `fast.rs` for the contract, docs/porting/performance.md).
//!
//! Loop head `0x54ce53`: `while [ebp-0x74] < [ebp-0xc4]`, alternating up/down triangles (`[ebp-0x5c]` = 1 / 0) over
//! the snapshot cells of one row (`cell = [ebp+8] + ([ebp-0x48] + [ebp-0x44]*130)*0x30`). Per triangle it reads three
//! corner heights, computes their screen y (`[ebp-0x98] - h`, +8 for some corners), keeps the minimum in
//! `[ebp-0x34]`, and draws only when a corner's dirty bit (`+5` bit 7) or one of the flags `[ebp-0x68]`,
//! `[ebp-0xe4]`, `[ebp-0xe8]` is set. In game almost all triangles are clean (the landscape is cached), so the
//! loop runs ~65 guest instructions per triangle, ~16 000 triangles per frame at 1536x600: 17-25 % of all guest
//! instructions. Only clean triangles are native; any other ends the native run at the loop head before it.

use s3_cpu::{layout, Cpu, GuestMemory, EAX, EBP, EBX, ECX, EDI, EDX, ESI};

use crate::res;

pub const START: u32 = 0x0054_ce53;
/// End of the code the native path stands for (the `jmp 0x54ce53` at 0x54e70d is its last instruction).
pub const END: u32 = 0x0054_e712;
/// FNV-1a of the code *after* the res patch (`res::code_patches`: row stride 258 in this loop).
pub const HASH: u64 = 0x6653_2149_bbd1_c4ee;
/// Cell offset of the same row in the next snapshot column (`0x500 + 0x1860` in the game's 130-row grid; the
/// res patch makes the stride [`res::SNAP_ROWS`]).
const NEXT: u32 = 0x500 + res::SNAP_COL_BYTES_NEW;
/// Bytes read from `cell + 0x500`: up to byte `+5` of the next column's next row.
const CELLS_LEN: u32 = NEXT + 0x36 - 0x500;

#[inline]
fn ok(a: u32, len: u32) -> bool {
    a >= layout::NULL_GUARD_END && a as u64 + len as u64 <= u32::MAX as u64
}

#[inline]
fn disjoint(a: u32, alen: u32, b: u32, blen: u32) -> bool {
    let (a, b) = (a as u64, b as u64);
    a + alen as u64 <= b || b + blen as u64 <= a
}

pub fn land_clean(cpu: &mut Cpu, mem: &mut GuestMemory, budget: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    let ebp = cpu.regs[EBP];
    if ebp < 0x1000 || !ok(ebp - 0xe8, 0xe8 + 0xc) {
        return None;
    }
    let fr = ebp - 0xe8; // frame range [ebp-0xe8, ebp+0xc)
    let rd = |mem: &GuestMemory, o: u32| mem.read_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(o));
    // Loop-invariant flags (only the loop body below writes the frame, and not these).
    if rd(mem, 0x68) == 1 || rd(mem, 0xe4) == 1 || rd(mem, 0xe8) == 1 {
        return None;
    }
    let base = mem.read_u32(ebp.wrapping_add(8));
    let v48 = rd(mem, 0x48);
    let v98 = rd(mem, 0x98);
    let v9c = rd(mem, 0x9c);
    let vc4 = rd(mem, 0xc4);
    let mut ecx = cpu.regs[ECX];
    let mut done = 0u64;
    let mut out = None::<(u32, u32, u32, u32, u32, u32, u32)>; // eax ecx edx ebx esi edi, phase of the last triangle
    loop {
        let v74 = rd(mem, 0x74);
        if (v74 as i32) >= (vc4 as i32) {
            break; // loop exit: the original takes it
        }
        let phase = rd(mem, 0x5c);
        let v44 = rd(mem, 0x44);
        let off = v48.wrapping_add(v44.wrapping_mul(res::SNAP_ROWS)).wrapping_mul(48);
        let cell = off.wrapping_add(base);
        if !ok(cell.wrapping_add(0x500), CELLS_LEN) || !disjoint(cell.wrapping_add(0x500), CELLS_LEN, fr, 0xf4) {
            break;
        }
        let b = |o: u32| mem.read_u8(cell.wrapping_add(o)) as u32;
        // (eax, edi, ebx) entering the min/max block 0x54cf66, guest instructions so far
        let (eax, edi, ebx, mut n) = if phase == 1 {
            let (h1, h0, h2) = (b(NEXT + 0x30), b(0x500), b(NEXT));
            if b(0x505) & 0x80 != 0 || b(NEXT + 0x35) & 0x80 != 0 || b(NEXT + 5) & 0x80 != 0 {
                break;
            }
            (v98.wrapping_sub(h1).wrapping_add(8), v98.wrapping_sub(h0), v98.wrapping_sub(h2), 4 + 7 + 31u64)
        } else {
            let (h0, h1, h3) = (b(0x500), b(NEXT + 0x30), b(0x530));
            if b(0x505) & 0x80 != 0 || b(NEXT + 0x35) & 0x80 != 0 || b(0x535) & 0x80 != 0 {
                break;
            }
            (v98.wrapping_sub(h0), v98.wrapping_sub(h3).wrapping_add(8), v98.wrapping_sub(h1).wrapping_add(8), 4 + 7 + 33u64)
        };
        // 0x54cf66 min/max
        n += 5;
        let (mut edx, mut cx) = (eax, edi);
        if (edi as i32) < (eax as i32) {
            edx = edi;
            cx = eax;
            n += 3;
        }
        n += 2;
        if (ebx as i32) < (edx as i32) {
            edx = ebx;
            n += 2;
        }
        n += 2;
        if (ebx as i32) > (cx as i32) {
            n += 1;
        }
        n += 8; // 0x54cf87 / 0x54cfac / 0x54cfc5 / 0x54cfde (cmp [ebp-0x2c],1 -> 0, jne)
        n += 4 + 8 + if phase == 1 { 1 } else { 0 }; // 0x54e6e8, (0x54e6f3), 0x54e6f6
        if done + n > budget {
            break;
        }
        // ---- commit (frame writes only)
        let wr = |mem: &mut GuestMemory, o: u32, v: u32| mem.write_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(o), v);
        ecx = ecx.wrapping_add(8);
        wr(mem, 0x30, ecx);
        wr(mem, 0x20, eax); // up: v98 - h1 + 8, down: v98 - h0
        wr(mem, 0x2c, 0);
        wr(mem, 0x34, edx);
        if phase == 1 {
            wr(mem, 0x44, v44.wrapping_add(1));
        }
        let nphase = 1u32.wrapping_sub(phase);
        wr(mem, 0x5c, nphase);
        wr(mem, 0x74, v74.wrapping_add(1));
        done += n;
        out = Some((v9c, ecx, nphase, ebx, cell, edi, phase));
    }
    let (eax, ecx, edx, ebx, esi, edi, phase) = out?;
    cpu.regs[EAX] = eax;
    cpu.regs[ECX] = ecx;
    cpu.regs[EDX] = edx;
    cpu.regs[EBX] = ebx;
    cpu.regs[ESI] = esi;
    cpu.regs[EDI] = edi;
    // flags: `sub edx,eax` (1 - phase) then `inc eax` ([ebp-0x74]+1; keeps CF)
    cpu.alu_sub(1, phase, 0, 4);
    let v74 = rd(mem, 0x74);
    cpu.alu_inc(v74.wrapping_sub(1), 4);
    cpu.eip = START;
    Some(done)
}
```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/fast_land_rows.rs`:

```rs
//! Native fast path: the row loop of the dirty-triangle rasteriser in the landscape pass `0x54cbd0` (draw thread),
//! see `fast.rs` for the contract and docs/porting/performance.md.
//!
//! A triangle that needs a redraw (dirty corner, or every triangle after a size switch: full landscape redraw) is set
//! up per triangle (`0x54d015..0x54e4bc`: edge slopes, texture choice), then drawn row by row from the row head
//! `0x54e4bc` (`while [ebp-0x14] > 0`) until `0x54e6e8` (back to the triangle loop). Per row: step both edges and
//! the texture/light coordinates (`[ebp-0x40]`/`[ebp-0xe0]` = right/left x in 24.8, `[ebp-0x94]`/`[ebp-0x84]` u,
//! `[ebp-0xbc]`/`[ebp-0xcc]` v, `[ebp-0x70]`/`[ebp-0xa0]` light), span width `(xr >> 8) - (xl >> 8)`; for a span of
//! `n >= 1` pixels three `idiv` give the per-pixel steps, then per pixel
//! `dst[i] = shade[tex[(u/256)*16 + v/256] * 128 + light/256]` (`tex` = `[ebp-0x24]`, 16-bit `shade` = `[obj+0xa4]`,
//! `obj` = `[ebp-0x88]`, C division by 256). Row end: destination row += `edx` (the pitch), screen row
//! `[ebp-0x28]` += `[ebp-0xb0]` with a wrap at `[obj+0x54] - 0x28` / -1 (the landscape buffer is a vertical ring),
//! `[ebp-0x54]` counts the rows of the first triangle half; at 0 `[ebp-0x38]` = 2 / 3 switches one edge's steps.
//!
//! Instructions: 3 (head) + 32 (edges) + either 12 (empty span) or 22 + 44/pixel + 13, + 2 or 10 or 12 (wrap
//! test / wrap), + 4, + 2 (or 3 + 12 / 3 + 2 + 10 / 3 + 2 + 2 at the half switch); exit 3. During a full redraw
//! this loop is ~90 % of the landscape pass (~70 % of all guest instructions while pinching out).
//!
//! The pixels of a row are computed into a buffer first and written at the row's commit; a row whose texel or
//! shade reads overlap its destination span or the stack frame, whose destination overlaps the frame or the two
//! object fields, that could fault (NULL guard), is wider than `MAX_SPAN` or exceeds the budget ends the native run
//! at the row head before it (the interpreter runs it).

use s3_cpu::{layout, Cpu, GuestMemory, EAX, EBP, EBX, ECX, EDI, EDX, ESI};

/// Row head (entry, and stop point after a budget end).
pub const START: u32 = 0x0054_e4bc;
/// Loop exit (`[ebp-0x14] <= 0`), back to the triangle loop.
pub const EXIT: u32 = 0x0054_e6e8;
pub const HASH: u64 = 0x5ad9_73cb_c5ee_4879;

const MAX_SPAN: usize = 2048;

/// Branch coverage for the differential test: 0 empty span, 1 pixel span, 2/3 wrap (row == height-0x28 / -1),
/// 4/5/6 half switch 2 / 3 / other, 7 aliasing/fault/width stop, 8 budget stop, 9 exit, 10 no half switch.
#[cfg(test)]
pub static COV: [std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32; 11] = [const { std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32::new(0) }; 11];

#[inline(always)]
fn cov(_i: usize) {
    #[cfg(test)]
    COV[_i].fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
}

#[inline]
fn ok(a: u32, len: u32) -> bool {
    a >= layout::NULL_GUARD_END && a as u64 + len as u64 <= u32::MAX as u64
}

#[inline]
fn disjoint(a: u32, alen: u32, b: u32, blen: u32) -> bool {
    let (a, b) = (a as u64, b as u64);
    a + alen as u64 <= b || b + blen as u64 <= a
}

/// `cdq; and edx,0xff; add eax,edx; sar eax,8`: signed division by 256 rounding toward zero.
#[inline(always)]
fn div256(x: u32) -> u32 {
    let t = x.wrapping_add(((x as i32) >> 31) as u32 & 0xff);
    ((t as i32) >> 8) as u32
}

/// `cdq; idiv d` quotient for `d >= 1` (no overflow possible).
#[inline(always)]
fn idiv(a: u32, d: u32) -> u32 {
    ((a as i32) / (d as i32)) as u32
}

pub fn land_rows(cpu: &mut Cpu, mem: &mut GuestMemory, budget: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    let ebp = cpu.regs[EBP];
    if ebp < 0x100 || !ok(ebp - 0x100, 0x100) {
        return None;
    }
    let fr = ebp - 0x100; // frame slots used: [ebp-0xfc, ebp-0x14]
    let rd = |mem: &GuestMemory, o: u32| mem.read_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(o));
    let obj = rd(mem, 0x88);
    let (o54, oa4) = (obj.wrapping_add(0x54), obj.wrapping_add(0xa4));
    if !ok(o54, 4) || !ok(oa4, 4) || !disjoint(o54, 4, fr, 0x100) || !disjoint(oa4, 4, fr, 0x100) {
        return None;
    }
    // Loop invariants: no frame write of the loop touches these slots, and pixel writes never hit the frame or
    // the two object fields (checked per row).
    let tex = rd(mem, 0x24);
    let shade = mem.read_u32(oa4);
    let fc8 = rd(mem, 0xc8);
    let ff8 = rd(mem, 0xf8);
    let [mut eax, mut ecx, mut edx, mut ebx, _esp, _ebp, mut esi, mut edi] = cpu.regs;
    let mut done = 0u64;
    // flags of the last finished step: Some((a, b, dec)) = `cmp a,b` (CF source) then `dec dec`; exit: `test`
    let mut flags: Option<(u32, u32, u32)> = None;
    let mut exited = false;
    let mut buf = [0u16; MAX_SPAN];
    loop {
        let f14 = rd(mem, 0x14);
        if (f14 as i32) <= 0 {
            if done + 3 <= budget {
                eax = f14;
                done += 3;
                exited = true;
                cov(9);
            }
            break;
        }
        // ---- 0x54e4c7: edges and coordinates (frame values, written at the commit)
        let f40 = rd(mem, 0x40).wrapping_add(rd(mem, 0xa8));
        let fe0 = rd(mem, 0xe0).wrapping_add(rd(mem, 0xb8));
        let fbc = rd(mem, 0xbc).wrapping_add(rd(mem, 0xd8));
        let f94 = rd(mem, 0x94).wrapping_add(rd(mem, 0x2c));
        let fcc = rd(mem, 0xcc).wrapping_add(rd(mem, 0xac));
        let f84 = rd(mem, 0x84).wrapping_add(rd(mem, 0x34));
        let f70 = rd(mem, 0x70).wrapping_add(rd(mem, 0xc0));
        let fa0 = rd(mem, 0xa0).wrapping_add(rd(mem, 0xa4));
        let xl = ((fe0 as i32) >> 8) as u32;
        let w = (((f40 as i32) >> 8) as u32).wrapping_sub(xl);
        let mut n = 3 + 32u64;
        // EBX and EDX after the span (the row end overwrites the other registers)
        let (mut r_ebx, mut r_edx) = (fbc, edx);
        let f20_in = rd(mem, 0x20);
        // span (0x54e554 .. 0x54e620): pixels into `buf`, frame values (f18, f1c, fec, ffc, ff0)
        let mut span: Option<(u32, usize, [u32; 5])> = None;
        if (w as i32) >= 1 {
            let cnt = w;
            if cnt as usize > MAX_SPAN {
                cov(7);
                break;
            }
            n += 22 + 44 * cnt as u64 + 13;
            cov(1);
            if done + n > budget {
                cov(8);
                break; // the rest of the row costs more; stop here already
            }
            let fec = idiv(fcc.wrapping_sub(fbc), cnt);
            let ffc = idiv(f84.wrapping_sub(f94), cnt);
            let ff0 = idiv(fa0.wrapping_sub(f70), cnt);
            let d0 = f20_in.wrapping_add(xl.wrapping_mul(2));
            let dlen = 2 * cnt;
            if !ok(d0, dlen)
                || !disjoint(d0, dlen, fr, 0x100)
                || !disjoint(d0, dlen, o54, 4)
                || !disjoint(d0, dlen, oa4, 4)
            {
                cov(7);
                break;
            }
            let (mut u, mut v, mut l) = (f94, fbc, f70);
            let mut bad = false;
            for px in buf.iter_mut().take(cnt as usize) {
                let ta = div256(v).wrapping_add(tex.wrapping_add(div256(u) << 4));
                if !ok(ta, 1) || !disjoint(ta, 1, d0, dlen) || !disjoint(ta, 1, fr, 0x100) {
                    bad = true;
                    break;
                }
                let t = mem.read_u8(ta) as u32;
                let sa = shade.wrapping_add(((t << 7).wrapping_add(div256(l))).wrapping_mul(2));
                if !ok(sa, 2) || !disjoint(sa, 2, d0, dlen) || !disjoint(sa, 2, fr, 0x100) {
                    bad = true;
                    break;
                }
                *px = mem.read_u16(sa);
                v = v.wrapping_add(fec);
                u = u.wrapping_add(ffc);
                l = l.wrapping_add(ff0);
            }
            if bad {
                cov(7);
                break;
            }
            r_ebx = v;
            r_edx = ff8; // 0x54e620
            span = Some((d0, cnt as usize, [u, l, fec, ffc, ff0])); // [ebp-0x18] ends as u, [ebp-0x1c] as l
        } else {
            n += 12;
            cov(0);
        }
        // ---- 0x54e626: row end (the object field is read after the pixel writes; they are disjoint)
        let h = mem.read_u32(o54);
        let mut f20 = f20_in.wrapping_add(r_edx);
        let fb0 = rd(mem, 0xb0);
        let mut f28 = rd(mem, 0x28).wrapping_add(fb0);
        let (mut r_ecx, mut r_esi, mut r_edi) = (fb0, f28, h.wrapping_sub(0x28));
        let (cf_a, cf_b);
        if f28 == h.wrapping_sub(0x28) || f28 == u32::MAX {
            n += if f28 == h.wrapping_sub(0x28) { 10 } else { 2 + 10 };
            cov(if f28 == h.wrapping_sub(0x28) { 2 } else { 3 });
            let a = h.wrapping_sub(0x28);
            let prod = a.wrapping_mul(fc8);
            let e = a.wrapping_mul(fb0);
            r_edi = e;
            r_ecx = f20;
            f28 = f28.wrapping_sub(e);
            r_esi = f28;
            f20 = f20.wrapping_add(0u32.wrapping_sub(prod).wrapping_mul(2));
            (cf_a, cf_b) = (0, prod); // neg eax
        } else {
            n += 2;
            (cf_a, cf_b) = (f28, u32::MAX); // cmp esi,-1
        }
        // 0x54e670
        n += 4;
        let f54 = rd(mem, 0x54).wrapping_sub(1);
        let mut r_eax = f54;
        let f38 = rd(mem, 0x38);
        // half switch writes: (slot, value)
        let mut sw: [(u32, u32); 4] = [(0, 0); 4];
        let mut nsw = 0;
        let fl;
        if f54 != 0 {
            n += 2;
            cov(10);
            fl = (cf_a, cf_b, f14);
        } else {
            n += 3;
            if f38 == 2 {
                n += 12;
                cov(4);
                let (f90, f8c, f3c, f6c) = (rd(mem, 0x90), rd(mem, 0x8c), rd(mem, 0x3c), rd(mem, 0x6c));
                sw = [(0xd8, f90), (0xc0, f3c), (0xb8, f8c), (0x2c, f6c)];
                nsw = 4;
                r_eax = f14.wrapping_sub(1);
                r_ecx = f6c;
                fl = (2, 2, f14);
            } else {
                n += 2;
                if f38 == 3 {
                    n += 10;
                    cov(5);
                    let (f90, f8c, f3c, f6c) = (rd(mem, 0x90), rd(mem, 0x8c), rd(mem, 0x3c), rd(mem, 0x6c));
                    sw = [(0xa8, f8c), (0xac, f90), (0x34, f6c), (0xa4, f3c)];
                    nsw = 4;
                    r_eax = f3c;
                    r_ecx = f6c;
                } else {
                    n += 2;
                    cov(6);
                    r_eax = f38;
                }
                fl = (f38, 3, f14);
            }
        }
        if done + n > budget {
            cov(8);
            break;
        }
        // ---- commit
        let wr = |mem: &mut GuestMemory, o: u32, v: u32| mem.write_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(o), v);
        wr(mem, 0x40, f40);
        wr(mem, 0xe0, fe0);
        wr(mem, 0xbc, fbc);
        wr(mem, 0x94, f94);
        wr(mem, 0xcc, fcc);
        wr(mem, 0x84, f84);
        wr(mem, 0x70, f70);
        wr(mem, 0xa0, fa0);
        if let Some((d0, cnt, [u, l, fec, ffc, ff0])) = span {
            wr(mem, 0x18, u);
            wr(mem, 0x1c, l);
            wr(mem, 0xec, fec);
            wr(mem, 0xfc, ffc);
            wr(mem, 0xf0, ff0);
            let dst = mem.slice_mut(d0, cnt * 2);
            for (i, &px) in buf[..cnt].iter().enumerate() {
                dst[2 * i..2 * i + 2].copy_from_slice(&px.to_le_bytes());
            }
        }
        wr(mem, 0x20, f20);
        wr(mem, 0x28, f28);
        wr(mem, 0x54, f54);
        for &(o, v) in &sw[..nsw] {
            wr(mem, o, v);
        }
        wr(mem, 0x14, f14.wrapping_sub(1));
        eax = r_eax;
        ebx = r_ebx;
        ecx = r_ecx;
        edx = r_edx;
        esi = r_esi;
        edi = r_edi;
        done += n;
        flags = Some(fl);
    }
    if done == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    cpu.regs[EAX] = eax;
    cpu.regs[ECX] = ecx;
    cpu.regs[EDX] = edx;
    cpu.regs[EBX] = ebx;
    cpu.regs[ESI] = esi;
    cpu.regs[EDI] = edi;
    if exited {
        cpu.alu_logic(eax, 4); // test eax,eax
        cpu.eip = EXIT;
    } else {
        let (a, b, d) = flags?;
        cpu.alu_sub(a, b, 0, 4);
        cpu.alu_dec(d, 4);
        cpu.eip = START;
    }
    Some(done)
}
```
