```rs
        }
    }
    eprintln!("differential_land_mark: native ran {ran} of 300");
    assert!(ran > 200, "too many declines: {ran}");
}

/// Row loop of the dirty-triangle rasteriser in `0x54cbd0` (`fast_land_rows::land_rows`): random triangle rows
/// (edges, u/v/light steps, half switch, ring-buffer wrap), textures, shade tables and budgets.
#[test]
fn differential_land_rows() {
    let Some(exe) = exe_bytes() else {
        eprintln!("differential_land_rows: S3.EXE not found, skipped");
        return;
    };
    const OBJ: u32 = 0x3400_0000;
    let mut r = Rng(0x54e4_bc00_1a2d_f011);
    let (mut ran, mut exits, mut insns) = (0, 0, 0u64);
    let cases = 600;
    for case in 0..cases {
        let budget = if case % 3 == 0 { 1 + r.below(3000) as u64 } else { 1 << 30 };
        let eflags = 0x202 | (r.next() & 0x8D5);
        let mut regs: [u32; 8] = std::array::from_fn(|_| r.next());
        let ebp = STACK + 0x1000;
        regs[EBP] = ebp;
        regs[ESP] = ebp - 0x200;
        let mut frame = random_bytes(&mut r, 0x200);
        let o = |d: i32| (0x100 + d) as usize; // frame buffer starts at ebp - 0x100
        let put = |f: &mut Vec<u8>, d: i32, v: u32| f[o(d)..o(d) + 4].copy_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
        let s = |r: &mut Rng, m: u32| (r.below(2 * m + 1) as i32 - m as i32) as u32; // signed in [-m, m]
        let pitch = 64 + r.below(448); // pixels
        regs[EDX] = if r.below(8) == 0 { r.next() & 0xffe } else { 2 * pitch };
        put(&mut frame, -0x14, if r.below(10) == 0 { s(&mut r, 2) } else { r.below(20) });
        put(&mut frame, -0x54, r.below(12));
        put(&mut frame, -0x38, r.below(5));
        let xl = r.below(300) << 8 | r.below(256);
        put(&mut frame, -0xe0, xl);
        put(&mut frame, -0x40, xl.wrapping_add(s(&mut r, 20 << 8)));
        for d in [-0xa8, -0xb8, -0x8c] {
            put(&mut frame, d, s(&mut r, 3 << 8)); // edge slopes
        }
        for d in [-0x94, -0x84, -0xbc, -0xcc] {
            put(&mut frame, d, s(&mut r, 20 << 8)); // u, v (texture 16x16, beyond it into neighbours)
        }
        for d in [-0x2c, -0x34, -0xd8, -0xac, -0x6c, -0x90] {
            put(&mut frame, d, s(&mut r, 1 << 8));
        }
        for d in [-0x70, -0xa0] {
            put(&mut frame, d, r.below(128 << 8)); // light
        }
        for d in [-0xc0, -0xa4, -0x3c] {
            put(&mut frame, d, s(&mut r, 4 << 8));
        }
        let h = 0x30 + r.below(0x100);
        put(&mut frame, -0x28, if r.below(3) == 0 { r.below(4).wrapping_sub(1) } else { r.below(h) });
        put(&mut frame, -0xb0, if r.below(2) == 0 { 1 } else { u32::MAX });
        put(&mut frame, -0xc8, pitch);
        put(&mut frame, -0xf8, 2 * pitch);
        put(&mut frame, -0x20, DST + 0x6_0000 + 2 * r.below(pitch));
        put(&mut frame, -0x24, SRC + 0x8000 + r.below(0x100));
        put(&mut frame, -0x88, OBJ);
        let mut objb = random_bytes(&mut r, 0x100);
        objb[0x54..0x58].copy_from_slice(&h.to_le_bytes());
        let shade = if r.below(20) == 0 { 0x100 } else { PAL };
        objb[0xa4..0xa8].copy_from_slice(&shade.to_le_bytes());
        if r.below(20) == 0 {
            put(&mut frame, -0x20, ebp - 0x80); // destination over the frame: must stop/decline
        }
        if r.below(20) == 0 {
            put(&mut frame, -0x24, DST + 0x6_0000); // texture inside the destination rows
        }
        let writes = vec![
            (ebp - 0x100, frame),
            (OBJ, objb),
            (SRC, random_bytes(&mut r, 0x1_0000)),
            (PAL, random_bytes(&mut r, 0x1_0000)),
            (DST, random_bytes(&mut r, 0x10_0000)),
        ];
        let regions = [(STACK, 0x2000), (OBJ, 0x100), (SRC, 0x1_0000), (PAL, 0x1_0000), (DST, 0x10_0000)];
        if check_in(&exe, fast_land_rows::land_rows, fast_land_rows::START, regs, eflags, &writes, budget, "land_rows", &regions) {
            ran += 1;
            // rerun natively for the statistics (exit reached, instructions)
            let mut mem = GuestMemory::new().unwrap();
            for (a, d) in &writes {
                mem.write_bytes(*a, d);
            }
            let mut nc = Cpu::new();
            nc.regs = regs;
            nc.eip = fast_land_rows::START;
            insns += fast_land_rows::land_rows(&mut nc, &mut mem, budget).unwrap();
            if nc.eip == fast_land_rows::EXIT {
                exits += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    let cov: Vec<u32> = fast_land_rows::COV.iter().map(|c| c.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed)).collect();
    eprintln!("differential_land_rows: native ran {ran} of {cases} ({exits} reached the exit, {insns} instructions)");
    eprintln!("differential_land_rows: branch coverage {cov:?}");
    assert!(cov.iter().all(|&c| c > 0), "a branch was never taken: {cov:?}");
    assert!(ran > 300, "too many declines: {ran}");
    assert!(exits > 100, "too few exits: {exits}");
}

```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/fast_tile.rs`:

```rs
//! Native fast paths: the tile loops of the frame renderer `0x4b26c0` (draw thread; see `fast.rs` for the contract,
//! docs/porting/performance.md).
//!
//! **`frame_tiles`** (`0x4b2e44..0x4b330e`): the main loop over the snapshot cells (rows `r = [ebp+0xc]` up to
//! `[ebp-0x44]`, columns `i = esi` from `[ebp-0x24]` to `[ebp-0x24] + [ebp-0x7c]`, cell
//! `snap + 0x500 + (r + i*130)*0x30`, `snap = [ebp+8]`, screen x `[ebp-0x18]` += 16 per cell, y `[ebp-0x14]` += 9
//! per row). Per cell the original computes the screen sector `x/40`, adds ambient-sound statistics for the cells of
//! the first 16 sectors (`[ebx+0x5f588/0x5f5cc + 4*(land>>4)]`), checks the 4x4 water-decoration grid, then calls
//! the per-tile object drawer `0x4d3050` (one of three call sites) and, for some cells, more drawers. It was
//! ~95 guest instructions per cell plus ~112 for the object call, ~16 000 cells per frame at 1944x760: 42 % of
//! all guest instructions in game (HUD). Native: cells whose object call is the empty case of `fast_obj` (done
//! inline with `fast_obj::plan`/`apply`), including the sound statistics, and the row advance. A cell that needs
//! anything else (water/shore sound weights `0x4b2f0e`, decoration `0x4b3046`, object type != 0, cell words
//! `+0x50a`/`+0x51e` != 0, `+0x508` kinds 0x800/0x1000/0x1800) ends the native run at the loop head before it.
//!
//! **`land_mark`** (`0x4b277e..0x4b27a7`): the inner loop of the pre-pass over one snapshot column (`eax` = cell
//! `+0x502`, stride 0x1860, `edi` cells): for cells with `(+0x505 & 0x3f)*4 <= 0x48` it sets the landscape byte to
//! 0x1c when bit 2 of `+0x509` is set, else turns 0x1c back into 0x10. 8-13 guest instructions per cell.

use s3_cpu::{layout, Cpu, GuestMemory, EAX, ECX, EDI, EDX, ESI, ESP};

use crate::{fast_obj, res};

/// Loop head of the cell loop (`mov edx,[ebp-0x7c]`, target of the `jmp` at 0x4b32ca).
pub const START: u32 = 0x004b_2e44;
/// End of the code the native path stands for: the cell loop and the row advance (0x4b32cf..0x4b330e).
pub const END: u32 = 0x004b_330e;
pub const HASH: u64 = 0xbdb2_cc00_0a03_439d; // patched code (res::code_patches)
/// Row loop head `0x4b2e30..0x4b2e44` (`cmp ecx,[ebp-0x44]; ja 0x4b330e`, four moves), run between rows; outside
/// the registered region, so its bytes are checked at each entry.
pub const HEAD: (u32, u32) = (0x004b_2e30, 0x004b_2e44);
const HEAD_HASH: u64 = 0x42e6_f725_ccdc_2517;
/// Exit of the row loop (the `ja` at 0x4b2e33 taken).
const ROWS_EXIT: u32 = 0x004b_330e;
/// Return addresses of the two `call 0x4d3050` sites handled natively.
const RET_H: u32 = 0x004b_30fa;
const RET_G: u32 = 0x004b_3207;
/// The instructions of `0x4d3050` that its empty case executes (`fast_obj`; traced, test
/// `obj_empty_path_hashed`), and the FNV-1a 64 hash of their bytes concatenated
/// (`tools/perf/code_hash.py --concat`). Checked at each entry of `frame_tiles`.
pub const OBJ_RANGES: [(u32, u32); 24] = [
    (0x004d_3050, 0x004d_30d8),
    (0x004d_3294, 0x004d_32a6),
    (0x004d_340d, 0x004d_3416),
    (0x004d_352e, 0x004d_3533),
    (0x004d_3595, 0x004d_359e),
    (0x004d_36de, 0x004d_36e7),
    (0x004d_3819, 0x004d_3822),
    (0x004d_3962, 0x004d_3967),
    (0x004d_39c9, 0x004d_39ce),
    (0x004d_3a2f, 0x004d_3a34),
    (0x004d_3a87, 0x004d_3a92),
    (0x004d_3bc0, 0x004d_3bcb),
    (0x004d_4119, 0x004d_4124),
    (0x004d_421e, 0x004d_4229),
    (0x004d_439a, 0x004d_43aa),
    (0x004d_4486, 0x004d_448f),
    (0x004d_456b, 0x004d_4574),
    (0x004d_465f, 0x004d_4668),
    (0x004d_4744, 0x004d_474d),
    (0x004d_4829, 0x004d_483e),
    (0x004d_4aea, 0x004d_4b18),
    (0x004d_52cc, 0x004d_52dd),
    (0x004d_53b2, 0x004d_53bc),
    (0x004d_5a42, 0x004d_5a4f),
];
pub(crate) const OBJ_HASH: u64 = 0xd4ce_d67a_3c03_19d3; // patched code

pub const MARK_START: u32 = 0x004b_277e;
/// First instruction after the loop (`jne` at 0x4b27a5 not taken).
pub const MARK_EXIT: u32 = 0x004b_27a7;
pub const MARK_HASH: u64 = 0xa5c3_7deb_4893_1a6b; // patched code

#[inline]
fn ok(a: u32, len: u32) -> bool {
    a >= layout::NULL_GUARD_END && a as u64 + len as u64 <= u32::MAX as u64
}

#[inline]
fn disjoint(a: (u32, u32), b: (u32, u32)) -> bool {
    let (a0, b0) = (a.0 as u64, b.0 as u64);
    a0 + a.1 as u64 <= b0 || b0 + b.1 as u64 <= a0
}

/// Test coverage counters: row advances, row-loop exits, cells with statistics, call site G, call site H.
#[cfg(test)]
pub static COVER: [std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64; 5] = [const { std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0) }; 5];

#[inline]
fn cover(_i: usize) {
    #[cfg(test)]
    COVER[_i].fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
}

fn ranges_hash(mem: &GuestMemory, ranges: &[(u32, u32)]) -> u64 {
    let mut h: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;
    for &(a, b) in ranges {
        for &x in mem.slice(a, (b - a) as usize) {
            h ^= x as u64;
            h = h.wrapping_mul(0x0000_0100_0000_01B3);
        }
    }
    h
}

/// Cell bytes read by one iteration: `+0x500..+0x520` and the neighbours `+0x592` (3 rows down), `+0x4e22`
/// (3 columns right) and `+0x4eb2` (3 columns right, 3 rows down); column offsets with the res patch's stride.
const CELL_LO: u32 = 0x500;
const COL3: u32 = 3 * res::SNAP_COL_BYTES_NEW;
const N_4E22: u32 = 0x502 + COL3;
const N_4EB2: u32 = 0x502 + COL3 + 0x90;
const CELL_LEN: u32 = N_4EB2 + 1 - 0x500;

/// What one cell iteration does (decided before anything is written).
struct Cell {
    /// Guest instructions from the loop head back to the loop head.
    n: u64,
    cell: u32,
    l: u32,
    /// Sound statistics: (index `land >> 4`, weight 1, weight 2).
    stats: Option<(u32, u32, u32)>,
    /// Call site G (`L < 0x49`): new `[ebp-0x28]` and `[ebp-0x60]`; else call site H.
    g: Option<(u32, u32)>,
    obj: fast_obj::Plan,
}

pub fn frame_tiles(cpu: &mut Cpu, mem: &mut GuestMemory, budget: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    let [mut eax, mut ecx, _, ebx, s, ebp, mut esi, edi] = cpu.regs;
    // Ranges the loop writes: frame [ebp-0x80, ebp+0x10), statistics, stack of the object call.
    let fr = (ebp.wrapping_sub(0x80), 0x90u32);
    let st = (ebx.wrapping_add(0x5f588), 0x84u32);
    let sk = (s.wrapping_sub(0x368), 0x368u32);
    if ebp < 0x1000 || !ok(fr.0, fr.1) || !ok(st.0, st.1) || s < 0x1000 || !ok(sk.0, sk.1) {
        return None;
    }
    if !disjoint(fr, st) || !disjoint(fr, sk) || !disjoint(st, sk) {
        return None;
    }
    let rd = |mem: &GuestMemory, o: i32| mem.read_u32(ebp.wrapping_add(o as u32));
    let snap = rd(mem, 8);
    if edi != snap || ecx != rd(mem, 0xc) {
        return None;
    }
    let hdr = (snap.wrapping_add(0x24), 0x40u32); // reads +0x24, +0x28, +0x60
    if !ok(hdr.0, hdr.1) || !disjoint(hdr, fr) || !disjoint(hdr, st) || !disjoint(hdr, sk) {
        return None;
    }
    let w = rd(mem, -0x7c);
    let rows = rd(mem, -0x44);
    let s24 = mem.read_u32(snap.wrapping_add(0x24));
    let s28 = mem.read_u32(snap.wrapping_add(0x28));
    let e = s - 0x1c; // ESP at the entry of 0x4d3050
    let mut done = 0u64;
    let mut moved = false;
    // The code outside the registered region (row head, the object call) is checked before the first change, so
    // a decline at the first cell (the interpreter runs it) costs no hashing.
    let code_ok = |mem: &GuestMemory| {
        ranges_hash(mem, &[HEAD]) == HEAD_HASH && ranges_hash(mem, &OBJ_RANGES) == OBJ_HASH && fast_obj::setter_ok(mem)
    };
    loop {
        let end = w.wrapping_add(eax);
        if esi > end {
            // ---- row advance: 0x4b2e44 (5), 0x4b32cf (7), odd 0x4b32e2 (9) / even 0x4b32fa (7), 0x4b2e30 (2),
            // 0x4b2e39 (4) unless the row loop ends.
            let r1 = ecx.wrapping_add(1);
            let odd = ecx & 1 == 1;
            let last = r1 > rows;
            let n = 5 + 7 + if odd { 9 } else { 7 } + 2 + if last { 0 } else { 4 };
            if done + n > budget || (!moved && !code_ok(mem)) {
                break;
            }
            mem.write_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(0x28), end);
            let y = rd(mem, -0x14).wrapping_add(9);
            mem.write_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(0x14), y);
            let x0 = if odd {
                eax = eax.wrapping_add(1);
                let x0 = rd(mem, -0x1c).wrapping_add(8);
                mem.write_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(0x24), eax);
                x0
            } else {
                rd(mem, -0x1c).wrapping_sub(8)
            };
            mem.write_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(0x1c), x0);
            mem.write_u32(ebp.wrapping_add(0xc), r1);
            ecx = r1;
            cpu.alu_sub(r1, rows, 0, 4); // cmp ecx,[ebp-0x44]
            done += n;
            moved = true;
            cpu.regs[EAX] = eax;
            cpu.regs[ECX] = ecx;
            cpu.regs[EDX] = x0;
            cover(0);
            if last {
                cover(1);
                cpu.regs[ESI] = 0;
                cpu.eip = ROWS_EXIT;
                return Some(done);
            }
            esi = eax;
            mem.write_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(0x18), x0);
            mem.write_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(0x4c), esi);
            cpu.regs[ESI] = esi;
            continue;
        }
        let Some(c) = plan_cell(mem, ebp, ecx, esi, snap, end, rows, s24, s28, e, (fr, st, sk)) else {
            break;
        };
        if done + c.n > budget || (!moved && !code_ok(mem)) {
            break;
        }
        // ---- commit, in the original order where it matters (no overlaps, checked above)
        let x = rd(mem, -0x18);
        let y = rd(mem, -0x14);
        mem.write_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(0x28), end);
        if let Some((k, w1, w2)) = c.stats {
            cover(2);
            let a1 = ebx.wrapping_add(0x5f588 + 4 * k);
            mem.write_u32(a1, mem.read_u32(a1).wrapping_add(w1));
            let a2 = ebx.wrapping_add(0x5f5cc + 4 * k);
            mem.write_u32(a2, mem.read_u32(a2).wrapping_add(w2));
        }
        mem.write_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(0x2c), c.l);
        mem.write_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(0x20), ecx.wrapping_add(esi.wrapping_mul(res::SNAP_ROWS)));
        cover(if c.g.is_some() { 3 } else { 4 });
        let ret = if let Some((v28, v60)) = c.g {
            mem.write_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(0x28), v28);
            mem.write_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(0x60), v60);
            RET_G
        } else {
            RET_H
        };
        // push a6=0, y, x, r, i, snap; call
        for (o, v) in [(4u32, 0u32), (8, y), (0xc, x), (0x10, ecx), (0x14, esi), (0x18, snap), (0x1c, ret)] {
            mem.write_u32(s - o, v);
        }
        cpu.regs[ESP] = e;
        cpu.regs[ESI] = esi;
        cpu.regs[EDI] = c.cell;
        fast_obj::apply(cpu, mem, e, snap, &c.obj);
        // 0x4b32b4: next cell
        let x1 = x.wrapping_add(0x10);
        cpu.alu_add(x, 0x10, 0, 4);
        cpu.alu_inc(esi, 4);
        esi = esi.wrapping_add(1);
        mem.write_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(0x18), x1);
        mem.write_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(0x4c), esi);
        eax = rd(mem, -0x24);
        ecx = rd(mem, 0xc);
        cpu.regs[EAX] = eax;
        cpu.regs[ECX] = ecx;
        cpu.regs[ESI] = esi;
        cpu.regs[EDI] = snap;
        done += c.n;
        moved = true;
    }
    if !moved {
        return None;
    }
    cpu.eip = START;
    Some(done)
}

/// Decide one cell iteration from the loop head (pure: reads only). `None` = not the native case.
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
#[inline]
fn plan_cell(
    mem: &GuestMemory,
    ebp: u32,
    r: u32,
    i: u32,
    snap: u32,
    end: u32,
    rows: u32,
    s24: u32,
    s28: u32,
    e: u32,
    wr: ((u32, u32), (u32, u32), (u32, u32)),
) -> Option<Cell> {
    let idx = r.wrapping_add(i.wrapping_mul(res::SNAP_ROWS));
    let cell = snap.wrapping_add(idx.wrapping_mul(48));
    let cr = (cell.wrapping_add(CELL_LO), CELL_LEN);
    if !ok(cr.0, cr.1) || !disjoint(cr, wr.0) || !disjoint(cr, wr.1) || !disjoint(cr, wr.2) {
        return None;
    }
    let b = |o: u32| mem.read_u8(cell.wrapping_add(o)) as u32;
    let x = mem.read_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(0x18));
    let y = mem.read_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(0x14));
    // 0x4b2e44 (5), 0x4b2e54 (8): q = x / 40 (the compiler's magic multiply)
    let mut n: u64 = 5 + 8;
    let hi = ((0x6666_6667i64 * x as i32 as i64) >> 32) as i32 >> 4;
    let q = hi.wrapping_add((hi as u32 >> 31) as i32);
    let mut stats = None;
    if q >= 0 {
        n += 2; // 0x4b2e6f
        if q <= 15 {
            n += 12; // 0x4b2e78
            let d = y.wrapping_sub(b(0x500)) as i32;
            if d >= 0 {
                n += 2; // 0x4b2e9b
                if d <= 0x258 {
                    n += 4; // 0x4b2ea3
                    let w1 = if q > 7 {
                        n += 2;
                        (15 - q) as u32
                    } else {
                        8
                    };
                    n += 3; // 0x4b2eb7
                    let w2 = if q < 8 {
                        n += 1;
                        q as u32
                    } else {
                        8
                    };
                    n += 12; // 0x4b2ec2
                    stats = Some((b(0x502) >> 4, w1, w2));
                }
            }
            n += 3; // 0x4b2ef8
            let al = b(0x503);
            if al >= 0xf8 {
                n += 2;
                if al <= 0xfd {
                    return None; // 0x4b2f0e: weighted water/shore statistics
                }
            }
        }
    }
    // 0x4b2f9e (18)
    n += 18;
    let l = (b(0x505) & 0x3f) << 2;
    let mut ea = l; // eax entering 0x4b30b4
    if i <= end.wrapping_sub(3) {
        n += 5; // 0x4b2fd8
        ea = r;
        if r <= rows.wrapping_sub(3) {
            n += 2;
            if b(0x502) < 0x10 {
                n += 2;
                if b(N_4EB2) < 0x10 {
                    n += 2;
                    if b(N_4E22) < 0x10 {
                        n += 2;
                        if b(0x592) < 0x10 {
                            n += 3; // 0x4b301d
                            ea = (r & !0xff) | b(0x503);
                            if b(0x503) == 0 {
                                n += 5; // 0x4b302b
                                ea = snap;
                                if s24.wrapping_add(i) & 3 == 0 {
                                    n += 5; // 0x4b3039
                                    ea = s28;
                                    if s28.wrapping_add(r) & 3 == 0 {
                                        return None; // 0x4b3046: water decoration
                                    }
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    n += 2; // 0x4b30b4
    let g;
    let post;
    if (l as i32) < 0x49 {
        // 0x4b31ae (7): word +0x508 kinds
        n += 7;
        let v28 = (ea & 0xffff_0000) | mem.read_u16(cell.wrapping_add(0x508)) as u32;
        let v60 = v28 & 0xf800;
        if v60 == 0x1800 {
            return None;
        }
        n += 12; // 0x4b31ed, call
        if v60 == 0x1000 {
            return None;
        }
        if v60 == 0x800 {
            return None;
        }
        post = 3 + 2; // 0x4b3207, 0x4b3244
        g = Some((v28, v60));
    } else {
        n += 4; // 0x4b30be
        if b(0x503) != 0 {
            return None; // object type
        }
        n += 2;
        if b(0x505) & 0x40 != 0 {
            n += 2;
            if b(0x502) & 0xf0 != 0 {
                return None; // type 0xfe
            }
        }
        n += 12; // 0x4b30e1, call
        if mem.read_u16(cell.wrapping_add(0x50a)) != 0 || mem.read_u16(cell.wrapping_add(0x51e)) != 0 {
            return None;
        }
        post = 3 + 3 + 2; // 0x4b30fa, 0x4b3124, 0x4b314e
        g = None;
    }
    let obj = fast_obj::plan(mem, e, snap, i, r, 0)?;
    n += obj.n + post + 9; // + 0x4b32b4
    Some(Cell { n, cell, l, stats, g, obj })
}

pub fn land_mark(cpu: &mut Cpu, mem: &mut GuestMemory, budget: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    let mut a = cpu.regs[EAX];
    let mut edi = cpu.regs[EDI];
    let mut done = 0u64;
    let mut last = None::<(u32, u32, u32)>; // eax before `add`, edi before `dec`, edx
    while done + 13 <= budget {
        if !ok(a, 8) {
            break;
        }
        let edx = (mem.read_u8(a + 3) as u32 & 0x3f) << 2;
        let n = if edx > 0x48 {
            8
        } else if mem.read_u8(a + 7) & 4 != 0 {
            mem.write_u8(a, 0x1c);
            12
        } else if mem.read_u8(a) == 0x1c {
            mem.write_u8(a, 0x10);
            13
        } else {
            12
        };
        done += n;
        last = Some((a, edi, edx));
        a = a.wrapping_add(res::SNAP_COL_BYTES_NEW);
        edi = edi.wrapping_sub(1);
        if edi == 0 {
            break;
        }
    }
    let (a0, e0, edx) = last?;
    cpu.alu_add(a0, res::SNAP_COL_BYTES_NEW, 0, 4);
    cpu.alu_dec(e0, 4);
    cpu.regs[EAX] = a;
    cpu.regs[EDI] = edi;
    cpu.regs[EDX] = edx;
    cpu.eip = if edi != 0 { MARK_START } else { MARK_EXIT };
    Some(done)
}

```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/fps.rs`:

```rs
//! FPS counter overlay (docs/porting/display.md "FPS counter"). Setting `display.fps_counter`:
//! `Off`, `Fps` (game frames per second) or `Detailed` (+ frame time avg / worst, guest MIPS, display rate).
//!
//! Counts real guest presents (`Machine::stats.presents`, overlay-only refreshes do not count) and guest
//! instructions over a 500 ms window. Drawn small in the top-right corner (Mobile HUD: top centre) of the part of the
//! window that shows the game, into the window layer ([`crate::layer`]): the same size on screen at every zoom
//! level. Presentation only.

use s3_runtime::Machine;

use s3_runtime::FrameBuffer;

use crate::display::{DisplayState, FpsCounter};
use crate::layer::Layer;
use crate::overlay::{measure_text, Rgba, Weight};
use crate::{Mod, ModsState};

/// Measurement window.
const WINDOW_MS: u64 = 500;

/// Rolling statistics (platform independent; unit tested).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct FpsStats {
    win_start_ms: u64,
    win_presents: u64,
    win_instr: u64,
    last_present_ms: Option<u64>,
    frame_sum_ms: u64,
    frame_n: u64,
    frame_max_ms: u64,
    /// Results of the last finished window.
    pub fps: f32,
    pub frame_avg_ms: f32,
    pub frame_max_ms_shown: u64,
    pub mips: f32,
    pub have: bool,
}

impl FpsStats {
    /// A real present happened at `now`.
    pub fn on_present(&mut self, now: u64) {
        if let Some(l) = self.last_present_ms {
            let d = now.saturating_sub(l);
            self.frame_sum_ms += d;
            self.frame_n += 1;
            self.frame_max_ms = self.frame_max_ms.max(d);
        }
        self.last_present_ms = Some(now);
    }

    /// Sample totals (`presents`, `instructions`) at `now`; closes the window every [`WINDOW_MS`].
    pub fn sample(&mut self, now: u64, presents: u64, instructions: u64) {
        if self.win_start_ms == 0 && !self.have && self.win_presents == 0 && self.win_instr == 0 {
            self.win_start_ms = now.max(1);
            self.win_presents = presents;
            self.win_instr = instructions;
            return;
        }
        let dt = now.saturating_sub(self.win_start_ms);
        if dt < WINDOW_MS {
            return;
        }
        let secs = dt as f32 / 1000.0;
        self.fps = presents.saturating_sub(self.win_presents) as f32 / secs;
        self.mips = instructions.saturating_sub(self.win_instr) as f32 / secs / 1e6;
        self.frame_avg_ms = if self.frame_n > 0 { self.frame_sum_ms as f32 / self.frame_n as f32 } else { 0.0 };
        self.frame_max_ms_shown = self.frame_max_ms;
        self.frame_sum_ms = 0;
        self.frame_n = 0;
        self.frame_max_ms = 0;
        self.win_start_ms = now;
        self.win_presents = presents;
        self.win_instr = instructions;
        self.have = true;
    }

    /// Text lines for the counter.
    pub fn lines(&self, mode: FpsCounter, host_fps: Option<f32>, refresh_hz: Option<f32>) -> Vec<String> {
        if !self.have {
            return vec!["-- fps".into()];
        }
        let mut v = vec![format!("{:.0} fps", self.fps)];
        if mode == FpsCounter::Detailed {
            v.push(format!("{:.1} ms (max {})", self.frame_avg_ms, self.frame_max_ms_shown));
            v.push(format!("{:.0} MIPS", self.mips));
            match (host_fps, refresh_hz) {
                (Some(h), Some(r)) => v.push(format!("disp {h:.0}/{r:.0} Hz")),
                (Some(h), None) => v.push(format!("disp {h:.0}")),
                (None, Some(r)) => v.push(format!("{r:.0} Hz")),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        v
    }
}

/// The overlay mod (installed by [`crate::install`]).
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct FpsMod {
    mode: FpsCounter,
    stats: FpsStats,
    seen_presents: u64,
}

/// Guest instructions retired so far (all threads).
fn total_instructions(m: &Machine) -> u64 {
    m.threads.iter().map(|t| t.cpu.instructions).sum::<u64>().max(m.stats.instructions)
}

impl Mod for FpsMod {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        "fps-counter"
    }

    fn tick(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, now_ms: u64) {
        self.mode = m.state::<ModsState>().borrow_mut().settings.display.fps_counter;
        if self.mode == FpsCounter::Off {
            self.stats = FpsStats::default();
            return;
        }
        let p = m.stats.presents;
        let i = total_instructions(m);
        self.stats.sample(now_ms, p, i);
    }

    fn wants_draw(&self) -> bool {
        self.mode != FpsCounter::Off
    }

    fn draw_window(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, c: &mut Layer, _frame: &FrameBuffer) {
        // In game only: not over the menus (user request 2026-11-08).
        if crate::draw_viewport(m).layout.is_some() || !crate::res::in_game_frame(m) {
            return;
        }
        let now = m.real_ms();
        let p = m.stats.presents;
        if p != self.seen_presents {
            self.seen_presents = p;
            self.stats.on_present(now);
        }
        let (host_fps, refresh) = {
            let st = m.state::<DisplayState>();
            let s = st.borrow_mut();
            (s.host_fps, s.refresh_hz)
        };
        let lines = self.stats.lines(self.mode, host_fps, refresh);
        let (vx, vy, vw, vh) = crate::draw_viewport(m).dst_rect_clipped();
        // Window pixels: 11 px at a 600 px high window (as it looked at a 600 px high frame shown full screen).
        let sk = c.ui().clamp(0.3, 4.0);
        let px = 11.0 * sk;
        let pad = (4.0 * sk).round().max(1.0) as i32;
        let lh = measure_text(px, Weight::Bold, "0").1.max(1);
        let w = lines.iter().map(|l| measure_text(px, Weight::Bold, l).0).max().unwrap_or(0) + 2 * pad;
        let h = lh * lines.len() as i32 + pad;
        // Position setting; Auto = top right, in the Mobile HUD top centre (its full-screen map "Close" and "Back to
        // HUD" sit top right). Never over the HUD's resource strip / bottom bar or the Classic panel.
        let hud = m.state::<crate::ModsState>().borrow_mut().settings.ui_mode == crate::settings::UiMode::MobileHud;
        let pos = crate::display::display_settings(m).fps_pos;
        let vp = crate::draw_viewport(m);
        let m2 = (2.0 * sk).round() as i32;
        let (bar, strip) = if hud { crate::ui_hud::bar_and_strip_h(m, vw, vh) } else { (0, 0) };
        // Left edge of the free area: right of the Classic panel (incl. the minimap frame's edge at the top).
        let left = match vp.panel {
            Some(p) => vp.game_to_window(p.art_right(0.0).max(p.w as f32) - 1.0, 0.0).0.round() as i32 + m2,
            None => vx + m2,
        };
        use crate::display::FpsPos as P;
        let pos = if pos == P::Auto { if hud { P::TopCenter } else { P::TopRight } } else { pos };
        let x = match pos {
            P::TopLeft | P::BottomLeft => left,
            // Centered on the whole window (not on the part right of the Classic panel).
            P::TopCenter | P::BottomCenter => vx + (vw - w) / 2,
            _ => (vx + vw - w - m2).max(left),
        };
        let y = match pos {
            P::TopLeft if hud => vy + strip + m2,
            P::BottomLeft | P::BottomCenter | P::BottomRight => vy + vh - bar - h - m2,
            _ => vy + m2,
        };
        c.fill_rect(x, y, w, h, Rgba::rgba(0, 0, 0, 150));
        let color = if !self.stats.have || self.stats.fps >= 55.0 {
            Rgba::rgb(140, 255, 140)
        } else if self.stats.fps >= 30.0 {
            Rgba::rgb(255, 230, 110)
        } else {
            Rgba::rgb(255, 130, 110)
        };
        for (k, l) in lines.iter().enumerate() {
            c.text(x + pad, y + pad / 2 + k as i32 * lh, px, Weight::Bold, if k == 0 { color } else { Rgba::WHITE }, l);
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn window_rates() {
        let mut s = FpsStats::default();
        s.sample(1000, 10, 1_000_000);
        for k in 0..31 {
            s.on_present(1000 + k * 16);
        }
        s.sample(1200, 20, 2_000_000);
        assert!(!s.have, "window not finished yet");
        s.sample(1500, 40, 51_000_000);
        assert!(s.have);
        assert!((s.fps - 60.0).abs() < 0.01, "{}", s.fps);
        assert!((s.mips - 100.0).abs() < 0.01, "{}", s.mips);
        assert!((s.frame_avg_ms - 16.0).abs() < 0.01);
        assert_eq!(s.frame_max_ms_shown, 16);
        assert_eq!(s.lines(FpsCounter::Fps, None, None), vec!["60 fps".to_string()]);
        let d = s.lines(FpsCounter::Detailed, Some(120.0), Some(120.0));
        assert_eq!(d.len(), 4);
        assert_eq!(d[2], "100 MIPS");
        assert_eq!(d[3], "disp 120/120 Hz");
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/game_time.rs`:

```rs
//! Game time display (user request 2026-11-08, like Settlers United): `h:mm:ss` of the running game, on by default,
//! switched in the menus (Classic floating menu column, Mobile HUD settings).
//!
//! Source: the game's own clock `[0x7dfd48]` (logic ticks of 64 ms; what its T-key clock prints, docs/reverse-engineering/
//! game-state-ui.md "What is drawn as text over the map"), so it follows game speed, pauses and saved games.
//! Drawn in the window layer: Classic top centre of the map part; Mobile HUD below its resource strip (top right
//! when the FPS counter sits top left).

use s3_runtime::Machine;

use s3_runtime::FrameBuffer;
use crate::layer::Layer;
use crate::overlay::{measure_text, Rgba, Weight};
use crate::Mod;

/// Game clock in logic ticks of 64 ms (15.6 per s at 1x). Verified 2026-11-08: 838 ticks -> the game's own
/// T-key clock showed 00:00:53.
const GAME_CLOCK_TICKS: u32 = 0x007d_fd48;
const TICK_MS: u64 = 64;

/// Game time in ms (0 outside a game).
pub fn game_ms(m: &mut Machine) -> u64 {
    if !crate::res::in_game_frame(m) {
        return 0;
    }
    m.mem.read_u32(GAME_CLOCK_TICKS) as u64 * TICK_MS
}

/// `h:mm:ss`.
pub fn format(ms: u64) -> String {
    let s = ms / 1000;
    format!("{}:{:02}:{:02}", s / 3600, s / 60 % 60, s % 60)
}

/// Is the display switched on?
pub fn enabled(m: &mut Machine) -> bool {
    crate::settings(m).show_game_time
}

/// Menu toggle; returns the new state.
pub fn toggle(m: &mut Machine) -> bool {
    let mut s = crate::settings(m);
    s.show_game_time = !s.show_game_time;
    let on = s.show_game_time;
    let _ = crate::set_settings(m, s);
    on
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct GameTimeMod {
    on: bool,
    shown: String,
}

impl Mod for GameTimeMod {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        "game-time"
    }

    fn tick(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, _now: u64) {
        self.on = m.state::<crate::ModsState>().borrow_mut().settings.show_game_time;
    }

    fn wants_draw(&self) -> bool {
        self.on
    }

    fn draw_window(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, c: &mut Layer, _frame: &FrameBuffer) {
        if crate::draw_viewport(m).layout.is_some() || !crate::res::in_game_frame(m) {
            return;
        }
        self.shown = format(game_ms(m));
        let vp = crate::draw_viewport(m);
        let (vx, vy, vw, vh) = vp.dst_rect_clipped();
        let sk = c.ui().clamp(0.3, 4.0);
        let px = 13.0 * sk;
        let pad = (4.0 * sk).round().max(1.0) as i32;
        let m2 = (3.0 * sk).round() as i32;
        let (tw, th) = measure_text(px, Weight::Bold, &self.shown);
        let (w, h) = (tw + 2 * pad, th + pad);
        let hud = crate::settings(m).ui_mode == crate::settings::UiMode::MobileHud;
        let (_, strip) = if hud { crate::ui_hud::bar_and_strip_h(m, vw, vh) } else { (0, 0) };
        let left = match vp.panel {
            Some(p) => vp.game_to_window(p.art_right(0.0).max(p.w as f32) - 1.0, 0.0).0.round() as i32 + m2,
            None => vx + m2,
        };
        let d = crate::display::display_settings(m);
        let fps_top_left = d.fps_counter != crate::display::FpsCounter::Off && d.fps_pos == crate::display::FpsPos::TopLeft;
        let fps_top_center = d.fps_counter != crate::display::FpsCounter::Off && d.fps_pos == crate::display::FpsPos::TopCenter;
        // Classic: top centre of the map part (its selection chip sits top left, Deselect top right); HUD: below
        // the resource strip. Away from the FPS counter when it is placed there.
        let (x, y) = if hud {
            if fps_top_left { (vx + vw - w - m2, vy + m2) } else { (left, vy + strip + m2) }
        } else if fps_top_center {
            (left, vy + (40.0 * sk) as i32)
        } else {
            (left + (vx + vw - left - w) / 2, vy + m2)
        };
        c.fill_rounded_rect(x, y, w, h, 5.0 * sk, Rgba::rgba(0, 0, 0, 140));
        c.text(x + pad, y + pad / 2, px, Weight::Bold, Rgba::rgb(240, 225, 170), &self.shown);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    #[test]
    fn formats() {
        assert_eq!(super::format(0), "0:00:00");
        assert_eq!(super::format(3_723_000), "1:02:03");
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/gesture.rs`:

```rs
//! Touch gesture recognizer (pure Rust, no machine access) shared by every frontend: frontends deliver raw
//! pointer events only ([`s3_runtime::HostEvent::Pointer`]); this turns them into [`TouchEvent`]s.
//!
//! Recognized (coordinates are game-screen pixels, `f32`):
//! - raw `Down` / `Move` / `Up` / `Cancel` per pointer id (always emitted first);
//! - `Tap` (one finger, < `tap_max_ms`, moved < `tap_slop`), plus `DoubleTap` when a second tap lands within
//!   `double_tap_ms` and `double_tap_slop` of the first (the second `Tap` is emitted too, so taps never wait);
//! - `LongPress` (one finger held >= `long_press_ms` without moving; fired from [`GestureRecognizer::tick`]);
//! - `Pan` with phases (one finger after it moved beyond the slop; `after_long_press` marks a long-press-drag;
//!   two fingers move together = `fingers: 2`);
//! - `Pinch` with phases (two fingers; `scale` = current distance / start distance);
//! - `TwoFingerTap` / `ThreeFingerTap` (all fingers lifted without moving, quickly).

/// Gesture phase.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Phase {
    Begin,
    Update,
    End,
}

/// High-level touch event delivered to mods (and then to the touch->mouse fallback).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub enum TouchEvent {
    Down { id: u32, x: f32, y: f32 },
    Move { id: u32, x: f32, y: f32 },
    Up { id: u32, x: f32, y: f32 },
    Cancel { id: u32 },
    Tap { x: f32, y: f32 },
    DoubleTap { x: f32, y: f32 },
    LongPress { x: f32, y: f32 },
    TwoFingerTap { x: f32, y: f32 },
    ThreeFingerTap { x: f32, y: f32 },
    /// `x, y` current position (centroid for two fingers), `dx, dy` delta since the previous Pan event,
    /// `start_x, start_y` where the gesture started.
    Pan { phase: Phase, fingers: u8, x: f32, y: f32, dx: f32, dy: f32, start_x: f32, start_y: f32, after_long_press: bool },
    /// `cx, cy` centroid, `scale` relative to the distance when the pinch began.
    Pinch { phase: Phase, cx: f32, cy: f32, scale: f32 },
}

impl TouchEvent {
    /// Is this a raw per-pointer event (Down/Move/Up/Cancel)?
    pub fn is_raw(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, TouchEvent::Down { .. } | TouchEvent::Move { .. } | TouchEvent::Up { .. } | TouchEvent::Cancel { .. })
    }
}

/// Thresholds.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub struct GestureConfig {
    pub long_press_ms: u64,
    pub tap_max_ms: u64,
    pub tap_slop: f32,
    pub double_tap_ms: u64,
    pub double_tap_slop: f32,
    /// Max duration of a two/three-finger tap.
    pub multi_tap_max_ms: u64,
}

impl Default for GestureConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        GestureConfig { long_press_ms: crate::settings::LONG_PRESS_MS, tap_max_ms: 500, tap_slop: 8.0, double_tap_ms: 300, double_tap_slop: 24.0, multi_tap_max_ms: 500 }
    }
}

impl From<&crate::settings::TouchSettings> for GestureConfig {
    fn from(t: &crate::settings::TouchSettings) -> Self {
        GestureConfig {
            long_press_ms: t.long_press_ms,
            tap_max_ms: t.tap_max_ms,
            tap_slop: t.tap_slop,
            double_tap_ms: t.double_tap_ms,
            double_tap_slop: t.double_tap_slop,
            ..GestureConfig::default()
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
struct Finger {
    id: u32,
    x: f32,
    y: f32,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
enum Mode {
    Idle,
    Single { x0: f32, y0: f32, t0: u64, panning: bool, long_fired: bool, last: (f32, f32) },
    Multi { max: u8, t0: u64, c0: (f32, f32), d0: f32, transforming: bool, last_c: (f32, f32) },
    /// Gesture over (or cancelled); ignore until all fingers are up.
    Ended,
}

pub struct GestureRecognizer {
    pub cfg: GestureConfig,
    fingers: Vec<Finger>,
    mode: Mode,
    /// Time and place of the last single tap (for DoubleTap).
    last_tap: Option<(u64, f32, f32)>,
    /// The current one-finger touch went down quickly after a tap near it (tap, then press-and-drag): dragging
    /// it starts a box selection at once, like a drag after a long press (user request 2026-11-08).
    double_drag: bool,
}

fn dist(a: (f32, f32), b: (f32, f32)) -> f32 {
    ((a.0 - b.0).powi(2) + (a.1 - b.1).powi(2)).sqrt()
}

impl GestureRecognizer {
    pub fn new(cfg: GestureConfig) -> Self {
        GestureRecognizer { cfg, fingers: Vec::new(), mode: Mode::Idle, last_tap: None, double_drag: false }
    }

    /// Number of fingers down.
    pub fn fingers(&self) -> usize {
        self.fingers.len()
    }

    fn centroid(&self) -> (f32, f32) {
        let n = self.fingers.len().max(1) as f32;
        let (sx, sy) = self.fingers.iter().fold((0.0, 0.0), |a, f| (a.0 + f.x, a.1 + f.y));
        (sx / n, sy / n)
    }

    fn spread(&self) -> f32 {
        if self.fingers.len() < 2 {
            return 0.0;
        }
        dist((self.fingers[0].x, self.fingers[0].y), (self.fingers[1].x, self.fingers[1].y))
    }

    /// End a running transform (pan/pinch) and push the End events.
    fn end_active(&mut self, out: &mut Vec<TouchEvent>) {
        match self.mode {
            Mode::Single { x0, y0, panning: true, long_fired, last, .. } => out.push(TouchEvent::Pan {
                phase: Phase::End,
                fingers: 1,
                x: last.0,
                y: last.1,
                dx: 0.0,
                dy: 0.0,
                start_x: x0,
                start_y: y0,
                after_long_press: long_fired,
            }),
            Mode::Multi { transforming: true, c0, last_c, .. } => {
                let scale = self.pinch_scale();
                out.push(TouchEvent::Pinch { phase: Phase::End, cx: last_c.0, cy: last_c.1, scale });
                out.push(TouchEvent::Pan {
                    phase: Phase::End,
                    fingers: 2,
                    x: last_c.0,
                    y: last_c.1,
                    dx: 0.0,
                    dy: 0.0,
                    start_x: c0.0,
                    start_y: c0.1,
                    after_long_press: false,
                });
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    fn pinch_scale(&self) -> f32 {
        match self.mode {
            Mode::Multi { d0, .. } if d0 > 0.0 && self.fingers.len() >= 2 => self.spread() / d0,
            _ => 1.0,
        }
    }

    fn enter_multi(&mut self, t: u64, max: u8) {
        let t0 = match self.mode {
            Mode::Single { t0, .. } | Mode::Multi { t0, .. } => t0,
            _ => t,
        };
        let c = self.centroid();
        self.mode = Mode::Multi { max, t0, c0: c, d0: self.spread(), transforming: false, last_c: c };
    }

    /// A finger touched down.
    pub fn down(&mut self, id: u32, x: f32, y: f32, t: u64, out: &mut Vec<TouchEvent>) {
        self.fingers.retain(|f| f.id != id);
        self.fingers.push(Finger { id, x, y });
        out.push(TouchEvent::Down { id, x, y });
        match (self.mode, self.fingers.len()) {
            (Mode::Idle, 1) => {
                self.double_drag = self.last_tap.is_some_and(|(lt, lx, ly)| {
                    t.saturating_sub(lt) <= self.cfg.double_tap_ms && dist((lx, ly), (x, y)) <= self.cfg.double_tap_slop * 2.0
                });
                self.mode = Mode::Single { x0: x, y0: y, t0: t, panning: false, long_fired: false, last: (x, y) }
            }
            (Mode::Single { panning, long_fired, .. }, 2) => {
                if panning || long_fired {
                    // A finger joined a running one-finger gesture: end it, then ignore the rest.
                    self.end_active(out);
                    self.mode = Mode::Ended;
                } else {
                    self.enter_multi(t, 2);
                }
            }
            (Mode::Multi { transforming: false, .. }, n) if n >= 2 => self.enter_multi(t, n.min(3) as u8),
            (Mode::Multi { transforming: true, .. }, _) => {
                self.end_active(out);
                self.mode = Mode::Ended;
            }
            (Mode::Ended, _) | (Mode::Idle, _) => {
                if self.mode == Mode::Idle {
                    self.mode = Mode::Ended;
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    /// A finger moved.
    pub fn moved(&mut self, id: u32, x: f32, y: f32, _t: u64, out: &mut Vec<TouchEvent>) {
        let Some(f) = self.fingers.iter_mut().find(|f| f.id == id) else { return };
        if f.x == x && f.y == y {
            return;
        }
        f.x = x;
        f.y = y;
        out.push(TouchEvent::Move { id, x, y });
        let slop = self.cfg.tap_slop;
        match self.mode {
            Mode::Single { x0, y0, t0, panning, long_fired, last } => {
                if !panning {
                    if dist((x, y), (x0, y0)) > slop {
                        // Tap, then press-and-drag: a box selection like after a long press.
                        let long_fired = if !long_fired && self.double_drag {
                            self.last_tap = None;
                            out.push(TouchEvent::LongPress { x: x0, y: y0 });
                            true
                        } else {
                            long_fired
                        };
                        out.push(TouchEvent::Pan {
                            phase: Phase::Begin,
                            fingers: 1,
                            x,
                            y,
                            dx: x - x0,
                            dy: y - y0,
                            start_x: x0,
                            start_y: y0,
                            after_long_press: long_fired,
                        });
                        self.mode = Mode::Single { x0, y0, t0, panning: true, long_fired, last: (x, y) };
                    }
                } else {
                    out.push(TouchEvent::Pan {
                        phase: Phase::Update,
                        fingers: 1,
                        x,
                        y,
                        dx: x - last.0,
                        dy: y - last.1,
                        start_x: x0,
                        start_y: y0,
                        after_long_press: long_fired,
                    });
                    self.mode = Mode::Single { x0, y0, t0, panning, long_fired, last: (x, y) };
                }
            }
            Mode::Multi { max: 2, t0, c0, d0, transforming, last_c } if self.fingers.len() == 2 => {
                let c = self.centroid();
                let d = self.spread();
                let phase = if transforming {
                    Phase::Update
                } else if dist(c, c0) > slop || (d - d0).abs() > slop {
                    Phase::Begin
                } else {
                    return;
                };
                let scale = if d0 > 0.0 { d / d0 } else { 1.0 };
                out.push(TouchEvent::Pinch { phase, cx: c.0, cy: c.1, scale });
                let (dx, dy) = if phase == Phase::Begin { (c.0 - c0.0, c.1 - c0.1) } else { (c.0 - last_c.0, c.1 - last_c.1) };
                out.push(TouchEvent::Pan { phase, fingers: 2, x: c.0, y: c.1, dx, dy, start_x: c0.0, start_y: c0.1, after_long_press: false });
                self.mode = Mode::Multi { max: 2, t0, c0, d0, transforming: true, last_c: c };
            }
            Mode::Multi { max: 3, c0, .. } => {
                // Three fingers moving: not a tap any more.
                if dist(self.centroid(), c0) > slop {
                    self.mode = Mode::Ended;
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    /// A finger lifted.
    pub fn up(&mut self, id: u32, x: f32, y: f32, t: u64, out: &mut Vec<TouchEvent>) {
        if !self.fingers.iter().any(|f| f.id == id) {
            return;
        }
        self.moved(id, x, y, t, out);
        out.push(TouchEvent::Up { id, x, y });
        match self.mode {
            Mode::Single { x0, y0, t0, panning, long_fired, .. } => {
                if panning {
                    self.end_active(out);
                } else if !long_fired && t.saturating_sub(t0) <= self.cfg.tap_max_ms {
                    out.push(TouchEvent::Tap { x: x0, y: y0 });
                    match self.last_tap {
                        Some((lt, lx, ly))
                            if t.saturating_sub(lt) <= self.cfg.double_tap_ms
                                && dist((lx, ly), (x0, y0)) <= self.cfg.double_tap_slop =>
                        {
                            out.push(TouchEvent::DoubleTap { x: x0, y: y0 });
                            self.last_tap = None;
                        }
                        _ => self.last_tap = Some((t, x0, y0)),
                    }
                }
                self.mode = Mode::Ended;
            }
            Mode::Multi { max, t0, transforming, .. } => {
                if transforming {
                    self.end_active(out);
                } else if t.saturating_sub(t0) <= self.cfg.multi_tap_max_ms {
                    let c = self.centroid();
                    out.push(if max >= 3 { TouchEvent::ThreeFingerTap { x: c.0, y: c.1 } } else { TouchEvent::TwoFingerTap { x: c.0, y: c.1 } });
                }
                self.mode = Mode::Ended;
            }
            _ => {}
        }
        self.fingers.retain(|f| f.id != id);
        if self.fingers.is_empty() {
            self.mode = Mode::Idle;
        }
    }

    /// The platform cancelled a pointer.
    pub fn cancel(&mut self, id: u32, out: &mut Vec<TouchEvent>) {
        if !self.fingers.iter().any(|f| f.id == id) {
            return;
        }
        out.push(TouchEvent::Cancel { id });
        self.end_active(out);
        self.mode = Mode::Ended;
        self.fingers.retain(|f| f.id != id);
        if self.fingers.is_empty() {
            self.mode = Mode::Idle;
        }
    }

    /// Time-based gestures (long press). Call regularly (each scheduler slice).
    pub fn tick(&mut self, t: u64, out: &mut Vec<TouchEvent>) {
        if let Mode::Single { x0, y0, t0, panning: false, long_fired: false, last } = self.mode {
            if t.saturating_sub(t0) >= self.cfg.long_press_ms {
                out.push(TouchEvent::LongPress { x: x0, y: y0 });
                self.mode = Mode::Single { x0, y0, t0, panning: false, long_fired: true, last };
            }
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn rec() -> GestureRecognizer {
        GestureRecognizer::new(GestureConfig::default())
    }

    fn high(v: &[TouchEvent]) -> Vec<TouchEvent> {
        v.iter().copied().filter(|e| !e.is_raw()).collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn tap_then_drag_is_box_select() {
        let mut g = GestureRecognizer::new(GestureConfig::default());
        let mut o = Vec::new();
        g.down(1, 100.0, 100.0, 0, &mut o);
        g.up(1, 100.0, 100.0, 80, &mut o);
        o.clear();
        g.down(2, 104.0, 100.0, 200, &mut o);
        g.moved(2, 160.0, 140.0, 260, &mut o);
        assert!(o.iter().any(|e| matches!(e, TouchEvent::LongPress { .. })));
        assert!(o.iter().any(|e| matches!(e, TouchEvent::Pan { phase: Phase::Begin, after_long_press: true, .. })));
        // A plain drag (no tap before) stays a camera pan.
        let mut g = GestureRecognizer::new(GestureConfig::default());
        let mut o = Vec::new();
        g.down(1, 100.0, 100.0, 0, &mut o);
        g.moved(1, 160.0, 140.0, 60, &mut o);
        assert!(o.iter().any(|e| matches!(e, TouchEvent::Pan { phase: Phase::Begin, after_long_press: false, .. })));
    }

    #[test]
    fn tap_and_double_tap() {
        let mut g = rec();
        let mut o = Vec::new();
        g.down(1, 100.0, 100.0, 0, &mut o);
        g.tick(50, &mut o);
        g.up(1, 102.0, 101.0, 80, &mut o);
        assert_eq!(high(&o), vec![TouchEvent::Tap { x: 100.0, y: 100.0 }]);
        o.clear();
        g.down(2, 105.0, 100.0, 200, &mut o);
        g.up(2, 105.0, 100.0, 260, &mut o);
        assert_eq!(high(&o), vec![TouchEvent::Tap { x: 105.0, y: 100.0 }, TouchEvent::DoubleTap { x: 105.0, y: 100.0 }]);
        // Third tap starts a new pair.
        o.clear();
        g.down(3, 105.0, 100.0, 400, &mut o);
        g.up(3, 105.0, 100.0, 450, &mut o);
        assert_eq!(high(&o), vec![TouchEvent::Tap { x: 105.0, y: 100.0 }]);
        // Too slow for a tap.
        o.clear();
        g.down(4, 10.0, 10.0, 2000, &mut o);
        g.up(4, 10.0, 10.0, 2000 + 501, &mut o);
        assert!(high(&o).is_empty(), "{o:?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn long_press_then_drag() {
        let mut g = rec();
        let mut o = Vec::new();
        g.down(1, 50.0, 60.0, 1000, &mut o);
        g.tick(1000 + crate::settings::LONG_PRESS_MS - 1, &mut o);
        assert!(high(&o).is_empty());
        g.tick(1000 + crate::settings::LONG_PRESS_MS, &mut o);
        g.tick(1600, &mut o);
        assert_eq!(high(&o), vec![TouchEvent::LongPress { x: 50.0, y: 60.0 }]);
        o.clear();
        g.moved(1, 80.0, 60.0, 1700, &mut o);
        g.moved(1, 90.0, 70.0, 1716, &mut o);
        g.up(1, 90.0, 70.0, 1730, &mut o);
        let h = high(&o);
        assert_eq!(h.len(), 3, "{h:?}");
        assert!(matches!(h[0], TouchEvent::Pan { phase: Phase::Begin, fingers: 1, after_long_press: true, dx, .. } if dx == 30.0));
        assert!(matches!(h[1], TouchEvent::Pan { phase: Phase::Update, dx, dy, .. } if dx == 10.0 && dy == 10.0));
        assert!(matches!(h[2], TouchEvent::Pan { phase: Phase::End, .. }));
    }

    #[test]
    fn pan_within_slop_is_tap() {
        let mut g = rec();
        let mut o = Vec::new();
        g.down(1, 0.0, 0.0, 0, &mut o);
        g.moved(1, 5.0, 5.0, 20, &mut o); // 7.07 < 8
        g.up(1, 5.0, 5.0, 40, &mut o);
        assert_eq!(high(&o), vec![TouchEvent::Tap { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }]);
        // Raw events are all there.
        assert!(matches!(o[0], TouchEvent::Down { id: 1, .. }));
        assert!(matches!(o[1], TouchEvent::Move { id: 1, .. }));
    }

    #[test]
    fn pinch_and_two_finger_pan() {
        let mut g = rec();
        let mut o = Vec::new();
        g.down(1, 100.0, 100.0, 0, &mut o);
        g.down(2, 200.0, 100.0, 10, &mut o);
        g.moved(1, 50.0, 100.0, 30, &mut o);
        g.moved(2, 250.0, 100.0, 30, &mut o);
        g.up(1, 50.0, 100.0, 60, &mut o);
        g.up(2, 250.0, 100.0, 70, &mut o);
        let h = high(&o);
        let pinches: Vec<_> = h.iter().filter_map(|e| if let TouchEvent::Pinch { phase, scale, .. } = e { Some((*phase, *scale)) } else { None }).collect();
        assert_eq!(pinches.first().unwrap().0, Phase::Begin);
        assert_eq!(pinches.last().unwrap(), &(Phase::End, 2.0), "{pinches:?}");
        assert!(pinches.iter().any(|(_, s)| (*s - 2.0).abs() < 1e-4), "{pinches:?}");
        assert!(!h.iter().any(|e| matches!(e, TouchEvent::Tap { .. } | TouchEvent::TwoFingerTap { .. })));
        assert!(h.iter().any(|e| matches!(e, TouchEvent::Pan { fingers: 2, phase: Phase::End, .. })));
    }

    #[test]
    fn two_and_three_finger_taps() {
        let mut g = rec();
        let mut o = Vec::new();
        g.down(1, 100.0, 100.0, 0, &mut o);
        g.down(2, 140.0, 100.0, 20, &mut o);
        g.up(2, 140.0, 100.0, 100, &mut o);
        g.up(1, 100.0, 100.0, 110, &mut o);
        assert_eq!(high(&o), vec![TouchEvent::TwoFingerTap { x: 120.0, y: 100.0 }]);
        o.clear();
        g.down(1, 0.0, 0.0, 1000, &mut o);
        g.down(2, 30.0, 0.0, 1010, &mut o);
        g.down(3, 60.0, 0.0, 1020, &mut o);
        g.up(3, 60.0, 0.0, 1100, &mut o);
        g.up(2, 30.0, 0.0, 1100, &mut o);
        g.up(1, 0.0, 0.0, 1100, &mut o);
        assert_eq!(high(&o), vec![TouchEvent::ThreeFingerTap { x: 30.0, y: 0.0 }]);
        assert_eq!(g.fingers(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn second_finger_ends_one_finger_pan_and_cancel() {
        let mut g = rec();
        let mut o = Vec::new();
        g.down(1, 0.0, 0.0, 0, &mut o);
        g.moved(1, 40.0, 0.0, 20, &mut o);
        g.down(2, 100.0, 0.0, 30, &mut o);
        g.moved(2, 150.0, 0.0, 40, &mut o);
        g.up(2, 150.0, 0.0, 50, &mut o);
        g.up(1, 40.0, 0.0, 60, &mut o);
        let h = high(&o);
        assert_eq!(h.len(), 2, "{h:?}");
        assert!(matches!(h[1], TouchEvent::Pan { phase: Phase::End, fingers: 1, .. }));
        o.clear();
        g.down(5, 0.0, 0.0, 100, &mut o);
        g.moved(5, 30.0, 0.0, 120, &mut o);
        g.cancel(5, &mut o);
        let h = high(&o);
        assert!(matches!(h.last(), Some(TouchEvent::Pan { phase: Phase::End, .. })));
        assert_eq!(g.fingers(), 0);
        // Next touch works normally.
        o.clear();
        g.down(6, 1.0, 1.0, 1000, &mut o);
        g.up(6, 1.0, 1.0, 1010, &mut o);
        assert_eq!(high(&o), vec![TouchEvent::Tap { x: 1.0, y: 1.0 }]);
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/haptics.rs`:

```rs
//! Vibration requests (user request 2026-11-08): a short buzz on long presses (box select start, group assign)
//! and on game messages / notifications, each switchable in the menus (`Settings::vibrate_touch`,
//! `Settings::vibrate_messages`). The mods only queue durations; the Android frontend drains the queue and
//! calls the system Vibrator (desktop ignores it).

use std::sync::Mutex;

use s3_runtime::Machine;

static QUEUE: Mutex<Vec<u32>> = Mutex::new(Vec::new());

/// Touch feedback buzz (long press recognised, box selection starts, group assigned).
pub const TOUCH_MS: u32 = 25;
/// Game message buzz.
pub const MESSAGE_MS: u32 = 60;

fn push(ms: u32) {
    let mut q = QUEUE.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
    if q.len() < 8 {
        q.push(ms);
    }
}

/// Touch feedback, if switched on.
pub fn touch(m: &mut Machine) {
    if crate::settings(m).vibrate_touch {
        push(TOUCH_MS);
    }
}

/// Game message feedback, if switched on.
pub fn message(m: &mut Machine) {
    if crate::settings(m).vibrate_messages {
        push(MESSAGE_MS);
    }
}

/// Drain the queued vibration durations (ms), oldest first.
pub fn take() -> Vec<u32> {
    QUEUE.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner()).drain(..).collect()
}
```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/hooks.rs`:

```rs
//! Guest-address hooks.
//!
//! A hook runs host code when a guest thread's EIP reaches an address (function entry or any instruction,
//! e.g. a call site), *before* that instruction executes. The CPU splits decoded blocks so a hooked address
//! always starts a block; when no hook is installed the cost is one flag test per executed block.
//!
//! In a hook ([`HookCtx`]) you can read/write registers and memory, call guest functions, and then
//! - continue with the original code ([`HookFlow::Continue`]),
//! - skip the original function and return a value ([`HookCtx::return_from_function`], function entry only),
//! - jump elsewhere ([`HookCtx::jump`]),
//! - get a post-call callback when the function returns ([`HookCtx::on_return`], function entry only): the
//!   return address on the stack is replaced by a trampoline thunk (`s3mods.dll!post_call_return`), which runs
//!   the callback with the function's EAX/EDX and then continues at the real return address.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::Arc;

use s3_cpu::{HookAddrs, EAX, ESP};
use s3_runtime::{HookFlow, LogLevel, Machine, ThunkResult};

use crate::ModsState;

/// A hook callback.
pub type HookFn = Arc<dyn Fn(&mut HookCtx) -> HookFlow + Send + Sync>;

/// A post-call callback (`EAX`/`EDX` of the returning function are in `ctx.m.cpu().regs`; it may change them).
pub type PostFn = Box<dyn FnOnce(&mut PostCtx) + Send>;

pub(crate) struct HookEntry {
    pub name: String,
    pub f: HookFn,
    pub hits: u64,
}

/// One pending post-call callback (per guest thread, LIFO).
pub(crate) struct PostFrame {
    /// ESP at function entry (pointing at the replaced return address).
    entry_esp: u32,
    ret_addr: u32,
    f: PostFn,
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct HookTable {
    pub by_addr: HashMap<u32, Vec<HookEntry>>,
    /// Hooks registered since the last [`commit`].
    pub dirty: bool,
    /// Pending post-call frames by guest thread id.
    pub post: HashMap<u32, Vec<PostFrame>>,
    /// Address of the `s3mods.dll!post_call_return` thunk (0 until installed).
    pub trampoline: u32,
    /// Host nanoseconds spent in hook callbacks (benchmarking).
    pub ns: u64,
}

/// Context passed to a hook.
pub struct HookCtx<'a> {
    pub m: &'a mut Machine,
    /// The hooked address (= EIP).
    pub eip: u32,
}

impl HookCtx<'_> {
    pub fn reg(&mut self, r: usize) -> u32 {
        self.m.cpu().regs[r]
    }
    pub fn set_reg(&mut self, r: usize, v: u32) {
        self.m.cpu().regs[r] = v;
    }
    pub fn esp(&mut self) -> u32 {
        self.m.cpu().regs[ESP]
    }
    /// `[esp + 4 + 4*i]`: argument `i` at a function entry (ESP points at the return address).
    pub fn arg(&mut self, i: u32) -> u32 {
        let esp = self.esp();
        self.m.mem.read_u32(esp.wrapping_add(4 + 4 * i))
    }
    /// Return address at a function entry.
    pub fn return_address(&mut self) -> u32 {
        let esp = self.esp();
        self.m.mem.read_u32(esp)
    }
    /// Skip the original function (call at its entry): EAX = `eax`, pop the return address and `stdcall_args`
    /// dwords (0 for cdecl/thiscall-without-args), continue at the caller. Return the result from the hook.
    pub fn return_from_function(&mut self, eax: u32, stdcall_args: u32) -> HookFlow {
        let m = &mut *self.m;
        let cpu = &mut m.threads[m.cur].cpu;
        let ret = cpu.pop32(&m.mem);
        cpu.regs[EAX] = eax;
        cpu.regs[ESP] = cpu.regs[ESP].wrapping_add(4 * stdcall_args);
        cpu.eip = ret;
        HookFlow::Redirected
    }
    /// Continue at another address (registers unchanged).
    pub fn jump(&mut self, addr: u32) -> HookFlow {
        self.m.cpu().eip = addr;
        HookFlow::Redirected
    }
    /// Run `f` when the function whose entry this is returns (call at a function entry only).
    pub fn on_return(&mut self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut PostCtx) + Send + 'static) {
        let st = self.m.state::<ModsState>();
        let mut s = st.borrow_mut();
        let tramp = s.hooks.trampoline;
        if tramp == 0 {
            drop(s);
            self.m.log(LogLevel::Warn, "mods: on_return without installed trampoline");
            return;
        }
        let tid = self.m.current_tid();
        let esp = self.m.threads[self.m.cur].cpu.regs[ESP];
        let ret_addr = self.m.mem.read_u32(esp);
        self.m.mem.write_u32(esp, tramp);
        s.hooks.post.entry(tid).or_default().push(PostFrame { entry_esp: esp, ret_addr, f: Box::new(f) });
    }
}

/// Context passed to a post-call callback.
pub struct PostCtx<'a> {
    pub m: &'a mut Machine,
    /// Return value (EAX) of the function; writes go back via [`PostCtx::set_eax`].
    pub eax: u32,
    /// Where the function returns to.
    pub ret_addr: u32,
}

impl PostCtx<'_> {
    pub fn set_eax(&mut self, v: u32) {
        self.eax = v;
        self.m.cpu().regs[EAX] = v;
    }
}

/// Register a hook at `addr`. Takes effect after [`commit`] (done automatically at the end of
/// `install` / patch-set application). Several hooks at one address run in registration order; the first
/// one that returns `Redirected` stops the chain.
pub fn add_hook(m: &mut Machine, addr: u32, name: &str, f: impl Fn(&mut HookCtx) -> HookFlow + Send + Sync + 'static) {
    let st = m.state::<ModsState>();
    let mut s = st.borrow_mut();
    s.hooks.by_addr.entry(addr).or_default().push(HookEntry { name: name.to_string(), f: Arc::new(f), hits: 0 });
    s.hooks.dirty = true;
}

/// Remove all hooks named `name`.
pub fn remove_hooks(m: &mut Machine, name: &str) {
    let st = m.state::<ModsState>();
    let mut s = st.borrow_mut();
    for v in s.hooks.by_addr.values_mut() {
        v.retain(|h| h.name != name);
    }
    s.hooks.by_addr.retain(|_, v| !v.is_empty());
    s.hooks.dirty = true;
}

/// Remove every hook (e.g. after a patch set failed half way).
pub fn remove_hooks_all(m: &mut Machine) {
    let st = m.state::<ModsState>();
    let mut s = st.borrow_mut();
    s.hooks.by_addr.clear();
    s.hooks.dirty = true;
    drop(s);
    st.borrow_mut().safe_points.clear();
}

/// Push the hook address set to every guest CPU (clears decode caches; cheap at load time, avoid per frame).
pub fn commit(m: &mut Machine) {
    let st = m.state::<ModsState>();
    let addrs: Option<HookAddrs> = {
        let mut s = st.borrow_mut();
        if !s.hooks.dirty {
            return;
        }
        s.hooks.dirty = false;
        Some(s.hooks.by_addr.keys().copied().collect())
    };
    m.set_hook_addrs(addrs);
    m.ext.hook_dispatch = Some(dispatch);
}

/// Hook statistics: (address, name, hits).
pub fn hook_stats(m: &mut Machine) -> Vec<(u32, String, u64)> {
    let st = m.state::<ModsState>();
    let s = st.borrow_mut();
    let mut v: Vec<_> =
        s.hooks.by_addr.iter().flat_map(|(a, hs)| hs.iter().map(move |h| (*a, h.name.clone(), h.hits))).collect();
    v.sort();
    v
}

/// Host time spent inside hook callbacks so far (ns).
pub fn hook_time_ns(m: &mut Machine) -> u64 {
    m.state::<ModsState>().borrow_mut().hooks.ns
}

/// `MachineExt::hook_dispatch` implementation.
pub(crate) fn dispatch(m: &mut Machine, eip: u32) -> HookFlow {
    let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
    let st = m.state::<ModsState>();
    let fs: Vec<HookFn> = {
        let mut s = st.borrow_mut();
        match s.hooks.by_addr.get_mut(&eip) {
            Some(v) => v.iter_mut().map(|h| {
                h.hits += 1;
                h.f.clone()
            }).collect(),
            None => Vec::new(),
        }
    };
    let mut flow = HookFlow::Continue;
    for f in fs {
        let mut ctx = HookCtx { m, eip };
        flow = f(&mut ctx);
        if flow == HookFlow::Redirected {
            break;
        }
    }
    // Deferred host->guest work runs at safe points.
    let safe = st.borrow_mut().safe_points.contains(&eip);
    if safe && flow == HookFlow::Continue {
        crate::run_deferred(m);
    }
    st.borrow_mut().hooks.ns += t0.elapsed().as_nanos() as u64;
    flow
}

/// `s3mods.dll!post_call_return`: a hooked function returned into the trampoline.
pub(crate) fn post_call_return(m: &mut Machine) -> ThunkResult {
    let tid = m.current_tid();
    let esp_now = m.threads[m.cur].cpu.regs[ESP];
    let st = m.state::<ModsState>();
    let frame = {
        let mut s = st.borrow_mut();
        let Some(stack) = s.hooks.post.get_mut(&tid) else {
            return ThunkResult::Error("mods: post_call_return without a pending frame".into());
        };
        // The returning frame is the newest one whose entry ESP lies below the current ESP; newer frames were
        // abandoned (exception unwinding) and are dropped.
        let mut found = None;
        while let Some(f) = stack.last() {
            if f.entry_esp < esp_now {
                found = stack.pop();
            } else {
                break;
            }
        }
        found
    };
    let Some(frame) = frame else {
        return ThunkResult::Error(format!("mods: post_call_return: no frame for esp {esp_now:#x}"));
    };
    let eax = m.cpu().regs[EAX];
    let mut ctx = PostCtx { m, eax, ret_addr: frame.ret_addr };
    (frame.f)(&mut ctx);
    m.cpu().eip = frame.ret_addr;
    ThunkResult::Done
}
```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/lan_autoselect.rs`:

```rs
//! LAN screen: select the (only) network provider automatically (user report 2026-11-08: New Game / Join Game
//! said "Before connecting, a provider has to be selected!"). Our DirectPlay HLE lists exactly one connection
//! ("Local network / Wi-Fi" or "Internet", docs/porting/multiplayer.md), so when the game's "Multi-player Game:
//! LAN" screen is shown (menu layout `lan-game` / `lan-game-full` detected) we click its first "Type of Network"
//! row once, like the player would. A popup over the screen (`lan-game+msg-box`) is left alone.

use s3_runtime::{Machine, MouseButton};

use crate::{Mod, ModsState};

/// First row of the "Type of Network" list (800x600 frame, list box 128..398 x 120..220).
const FIRST_PROVIDER_ROW: (i32, i32) = (200, 132);
/// Wait after the screen appeared (the list is filled when the screen opens).
const DELAY_MS: u64 = 700;

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct LanAutoSelect {
    since: u64,
    done: bool,
}

impl Mod for LanAutoSelect {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        "lan-autoselect"
    }

    fn tick(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, now: u64) {
        let on_lan = crate::draw_viewport(m).layout.is_some_and(|l| l.name == "lan-game" || l.name == "lan-game-full");
        if !on_lan {
            // A popup ("+msg-box") keeps the visit going; leaving the screen resets it.
            let popup = crate::draw_viewport(m).layout.is_some_and(|l| l.name.starts_with("lan-game+"));
            if !popup {
                self.since = 0;
                self.done = false;
            }
            return;
        }
        if self.since == 0 {
            self.since = now.max(1);
        }
        if !self.done && now.saturating_sub(self.since) >= DELAY_MS {
            self.done = true;
            m.state::<ModsState>().borrow_mut().fallback.click(now, FIRST_PROVIDER_ROW, MouseButton::Left);
        }
    }
}
```
