`port/crates/s3-mods/src/patchset.rs`:

```rs
//! Per-exe patch sets. A patch set (hooks + byte patches) is applied only when the S3.EXE sha256 matches;
//! any other exe runs unpatched (logged). The generic framework (input gestures, overlay, settings) is
//! exe-independent and always active.

use s3_runtime::{HookFlow, LogLevel, Machine};

use crate::hooks;

/// GOG "Ultimate Collection" S3.EXE (docs/game-files/inventory.md).
pub const GOG_SHA256: &str = "00a925cfdcfc3349b5d0f3b8a4c312f01b813e363b4464f6f3d6de17804d950b";

/// A named set of patches for one exact exe build.
pub struct PatchSet {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub exe_sha256: &'static str,
    pub apply: fn(&mut Machine) -> Result<(), String>,
}

/// Patch sets shipped with the port. W2/W3/W4 add their hooks to the GOG set (or add sets).
pub fn builtin() -> Vec<PatchSet> {
    vec![PatchSet { name: "gog-base", exe_sha256: GOG_SHA256, apply: gog_base }]
}

/// Patch set for `sha256`, if any.
pub fn find(sha256: &str) -> Option<PatchSet> {
    builtin().into_iter().find(|p| p.exe_sha256.eq_ignore_ascii_case(sha256))
}

/// Write `new` at `addr` after checking the original bytes are `expect` (guards against wrong exe/offsets).
/// Invalidates decoded code in every thread.
pub fn patch_bytes(m: &mut Machine, addr: u32, expect: &[u8], new: &[u8]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let cur = m.mem.read_bytes(addr, expect.len());
    if cur != expect {
        return Err(format!("patch at {addr:#x}: expected {expect:02x?}, found {cur:02x?}"));
    }
    m.mem.write_bytes(addr, new);
    m.invalidate_code(addr, new.len().max(expect.len()) as u32);
    Ok(())
}

/// GOG S3.EXE main-thread message-loop functions (docs/reverse-engineering/static-startup.md §3), used as
/// safe points for deferred host->guest calls:
/// - `0x60d9e0` "message waiting?" test, called once per iteration of `Run` (`0x404860`);
/// - `0x60d740` one GetMessage/Translate/Dispatch step.
/// HYPOTHESIS: both run only on the main thread, between game-logic steps; verified only by hit counts.
pub const GOG_SAFE_POINTS: [u32; 2] = [0x0060_d9e0, 0x0060_d740];

fn gog_base(m: &mut Machine) -> Result<(), String> {
    // Sanity: the hooked addresses must hold code (first bytes of these functions, from the GOG exe).
    for a in GOG_SAFE_POINTS {
        if m.mem.read_bytes(a, 4).iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
            return Err(format!("gog-base: no code at {a:#x}"));
        }
    }
    for a in GOG_SAFE_POINTS {
        hooks::add_hook(m, a, "gog-base:safe-point", |_| HookFlow::Continue);
        crate::add_safe_point(m, a);
    }
    m.log(LogLevel::Info, "mods: gog-base: safe points 0x60d9e0, 0x60d740");
    // Camera clamp 0x51b4d0: the y limit `9*W + 0x176 - mapW` uses the map view WIDTH (game bug, harmless at
    // 640/800 px). With our wide custom resolutions (~2000 px) it shrinks the y range, on small maps (tutorial) to
    // the top half or nothing. Use the view HEIGHT [0x730f1c] instead (docs/reverse-engineering/game-state-ui.md).
    // View-only state (camera), not simulation: lockstep MP is unaffected.
    patch_bytes(m, 0x0051_b528, &[0x8b, 0x3d, 0x18, 0x0f, 0x73, 0x00], &[0x8b, 0x3d, 0x1c, 0x0f, 0x73, 0x00])?;
    m.log(LogLevel::Info, "mods: gog-base: camera y clamp uses the view height (0x51b528)");
    Ok(())
}

```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/res.rs`:

```rs
//! Custom game resolutions for the GOG S3.EXE (res-zoom, docs/porting/resolution-zoom.md).
//!
//! The original game knows three layouts (640x480, 800x600, 1024x768; `0x4c6d70` / runtime switch `0x4c7490`).
//! This module lets the game run at any size `W x H` (`MIN_W..=MAX_W` x `MIN_H..=MAX_H`) while a game is running:
//!
//! - **Render snapshot grid** (`[logic+0x3d0]`, allocated once by `0x51f110`, size `0xc7720`): the logic thread
//!   copies the visible tiles into a grid of 130 rows x 130 columns (`snap+0x500`, 0x30 bytes per tile,
//!   index `row + col*130`). Because the map rows are sheared, a view needs `cols + rows/2` columns
//!   (`cols = (mapW+23)/16+10`, `rows = (mapH+255)/9+11`, `0x51f990..`); 1024x768 already uses 123 of 130.
//!   [`patch_snapshot`] moves the fields behind the grid (`0xc65c0..0xc7720`, 55 code sites listed in
//!   [`SNAP_TAIL_SITES`], generated by `tools/res-zoom/snap_sites.py` + 4 found by res-tall) so the grid gets
//!   [`SNAP_COLS`] columns, and changes the row stride 130 to [`SNAP_ROWS`] (res-tall, 2026-11-08): the ten
//!   `x*130` index computations ([`STRIDE_SHL_SITES`]), the column steps and neighbour displacements
//!   ([`STRIDE_DISP_SITES`], [`STRIDE_INDEX_SITES`]).
//! - **Sprite lists** of the frame renderer (`gfx+0x20c..`, buckets = 2 per snapshot row, 250 buckets): the
//!   bucket arrays move behind the `gfx` object (allocation `0x42c6b9` grows) and get [`SPRITE_BUCKETS`] entries
//!   ([`SPRITE_SITES`]); with 250 the objects of rows >= 125 were not drawn.
//! - **Landscape ring buffer** (`0x54bec0`) and **text DIB** (`0x4a78f0`) are sized once at game start (display
//!   setup `0x42e430`) from the screen; [`install`] makes them [`MAX_W`] x [`MAX_H`] so any later size fits (the
//!   F1-F3 switch never re-created them: the black band of the HUD after a runtime switch).
//! - **Mode set**: the game posts `0x804(index)` and `0x405c80` calls `SetDisplayMode` with 640/800/1024 constants;
//!   the call sites `0x405cc3` / `0x405cf2` get the custom size when `0x42ce90` was asked for a non-standard size.
//! - **Switch**: a hook at `0x4c7490` entry (render thread, once per in-game frame) does what the F1-F3 switch does
//!   with custom numbers: write the layout globals ([`write_layout`]), `0x42ce90(W, H, 16, 0, 0)` on `gfx`,
//!   `[0x7dfd44] = 0xfa` (the logic thread then forces a full landscape redraw and clamps the camera, `0x53db67`)
//!   and skips the frame.
//!
//! Panel art, minimap and panel grid keep the values of the "variant" (1..3 = the original layout whose height
//! fits, [`variant_for`]); the map view takes the rest of the screen. Nothing here touches simulation state (the
//! game itself supports different resolutions per multiplayer peer); see resolution-zoom.md for the MP check.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use s3_cpu::{ECX, ESP};
use s3_runtime::{HookFlow, LogLevel, Machine};

use crate::hooks::{self, HookCtx};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- limits

/// Largest width (game pixels; the snapshot grid needs `cols + rows/2 + 3 <= SNAP_COLS`).
pub const MAX_W: u32 = 3200;
/// Largest height (the snapshot grid rows `(H+255)/9 + 11 + 3` must stay below [`SNAP_ROWS`]; 1932 would fit, the
/// limit is the frame cost: 3200x1200 is 3.8 M pixels).
pub const MAX_H: u32 = 1200;
pub const MIN_W: u32 = 320;
pub const MIN_H: u32 = 200;
/// Columns of the enlarged snapshot grid (needs `cols + rows/2 + 3`; 3200x1200 needs 300).
pub const SNAP_COLS: u32 = 320;
/// Rows per grid column (row stride) after the patch; the game's is [`ORIG_ROWS`]. 258 because the index
/// computation `col*130` is `(col<<6 + col)*2` and `shl 7` makes it `col*258` without changing instruction lengths.
pub const SNAP_ROWS: u32 = 258;
pub const ORIG_ROWS: u32 = 130;
/// Sprite-list buckets after the patch (the game's 250; a view needs `2*rows + 4`, see [`sprite_buckets_needed`]).
pub const SPRITE_BUCKETS: u32 = 360;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- GOG addresses

pub const L_RES: u32 = 0x0073_0f08;
pub const L_SCREEN_W: u32 = 0x0073_0f0c;
pub const L_SCREEN_H: u32 = 0x0073_0f10;
pub const L_MAP_W: u32 = 0x0073_0f18;
pub const L_MAP_H: u32 = 0x0073_0f1c;
pub const L_PANEL_W: u32 = 0x0073_0f24;
/// Resolution request / switch state: 0 idle, 1..3 = F1..F3 pressed, 0xfa = switched (logic acknowledges).
pub const RES_REQUEST: u32 = 0x007d_fd44;
/// `gfx::RuntimeSwitch(snap)` (thiscall, ret 4, returns al = skip frame), called by the frame renderer `0x4b26c0`.
pub const FN_RUNTIME_SWITCH: u32 = 0x004c_7490;
/// `gfx::DisplaySwitch(w, h, bpp, 0, 0)` (thiscall, ret 0x14): posts `0x804(index)` -> `SetDisplayMode`.
pub const FN_DISPLAY_SWITCH: u32 = 0x0042_ce90;
/// `call [reg+0x54]` (= `IDirectDraw2::SetDisplayMode(this, w, h, 16, 0, 0)`) in `0x405c80`: index 1, index 0/2.
pub const SETMODE_CALLS: [u32; 2] = [0x0040_5cc3, 0x0040_5cf2];
/// Landscape ring buffer init (thiscall `(w, h, surface, rect)`, ret 0x1c).
pub const FN_LANDSCAPE_INIT: u32 = 0x0054_bec0;
/// Text DIB creation (thiscall `(w, h)`), called once by the display setup with the screen size.
pub const FN_TEXT_DIB: u32 = 0x004a_78f0;
/// `[0x730f44]`: landscape buffer width margin (32).
pub const L_LANDSCAPE_MARGIN_W: u32 = 0x0073_0f44;

/// Bytes the fields behind the grid move by (the grid becomes `SNAP_COLS x SNAP_ROWS` cells).
pub const fn snap_delta() -> u32 {
    SNAP_GRID + SNAP_COLS * SNAP_COL_BYTES_NEW - SNAP_TAIL
}

/// `shl r,6` of the grid index `row + col*130` (`mov r,col; shl r,6; add r,col; lea x,[row+r*2]`): imm8 at +2
/// becomes 7 (`col*258`). Found by `tools/res-tall/x130.py` + review of every function that touched the grid in a
/// memory trace (res-tall progress note): object drawers `0x4a9960`, `0x4c85a0`, `0x4d3050`, `0x4d5a50`, frame
/// renderer `0x4b26c0` (2), snapshot fill `0x51f110` (2), landscape rasteriser `0x54cbd0` (2).
pub const STRIDE_SHL_SITES: [u32; 10] =
    [0x4a99c5, 0x4b2e7a, 0x4b2fa3, 0x4c8603, 0x4d309a, 0x4d5a95, 0x52240f, 0x522f66, 0x54ce80, 0x54cef8];

/// Immediates that are a number of grid columns in cells (`n*130`): (instruction, offset, original, n).
pub const STRIDE_INDEX_SITES: [(u32, u32, u32, u32); 2] = [

];

/// `gfx` object size (`push 0x5f700` at `0x42c6b9`) and the sprite-list bucket arrays in it (250 dwords each):
/// list 1 heads/counts, list 2 heads/counts, list 3 heads/counts (`0x4d7c90..0x4d8232` inserts, `0x4b2d6c` init,
/// `0x4b34d3`/`0x4b3565` draw loops).
pub const GFX_SIZE: u32 = 0x5f700;
pub const GFX_ALLOC_SITE: (u32, u32) = (0x42c6b9, 1);
pub const SPRITE_ARRAYS: [u32; 6] = [0x13a8c, 0x13e74, 0x4ad60, 0x4b148, 0x5edb4, 0x5f19c];
pub const ORIG_BUCKETS: u32 = 250;

/// Code sites of the sprite lists: (instruction, offset, original value). Values in [`SPRITE_ARRAYS`] move to
/// `GFX_SIZE + i*SPRITE_BUCKETS*4`, 0xfa (bucket bound / first free node) becomes [`SPRITE_BUCKETS`], 0xfb (list 3
/// first free node, node 0 = none) `SPRITE_BUCKETS + 1`. Offsets from `tools/res-tall/sites.py`.
pub const SPRITE_SITES: [(u32, u32, u32); 74] = [
    (0x4b2d73, 3, 0x13a8c), (0x4b2d7a, 3, 0x13e74), (0x4b2d81, 3, 0x4ad60), (0x4b2d8b, 3, 0x4b148),
    (0x4b2d92, 3, 0x5edb4), (0x4b2d99, 3, 0x5f19c), (0x4b34e2, 3, 0x13e74), (0x4b3574, 3, 0x4b148),
    (0x4d7cb7, 3, 0x13a8c), (0x4d7ccd, 3, 0x13a8c), (0x4d7ce2, 3, 0x13a8c), (0x4d7cf6, 3, 0x13a8c),
    (0x4d7d0b, 3, 0x13a8c), (0x4d7d28, 3, 0x13a8c), (0x4d7d3c, 3, 0x13e74), (0x4d7d45, 3, 0x13e74),
    (0x4d7d77, 3, 0x13a8c), (0x4d7d8d, 3, 0x13a8c), (0x4d7da2, 3, 0x13a8c), (0x4d7db6, 3, 0x13a8c),
    (0x4d7dcb, 3, 0x13a8c), (0x4d7de8, 3, 0x13a8c), (0x4d7dfc, 3, 0x13e74), (0x4d7e05, 3, 0x13e74),
    (0x4d7e37, 3, 0x4ad60), (0x4d7e53, 3, 0x4ad60), (0x4d7e6e, 3, 0x4ad60), (0x4d7e89, 3, 0x4ad60),
    (0x4d7ea4, 3, 0x4ad60), (0x4d7ec1, 3, 0x4ad60), (0x4d7edc, 3, 0x4ad60), (0x4d7eff, 3, 0x4ad60),
    (0x4d7f13, 3, 0x4b148), (0x4d7f1c, 3, 0x4b148), (0x4d7f57, 3, 0x4ad60), (0x4d7f73, 3, 0x4ad60),
    (0x4d7f8e, 3, 0x4ad60), (0x4d7fa9, 3, 0x4ad60), (0x4d7fc4, 3, 0x4ad60), (0x4d7fe1, 3, 0x4ad60),
    (0x4d7ffc, 3, 0x4ad60), (0x4d801f, 3, 0x4ad60), (0x4d8033, 3, 0x4b148), (0x4d803c, 3, 0x4b148),
    (0x4d8077, 3, 0x4ad60), (0x4d8093, 3, 0x4ad60), (0x4d80ae, 3, 0x4ad60), (0x4d80c9, 3, 0x4ad60),
    (0x4d80e4, 3, 0x4ad60), (0x4d8101, 3, 0x4ad60), (0x4d811c, 3, 0x4ad60), (0x4d813f, 3, 0x4ad60),
    (0x4d8153, 3, 0x4b148), (0x4d815c, 3, 0x4b148), (0x4d8177, 3, 0x5edb4), (0x4d81af, 3, 0x5edb4),
    (0x4d81c6, 3, 0x5edb4), (0x4d81db, 3, 0x5edb4), (0x4d81f0, 3, 0x5edb4), (0x4d820d, 3, 0x5edb4),
    (0x4d8221, 3, 0x5f19c), (0x4d822a, 3, 0x5f19c),
    (0x4b2d6c, 1, 0xfa), // init loop bound
    (0x4b2da7, 6, 0xfa), // first free node list 1 (nodes 0..249 are the bucket tails)
    (0x4b2db1, 6, 0xfa), // list 2
    (0x4b2dbb, 6, 0xfb), // list 3
    (0x4b34d3, 2, 0xfa), // draw loops
    (0x4b3565, 2, 0xfa),
    (0x4d7c9c, 1, 0xfa), // insert functions: bucket < 250
    (0x4d7d5c, 1, 0xfa),
    (0x4d7e1c, 1, 0xfa),
    (0x4d7f3c, 1, 0xfa),
    (0x4d805c, 1, 0xfa),
    (0x4d8184, 2, 0xfa),
];

/// New value of a [`SPRITE_SITES`] entry.
pub fn sprite_site_value(orig: u32) -> u32 {
    match SPRITE_ARRAYS.iter().position(|&a| a == orig) {
        Some(i) => GFX_SIZE + i as u32 * SPRITE_BUCKETS * 4,
        None if orig == ORIG_BUCKETS + 1 => SPRITE_BUCKETS + 1,
        None => SPRITE_BUCKETS,
    }
}

/// New `gfx` allocation size (the bucket arrays behind the original object).
pub const fn gfx_size_new() -> u32 {
    GFX_SIZE + SPRITE_ARRAYS.len() as u32 * SPRITE_BUCKETS * 4
}

/// Every code change of the resolution patch as (address, original bytes, new bytes), in a fixed order: snapshot
/// tail moves, row stride, sprite buckets, `gfx` size. Pure (no game bytes beyond the original values of the
/// patched immediates).
pub fn code_patches() -> Vec<(u32, Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)> {
    let le = |v: u32| v.to_le_bytes().to_vec();
    let d = snap_delta();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for &(a, off, v) in SNAP_TAIL_SITES {
        out.push((a + off, le(v), le(v.wrapping_add(d))));
    }
    for a in STRIDE_SHL_SITES {
        out.push((a + 2, vec![6], vec![7]));
    }
    for (a, off, v, n) in STRIDE_INDEX_SITES {
        debug_assert_eq!(v, n * ORIG_ROWS);
        out.push((a + off, le(v), le(n * SNAP_ROWS)));
    }
    for (a, off, v, n) in STRIDE_DISP_SITES {
        let add = (n * (SNAP_ROWS - ORIG_ROWS) as i32 * SNAP_CELL as i32) as u32;
        out.push((a + off, le(v), le(v.wrapping_add(add))));
    }
    for (a, off, v) in SPRITE_SITES {
        out.push((a + off, le(v), le(sprite_site_value(v))));
    }
    out.push((GFX_ALLOC_SITE.0 + GFX_ALLOC_SITE.1, le(GFX_SIZE), le(gfx_size_new())));
    out
}

/// Apply [`code_patches`] to raw guest memory (all or nothing; `Err` names the first site whose bytes differ).
/// Used by [`patch_snapshot`] and by the fast-path tests (which run the patched code).
pub fn apply_code_patches(mem: &mut s3_cpu::GuestMemory) -> Result<(), String> {
    let p = code_patches();
    for (a, old, _) in &p {
        let cur = mem.read_bytes(*a, old.len());
        if &cur != old {
            return Err(format!("res: patch site {a:#x}: expected {old:02x?}, found {cur:02x?}"));
        }
    }
    for (a, _, new) in &p {
        mem.write_bytes(*a, new);
    }
    Ok(())
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- layout math (pure)

/// Original layout per variant (resolution index 1..3, `0x4c6d70`): screen w, h, panel width, minimap width,
/// minimap x, minimap y, minimap bottom, panel cell, grid x, grid y, `[0x730f20]`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Variant {
    pub index: u32,
    pub w: u32,
    pub h: u32,
    pub panel_w: u32,
    pub mini_w: u32,
    pub mini_x: u32,
    pub mini_y: u32,
    pub mini_bottom: u32,
    pub cell: u32,
    pub grid_x: u32,
    pub grid_y: u32,
    pub msg_w: u32,
}

pub const VARIANTS: [Variant; 3] = [
    Variant { index: 1, w: 640, h: 480, panel_w: 136, mini_w: 128, mini_x: 5, mini_y: 10, mini_bottom: 142, cell: 3, grid_x: 8, grid_y: 152, msg_w: 437 },
    Variant { index: 2, w: 800, h: 600, panel_w: 176, mini_w: 160, mini_x: 8, mini_y: 5, mini_bottom: 170, cell: 4, grid_x: 8, grid_y: 171, msg_w: 540 },
    Variant { index: 3, w: 1024, h: 768, panel_w: 216, mini_w: 208, mini_x: 6, mini_y: 8, mini_bottom: 224, cell: 5, grid_x: 8, grid_y: 228, msg_w: 697 },
];

/// The original layout whose panel fits the height `h` (largest variant with `variant.h <= h`, at least 1).
pub fn variant_for(h: u32) -> Variant {
    *VARIANTS.iter().rev().find(|v| v.h <= h).unwrap_or(&VARIANTS[0])
}

/// The single variant UI mode A uses at every custom size (the 640x480 panel, the only one that fits the Classic
/// zoom range from 480 up). With a variant per height the game swapped the panel art when the zoom crossed 600 /
/// 768: the panel changed width and arrangement on screen and flickered while pinching around a border (phone
/// report 2026-11-08). The panel is shown at a constant on-screen scale anyway (`display::PanelSplit`).
pub const CLASSIC_VARIANT: Variant = VARIANTS[0];

/// Variant for a custom size: [`CLASSIC_VARIANT`] at every height, in both UI modes. The Mobile HUD used
/// [`variant_for`]: after a zoom from a big variant (fonts of the 1024x768 panel) down to the 640x480 one the game
/// kept the big panel fonts, so the HUD's panel pages (save list etc.) showed "Save Game" huge and cut (user
/// report 2026-11-08). (Heights below 480 get the 640x480 variant from `variant_for` anyway.)
pub fn variant_for_mode(_m: &mut Machine, _h: u32) -> Variant {
    CLASSIC_VARIANT
}

pub fn variant(index: u32) -> Option<Variant> {
    VARIANTS.iter().copied().find(|v| v.index == index)
}

/// Is `(w, h)` one of the three original sizes?
pub fn is_standard(w: u32, h: u32) -> bool {
    VARIANTS.iter().any(|v| v.w == w && v.h == h)
}

/// Clamp a wanted size to what the patched game supports (width a multiple of 8).
pub fn clamp_size(w: u32, h: u32) -> (u32, u32) {
    let h = h.clamp(MIN_H, MAX_H);
    let w = (w.clamp(MIN_W, MAX_W) / 8) * 8;
    (w, h)
}

/// Snapshot grid columns a view needs (`0x51f990..`): `cols + rows/2 + 3` (shear + neighbour reads).
pub fn grid_columns_needed(map_w: u32, map_h: u32) -> u32 {
    let cols = (map_w + 23) / 16 + 10;
    let rows = (map_h + 255) / 9 + 11;
    cols + rows / 2 + 3
}

/// Snapshot grid rows a view needs (`rows + 3`, must stay below [`SNAP_ROWS`]; the game's grid has 130).
pub fn grid_rows_needed(map_h: u32) -> u32 {
    (map_h + 255) / 9 + 11 + 3
}

/// Sprite-list buckets a view needs: the drawers use bucket `2*row` (+-2 for some objects) for snapshot rows up
/// to `rows + 3`.
pub fn sprite_buckets_needed(map_h: u32) -> u32 {
    2 * grid_rows_needed(map_h) + 4
}

/// The layout globals `0x730f08..0x730f40` for a `w x h` screen (map view = screen minus the variant's panel).
pub fn layout_values(w: u32, h: u32) -> [(u32, u32); 14] {
    layout_values_v(w, h, variant_for(h))
}

/// [`layout_values`] with the panel variant `v`.
pub fn layout_values_v(w: u32, h: u32, v: Variant) -> [(u32, u32); 14] {
    [
        (L_RES, v.index),
        (L_SCREEN_W, w),
        (L_SCREEN_H, h),
        (0x0073_0f14, 16),
        (L_MAP_W, w - v.panel_w),
        (L_MAP_H, h),
        (0x0073_0f20, v.msg_w),
        (L_PANEL_W, v.panel_w),
        (0x0073_0f28, v.mini_w),
        (0x0073_0f2c, v.mini_x),
        (0x0073_0f30, v.mini_y),
        (0x0073_0f34, v.mini_bottom),
        (0x0073_0f38, v.cell),
        (0x0073_0f3c, v.grid_x),
    ]
}

/// Write the layout globals for `w x h` (also `[0x730f40]` grid y and `[0x7dfd58] = 0`).
pub fn write_layout(m: &mut Machine, w: u32, h: u32) {
    let var = variant_for_mode(m, h);
    for (a, v) in layout_values_v(w, h, var) {
        m.mem.write_u32(a, v);
    }
    m.mem.write_u32(0x0073_0f40, var.grid_y);
    m.mem.write_u32(0x007d_fd58, 0);
}

/// Panel width and map view width of the classic (panel visible) layout for the current screen, for UI modes
/// that restore the panel (the HUD's "panel peek"): `None` if the layout globals are not set.
pub fn classic_layout(m: &Machine) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
    let v = variant(m.mem.read_u32(L_RES))?;
    let sw = m.mem.read_u32(L_SCREEN_W);
    (sw > v.panel_w).then(|| (v.panel_w, sw - v.panel_w))
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- settings

/// `res` section of `mods-settings.json`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct ResSettings {
    /// Custom resolution + zoom on (GOG exe only). Off = the game's own 640x480 / 800x600 / 1024x768.
    pub enabled: bool,
    /// Zoom level index into [`crate::zoom::LEVEL_HEIGHTS`] (0 = zoomed in, last = zoomed out).
    pub zoom_level: u32,
    /// Exact render height a pinch ended on (between the levels); `None` = use `zoom_level`. Menu zoom steps clear it.
    pub zoom_height: Option<u32>,
}

impl Default for ResSettings {
    fn default() -> Self {
        ResSettings { enabled: true, zoom_level: crate::zoom::DEFAULT_LEVEL, zoom_height: None }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- state

/// Runtime state (`m.state::<ResState>()`).
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct ResState {
    /// Hooks + snapshot patch installed.
    pub installed: bool,
    /// The snapshot grid was enlarged (code patched).
    pub snap_patched: bool,
    /// Size `0x42ce90` was asked for (non-standard): the next `SetDisplayMode` call site uses it.
    pub pending_mode: Option<(u32, u32)>,
    /// Custom size currently applied by us (layout + mode).
    pub applied: Option<(u32, u32)>,
    /// Size the renderer should switch to (set by the zoom logic every slice; `None` = leave the game alone).
    pub target: Option<(u32, u32)>,
    /// Display mode to use while `target` is active: the largest zoom size for the window aspect, so zoom steps
    /// only change the layout and the presented ("logical") size, not the mode (fast path).
    pub target_mode: Option<(u32, u32)>,
    /// Display mode we set (physical surface size).
    pub mode: Option<(u32, u32)>,
    /// `IDirectDraw2*` seen at the game's SetDisplayMode call (for logical-size calls).
    pub ddraw2: u32,
    /// Frames to skip after a fast switch until the logic thread made a snapshot for the new view size.
    pub settle_frames: u32,
    /// Keep this screen point (fractions of the frame) fixed over the next switch (pinch centre).
    pub anchor: Option<(f32, f32)>,
    /// `anchor.0` is a fraction of the map view instead of the frame (UI mode A with the panel shown at its own
    /// scale, `display::PanelSplit`: the panel keeps its screen width, the map part is scaled).
    pub anchor_map: bool,
    /// Number of switches done (stats / tests).
    pub switches: u32,
    /// `now_ms` of the last switch.
    pub last_switch_ms: u64,
    /// Landscape buffer / text DIB sizes requested at the last display setup (debug).
    pub landscape: Option<(u32, u32)>,
    pub text_dib: Option<(u32, u32)>,
    /// Frames after a switch that still get a forced full landscape redraw.
    pub redraw_frames: u32,
    /// Render frames seen by the switch hook (in-game frames).
    pub frames: u64,
    pub last_frame_ms: u64,
}

/// Frames with a forced full landscape redraw after a switch `cur -> want`. Each such frame redraws the whole
/// landscape (100-280 ms on the phone-size view), which made pinch zoom stutter: one frame is enough when the view
/// grows, none when it only shrinks (the landscape buffer already holds the smaller view; verified with
/// screenshots of in/out pinches, 2026-11-07). Env `S3_RES_REDRAW=N` / `S3_RES_REDRAW_SHRINK=N` override.
fn redraw_frames_after(cur: (u32, u32), want: (u32, u32)) -> u32 {
    let env = |k: &str| std::env::var(k).ok().and_then(|v| v.parse::<u32>().ok());
    let shrink = want.0 <= cur.0 && want.1 <= cur.1;
    if shrink {
        env("S3_RES_REDRAW_SHRINK").unwrap_or(0)
    } else {
        env("S3_RES_REDRAW").unwrap_or(1)
    }
}

fn trace() -> bool {
    std::env::var_os("S3_RES_TRACE").is_some()
}

/// Currently applied custom size (game pixels), if any.
pub fn applied(m: &mut Machine) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
    m.state::<ResState>().borrow_mut().applied
}

/// Set the wanted size (`None` = no custom resolution; the standard size of the current variant is restored
/// if a custom one was applied). Applied by the render-thread hook at the next in-game frame.
pub fn set_target(m: &mut Machine, t: Option<(u32, u32)>) {
    set_target_mode(m, t, t);
}

/// Like [`set_target`] with the display mode to use (`mode` >= `t`; zoom passes its largest level so zoom
/// steps take the fast path).
pub fn set_target_mode(m: &mut Machine, t: Option<(u32, u32)>, mode: Option<(u32, u32)>) {
    let st = m.state::<ResState>();
    let mut s = st.borrow_mut();
    s.target = t.map(|(w, h)| clamp_size(w, h));
    s.target_mode = match (s.target, mode) {
        (Some((w, h)), Some((mw, mh))) => {
            let (mw, mh) = clamp_size(mw, mh);
            Some((mw.max(w), mh.max(h)))
        }
        (t, _) => t,
    };
}

/// In the frame renderer's minimap block, right after the camera rectangle (minimap image px) is computed from the
/// snapshot's view (`0x4b3a3c..0x4b3ab7`): x = `[ebp-0x1c]`, y = `esi`, w = `[ebp-0x2c]`, h = `[ebp-0x44]`.
const MINIMAP_RECT_DONE: u32 = 0x004b_3aba;

/// UI mode A zoomed in below 480 rows shows only a centred crop of the map view (`zoom::classic_crop`), but the
/// game's minimap rectangle still covers the whole 480-row view, so it stopped shrinking at that zoom (user report
/// 2026-11-08). Shrink it to the shown part (presentation only: the rectangle is just drawn).
fn minimap_rect_hook(c: &mut HookCtx) -> HookFlow {
    let Some(crop) = crate::zoom::classic_crop(c.m) else { return HookFlow::Continue };
    let (gw, gh) = (c.m.mem.read_u32(L_SCREEN_W) as f32, c.m.mem.read_u32(L_SCREEN_H) as f32);
    let pw = c.m.mem.read_u32(L_PANEL_W) as f32;
    if crop as f32 >= gh || gw <= pw + 1.0 || gh <= 1.0 {
        return HookFlow::Continue;
    }
    // Shown part of the map view (same formula as `display::Viewport::map_src`), as fractions of the view.
    let x0 = pw + crate::display::map_skip(pw as u32, CLASSIC_VARIANT.h) as f32;
    let mw = gw - x0;
    let (ch, cw) = (crop as f32, mw * crop as f32 / gh);
    let (sx, sy) = (x0 + (mw - cw) / 2.0, (gh - ch) / 2.0);
    let view_w = gw - pw;
    let (ox, fw) = ((sx - pw) / view_w, cw / view_w);
    let (oy, fh) = (sy / gh, ch / gh);
    let ebp = c.reg(s3_cpu::EBP);
    let rd = |c: &mut HookCtx, o: u32| c.m.mem.read_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(o)) as i32 as f32;
    let (x, w, h) = (rd(c, 0x1c), rd(c, 0x2c), rd(c, 0x44));
    let y = c.reg(s3_cpu::ESI) as i32 as f32;
    let (nx, ny) = ((x + w * ox).round() as i32, (y + h * oy).round() as i32);
    let (nw, nh) = ((w * fw).round().max(1.0) as i32, (h * fh).round().max(1.0) as i32);
    c.m.mem.write_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(0x1c), nx as u32);
    c.m.mem.write_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(0x2c), nw as u32);
    c.m.mem.write_u32(ebp.wrapping_sub(0x44), nh as u32);
    c.set_reg(s3_cpu::ESI, ny as u32);
    HookFlow::Continue
}

/// Is a game frame being rendered (switch hook seen within the last second)?
pub fn in_game(m: &mut Machine) -> bool {
    let now = m.real_ms();
    let s = m.state::<ResState>();
    let s = s.borrow_mut();
    s.frames > 0 && now.saturating_sub(s.last_frame_ms) < 1000
}

/// [`in_game`] for showing the last frame: also true for up to 10 s without a new game frame while the shown
/// frame has a custom (non-standard) size. A big zoom step can keep the render thread busy for over a second
/// (full landscape redraw; the layout globals already have the next size while the old frame is still shown);
/// the 1 s rule then dropped the Classic panel split for that time and the panel jumped to the frame's scale
/// (flicker, 2026-11-08). Menus use standard sizes.
pub fn in_game_frame(m: &mut Machine) -> bool {
    if in_game(m) {
        return true;
    }
    let now = m.real_ms();
    let (frames, last) = {
        let s = m.state::<ResState>();
        let s = s.borrow_mut();
        (s.frames, s.last_frame_ms)
    };
    let size = m.last_frame_size();
    frames > 0
        && now.saturating_sub(last) < 10_000
        && size.0 > 0
        && !is_standard(size.0, size.1)
}

/// Is a resolution switch still being processed by the game (`[0x7dfd44] != 0`)?
pub fn switch_pending(m: &Machine) -> bool {
    m.mem.read_u32(RES_REQUEST) != 0
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- install

/// Enlarge the render snapshot grid to [`SNAP_COLS`] x [`SNAP_ROWS`] and the sprite lists to [`SPRITE_BUCKETS`]
/// buckets (code patch, see module docs).
pub fn patch_snapshot(m: &mut Machine) -> Result<(), String> {
    let p = code_patches();
    // Check every site first (all or nothing).
    for (a, old, _) in &p {
        let cur = m.mem.read_bytes(*a, old.len());
        if &cur != old {
            return Err(format!("res: patch site {a:#x}: expected {old:02x?}, found {cur:02x?}"));
        }
    }
    for (a, old, new) in &p {
        crate::patchset::patch_bytes(m, *a, old, new)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Install the resolution patch (GOG exe). Hooks are always installed with the GOG patch set (so every peer has
/// the same heap layout); custom sizes are only used while `settings.res.enabled`.
pub fn install(m: &mut Machine) -> Result<(), String> {
    patch_snapshot(m)?;
    {
        let st = m.state::<ResState>();
        let mut s = st.borrow_mut();
        s.installed = true;
        s.snap_patched = true;
    }
    hooks::add_hook(m, FN_DISPLAY_SWITCH, "res:display-switch", |c: &mut HookCtx| {
        let (w, h) = (c.arg(0), c.arg(1));
        let custom = !is_standard(w, h);
        if trace() {
            let ra = c.return_address();
            eprintln!("res: 0x42ce90({w}, {h}) from {ra:#x} custom {custom}");
        }
        c.m.state::<ResState>().borrow_mut().pending_mode = custom.then_some((w, h));
        HookFlow::Continue
    });
    for a in SETMODE_CALLS {
        hooks::add_hook(m, a, "res:set-display-mode", |c: &mut HookCtx| {
            let esp0 = c.esp();
            let this = c.m.mem.read_u32(esp0);
            let p = {
                let st = c.m.state::<ResState>();
                let mut s = st.borrow_mut();
                s.ddraw2 = this;
                s.pending_mode.take()
            };
            let esp = c.esp();
            if let Some((w, h)) = p {
                let (ow, oh) = (c.m.mem.read_u32(esp + 4), c.m.mem.read_u32(esp + 8));
                c.m.mem.write_u32(esp + 4, w);
                c.m.mem.write_u32(esp + 8, h);
                if trace() {
                    eprintln!("res: SetDisplayMode {ow}x{oh} -> {w}x{h}");
                }
            }
            // Every real mode change of the game (menus: 800x600, game start: the registry size) goes through here.
            let set = (c.m.mem.read_u32(esp + 4), c.m.mem.read_u32(esp + 8));
            c.m.state::<ResState>().borrow_mut().mode = Some(set);
            HookFlow::Continue
        });
    }
    hooks::add_hook(m, FN_LANDSCAPE_INIT, "res:landscape-max", |c: &mut HookCtx| {
        // Called by the display setup (0x42e430) at game start: make the ring buffer big enough for every size.
        let ra = c.return_address();
        if !(0x0042_e430..0x0042_f7e0).contains(&ra) {
            return HookFlow::Continue;
        }
        let esp = c.esp();
        let (w, h) = (c.m.mem.read_u32(esp + 4), c.m.mem.read_u32(esp + 8));
        let mw = MAX_W + c.m.mem.read_u32(L_LANDSCAPE_MARGIN_W);
        let mh = MAX_H + c.m.mem.read_u32(L_LANDSCAPE_MARGIN_H);
        let (nw, nh) = (w.max(mw), h.max(mh));
        c.m.mem.write_u32(esp + 4, nw);
        c.m.mem.write_u32(esp + 8, nh);
        c.m.state::<ResState>().borrow_mut().landscape = Some((nw, nh));
        if trace() {
            eprintln!("res: landscape buffer {w}x{h} -> {nw}x{nh} (from {ra:#x})");
        }
        HookFlow::Continue
    });
    hooks::add_hook(m, FN_TEXT_DIB, "res:text-dib-max", |c: &mut HookCtx| {
        let esp = c.esp();
        let (w, h) = (c.m.mem.read_u32(esp + 4), c.m.mem.read_u32(esp + 8));
        let (nw, nh) = (w.max(MAX_W), h.max(MAX_H));
        c.m.mem.write_u32(esp + 4, nw);
        c.m.mem.write_u32(esp + 8, nh);
        c.m.state::<ResState>().borrow_mut().text_dib = Some((nw, nh));
        if trace() {
            eprintln!("res: text DIB {w}x{h} -> {nw}x{nh}");
        }
        HookFlow::Continue
    });
    hooks::add_hook(m, FN_RUNTIME_SWITCH, "res:switch", switch_hook);
    hooks::add_hook(m, MINIMAP_RECT_DONE, "res:minimap-rect", minimap_rect_hook);
    if trace() {
        for (a, n) in [(0x0053_db30u32, "logic-tick"), (0x004c_74f0, "game-switch-1"), (0x004c_75ae, "game-switch-2"), (0x004c_767a, "game-switch-3"), (0x004c_6d70, "layout")] {
            hooks::add_hook(m, a, "res:trace", move |c: &mut HookCtx| {
                static N: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32::new(0);
                let k = N.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
                if k < 5 || k % 500 == 0 || c.m.mem.read_u32(RES_REQUEST) != 0 {
                    let r = c.m.mem.read_u32(RES_REQUEST);
                    let mw = c.m.mem.read_u32(L_MAP_W);
                    let t = c.m.current_tid();
                    eprintln!("res-trace: {n} #{k} tid {t} req {r:#x} mapw {mw}");
                }
                HookFlow::Continue
            });
        }
    }
    m.log(LogLevel::Info, &format!("mods: res: snapshot grid {SNAP_COLS}x{SNAP_ROWS}, {SPRITE_BUCKETS} sprite buckets, sizes up to {MAX_W}x{MAX_H}"));
    Ok(())
}

/// `0x4c7490` entry (render thread, every in-game frame, before the game's own F1-F3 check).
fn switch_hook(c: &mut HookCtx) -> HookFlow {
    let now = c.m.real_ms();
    let gfx = c.reg(ECX);
    let snap = c.arg(0);
    let (target, applied, anchor, anchor_map) = {
        let st = c.m.state::<ResState>();
        let mut s = st.borrow_mut();
        s.frames += 1;
        s.last_frame_ms = now;
        (s.target, s.applied, s.anchor, s.anchor_map)
    };
    if trace() {
        let last = c.m.state::<ResState>().borrow_mut().last_switch_ms;
        if last > 0 && now.saturating_sub(last) < 3000 {
            let r = |o: u32| c.m.mem.read_u32(snap + o);
            eprintln!("res-frame: t {now} cam {},{} prev {},{} req {:#x} glob {:#x}", r(4), r(8), r(0xc), r(0x10), r(0xa0), c.m.mem.read_u32(RES_REQUEST));
        }
    }
    if trace() && c.m.state::<ResState>().borrow_mut().frames % 300 == 1 {
        // Fill level of the fixed-size render lists after the previous frame (they are reset later in this frame,
        // `0x4b2da7`): sprite nodes (incl. one tail node per bucket), hit list `0x7ade12` (10000 entries).
        let r = |o: u32| c.m.mem.read_u32(gfx + o);
        let (l1, l2, l3) = (r(0x1425c), r(0x4b530), r(0x5f584));
        let hits = c.m.mem.read_u32(0x007d_fd60);
        eprintln!("res: lists sprite {l1}/4000 {l2}/8000 {l3}/4000 hits {hits}/10000");
    }
    // A switch (ours or F1-F3) is still being processed: let the game finish it.
    if c.m.mem.read_u32(RES_REQUEST) != 0 || c.m.mem.read_u32(snap + 0xa0) != 0 {
        return HookFlow::Continue;
    }
    // The display setup caches the map view rectangle in the landscape object; UI mode B changes the layout
    // afterwards (full-screen map, panel peek), which left a black band with a zigzag edge after F1-F3 (the
    // landscape was only drawn as wide as the cached rectangle). Keep it in sync and redraw when it changed.
    let synced = sync_view_rects(c.m, gfx);
    let cur = (c.m.mem.read_u32(L_SCREEN_W), c.m.mem.read_u32(L_SCREEN_H));
    let (target_mode, mode, settle) = {
        let st = c.m.state::<ResState>();
        let s = st.borrow_mut();
        (s.target_mode, s.mode, s.settle_frames)
    };
    // After a fast switch: skip frames until the logic thread's snapshot matches the new view (else one frame is
    // drawn from a snapshot of the old size).
    if settle > 0 {
        let matches = snapshot_matches(c.m, snap);
        let st = c.m.state::<ResState>();
        let mut s = st.borrow_mut();
        if !matches {
            s.settle_frames -= 1;
            drop(s);
            return c.return_from_function(1, 1);
        }
        s.settle_frames = 0;
    }
    // Force a full landscape redraw (previous camera far away, what the logic thread's acknowledgement does via
    // gd+0x2d254) on the first frames after a switch / view change whose snapshot already has the new view size
    // (a redraw from a snapshot of the old size left a black band with a zigzag edge).
    {
        let st = c.m.state::<ResState>();
        let mut s = st.borrow_mut();
        if synced {
            s.redraw_frames = s.redraw_frames.max(2);
        }
        if s.redraw_frames > 0 && snapshot_matches(c.m, snap) {
            s.redraw_frames -= 1;
            drop(s);
            c.m.mem.write_u32(snap + 0xc, 10_000_000);
            c.m.mem.write_u32(snap + 0x10, 10_000_000);
        }
    }
    let (want, want_mode) = match target {
        Some(t) => (t, target_mode.unwrap_or(t)),
        None => match applied {
            // Custom size turned off: back to the variant's standard size.
            Some(_) => {
                let v = variant_for(cur.1);
                ((v.w, v.h), (v.w, v.h))
            }
            None => return HookFlow::Continue,
        },
    };
    let fast = mode == Some(want_mode) && applied.is_some();
    if want == cur && fast {
        fix_map_width(c.m, want.0);
        return HookFlow::Continue;
    }
    // Camera: keep the anchored screen point over the same world point. Without an anchor (game start, F1-F3)
    // keep the view centre: the game centres the castle for the old (narrow) view, and keeping the camera's
    // top-left corner put it in the upper-left part of a wide view (user report 2026-11-07).
    let gd = crate::ui_hud_game::gd(c.m);
    if let (Some(g), Some((fx, fy))) = (gd, anchor.or(Some((0.5, 0.5)))) {
        let old_pw = c.m.mem.read_u32(L_PANEL_W) as f32;
        let new_pw = if old_pw == 0.0 { 0.0 } else { variant_for_mode(c.m, want.1).panel_w as f32 };
        let (cx, cy) = (c.m.mem.read_u32(g + GD_CAM_X) as i32, c.m.mem.read_u32(g + GD_CAM_Y) as i32);
        let (nx, ny) = if anchor_map && anchor.is_some() {
            crate::zoom::anchor_camera_map((cx, cy), (fx, fy), cur, want, old_pw, new_pw)
        } else {
            crate::zoom::anchor_camera((cx, cy), (fx, fy), cur, want, old_pw, new_pw)
        };
        c.m.mem.write_u32(g + GD_CAM_X, nx.max(0) as u32);
        c.m.mem.write_u32(g + GD_CAM_Y, ny.max(0) as u32);
    }
    let old_variant = c.m.mem.read_u32(L_RES);
    let hud_full = c.m.mem.read_u32(L_PANEL_W) == 0;
    write_layout(c.m, want.0, want.1);
    if hud_full {
        // UI mode B keeps its full-screen map (its panel hook re-applies it too; avoid one narrow frame).
        c.m.mem.write_u32(L_PANEL_W, 0);
        c.m.mem.write_u32(L_MAP_W, want.0);
    }
    let mut ack = true;
    if fast {
        // Fast path: same display mode, only the layout and the presented size change.
        update_view_rects(c.m, gfx);
        set_logical(c.m, want);
        // The logic acknowledgement (0x53db67) rebuilds the minimap (size depends on the variant), clamps the
        // camera and forces a redraw; only needed when the variant changes.
        ack = variant_for_mode(c.m, want.1).index != old_variant;
        if !ack {
            clamp_camera(c.m, gd);
        }
    } else {
        // Mode set: the display setup (0x42e430, run by the game after the mode change) creates its render
        // surfaces from the layout globals, so it must see the full mode size (VERIFIED: with the zoom size there,
        // later bigger zoom steps were clipped to it). Then switch the layout to the zoom size.
        write_layout(c.m, want_mode.0, want_mode.1);
        if hud_full {
            c.m.mem.write_u32(L_PANEL_W, 0);
            c.m.mem.write_u32(L_MAP_W, want_mode.0);
        }
        c.m.state::<ResState>().borrow_mut().pending_mode = (!is_standard(want_mode.0, want_mode.1)).then_some(want_mode);
        crate::call::call_thiscall(c.m, FN_DISPLAY_SWITCH, gfx, &[want_mode.0, want_mode.1, 16, 0, 0]);
        c.m.state::<ResState>().borrow_mut().pending_mode = None;
        write_layout(c.m, want.0, want.1);
        if hud_full {
            c.m.mem.write_u32(L_PANEL_W, 0);
            c.m.mem.write_u32(L_MAP_W, want.0);
        }
        // The setup stored the mode-size rectangles; use the zoom size.
        let gfx_now = gfx;
        update_view_rects(c.m, gfx_now);
        set_logical(c.m, want);
    }
    // The panel is only redrawn when dirty (map pixels would stay in the panel area otherwise).
    if let Some(g) = gd {
        c.m.mem.write_u32(g + 0x2d27c, 1);
    }
    if ack {
        // The F1-F3 key handler (0x525b5b) releases one token of the semaphore `[0x7a800c]` that the logic
        // thread's acknowledgement (0x53db80, after seeing 0xfa) waits for; without it the logic thread blocks
        // (VERIFIED).
        let sem = c.m.mem.read_u32(SWITCH_SEMAPHORE);
        if sem != 0 {
            let h = c.m.mem.read_u32(sem + 8);
            let release = c.m.mem.read_u32(IAT_RELEASE_SEMAPHORE);
            crate::call::call_stdcall(c.m, release, &[h, 1, 0]);
        }
        c.m.mem.write_u32(RES_REQUEST, 0xfa);
    }
    {
        let st = c.m.state::<ResState>();
        let mut s = st.borrow_mut();
        s.mode = Some(want_mode);
        s.applied = (!is_standard(want.0, want.1) || target.is_some()).then_some(want);
        s.anchor = None;
        s.anchor_map = false;
        s.redraw_frames = redraw_frames_after(cur, want);
        s.settle_frames = if ack { 0 } else { 6 };
        s.switches += 1;
        s.last_switch_ms = now;
    }
    if trace() {
        let esp = c.m.cpu().regs[ESP];
        eprintln!(
            "res: switch {}x{} -> {}x{} mode {}x{} ({}, variant {}, esp {esp:#x})",
            cur.0, cur.1, want.0, want.1, want_mode.0, want_mode.1, if fast { "fast" } else { "mode set" }, variant_for(want.1).index
        );
    }
    c.m.log(LogLevel::Info, &format!("res: {}x{} -> {}x{} ({})", cur.0, cur.1, want.0, want.1, if fast { "fast" } else { "mode set" }));
    // Skip this frame (what the game does after its own switch): al = 1, thiscall with one argument.
    c.return_from_function(1, 1)
}

/// Presented size = `size` (ddraw port extension `DDSDM_PORT_LOGICAL`, see s3-dx ddraw.rs).
fn set_logical(m: &mut Machine, size: (u32, u32)) {
    let dd = m.state::<ResState>().borrow_mut().ddraw2;
    if dd == 0 || !crate::ui_hud_game::readable(m, dd, 4) {
        return;
    }
    let vt = m.mem.read_u32(dd);
    let f = m.mem.read_u32(vt + 0x54);
    let r = crate::call::call_stdcall(m, f, &[dd, size.0, size.1, 16, 0, DDSDM_PORT_LOGICAL]);
    if r != 0 && trace() {
        eprintln!("res: logical size {}x{} rejected: {r:#x}", size.0, size.1);
    }
}

/// The view rectangles cached by the display setup (`0x42ef70..`): `gfx+0x5f6e8` and the landscape object's
/// `+0x58/+0x5c` (size) and `+0x74..+0x80` (rect).
fn update_view_rects(m: &mut Machine, gfx: u32) {
    let pw = m.mem.read_u32(L_PANEL_W);
    let top = m.mem.read_u32(0x007d_fd58);
    let (mw, mh) = (m.mem.read_u32(L_MAP_W), m.mem.read_u32(L_MAP_H));
    let rect = [pw, top, pw + mw, top + mh];
    for (i, v) in rect.iter().enumerate() {
        m.mem.write_u32(gfx + 0x5f6e8 + 4 * i as u32, *v);
    }
    let land = m.mem.read_u32(gfx + 0x5f6cc);
    if land != 0 && crate::ui_hud_game::readable(m, land, 0xa8) {
        m.mem.write_u32(land + 0x58, mw);
        m.mem.write_u32(land + 0x5c, mh);
        for (i, v) in rect.iter().enumerate() {
            m.mem.write_u32(land + 0x74 + 4 * i as u32, *v);
        }
    }
}

/// Was the logic thread's snapshot made for the current view size (`0x51f990..`: cols / rows)?
fn snapshot_matches(m: &Machine, snap: u32) -> bool {
    let cols = (m.mem.read_u32(L_MAP_W) + 23) / 16 + 10;
    let rows = (m.mem.read_u32(L_MAP_H) + 255) / 9 + 11;
    m.mem.read_u32(snap + 0x30) == cols && m.mem.read_u32(snap + 0x34) == rows
}

/// Update the cached view rectangles if they differ from the layout globals; true if something changed.
fn sync_view_rects(m: &mut Machine, gfx: u32) -> bool {
    let land = m.mem.read_u32(gfx + 0x5f6cc);
    if land == 0 || !crate::ui_hud_game::readable(m, land, 0xa8) {
        return false;
    }
    let pw = m.mem.read_u32(L_PANEL_W);
    let (mw, mh) = (m.mem.read_u32(L_MAP_W), m.mem.read_u32(L_MAP_H));
    if m.mem.read_u32(land + 0x58) == mw && m.mem.read_u32(land + 0x5c) == mh && m.mem.read_u32(land + 0x74) == pw {
        return false;
    }
    update_view_rects(m, gfx);
    if trace() {
        let f: Vec<String> = (0..14).map(|i| format!("{:x}", m.mem.read_u32(land + 0x50 + 4 * i))).collect();
        eprintln!("res: view rect synced: panel {pw} map {mw}x{mh}; landscape {land:#x} +0x50..: {}", f.join(" "));
    }
    true
}

/// Camera clamp of `0x51b4d0` done host-side (the logic acknowledgement is skipped on the fast path).
fn clamp_camera(m: &mut Machine, gd: Option<u32>) {
    let Some(g) = gd else { return };
    let world = m.mem.read_u32(g + 0x2d2d0) as i32;
    let mw = m.mem.read_u32(L_MAP_W) as i32;
    let mh = m.mem.read_u32(L_MAP_H) as i32;
    let (x, y) = (m.mem.read_u32(g + GD_CAM_X) as i32 as f32, m.mem.read_u32(g + GD_CAM_Y) as i32 as f32);
    let (nx, ny) = crate::touch_logic::clamp_camera(x, y, world, mw, mh);
    m.mem.write_u32(g + GD_CAM_X, nx as i32 as u32);
    m.mem.write_u32(g + GD_CAM_Y, ny as i32 as u32);
}

/// The HUD restores the panel with the original map width of the variant; with a custom width the map view must
/// be `screen - panel`.
fn fix_map_width(m: &mut Machine, sw: u32) {
    let pw = m.mem.read_u32(L_PANEL_W);
    if pw == 0 {
        return;
    }
    if let Some(v) = variant(m.mem.read_u32(L_RES)) {
        if pw == v.panel_w && m.mem.read_u32(L_MAP_W) != sw - pw {
            m.mem.write_u32(L_MAP_W, sw - pw);
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn variants_and_layout() {
        assert_eq!(variant_for(480).index, 1);
        assert_eq!(variant_for(599).index, 1);
        assert_eq!(variant_for(600).index, 2);
        assert_eq!(variant_for(780).index, 3);
        assert_eq!(variant_for(360).index, 1);
        let l = layout_values(1480, 600);
        assert!(l.contains(&(L_MAP_W, 1480 - 176)));
        assert!(l.contains(&(L_RES, 2)));
        // The original sizes reproduce the game's own table.
        for v in VARIANTS {
            let l = layout_values(v.w, v.h);
            let map_w = l.iter().find(|e| e.0 == L_MAP_W).unwrap().1;
            assert_eq!(map_w, [504, 624, 808][v.index as usize - 1]);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn grid_budget() {
        // 1024x768 (map 808x768): 123 columns of the original 130 (+3 neighbour reads).
        assert_eq!(grid_columns_needed(808, 768), 126);
        assert!(grid_rows_needed(768) <= 129);
        // Every size we allow fits the enlarged grid and sprite lists.
        assert!(grid_columns_needed(MAX_W, MAX_H) <= SNAP_COLS);
        assert!(grid_rows_needed(MAX_H) < SNAP_ROWS, "{}", grid_rows_needed(MAX_H));
        assert!(sprite_buckets_needed(MAX_H) <= SPRITE_BUCKETS, "{}", sprite_buckets_needed(MAX_H));
        // The game's 250 buckets were too few already at 780 (rows >= 125 lost their objects).
        assert!(sprite_buckets_needed(780) > ORIG_BUCKETS);
        assert_eq!(clamp_size(2229, 904), (2224, 904));
        assert_eq!(clamp_size(4000, 2000), (MAX_W, MAX_H));
        assert_eq!(clamp_size(100, 100), (MIN_W, MIN_H));
        assert!(is_standard(800, 600) && !is_standard(1480, 600));
    }

    #[test]
    fn snapshot_sites_sane() {
        assert_eq!(SNAP_TAIL_SITES.len(), 55);
        for &(a, off, v) in SNAP_TAIL_SITES {
            assert!((0x401000..0x650000).contains(&a) && off <= 3);
            assert!((SNAP_TAIL..=SNAP_SIZE).contains(&v) || (a, v) == (0x51f1f8, 0xc636c), "{a:#x}");
        }
        // The grid of SNAP_COLS x SNAP_ROWS cells ends exactly where the moved tail starts.
        assert_eq!(SNAP_GRID + SNAP_COLS * SNAP_COL_BYTES_NEW, SNAP_TAIL + snap_delta());
        assert_eq!(SNAP_GRID + 130 * SNAP_COL_BYTES, SNAP_TAIL);
        // shl 6 -> 7 turns (c<<6 + c)*2 = c*130 into c*258.
        assert_eq!(((1u32 << 7) + 1) * 2, SNAP_ROWS);
        for (_, _, v, n) in STRIDE_DISP_SITES {
            // n columns + a small row/field offset (+ the grid base 0x500 for the cell-pointer displacements).
            let rest = (v as i32 - n * SNAP_COL_BYTES as i32).rem_euclid(SNAP_COL_BYTES as i32);
            assert!(rest <= 0x500 + 0x95, "{v:#x}");
        }
        // No address is patched twice; patches do not overlap.
        let mut p: Vec<(u32, usize)> = code_patches().iter().map(|(a, o, _)| (*a, o.len())).collect();
        p.sort();
        for w in p.windows(2) {
            assert!(w[0].0 + w[0].1 as u32 <= w[1].0, "{:#x} {:#x}", w[0].0, w[1].0);
        }
        assert_eq!(p.len(), 55 + 10 + 2 + 30 + 74 + 1);
        assert_eq!(sprite_site_value(0x13a8c), GFX_SIZE);
        assert_eq!(sprite_site_value(0x5f19c), GFX_SIZE + 5 * SPRITE_BUCKETS * 4);
        assert_eq!(sprite_site_value(0xfb), SPRITE_BUCKETS + 1);
        assert_eq!(sprite_site_value(0xfa), SPRITE_BUCKETS);
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/settings.rs`:

```rs
//! Mod/UI settings, persisted as JSON in `<data_dir>/mods-settings.json`. Unknown or missing fields fall back
//! to defaults, so old files keep loading after new fields are added.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// File name inside the data dir.
pub const SETTINGS_FILE: &str = "mods-settings.json";

/// The two selectable mobile UI modes (docs/porting/mobile-vision.md).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
pub enum UiMode {
    /// A: the original panel and game UI, patched for touch.
    #[default]
    ClassicTouch,
    /// B: a native large-button HUD on top of / instead of the original panel.
    MobileHud,
}

/// Gesture thresholds (game pixels / milliseconds), see [`crate::gesture::GestureConfig`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct TouchSettings {
    pub long_press_ms: u64,
    pub tap_max_ms: u64,
    pub tap_slop: f32,
    pub double_tap_ms: u64,
    pub double_tap_slop: f32,
    /// Fallback touch->mouse mapping: a long press right-clicks (legacy behaviour; with `context` on, the
    /// context-aware touch mod consumes long presses, so this only applies when `context` is off).
    pub long_press_right_click: bool,
    /// Context-aware touch (W3, `touch.rs`; GOG exe only). Off = legacy touch->mouse mapping only.
    pub context: bool,
}

impl Default for TouchSettings {
    fn default() -> Self {
        TouchSettings {
            long_press_ms: LONG_PRESS_MS,
            tap_max_ms: 500,
            tap_slop: 8.0,
            double_tap_ms: 300,
            double_tap_slop: 24.0,
            long_press_right_click: true,
            context: true,
        }
    }
}

/// All mod settings.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct Settings {
    pub version: u32,
    pub ui_mode: UiMode,
    /// Master switch for exe patch sets (hooks/byte patches). Input/overlay framework stays active.
    pub patches_enabled: bool,
    /// Draw touch points and recognized gestures (also `S3_MODS_DEBUG=1`).
    pub debug_overlay: bool,
    /// Scale factor for native HUD elements (mode B).
    pub hud_scale: f32,
    pub touch: TouchSettings,
    /// Display mode / filter / FPS counter / refresh rate (docs/porting/display.md, `crate::display`).
    pub display: crate::display::DisplaySettings,
    /// Custom game resolution + zoom level (docs/porting/resolution-zoom.md, `crate::res` / `crate::zoom`).
    pub res: crate::res::ResSettings,
    /// Game speed the speed button switches to (2..=8, `crate::speed`); chosen in the menus.
    pub fast_speed: u32,
    /// Show the game time (`crate::game_time`); on by default.
    pub show_game_time: bool,
    /// Old on/off form of [`Settings::unit_paths`] (true = all); migrated on load, then false.
    pub show_unit_paths: bool,
    /// Whose paths are drawn besides the selected units' (`crate::unit_orders`).
    pub unit_paths: PathMode,
    /// Vibrate on long presses (box select start, group assign) (`crate::haptics`).
    pub vibrate_touch: bool,
    /// Vibrate on game messages and their notifications (`crate::haptics`, Android background notifications).
    pub vibrate_messages: bool,
    /// Control-group buttons 1..6 (tap = select / centre, long press = assign; `crate::unit_orders`).
    pub group_shortcuts: bool,
}

impl Default for Settings {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Settings {
            version: 1,
            ui_mode: UiMode::default(),
            patches_enabled: true,
            debug_overlay: false,
            hud_scale: 1.0,
            touch: TouchSettings::default(),
            display: crate::display::DisplaySettings::default(),
            res: crate::res::ResSettings::default(),
            fast_speed: crate::speed::DEFAULT_FAST,
            show_game_time: true,
            show_unit_paths: false,
            unit_paths: PathMode::Selected,
            vibrate_touch: true,
            vibrate_messages: true,
            group_shortcuts: false,
        }
    }
}

/// Whose unit paths are drawn (selected units always show theirs).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum PathMode {
    /// Only the selected units.
    #[default]
    Selected,
    /// Also every own selectable unit on its way (soldiers, specialists, war machines, ships).
    Units,
    /// Also every own settler on its way (carriers and workers too).
    All,
}

impl PathMode {
    pub fn next(self) -> PathMode {
        match self {
            PathMode::Selected => PathMode::Units,
            PathMode::Units => PathMode::All,
            PathMode::All => PathMode::Selected,
        }
    }
    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            PathMode::Selected => "selected",
            PathMode::Units => "units",
            PathMode::All => "all",
        }
    }
}

/// Vibration menu label and cycle: (touch, messages) all -> touch -> messages -> off.
pub fn vibration_label(s: &Settings) -> &'static str {
    match (s.vibrate_touch, s.vibrate_messages) {
        (true, true) => "Vibration: all",
        (true, false) => "Vibration: touch",
        (false, true) => "Vibration: messages",
        (false, false) => "Vibration: off",
    }
}

pub fn cycle_vibration(s: &mut Settings) {
    (s.vibrate_touch, s.vibrate_messages) = match (s.vibrate_touch, s.vibrate_messages) {
        (true, true) => (true, false),
        (true, false) => (false, true),
        (false, true) => (false, false),
        (false, false) => (true, true),
    };
}

/// Hold time before a touch becomes a long press (box select / drag start). Was 500 ms until 2026-11-08
/// ("press and drag takes too long").
pub const LONG_PRESS_MS: u64 = 350;
const OLD_LONG_PRESS_MS: u64 = 500;

impl Settings {
    pub fn path(data_dir: &Path) -> PathBuf {
        data_dir.join(SETTINGS_FILE)
    }

    /// Load from `data_dir` (defaults if the file is missing or broken; the error is returned for logging).
    pub fn load(data_dir: &Path) -> (Settings, Option<String>) {
        let p = Self::path(data_dir);
        match std::fs::read(&p) {
            Ok(b) => match serde_json::from_slice::<Settings>(&b) {
                Ok(mut s) => {
                    // The old default was saved into every settings file: move it to the new one.
                    if s.show_unit_paths {
                        s.show_unit_paths = false;
                        if s.unit_paths == PathMode::Selected {
                            s.unit_paths = PathMode::All;
                        }
                    }
                    if s.touch.long_press_ms == OLD_LONG_PRESS_MS {
                        s.touch.long_press_ms = LONG_PRESS_MS;
                    }
                    (s, None)
                }
                Err(e) => (Settings::default(), Some(format!("{}: {e}", p.display()))),
            },
            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => (Settings::default(), None),
            Err(e) => (Settings::default(), Some(format!("{}: {e}", p.display()))),
        }
    }

    /// Save atomically (write temp file, rename).
    pub fn save(&self, data_dir: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(data_dir).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let p = Self::path(data_dir);
        let tmp = p.with_extension("json.tmp");
        let s = serde_json::to_string_pretty(self).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        std::fs::write(&tmp, s).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        std::fs::rename(&tmp, &p).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn roundtrip_and_partial_files() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("s3mods-settings-{}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        let (s, err) = Settings::load(&dir);
        assert_eq!(s, Settings::default());
        assert!(err.is_none());
        let mut s2 = Settings::default();
        s2.ui_mode = UiMode::MobileHud;
        s2.touch.long_press_ms = 700;
        s2.save(&dir).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(Settings::load(&dir).0, s2);
        // Partial file: missing fields use defaults.
        std::fs::write(Settings::path(&dir), r#"{"ui_mode":"MobileHud","touch":{"tap_slop":12.5}}"#).unwrap();
        let s3 = Settings::load(&dir).0;
        assert_eq!(s3.ui_mode, UiMode::MobileHud);
        assert_eq!(s3.touch.tap_slop, 12.5);
        assert_eq!(s3.touch.long_press_ms, LONG_PRESS_MS);
        // Broken file: defaults + error.
        std::fs::write(Settings::path(&dir), "{").unwrap();
        let (s4, err) = Settings::load(&dir);
        assert_eq!(s4, Settings::default());
        assert!(err.is_some());
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/sha256.rs`:

```rs
//! Minimal SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) for identifying the user's S3.EXE. Dependency-free; hashing ~2.5 MB once at
//! start takes a few ms.

const K: [u32; 64] = [
    0x428a2f98, 0x71374491, 0xb5c0fbcf, 0xe9b5dba5, 0x3956c25b, 0x59f111f1, 0x923f82a4, 0xab1c5ed5, 0xd807aa98,
    0x12835b01, 0x243185be, 0x550c7dc3, 0x72be5d74, 0x80deb1fe, 0x9bdc06a7, 0xc19bf174, 0xe49b69c1, 0xefbe4786,
    0x0fc19dc6, 0x240ca1cc, 0x2de92c6f, 0x4a7484aa, 0x5cb0a9dc, 0x76f988da, 0x983e5152, 0xa831c66d, 0xb00327c8,
    0xbf597fc7, 0xc6e00bf3, 0xd5a79147, 0x06ca6351, 0x14292967, 0x27b70a85, 0x2e1b2138, 0x4d2c6dfc, 0x53380d13,
    0x650a7354, 0x766a0abb, 0x81c2c92e, 0x92722c85, 0xa2bfe8a1, 0xa81a664b, 0xc24b8b70, 0xc76c51a3, 0xd192e819,
    0xd6990624, 0xf40e3585, 0x106aa070, 0x19a4c116, 0x1e376c08, 0x2748774c, 0x34b0bcb5, 0x391c0cb3, 0x4ed8aa4a,
    0x5b9cca4f, 0x682e6ff3, 0x748f82ee, 0x78a5636f, 0x84c87814, 0x8cc70208, 0x90befffa, 0xa4506ceb, 0xbef9a3f7,
    0xc67178f2,
];

fn compress(h: &mut [u32; 8], block: &[u8]) {
    let mut w = [0u32; 64];
    for i in 0..16 {
        w[i] = u32::from_be_bytes([block[4 * i], block[4 * i + 1], block[4 * i + 2], block[4 * i + 3]]);
    }
    for i in 16..64 {
        let s0 = w[i - 15].rotate_right(7) ^ w[i - 15].rotate_right(18) ^ (w[i - 15] >> 3);
        let s1 = w[i - 2].rotate_right(17) ^ w[i - 2].rotate_right(19) ^ (w[i - 2] >> 10);
        w[i] = w[i - 16].wrapping_add(s0).wrapping_add(w[i - 7]).wrapping_add(s1);
    }
    let [mut a, mut b, mut c, mut d, mut e, mut f, mut g, mut hh] = *h;
    for i in 0..64 {
        let s1 = e.rotate_right(6) ^ e.rotate_right(11) ^ e.rotate_right(25);
        let ch = (e & f) ^ (!e & g);
        let t1 = hh.wrapping_add(s1).wrapping_add(ch).wrapping_add(K[i]).wrapping_add(w[i]);
        let s0 = a.rotate_right(2) ^ a.rotate_right(13) ^ a.rotate_right(22);
        let maj = (a & b) ^ (a & c) ^ (b & c);
        let t2 = s0.wrapping_add(maj);
        hh = g;
        g = f;
        f = e;
        e = d.wrapping_add(t1);
        d = c;
        c = b;
        b = a;
        a = t1.wrapping_add(t2);
    }
    for (x, v) in h.iter_mut().zip([a, b, c, d, e, f, g, hh]) {
        *x = x.wrapping_add(v);
    }
}

/// SHA-256 of `data`.
pub fn sha256(data: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {
    let mut h: [u32; 8] =
        [0x6a09e667, 0xbb67ae85, 0x3c6ef372, 0xa54ff53a, 0x510e527f, 0x9b05688c, 0x1f83d9ab, 0x5be0cd19];
    let mut chunks = data.chunks_exact(64);
    for c in &mut chunks {
        compress(&mut h, c);
    }
    let rem = chunks.remainder();
    let mut tail = [0u8; 128];
    tail[..rem.len()].copy_from_slice(rem);
    tail[rem.len()] = 0x80;
    let n = if rem.len() < 56 { 64 } else { 128 };
    tail[n - 8..n].copy_from_slice(&((data.len() as u64) * 8).to_be_bytes());
    for c in tail[..n].chunks_exact(64) {
        compress(&mut h, c);
    }
    let mut out = [0u8; 32];
    for (i, v) in h.iter().enumerate() {
        out[4 * i..4 * i + 4].copy_from_slice(&v.to_be_bytes());
    }
    out
}

/// Lower-case hex SHA-256 of `data`.
pub fn sha256_hex(data: &[u8]) -> String {
    sha256(data).iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn known_vectors() {
        assert_eq!(sha256_hex(b""), "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855");
        assert_eq!(sha256_hex(b"abc"), "ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad");
        assert_eq!(
            sha256_hex(b"abcdbcdecdefdefgefghfghighijhijkijkljklmklmnlmnomnopnopq"),
            "248d6a61d20638b8e5c026930c3e6039a33ce45964ff2167f6ecedd419db06c1"
        );
        let a = vec![b'a'; 1_000_000];
        assert_eq!(sha256_hex(&a), "cdc76e5c9914fb9281a1c7e284d73e67f1809a48a497200e046d39ccc7112cd0");
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/speed.rs`:

```rs
//! Game speed (single player): normal or a chosen fast speed 2x..8x, like Settlers United's speed-up (user
//! requests 2026-11-08: "up to 8x; the button toggles the chosen speed; the speed is chosen in the menu").
//!
//! The guest clock runs `scale` times as fast as the wall clock (`Machine::set_time_scale`: GetTickCount,
//! timeGetTime, QueryPerformanceCounter, waits and timers), so the game's logic ticks faster; display pacing,
//! audio and the mods' UI stay on the wall clock (`Machine::real_ms`). The game itself is not patched. Only in a
//! single-player game (`*(0x7e3408)` is 0 in multiplayer, where lockstep peers must share one speed); back to 1x
//! outside a game. If the phone cannot keep up, the game simply runs as fast as it can.

use s3_runtime::{LogLevel, Machine};

use crate::Mod;

/// Fast speeds selectable in the menus.
pub const FAST_CHOICES: [u32; 7] = [2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8];
/// Default fast speed.
pub const DEFAULT_FAST: u32 = 2;

/// `CGameData*` global: non-zero in a single-player game, 0 in multiplayer (game-state-ui.md).
const GD_GLOBAL_SP: u32 = 0x007e_3408;

/// Can the speed be changed now (single-player game running)?
pub fn allowed(m: &mut Machine) -> bool {
    m.mem.read_u32(GD_GLOBAL_SP) != 0 && crate::res::in_game_frame(m)
}

/// Current speed factor.
pub fn current(m: &Machine) -> f64 {
    m.time_scale()
}

/// Is the game running fast now?
pub fn is_fast(m: &Machine) -> bool {
    current(m) > 1.001
}

/// The chosen fast speed (settings, clamped to [`FAST_CHOICES`]).
pub fn fast_choice(m: &mut Machine) -> u32 {
    crate::settings(m).fast_speed.clamp(FAST_CHOICES[0], FAST_CHOICES[FAST_CHOICES.len() - 1])
}

/// Label of the chosen fast speed, e.g. "4x".
pub fn choice_label(m: &mut Machine) -> String {
    format!("{}x", fast_choice(m))
}

/// Speed button: normal <-> chosen fast speed. Returns the new factor (1 when not allowed).
pub fn toggle(m: &mut Machine) -> f64 {
    let next = if allowed(m) && !is_fast(m) { fast_choice(m) as f64 } else { 1.0 };
    set(m, next);
    next
}

/// Menu: next fast speed choice (wraps); applied at once while running fast. Returns the new choice.
pub fn cycle_choice(m: &mut Machine) -> u32 {
    let cur = fast_choice(m);
    let i = FAST_CHOICES.iter().position(|&c| c == cur).unwrap_or(0);
    let next = FAST_CHOICES[(i + 1) % FAST_CHOICES.len()];
    let mut s = crate::settings(m);
    s.fast_speed = next;
    let _ = crate::set_settings(m, s);
    if is_fast(m) && allowed(m) {
        set(m, next as f64);
    }
    next
}

/// Set the speed factor.
pub fn set(m: &mut Machine, s: f64) {
    if (current(m) - s).abs() > 0.001 {
        m.set_time_scale(s);
        m.log(LogLevel::Info, &format!("speed: {s}x"));
    }
}

/// Speed button state for the UIs: (chosen label, running fast) while the speed can be changed.
pub fn button_state(m: &mut Machine) -> Option<(String, bool)> {
    allowed(m).then(|| (choice_label(m), is_fast(m)))
}

/// Resets the speed to 1x outside a single-player game.
#[derive(Default)]
struct SpeedMod {
    out_since: u64,
}

impl Mod for SpeedMod {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        "speed"
    }
    fn tick(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, now: u64) {
        if !is_fast(m) {
            self.out_since = 0;
            return;
        }
        if allowed(m) {
            self.out_since = 0;
        } else if self.out_since == 0 {
            self.out_since = now.max(1);
        } else if now.saturating_sub(self.out_since) > 1500 {
            set(m, 1.0);
        }
    }
}

pub fn install(m: &mut Machine) {
    crate::add_mod(m, Box::new(SpeedMod::default()));
}
```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/stone.rs`:

```rs
//! Procedural stone texture for the window area around the full-screen menu layouts (user request 2026-11-08:
//! "use the Settlers stone background instead of a flat colour, so everything looks smooth").
//!
//! Our own generated image (no game asset): blue-grey value noise with diagonal streaks like the game's stone
//! screens, tileable ([`TILE`] x [`TILE`], every term periodic), drawn at the layout's scale (one texel = one game
//! pixel) by the CPU renderer (`menu_layout::render_xrgb`) and the Android GLES presenter (`GL_REPEAT` texture).

use std::sync::OnceLock;

/// Tile size (texels, power of two for `GL_REPEAT` on GLES 2).
pub const TILE: usize = 256;

/// Colour ramp dark -> light (sampled from the game's stone screens, rgb565-rounded there).
const RAMP: [(f32, [f32; 3]); 4] = [
    (0.0, [33.0, 48.0, 66.0]),
    (0.3, [70.0, 88.0, 108.0]),
    (0.6, [88.0, 120.0, 150.0]),
    (1.0, [132.0, 160.0, 172.0]),
];

fn hash(x: u32, y: u32, seed: u32) -> f32 {
    let mut h = x.wrapping_mul(0x8da6_b343) ^ y.wrapping_mul(0xd816_3841) ^ seed.wrapping_mul(0xcb1a_b31f);
    h ^= h >> 13;
    h = h.wrapping_mul(0x5bd1_e995);
    h ^= h >> 15;
    (h & 0xffff) as f32 / 65535.0
}

fn smooth(t: f32) -> f32 {
    t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t)
}

/// Periodic 2D value noise: lattice of `cells` per tile in each direction.
fn noise2(x: f32, y: f32, cells: u32, seed: u32) -> f32 {
    let f = cells as f32 / TILE as f32;
    let (gx, gy) = (x * f, y * f);
    let (ix, iy) = (gx.floor() as i64, gy.floor() as i64);
    let (tx, ty) = (smooth(gx - ix as f32), smooth(gy - iy as f32));
    let c = cells as i64;
    let at = |dx: i64, dy: i64| hash((ix + dx).rem_euclid(c) as u32, (iy + dy).rem_euclid(c) as u32, seed);
    let a = at(0, 0) + (at(1, 0) - at(0, 0)) * tx;
    let b = at(0, 1) + (at(1, 1) - at(0, 1)) * tx;
    a + (b - a) * ty
}

/// Periodic 1D value noise over `t` in [0, TILE).
fn noise1(t: f32, cells: u32, seed: u32) -> f32 {
    let g = t * cells as f32 / TILE as f32;
    let i = g.floor() as i64;
    let f = smooth(g - i as f32);
    let c = cells as i64;
    let a = hash(i.rem_euclid(c) as u32, 7, seed);
    let b = hash((i + 1).rem_euclid(c) as u32, 7, seed);
    a + (b - a) * f
}

fn value(x: usize, y: usize) -> f32 {
    let (fx, fy) = (x as f32, y as f32);
    // Blotchy rock: fBm, contrast stretched (light blue patches on grey-blue).
    let mut base = 0.0;
    let mut amp = 0.5;
    let mut norm = 0.0;
    for (k, cells) in [16u32, 32, 64, 128].iter().enumerate() {
        base += amp * noise2(fx, fy, *cells, 11 + k as u32);
        norm += amp;
        amp *= 0.75;
    }
    let b = smooth(((base / norm - 0.28) / 0.44).clamp(0.0, 1.0));
    // Thin dark cracks rising to the right like the game's stone: ridges of a 1D noise along t = x + 2y (constant
    // along (2, -1); integer coefficients keep the tile periodic), warped and broken up by 2D noise.
    let warp = (noise2(fx, fy, 32, 31) - 0.5) * 10.0;
    let t = (x as i64 + 2 * y as i64) as f32 + warp;
    let r = (noise1(t, 160, 3) - 0.5).abs();
    let crack = (1.0 - r / 0.06).clamp(0.0, 1.0) * smooth(((noise2(fx, fy, 32, 41) - 0.15) / 0.3).clamp(0.0, 1.0));
    let r2 = (noise1(t + 37.0, 256, 9) - 0.5).abs();
    let crack2 = (1.0 - r2 / 0.06).clamp(0.0, 1.0) * smooth(((noise2(fx, fy, 64, 43) - 0.2) / 0.3).clamp(0.0, 1.0));
    let grain = (noise2(fx, fy, 256, 99) - 0.5) * 0.22;
    (0.17 + 0.58 * b - 0.6 * crack - 0.45 * crack2 + grain).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
}

fn ramp(v: f32) -> [u8; 3] {
    for w in RAMP.windows(2) {
        let ((a, ca), (b, cb)) = (w[0], w[1]);
        if v <= b {
            let t = ((v - a) / (b - a)).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
            return [0, 1, 2].map(|i| (ca[i] + (cb[i] - ca[i]) * t).round() as u8);
        }
    }
    RAMP[RAMP.len() - 1].1.map(|c| c as u8)
}

/// The tile as RGBA8 rows (`TILE * TILE * 4` bytes), generated once.
pub fn tile_rgba() -> &'static [u8] {
    static T: OnceLock<Vec<u8>> = OnceLock::new();
    T.get_or_init(|| {
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(TILE * TILE * 4);
        for y in 0..TILE {
            for x in 0..TILE {
                let [r, g, b] = ramp(value(x, y));
                out.extend_from_slice(&[r, g, b, 255]);
            }
        }
        out
    })
}

/// Texel at (x, y) (wrapped) as XRGB8888.
pub fn texel_xrgb(x: i64, y: i64) -> u32 {
    let t = tile_rgba();
    let (x, y) = (x.rem_euclid(TILE as i64) as usize, y.rem_euclid(TILE as i64) as usize);
    let i = (y * TILE + x) * 4;
    ((t[i] as u32) << 16) | ((t[i + 1] as u32) << 8) | t[i + 2] as u32
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn tile_wraps_seamlessly() {
        // Neighbouring texels across the wrap differ about as much as inside the tile.
        let d = |a: u32, b: u32| ((a >> 16 & 255) as i32 - (b >> 16 & 255) as i32).abs();
        let mut edge = 0;
        let mut inner = 0;
        for y in 0..TILE as i64 {
            edge += d(texel_xrgb(TILE as i64 - 1, y), texel_xrgb(TILE as i64, y));
            inner += d(texel_xrgb(100, y), texel_xrgb(101, y));
        }
        assert!(edge < inner * 2 + TILE as i32, "edge {edge} inner {inner}");
        assert_eq!(tile_rgba().len(), TILE * TILE * 4);
    }
}
```
