`port/crates/s3-mods/src/ui_hud_minimap.rs`:

```rs
//! Mobile HUD minimap widget + full-screen map overlay (docs/porting/ui-hud.md "Minimap").
//!
//! The game keeps its minimap as a square RGB565 image of `mw x mw` pixels (`mw = [0x730f28]`) at
//! `[snap+0x4c]` (`snap` = the per-frame render snapshot, argument of the panel renderer `0x4b4d00`). Image column
//! `c` / row `r` is tile `(c*W/mw, r*W/mw)` (W = world size in tiles). The frame renderer `0x4b26c0` draws it
//! sheared: screen `x = mx + (mw - r - 1)/2 + c`, `y = my + r` (blocks `0x4b2b34..0x4b2ce5` and
//! `0x4b366a..0x4b3cf3`, which also draw the frame art and the white camera rectangle). In HUD mode those blocks
//! are skipped (`ui_hud_game`) and this module draws the same image itself, in the same sheared shape, from guest
//! memory (nothing shipped). Camera rectangle, in image coordinates, as the game computes it at `0x4b3a3c`:
//! `k = (mw << 8) / [snap+0x2c]`, `x = ([snap+0x24] + 11)*k >> 8`, `y = ([snap+0x28] + 16)*k >> 8`,
//! `w = [snap+0x30]*k >> 8`, `h = ([snap+0x34] - 40)*k >> 8` (`>>` = signed division by 256).
//!
//! Pure presentation + `gd::CenterOn` queued on the logic thread (the same call the game's minimap click makes),
//! so lockstep multiplayer is unaffected.

use s3_runtime::Machine;

use crate::layer::{ImageRef, Layer};
use crate::overlay::{Image, Rgba};
use crate::ui_hud_game::{self as game, readable};

/// Minimap data read from the game (host copy).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Default)]
pub struct MiniData {
    /// Image side in pixels (`[0x730f28]`).
    pub n: u32,
    /// `n * n` RGB565 pixels, row-major.
    pub pixels: Vec<u16>,
    /// World size in tiles.
    pub world: u32,
    /// Camera rectangle in image coordinates (x, y, w, h).
    pub cam: (i32, i32, i32, i32),
}

/// Signed `a >> 8` the way MSVC emits it (`cdq; and edx, 0xff; add; sar 8` = truncating division by 256).
fn div256(a: i32) -> i32 {
    a / 256
}

/// The game's camera rectangle formula (`0x4b3a3c..`), in image coordinates.
pub fn cam_rect(n: u32, s24: i32, s28: i32, s2c: u32, s30: i32, s34: i32) -> (i32, i32, i32, i32) {
    if s2c == 0 {
        return (0, 0, 0, 0);
    }
    let k = ((n << 8) / s2c) as i32;
    (
        div256((s24 + 11).wrapping_mul(k)),
        div256((s28 + 16).wrapping_mul(k)),
        div256(s30.wrapping_mul(k)),
        div256((s34 - 40).wrapping_mul(k)),
    )
}

/// Read the minimap image and camera rectangle (`None` if no game / snapshot yet).
pub fn read(m: &mut Machine) -> Option<MiniData> {
    let snap = m.state::<game::HudShared>().borrow_mut().snap;
    if snap == 0 || !readable(m, snap, 0x50) {
        return None;
    }
    let n = m.mem.read_u32(game::L_MINI_W);
    if !(16..=512).contains(&n) {
        return None;
    }
    let img = m.mem.read_u32(snap + 0x4c);
    let len = n * n * 2;
    if !readable(m, img, len) {
        return None;
    }
    let bytes = m.mem.slice(img, len as usize);
    let pixels: Vec<u16> = bytes.chunks_exact(2).map(|b| u16::from_le_bytes([b[0], b[1]])).collect();
    let g = game::gd(m)?;
    let world = m.mem.read_u32(g + game::GD_WORLD_W);
    if world == 0 || world > 1024 {
        return None;
    }
    let r = |o: u32| m.mem.read_u32(snap + o);
    let cam = cam_rect(n, r(0x24) as i32, r(0x28) as i32, r(0x2c), r(0x30) as i32, r(0x34) as i32);
    Some(MiniData { n, pixels, world, cam })
}

/// Where a map image is drawn: the sheared parallelogram of an `n x n` image scaled by `s` with its bounding box
/// at `(x, y)` (box size `1.5*n*s x n*s`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub struct MapGeom {
    pub x: f32,
    pub y: f32,
    pub s: f32,
    pub n: u32,
}

impl MapGeom {
    /// The largest geometry that fits `(x, y, w, h)`, centred.
    pub fn fit(n: u32, x: i32, y: i32, w: i32, h: i32) -> MapGeom {
        let nf = n.max(1) as f32;
        let s = (w as f32 / (1.5 * nf)).min(h as f32 / nf).max(0.01);
        let (bw, bh) = (1.5 * nf * s, nf * s);
        MapGeom { x: x as f32 + (w as f32 - bw) / 2.0, y: y as f32 + (h as f32 - bh) / 2.0, s, n }
    }
    pub fn box_size(&self) -> (f32, f32) {
        (1.5 * self.n as f32 * self.s, self.n as f32 * self.s)
    }
    /// Image point (col, row) -> screen.
    pub fn to_screen(&self, c: f32, r: f32) -> (f32, f32) {
        let n = self.n as f32;
        (self.x + ((n - r) / 2.0 + c) * self.s, self.y + r * self.s)
    }
    /// Screen -> image point (col, row), `None` outside the parallelogram.
    pub fn to_image(&self, sx: f32, sy: f32) -> Option<(f32, f32)> {
        let n = self.n as f32;
        let r = (sy - self.y) / self.s;
        let c = (sx - self.x) / self.s - (n - r) / 2.0;
        if r < 0.0 || r >= n || c < 0.0 || c >= n {
            return None;
        }
        Some((c, r))
    }
    /// Is the screen point inside the bounding box (a touch slightly outside the parallelogram still counts)?
    pub fn in_box(&self, sx: f32, sy: f32) -> bool {
        let (w, h) = self.box_size();
        sx >= self.x && sy >= self.y && sx < self.x + w && sy < self.y + h
    }
    /// Screen point -> tile, clamped into the image (for touches near the parallelogram's slanted edges).
    pub fn to_tile_clamped(&self, sx: f32, sy: f32, world: u32) -> (u32, u32) {
        let n = self.n as f32;
        let r = ((sy - self.y) / self.s).clamp(0.0, n - 0.01);
        let c = ((sx - self.x) / self.s - (n - r) / 2.0).clamp(0.0, n - 0.01);
        image_to_tile(c, r, self.n, world)
    }
}

/// Image point -> tile.
pub fn image_to_tile(c: f32, r: f32, n: u32, world: u32) -> (u32, u32) {
    let k = world as f32 / n.max(1) as f32;
    let w1 = world.saturating_sub(1);
    (((c * k) as u32).min(w1), ((r * k) as u32).min(w1))
}

/// The minimap pixels as an opaque RGBA image (for the window layer).
pub fn to_image(d: &MiniData) -> Image {
    let n = d.n;
    let mut img = Image::new(n, n);
    for (i, &p) in d.pixels.iter().take((n * n) as usize).enumerate() {
        let (r, g, b) = s3_runtime::host::rgb565_to_rgb888(p);
        img.rgba[i * 4..i * 4 + 4].copy_from_slice(&[r, g, b, 255]);
    }
    img
}

/// Draw the image (`img` = [`to_image`] of `d`, nearest sampling, the game's sheared shape) and the camera rectangle.
pub fn draw(c: &mut Layer, img: &ImageRef, d: &MiniData, g: &MapGeom, cam_color: Rgba) {
    if img.width != d.n {
        return;
    }
    c.blit_map(img, g.x, g.y, g.s);
    // Camera rectangle (a parallelogram on screen, like the game's white frame).
    let (cx, cy, cw, ch) = d.cam;
    if cw > 0 && ch > 0 {
        let pts = [
            g.to_screen(cx as f32, cy as f32),
            g.to_screen((cx + cw) as f32, cy as f32),
            g.to_screen((cx + cw) as f32, (cy + ch) as f32),
            g.to_screen(cx as f32, (cy + ch) as f32),
        ];
        let t = (g.s * 0.9).clamp(1.0, 3.0);
        for i in 0..4 {
            let (a, b) = (pts[i], pts[(i + 1) % 4]);
            thick_line(c, a.0, a.1, b.0, b.1, t, cam_color);
        }
    }
}

/// Outline of the parallelogram (frame around the map).
pub fn draw_outline(c: &mut Layer, g: &MapGeom, col: Rgba) {
    let n = g.n as f32;
    let pts = [g.to_screen(0.0, 0.0), g.to_screen(n, 0.0), g.to_screen(n, n), g.to_screen(0.0, n)];
    for i in 0..4 {
        let (a, b) = (pts[i], pts[(i + 1) % 4]);
        thick_line(c, a.0, a.1, b.0, b.1, 1.0, col);
    }
}

fn thick_line(c: &mut Layer, x0: f32, y0: f32, x1: f32, y1: f32, t: f32, col: Rgba) {
    c.line(x0, y0, x1, y1, t, col);
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn geom_roundtrip() {
        let g = MapGeom::fit(128, 10, 20, 300, 200);
        let (w, h) = g.box_size();
        assert!(w <= 300.0 + 0.01 && h <= 200.0 + 0.01);
        for &(c, r) in &[(0.5, 0.5), (64.0, 64.0), (127.0, 3.0), (5.0, 120.0)] {
            let (sx, sy) = g.to_screen(c, r);
            let (c2, r2) = g.to_image(sx, sy).unwrap();
            assert!((c - c2).abs() < 0.01 && (r - r2).abs() < 0.01, "{c},{r} -> {c2},{r2}");
        }
        // Top-left corner of the bounding box is outside the sheared shape.
        assert!(g.to_image(g.x + 1.0, g.y + 1.0).is_none());
        assert!(g.in_box(g.x + 1.0, g.y + 1.0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn same_shear_as_game() {
        // The game: x = mx + (mw - r - 1)/2 + c. Ours with s = 1, x = mx: x = mx + (mw - r)/2 + c (half a pixel
        // to the right, pixel centres).
        let g = MapGeom { x: 5.0, y: 10.0, s: 1.0, n: 128 };
        let (sx, sy) = g.to_screen(10.0, 20.0);
        assert_eq!(sy, 30.0);
        assert_eq!(sx, 5.0 + (128.0 - 20.0) / 2.0 + 10.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn tiles() {
        assert_eq!(image_to_tile(64.0, 32.0, 128, 384), (192, 96));
        assert_eq!(image_to_tile(127.99, 127.99, 128, 384), (383, 383));
        let g = MapGeom { x: 0.0, y: 0.0, s: 2.0, n: 128 };
        // Far left of the box: clamped to column 0.
        assert_eq!(g.to_tile_clamped(0.0, 0.0, 384).0, 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn cam_formula() {
        // 128 px image, 384 world: k = 85.
        assert_eq!(cam_rect(128, 0, 0, 384, 0, 40), (11 * 85 / 256, 16 * 85 / 256, 0, 0));
        assert_eq!(cam_rect(128, 1, 1, 0, 1, 1), (0, 0, 0, 0));
        assert_eq!(div256(-255), 0);
        assert_eq!(div256(-256), -1);
    }
}

```

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/unit_orders.rs`:

```rs
//! Unit orders for touch, shared by both UI modes (docs/porting/touch.md "Unit orders, paths, groups"; RE in
//! docs/reverse-engineering/game-state-units.md "Orders, waypoints, patrol" and "Control groups"). GOG S3.EXE only.
//!
//! - **Orders** the PC game gives with a modifier + right click on the map while units are selected:
//!   Shift = add a waypoint (up to three after the normal move), Alt = patrol between the current position and the
//!   target, Ctrl = move ignoring enemies on the way. [`arm`] makes the next map tap a right click with that key
//!   held (the touch->mouse fallback sends key down, click, key up), so the game builds its own command
//!   (0x0d / 0x0e / 0x0f) exactly like on a PC. "Waypoint" stays armed for the following taps (up to four: the
//!   first tap of an idle group is a normal move) until its button is tapped again.
//!   Mode B (Mobile HUD) shows the buttons in its selection card (`ui_hud.rs`), mode A (Classic Touch) gets a
//!   column below the Deselect ✕ drawn here.
//! - **Paths**: dotted, marching lines from each unit to its target and on through its queued waypoints (patrol
//!   routes as a loop), for the selected units, and for every own unit under a move order when the setting
//!   `show_unit_paths` is on. Read from the settler table (+0x24 target, +0x30..+0x3b waypoint queue), drawn in
//!   the window layer with the game's own map -> screen transform.
//! - **Control groups** (setting `group_shortcuts`): buttons 1..6. Tap = the game's "key n" (`0x542660`: select
//!   group n; tapping it again while it is selected centres the camera on it), long press = "Alt + n"
//!   (`0x542820`: assign the current selection to group n). Both are called on the logic thread at
//!   `HandleInput` entry, like the key handler does; non-empty groups are highlighted.

use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, Ordering};

use s3_runtime::{FrameBuffer, HookFlow, LogLevel, Machine};

use crate::gesture::TouchEvent;
use crate::layer::Layer;
use crate::overlay::{measure_text, Rgba, Weight};
use crate::settings::UiMode;
use crate::touch_game as game;
use crate::{Mod, ModEvent, ModsState};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- addresses (GOG exe only)

/// `CLogicThread::HandleInput` (thiscall logic), logic thread, every tick in game.
const HANDLE_INPUT: u32 = 0x0052_4fa0;
/// `CLogicThread::SelectGroup(n)` (thiscall logic, ret 4): digit key without Alt (`0x525cfa`).
pub const FN_SELECT_GROUP: u32 = 0x0054_2660;
/// `CLogicThread::AssignGroup(n)` (thiscall logic, ret 4): Alt + digit (`0x525cf0`).
pub const FN_ASSIGN_GROUP: u32 = 0x0054_2820;
const SEL_SLOT: u32 = 0x007d_fd68;
const SEL_COUNT: u32 = 0x007a_d620;
/// Resolution index 1..3 (`0x4c6d70` layout table).
const L_RES: u32 = 0x0073_0f08;
const GD_CAM_X: u32 = 0x2d254;
const GD_CAM_Y: u32 = 0x2d258;
const GD_PAGE: u32 = 0x2d284;
const GD_WORLD: u32 = 0x2d2d0;
const GD_LOCAL_PLAYER: u32 = 0x2d2d4;
const GD_TILES: u32 = 0x67444;
const GD_SETTLERS: u32 = 0x12a5e60;
const GD_SETTLERS_MAX: u32 = 0x12a5e5c;

/// Number of group buttons (the game has 1..9).
pub const GROUPS: u32 = 6;
/// A logic tick within this many ms means a game is running.
const IN_GAME_MS: u64 = 1500;
/// Settler job "walking on a player's order" (`+0x0e`; 0x37 = idle soldier). VERIFIED 2026-11-08.
const JOB_ORDERED_WALK: u16 = 0x35;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- orders

/// A modifier order (PC: modifier + right click).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Order {
    /// Shift: queue a waypoint (command 0x0d).
    Waypoint,
    /// Alt: patrol between here and the target (command 0x0e).
    Patrol,
    /// Ctrl: move, ignoring enemies on the way (command 0x0f).
    NoFight,
}

impl Order {
    pub const ALL: [Order; 3] = [Order::Waypoint, Order::Patrol, Order::NoFight];

    /// Windows VK of the modifier the game reads (`0x45b370`: Shift 1, Alt 2, Ctrl 4 in the event's modifier byte).
    pub fn vk(self) -> u32 {
        match self {
            Order::Waypoint => 0x10,
            Order::Patrol => 0x12,
            Order::NoFight => 0x11,
        }
    }

    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Order::Waypoint => "Waypoint",
            Order::Patrol => "Patrol",
            Order::NoFight => "No fight",
        }
    }

    pub fn hint(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Order::Waypoint => "Tap the next waypoint",
            Order::Patrol => "Tap the far end of the patrol",
            Order::NoFight => "Tap the target (no fighting on the way)",
        }
    }

    fn from_vk(vk: u32) -> Option<Order> {
        Order::ALL.into_iter().find(|o| o.vk() == vk)
    }
}

/// Taps "Waypoint" stays armed for: the first move of an idle group plus the game's three waypoints.
const WAYPOINT_TAPS: u32 = 4;

/// Arm `o` for the next map tap (or disarm if it is armed already). Returns whether it is armed now.
pub fn arm(m: &mut Machine, o: Order) -> bool {
    let on = armed(m) != Some(o);
    m.state::<OrdersShared>().borrow_mut().sticky = (on && o == Order::Waypoint).then_some(WAYPOINT_TAPS - 1);
    if on {
        crate::set_order_next(m, o.vk());
    } else {
        crate::set_right_next(m, false);
    }
    on
}

/// The order armed for the next map tap, if any.
pub fn armed(m: &mut Machine) -> Option<Order> {
    let (on, vk) = crate::order_next(m);
    if on {
        Order::from_vk(vk)
    } else {
        None
    }
}

/// Disarm (selection gone, UI mode changed).
pub fn disarm(m: &mut Machine) {
    if armed(m).is_some() {
        crate::set_right_next(m, false);
    }
    m.state::<OrdersShared>().borrow_mut().sticky = None;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- shared state (hook <-> mod)

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum GroupAction {
    Select(u32),
    Assign(u32),
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct OrdersShared {
    last_tick_ms: u64,
    pending: Vec<GroupAction>,
    /// Remaining extra taps "Waypoint" is re-armed for.
    sticky: Option<u32>,
    hooked: bool,
}

/// Install the hook (GOG exe with its patch set) and the mod. Before the UI modes: they get touches first and
/// draw on top (HUD sheets cover the group buttons).
pub fn install(m: &mut Machine, gog: bool) {
    if gog {
        crate::hooks::add_hook(m, HANDLE_INPUT, "unit-orders:logic", |c| {
            let logic = c.reg(s3_cpu::ECX);
            on_logic_tick(c.m, logic);
            HookFlow::Continue
        });
        m.state::<OrdersShared>().borrow_mut().hooked = true;
    }
    crate::add_mod(m, Box::new(UnitOrders::default()));
}

fn on_logic_tick(m: &mut Machine, logic: u32) {
    let now = m.real_ms();
    let st = m.state::<OrdersShared>();
    let pending = {
        let mut s = st.borrow_mut();
        s.last_tick_ms = now;
        if s.pending.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        std::mem::take(&mut s.pending)
    };
    for a in pending {
        match a {
            GroupAction::Select(n) => {
                crate::call::call_thiscall(m, FN_SELECT_GROUP, logic, &[n]);
            }
            GroupAction::Assign(n) => {
                // The game copies the current slot's ids; only with a unit selection (slot 0..9, count > 0).
                let slot = m.mem.read_i32(SEL_SLOT);
                if (0..10).contains(&slot) && m.mem.read_u16(SEL_COUNT + slot as u32 * 2) > 0 {
                    crate::call::call_thiscall(m, FN_ASSIGN_GROUP, logic, &[n]);
                }
            }
        }
        m.log(LogLevel::Debug, &format!("unit-orders: {a:?}"));
    }
}

/// Units in group `n` (1..9) as the game keeps them (`word [0x7ad620 + n*2]`; may include fallen soldiers).
pub fn group_count(m: &Machine, n: u32) -> u32 {
    if !(1..10).contains(&n) {
        return 0;
    }
    m.mem.read_u16(SEL_COUNT + n * 2) as u32
}

/// Current selection slot (-1 none, 0 plain selection, 1..9 a group).
pub fn current_slot(m: &Machine) -> i32 {
    m.mem.read_i32(SEL_SLOT)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- paths (pure parts, unit tested)

/// One settler's order route in tiles.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Default)]
pub struct Route {
    pub pos: (u16, u16),
    /// Target, then queued waypoints (in order).
    pub points: Vec<(u16, u16)>,
    /// Patrol between these two tiles (after reaching `points`).
    pub patrol: Option<((u16, u16), (u16, u16))>,
}

/// Waypoint slot value: empty.
const WP_EMPTY: u16 = 0xffff;
/// Settler types the player can select and order (soldiers of all levels, priest, geologist, thief, pioneer, war
/// machines, ships; game-state-units.md "Settler types").
pub fn selectable_type(t: u8) -> bool {
    matches!(t, 0x05 | 0x08 | 0x0f | 0x1e..=0x24 | 0x16 | 0x17 | 0x28 | 0x29 | 0x2b | 0x2c)
}

/// Third waypoint slot = this marks a patrol (`0x536c01`).
const WP_PATROL: u16 = 0xfffe;

/// Route from a settler entry (0x40 bytes). `force` = show even without a player's order (selected units).
pub fn route_from_entry(e: &[u8], world: u16, force: bool) -> Option<Route> {
    if e.len() < 0x40 {
        return None;
    }
    let w = |o: usize| u16::from_le_bytes([e[o], e[o + 1]]);
    let ok = |x: u16, y: u16| x < world && y < world && (x, y) != (0, 0);
    let pos = (w(4), w(6));
    if !ok(pos.0, pos.1) {
        return None;
    }
    let job = w(0x0e);
    let tgt = (w(0x24), w(0x26));
    let wp = [(w(0x30), w(0x32)), (w(0x34), w(0x36)), (w(0x38), w(0x3a))];
    let mut r = Route { pos, ..Default::default() };
    let ordered = job == JOB_ORDERED_WALK;
    if ordered || force {
        if ok(tgt.0, tgt.1) && tgt != pos {
            r.points.push(tgt);
        }
    }
    if wp[2] == (WP_PATROL, WP_PATROL) {
        if ok(wp[0].0, wp[0].1) && ok(wp[1].0, wp[1].1) {
            r.patrol = Some((wp[0], wp[1]));
        }
    } else if ordered || force {
        for &(x, y) in &wp {
            if x == WP_EMPTY || !ok(x, y) {
                break;
            }
            r.points.push((x, y));
        }
    }
    (!r.points.is_empty() || r.patrol.is_some()).then_some(r)
}

/// Map tile -> game screen pixel (the unit's feet), the inverse of `gd::ScreenToMap` (`0x4ff170`) for the
/// original layout: `sx = 16x - 8y - camX + 8W + 280 + 32 res`, `sy = 9y - h - camY + 182` (`h` = tile height,
/// `camX/Y` = `[gd+0x2d254/8]`, `W` = world size, `res` = `[0x730f08]`). VERIFIED against the hit list: exact for
/// 14 of 14 units (2026-11-08).
pub fn tile_to_screen(x: i32, y: i32, h: i32, cam: (i32, i32), world: i32, res: i32) -> (i32, i32) {
    (16 * x - 8 * y - cam.0 + 8 * world + 280 + 32 * res, 9 * y - h - cam.1 + 182)
}

/// Points every `step` px along a polyline, shifted by `phase` (0..step): the marching dots.
pub fn dots_along(pts: &[(f32, f32)], step: f32, phase: f32) -> Vec<(f32, f32)> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    if step <= 0.5 {
        return out;
    }
    let mut carry = phase.rem_euclid(step);
    for s in pts.windows(2) {
        let (a, b) = (s[0], s[1]);
        let len = ((b.0 - a.0).powi(2) + (b.1 - a.1).powi(2)).sqrt();
        let mut t = carry;
        while t < len {
            let k = t / len;
            out.push((a.0 + (b.0 - a.0) * k, a.1 + (b.1 - a.1) * k));
            if out.len() > 4000 {
                return out;
            }
            t += step;
        }
        carry = t - len;
    }
    out
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the mod

/// One group button touch: (pointer, group, down ms, long press fired).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
struct GroupPress {
    id: u32,
    n: u32,
    t0: u64,
    fired: bool,
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct UnitOrders {
    in_game: bool,
    now: u64,
    mode: UiMode,
    show_paths: crate::settings::PathMode,
    /// The game layout matches the shown frame (map coordinates usable for the paths).
    layout_ok: bool,
    groups_on: bool,
    long_press_ms: u64,
    /// Units selected (page 5) right now.
    units_selected: bool,
    press: Option<GroupPress>,
    /// Order button pressed (pointer id, order).
    order_press: Option<(u32, Order)>,
    toast: Option<(String, u64)>,
    /// Map x offset of the hit list against [`tile_to_screen`] (the HUD's full-screen layout moves the map), from
    /// the last frame with units on screen.
    x_off: Option<i32>,
    dirty: bool,
    /// Last armed order seen (to notice the fallback taking it).
    last_armed: Option<Order>,
}

static DRAWN_PATHS: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);

/// Routes drawn in the last frame (tests / debugging).
pub fn drawn_paths() -> u32 {
    DRAWN_PATHS.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
}

impl UnitOrders {
    fn q(&self, m: &mut Machine, v: f32) -> i32 {
        let vp = crate::draw_viewport(m);
        (v * vp.win_h as f32 / 600.0).round() as i32
    }

    /// Group buttons in window pixels.
    fn group_rects(&self, m: &mut Machine) -> Vec<(u32, (i32, i32, i32, i32))> {
        if !self.groups_on || !self.in_game {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        let vp = crate::draw_viewport(m);
        // Window rect, not the shown frame's: that moves with the zoom (crop / bars), the buttons must not
        // (user report 2026-11-08).
        let (vx, vy, vw, vh) = (0, 0, vp.win_w as i32, vp.win_h as i32);
        if vw < 160 || vh < 120 {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        let (x0, y, bw, bh, gap) = match self.mode {
            UiMode::MobileHud => {
                // Same scale as the HUD (`ui_hud::MobileHud::k`): row right above the bottom bar, right of the
                // minimap card; above the minimap card when the selection card would be in the way.
                let (bar, _) = crate::ui_hud::bar_and_strip_h(m, vw, vh);
                let k = bar as f32 / 54.0;
                let u = |v: f32| (v * k).round() as i32;
                let (bw, bh, gap) = (u(40.0), u(34.0), u(5.0));
                let row_w = GROUPS as i32 * (bw + gap);
                let mini_w = u(96.0) * 3 / 2 + u(10.0);
                let x = vx + u(6.0) + mini_w + u(8.0);
                let card_left = vx + vw - u(256.0);
                let bottom = vy + vh - bar - u(6.0);
                // Same place with and without a selection (the card appears with one).
                if x + row_w <= card_left {
                    (x, bottom - bh, bw, bh, gap)
                } else {
                    (vx + u(6.0), bottom - u(106.0) - u(6.0) - bh, bw, bh, gap)
                }
            }
            UiMode::ClassicTouch => {
                // Bottom of the map, right of the panel; the Menu / speed buttons sit bottom right.
                let q = |v: f32| (v * vp.win_h as f32 / 600.0).round() as i32;
                let (bw, bh, gap) = (q(46.0), q(40.0), q(8.0));
                // Right edge of the panel, from the window height alone: the panel (`res::CLASSIC_VARIANT`) is
                // always drawn full window height (`display::Viewport::split`), so this never moves with the zoom
                // (the shown frame's split can be missing for a frame during a zoom step: jitter, 2026-11-08).
                let v = crate::res::CLASSIC_VARIANT;
                let x = (v.panel_w as f32 * vp.win_h as f32 / v.h as f32).round() as i32 + q(10.0);
                (x.max(vx + q(8.0)), vy + vh - bh - q(14.0), bw, bh, gap)
            }
        };
        (1..=GROUPS).map(|n| (n, (x0 + (n as i32 - 1) * (bw + gap), y, bw, bh))).collect()
    }

    /// Order buttons of mode A (a column below the Deselect ✕, top right), window pixels.
    fn order_rects(&self, m: &mut Machine) -> Vec<(Order, (i32, i32, i32, i32))> {
        if !self.in_game || self.mode != UiMode::ClassicTouch || !self.units_selected {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        let vp = crate::draw_viewport(m);
        let u = vp.win_h as f32 / 600.0;
        let top = match crate::display::display_settings(m).fps_counter {
            crate::display::FpsCounter::Off => 0.0,
            crate::display::FpsCounter::Fps => 22.0,
            crate::display::FpsCounter::Detailed => 62.0,
        };
        let (cx, cy, cw, ch) = crate::touch_fx::cancel_rect(vp.dst_rect_clipped(), top, u);
        let q = |v: f32| (v * u).round() as i32;
        let (bw, bh) = (q(104.0), q(38.0));
        let right = cx + cw;
        // Below the ✕ and its "Deselect" caption.
        let mut y = cy + ch + q(26.0);
        let mut v = Vec::new();
        for o in Order::ALL {
            v.push((o, (right - bw, y, bw, bh)));
            y += bh + q(8.0);
        }
        v
    }

    fn group_at(&self, m: &mut Machine, x: f32, y: f32) -> Option<u32> {
        let e = self.q(m, 3.0);
        self.group_rects(m).into_iter().find_map(|(n, r)| inside(r, x, y, e).then_some(n))
    }

    fn order_at(&self, m: &mut Machine, x: f32, y: f32) -> Option<Order> {
        let e = self.q(m, 4.0);
        self.order_rects(m).into_iter().find_map(|(o, r)| inside(r, x, y, e).then_some(o))
    }

    fn set_toast(&mut self, t: String) {
        self.toast = Some((t, self.now + 1800));
        self.dirty = true;
    }

    fn queue(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, a: GroupAction) {
        m.state::<OrdersShared>().borrow_mut().pending.push(a);
    }

    fn refresh(&mut self, m: &mut Machine) {
        let (last, hooked) = {
            let st = m.state::<OrdersShared>();
            let s = st.borrow_mut();
            (s.last_tick_ms, s.hooked)
        };
        let (frame, settings) = {
            let st = m.state::<ModsState>();
            let s = st.borrow_mut();
            (s.frame_size, s.settings.clone())
        };
        self.mode = settings.ui_mode;
        self.show_paths = settings.unit_paths;
        self.groups_on = settings.group_shortcuts;
        self.long_press_ms = settings.touch.long_press_ms.max(150);
        let gd = game::gd(m);
        let lay = game::layout(m);
        // During a zoom step the layout globals already have the next size while the old frame is shown: still in
        // game (the buttons must not blink, 2026-11-08), only the paths (map coordinates) wait for a match.
        self.layout_ok = lay.is_some_and(|l| (l.screen_w as u32, l.screen_h as u32) == frame);
        let in_frame = self.layout_ok || crate::res::in_game_frame(m);
        self.in_game = hooked && gd.is_some() && lay.is_some() && in_frame && self.now.saturating_sub(last) < IN_GAME_MS;
        self.units_selected = self.in_game
            && gd.is_some_and(|g| m.mem.read_u32(g + GD_PAGE) == 5)
            && game::selection_count(m) > 0;
    }

    /// Routes to draw: selected units (always) plus every own unit walking to a target with `show_paths`.
    fn routes(&self, m: &Machine, gd: u32) -> Vec<(Route, bool)> {
        let world = m.mem.read_u32(gd + GD_WORLD).min(1024) as u16;
        let me = m.mem.read_u32(gd + GD_LOCAL_PLAYER) as u8;
        let max = m.mem.read_u32(gd + GD_SETTLERS_MAX).min(60_000);
        let sel = game::selection(m);
        let entry = |id: u32| m.mem.read_bytes(gd + GD_SETTLERS + id * 0x40, 0x40);
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for &id in &sel {
            if (id as u32) == 0 || id as u32 > max {
                continue;
            }
            let e = entry(id as u32);
            if e[0] == me {
                if let Some(r) = route_from_entry(&e, world, true) {
                    out.push((r, true));
                }
            }
        }
        if self.show_paths != crate::settings::PathMode::Selected {
            let units_only = self.show_paths == crate::settings::PathMode::Units;
            for id in 1..=max {
                let a = gd + GD_SETTLERS + id * 0x40;
                if m.mem.read_u8(a) != me || sel.contains(&(id as u16)) {
                    continue;
                }
                // Every own unit on its way somewhere (carriers and workers too, not only player orders; user report
                // 2026-11-08). Cheap pre-check before copying the entry: a target other than the position, or a
                // patrol marker.
                let (px, py, tx, ty) = (m.mem.read_u16(a + 4), m.mem.read_u16(a + 6), m.mem.read_u16(a + 0x24), m.mem.read_u16(a + 0x26));
                let moving = (tx, ty) != (px, py) && (tx, ty) != (0, 0) && tx < world && ty < world;
                if units_only && !selectable_type(m.mem.read_u8(a + 1)) {
                    continue;
                }
                if !moving && m.mem.read_u16(a + 0x38) != WP_PATROL {
                    continue;
                }
                if let Some(r) = route_from_entry(&entry(id), world, true) {
                    out.push((r, false));
                }
                if out.len() > 400 {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        out
    }

    fn draw_paths(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, c: &mut Layer) {
        DRAWN_PATHS.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
        let Some(gd) = game::gd(m) else { return };
        let Some(l) = game::layout(m) else { return };
        let routes = self.routes(m, gd);
        if routes.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        let world = m.mem.read_u32(gd + GD_WORLD) as i32;
        let cam = (m.mem.read_u32(gd + GD_CAM_X) as i32, m.mem.read_u32(gd + GD_CAM_Y) as i32);
        let res = m.mem.read_u32(L_RES) as i32;
        // Calibrate x against the hit list (units on screen); the HUD's full-screen map shifts the view.
        let hits = game::hits(m, gd);
        let mut dxs: Vec<i32> = hits
            .iter()
            .filter(|h| !h.is_building())
            .filter_map(|h| {
                let a = gd + GD_SETTLERS + h.id as u32 * 0x40;
                let (tx, ty) = (m.mem.read_u16(a + 4) as i32, m.mem.read_u16(a + 6) as i32);
                (tx < world && ty < world).then(|| h.x - tile_to_screen(tx, ty, 0, cam, world, res).0)
            })
            .take(40)
            .collect();
        if !dxs.is_empty() {
            dxs.sort_unstable();
            self.x_off = Some(dxs[dxs.len() / 2]);
        }
        let x_off = self.x_off.unwrap_or_else(|| {
            if crate::ui_hud_game::full_layout_active(m) {
                -(crate::ui_hud_game::current_original_layout(m).map_or(0, |(pw, _)| pw as i32))
            } else {
                0
            }
        });
        let vp = crate::draw_viewport(m);
        let height = |x: u16, y: u16| m.mem.read_u8(gd + GD_TILES + (x as u32 * 768 + y as u32) * 0x18 + 4) as i32;
        let to_win = |p: (u16, u16)| {
            let (sx, sy) = tile_to_screen(p.0 as i32, p.1 as i32, height(p.0, p.1), cam, world, res);
            vp.game_to_window((sx + x_off) as f32, sy as f32)
        };
        let u = vp.win_h as f32 / 600.0;
        let mx = vp.game_to_window(l.panel_w as f32, 0.0).0.round() as i32;
        let (_, wy0, _, wh) = vp.dst_rect_clipped();
        c.set_clip(mx, wy0, c.width() as i32 - mx, wh);
        let step = 11.0 * u;
        let phase = (self.now % 1000) as f32 / 1000.0 * step;
        let mut ends: Vec<((u16, u16), bool, bool)> = Vec::new();
        for (r, sel) in &routes {
            let mut pts = vec![to_win(r.pos)];
            pts.extend(r.points.iter().map(|&p| to_win(p)));
            let (col, rad) = if *sel { (Rgba::rgba(255, 255, 255, 235), 2.4 * u) } else { (Rgba::rgba(235, 235, 200, 170), 1.8 * u) };
            for (x, y) in dots_along(&pts, step, phase) {
                c.fill_circle(x, y, rad + 1.2 * u, Rgba::rgba(0, 0, 0, 120));
                c.fill_circle(x, y, rad, col);
            }
            for (i, &p) in r.points.iter().enumerate() {
                ends.push((p, *sel, i + 1 == r.points.len() && r.patrol.is_none()));
            }
            if let Some((a, b)) = r.patrol {
                let (pa, pb) = (to_win(a), to_win(b));
                let pcol = Rgba::rgba(255, 196, 70, if *sel { 235 } else { 170 });
                let loop_pts = [pa, pb, pa];
                for (x, y) in dots_along(&loop_pts, step, phase) {
                    c.fill_circle(x, y, rad + 1.2 * u, Rgba::rgba(0, 0, 0, 120));
                    c.fill_circle(x, y, rad, pcol);
                }
                for p in [pa, pb] {
                    c.ring(p.0, p.1, 6.0 * u, 2.0 * u, pcol);
                }
            }
        }
        // Target / waypoint markers once per tile (a group's units share nearby tiles).
        ends.sort_by_key(|e| (e.0, !e.2));
        ends.dedup_by_key(|e| e.0);
        for (p, sel, last) in ends {
            let (x, y) = to_win(p);
            let a = if sel { 235 } else { 160 };
            if last {
                c.ring(x, y, 7.0 * u, 2.4 * u, Rgba::rgba(0, 0, 0, 120));
                c.ring(x, y, 6.0 * u, 2.0 * u, Rgba::rgba(120, 255, 120, a));
            } else {
                c.ring(x, y, 4.5 * u, 1.6 * u, Rgba::rgba(255, 255, 255, a));
            }
        }
        c.reset_clip();
        DRAWN_PATHS.store(routes.len() as u32, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }

    fn draw_groups(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, c: &mut Layer) {
        let rects = self.group_rects(m);
        if rects.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        let vp = crate::draw_viewport(m);
        let u = vp.win_h as f32 / 600.0;
        let cur = current_slot(m);
        let gold = Rgba::rgb(236, 196, 92);
        for (n, (x, y, w, h)) in rects {
            let count = group_count(m, n);
            let pressed = self.press.is_some_and(|p| p.n == n);
            let selected = cur == n as i32 && count > 0;
            let bg = if pressed {
                gold.fade(0.85)
            } else if selected {
                Rgba::rgba(120, 90, 30, 230)
            } else if count > 0 {
                Rgba::rgba(30, 26, 18, 215)
            } else {
                Rgba::rgba(20, 16, 10, 140)
            };
            let r = 8.0 * u;
            c.fill_rounded_rect(x, y, w, h, r, bg);
            c.stroke_rounded_rect(x, y, w, h, r, if selected { 2.5 * u } else { 1.5 * u }, if count > 0 { gold } else { gold.fade(0.45) });
            let fg = if pressed { Rgba::BLACK } else if count > 0 { Rgba::WHITE } else { Rgba::rgba(255, 255, 255, 120) };
            let px = (h as f32 * 0.5).max(10.0);
            if count > 0 {
                c.text_centered(x, y - (h as f32 * 0.16) as i32, w, h, px * 0.85, Weight::Bold, fg, &n.to_string());
                let small = (h as f32 * 0.25).max(8.0);
                c.text_centered(x, y + (h as f32 * 0.42) as i32, w, h - (h as f32 * 0.5) as i32, small, Weight::Regular, fg, &count.to_string());
            } else {
                c.text_centered(x, y, w, h, px, Weight::Bold, fg, &n.to_string());
            }
            // Long-press progress.
            if let Some(p) = self.press.filter(|p| p.n == n && !p.fired) {
                let k = (self.now.saturating_sub(p.t0) as f32 / self.long_press_ms as f32).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
                c.fill_rect(x + (4.0 * u) as i32, y + h - (5.0 * u) as i32, ((w as f32 - 8.0 * u) * k) as i32, (3.0 * u).max(1.0) as i32, Rgba::BLACK);
            }
        }
    }

    fn draw_orders(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, c: &mut Layer) {
        let rects = self.order_rects(m);
        if rects.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        let vp = crate::draw_viewport(m);
        let u = vp.win_h as f32 / 600.0;
        let armed = armed(m);
        let gold = Rgba::rgb(236, 196, 92);
        for (o, (x, y, w, h)) in rects {
            let on = armed == Some(o) || self.order_press.is_some_and(|p| p.1 == o);
            c.fill_rounded_rect(x, y, w, h, 9.0 * u, if on { gold.fade(0.9) } else { Rgba::rgba(20, 16, 10, 200) });
            c.stroke_rounded_rect(x, y, w, h, 9.0 * u, 2.0 * u, gold);
            c.text_centered(x, y, w, h, 16.0 * u, Weight::Bold, if on { Rgba::BLACK } else { Rgba::WHITE }, o.label());
        }
    }

    fn draw_hint(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, c: &mut Layer) {
        let vp = crate::draw_viewport(m);
        let u = vp.win_h as f32 / 600.0;
        let text = match (&self.toast, armed(m)) {
            (Some((t, until)), _) if self.now < *until => t.clone(),
            // Mode B shows its own toast for the order; mode A shows the hint while armed.
            (_, Some(o)) if self.mode == UiMode::ClassicTouch && self.units_selected => {
                let left = m.state::<OrdersShared>().borrow_mut().sticky.unwrap_or(0);
                if o == Order::Waypoint {
                    format!("{} ({} left)", o.hint(), left + 1)
                } else {
                    o.hint().to_string()
                }
            }
            _ => return,
        };
        let px = 15.0 * u;
        let (tw, th) = measure_text(px, Weight::Bold, &text);
        let (vx, vy, vw, vh) = vp.dst_rect_clipped();
        let (w, h) = (tw + (24.0 * u) as i32, th + (14.0 * u) as i32);
        let x = vx + (vw - w) / 2;
        let y = match self.group_rects(m).first() {
            Some(&(_, (_, gy, _, _))) => gy - h - (8.0 * u) as i32,
            None => vy + vh - h - (70.0 * u) as i32,
        };
        c.fill_rounded_rect(x, y, w, h, 8.0 * u, Rgba::rgba(20, 16, 10, 215));
        c.text(x + (12.0 * u) as i32, y + (7.0 * u) as i32, px, Weight::Bold, Rgba::rgb(236, 196, 92), &text);
    }
}

fn inside(r: (i32, i32, i32, i32), x: f32, y: f32, e: i32) -> bool {
    x >= (r.0 - e) as f32 && x < (r.0 + r.2 + e) as f32 && y >= (r.1 - e) as f32 && y < (r.1 + r.3 + e) as f32
}

impl Mod for UnitOrders {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        "unit-orders"
    }

    fn on_touch(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, ev: &TouchEvent) -> ModEvent {
        self.now = m.real_ms();
        match *ev {
            TouchEvent::Down { id, .. } => {
                self.refresh(m);
                if !self.in_game {
                    return ModEvent::Pass;
                }
                let (wx, wy) = crate::touch_window_pos(m, ev);
                if let Some(n) = self.group_at(m, wx, wy) {
                    self.press = Some(GroupPress { id, n, t0: self.now, fired: false });
                    self.dirty = true;
                    return ModEvent::Consumed;
                }
                if let Some(o) = self.order_at(m, wx, wy) {
                    self.order_press = Some((id, o));
                    self.dirty = true;
                    return ModEvent::Consumed;
                }
                ModEvent::Pass
            }
            TouchEvent::Move { id, .. } => {
                if self.press.is_some_and(|p| p.id == id) || self.order_press.is_some_and(|p| p.0 == id) {
                    return ModEvent::Consumed;
                }
                ModEvent::Pass
            }
            TouchEvent::Up { id, .. } => {
                let (wx, wy) = crate::touch_window_pos(m, ev);
                if let Some(p) = self.press.filter(|p| p.id == id) {
                    self.press = None;
                    self.dirty = true;
                    if !p.fired && self.group_at(m, wx, wy) == Some(p.n) {
                        if group_count(m, p.n) == 0 {
                            self.set_toast(format!("Group {} is empty: hold the button to assign the selection", p.n));
                        } else {
                            let again = current_slot(m) == p.n as i32;
                            self.queue(m, GroupAction::Select(p.n));
                            if again {
                                self.set_toast(format!("Group {}: camera centred", p.n));
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    return ModEvent::Consumed;
                }
                if let Some((pid, o)) = self.order_press.filter(|p| p.0 == id) {
                    self.order_press = None;
                    self.dirty = true;
                    let _ = pid;
                    if self.order_at(m, wx, wy) == Some(o) {
                        arm(m, o);
                    }
                    return ModEvent::Consumed;
                }
                ModEvent::Pass
            }
            TouchEvent::Cancel { id } => {
                if self.press.is_some_and(|p| p.id == id) {
                    self.press = None;
                }
                if self.order_press.is_some_and(|p| p.0 == id) {
                    self.order_press = None;
                }
                ModEvent::Pass
            }
            _ => ModEvent::Pass,
        }
    }

    fn tick(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, now: u64) {
        self.now = now;
        self.refresh(m);
        if !self.in_game {
            self.press = None;
            self.order_press = None;
            if self.last_armed.take().is_some() {
                disarm(m);
            }
            return;
        }
        // Long press on a group button = assign.
        if let Some(p) = self.press.as_mut() {
            if !p.fired && now.saturating_sub(p.t0) >= self.long_press_ms {
                p.fired = true;
                let n = p.n;
                let sel = game::selection_count(m);
                if self.units_selected && sel > 0 {
                    self.queue(m, GroupAction::Assign(n));
                    crate::haptics::touch(m);
                    self.set_toast(format!("Group {n}: {sel} units assigned"));
                } else {
                    self.set_toast("Select units first, then hold a group button".to_string());
                }
            }
            self.dirty = true;
        }
        // Order taps: the fallback clears "right click next" when it sends the order; re-arm a waypoint run.
        let a = armed(m);
        if a.is_none() {
            if let Some(Order::Waypoint) = self.last_armed {
                let st = m.state::<OrdersShared>();
                let left = st.borrow_mut().sticky;
                if let Some(left) = left.filter(|&l| l > 0 && self.units_selected) {
                    st.borrow_mut().sticky = Some(left - 1);
                    crate::set_order_next(m, Order::Waypoint.vk());
                } else {
                    st.borrow_mut().sticky = None;
                }
            }
        }
        if !self.units_selected && a.is_some() {
            disarm(m);
        }
        let a = armed(m);
        if a != self.last_armed {
            self.dirty = true;
        }
        self.last_armed = a;
    }

    fn wants_draw(&self) -> bool {
        self.in_game
    }

    fn needs_redraw(&self) -> bool {
        self.dirty || self.press.is_some()
    }

    fn draw_window(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, c: &mut Layer, _frame: &FrameBuffer) {
        self.dirty = false;
        if !self.in_game {
            return;
        }
        if self.layout_ok {
            self.draw_paths(m, c);
        }
        self.draw_groups(m, c);
        self.draw_orders(m, c);
        self.draw_hint(m, c);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn entry(pos: (u16, u16), job: u16, tgt: (u16, u16), wp: [(u16, u16); 3]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut e = vec![0u8; 0x40];
        let mut put = |o: usize, v: u16| e[o..o + 2].copy_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
        put(4, pos.0);
        put(6, pos.1);
        put(0x0e, job);
        put(0x24, tgt.0);
        put(0x26, tgt.1);
        for (i, (x, y)) in wp.into_iter().enumerate() {
            put(0x30 + i * 4, x);
            put(0x32 + i * 4, y);
        }
        e
    }

    const E: (u16, u16) = (0xffff, 0xffff);

    #[test]
    fn routes_from_runtime_dumps() {
        // Move + two Shift waypoints (s3run 2026-11-08, settler 0x35).
        let e = entry((264, 257), 0x35, (278, 248), [(293, 253), (298, 276), E]);
        let r = route_from_entry(&e, 384, false).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r.points, vec![(278, 248), (293, 253), (298, 276)]);
        assert!(r.patrol.is_none());
        // Patrol (Alt): start, target, 0xfffe marker.
        let e = entry((226, 182), 0x35, (237, 159), [(223, 182), (237, 159), (0xfffe, 0xfffe)]);
        let r = route_from_entry(&e, 384, false).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r.points, vec![(237, 159)]);
        assert_eq!(r.patrol, Some(((223, 182), (237, 159))));
        // Idle soldier: nothing, even when selected (target = position).
        let e = entry((235, 188), 0x37, (235, 188), [E, E, E]);
        assert!(route_from_entry(&e, 384, true).is_none());
        // Never commanded (zeros): nothing.
        let e = entry((264, 262), 0x37, (0, 0), [(0, 0), (0, 0), (0, 0)]);
        assert!(route_from_entry(&e, 384, true).is_none());
        // Walking without a player's order: only when selected.
        let e = entry((10, 10), 0x17, (20, 20), [E, E, E]);
        assert!(route_from_entry(&e, 384, false).is_none());
        assert_eq!(route_from_entry(&e, 384, true).unwrap().points, vec![(20, 20)]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn tile_to_screen_matches_hit_list() {
        // s3run 2026-11-08: cam (x 0x2d254, y 0x2d258), W 384, res 1; hit list (sx, sy) vs tile / height.
        let cam = (4928, 1166);
        // Unit 46 at tile (234, 185): hit (720, 630). Height unknown in that dump: check x only.
        assert_eq!(tile_to_screen(234, 185, 0, cam, 384, 1).0, 720);
        // Second run: unit 54 at (225, 246), h 68, dy + h = 182 with cam y from that run.
        let (_, sy) = tile_to_screen(225, 246, 68, (0, 0), 384, 1);
        assert_eq!(sy, 9 * 246 - 68 + 182);
    }

    #[test]
    fn dots_are_evenly_spaced() {
        let d = dots_along(&[(0.0, 0.0), (100.0, 0.0)], 10.0, 0.0);
        assert_eq!(d.len(), 10);
        assert!((d[1].0 - d[0].0 - 10.0).abs() < 1e-3);
        // Spacing continues over a corner.
        let d = dots_along(&[(0.0, 0.0), (15.0, 0.0), (15.0, 15.0)], 10.0, 0.0);
        assert_eq!(d.len(), 3);
        assert!((d[2].0 - 15.0).abs() < 1e-3 && (d[2].1 - 5.0).abs() < 1e-3);
        assert!(dots_along(&[(0.0, 0.0)], 10.0, 0.0).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn order_keys() {
        assert_eq!(Order::Waypoint.vk(), 0x10);
        assert_eq!(Order::Patrol.vk(), 0x12);
        assert_eq!(Order::NoFight.vk(), 0x11);
        assert_eq!(Order::from_vk(0x12), Some(Order::Patrol));
    }
}

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/view.rs`:

```rs
//! Typed views of guest memory.
//!
//! - [`GuestPtr<T>`]: a guest address of a plain value (`u8/u16/u32/i8/i16/i32/f32`).
//! - [`guest_struct!`](crate::guest_struct): declares a host-side view type for a guest struct with field
//!   offsets, so mod code reads `player.wood(mem)` instead of `mem.read_u16(base + 0x24)`.
//!
//! ```
//! s3_mods::guest_struct! {
//!     /// Example (offsets are made up).
//!     pub struct Example {
//!         0x00 => id / set_id: u32,
//!         0x04 => hp / set_hp: i16,
//!     }
//! }
//! let mut mem = s3_mem::GuestMemory::new().unwrap();
//! let e = Example::at(0x0060_0000);
//! e.set_hp(&mut mem, -3);
//! assert_eq!(e.hp(&mem), -3);
//! ```

use std::marker::PhantomData;

use s3_mem::GuestMemory;

/// A value type that can live in guest memory (little endian).
pub trait GuestValue: Copy {
    const SIZE: u32;
    fn read(mem: &GuestMemory, addr: u32) -> Self;
    fn write(self, mem: &mut GuestMemory, addr: u32);
}

macro_rules! gv {
    ($t:ty, $n:expr, $r:ident, $w:ident, $cast_r:ty) => {
        impl GuestValue for $t {
            const SIZE: u32 = $n;
            #[inline]
            fn read(mem: &GuestMemory, addr: u32) -> Self {
                mem.$r(addr) as $cast_r as $t
            }
            #[inline]
            fn write(self, mem: &mut GuestMemory, addr: u32) {
                mem.$w(addr, self as $cast_r);
            }
        }
    };
}
gv!(u8, 1, read_u8, write_u8, u8);
gv!(i8, 1, read_u8, write_u8, u8);
gv!(u16, 2, read_u16, write_u16, u16);
gv!(i16, 2, read_u16, write_u16, u16);
gv!(u32, 4, read_u32, write_u32, u32);
gv!(i32, 4, read_u32, write_u32, u32);

impl GuestValue for f32 {
    const SIZE: u32 = 4;
    fn read(mem: &GuestMemory, addr: u32) -> Self {
        f32::from_bits(mem.read_u32(addr))
    }
    fn write(self, mem: &mut GuestMemory, addr: u32) {
        mem.write_u32(addr, self.to_bits());
    }
}

/// Guest address of a `T`.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct GuestPtr<T> {
    pub addr: u32,
    _t: PhantomData<T>,
}

impl<T> Clone for GuestPtr<T> {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        *self
    }
}
impl<T> Copy for GuestPtr<T> {}

impl<T: GuestValue> GuestPtr<T> {
    pub const fn new(addr: u32) -> Self {
        GuestPtr { addr, _t: PhantomData }
    }
    pub fn is_null(&self) -> bool {
        self.addr == 0
    }
    pub fn get(&self, mem: &GuestMemory) -> T {
        T::read(mem, self.addr)
    }
    pub fn set(&self, mem: &mut GuestMemory, v: T) {
        v.write(mem, self.addr)
    }
    /// Element `i` of an array starting here.
    pub fn index(&self, i: u32) -> GuestPtr<T> {
        GuestPtr::new(self.addr.wrapping_add(i.wrapping_mul(T::SIZE)))
    }
}

/// Declare a view of a guest struct. Each field: `offset => getter / setter: type` (type implements
/// [`GuestValue`]). Generates `Name::at(addr)`, `Name::addr()`, the getters/setters and `Name::ptr_<getter>`
/// is not generated (use `GuestPtr::new(v.addr() + off)` for raw pointers).
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! guest_struct {
    ($(#[$meta:meta])* $vis:vis struct $name:ident { $($off:literal => $get:ident / $set:ident : $t:ty),* $(,)? }) => {
        $(#[$meta])*
        #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
        $vis struct $name { base: u32 }
        #[allow(dead_code)]
        impl $name {
            pub const fn at(base: u32) -> Self { $name { base } }
            pub const fn addr(&self) -> u32 { self.base }
            $(
                pub fn $get(&self, mem: &$crate::s3_mem::GuestMemory) -> $t {
                    <$t as $crate::view::GuestValue>::read(mem, self.base.wrapping_add($off))
                }
                pub fn $set(&self, mem: &mut $crate::s3_mem::GuestMemory, v: $t) {
                    <$t as $crate::view::GuestValue>::write(v, mem, self.base.wrapping_add($off))
                }
            )*
        }
    };
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    crate::guest_struct! {
        struct Demo {
            0x0 => a / set_a: u32,
            0x4 => b / set_b: i8,
            0x6 => c / set_c: u16,
            0x8 => f / set_f: f32,
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn struct_and_ptr() {
        let mut mem = GuestMemory::new().unwrap();
        let d = Demo::at(0x0060_0000);
        d.set_a(&mut mem, 0xDEAD_BEEF);
        d.set_b(&mut mem, -2);
        d.set_c(&mut mem, 0x1234);
        d.set_f(&mut mem, 1.5);
        assert_eq!(d.a(&mem), 0xDEAD_BEEF);
        assert_eq!(d.b(&mem), -2);
        assert_eq!(mem.read_u8(0x0060_0004), 0xFE);
        assert_eq!(d.c(&mem), 0x1234);
        assert_eq!(d.f(&mem), 1.5);
        let p: GuestPtr<u16> = GuestPtr::new(0x0060_0000);
        assert_eq!(p.index(3).get(&mem), 0x1234);
        p.index(3).set(&mut mem, 7);
        assert_eq!(d.c(&mem), 7);
    }
}

`port/crates/s3-mods/src/zoom.rs`:

```rs
//! Zoom = the game's internal render resolution (res-zoom, docs/porting/resolution-zoom.md).
//!
//! A zoom level is a render height from [`LEVEL_HEIGHTS`]; the width follows the aspect ratio of the window
//! (display mode "Native wide") or 4:3. The frontend scales the frame to the screen, so a smaller render size
//! shows less map with bigger pixels (zoomed in) and a bigger one more map (zoomed out). Pinch (both UI modes,
//! [`pinch`]) moves through the levels continuously and keeps the map point under the fingers fixed
//! ([`anchor_camera`]); menus call [`zoom_in`] / [`zoom_out`] / [`set_level`]. The level is saved in
//! `mods-settings.json` (`res.zoom_level`). [`ZoomMod`] publishes the wanted size to [`crate::res`] every slice.

use s3_runtime::Machine;

use crate::display::DisplayMode;
use crate::gesture::Phase;
use crate::res;
use crate::settings::UiMode;

/// Render heights of the zoom levels (index 0 = most zoomed in). Max = [`res::MAX_H`], min = [`res::MIN_H`].
/// 280 and 320 added 2026-11-08 (more zoom in); 200 and 240 by overlay-window (the HUD is drawn in the window layer
/// now, so it no longer depends on the render size); 840..1200 added by res-tall (taller snapshot grid).
pub const LEVEL_HEIGHTS: [u32; 22] =
    [200, 240, 280, 320, 360, 400, 440, 480, 520, 560, 600, 640, 680, 720, 760, 780, 840, 900, 960, 1040, 1120, 1200];
/// Default level: 600 px high (like the game's 800x600).
pub const DEFAULT_LEVEL: u32 = 10;
/// Lowest level in UI mode A (the original panel art needs at least 480 px).
pub const CLASSIC_MIN_LEVEL: u32 = 7;
/// Pinch scale factor per level (fingers apart by this factor = one level zoomed in).
pub const PINCH_STEP: f32 = 1.12;
/// Minimum time between two switches during a pinch (ms). The next switch also waits until the game finished
/// the previous one.
pub const PINCH_SWITCH_MS: u64 = 33;
/// During a pinch the render height follows the fingers continuously in steps of this many pixels (the levels
/// of [`LEVEL_HEIGHTS`] are 40 px apart, which looked like jumps); the end of the pinch snaps to the nearest level.
pub const PINCH_STEP_H: u32 = 8;

/// Size for a level: height from the table, width = height * aspect (multiple of 8), clamped to the limits.
pub fn size_for(level: u32, aspect: f32, min_level: u32) -> (u32, u32) {
    let l = level.clamp(min_level, LEVEL_HEIGHTS.len() as u32 - 1) as usize;
    size_for_height(LEVEL_HEIGHTS[l], aspect)
}

/// Size for a render height: width = height * aspect (multiple of 8), clamped to the limits.
pub fn size_for_height(h: u32, aspect: f32) -> (u32, u32) {
    let aspect = if aspect.is_finite() && aspect > 0.3 { aspect } else { 4.0 / 3.0 };
    let w = ((h as f32 * aspect / 8.0).round() as u32) * 8;
    // Wider than MAX_W: keep the width, lower the height (same aspect).
    let (w, h) = if w > res::MAX_W { (res::MAX_W, ((res::MAX_W as f32 / aspect).round() as u32).max(res::MIN_H)) } else { (w, h) };
    // Narrower than MIN_W (near-square windows zoomed far in, e.g. a foldable's inner screen at 1.2:1): keep the
    // window's aspect with the minimum width and a taller frame. Clamping only the width made the frame wider
    // than the window: black bars above and below (user report 2026-11-08).
    let (w, h) = if w < res::MIN_W { (res::MIN_W, ((res::MIN_W as f32 / aspect).round() as u32).min(res::MAX_H)) } else { (w, h) };
    res::clamp_size(w, h)
}

/// Level after a pinch of `scale` (current finger distance / start distance) that began at `start`.
pub fn pinch_level(start: u32, scale: f32, min_level: u32) -> u32 {
    let max = LEVEL_HEIGHTS.len() as i32 - 1;
    if !(scale.is_finite() && scale > 0.0) {
        return start;
    }
    // Fingers apart (scale > 1) = zoom in = smaller render size = lower level.
    let steps = -(scale.ln() / PINCH_STEP.ln());
    let steps = if steps.abs() < 0.6 { 0 } else { steps.round() as i32 };
    (start as i32 + steps).clamp(min_level as i32, max) as u32
}

/// Render width for height `h` in UI mode A with the panel shown at its own scale ([`crate::display::PanelSplit`],
/// window `ww` x `wh`): panel width + the map part that fills the rest of the window at the map's scale
/// (`wh / h`), a multiple of 8.
pub fn classic_width(h: u32, ww: u32, wh: u32) -> u32 {
    let v = if h >= res::CLASSIC_VARIANT.h { res::CLASSIC_VARIANT } else { res::variant_for(h) };
    let pw_win = (v.panel_w as f64 * wh as f64 / v.h as f64).round();
    let map = (ww as f64 - pw_win).max(64.0) * h as f64 / wh.max(1) as f64;
    let w = (v.panel_w + crate::display::map_skip(v.panel_w, v.h)) as f64 + map;
    ((((w / 8.0).round() as u32) * 8).clamp(res::MIN_W, res::MAX_W)).max(v.panel_w + 64)
}

/// Window size when UI mode A will show the panel at its own scale (Classic, `NativeWide`, window known).
fn classic_split_window(m: &mut Machine) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
    let (ui, mode) = {
        let st = m.state::<crate::ModsState>();
        let s = st.borrow_mut();
        (s.settings.ui_mode, s.settings.display.mode)
    };
    if ui != UiMode::ClassicTouch || mode != DisplayMode::NativeWide || std::env::var("S3_PANEL_SPLIT").is_ok_and(|v| v == "0") {
        return None;
    }
    if env_size("S3_RES_ASPECT").is_some() {
        return None;
    }
    crate::display::window_size(m).filter(|&(w, h)| w > 0 && h > 0)
}

/// Size for height `h` with the current aspect (and the Classic panel split's width rule). With the split, heights
/// below the panel art (480) render at 480 and the map part is cropped instead ([`classic_crop`]).
fn size_now(m: &mut Machine, h: u32, a: f32) -> (u32, u32) {
    let split = classic_split_window(m);
    let h = if split.is_some() { h.max(res::CLASSIC_VARIANT.h) } else { h };
    let (w, h) = size_for_height(h, a);
    match classic_split_window(m) {
        Some((ww, wh)) => (classic_width(h, ww, wh).min(w.max(res::MIN_W)), h),
        None => (w, h),
    }
}

/// [`anchor_camera`] with `fx` a fraction of the map view (`size.0 - pw`) instead of the frame.
pub fn anchor_camera_map(cam: (i32, i32), (fx, fy): (f32, f32), old: (u32, u32), new: (u32, u32), old_pw: f32, new_pw: f32) -> (i32, i32) {
    let (fx, fy) = (fx.clamp(0.0, 1.0), fy.clamp(0.0, 1.0));
    let (ox, oy) = (fx * (old.0 as f32 - old_pw), fy * old.1 as f32);
    let (nx, ny) = (fx * (new.0 as f32 - new_pw), fy * new.1 as f32);
    (cam.0 + (ox - nx).round() as i32, cam.1 + (oy - ny).round() as i32)
}

/// New camera so that the world point under screen fraction `(fx, fy)` stays there when the frame size changes
/// from `old` to `new`. `old_pw` / `new_pw` = map view x origin (panel width) before / after.
pub fn anchor_camera(cam: (i32, i32), (fx, fy): (f32, f32), old: (u32, u32), new: (u32, u32), old_pw: f32, new_pw: f32) -> (i32, i32) {
    let (fx, fy) = (fx.clamp(0.0, 1.0), fy.clamp(0.0, 1.0));
    let (ox, oy) = (fx * old.0 as f32 - old_pw, fy * old.1 as f32);
    let (nx, ny) = (fx * new.0 as f32 - new_pw, fy * new.1 as f32);
    (cam.0 + (ox - nx).round() as i32, cam.1 + (oy - ny).round() as i32)
}

/// Aspect ratio (w/h) the render size should have now.
pub fn aspect(m: &mut Machine) -> f32 {
    if let Some((w, h)) = env_size("S3_RES_ASPECT") {
        return w as f32 / h as f32;
    }
    let d = crate::display::display_settings(m);
    if d.mode != DisplayMode::Fit {
        if let Some((w, h)) = crate::display::window_size(m) {
            if w > 0 && h > 0 {
                return w as f32 / h as f32;
            }
        }
    }
    4.0 / 3.0
}

fn env_size(name: &str) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
    let v = std::env::var(name).ok()?;
    let (a, b) = v.split_once(['x', 'X', ':'])?;
    Some((a.trim().parse().ok()?, b.trim().parse().ok()?))
}

fn min_level(m: &mut Machine) -> u32 {
    let mode = m.state::<crate::ModsState>().borrow_mut().settings.ui_mode;
    // UI mode A with the panel split zooms below the panel art by cropping ([`classic_crop`]).
    if mode == UiMode::MobileHud || classic_split_window(m).is_some() { 0 } else { CLASSIC_MIN_LEVEL }
}

/// UI mode A with the panel split, wanted height below the 480 px panel art: the frame stays 480 high and only
/// this many rows of the map part are shown (centred, the width to match), scaled to the window. A smaller
/// render size would show exactly the same map pixels, but the panel art needs 480 rows of the frame. Pure
/// presentation (no render-size switch), so it is also instant. `None` = no crop.
pub fn classic_crop(m: &mut Machine) -> Option<u32> {
    if !enabled(m) || classic_split_window(m).is_none() || env_size("S3_RES").is_some() {
        return None;
    }
    let h = wanted_height(m);
    (h < res::CLASSIC_VARIANT.h).then_some(h.max(res::MIN_H))
}

/// Number of zoom levels.
pub fn level_count() -> u32 {
    LEVEL_HEIGHTS.len() as u32
}

/// Current zoom level (from the settings).
pub fn level(m: &mut Machine) -> u32 {
    m.state::<crate::ModsState>().borrow_mut().settings.res.zoom_level.min(level_count() - 1)
}

/// Is the custom resolution / zoom active (setting on and the patch installed)?
pub fn enabled(m: &mut Machine) -> bool {
    let on = m.state::<crate::ModsState>().borrow_mut().settings.res.enabled;
    on && m.state::<res::ResState>().borrow_mut().installed
}

/// Set the zoom level (clamped; saved to the settings). `anchor` = screen fractions to keep fixed.
pub fn set_level_anchored(m: &mut Machine, l: u32, anchor: Option<(f32, f32)>, persist: bool) {
    let l = l.clamp(min_level(m), level_count() - 1);
    let mut s = crate::settings(m);
    if s.res.zoom_level == l && s.res.zoom_height.is_none() {
        return;
    }
    s.res.zoom_level = l;
    s.res.zoom_height = None;
    if persist {
        let _ = crate::set_settings(m, s);
    } else {
        m.state::<crate::ModsState>().borrow_mut().settings = s;
    }
    let split = crate::display::panel_split(m).is_some();
    {
        let st = m.state::<res::ResState>();
        let mut r = st.borrow_mut();
        r.anchor = Some(anchor.unwrap_or((0.5, 0.5)));
        r.anchor_map = split && anchor.is_none();
    }
    update_target(m);
}

pub fn set_level(m: &mut Machine, l: u32) {
    set_level_anchored(m, l, None, true);
}

/// One level zoomed in (smaller render size).
pub fn zoom_in(m: &mut Machine) {
    let l = level(m);
    set_level(m, l.saturating_sub(1));
}

/// One level zoomed out (bigger render size).
pub fn zoom_out(m: &mut Machine) {
    let l = level(m);
    set_level(m, l + 1);
}

/// Turn the custom resolution on/off (saved).
pub fn set_enabled(m: &mut Machine, on: bool) {
    let mut s = crate::settings(m);
    s.res.enabled = on;
    let _ = crate::set_settings(m, s);
    update_target(m);
}

/// Render size of the current level (what [`res`] switches to), `None` when off.
pub fn target_size(m: &mut Machine) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
    if !enabled(m) {
        return None;
    }
    if let Some((w, h)) = env_size("S3_RES") {
        return Some(res::clamp_size(w, h));
    }
    let a = aspect(m);
    let h = wanted_height(m);
    Some(size_now(m, h, a))
}

/// The zoom height wanted now (pinch in progress, saved pinch height or level), before [`size_now`].
fn wanted_height(m: &mut Machine) -> u32 {
    let a = aspect(m);
    // The Mobile HUD reads its building icons from the game's panel once: that needs >= 480 px for a moment.
    let harvesting = m.state::<crate::ui_hud_game::HudShared>().borrow_mut().harvesting;
    if harvesting {
        return m.state::<PinchState>().borrow_mut().height.unwrap_or(0).max(crate::ui_hud_game::HARVEST_MIN_H);
    }
    (|| {
        if let Some(h) = m.state::<PinchState>().borrow_mut().height {
            return h;
        }
        let ml = min_level(m);
        let saved = m.state::<crate::ModsState>().borrow_mut().settings.res.zoom_height;
        if let Some(h) = saved {
            let (lo, hi) = (LEVEL_HEIGHTS[ml as usize], LEVEL_HEIGHTS[LEVEL_HEIGHTS.len() - 1]);
            return h.clamp(lo, hi);
        }
        size_for(level(m), a, ml).1
    })()
}

/// Render height a pinch in progress asks for (overrides the level until the pinch ends).
#[derive(Default)]
struct PinchState {
    height: Option<u32>,
}

/// Level whose height is nearest to `h`.
fn nearest_level(h: u32, min_level: u32) -> u32 {
    (min_level..level_count()).min_by_key(|&l| (LEVEL_HEIGHTS[l as usize] as i32 - h as i32).abs()).unwrap_or(min_level)
}

/// Display mode for the current aspect: the largest zoom size (zoom steps then only change the presented
/// size, the fast path of [`res`]).
pub fn mode_size(m: &mut Machine) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
    if !enabled(m) {
        return None;
    }
    if let Some((w, h)) = env_size("S3_RES") {
        return Some(res::clamp_size(w, h));
    }
    let a = aspect(m);
    Some(size_for(level_count() - 1, a, 0))
}

/// Publish the wanted size to the resolution patch.
pub fn update_target(m: &mut Machine) {
    let t = target_size(m);
    let mode = mode_size(m);
    let installed = m.state::<res::ResState>().borrow_mut().installed;
    if installed {
        res::set_target_mode(m, t, mode);
    }
}

/// Short label for menus, e.g. "Zoom 7/12 (1480x600)".
pub fn label(m: &mut Machine) -> String {
    match target_size(m) {
        Some((w, h)) => format!("Zoom {}/{} ({w}x{h})", level(m) + 1, level_count()),
        None => "Zoom off".to_string(),
    }
}

/// Pinch state (owned by the caller, e.g. the touch mod).
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
pub struct Pinch {
    start_level: Option<u32>,
    /// Frame width when the pinch began: pointer positions are in game pixels of the current frame, so the
    /// recognizer's scale must be corrected after each resolution switch (else zooming feeds back on itself).
    start_frame_w: u32,
    start_frame_h: u32,
    /// Panel width of the start frame when UI mode A shows the panel at its own scale (anchor = map fraction).
    start_split_pw: Option<u32>,
    last_switch_ms: u64,
    /// Direction of the last switch in this pinch (+1 bigger, -1 smaller, 0 none).
    dir: i8,
}

/// Handle a pinch event (game-pixel centre `cx, cy`). Returns true if zoom handled it (custom resolution on).
///
/// While the fingers move the render height follows them continuously ([`PINCH_STEP_H`] px steps, one switch at a
/// time); the end snaps to the nearest level (saved). Each switch keeps the map point under the fingers fixed.
pub fn pinch(m: &mut Machine, p: &mut Pinch, phase: Phase, cx: f32, cy: f32, scale: f32) -> bool {
    if !enabled(m) {
        return false;
    }
    let now = m.real_ms();
    let (fw, fh) = m.last_frame_size();
    // Size of the frame on screen (the viewport the touches were mapped through at the gesture start).
    let (mapped_w, mapped_h) =
        crate::display::viewport(m).map(|v| (v.game_w, v.game_h)).filter(|&(w, h)| w > 0 && h > 0).unwrap_or((fw, fh));
    // UI mode A crop below 480 rows: the effective zoom height is the shown map height.
    let crop = crate::display::panel_split(m).and_then(|p| p.crop());
    let start_h = crate::display::viewport(m).and_then(|v| v.panel).and_then(|p| p.crop()).unwrap_or(mapped_h);
    let fh = crop.unwrap_or(fh);
    if phase == Phase::Begin || p.start_level.is_none() {
        p.start_level = Some(level(m));
        p.start_frame_w = mapped_w;
        p.start_frame_h = start_h;
        p.start_split_pw = crate::display::panel_split(m).map(|s| s.w);
        p.dir = 0;
    }
    // Pointer positions of one multi-finger gesture are all mapped through the viewport the gesture started on
    // (frontends freeze it: s3-android pinch_vp; s3run injects fixed game coordinates), so `scale` is the real
    // on-screen ratio and the centre is in pixels of the start frame.
    let ml = min_level(m);
    let (hmin, hmax) = (LEVEL_HEIGHTS[ml as usize], LEVEL_HEIGHTS[LEVEL_HEIGHTS.len() - 1]);
    let h0 = if p.start_frame_h > 0 { p.start_frame_h } else { LEVEL_HEIGHTS[level(m) as usize] };
    // Fingers apart (scale > 1) = zoom in = smaller render height.
    let want_h = if scale.is_finite() && scale > 0.0 { (h0 as f32 / scale).round() as u32 } else { h0 };
    let want_h = (want_h.clamp(hmin, hmax) / PINCH_STEP_H) * PINCH_STEP_H;
    let end = phase == Phase::End;
    let (sw, sh) = (p.start_frame_w, p.start_frame_h);
    let anchor = (sw > 0 && sh > 0).then(|| match p.start_split_pw.filter(|&pw| pw + 1 < sw) {
        // Panel at its own scale: the map part is what zooms; anchor in its fractions.
        Some(pw) => (((cx - pw as f32) / (sw - pw) as f32).clamp(0.0, 1.0), (cy / sh as f32).clamp(0.0, 1.0)),
        None => ((cx / sw as f32).clamp(0.0, 1.0), (cy / sh as f32).clamp(0.0, 1.0)),
    });
    let anchor_map = p.start_split_pw.is_some();
    let busy = res::switch_pending(m) || now.saturating_sub(p.last_switch_ms) < PINCH_SWITCH_MS;
    if end {
        // Stay exactly where the fingers stopped (snapping to the nearest 40 px level made a last jump, sometimes
        // backwards); the level is kept as the nearest one for the menus' zoom steps.
        let l = nearest_level(want_h, ml);
        let end_h = m.state::<PinchState>().borrow_mut().height.take().unwrap_or(fh);
        let mut s = crate::settings(m);
        s.res.zoom_level = l;
        s.res.zoom_height = Some(end_h);
        let _ = crate::set_settings(m, s);
        if target_size(m) != Some((fw, fh)) {
            let st = m.state::<res::ResState>();
            let mut r = st.borrow_mut();
            r.anchor = Some(anchor.unwrap_or((0.5, 0.5)));
            r.anchor_map = anchor_map;
        }
        update_target(m);
        p.start_level = None;
        p.last_switch_ms = now;
    } else if !busy && want_h.abs_diff(fh) >= PINCH_STEP_H * if (want_h as i64 - fh as i64).signum() as i8 == -p.dir { 3 } else { 1 } {
        // Reversing the direction needs a bigger change (no back-and-forth on finger jitter).
        p.dir = (want_h as i64 - fh as i64).signum() as i8;
        m.state::<PinchState>().borrow_mut().height = Some(want_h);
        {
            let st = m.state::<res::ResState>();
            let mut r = st.borrow_mut();
            r.anchor = Some(anchor.unwrap_or((0.5, 0.5)));
            r.anchor_map = anchor_map;
        }
        update_target(m);
        p.last_switch_ms = now;
    }
    if std::env::var_os("S3_TOUCH_TRACE").is_some() {
        eprintln!("zoom: pinch {phase:?} scale {scale:.2} want_h {want_h} cur_h {fh} busy {busy}");
    }
    true
}

/// Host-side mod: keeps [`res::ResState::target`] in sync with the settings / window aspect every slice.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct ZoomMod {
    last: (Option<(u32, u32)>, Option<(u32, u32)>),
    /// Since when no game frame was rendered (ms; 0 = in game).
    out_since: u64,
    /// The start zoom was set for the next game.
    start_zoom_set: bool,
}

/// Time outside a game (no game frame) before the start zoom is set: longer than any zoom step's pause.
const START_ZOOM_AFTER_MS: u64 = 3000;

/// Size of a starting territory (castle area incl. its border) in game pixels, with a small margin; measured on
/// the random 384 maps (border about 1130 x 800 px).
const START_AREA: (f32, f32) = (1250.0, 850.0);

/// Render height that shows the whole start area: the Mobile HUD's bars take ~15 % of the height, the Classic
/// panel ~12 % of the width.
pub fn start_height(m: &mut Machine) -> u32 {
    let a = aspect(m);
    let map_w = if classic_split_window(m).is_some() { 0.88 } else { 1.0 };
    let h = (START_AREA.1 / 0.85).max(START_AREA.0 / (a * map_w));
    (((h / 8.0).round() as u32) * 8).clamp(res::MIN_H, res::MAX_H)
}

impl crate::Mod for ZoomMod {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        "zoom"
    }
    fn tick(&mut self, m: &mut Machine, now: u64) {
        // Outside a game (menus) for a while: the next game starts at the zoom that shows the whole start area,
        // not at the last zoom of the previous game (user request 2026-11-08). The game centres the camera on
        // the castle itself (res switch hook, anchor centre).
        // "Out of a game" = no game frame for a while, or a full-screen menu layout is shown (briefing, loading
        // screen, menus): campaign briefings and the statistics screen can keep the frame renderer busy, so
        // `in_game` alone could stay true from one mission to the next (user report 2026-11-08: zoom kept after
        // re-entering a campaign). Layouts are never used in a running game.
        let menu_frame = crate::draw_viewport(m).layout.is_some();
        if res::in_game(m) && !menu_frame {
            self.out_since = 0;
            self.start_zoom_set = false;
        } else if self.out_since == 0 {
            self.out_since = now.max(1);
        } else if !self.start_zoom_set && now.saturating_sub(self.out_since) >= START_ZOOM_AFTER_MS && enabled(m) {
            self.start_zoom_set = true;
            let h = start_height(m);
            let ml = min_level(m);
            let st = m.state::<crate::ModsState>();
            let mut s = st.borrow_mut();
            s.settings.res.zoom_height = Some(h);
            s.settings.res.zoom_level = nearest_level(h, ml);
        }
        let t = target_size(m);
        let mode = mode_size(m);
        if (t, mode) != self.last {
            self.last = (t, mode);
            res::set_target_mode(m, t, mode);
        }
    }
}

/// Register the zoom mod (after [`res::install`]).
pub fn install(m: &mut Machine) {
    crate::add_mod(m, Box::new(ZoomMod::default()));
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn sizes_for_levels() {
        // 4:3 reproduces the game's sizes at 480 / 600.
        assert_eq!(size_for(7, 4.0 / 3.0, 0), (640, 480));
        assert_eq!(size_for(DEFAULT_LEVEL, 4.0 / 3.0, 0), (800, 600));
        // Phone cover screen 2229x904 (aspect 2.466): 600 high -> 1480x600 (the user's example).
        let a = 2229.0 / 904.0;
        assert_eq!(size_for(10, a, 0), (1480, 600));
        assert_eq!(size_for(13, a, 0), (1776, 720));
        let (w, h) = size_for(15, a, 0);
        assert_eq!(h, 780);
        assert_eq!(w, 1920);
        // Classic mode never goes below 480.
        assert_eq!(size_for(0, 4.0 / 3.0, CLASSIC_MIN_LEVEL), (640, 480));
        // The new bottom (HUD): 200 high, at least MIN_W wide; narrower windows keep their aspect (taller frame).
        assert_eq!(size_for(0, 2316.0 / 904.0, 0), (512, 200));
        assert_eq!(size_for(0, 4.0 / 3.0, 0), (res::MIN_W, 240));
        assert_eq!(size_for(0, 2176.0 / 1812.0, 0), (res::MIN_W, 266));
        // Classic panel split widths: map part keeps the window aspect.
        for h in [480u32, 520, 600, 700, 768, 900, 1200] {
            let w = classic_width(h, 2316, 904);
            let v = res::CLASSIC_VARIANT;
            let pw_win = (v.panel_w as f32 * 904.0 / v.h as f32).round();
            let map_scale_x = (2316.0 - pw_win) / (w - v.panel_w - crate::display::map_skip(v.panel_w, v.h)) as f32;
            let map_scale_y = 904.0 / h as f32;
            assert!((map_scale_x / map_scale_y - 1.0).abs() < 0.012, "{h}: {w} {map_scale_x} {map_scale_y}");
            assert!(w <= size_for_height(h, 2316.0 / 904.0).0 + 16);
        }
        // Very wide: width capped, height follows.
        let (w, h) = size_for(level_count() - 1, 4.0, 0);
        assert_eq!(w, res::MAX_W);
        assert_eq!(h, res::MAX_W / 4);
        // The top level is the largest size the patched game supports.
        assert_eq!(size_for(level_count() - 1, 2316.0 / 904.0, 0), (3072, 1200));
        // Every level of a few aspects fits the snapshot grid.
        for a in [4.0 / 3.0, 16.0 / 9.0, 2229.0 / 904.0, 2176.0 / 1812.0, 3.0] {
            for l in 0..level_count() {
                let (w, h) = size_for(l, a, 0);
                assert!(res::grid_columns_needed(w, h) <= res::SNAP_COLS && res::grid_rows_needed(h) < res::SNAP_ROWS);
                assert!(res::sprite_buckets_needed(h) <= res::SPRITE_BUCKETS);
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn pinch_levels() {
        assert_eq!(pinch_level(6, 1.0, 0), 6);
        assert_eq!(pinch_level(6, 1.05, 0), 6);
        assert_eq!(pinch_level(6, 1.12, 0), 5);
        assert_eq!(pinch_level(6, 1.12f32.powi(3), 0), 3);
        assert_eq!(pinch_level(6, 1.0 / 1.12, 0), 7);
        assert_eq!(pinch_level(6, 0.01, 0), level_count() - 1);
        assert_eq!(pinch_level(6, 10.0, 0), 0);
        assert_eq!(pinch_level(6, 10.0, 3), 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn camera_anchor_keeps_point() {
        // Centre anchor, 800x600 -> 1480x600, full-screen map: x moves by half the width difference.
        let c = anchor_camera((1000, 500), (0.5, 0.5), (800, 600), (1480, 600), 0.0, 0.0);
        assert_eq!(c, (1000 - 340, 500));
        // World point under the anchor is the same before and after.
        let (fx, fy) = (0.25, 0.75);
        let (old, new) = ((1480, 600), (1184, 480));
        let c0 = (2000, 900);
        let c1 = anchor_camera(c0, (fx, fy), old, new, 176.0, 136.0);
        let w0 = (c0.0 as f32 + fx * 1480.0 - 176.0, c0.1 as f32 + fy * 600.0);
        let w1 = (c1.0 as f32 + fx * 1184.0 - 136.0, c1.1 as f32 + fy * 480.0);
        assert!((w0.0 - w1.0).abs() <= 1.0 && (w0.1 - w1.1).abs() <= 1.0, "{w0:?} {w1:?}");
    }
}
