`port/crates/s3-relay/src/main.rs`:

```rs
//! `s3-relay [--listen ADDR] [--allow-exe SHA256]... [--gog-only] [--grace SECS] [-v]`
//!
//! Defaults: listen 127.0.0.1:7777, any exe (sessions still only match identical exes).

use std::time::Duration;

struct StderrLog(log::LevelFilter);

impl log::Log for StderrLog {
    fn enabled(&self, m: &log::Metadata) -> bool {
        m.level() <= self.0
    }
    fn log(&self, r: &log::Record) {
        if self.enabled(r.metadata()) {
            let t = std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).map(|d| d.as_secs()).unwrap_or(0);
            eprintln!("{t} {:5} {}", r.level(), r.args());
        }
    }
    fn flush(&self) {}
}

fn usage() -> ! {
    eprintln!("usage: s3-relay [--listen ADDR:PORT] [--allow-exe SHA256]... [--gog-only] [--grace SECS] [-v]");
    std::process::exit(2);
}

fn main() {
    let mut cfg = s3_relay::RelayConfig { listen: "127.0.0.1:7777".parse().unwrap(), ..Default::default() };
    let mut level = log::LevelFilter::Info;
    let mut args = std::env::args().skip(1);
    while let Some(a) = args.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--listen" => cfg.listen = args.next().and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).unwrap_or_else(|| usage()),
            "--allow-exe" => cfg.allowed_exes.push(args.next().and_then(|v| s3_net::parse_sha256(&v)).unwrap_or_else(|| usage())),
            "--gog-only" => cfg.allowed_exes.push(s3_net::GOG_EXE_SHA256),
            "--grace" => {
                cfg.resume_grace = Duration::from_secs(args.next().and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).unwrap_or_else(|| usage()))
            }
            "-v" => level = log::LevelFilter::Debug,
            "-h" | "--help" => usage(),
            _ => usage(),
        }
    }
    let logger: &'static StderrLog = Box::leak(Box::new(StderrLog(level)));
    let _ = log::set_logger(logger);
    log::set_max_level(level);
    let rt = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread().worker_threads(2).enable_all().build().expect("tokio runtime");
    rt.block_on(async move {
        let handle = match s3_relay::start(cfg).await {
            Ok(h) => h,
            Err(e) => {
                eprintln!("s3-relay: cannot listen: {e}");
                std::process::exit(1);
            }
        };
        eprintln!("s3-relay: {}", handle.url());
        let _ = tokio::signal::ctrl_c().await;
        eprintln!("s3-relay: shutting down ({:?})", handle.stats().await);
    });
}

```

`port/crates/s3-relay/tests/two_clients.rs`:

```rs
//! Integration tests: real relay on 127.0.0.1 + real `s3_net::client::NetClient`s (each with its own thread),
//! exercising the DirectPlay-like flow S3.EXE performs (see docs/porting/multiplayer.md).

use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use s3_net::client::{ClientConfig, Event, LinkState, NetClient, NetError};
use s3_net::dplay::{DPSEND_GUARANTEED, DPSESSION_KEEPALIVE, DPSESSION_MIGRATEHOST};
use s3_net::protocol::{ErrorCode, SessionDesc};
use s3_net::S3_APP_GUID;
use s3_relay::{RelayConfig, RelayHandle};

struct Relay {
    rt: tokio::runtime::Runtime,
    handle: Option<RelayHandle>,
}

impl Relay {
    fn start(cfg: RelayConfig) -> Relay {
        let rt = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread().worker_threads(2).enable_all().build().unwrap();
        let handle = rt.block_on(s3_relay::start(cfg)).unwrap();
        Relay { rt, handle: Some(handle) }
    }
    fn url(&self) -> String {
        self.handle.as_ref().unwrap().url()
    }
    fn stats(&self) -> s3_relay::Stats {
        self.rt.block_on(self.handle.as_ref().unwrap().stats())
    }
    fn kick(&self, cid: u32) {
        self.handle.as_ref().unwrap().kick_connection(cid);
    }
}

impl Drop for Relay {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if let Some(h) = self.handle.take() {
            h.shutdown();
        }
    }
}

fn client(relay: &Relay, name: &str) -> NetClient {
    NetClient::connect(ClientConfig::new(relay.url(), name)).unwrap()
}

/// The session description S3.EXE builds at 0x46ff80 (flags MIGRATEHOST|KEEPALIVE, app GUID, user dwords).
fn s3_desc(name: &str) -> SessionDesc {
    SessionDesc {
        flags: DPSESSION_MIGRATEHOST | DPSESSION_KEEPALIVE,
        application: S3_APP_GUID,
        max_players: 8,
        name: name.into(),
        user: [0, 0, 0xa0, 0],
        ..Default::default()
    }
}

/// Wait for an event matching `pred`, skipping others (returned so tests can inspect them).
fn wait_for(c: &NetClient, what: &str, mut pred: impl FnMut(&Event) -> bool) -> Event {
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(10);
    while Instant::now() < deadline {
        if let Some(e) = c.wait_event(Duration::from_millis(100)) {
            if pred(&e) {
                return e;
            }
        }
    }
    panic!("timed out waiting for {what}");
}

#[test]
fn host_join_exchange_and_leave() {
    let relay = Relay::start(RelayConfig::default());
    let host = client(&relay, "host");
    let guest = client(&relay, "guest");
    assert_ne!(host.client_id(), guest.client_id());

    // Host: DPOPEN_CREATE, then CreatePlayer.
    let joined = host.create_session(s3_desc("Römer 2v2")).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(joined.host, host.client_id());
    assert_ne!(joined.desc.instance, [0; 16]);
    let hp = host.create_player("Hans", "", b"host-data", 0).unwrap();
    assert!(hp > 1);
    assert!(host.snapshot().is_host());

    // Guest: EnumSessions finds it (password hidden), joins, sees the host's player.
    let list = guest.list_sessions(S3_APP_GUID).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(list.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(list[0].name, "Römer 2v2");
    assert_eq!(list[0].current_players, 1);
    assert!(guest.list_sessions([9; 16]).unwrap().is_empty(), "other application GUIDs are filtered");
    let gj = guest.join_session(list[0].instance, "").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(gj.host, host.client_id());
    assert_eq!(gj.players.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(gj.players[0].dpid, hp);
    assert_eq!(gj.players[0].data, b"host-data");
    let gp = guest.create_player("Grete", "", &[], 0).unwrap();
    assert_ne!(gp, hp);

    // Host gets DPSYS_CREATEPLAYERORGROUP.
    match wait_for(&host, "PlayerAdded", |e| matches!(e, Event::PlayerAdded(_))) {
        Event::PlayerAdded(p) => {
            assert_eq!(p.dpid, gp);
            assert_eq!(p.short_name, "Grete");
            assert_eq!(p.owner, guest.client_id());
        }
        _ => unreachable!(),
    }

    // Ordered data both ways, broadcast and directed, guaranteed and not.
    for i in 0..200u32 {
        let flags = if i % 2 == 0 { DPSEND_GUARANTEED } else { 0 };
        guest.send(gp, if i % 3 == 0 { 0 } else { hp }, flags, &i.to_le_bytes()).unwrap();
    }
    for i in 0..200u32 {
        match wait_for(&host, "data", |e| matches!(e, Event::Message { .. })) {
            Event::Message { from, to, payload, .. } => {
                assert_eq!(from, gp);
                assert_eq!(to, hp, "broadcast is delivered addressed to the receiving player");
                assert_eq!(payload, i.to_le_bytes(), "order preserved");
            }
            _ => unreachable!(),
        }
    }
    host.send(hp, gp, DPSEND_GUARANTEED, &[0x19; 315]).unwrap(); // GameSetup-sized message
    match wait_for(&guest, "data", |e| matches!(e, Event::Message { .. })) {
        Event::Message { from, payload, .. } => {
            assert_eq!(from, hp);
            assert_eq!(payload.len(), 315);
        }
        _ => unreachable!(),
    }

    // Spoofing another player's DPID is ignored: the next message the host sees is the sentinel.
    guest.send(hp, hp, DPSEND_GUARANTEED, b"spoof").unwrap();
    guest.send(gp, hp, DPSEND_GUARANTEED, b"sentinel").unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(wait_for(&host, "sentinel", |e| matches!(e, Event::Message { .. })),
        Event::Message { payload, .. } if payload == b"sentinel"));
    // Player data / name / session desc changes reach the other side.
    guest.set_player_data(gp, b"slot=2").unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(wait_for(&host, "PlayerData", |e| matches!(e, Event::PlayerData { .. })),
        Event::PlayerData { dpid, data } if dpid == gp && data == b"slot=2"));
    assert_eq!(guest.set_player_data(hp, b"x").unwrap_err().code(), ErrorCode::NotOwner);
    let mut d = joined.desc.clone();
    d.user[3] = 7;
    assert_eq!(guest.set_session_desc(d.clone()).unwrap_err().code(), ErrorCode::NotOwner);
    host.set_session_desc(d).unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(wait_for(&guest, "SessionDesc", |e| matches!(e, Event::SessionDesc(_))),
        Event::SessionDesc(sd) if sd.user[3] == 7));

    // Desync report is relayed to the other members.
    guest.report_desync(1234, 0xdead_beef, "Desync Settler!").unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(wait_for(&host, "Desync", |e| matches!(e, Event::Desync { .. })),
        Event::Desync { step: 1234, checksum: 0xdead_beef, .. }));

    // Guest leaves: host sees DPSYS_DESTROYPLAYERORGROUP.
    guest.leave_session().unwrap();
    assert!(guest.snapshot().session.is_none());
    assert!(matches!(wait_for(&host, "PlayerRemoved", |e| matches!(e, Event::PlayerRemoved(_))),
        Event::PlayerRemoved(p) if p.dpid == gp && p.short_name == "Grete"));
    let st = relay.stats();
    assert_eq!(st.desync_reports, 1);
    assert!(st.delivered >= 201);
    guest.close();
    host.close();
}

#[test]
fn host_migration_when_host_leaves() {
    let relay = Relay::start(RelayConfig::default());
    let a = client(&relay, "a");
    let b = client(&relay, "b");
    let c = client(&relay, "c");
    let s = a.create_session(s3_desc("mig")).unwrap();
    let pa = a.create_player("A", "", &[], 0).unwrap();
    b.join_session(s.desc.instance, "").unwrap();
    let pb = b.create_player("B", "", &[], 0).unwrap();
    c.join_session(s.desc.instance, "").unwrap();
    let _pc = c.create_player("C", "", &[], 0).unwrap();
    a.close(); // Bye: immediate removal
    // b joined first -> new host (DPSYS_HOST), c only sees the player leave.
    wait_for(&b, "BecameHost", |e| matches!(e, Event::BecameHost));
    assert!(b.snapshot().is_host());
    assert!(matches!(wait_for(&c, "PlayerRemoved", |e| matches!(e, Event::PlayerRemoved(_))), Event::PlayerRemoved(p) if p.dpid == pa));
    assert!(!c.snapshot().is_host());
    assert_eq!(relay.stats().host_migrations, 1);
    // Without MIGRATEHOST the session is lost for everyone when the host goes.
    let mut d = s3_desc("nomig");
    d.flags = DPSESSION_KEEPALIVE;
    b.leave_session().unwrap();
    let _ = pb;
    let s2 = b.create_session(d).unwrap();
    c.leave_session().unwrap();
    c.join_session(s2.desc.instance, "").unwrap();
    b.close();
    assert!(matches!(wait_for(&c, "SessionLost", |e| matches!(e, Event::SessionLost(_))), Event::SessionLost(ErrorCode::Disconnected)));
    assert!(c.snapshot().session.is_none());
}

#[test]
fn join_rules() {
    let relay = Relay::start(RelayConfig::default());
    let a = client(&relay, "a");
    let b = client(&relay, "b");
    let mut d = s3_desc("locked");
    d.password = "geheim".into();
    d.max_players = 1;
    let s = a.create_session(d).unwrap();
    let list = b.list_sessions(S3_APP_GUID).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(list[0].password, "", "password never leaves the relay");
    assert_ne!(list[0].flags & s3_net::dplay::DPSESSION_PASSWORDREQUIRED, 0);
    assert_eq!(b.join_session(s.desc.instance, "falsch").unwrap_err().code(), ErrorCode::WrongPassword);
    assert_eq!(b.join_session(s.desc.instance, "geheim").unwrap_err().code(), ErrorCode::SessionFull);
    assert_eq!(b.join_session([1; 16], "").unwrap_err().code(), ErrorCode::NoSuchSession);
    assert_eq!(a.create_session(s3_desc("x")).unwrap_err().code(), ErrorCode::AlreadyInSession);
    assert_eq!(b.leave_session().unwrap_err().code(), ErrorCode::NotInSession);

    // A different S3.EXE neither sees nor joins the session.
    let mut cfg = ClientConfig::new(relay.url(), "other-exe");
    cfg.exe_sha256 = [0x11; 32];
    let other = NetClient::connect(cfg).unwrap();
    assert!(other.list_sessions(S3_APP_GUID).unwrap().is_empty());
    assert_eq!(other.join_session(s.desc.instance, "geheim").unwrap_err().code(), ErrorCode::ExeMismatch);
}

#[test]
fn relay_rejects_unknown_exe_when_restricted() {
    let relay = Relay::start(RelayConfig { allowed_exes: vec![s3_net::GOG_EXE_SHA256], ..Default::default() });
    let _ok = client(&relay, "gog");
    let mut cfg = ClientConfig::new(relay.url(), "bad");
    cfg.exe_sha256 = [0x22; 32];
    match NetClient::connect(cfg) {
        Err(NetError::Rejected(ErrorCode::ExeMismatch, _)) => {}
        Err(e) => panic!("unexpected error {e:?}"),
        Ok(_) => panic!("should be rejected"),
    }
}

#[test]
fn resume_after_connection_drop_loses_nothing() {
    let relay = Relay::start(RelayConfig::default());
    let host = client(&relay, "host");
    let guest = client(&relay, "guest");
    let s = host.create_session(s3_desc("resume")).unwrap();
    let hp = host.create_player("H", "", &[], 0).unwrap();
    guest.join_session(s.desc.instance, "").unwrap();
    let gp = guest.create_player("G", "", &[], 0).unwrap();
    wait_for(&host, "PlayerAdded", |e| matches!(e, Event::PlayerAdded(_)));

    // Cut the guest's TCP connection; meanwhile the host keeps sending.
    relay.kick(guest.client_id());
    for i in 0..50u32 {
        host.send(hp, gp, DPSEND_GUARANTEED, &i.to_le_bytes()).unwrap();
    }
    wait_for(&guest, "Resumed", |e| matches!(e, Event::Link(LinkState::Resumed)));
    for i in 0..50u32 {
        match wait_for(&guest, "data", |e| matches!(e, Event::Message { .. })) {
            Event::Message { payload, .. } => assert_eq!(payload, i.to_le_bytes()),
            _ => unreachable!(),
        }
    }
    // The guest still owns its player and can talk; the host never saw it leave.
    guest.send(gp, hp, DPSEND_GUARANTEED, b"back").unwrap();
    match wait_for(&host, "data", |e| matches!(e, Event::Message { .. } | Event::PlayerRemoved(_))) {
        Event::Message { payload, .. } => assert_eq!(payload, b"back"),
        e => panic!("unexpected {e:?}"),
    }
    assert_eq!(relay.stats().resumes, 1);
}

#[test]
fn slot_expires_after_grace() {
    let relay = Relay::start(RelayConfig { resume_grace: Duration::from_millis(300), ..Default::default() });
    let host = client(&relay, "host");
    let mut cfg = ClientConfig::new(relay.url(), "guest");
    cfg.resume_window = Duration::ZERO; // never resume
    let guest = NetClient::connect(cfg).unwrap();
    let s = host.create_session(s3_desc("grace")).unwrap();
    host.create_player("H", "", &[], 0).unwrap();
    guest.join_session(s.desc.instance, "").unwrap();
    let gp = guest.create_player("G", "", &[], 0).unwrap();
    relay.kick(guest.client_id());
    assert!(matches!(wait_for(&guest, "SessionLost", |e| matches!(e, Event::SessionLost(_))), Event::SessionLost(_)));
    // After the grace period the relay destroys the guest's player for everyone else.
    assert!(matches!(wait_for(&host, "PlayerRemoved", |e| matches!(e, Event::PlayerRemoved(_))), Event::PlayerRemoved(p) if p.dpid == gp));
}
```

`port/crates/s3-runtime/src/audio.rs`:

```rs
//! Extra PCM streams mixed into the one audio output (added by the directx agent, 2026-11-05).
//!
//! The DirectSound software mixer (s3-dx `dsound.rs`) is the only caller of `Host::queue_audio` (44100 Hz
//! stereo i16). Other sound sources (winmm waveOut / CD-audio music from `MUSIC\TrackNN.ogg`) push interleaved
//! PCM into `m.state::<AudioStreams>()`; the mixer pulls, resamples (linear) and mixes it. The mixer service is
//! registered by `s3_dx::register_factories`, so it runs even if the game never creates DirectSound.
//! Producers should keep roughly 100-300 ms queued (`AudioStream::queued_frames`) and top up from a service.

use std::collections::{HashMap, VecDeque};

/// One PCM stream fed by a non-DirectSound producer.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct AudioStream {
    /// Sample rate of `samples`.
    pub rate: u32,
    /// 1 or 2.
    pub channels: u16,
    /// Interleaved signed 16-bit samples, consumed from the front by the mixer.
    pub samples: VecDeque<i16>,
    /// Linear gain 0.0..=1.0 (1.0 if left at 0.0 and `gain_set` is false).
    pub gain: f32,
    pub gain_set: bool,
}

impl AudioStream {
    /// Frames (per-channel samples) still queued.
    pub fn queued_frames(&self) -> usize {
        self.samples.len() / self.channels.max(1) as usize
    }
}

/// Extra audio streams mixed by the DirectSound mixer, keyed by a producer-chosen id.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct AudioStreams {
    pub streams: HashMap<u32, AudioStream>,
}
```

`port/crates/s3-runtime/src/com.rs`:

```rs
//! Minimal COM support: GUIDs, vtables made of thunks, object allocation, and a CLSID factory table used by
//! `ole32!CoCreateInstance`.
//!
//! An HLE COM object lives in guest memory: `[vtable ptr][refcount][impl data...]`. The vtable is an array of
//! thunk addresses; method `Iface::Method` is a normal registry entry in the implementing DLL (e.g.
//! `ddraw.dll!IDirectDrawSurface::Flip`), so the usual UNIMPLEMENTED reporting and tracing apply. `this` is
//! the first stdcall argument (`m.arg_u32(0)`).

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::fmt;

use crate::Machine;

/// A GUID as stored in memory (little-endian Data1..3 then 8 bytes).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default)]
pub struct Guid(pub [u8; 16]);

impl Guid {
    /// Parse `"D7B70EE0-4340-11CF-B063-0020AFC2CD35"` (braces optional).
    pub const fn parse(s: &str) -> Guid {
        let b = s.as_bytes();
        let mut hex = [0u8; 32];
        let mut n = 0;
        let mut i = 0;
        while i < b.len() {
            let c = b[i];
            let v = match c {
                b'0'..=b'9' => Some(c - b'0'),
                b'a'..=b'f' => Some(c - b'a' + 10),
                b'A'..=b'F' => Some(c - b'A' + 10),
                _ => None,
            };
            if let Some(v) = v {
                hex[n] = v;
                n += 1;
            }
            i += 1;
        }
        assert!(n == 32, "bad GUID string");
        let mut raw = [0u8; 16];
        let mut k = 0;
        while k < 16 {
            raw[k] = hex[2 * k] << 4 | hex[2 * k + 1];
            k += 1;
        }
        // Data1 (4), Data2 (2), Data3 (2) are little-endian in memory.
        let mut out = [0u8; 16];
        out[0] = raw[3];
        out[1] = raw[2];
        out[2] = raw[1];
        out[3] = raw[0];
        out[4] = raw[5];
        out[5] = raw[4];
        out[6] = raw[7];
        out[7] = raw[6];
        let mut j = 8;
        while j < 16 {
            out[j] = raw[j];
            j += 1;
        }
        Guid(out)
    }

    /// Read a GUID from guest memory.
    pub fn read(m: &Machine, addr: u32) -> Guid {
        let mut g = [0u8; 16];
        g.copy_from_slice(m.mem.slice(addr, 16));
        Guid(g)
    }

    /// Write a GUID to guest memory.
    pub fn write(&self, m: &mut Machine, addr: u32) {
        m.mem.write_bytes(addr, &self.0);
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for Guid {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        let g = &self.0;
        write!(
            f,
            "{{{:02X}{:02X}{:02X}{:02X}-{:02X}{:02X}-{:02X}{:02X}-{:02X}{:02X}-{:02X}{:02X}{:02X}{:02X}{:02X}{:02X}}}",
            g[3], g[2], g[1], g[0], g[5], g[4], g[7], g[6], g[8], g[9], g[10], g[11], g[12], g[13], g[14], g[15]
        )
    }
}

impl fmt::Debug for Guid {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        fmt::Display::fmt(self, f)
    }
}

/// Creates an object for `CoCreateInstance(clsid, ..., iid)`. Returns the interface pointer or an HRESULT.
pub type ComFactory = fn(&mut Machine, iid: Guid) -> Result<u32, u32>;

/// HRESULTs.
pub const S_OK: u32 = 0;
pub const E_NOINTERFACE: u32 = 0x8000_4002;
pub const E_FAIL: u32 = 0x8000_4005;
pub const E_OUTOFMEMORY: u32 = 0x8007_000E;
pub const CLASS_E_CLASSNOTAVAILABLE: u32 = 0x8004_0111;
pub const REGDB_E_CLASSNOTREG: u32 = 0x8004_0154;

/// CLSID factories and built vtables.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct ComRegistry {
    pub factories: HashMap<Guid, (String, ComFactory)>,
    vtables: HashMap<String, u32>,
}

impl ComRegistry {
    /// Register a class factory for `CoCreateInstance`.
    pub fn register_class(&mut self, clsid: Guid, name: &str, f: ComFactory) {
        self.factories.insert(clsid, (name.to_string(), f));
    }
}

impl Machine {
    /// Vtable for `iface` implemented by `dll`: one thunk per method name (in vtable order), declared in the
    /// registry as `dll!iface::method`. Built once and cached by `dll!iface`.
    pub fn com_vtable(&mut self, dll: &str, iface: &str, methods: &[&str]) -> u32 {
        let key = format!("{dll}!{iface}");
        if let Some(&v) = self.com.vtables.get(&key) {
            return v;
        }
        let vt = self.mem.alloc(methods.len() as u32 * 4);
        for (i, meth) in methods.iter().enumerate() {
            let a = self.registry.declare(dll, &format!("{iface}::{meth}"));
            self.mem.write_u32(vt + i as u32 * 4, a);
        }
        self.com.vtables.insert(key, vt);
        vt
    }

    /// Allocate a COM object: `size` bytes (>= 8), `[0]` = vtable, `[4]` = refcount 1. Returns the pointer.
    pub fn com_new_object(&mut self, vtable: u32, size: u32) -> u32 {
        let p = self.mem.alloc(size.max(8));
        self.mem.write_u32(p, vtable);
        self.mem.write_u32(p + 4, 1);
        p
    }

    /// Generic `IUnknown::AddRef` on the standard object layout. Use as a handler.
    pub fn com_addref(m: &mut Machine) -> crate::ThunkResult {
        let this = m.arg_u32(0);
        let n = m.mem.read_u32(this + 4).wrapping_add(1);
        m.mem.write_u32(this + 4, n);
        crate::ThunkResult::stdcall(n, 1)
    }

    /// Generic `IUnknown::Release` on the standard object layout (memory is not freed: objects are few and
    /// the guest may still hold aliases). Use as a handler.
    pub fn com_release(m: &mut Machine) -> crate::ThunkResult {
        let this = m.arg_u32(0);
        let n = m.mem.read_u32(this + 4).saturating_sub(1);
        m.mem.write_u32(this + 4, n);
        crate::ThunkResult::stdcall(n, 1)
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-runtime/src/cursor.rs`:

```rs
//! Mouse cursor emulation (the game runs with registry `GDIMouse`=1, i.e. it uses the Windows cursor).
//!
//! - Decoding of Win32 cursor resources (`RT_GROUP_CURSOR` -> `RT_CURSOR`): monochrome AND/XOR cursors and
//!   colour DIB cursors (1/4/8/24/32 bpp, 32 bpp with per-pixel alpha).
//! - A built-in arrow for system cursors (`LoadCursorA(NULL, IDC_*)`), drawn from code here (not copied from
//!   Windows).
//! - [`CursorState`] (machine state, written by user32 `LoadCursorA`/`SetCursor`/`ShowCursor`/`ClipCursor`).
//! - [`CursorState::compose`]: called by [`Machine::present`](crate::Machine::present) to draw the current
//!   cursor at the emulated mouse position into a host-side copy of the frame. Guest surfaces are never written,
//!   so every frontend gets the cursor for free.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::Arc;

use crate::host::FrameBuffer;
use crate::resources::{find_resource, rt, ResId};
use crate::Machine;

/// One cursor pixel.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum CursorPixel {
    /// Screen shows through (AND=1, XOR=0).
    Clear,
    /// Opaque RGB565 colour (AND=0).
    Color(u16),
    /// Screen XOR RGB565 colour (AND=1, XOR!=0; white = invert).
    Xor(u16),
    /// RGB565 colour blended with alpha 1..254 (32 bpp alpha cursors).
    Blend(u16, u8),
}

/// A decoded cursor image.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct CursorImage {
    pub width: u32,
    pub height: u32,
    pub hot_x: i32,
    pub hot_y: i32,
    /// Row-major, top row first.
    pub pixels: Vec<CursorPixel>,
}

#[inline]
fn rgb565(r: u8, g: u8, b: u8) -> u16 {
    ((r as u16 >> 3) << 11) | ((g as u16 >> 2) << 5) | (b as u16 >> 3)
}

fn rd16(b: &[u8], o: usize) -> Option<u16> {
    Some(u16::from_le_bytes(b.get(o..o + 2)?.try_into().ok()?))
}

fn rd32(b: &[u8], o: usize) -> Option<u32> {
    Some(u32::from_le_bytes(b.get(o..o + 4)?.try_into().ok()?))
}

/// Pick the `RT_CURSOR` id from `RT_GROUP_CURSOR` data (`NEWHEADER` + 14-byte `CURSORDIRENTRY`s):
/// the entry whose width is closest to `want` (ties: higher bit count).
pub fn pick_group_entry(grp: &[u8], want: u32) -> Option<u16> {
    let count = rd16(grp, 4)? as usize;
    let mut best: Option<(u32, u16, u16)> = None; // (distance, bitcount, id)
    for i in 0..count {
        let e = 6 + i * 14;
        let w = rd16(grp, e)? as u32;
        let bits = rd16(grp, e + 6)?;
        let id = rd16(grp, e + 12)?;
        let w = if w == 0 { 256 } else { w };
        let d = w.abs_diff(want);
        let better = match best {
            None => true,
            Some((bd, bb, _)) => d < bd || (d == bd && bits > bb),
        };
        if better {
            best = Some((d, bits, id));
        }
    }
    best.map(|b| b.2)
}

/// Decode `RT_CURSOR` resource data: `u16 hot_x, u16 hot_y`, then a DIB (`BITMAPINFOHEADER`, colour table,
/// XOR bitmap, AND mask; `biHeight` counts both bitmaps).
pub fn decode_cursor_resource(data: &[u8]) -> Option<CursorImage> {
    let hx = rd16(data, 0)? as i32;
    let hy = rd16(data, 2)? as i32;
    decode_dib_cursor(data.get(4..)?, hx, hy)
}

/// Decode a cursor/icon DIB (XOR image + AND mask) with the given hot spot.
pub fn decode_dib_cursor(dib: &[u8], hot_x: i32, hot_y: i32) -> Option<CursorImage> {
    let hsize = rd32(dib, 0)? as usize;
    if hsize < 40 {
        return None;
    }
    let w = rd32(dib, 4)? as i32;
    let h2 = rd32(dib, 8)? as i32;
    let bpp = rd16(dib, 14)? as u32;
    let compression = rd32(dib, 16)?;
    let clr_used = rd32(dib, 32)? as usize;
    if w <= 0 || w > 256 || h2 == 0 || compression != 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let (w, h) = (w as u32, (h2.unsigned_abs() / 2).max(1));
    if h > 256 {
        return None;
    }
    let top_down = h2 < 0;
    let ncolors = if bpp <= 8 { if clr_used != 0 { clr_used } else { 1usize << bpp } } else { 0 };
    let pal_off = hsize;
    let palette: Vec<(u8, u8, u8)> = (0..ncolors)
        .map(|i| {
            let o = pal_off + i * 4;
            dib.get(o..o + 3).map(|c| (c[2], c[1], c[0]))
        })
        .collect::<Option<_>>()?;
    let xor_off = pal_off + ncolors * 4;
    let xor_stride = ((w * bpp + 31) / 32 * 4) as usize;
    let and_off = xor_off + xor_stride * h as usize;
    let and_stride = ((w + 31) / 32 * 4) as usize;
    let has_and = dib.len() >= and_off + and_stride * h as usize;
    if dib.len() < and_off {
        return None;
    }
    let row_of = |y: u32| if top_down { y } else { h - 1 - y } as usize;
    // 32 bpp with any non-zero alpha: alpha channel is authoritative.
    let use_alpha = bpp == 32
        && (0..h).any(|y| (0..w).any(|x| dib[xor_off + row_of(y) * xor_stride + x as usize * 4 + 3] != 0));
    let mut pixels = Vec::with_capacity((w * h) as usize);
    for y in 0..h {
        let xr = xor_off + row_of(y) * xor_stride;
        let ar = and_off + row_of(y) * and_stride;
        for x in 0..w {
            let (r, g, b, a) = match bpp {
                1 | 4 | 8 => {
                    let bit = (x * bpp) as usize;
                    let byte = dib[xr + bit / 8];
                    let idx = (byte >> (8 - bpp as usize - bit % 8)) & ((1u16 << bpp) - 1) as u8;
                    let (r, g, b) = palette.get(idx as usize).copied().unwrap_or((0, 0, 0));
                    (r, g, b, 255)
                }
                24 => {
                    let o = xr + x as usize * 3;
                    (dib[o + 2], dib[o + 1], dib[o], 255)
                }
                32 => {
                    let o = xr + x as usize * 4;
                    (dib[o + 2], dib[o + 1], dib[o], dib[o + 3])
                }
                _ => return None,
            };
            let and = has_and && (dib[ar + x as usize / 8] >> (7 - x % 8)) & 1 != 0;
            let c = rgb565(r, g, b);
            let px = if use_alpha {
                match a {
                    0 => CursorPixel::Clear,
                    255 => CursorPixel::Color(c),
                    a => CursorPixel::Blend(c, a),
                }
            } else if !and {
                CursorPixel::Color(c)
            } else if c == 0 {
                CursorPixel::Clear
            } else {
                CursorPixel::Xor(c)
            };
            pixels.push(px);
        }
    }
    Some(CursorImage { width: w, height: h, hot_x, hot_y, pixels })
}

/// Our own arrow (12x19, black outline, white fill, hot spot at the tip), used for every system cursor.
pub fn builtin_arrow() -> CursorImage {
    const ART: [&str; 19] = [
        "B...........",
        "BB..........",
        "BWB.........",
        "BWWB........",
        "BWWWB.......",
        "BWWWWB......",
        "BWWWWWB.....",
        "BWWWWWWB....",
        "BWWWWWWWB...",
        "BWWWWWWWWB..",
        "BWWWWWWWWWB.",
        "BWWWWWWBBBBB",
        "BWWWBWWB....",
        "BWWBBWWB....",
        "BWB..BWWB...",
        "BB...BWWB...",
        "B.....BWWB..",
        "......BWWB..",
        ".......BB...",
    ];
    let pixels = ART
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|row| {
            row.bytes().map(|c| match c {
                b'B' => CursorPixel::Color(0x0000),
                b'W' => CursorPixel::Color(0xFFFF),
                _ => CursorPixel::Clear,
            })
        })
        .collect();
    CursorImage { width: 12, height: 19, hot_x: 0, hot_y: 0, pixels }
}

/// Load a cursor from the `.rsrc` of the module mapped at `module_base` (`RT_GROUP_CURSOR` `name`, best
/// entry for 32x32). Falls back to a direct `RT_CURSOR` lookup.
pub fn load_cursor_resource(m: &Machine, module_base: u32, name: &ResId) -> Option<CursorImage> {
    let cur_id = match find_resource(m, module_base, &ResId::Id(rt::GROUP_CURSOR), name, None) {
        Some((addr, size)) => ResId::Id(pick_group_entry(m.mem.slice(addr, size as usize), 32)?),
        None => name.clone(),
    };
    let (addr, size) = find_resource(m, module_base, &ResId::Id(rt::CURSOR), &cur_id, None)?;
    decode_cursor_resource(m.mem.slice(addr, size as usize))
}

/// Cursor state shared between user32 (writer) and [`Machine::present`](crate::Machine::present) (reader).
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct CursorState {
    /// Decoded images by HCURSOR value.
    pub images: HashMap<u32, Arc<CursorImage>>,
    /// Current HCURSOR (`SetCursor`); 0 = no cursor.
    pub current: u32,
    /// `ShowCursor` display counter; drawn when >= 0.
    pub show_count: i32,
    /// `ClipCursor` rectangle (left, top, right, bottom) the drawn position is clamped to.
    pub clip: Option<(i32, i32, i32, i32)>,
    /// Frontend switch: set to true to never draw the cursor.
    pub disabled: bool,
    /// Copy of the last frame the guest presented, with the cursor drawn in when `drawn` is set (one copy per
    /// present; perf-r2: was two full-frame copies).
    src: Option<FrameBuffer>,
    /// Pixels of `src` under the drawn cursor: (x0, y0, w, h, pixels), restored before the cursor moves.
    under: Option<(i32, i32, i32, i32, Vec<u16>)>,
    /// What the host shows now: (x, y, HCURSOR) of the drawn cursor, `None` = no cursor drawn.
    drawn: Option<(i32, i32, u32)>,
}

impl CursorState {
    /// The image to draw now, if the cursor is visible.
    pub fn visible_image(&self) -> Option<&Arc<CursorImage>> {
        if self.disabled || self.show_count < 0 || self.current == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        self.images.get(&self.current)
    }

    fn clamp(&self, x: i32, y: i32) -> (i32, i32) {
        match self.clip {
            Some((l, t, r, b)) => (x.clamp(l, (r - 1).max(l)), y.clamp(t, (b - 1).max(t))),
            None => (x, y),
        }
    }

    /// Wanted cursor at mouse (`x`, `y`): (x, y, HCURSOR) or `None` if hidden.
    fn wanted(&self, x: i32, y: i32) -> Option<(i32, i32, u32)> {
        self.visible_image()?;
        let (x, y) = self.clamp(x, y);
        Some((x, y, self.current))
    }

    /// A guest frame is presented: remember it and compose the visible cursor at mouse position (`x`, `y`)
    /// over a copy. Returns `None` when no cursor is visible (present `fb` itself then).
    pub fn compose(&mut self, fb: &FrameBuffer, x: i32, y: i32) -> Option<&FrameBuffer> {
        let mut src = self.src.take().unwrap_or_else(|| FrameBuffer::new(0, 0));
        copy_frame(&mut src, fb);
        self.src = Some(src);
        self.under = None;
        self.drawn = self.wanted(x, y);
        self.drawn?;
        self.recompose()
    }

    /// Like [`CursorState::compose`] but takes the frame (no copy) and returns the previous buffer for reuse.
    /// The frame to show is then [`CursorState::shown`].
    pub fn compose_owned(&mut self, fb: FrameBuffer, x: i32, y: i32) -> Option<FrameBuffer> {
        let old = self.src.replace(fb);
        self.under = None;
        self.drawn = self.wanted(x, y);
        if self.drawn.is_some() && self.recompose().is_none() {
            self.drawn = None;
        }
        old
    }

    /// The frame last composed by [`CursorState::compose_owned`] (with the cursor if one is drawn).
    pub fn shown(&self) -> Option<&FrameBuffer> {
        self.src.as_ref()
    }

    /// Cursor-only update between guest presents (the game redraws nothing when only the mouse moves; a
    /// real Windows cursor is a hardware overlay). Returns the frame to show if the cursor moved, changed
    /// shape or visibility since the last frame handed to the host.
    pub fn refresh(&mut self, x: i32, y: i32) -> Option<&FrameBuffer> {
        let want = self.wanted(x, y);
        if want == self.drawn || self.src.is_none() {
            return None;
        }
        self.restore_under();
        self.drawn = want;
        if want.is_none() {
            return self.src.as_ref();
        }
        self.recompose()
    }

    /// Put back the pixels the drawn cursor covered (`src` is then the plain guest frame again).
    fn restore_under(&mut self) {
        let (Some(src), Some((x0, y0, w, h, px))) = (self.src.as_mut(), self.under.take()) else { return };
        let fw = src.width as usize;
        for row in 0..h as usize {
            let at = (y0 as usize + row) * fw + x0 as usize;
            src.pixels[at..at + w as usize].copy_from_slice(&px[row * w as usize..(row + 1) * w as usize]);
        }
    }

    /// Draw the cursor into `src` (saving what it covers).
    fn recompose(&mut self) -> Option<&FrameBuffer> {
        let (x, y, _) = self.drawn?;
        let img = self.visible_image()?.clone();
        let src = self.src.as_mut()?;
        let (fw, fh) = (src.width as i32, src.height as i32);
        if src.pixels.len() < (fw * fh) as usize {
            return None;
        }
        let (ox, oy) = (x - img.hot_x, y - img.hot_y);
        let (x0, y0) = (ox.clamp(0, fw), oy.clamp(0, fh));
        let (x1, y1) = ((ox + img.width as i32).clamp(0, fw), (oy + img.height as i32).clamp(0, fh));
        let (w, h) = (x1 - x0, y1 - y0);
        let mut px = Vec::with_capacity((w.max(0) * h.max(0)) as usize);
        for row in y0..y1 {
            let at = (row * fw + x0) as usize;
            px.extend_from_slice(&src.pixels[at..at + w as usize]);
        }
        self.under = Some((x0, y0, w.max(0), h.max(0), px));
        draw_cursor(src, &img, x, y);
        self.src.as_ref()
    }
}

fn copy_frame(dst: &mut FrameBuffer, src: &FrameBuffer) {
    dst.width = src.width;
    dst.height = src.height;
    dst.pixels.clear();
    dst.pixels.extend_from_slice(&src.pixels);
}

/// Draw `img` with its hot spot at (`x`, `y`) into `fb` (clipped to the frame).
pub fn draw_cursor(fb: &mut FrameBuffer, img: &CursorImage, x: i32, y: i32) {
    let (fw, fh) = (fb.width as i32, fb.height as i32);
    if fb.pixels.len() < (fw * fh) as usize {
        return;
    }
    let (ox, oy) = (x - img.hot_x, y - img.hot_y);
    for cy in 0..img.height as i32 {
        let sy = oy + cy;
        if sy < 0 || sy >= fh {
            continue;
        }
        for cx in 0..img.width as i32 {
            let sx = ox + cx;
            if sx < 0 || sx >= fw {
                continue;
            }
            let d = &mut fb.pixels[(sy * fw + sx) as usize];
            match img.pixels[(cy * img.width as i32 + cx) as usize] {
                CursorPixel::Clear => {}
                CursorPixel::Color(c) => *d = c,
                CursorPixel::Xor(c) => *d ^= c,
                CursorPixel::Blend(c, a) => *d = blend565(*d, c, a),
            }
        }
    }
}

fn blend565(dst: u16, src: u16, a: u8) -> u16 {
    let a = a as u32;
    let mix = |s: u32, d: u32| (s * a + d * (255 - a)) / 255;
    let (s, d) = (src as u32, dst as u32);
    let r = mix(s >> 11, d >> 11);
    let g = mix((s >> 5) & 0x3F, (d >> 5) & 0x3F);
    let b = mix(s & 0x1F, d & 0x1F);
    ((r << 11) | (g << 5) | b) as u16
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Synthetic 4x4 monochrome cursor (hot spot 1,2), stored as in a PE `RT_CURSOR` (bottom-up rows).
    /// Top row (y=0): AND 0, XOR 1 -> white; y=1: AND 0, XOR 0 -> black; y=2: AND 1, XOR 0 -> clear;
    /// y=3: AND 1, XOR 1 -> invert. Column 3 of row 0 is black (XOR bit clear).
    fn synthetic_mono() -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut v = Vec::new();
        v.extend_from_slice(&1u16.to_le_bytes());
        v.extend_from_slice(&2u16.to_le_bytes());
        // BITMAPINFOHEADER
        v.extend_from_slice(&40u32.to_le_bytes());
        v.extend_from_slice(&4i32.to_le_bytes());
        v.extend_from_slice(&8i32.to_le_bytes()); // 2 * height
        v.extend_from_slice(&1u16.to_le_bytes());
        v.extend_from_slice(&1u16.to_le_bytes()); // 1 bpp
        v.extend_from_slice(&[0u8; 24]);
        // palette: black, white
        v.extend_from_slice(&[0, 0, 0, 0, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0]);
        // XOR rows, bottom-up: y=3, y=2, y=1, y=0 (each 4-byte stride)
        for row in [0xF0u8, 0x00, 0x00, 0xE0] {
            v.extend_from_slice(&[row, 0, 0, 0]);
        }
        // AND rows, bottom-up
        for row in [0xF0u8, 0xF0, 0x00, 0x00] {
            v.extend_from_slice(&[row, 0, 0, 0]);
        }
        v
    }

    #[test]
    fn decodes_monochrome_cursor() {
        let img = decode_cursor_resource(&synthetic_mono()).expect("decode");
        assert_eq!((img.width, img.height, img.hot_x, img.hot_y), (4, 4, 1, 2));
        use CursorPixel::*;
        assert_eq!(&img.pixels[0..4], &[Color(0xFFFF), Color(0xFFFF), Color(0xFFFF), Color(0)]);
        assert_eq!(&img.pixels[4..8], &[Color(0); 4]);
        assert_eq!(&img.pixels[8..12], &[Clear; 4]);
        assert_eq!(&img.pixels[12..16], &[Xor(0xFFFF); 4]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn decodes_32bpp_alpha_cursor() {
        let mut v = vec![0u8; 4];
        v.extend_from_slice(&40u32.to_le_bytes());
        v.extend_from_slice(&2i32.to_le_bytes());
        v.extend_from_slice(&2i32.to_le_bytes()); // 1 row
        v.extend_from_slice(&1u16.to_le_bytes());
        v.extend_from_slice(&32u16.to_le_bytes());
        v.extend_from_slice(&[0u8; 24]);
        v.extend_from_slice(&[0xFF, 0, 0, 0xFF, 0, 0xFF, 0, 0x80]); // blue opaque, green half
        v.extend_from_slice(&[0u8; 4]); // AND row
        let img = decode_dib_cursor(&v[4..], 0, 0).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(img.pixels, vec![CursorPixel::Color(0x001F), CursorPixel::Blend(0x07E0, 0x80)]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn picks_group_entry_and_composes_with_hotspot_and_show_count() {
        // NEWHEADER (reserved, type 2, count 2) + 2 entries: 16px id 7, 32px id 9
        let mut g = vec![0, 0, 2, 0, 2, 0];
        for (w, id) in [(16u16, 7u16), (32, 9)] {
            g.extend_from_slice(&w.to_le_bytes());
            g.extend_from_slice(&(w * 2).to_le_bytes());
            g.extend_from_slice(&1u16.to_le_bytes());
            g.extend_from_slice(&1u16.to_le_bytes());
            g.extend_from_slice(&308u32.to_le_bytes());
            g.extend_from_slice(&id.to_le_bytes());
        }
        assert_eq!(pick_group_entry(&g, 32), Some(9));

        let img = decode_cursor_resource(&synthetic_mono()).unwrap();
        let mut st = CursorState::default();
        st.images.insert(0x55, Arc::new(img));
        let fb = FrameBuffer { width: 8, height: 8, pixels: vec![0x1234; 64] };
        assert!(st.compose(&fb, 4, 4).is_none(), "no SetCursor yet");
        st.current = 0x55;
        let out = st.compose(&fb, 4, 4).unwrap().clone();
        // hot spot (1,2) at (4,4): image origin (3,2)
        assert_eq!(out.pixels[2 * 8 + 3], 0xFFFF);
        assert_eq!(out.pixels[2 * 8 + 6], 0x0000);
        assert_eq!(out.pixels[4 * 8 + 3], 0x1234); // clear row
        assert_eq!(out.pixels[5 * 8 + 3], 0x1234 ^ 0xFFFF); // invert row
        assert_eq!(fb.pixels[2 * 8 + 3], 0x1234, "source frame untouched");
        st.show_count = -1;
        assert!(st.compose(&fb, 4, 4).is_none(), "hidden by ShowCursor(FALSE)");
        // clipped at the frame edge: no panic
        st.show_count = 0;
        assert!(st.compose(&fb, 7, 7).is_some());
        assert!(st.compose(&fb, -10, 100).is_some());
        // refresh: unchanged -> nothing; moved -> redrawn from the remembered frame; hidden -> plain frame
        assert!(st.refresh(-10, 100).is_none());
        let moved = st.refresh(1, 2).unwrap().clone();
        assert_eq!(moved.pixels[0], 0xFFFF);
        st.show_count = -1;
        assert_eq!(st.refresh(1, 2).unwrap().pixels, fb.pixels);
        assert!(st.refresh(1, 2).is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn builtin_arrow_is_well_formed() {
        let a = builtin_arrow();
        assert_eq!(a.pixels.len(), (a.width * a.height) as usize);
        assert_eq!(a.pixels[0], CursorPixel::Color(0));
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-runtime/src/ext.rs`:

```rs
//! Extension points for host-side mods (`s3-mods`): guest-address hooks, an input filter in front of the
//! game, and an overlay compose step on every presented frame. All are plain function pointers that keep
//! their state in [`Machine::state`]; when nothing is installed they cost (almost) nothing.

use std::sync::Arc;

use s3_cpu::HookAddrs;

use crate::host::{FrameBuffer, HostEvent};
use crate::machine::Machine;

/// What the CPU does after a hook ran.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum HookFlow {
    /// Execute the original code at the hooked EIP (the hook only observed / changed state).
    Continue,
    /// The hook set EIP (and usually ESP/EAX) itself, e.g. emulated a `ret` to skip the original function.
    Redirected,
}

/// Called when EIP reaches a hooked address (`eip`). The current thread is `m.cur`.
pub type HookDispatch = fn(&mut Machine, u32) -> HookFlow;
/// Called for every host event before the game sees it. Push the events the game should see into `out`
/// (none = consumed; the identity filter pushes `e`).
pub type EventFilter = fn(&mut Machine, HostEvent, &mut Vec<HostEvent>);
/// Overlay compose: `src` is the guest frame; draw into `out` (prefilled with a copy of `src`) and return true,
/// or return false to present `src` unchanged (no copy made by the caller beyond the prefill skip, see
/// [`OverlayWanted`]).
pub type OverlayCompose = fn(&mut Machine, &mut FrameBuffer) -> bool;
/// Cheap check before [`OverlayCompose`]: does the overlay draw anything now? (avoids a frame copy).
pub type OverlayWanted = fn(&mut Machine) -> bool;
/// Window-resolution overlay (s3-mods `layer`): called with the raw guest frame (read-only) on every present and
/// overlay refresh, before the host sees the frame. The mods record their UI and hand it to the frontend
/// themselves; the frame is not changed.
pub type WindowOverlay = fn(&mut Machine, &FrameBuffer);

/// Installed extensions (see [`Machine::ext`]).
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct MachineExt {
    pub hook_dispatch: Option<HookDispatch>,
    pub event_filter: Option<EventFilter>,
    pub overlay_wanted: Option<OverlayWanted>,
    pub overlay_compose: Option<OverlayCompose>,
    pub window_overlay: Option<WindowOverlay>,
    /// A frame-space overlay is currently on screen (an overlay-only refresh must re-present the raw frame once
    /// it is gone).
    pub(crate) frame_overlay_shown: bool,
    /// Hook address set given to every guest CPU (also to threads created later).
    pub(crate) hook_addrs: Option<Arc<HookAddrs>>,
    /// Native fast paths given to every guest CPU (also to threads created later); see `Cpu::set_native_blocks`.
    pub(crate) native_blocks: Option<Arc<s3_cpu::NativeBlocks>>,
    /// Reused frame for overlay composition.
    pub(crate) overlay_buf: Option<FrameBuffer>,
    /// Last guest frame (kept only while an overlay is installed) for overlay-only refreshes.
    pub(crate) last_guest_frame: Option<FrameBuffer>,
    /// Size of the last guest frame (valid also while `last_guest_frame` is taken out for composing).
    pub(crate) last_guest_size: (u32, u32),
}

impl Machine {
    /// Install the guest hook address set in every thread's CPU (clears their decode caches). `None` or an
    /// empty set disables hooks.
    pub fn set_hook_addrs(&mut self, addrs: Option<HookAddrs>) {
        let a = addrs.filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).map(Arc::new);
        for t in &mut self.threads {
            t.cpu.set_hooks(a.clone());
        }
        self.ext.hook_addrs = a;
        if let Some(mt) = self.mt.as_ref() {
            mt.shared.ext_gen.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
        }
    }

    /// Install native fast paths (perf-cpu, docs/porting/performance.md) in every thread's CPU (clears their
    /// decode caches). `None` or an empty map disables them.
    pub fn set_native_blocks(&mut self, natives: Option<s3_cpu::NativeBlocks>) {
        let n = natives.filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).map(Arc::new);
        for t in &mut self.threads {
            t.cpu.set_native_blocks(n.clone());
        }
        self.ext.native_blocks = n;
        if let Some(mt) = self.mt.as_ref() {
            mt.shared.ext_gen.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
        }
    }

    /// Current native fast paths.
    pub fn native_blocks(&self) -> Option<&s3_cpu::NativeBlocks> {
        self.ext.native_blocks.as_deref()
    }

    /// Size of the last guest frame seen by the overlay step ((0, 0) before the first present).
    pub fn last_frame_size(&self) -> (u32, u32) {
        self.ext.last_guest_size
    }

    /// Current hook address set.
    pub fn hook_addrs(&self) -> Option<&HookAddrs> {
        self.ext.hook_addrs.as_deref()
    }

    /// Run the hook for `eip` on the current thread and prepare the CPU to continue.
    pub(crate) fn dispatch_hook(&mut self, eip: u32) {
        let slot = self.cur;
        self.stats.hooks += 1;
        let t0 = self.stats.host_prof.is_some().then(std::time::Instant::now);
        let flow = match self.ext.hook_dispatch {
            Some(f) => f(self, eip),
            None => HookFlow::Continue,
        };
        if let Some(t0) = t0 {
            self.stats.host_prof_add(eip, t0.elapsed().as_nanos() as u64);
        }
        self.cur = slot;
        if flow == HookFlow::Continue {
            let cpu = &mut self.threads[slot].cpu;
            if cpu.eip == eip {
                cpu.skip_hook_once(eip);
            }
        }
    }

    /// Feed one host event through the installed filter into `self.input`.
    pub(crate) fn filter_event(&mut self, e: HostEvent) {
        match self.ext.event_filter {
            Some(f) => {
                let mut out = Vec::new();
                f(self, e, &mut out);
                for e in out {
                    self.input.push(e);
                }
            }
            None => self.input.push(e),
        }
    }

    /// Is any overlay step installed (frame-space or window layer)?
    pub(crate) fn has_overlay(&self) -> bool {
        self.ext.overlay_compose.is_some() || self.ext.window_overlay.is_some()
    }

    /// Run the window-layer overlay for a guest frame (no-op when not installed).
    pub(crate) fn run_window_overlay(&mut self, fb: &FrameBuffer) {
        if let Some(f) = self.ext.window_overlay {
            f(self, fb);
        }
    }

    /// Apply the overlay to a guest frame. Returns the frame to present (`None` = present `fb` unchanged).
    pub(crate) fn apply_overlay(&mut self, fb: &FrameBuffer) -> Option<FrameBuffer> {
        if !self.has_overlay() {
            return None;
        }
        // Remember the raw guest frame for overlay-only refreshes.
        let mut last = self.ext.last_guest_frame.take().unwrap_or_default();
        copy_frame(&mut last, fb);
        self.ext.last_guest_size = (fb.width, fb.height);
        self.ext.last_guest_frame = Some(last);
        self.run_window_overlay(fb);
        self.apply_overlay_to(fb)
    }

    /// Overlay over a copy of `fb` (which is already remembered as the last guest frame, or a refresh of it).
    pub(crate) fn apply_overlay_to(&mut self, fb: &FrameBuffer) -> Option<FrameBuffer> {
        let compose = self.ext.overlay_compose?;
        if let Some(w) = self.ext.overlay_wanted {
            if !w(self) {
                return None;
            }
        }
        let mut out = self.ext.overlay_buf.take().unwrap_or_default();
        copy_frame(&mut out, fb);
        if compose(self, &mut out) {
            self.ext.frame_overlay_shown = true;
            Some(out)
        } else {
            self.ext.overlay_buf = Some(out);
            None
        }
    }

    /// Give a frame buffer back to the overlay buffer pool.
    pub(crate) fn recycle_overlay(&mut self, fb: FrameBuffer) {
        self.ext.overlay_buf = Some(fb);
    }

    /// Re-present the last guest frame with the current overlay (call when only the overlay changed, e.g.
    /// a HUD animation or touch feedback while the game presents nothing). Not counted in `stats.presents`.
    pub fn refresh_overlay(&mut self) {
        let Some(src) = self.ext.last_guest_frame.take() else { return };
        self.run_window_overlay(&src);
        // The window layer reaches the frontend by itself; the frame is re-presented only for frame-space overlays.
        let shown = std::mem::take(&mut self.ext.frame_overlay_shown);
        match self.apply_overlay_to(&src) {
            Some(out) => self.present_cursor_owned(out),
            None if shown => self.present_cursor(&src),
            None => {}
        }
        if self.ext.last_guest_frame.is_none() {
            self.ext.last_guest_frame = Some(src);
        }
    }
}

fn copy_frame(dst: &mut FrameBuffer, src: &FrameBuffer) {
    dst.width = src.width;
    dst.height = src.height;
    dst.pixels.clear();
    dst.pixels.extend_from_slice(&src.pixels);
}
```

`port/crates/s3-runtime/src/gdi.rs`:

```rs
//! Device-context bridge between DirectDraw (s3-dx) and GDI (s3-win32 gdi32).
//!
//! `IDirectDrawSurface::GetDC` must return an HDC whose drawing (TextOutA, DrawTextA, LineTo, ...) lands in the
//! surface pixels. s3-dx describes the surface memory with a [`DcTarget`] and calls [`create_dc`]; gdi32
//! (s3-win32) installs the implementation with [`install`] at registration time. `ReleaseDC` on the surface
//! calls [`release_dc`]. Without gdi32 installed, `create_dc` returns 0.

use crate::Machine;

/// Pixel memory a DC draws into (guest memory, top-down rows).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct DcTarget {
    /// Guest address of the first (top) row.
    pub addr: u32,
    /// Bytes per row.
    pub pitch: u32,
    pub width: u32,
    pub height: u32,
    /// Bits per pixel: 16 (RGB565/RGB555), 24, 32 (and 8, drawn as palette index, rarely used).
    pub bpp: u32,
    /// For 16 bpp: true = RGB565 (F800/07E0/001F), false = RGB555 (7C00/03E0/001F).
    pub rgb565: bool,
}

/// Functions installed by gdi32.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct DcHooks {
    /// Create a DC drawing into `target`; returns the HDC (0 on failure).
    pub create: fn(&mut Machine, DcTarget) -> u32,
    /// Destroy a DC created by `create`.
    pub release: fn(&mut Machine, u32),
}

static HOOKS: std::sync::OnceLock<DcHooks> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();

/// Install the gdi32 implementation (called by `s3_win32::gdi32::register`; process-global, first call wins).
pub fn install(hooks: DcHooks) {
    let _ = HOOKS.set(hooks);
}

/// Create an HDC drawing into `target` (0 if no GDI implementation is installed).
pub fn create_dc(m: &mut Machine, target: DcTarget) -> u32 {
    match HOOKS.get() {
        Some(h) => (h.create)(m, target),
        None => 0,
    }
}

/// Release an HDC obtained from [`create_dc`].
pub fn release_dc(m: &mut Machine, hdc: u32) {
    if let Some(h) = HOOKS.get() {
        (h.release)(m, hdc)
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-runtime/src/handles.rs`:

```rs
//! Win32 handle table. Handles are small multiples of 4 (like NT). Several handles can refer to one object
//! (`DuplicateHandle`, named objects); the object dies when its last handle is closed.

use std::any::Any;
use std::collections::HashMap;

/// Pseudo handle returned by `GetCurrentProcess`.
pub const CURRENT_PROCESS: u32 = 0xFFFF_FFFF;
/// Pseudo handle returned by `GetCurrentThread`.
pub const CURRENT_THREAD: u32 = 0xFFFF_FFFE;
/// `INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE`.
pub const INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE: u32 = 0xFFFF_FFFF;

/// A kernel object. Waitable kinds are understood by `Machine::is_signaled` / `Machine::try_acquire`.
pub enum KernelObject {
    Event { manual_reset: bool, signaled: bool },
    Mutex { owner: Option<u32>, recursion: u32 },
    Semaphore { count: i32, max: i32 },
    /// A guest thread (signaled when it has exited).
    Thread { tid: u32 },
    Process,
    /// Waitable timer (`CreateWaitableTimerA`). Signaled once host time reaches `due_ms`; `period_ms > 0`
    /// re-arms it (see `Machine::is_signaled` / `try_acquire`).
    Timer { manual_reset: bool, signaled: bool, due_ms: Option<u64>, period_ms: u32 },
    /// Anything owned by an HLE module (files, find handles, file mappings, MCI devices, ...).
    /// The string is a short type tag for debugging.
    Other(&'static str, Box<dyn Any + Send>),
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for KernelObject {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            KernelObject::Event { manual_reset, signaled } => write!(f, "Event(manual={manual_reset}, set={signaled})"),
            KernelObject::Mutex { owner, recursion } => write!(f, "Mutex(owner={owner:?}, rec={recursion})"),
            KernelObject::Semaphore { count, max } => write!(f, "Semaphore({count}/{max})"),
            KernelObject::Thread { tid } => write!(f, "Thread({tid:#x})"),
            KernelObject::Process => write!(f, "Process"),
            KernelObject::Timer { due_ms, period_ms, .. } => write!(f, "Timer(due={due_ms:?}, period={period_ms})"),
            KernelObject::Other(t, _) => write!(f, "{t}"),
        }
    }
}

struct ObjEntry {
    obj: KernelObject,
    name: Option<String>,
    refs: u32,
}

/// The process handle table.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct HandleTable {
    next_handle: u32,
    next_obj: u32,
    handles: HashMap<u32, u32>,
    objects: HashMap<u32, ObjEntry>,
}

impl HandleTable {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        HandleTable { next_handle: 0x100, next_obj: 1, ..Default::default() }
    }

    fn alloc_handle(&mut self, obj: u32) -> u32 {
        let h = self.next_handle;
        self.next_handle += 4;
        self.handles.insert(h, obj);
        h
    }

    /// Insert a new object and return a handle to it.
    pub fn insert(&mut self, obj: KernelObject) -> u32 {
        self.insert_named(obj, None)
    }

    /// Insert a new (optionally named) object.
    pub fn insert_named(&mut self, obj: KernelObject, name: Option<String>) -> u32 {
        let id = self.next_obj;
        self.next_obj += 1;
        self.objects.insert(id, ObjEntry { obj, name, refs: 1 });
        self.alloc_handle(id)
    }

    /// New handle to an existing named object (for `Create*`/`Open*` with an existing name).
    pub fn open_named(&mut self, name: &str) -> Option<u32> {
        let id = *self.objects.iter().find(|(_, e)| e.name.as_deref() == Some(name))?.0;
        self.objects.get_mut(&id)?.refs += 1;
        Some(self.alloc_handle(id))
    }

    /// The object behind a handle.
    pub fn get(&self, h: u32) -> Option<&KernelObject> {
        self.objects.get(self.handles.get(&h)?).map(|e| &e.obj)
    }

    /// Mutable object behind a handle.
    pub fn get_mut(&mut self, h: u32) -> Option<&mut KernelObject> {
        let id = *self.handles.get(&h)?;
        self.objects.get_mut(&id).map(|e| &mut e.obj)
    }

    /// Downcast an `Other` object.
    pub fn get_other<T: 'static>(&self, h: u32) -> Option<&T> {
        match self.get(h)? {
            KernelObject::Other(_, b) => b.downcast_ref(),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// Mutable downcast of an `Other` object.
    pub fn get_other_mut<T: 'static>(&mut self, h: u32) -> Option<&mut T> {
        match self.get_mut(h)? {
            KernelObject::Other(_, b) => b.downcast_mut(),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// `DuplicateHandle`.
    pub fn duplicate(&mut self, h: u32) -> Option<u32> {
        let id = *self.handles.get(&h)?;
        self.objects.get_mut(&id)?.refs += 1;
        Some(self.alloc_handle(id))
    }

    /// `CloseHandle`. Returns the object if this was its last handle.
    pub fn close(&mut self, h: u32) -> Result<Option<KernelObject>, ()> {
        let id = self.handles.remove(&h).ok_or(())?;
        let e = self.objects.get_mut(&id).ok_or(())?;
        e.refs -= 1;
        if e.refs == 0 {
            return Ok(self.objects.remove(&id).map(|e| e.obj));
        }
        Ok(None)
    }

    /// Identity of the object behind a handle (equal for duplicated / re-opened handles).
    pub fn object_id(&self, h: u32) -> Option<u32> {
        self.handles.get(&h).copied()
    }

    /// Name of the object behind a handle, if it was created named.
    pub fn name_of(&self, h: u32) -> Option<&str> {
        self.objects.get(self.handles.get(&h)?)?.name.as_deref()
    }

    /// Whether `h` is a live handle.
    pub fn contains(&self, h: u32) -> bool {
        self.handles.contains_key(&h)
    }

    /// Number of open handles.
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.handles.len()
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.handles.is_empty()
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-runtime/src/host.rs`:

```rs
//! The interface between the emulated machine and the platform frontend (desktop window, Android activity,
//! headless test runner).

use std::path::PathBuf;

/// A presented frame. Always RGB565 (`0bRRRRRGGGGGGBBBBB`); 8-bit palettized surfaces are converted by s3-dx.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct FrameBuffer {
    pub width: u32,
    pub height: u32,
    /// `width * height` pixels, row-major, no padding.
    pub pixels: Vec<u16>,
}

impl FrameBuffer {
    pub fn new(width: u32, height: u32) -> Self {
        FrameBuffer { width, height, pixels: vec![0; (width * height) as usize] }
    }

    /// Convert to packed 8-bit RGB triples.
    pub fn to_rgb888(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(self.pixels.len() * 3);
        for &p in &self.pixels {
            let (r, g, b) = rgb565_to_rgb888(p);
            out.extend_from_slice(&[r, g, b]);
        }
        out
    }
}

/// Expand one RGB565 pixel.
#[inline]
pub fn rgb565_to_rgb888(p: u16) -> (u8, u8, u8) {
    let r = ((p >> 11) & 0x1F) as u8;
    let g = ((p >> 5) & 0x3F) as u8;
    let b = (p & 0x1F) as u8;
    ((r << 3) | (r >> 2), (g << 2) | (g >> 4), (b << 3) | (b >> 2))
}

/// Mouse buttons.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum MouseButton {
    Left,
    Right,
    Middle,
}

/// Input / lifecycle events from the frontend. Coordinates are in game-screen pixels (the frontend undoes
/// its scaling/letterboxing).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum HostEvent {
    MouseMove { x: i32, y: i32 },
    MouseButton { button: MouseButton, down: bool },
    /// Windows virtual-key code (VK_*).
    Key { vk: u32, down: bool },
    /// Text input (WM_CHAR), already translated.
    Char(u32),
    Quit,
    Pause,
    Resume,
    /// Raw touch pointer (finger `id`) in game-screen pixels (`x`, `y`) and window pixels (`wx`, `wy`; negative =
    /// unknown, the mods then map the game position through the viewport). Consumed by the mod layer (`s3-mods`
    /// gesture recognizer; window-layer UI hit-tests with the window position) when installed; the game itself
    /// ignores it.
    Pointer { id: u32, phase: PointerPhase, x: i32, y: i32, wx: i32, wy: i32 },
}

/// Phase of a [`HostEvent::Pointer`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum PointerPhase {
    Down,
    Move,
    Up,
    /// The platform cancelled the gesture (e.g. system gesture took over).
    Cancel,
}

/// Log levels for [`Host::log`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub enum LogLevel {
    Error,
    Warn,
    Info,
    Debug,
    Trace,
}

/// Platform services. Implemented by s3-desktop (`s3run`), s3-android and tests.
pub trait Host: Send {
    /// Show a frame (called on DirectDraw Flip / primary-surface Blt).
    fn present(&mut self, fb: &FrameBuffer);
    /// Drain pending input / lifecycle events.
    fn poll_events(&mut self) -> Vec<HostEvent>;
    /// Queue interleaved PCM for playback.
    fn queue_audio(&mut self, _samples: &[i16], _rate: u32, _channels: u16) {}
    /// Frames queued in the host audio sink and not yet played (for mixer pacing). 0 if unknown.
    fn audio_queued_frames(&self) -> usize {
        0
    }
    /// Monotonic milliseconds (time base for GetTickCount/timeGetTime).
    fn now_ms(&self) -> u64;
    /// Read-only directory holding the user's game files (S3.EXE, GFX/, SND/, ...).
    fn game_dir(&self) -> PathBuf;
    /// Writable directory: saves, registry JSON, config, overlay of written files.
    fn data_dir(&self) -> PathBuf;
    /// Log a message.
    fn log(&self, level: LogLevel, msg: &str) {
        eprintln!("[{level:?}] {msg}");
    }
    /// Called when every guest thread is blocked; sleep a little instead of spinning.
    fn idle(&mut self, ms: u32) {
        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(ms as u64));
    }
}

/// Headless host for tests and `s3run --headless`: discards frames (but keeps the last one), no input.
pub struct NullHost {
    pub game_dir: PathBuf,
    pub data_dir: PathBuf,
    pub start: std::time::Instant,
    pub last_frame: Option<FrameBuffer>,
    pub presents: u64,
    pub events: Vec<HostEvent>,
    pub quiet: bool,
}

impl NullHost {
    pub fn new(game_dir: PathBuf, data_dir: PathBuf) -> Self {
        NullHost {
            game_dir,
            data_dir,
            start: std::time::Instant::now(),
            last_frame: None,
            presents: 0,
            events: Vec::new(),
            quiet: false,
        }
    }
}

impl Host for NullHost {
    fn present(&mut self, fb: &FrameBuffer) {
        self.presents += 1;
        self.last_frame = Some(fb.clone());
    }
    fn poll_events(&mut self) -> Vec<HostEvent> {
        std::mem::take(&mut self.events)
    }
    fn now_ms(&self) -> u64 {
        self.start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64
    }
    fn game_dir(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.game_dir.clone()
    }
    fn data_dir(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.data_dir.clone()
    }
    fn log(&self, level: LogLevel, msg: &str) {
        if !self.quiet || level <= LogLevel::Warn {
            eprintln!("[{level:?}] {msg}");
        }
    }
}
```

`port/crates/s3-runtime/src/hosttime.rs`:

```rs
//! Host wall-clock helpers for kernel32 time functions (FILETIME = 100 ns ticks since 1601-01-01 UTC).

use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

/// 100 ns ticks between 1601-01-01 and 1970-01-01.
pub const FILETIME_UNIX_EPOCH: u64 = 116_444_736_000_000_000;

/// Current UTC time as FILETIME.
pub fn now_filetime() -> u64 {
    let d = SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap_or_default();
    FILETIME_UNIX_EPOCH + d.as_secs() * 10_000_000 + d.subsec_nanos() as u64 / 100
}

/// FILETIME of a host `SystemTime` (file timestamps).
pub fn systemtime_to_filetime(t: SystemTime) -> u64 {
    match t.duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH) {
        Ok(d) => FILETIME_UNIX_EPOCH + d.as_secs() * 10_000_000 + d.subsec_nanos() as u64 / 100,
        Err(_) => FILETIME_UNIX_EPOCH,
    }
}

/// Host local time offset from UTC in seconds (east positive), e.g. +3600 for CET. 0 if unknown.
pub fn utc_offset_secs() -> i32 {
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        // SAFETY: localtime_r writes into our zeroed tm; time(NULL) is always safe.
        unsafe {
            let t = libc::time(std::ptr::null_mut());
            let mut tm: libc::tm = std::mem::zeroed();
            if !libc::localtime_r(&t, &mut tm).is_null() {
                return tm.tm_gmtoff as i32;
            }
        }
    }
    0
}
```

```rs
//! Input state fed from [`Host::poll_events`](crate::Host::poll_events). Several consumers (USER32 message
//! queue, DirectInput buffers) read the same event stream, each with its own cursor.

use std::collections::VecDeque;

use crate::host::{HostEvent, MouseButton};

const LOG_CAP: usize = 4096;

/// Current input state plus a short event log.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct InputState {
    pub mouse_x: i32,
    pub mouse_y: i32,
    /// Left, right, middle.
    pub buttons: [bool; 3],
    /// Indexed by VK code.
    pub keys: Vec<bool>,
    log: VecDeque<(u64, HostEvent)>,
    next_seq: u64,
    /// Set when the host asked to quit.
    pub quit_requested: bool,
    /// Set while the host app is paused (Android onPause).
    pub paused: bool,
}

impl InputState {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        InputState { keys: vec![false; 256], ..Default::default() }
    }

    /// Record an event and update the state.
    pub fn push(&mut self, e: HostEvent) {
        match e {
            HostEvent::MouseMove { x, y } => {
                self.mouse_x = x;
                self.mouse_y = y;
            }
            HostEvent::MouseButton { button, down } => {
                let i = match button {
                    MouseButton::Left => 0,
                    MouseButton::Right => 1,
                    MouseButton::Middle => 2,
                };
                self.buttons[i] = down;
            }
            HostEvent::Key { vk, down } => {
                if let Some(k) = self.keys.get_mut(vk as usize & 0xFF) {
                    *k = down;
                }
            }
            HostEvent::Quit => self.quit_requested = true,
            HostEvent::Pause => self.paused = true,
            HostEvent::Resume => self.paused = false,
            HostEvent::Char(_) => {}
            // Raw touch is for the mod layer; game consumers never see it.
            HostEvent::Pointer { .. } => return,
        }
        if self.log.len() == LOG_CAP {
            self.log.pop_front();
        }
        self.log.push_back((self.next_seq, e));
        self.next_seq += 1;
    }

    /// Events newer than `*cursor`; advances the cursor. A new consumer should start with
    /// [`InputState::cursor_now`] to skip history.
    pub fn events_since(&self, cursor: &mut u64) -> Vec<HostEvent> {
        let out: Vec<HostEvent> = self.log.iter().filter(|(s, _)| *s >= *cursor).map(|(_, e)| *e).collect();
        *cursor = self.next_seq;
        out
    }

    /// Cursor value that skips all events so far.
    pub fn cursor_now(&self) -> u64 {
        self.next_seq
    }
}
```

```rs
//! The machine: guest memory, guest threads (each with its own [`Cpu`]), the cooperative scheduler, thunk
//! dispatch, host->guest calls.

use std::any::{Any, TypeId};
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, MutexGuard};

use s3_cpu::{Context, Cpu, CpuExit, EAX, EDX, ESP};
use s3_mem::layout;
use s3_mem::{align_up, GuestMemory, RegionKind};

use crate::com::ComRegistry;
use crate::handles::{HandleTable, KernelObject};
use crate::host::{Host, LogLevel};
use crate::input::InputState;
use crate::registry::{Registry, ThunkResult};
use crate::vfs::Vfs;

/// Debug (env `S3_TIMELINE=<host ms>`): print host-µs timestamps of completed HLE calls for 200 ms from then.
static TIMELINE_FROM: std::sync::LazyLock<Option<u64>> =
    std::sync::LazyLock::new(|| std::env::var("S3_TIMELINE").ok().and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()));

/// Default instructions per scheduling quantum.
pub const DEFAULT_QUANTUM: u64 = 200_000;

/// TEB field offsets (x86).
pub mod teb {
    pub const EXCEPTION_LIST: u32 = 0x00;
    pub const STACK_BASE: u32 = 0x04;
    pub const STACK_LIMIT: u32 = 0x08;
    pub const SELF: u32 = 0x18;
    pub const PROCESS_ID: u32 = 0x20;
    pub const THREAD_ID: u32 = 0x24;
    pub const TLS_POINTER: u32 = 0x2C;
    pub const PEB: u32 = 0x30;
    pub const LAST_ERROR: u32 = 0x34;
    /// 64 TLS slots (TlsGetValue/TlsSetValue).
    pub const TLS_SLOTS: u32 = 0xE10;
    pub const TLS_SLOT_COUNT: u32 = 64;
}

/// Fake process id.
pub const PROCESS_ID: u32 = 0x10;

/// Guest thread state.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ThreadState {
    Runnable,
    /// Waiting in a thunk that returned `Block`; retried every scheduling round.
    Blocked,
    /// `CREATE_SUSPENDED` / `SuspendThread` count.
    Suspended(u32),
    Exited(u32),
}

/// One guest thread.
pub struct Thread {
    pub tid: u32,
    /// Handle created with the thread (also returned by CreateThread).
    pub handle: u32,
    pub cpu: Cpu,
    pub state: ThreadState,
    pub teb: u32,
    /// Highest stack address (initial ESP area).
    pub stack_top: u32,
    /// Lowest stack address.
    pub stack_bottom: u32,
    /// When the current blocking wait started (host ms), cleared when the thunk returns.
    pub block_since: Option<u64>,
    /// Depth of `call_guest` frames on the host stack for this thread.
    pub nested: u32,
    /// Exception dispatches in progress (see seh.rs).
    pub(crate) seh: Vec<crate::seh::Dispatch>,
    /// Object ids (`HandleTable::object_id`) this thread is blocked on in [`Machine::poll_wait`].
    pub wait_objs: Vec<u32>,
    /// Set by [`Machine::pulse_event`]: the object id that released this thread's pending wait.
    pub pulsed: Option<u32>,
    /// Guest address of the CRITICAL_SECTION this thread is blocked on (0 = none).
    pub wait_cs: u32,
    /// The critical section in `wait_cs` was handed over to this thread by its previous owner.
    pub cs_granted: bool,
    /// Host-side scheduling priority (SetThreadPriority); informational.
    pub priority: i32,
    /// Multi-core mode (`mt.rs`): the thread's CPU runs on the draw worker; `cpu` is a placeholder (counters
    /// mirrored) except while the worker dispatches one of its exits. The main scheduler skips it.
    pub offloaded: bool,
    /// Multi-core mode: the main thread runs this CPU outside the big lock right now (`cpu` is a spare).
    pub running_unlocked: bool,
    /// Host ns this thread spent in `Cpu::run` (profiling).
    pub cpu_ns: u64,
}

/// Why the machine stopped.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum StopReason {
    /// ExitProcess or all threads ended.
    Exited(u32),
    /// A function without implementation was called.
    Unimplemented(String),
    /// Unhandled CPU exception / unimplemented instruction.
    Fault(String),
    /// Any other error (handler bug, bad state).
    Error(String),
    /// Host requested quit.
    Quit,
}

impl std::fmt::Display for StopReason {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            StopReason::Exited(c) => write!(f, "process exited with code {c}"),
            StopReason::Unimplemented(s) => write!(f, "{s}"),
            StopReason::Fault(s) => write!(f, "fault: {s}"),
            StopReason::Error(s) => write!(f, "error: {s}"),
            StopReason::Quit => write!(f, "quit requested"),
        }
    }
}

/// Result of [`Machine::run_slice`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SliceResult {
    /// Guest code ran (instructions executed).
    Ran(u64),
    /// Every thread is blocked; the frontend may sleep.
    Idle,
    /// The machine stopped; see [`Machine::stop_reason`].
    Stopped,
}

/// Tracing (env `S3_TRACE=thunks` or `S3_TRACE=calls`, `S3_TRACE_LIMIT=n`, default 20000 lines).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct TraceConfig {
    pub thunks: bool,
    pub calls: bool,
    pub limit: u64,
    pub printed: u64,
}

impl TraceConfig {
    pub fn from_env() -> Self {
        let v = std::env::var("S3_TRACE").unwrap_or_default();
        let limit = std::env::var("S3_TRACE_LIMIT").ok().and_then(|s| s.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(20_000);
        TraceConfig { thunks: v.contains("thunks") || v.contains("calls"), calls: v.contains("calls"), limit, printed: 0 }
    }
}

/// Counters.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct Stats {
    pub instructions: u64,
    pub thunk_calls: u64,
    pub presents: u64,
    pub exceptions: u64,
    /// Guest-address hooks dispatched (see `ext.rs`).
    pub hooks: u64,
    /// Host nanoseconds spent inside the interpreter (`Cpu::run`), for profiling (S3_SAMPLE).
    pub cpu_ns: u64,
    /// Host-time profile of HLE handlers and hooks (env `S3_HOST_PROF=1`): key = thunk address or hook EIP,
    /// value = (calls, host ns). `None` = off. Diagnostics only; never changes guest behaviour.
    pub host_prof: Option<HashMap<u32, (u64, u64)>>,
    /// Named sections inside handlers (same switch), see [`Stats::host_prof_section`].
    pub host_prof_named: HashMap<&'static str, (u64, u64)>,
}

impl Stats {
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn host_prof_add(&mut self, key: u32, ns: u64) {
        if let Some(p) = &mut self.host_prof {
            let e = p.entry(key).or_default();
            e.0 += 1;
            e.1 += ns;
        }
    }

    /// Start timing a named section when `S3_HOST_PROF` is on (`None` otherwise); finish with
    /// [`Stats::host_prof_section`].
    #[inline]
    pub fn host_prof_start(&self) -> Option<std::time::Instant> {
        self.host_prof.is_some().then(std::time::Instant::now)
    }

    /// Add the time since `t0` (from [`Stats::host_prof_start`]) to the named section.
    #[inline]
    pub fn host_prof_section(&mut self, name: &'static str, t0: Option<std::time::Instant>) {
        if let Some(t0) = t0 {
            let e = self.host_prof_named.entry(name).or_default();
            e.0 += 1;
            e.1 += t0.elapsed().as_nanos() as u64;
        }
    }
}

/// Process-wide guest data created by [`Machine::setup_process`].

    pub cmdline_a: u32,

    pub module_path: String,
    /// ANSI / UTF-16 environment blocks (GetEnvironmentStrings[W]).
    pub env_a: u32,

    pub stack_reserve: u32,
```
