```rs
/// Shared HLE-module state stored in the machine (see [`Machine::state`]).
pub struct Shared<T>(Arc<Mutex<T>>);

impl<T> Clone for Shared<T> {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        Shared(self.0.clone())
    }
}

impl<T> Shared<T> {
    /// Borrow the state. Panics if it is already borrowed (e.g. held across `call_guest` and re-entered) —
    /// drop the guard before calling into the guest.
    pub fn borrow_mut(&self) -> MutexGuard<'_, T> {
        match self.0.try_lock() {
            Ok(g) => g,
            Err(std::sync::TryLockError::Poisoned(p)) => p.into_inner(),
            Err(std::sync::TryLockError::WouldBlock) => {
                panic!("HLE state {} borrowed twice (held across call_guest?)", std::any::type_name::<T>())
            }
        }
    }
}

/// A periodic host-side hook run by the scheduler once per `run_slice` (audio mixing, timers, input pumps).
pub type Service = fn(&mut Machine);

/// The emulated machine.
pub struct Machine {
    pub mem: GuestMemory,
    pub threads: Vec<Thread>,
    /// Index into `threads` of the running thread.
    pub cur: usize,
    pub registry: Registry,
    pub handles: HandleTable,
    pub host: Box<dyn Host>,
    pub vfs: Vfs,
    pub com: ComRegistry,
    pub input: InputState,
    pub process: ProcessInfo,
    pub trace: TraceConfig,
    pub stats: Stats,
    /// Instructions per scheduling quantum.
    pub quantum: u64,
    /// Mod extension points (hooks, input filter, overlay), see `ext.rs`.
    pub ext: crate::ext::MachineExt,
    services: Vec<(String, Service)>,
    state: HashMap<TypeId, Box<dyn Any + Send>>,
    stop: Option<StopReason>,
    pub(crate) thread_exit_thunk: u32,
    pub(crate) seh_return_thunk: u32,
    next_tid: u32,
    rr: usize,
    /// Multi-core mode (`mt.rs`); `None` = the default single-host-thread scheduler.
    pub(crate) mt: Option<Box<crate::mt::MtState>>,
    /// Debug/analysis hook called before (`false`) and after (`true`) each top-level scheduling turn of a thread
    /// (`run_thread`), e.g. `s3det --write-trace` (which memory each thread writes). Never changes guest state.
    pub run_observer: Option<RunObserver>,
    /// Guest time base (game speed, [`Machine::set_time_scale`]).
    clock: GuestClock,
}

/// The guest's clock: host time scaled by the game speed, continuous across speed changes.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
struct GuestClock {
    scale: f64,
    base_host: u64,
    base_guest: u64,
}

impl GuestClock {
    fn at(&self, host_ms: u64) -> u64 {
        if self.scale == 1.0 {
            return self.base_guest + host_ms.saturating_sub(self.base_host);
        }
        self.base_guest + (host_ms.saturating_sub(self.base_host) as f64 * self.scale) as u64
    }
}

/// See [`Machine::run_observer`]: `(machine, thread slot, after)`.
pub type RunObserver = fn(&mut Machine, usize, bool);

impl Drop for Machine {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // The draw worker uses the guest mapping: stop it before `mem` is released.
        self.mt_shutdown();
    }
}

impl Machine {
    /// New machine with empty address space, internal thunks registered and the VFS rooted at the host's
    /// game/data dirs. HLE modules are registered by the caller (s3-engine).
    pub fn new(host: Box<dyn Host>) -> Result<Machine, String> {
        let mut mem = GuestMemory::new().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        // System area (PEB + TEBs) and the thunk page are runtime-owned allocations.
        mem.alloc_region(
            Some(layout::SYSTEM_AREA_START),
            layout::SYSTEM_AREA_END - layout::SYSTEM_AREA_START,
            RegionKind::Private,
            (0, 0),
        )
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        mem.alloc_region(Some(layout::THUNK_BASE), layout::THUNK_END - layout::THUNK_BASE, RegionKind::Image, (0, 0))
            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let vfs = Vfs::new(host.game_dir(), host.data_dir());
        let mut registry = Registry::new();
        let thread_exit_thunk = registry.register("s3port.dll", "thread_exit", thread_exit);
        let seh_return_thunk = registry.register("s3port.dll", "seh_handler_return", crate::seh::handler_return);
        Ok(Machine {
            mem,
            threads: Vec::new(),
            cur: 0,
            registry,
            handles: HandleTable::new(),
            host,
            vfs,
            com: ComRegistry::default(),
            input: InputState::new(),
            process: ProcessInfo::default(),
            trace: TraceConfig::from_env(),
            stats: Stats {
                host_prof: std::env::var_os("S3_HOST_PROF").map(|_| HashMap::new()),
                ..Stats::default()
            },
            quantum: DEFAULT_QUANTUM,
            ext: Default::default(),
            services: Vec::new(),
            state: HashMap::new(),
            stop: None,
            thread_exit_thunk,
            seh_return_thunk,
            next_tid: 0x104,
            rr: 0,
            mt: None,
            run_observer: None,
            clock: GuestClock { scale: 1.0, base_host: 0, base_guest: 0 },
        })
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ small accessors

    /// The running thread.
    pub fn thread(&mut self) -> &mut Thread {
        &mut self.threads[self.cur]
    }

    /// The running thread's CPU.
    pub fn cpu(&mut self) -> &mut Cpu {
        &mut self.threads[self.cur].cpu
    }

    /// Thread id of the running thread.
    pub fn current_tid(&self) -> u32 {
        self.threads.get(self.cur).map(|t| t.tid).unwrap_or(0)
    }

    /// Thread slot by thread id.
    pub fn thread_by_tid(&self, tid: u32) -> Option<usize> {
        self.threads.iter().position(|t| t.tid == tid)
    }

    /// Guest time in ms: what the game sees (GetTickCount, timeGetTime, waits, timers). Host time scaled by the
    /// game speed ([`Machine::set_time_scale`]); equal to [`Machine::real_ms`] at speed 1.
    pub fn now_ms(&self) -> u64 {
        self.clock.at(self.host.now_ms())
    }

    /// Host monotonic time in ms (wall clock): UI timing, audio, display pacing.
    pub fn real_ms(&self) -> u64 {
        self.host.now_ms()
    }

    /// Game speed (1.0 = normal).
    pub fn time_scale(&self) -> f64 {
        self.clock.scale
    }

    /// Set the game speed: guest time then runs `scale` times as fast as the wall clock (continuous: no jump).
    /// Single-player only (lockstep multiplayer peers must share one speed).
    pub fn set_time_scale(&mut self, scale: f64) {
        let scale = if scale.is_finite() && scale > 0.0 { scale } else { 1.0 };
        let host = self.host.now_ms();
        let guest = self.clock.at(host);
        self.clock = GuestClock { scale, base_host: host, base_guest: guest };
    }

    /// Present a frame through the host (counts presents).
    /// The current mouse cursor (`crate::cursor::CursorState`) is composed into a host-side copy of `fb`.
    pub fn present(&mut self, fb: &crate::FrameBuffer) {
        self.stats.presents += 1;
        if self.mt.is_some() {
            self.mt_note_present();
        }
        self.present_inner(fb);
    }

    /// Like [`Machine::present`], but takes the frame by value and returns a buffer for the next frame (the
    /// previous one, to reuse its allocation). With an overlay the frame becomes the remembered guest frame
    /// without a copy (perf-r2).
    pub fn present_owned(&mut self, fb: crate::FrameBuffer) -> crate::FrameBuffer {
        self.stats.presents += 1;
        if self.mt.is_some() {
            // Multi-core mode: the draw worker only queues the frame; the main host thread composes and presents
            // it (`mt.rs`), so the overlay/cursor/host work leaves the draw thread's critical path and the lock.
            if self.threads.get(self.cur).is_some_and(|t| t.offloaded) {
                return self.mt_defer_present(fb);
            }
            self.mt_note_present();
        }
        self.present_owned_now(fb)
    }

    /// The composing part of [`Machine::present_owned`] (overlay, cursor, `Host::present`).
    pub(crate) fn present_owned_now(&mut self, fb: crate::FrameBuffer) -> crate::FrameBuffer {
        if !self.has_overlay() {
            self.present_cursor(&fb);
            return fb;
        }
        let old = self.ext.last_guest_frame.take().unwrap_or_default();
        self.ext.last_guest_size = (fb.width, fb.height);
        let last = fb;
        let t0 = self.stats.host_prof_start();
        self.run_window_overlay(&last);
        self.ext.frame_overlay_shown = false;
        let composed = self.apply_overlay_to(&last);
        self.stats.host_prof_section("present: overlay copy + compose", t0);
        let t1 = self.stats.host_prof_start();
        match composed {
            Some(out) => self.present_cursor_owned(out),
            None => self.present_cursor(&last),
        }
        self.stats.host_prof_section("present: cursor + Host::present", t1);
        self.ext.last_guest_frame = Some(last);
        old
    }

    /// Overlay (mods) + cursor composition, then `Host::present`.
    pub(crate) fn present_inner(&mut self, fb: &crate::FrameBuffer) {
        if self.has_overlay() {
            self.ext.frame_overlay_shown = false;
            if let Some(out) = self.apply_overlay(fb) {
                self.present_cursor(&out);
                self.recycle_overlay(out);
                return;
            }
        }
        self.present_cursor(fb);
    }

    /// Present an owned composed frame (overlay output): the cursor state keeps it without a copy and the
    /// buffer it held goes back to the overlay pool.
    pub(crate) fn present_cursor_owned(&mut self, fb: crate::FrameBuffer) {
        let (x, y) = (self.input.mouse_x, self.input.mouse_y);
        let cs = self.state::<crate::cursor::CursorState>();
        let mut c = cs.borrow_mut();
        let old = c.compose_owned(fb, x, y);
        if let Some(f) = c.shown() {
            self.host.present(f);
        }
        drop(c);
        if let Some(o) = old {
            self.recycle_overlay(o);
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn present_cursor(&mut self, fb: &crate::FrameBuffer) {
        let (x, y) = (self.input.mouse_x, self.input.mouse_y);
        let cs = self.state::<crate::cursor::CursorState>();
        let mut c = cs.borrow_mut();
        match c.compose(fb, x, y) {
            Some(out) => self.host.present(out),
            None => self.host.present(fb),
        }
    }

    /// Re-present the last guest frame if only the cursor changed (moved, new shape, shown/hidden). Called
    /// by the user32 "cursor" service once per `run_slice`; not counted in `stats.presents`.
    pub fn refresh_cursor(&mut self) {
        let (x, y) = (self.input.mouse_x, self.input.mouse_y);
        let cs = self.state::<crate::cursor::CursorState>();
        let mut c = cs.borrow_mut();
        if let Some(out) = c.refresh(x, y) {
            self.host.present(out);
        }
    }

    /// Log through the host.
    pub fn log(&self, level: LogLevel, msg: &str) {
        self.host.log(level, msg);
    }

    /// Typed HLE-module state, created with `Default` on first use. Clone the handle, then
    /// `borrow_mut()`; do not hold the guard across [`Machine::call_guest`].
    pub fn state<T: Default + Send + 'static>(&mut self) -> Shared<T> {
        let e = self
            .state
            .entry(TypeId::of::<T>())
            .or_insert_with(|| Box::new(Shared(Arc::new(Mutex::new(T::default())))));
        e.downcast_ref::<Shared<T>>().expect("state type").clone()
    }

    /// Add a host-side service run once per `run_slice`.
    pub fn add_service(&mut self, name: &str, f: Service) {
        if !self.services.iter().any(|(n, _)| n == name) {
            self.services.push((name.to_string(), f));
        }
    }

    /// Human-readable host-time profile (`S3_HOST_PROF=1`): top `n` handlers/hooks/services by host time.
    pub fn host_prof_report(&self, n: usize) -> String {
        let Some(p) = &self.stats.host_prof else { return String::new() };
        let mut v: Vec<_> = p.iter().collect();
        v.sort_by_key(|(_, (_, ns))| std::cmp::Reverse(*ns));
        let total: u64 = v.iter().map(|(_, (_, ns))| *ns).sum();
        let mut s = format!("host time in HLE handlers/hooks/services: {} ms\n", total / 1_000_000);
        for (k, (calls, ns)) in v.into_iter().take(n) {
            let name = if (*k as usize) < self.services.len() {
                format!("service {}", self.services[*k as usize].0)
            } else if *k >= layout::THUNK_BASE {
                self.registry.describe(*k)
            } else {
                format!("hook {k:#x}")
            };
            s.push_str(&format!("  {:>8} ms {:>9} calls  {}\n", ns / 1_000_000, calls, name));
        }
        let mut v: Vec<_> = self.stats.host_prof_named.iter().collect();
        v.sort_by_key(|(_, (_, ns))| std::cmp::Reverse(*ns));
        for (k, (calls, ns)) in v {
            s.push_str(&format!("  {:>8} ms {:>9} calls  section {}\n", ns / 1_000_000, calls, k));
        }
        s
    }

    /// Stop the machine (first reason wins).
    pub fn stop(&mut self, reason: StopReason) {
        if self.stop.is_none() {
            self.host.log(LogLevel::Warn, &format!("machine stopping: {reason}"));
            self.stop = Some(reason);
        }
    }

    pub fn stop_reason(&self) -> Option<&StopReason> {
        self.stop.as_ref()
    }

    pub fn is_stopped(&self) -> bool {
        self.stop.is_some()
    }

    /// Invalidate decoded code in all threads (after the guest wrote code / VirtualProtect to executable).
    pub fn invalidate_code(&mut self, start: u32, len: u32) {
        for t in &mut self.threads {
            t.cpu.invalidate_range(start, len);
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ arguments (stdcall/cdecl)

    /// Argument `i` (0-based) of the current thunk call: `[esp + 4 + 4*i]` (ESP points at the return address).
    pub fn arg_u32(&self, i: u32) -> u32 {
        let esp = self.threads[self.cur].cpu.regs[ESP];
        self.mem.read_u32(esp.wrapping_add(4 + 4 * i))
    }

    pub fn arg_i32(&self, i: u32) -> i32 {
        self.arg_u32(i) as i32
    }

    /// Pointer argument (same as `arg_u32`, for readability).
    pub fn arg_ptr(&self, i: u32) -> u32 {
        self.arg_u32(i)
    }

    /// ANSI string argument (`None` for a NULL pointer).
    pub fn arg_str(&self, i: u32) -> Option<String> {
        let p = self.arg_u32(i);
        if p == 0 {
            None
        } else {
            Some(self.mem.read_cstr(p))
        }
    }

    /// UTF-16 string argument (`None` for a NULL pointer).
    pub fn arg_wstr(&self, i: u32) -> Option<String> {
        let p = self.arg_u32(i);
        if p == 0 {
            None
        } else {
            Some(self.mem.read_wstr(p))
        }
    }

    /// Return address of the current thunk call.
    pub fn return_address(&self) -> u32 {
        self.mem.read_u32(self.threads[self.cur].cpu.regs[ESP])
    }

    /// `SetLastError` for the running thread (TEB+0x34).
    pub fn set_last_error(&mut self, v: u32) {
        let teb = self.threads[self.cur].teb;
        self.mem.write_u32(teb + teb::LAST_ERROR, v);
    }

    /// `GetLastError` for the running thread.
    pub fn last_error(&self) -> u32 {
        self.mem.read_u32(self.threads[self.cur].teb + teb::LAST_ERROR)
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ process & threads

    /// Create PEB, process parameters, command line and environment. Call after loading the image.
    pub fn setup_process(&mut self, image_base: u32, image_size: u32, entry: u32, stack_reserve: u32, exe_name: &str) {
        crate::process::setup_process(self, image_base, image_size, entry, stack_reserve, exe_name);
    }

    /// Create a guest thread that starts at `entry(param)` (stdcall, returning into ExitThread).
    /// Returns the slot index; the thread's handle and tid are in `threads[slot]`.
    pub fn create_thread(&mut self, entry: u32, param: u32, stack_size: u32, suspended: bool) -> Result<usize, String> {
        let slot = self.threads.len();
        let teb_addr = layout::TEB_TOP - slot as u32 * layout::PAGE_SIZE;
        if teb_addr <= layout::SYSTEM_AREA_START + 0x1_0000 {
            return Err("too many threads".into());
        }
        let size = align_up(stack_size.max(0x1_0000), layout::ALLOC_GRANULARITY);
        let bottom = self
            .mem
            .alloc_region(None, size, RegionKind::Private, (layout::STACK_ARENA_START, layout::STACK_ARENA_END))
            .map_err(|e| format!("thread stack: {e}"))?;
        let top = bottom + size;
        let tid = self.next_tid;
        self.next_tid += 4;

        self.mem.fill(teb_addr, layout::PAGE_SIZE as usize, 0);
        self.mem.write_u32(teb_addr + teb::EXCEPTION_LIST, 0xFFFF_FFFF);
        self.mem.write_u32(teb_addr + teb::STACK_BASE, top);
        self.mem.write_u32(teb_addr + teb::STACK_LIMIT, bottom);
        self.mem.write_u32(teb_addr + teb::SELF, teb_addr);
        self.mem.write_u32(teb_addr + teb::PROCESS_ID, PROCESS_ID);
        self.mem.write_u32(teb_addr + teb::THREAD_ID, tid);
        self.mem.write_u32(teb_addr + teb::TLS_POINTER, teb_addr + teb::TLS_SLOTS);
        self.mem.write_u32(teb_addr + teb::PEB, self.process.peb);

        let mut cpu = Cpu::new();
        cpu.fs_base = teb_addr;
        cpu.set_hooks(self.ext.hook_addrs.clone());
        cpu.set_native_blocks(self.ext.native_blocks.clone());
        cpu.regs[ESP] = top - 16;
        cpu.push32(&mut self.mem, param);
        cpu.push32(&mut self.mem, self.thread_exit_thunk);
        cpu.eip = entry;

        let handle = self.handles.insert(KernelObject::Thread { tid });
        self.threads.push(Thread {
            tid,
            handle,
            cpu,
            state: if suspended { ThreadState::Suspended(1) } else { ThreadState::Runnable },
            teb: teb_addr,
            stack_top: top,
            stack_bottom: bottom,
            block_since: None,
            nested: 0,
            seh: Vec::new(),
            wait_objs: Vec::new(),
            pulsed: None,
            wait_cs: 0,
            cs_granted: false,
            priority: 0,
            offloaded: false,
            running_unlocked: false,
            cpu_ns: 0,
        });
        Ok(slot)
    }

    /// Mark a thread exited (its handle becomes signaled).
    pub fn exit_thread(&mut self, slot: usize, code: u32) {
        self.threads[slot].state = ThreadState::Exited(code);
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ waits

    /// Is the object behind `h` signaled? `None` if `h` is not a waitable handle.
    pub fn is_signaled(&self, h: u32) -> Option<bool> {
        let tid = self.current_tid();
        match self.handles.get(h)? {
            KernelObject::Event { signaled, .. } => Some(*signaled),
            KernelObject::Mutex { owner, .. } => Some(owner.is_none() || *owner == Some(tid)),
            KernelObject::Semaphore { count, .. } => Some(*count > 0),
            KernelObject::Thread { tid: t } => {
                let s = self.thread_by_tid(*t)?;
                Some(matches!(self.threads[s].state, ThreadState::Exited(_)))
            }
            KernelObject::Process => Some(false),
            KernelObject::Timer { signaled, due_ms, .. } => {
                Some(*signaled || due_ms.map(|d| self.now_ms() >= d).unwrap_or(false))
            }
            KernelObject::Other(..) => None,
        }
    }

    /// If `h` is signaled, consume it (auto-reset event -> reset, semaphore -> count-1, mutex -> owned by
    /// the current thread) and return true.
    pub fn try_acquire(&mut self, h: u32) -> bool {
        if self.is_signaled(h) != Some(true) {
            return false;
        }
        let tid = self.current_tid();
        match self.handles.get_mut(h) {
            Some(KernelObject::Event { manual_reset, signaled }) => {
                if !*manual_reset {
                    *signaled = false;
                }
            }
            Some(KernelObject::Semaphore { count, .. }) => *count -= 1,
            Some(KernelObject::Mutex { owner, recursion }) => {
                *owner = Some(tid);
                *recursion += 1;
            }
            Some(KernelObject::Timer { manual_reset, signaled, due_ms, period_ms }) => {
                let now = self.clock.at(self.host.now_ms());
                if let Some(d) = *due_ms {
                    if now >= d {
                        *due_ms = if *period_ms > 0 {
                            let next = d + *period_ms as u64;
                            Some(if next <= now { now + *period_ms as u64 } else { next })
                        } else {
                            None
                        };
                    }
                }
                *signaled = *manual_reset;
            }
            _ => {}
        }
        true
    }

    /// Generic Win32 wait for the running thread (WaitForSingleObject / WaitForMultipleObjects /
    /// MsgWaitForMultipleObjects). Call it from a thunk handler; on [`WaitPoll::Pending`] return
    /// `ThunkResult::Block` (the handler is called again later). `timeout_ms` = `INFINITE` (0xFFFFFFFF) never
    /// times out; the timeout is measured from the first call (`Thread::block_since`).
    /// On success the object is consumed (auto-reset event reset, semaphore decremented, mutex owned).
    pub fn poll_wait(&mut self, handles: &[u32], wait_all: bool, timeout_ms: u32) -> WaitPoll {
        let slot = self.cur;
        let mut ids = Vec::with_capacity(handles.len());
        for &h in handles {
            match (self.is_signaled(h), self.handles.object_id(h)) {
                (Some(_), Some(id)) => ids.push(id),
                _ => {
                    self.threads[slot].wait_objs.clear();
                    return WaitPoll::Failed;
                }
            }
        }
        // Released by PulseEvent while blocked?
        if let Some(p) = self.threads[slot].pulsed.take() {
            if let Some(i) = ids.iter().position(|&id| id == p) {
                if !wait_all || handles.len() == 1 {
                    self.threads[slot].wait_objs.clear();
                    return WaitPoll::Ready(i as u32);
                }
            }
        }
        if wait_all {
            if handles.iter().all(|&h| self.is_signaled(h) == Some(true)) {
                for &h in handles {
                    self.try_acquire(h);
                }
                self.threads[slot].wait_objs.clear();
                return WaitPoll::Ready(0);
            }
        } else {
            for (i, &h) in handles.iter().enumerate() {
                if self.try_acquire(h) {
                    self.threads[slot].wait_objs.clear();
                    return WaitPoll::Ready(i as u32);
                }
            }
        }
        if self.wait_timed_out(timeout_ms) {
            self.threads[slot].wait_objs.clear();
            return WaitPoll::Timeout;
        }
        self.threads[slot].wait_objs = ids;
        WaitPoll::Pending
    }

    /// Has the running thread's current wait (started at `block_since`) exceeded `timeout_ms`?
    /// `timeout_ms == 0` is always timed out; `INFINITE` never.
    pub fn wait_timed_out(&self, timeout_ms: u32) -> bool {
        if timeout_ms == 0 {
            return true;
        }
        if timeout_ms == 0xFFFF_FFFF {
            return false;
        }
        match self.threads[self.cur].block_since {
            Some(t0) => self.now_ms().saturating_sub(t0) >= timeout_ms as u64,
            None => false,
        }
    }

    /// `PulseEvent`: release waiters blocked on the event `h` (all for manual-reset, one for auto-reset),
    /// then leave the event non-signaled. Returns false if `h` is not an event.
    pub fn pulse_event(&mut self, h: u32) -> bool {
        let Some(id) = self.handles.object_id(h) else { return false };
        let manual = match self.handles.get_mut(h) {
            Some(KernelObject::Event { manual_reset, signaled }) => {
                *signaled = false;
                *manual_reset
            }
            _ => return false,
        };
        for t in self.threads.iter_mut() {
            if t.state == ThreadState::Blocked && t.pulsed.is_none() && t.wait_objs.contains(&id) {
                t.pulsed = Some(id);
                if !manual {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        true
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ scheduler

    /// Run guest code for about `max_instructions` instructions across all threads (round robin, each thread
    /// up to `quantum` per turn). Polls host input first and runs services.
    pub fn run_slice(&mut self, max_instructions: u64) -> SliceResult {
        if self.stop.is_some() {
            return SliceResult::Stopped;
        }
        if self.mt.is_some() {
            self.mt_maintain();
        }
        for e in self.host.poll_events() {
            self.filter_event(e);
        }
        let services: Vec<Service> = self.services.iter().map(|(_, f)| *f).collect();
        for (i, s) in services.into_iter().enumerate() {
            if self.stats.host_prof.is_some() {
                let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
                s(self);
                self.stats.host_prof_add(i as u32, t0.elapsed().as_nanos() as u64);
            } else {
                s(self);
            }
        }
        let start = self.stats.instructions;
        let mut progressed = false;
        loop {
            let n = self.threads.len();
            if n == 0 {
                self.stop(StopReason::Error("no threads".into()));
                return SliceResult::Stopped;
            }
            let mut round_progress = false;
            for k in 0..n {
                let slot = (self.rr + k) % n;
                let t = &self.threads[slot];
                if matches!(t.state, ThreadState::Exited(_) | ThreadState::Suspended(_)) || t.nested > 0 || t.offloaded
                {
                    continue;
                }
                let budget = self.quantum.min(max_instructions.saturating_sub(self.stats.instructions - start)).max(1);
                if self.run_thread_top(slot, budget) {
                    round_progress = true;
                }
                if self.stop.is_some() {
                    return SliceResult::Stopped;
                }
            }
            self.rr = (self.rr + 1) % n.max(1);
            if self.threads.iter().all(|t| matches!(t.state, ThreadState::Exited(_))) {
                self.stop(StopReason::Exited(0));
                return SliceResult::Stopped;
            }
            progressed |= round_progress;
            if !round_progress || self.stats.instructions - start >= max_instructions {
                break;
            }
        }
        if progressed {
            SliceResult::Ran(self.stats.instructions - start)
        } else {
            SliceResult::Idle
        }
    }

    /// Run one thread for up to `budget` instructions (nested scheduling, e.g. from `call_guest`: the big lock of
    /// the multi-core mode stays held). Returns true if it made progress.
    fn run_thread(&mut self, slot: usize, budget: u64) -> bool {
        self.run_thread_ex(slot, budget, false)
    }

    /// Like [`Machine::run_thread`], from the top-level scheduler: with a draw worker running, the guest code
    /// runs with the big lock released (`mt.rs`).
    fn run_thread_top(&mut self, slot: usize, budget: u64) -> bool {
        self.run_thread_ex(slot, budget, true)
    }

    fn run_thread_ex(&mut self, slot: usize, budget: u64, top: bool) -> bool {
        if let (true, Some(f)) = (top, self.run_observer) {
            f(self, slot, false);
            let r = self.run_thread_inner(slot, budget, top);
            f(self, slot, true);
            return r;
        }
        self.run_thread_inner(slot, budget, top)
    }

    fn run_thread_inner(&mut self, slot: usize, budget: u64, top: bool) -> bool {
        self.cur = slot;
        let mut left = budget;
        let mut progress = false;
        loop {
            let before = self.threads[slot].cpu.instructions;
            let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
            // A blocked thread only re-enters its thunk (no guest code): no need to drop the lock for that.
            let exit = if top && self.threads[slot].state == ThreadState::Runnable && self.mt_active() {
                self.run_cpu_unlocked(slot, left)
            } else {
                let t = &mut self.threads[slot];
                t.cpu.run(&mut self.mem, left)
            };
            let dt = t0.elapsed().as_nanos() as u64;
            self.stats.cpu_ns += dt;
            let t = &mut self.threads[slot];
            t.cpu_ns += dt;
            let ran = t.cpu.instructions - before;
            self.stats.instructions += ran;
            left = left.saturating_sub(ran);
            if ran > 0 {
                progress = true;
            }
            self.cur = slot;
            match exit {
                CpuExit::Budget => return progress,
                CpuExit::Thunk(a) => match self.dispatch_thunk(a) {
                    Disp::Continue => {
                        progress = true;
                        if left == 0 {
                            return true;
                        }
                    }
                    Disp::Blocked => return progress,
                    Disp::ThreadExited => return true,
                    Disp::Stop => return progress,
                },
                CpuExit::Hook(a) => {
                    progress = true;
                    self.dispatch_hook(a);
                }
                CpuExit::ReturnMagic => {
                    self.stop(StopReason::Error(format!("thread {slot}: return to magic address outside call_guest")));
                    return progress;
                }
                other => {
                    if !crate::seh::handle_cpu_exit(self, other) {
                        return progress;
                    }
                    progress = true;
                }
            }
            if self.stop.is_some() {
                return progress;
            }
        }
    }

    /// Run all other runnable threads once (used while the current thread waits inside a nested call).
    fn run_others(&mut self, except: usize) -> bool {
        let mut progress = false;
        for slot in 0..self.threads.len() {
            if slot == except {
                continue;
            }
            let t = &self.threads[slot];
            if matches!(t.state, ThreadState::Exited(_) | ThreadState::Suspended(_))
                || t.nested > 0
                || t.offloaded
                || t.running_unlocked
            {
                continue;
            }
            if self.run_thread(slot, self.quantum) {
                progress = true;
            }
            if self.stop.is_some() {
                break;
            }
        }
        self.cur = except;
        progress
    }

    pub(crate) fn dispatch_thunk(&mut self, addr: u32) -> Disp {
        let slot = self.cur;
        let retry = self.threads[slot].block_since.is_some();
        let handler = match self.registry.entry_mut(addr) {
            Some(e) => {
                if !retry {
                    e.calls += 1;
                }
                e.handler
            }
            None => {
                self.stop(StopReason::Error(format!("jump into unused thunk {addr:#x}")));
                return Disp::Stop;
            }
        };
        if !retry {
            self.stats.thunk_calls += 1;
            if self.trace.thunks && self.trace.printed < self.trace.limit {
                self.trace.printed += 1;
                let mut s = format!("[t{}] {} from {:#x}", slot, self.registry.describe(addr), self.return_address());
                if self.trace.calls {
                    s.push_str(&format!(
                        " ({:#x}, {:#x}, {:#x}, {:#x})",
                        self.arg_u32(0),
                        self.arg_u32(1),
                        self.arg_u32(2),
                        self.arg_u32(3)
                    ));
                }
                self.host.log(LogLevel::Trace, &s);
            }
        }
        let Some(h) = handler else {
            let msg = format!("UNIMPLEMENTED {} (called from {:#x})", self.registry.describe(addr), self.return_address());
            self.stop(StopReason::Unimplemented(msg));
            return Disp::Stop;
        };
        let r = if self.stats.host_prof.is_some() {
            let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
            let r = h(self);
            self.stats.host_prof_add(addr, t0.elapsed().as_nanos() as u64);
            r
        } else {
            h(self)
        };
        self.cur = slot;
        if let Some(from) = *TIMELINE_FROM {
            let now = self.host.now_ms();
            if now >= from && now < from + 200 && (!retry || !matches!(r, ThunkResult::Block)) {
                let res = match r {
                    ThunkResult::Return { eax, .. } => format!("-> {eax:#x}"),
                    ThunkResult::Block => "BLOCK".into(),
                    _ => String::new(),
                };
                eprintln!(
                    "timeline {} us t{} {} ({:#x}, {:#x}, {:#x}) from {:#x} {res}",
                    crate::mt::now_us(),
                    slot,
                    self.registry.describe(addr),
                    self.arg_u32(0),
                    self.arg_u32(1),
                    self.arg_u32(2),
                    self.return_address()
                );
            }
        }
        // Multi-core mode: wake the other host thread if this call may have signaled something it waits for
        // (blocking handlers have no side effects before they block, so a `Block` changes nothing).
        if self.mt.is_some() && !matches!(r, ThunkResult::Block) {
            self.mt_bump();
        }
        if self.trace.calls && self.trace.printed < self.trace.limit {
            if let ThunkResult::Return { eax, .. } | ThunkResult::Return64 { eax, .. } = r {
                self.trace.printed += 1;
                self.host.log(LogLevel::Trace, &format!("[t{}]   {} -> {:#x}", slot, self.registry.describe(addr), eax));
            }
        }
        self.apply_result(slot, r)
    }

    fn apply_result(&mut self, slot: usize, r: ThunkResult) -> Disp {
        let t = &mut self.threads[slot];
        match r {
            ThunkResult::Return { eax, pop_bytes } => {
                t.cpu.regs[EAX] = eax;
                let ret = t.cpu.pop32(&self.mem);
                t.cpu.regs[ESP] = t.cpu.regs[ESP].wrapping_add(pop_bytes);
                t.cpu.eip = ret;
                t.block_since = None;
                if t.state == ThreadState::Blocked {
                    t.state = ThreadState::Runnable;
                }
                Disp::Continue
            }
            ThunkResult::Return64 { eax, edx, pop_bytes } => {
                t.cpu.regs[EAX] = eax;
                t.cpu.regs[EDX] = edx;
                let ret = t.cpu.pop32(&self.mem);
                t.cpu.regs[ESP] = t.cpu.regs[ESP].wrapping_add(pop_bytes);
                t.cpu.eip = ret;
                t.block_since = None;
                if t.state == ThreadState::Blocked {
                    t.state = ThreadState::Runnable;
                }
                Disp::Continue
            }
            ThunkResult::Done => {
                t.block_since = None;
                if t.state == ThreadState::Blocked {
                    t.state = ThreadState::Runnable;
                }
                Disp::Continue
            }
            ThunkResult::Block => {
                if t.block_since.is_none() {
                    t.block_since = Some(self.clock.at(self.host.now_ms()));
                }
                t.state = ThreadState::Blocked;
                Disp::Blocked
            }
            ThunkResult::Exit(code) => {
                self.stop(StopReason::Exited(code));
                Disp::Stop
            }
            ThunkResult::ExitThread(code) => {
                t.state = ThreadState::Exited(code);
                t.block_since = None;
                Disp::ThreadExited
            }
            ThunkResult::Error(e) => {
                self.stop(StopReason::Error(e));
                Disp::Stop
            }
        }
    }

    /// Call guest code `addr(args...)` on the current thread and return EAX. Works for stdcall and cdecl
    /// callees (all registers, including ESP, are restored afterwards). Nested calls are fine. While the guest
    /// code blocks, other threads run. Returns 0 if the machine stopped meanwhile.
    pub fn call_guest(&mut self, addr: u32, args: &[u32]) -> u32 {
        let slot = self.cur;
        let saved: Context = self.threads[slot].cpu.context();
        {
            let t = &mut self.threads[slot];
            for &a in args.iter().rev() {
                t.cpu.push32(&mut self.mem, a);
            }
            t.cpu.push32(&mut self.mem, layout::MAGIC_RETURN);
            t.cpu.eip = addr;
            t.nested += 1;
        }
        let result = loop {
            if self.stop.is_some() {
                break 0;
            }
            self.cur = slot;
            let t = &mut self.threads[slot];
            let before = t.cpu.instructions;
            let exit = t.cpu.run(&mut self.mem, self.quantum);
            self.stats.instructions += t.cpu.instructions - before;
            match exit {
                CpuExit::ReturnMagic => break self.threads[slot].cpu.regs[EAX],
                CpuExit::Budget => {
                    self.run_others(slot);
                }
                CpuExit::Hook(a) => self.dispatch_hook(a),
                CpuExit::Thunk(a) => match self.dispatch_thunk(a) {
                    Disp::Continue => {}
                    Disp::Blocked => {
                        if !self.run_others(slot) {
                            // Multi-core mode: releases the big lock while waiting (the thread that can
                            // wake this one may be on the other host thread).
                            self.idle(1);
                        }
                    }
                    Disp::ThreadExited => {
                        self.stop(StopReason::Error("thread exited inside a host->guest call".into()));
                        break 0;
                    }
                    Disp::Stop => break 0,
                },
                other => {
                    if !crate::seh::handle_cpu_exit(self, other) {
                        break 0;
                    }
                }
            }
        };
        self.cur = slot;
        let t = &mut self.threads[slot];
        t.nested -= 1;
        t.cpu.set_context(&saved);
        result
    }
}

/// Result of [`Machine::poll_wait`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum WaitPoll {
    /// Object `index` was signaled (and consumed); for wait-all always 0.
    Ready(u32),
    Timeout,
    /// A handle is invalid or not waitable (ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE).
    Failed,
    /// Not yet: return `ThunkResult::Block`.
    Pending,
}

/// Outcome of dispatching one thunk.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Disp {
    Continue,
    Blocked,
    ThreadExited,
    Stop,
}

/// `s3port.dll!thread_exit`: thread entry functions return here.
fn thread_exit(m: &mut Machine) -> ThunkResult {
    let code = m.cpu().regs[EAX];
    ThunkResult::ExitThread(code)
}
```

`port/crates/s3-runtime/src/mapfile.rs`:

```rs
//! Memory-mapped files for `CreateFileMappingA` / `MapViewOfFile`: the host file is `mmap`ed (MAP_PRIVATE |
//! MAP_FIXED) straight into the guest window, so the ~230 MB of GFX `.dat` files the game maps cost no RAM
//! until touched. Guest writes to a view stay private (copy-on-write; HYPOTHESIS: the game never writes
//! through a file view — wine-trace shows read-only mappings only).
//!
//! Pages wholly beyond EOF are left as the window's anonymous zero pages (an mmap there would SIGBUS).
//! If `mmap` fails (or on non-Unix hosts) the bytes are copied instead.

use std::fs::File;
use std::io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom};

use s3_mem::GuestMemory;

fn host_page() -> u64 {
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        // SAFETY: sysconf is always safe.
        let v = unsafe { libc::sysconf(libc::_SC_PAGESIZE) };
        if v > 0 {
            return v as u64;
        }
    }
    4096
}

/// Map `len` bytes of `file` starting at `offset` to guest `addr` (which must be 64 KiB aligned, inside a
/// region at least `align_up(len, 64 KiB)` long). Returns the number of bytes backed by the file.
pub fn map_file_into(mem: &mut GuestMemory, addr: u32, file: &File, offset: u64, len: u32) -> std::io::Result<u32> {
    let flen = file.metadata()?.len();
    let avail = flen.saturating_sub(offset).min(len as u64);
    if avail == 0 {
        return Ok(0);
    }
    let hp = host_page();
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        use std::os::unix::io::AsRawFd;
        if offset % hp == 0 && (mem.host_ptr(addr) as u64) % hp == 0 {
            let map_len = avail.div_ceil(hp) * hp;
            // SAFETY: the target range lies inside our own guest window reservation (MAP_FIXED replaces the
            // anonymous pages there); fd is a valid open file.
            let p = unsafe {
                libc::mmap(
                    mem.host_ptr(addr) as *mut libc::c_void,
                    map_len as usize,
                    libc::PROT_READ | libc::PROT_WRITE,
                    libc::MAP_PRIVATE | libc::MAP_FIXED,
                    file.as_raw_fd(),
                    offset as libc::off_t,
                )
            };
            if p != libc::MAP_FAILED {
                // Zero the tail of the last page beyond `len` is not needed: the guest only sees `len` + the
                // file's own bytes up to the page end (Windows views also expose the rest of the page).
                return Ok(avail as u32);
            }
        }
    }
    let _ = hp;
    let mut f = file.try_clone()?;
    f.seek(SeekFrom::Start(offset))?;
    let mut buf = vec![0u8; avail as usize];
    f.read_exact(&mut buf)?;
    mem.write_bytes(addr, &buf);
    Ok(avail as u32)
}

/// Undo [`map_file_into`]: put anonymous zero pages back over `[addr, addr+len)` (rounded up to host pages).
pub fn unmap_file(mem: &mut GuestMemory, addr: u32, len: u32) {
    if len == 0 {
        return;
    }
    let hp = host_page();
    let map_len = (len as u64).div_ceil(hp) * hp;
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        // SAFETY: range inside our guest window; replaces whatever is mapped there with fresh anonymous memory.
        let p = unsafe {
            libc::mmap(
                mem.host_ptr(addr) as *mut libc::c_void,
                map_len as usize,
                libc::PROT_READ | libc::PROT_WRITE,
                libc::MAP_PRIVATE | libc::MAP_ANONYMOUS | libc::MAP_NORESERVE | libc::MAP_FIXED,
                -1,
                0,
            )
        };
        if p != libc::MAP_FAILED {
            return;
        }
    }
    mem.fill(addr, map_len as usize, 0);
}
```

`port/crates/s3-runtime/src/mt.rs`:

```rs
//! Multi-core mode (perf-mt, `docs/porting/multicore.md`): the presenting guest thread (the game's draw thread)
//! runs its CPU on a second host thread, the "draw worker", truly in parallel with the cooperative scheduler on
//! the main host thread.
//!
//! Rules:
//! - Guest memory is shared (one mapping; the worker uses a non-owning [`GuestMemory::alias_view`]).
//! - Everything else in [`Machine`] (HLE state, handles, threads, host) is guarded by one **big lock**. The main
//!   host thread holds it all the time (also while the frontend runs between slices) and releases it only while
//!   it executes guest code of a top-level scheduled thread ([`Machine::run_cpu_unlocked`]) or idles
//!   ([`Machine::idle`]). The worker takes it for every CPU exit (thunk, hook, fault, budget) and releases it
//!   while its CPU runs.
//! - A CPU that runs without the lock is moved out of `Machine::threads` (swapped with a spare) so the other host
//!   thread never sees it; `Thread::offloaded` / `Thread::running_unlocked` make both schedulers skip it.
//! - Off by default: nothing here runs unless a frontend calls [`Machine::enable_mt`]. `s3det` never does, so the
//!   deterministic single-thread scheduler stays the reference.

use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicPtr, AtomicU32, AtomicU64, Ordering::SeqCst};
use std::sync::{Arc, Condvar, Mutex};
use std::thread::JoinHandle;
use std::time::Duration;

use s3_cpu::{Cpu, CpuExit};
use s3_mem::GuestMemory;

use crate::host::LogLevel;
use crate::machine::{Disp, Machine, StopReason, ThreadState};

/// Frames a non-main guest thread must present in a row before it is moved to the draw worker.
const OFFLOAD_AFTER_FRAMES: u32 = 30;
/// Instructions the worker runs per lock-free window (same as the scheduler quantum).
const WORKER_QUANTUM: u64 = crate::machine::DEFAULT_QUANTUM;
/// Yield-spin before a waiting host thread sleeps (µs), env `S3_MT_SPIN_US` (default 300).
static SPIN_US: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(300);
/// Delay before the main thread composes a frame queued by the draw worker (µs), env `S3_MT_PRESENT_DELAY_US`.
static PRESENT_DELAY_US: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(600);

/// The big HLE lock: a flag under a mutex (held across arbitrary code, so not a `MutexGuard`), with a
/// "worker wants it" hint so the main thread does not re-take it in a tight loop.
pub(crate) struct BigLock {
    held: Mutex<bool>,
    cv: Condvar,
    want: AtomicBool,
}

impl BigLock {
    fn new() -> Self {
        BigLock {
            held: Mutex::new(false),
            cv: Condvar::new(),
            want: AtomicBool::new(false),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn acquire(&self) {
        let mut g = self.held.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        while *g {
            g = self.cv.wait(g).unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        }
        *g = true;
    }

    /// Main thread: let a waiting worker go first.
    pub(crate) fn acquire_main(&self) {
        let mut spins = 0u32;
        while self.want.load(SeqCst) && spins < 10_000 {
            std::thread::yield_now();
            spins += 1;
        }
        self.acquire();
    }

    fn acquire_worker(&self) {
        self.want.store(true, SeqCst);
        self.acquire();
        self.want.store(false, SeqCst);
    }

    pub(crate) fn release(&self) {
        let mut g = self.held.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        *g = false;
        drop(g);
        self.cv.notify_one();
    }
}

/// "Something changed" notification between the two host threads (any HLE call may signal an object the other
/// side waits for). Waiters sleep until the epoch moves or the timeout passes (timers, timeouts).
pub(crate) struct Wake {
    epoch: AtomicU64,
    waiters: AtomicU32,
    m: Mutex<()>,
    cv: Condvar,
}

impl Wake {
    fn new() -> Self {
        Wake {
            epoch: AtomicU64::new(0),
            waiters: AtomicU32::new(0),
            m: Mutex::new(()),
            cv: Condvar::new(),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn epoch(&self) -> u64 {
        self.epoch.load(SeqCst)
    }

    pub(crate) fn bump(&self) {
        self.epoch.fetch_add(1, SeqCst);
        if self.waiters.load(SeqCst) > 0 {
            let _g = self.m.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
            self.cv.notify_all();
        }
    }

    /// Wait until the epoch differs from `seen` or `timeout` passed: first a short yield-spin (the other side
    /// usually answers within a fraction of a frame: snapshot handover), then a condvar wait that the other side's
    /// `bump` ends at once.
    pub(crate) fn wait(&self, seen: u64, timeout: Duration) {
        let start = std::time::Instant::now();
        let spin = Duration::from_micros(SPIN_US.load(SeqCst) as u64).min(timeout);
        while start.elapsed() < spin {
            if self.epoch() != seen {
                return;
            }
            std::thread::yield_now();
        }
        if cfg!(windows) {
            // Condvar timeouts on Windows follow the system tick (15.6 ms, measured: the draw thread's timed
            // waits took 15 ms instead of 1). `thread::sleep` uses a high-resolution timer: poll in 100 µs steps.
            while self.epoch() == seen && start.elapsed() < timeout {
                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_micros(100));
            }
            return;
        }
        self.waiters.fetch_add(1, SeqCst);
        let g = self.m.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        if self.epoch() == seen {
            let _ = self.cv.wait_timeout(
                g,
                timeout
                    .saturating_sub(start.elapsed())
                    .max(Duration::from_micros(100)),
            );
        }
        self.waiters.fetch_sub(1, SeqCst);
    }
}

/// State shared between the main host thread and the draw worker.
pub(crate) struct MtShared {
    pub(crate) lock: BigLock,
    pub(crate) wake: Wake,
    stop: AtomicBool,
    /// The machine (updated by the main thread under the lock if the `Machine` value moved).
    machine: AtomicPtr<Machine>,
    /// Host ns: [main waits for the lock, main idle, worker waits for the lock, worker waits for a change,
    /// worker holds the lock].
    pub(crate) prof: [AtomicU64; 6],
    /// Bumped by `set_hook_addrs` / `set_native_blocks`; the worker re-applies them to its CPU.
    pub(crate) ext_gen: AtomicU64,
}

/// `S3_MT_DEBUG=1`: log long waits of the worker.
static MT_DEBUG: std::sync::LazyLock<bool> =
    std::sync::LazyLock::new(|| std::env::var_os("S3_MT_DEBUG").is_some());

/// Host µs since the first call (debug timelines).
pub fn now_us() -> u64 {
    static T0: std::sync::OnceLock<std::time::Instant> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    T0.get_or_init(std::time::Instant::now)
        .elapsed()
        .as_micros() as u64
}

/// Run `f` and add its host time to `c`.
#[inline]
fn timed<R>(c: &AtomicU64, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R {
    let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
    let r = f();
    c.fetch_add(t0.elapsed().as_nanos() as u64, SeqCst);
    r
}

/// A CPU moved to the worker thread. `Cpu` holds raw pointers into its own decode cache, so it is not `Send`;
/// it is moved, never shared.
struct SendCpu(Cpu);
unsafe impl Send for SendCpu {}

/// Per-machine multi-core state ([`Machine::mt`]).
pub struct MtState {
    pub(crate) shared: Arc<MtShared>,
    worker: Option<JoinHandle<()>>,
    /// Guest thread id running on the worker.
    pub(crate) worker_tid: Option<u32>,
    /// Offload candidate: (tid, frames presented in a row).
    candidate: (u32, u32),
    /// Memory view used by the main thread's lock-free windows.
    pub(crate) main_view: GuestMemory,
    /// Spare CPU swapped into `threads[slot]` while the main thread runs a CPU without the lock.
    pub(crate) spare: Cpu,
    /// Total worker instructions / host ns in `Cpu::run` (also added to `Machine::stats`).
    pub worker_instructions: u64,
    /// Frame queued by the draw worker's present, composed and presented by the main thread.
    pending_frame: Option<crate::FrameBuffer>,
    /// When `pending_frame` was queued: the main thread composes it only after `PRESENT_DELAY_US`, when the
    /// draw thread is past its frame-start HLE calls and inside the long lock-free render stretch.
    pending_since: Option<std::time::Instant>,
    /// Spare frame buffers handed back to the worker's presents.
    frame_pool: Vec<crate::FrameBuffer>,
    /// Frames replaced in `pending_frame` before the main thread presented them.
    pub frames_dropped: u64,
    pub frames_presented: u64,
}

impl Machine {
    /// Turn on the multi-core mode (`S3_MT=1` in the frontends). Must be called on the thread that runs the
    /// machine, before or between slices. Not deterministic (host timing decides the interleaving); never used by
    /// `s3det`.
    pub fn enable_mt(&mut self) {
        if self.mt.is_some() {
            return;
        }
        if let Some(v) = std::env::var("S3_MT_SPIN_US")
            .ok()
            .and_then(|v| v.parse().ok())
        {
            SPIN_US.store(v, SeqCst);
        }
        if let Some(v) = std::env::var("S3_MT_PRESENT_DELAY_US")
            .ok()
            .and_then(|v| v.parse().ok())
        {
            PRESENT_DELAY_US.store(v, SeqCst);
        }
        let shared = Arc::new(MtShared {
            lock: BigLock::new(),
            wake: Wake::new(),
            stop: AtomicBool::new(false),
            machine: AtomicPtr::new(self as *mut Machine),
            prof: Default::default(),
            ext_gen: AtomicU64::new(0),
        });
        // The main thread holds the big lock from now on (see module docs).
        shared.lock.acquire();
        // SAFETY: the view lives in `self.mt`, dropped before `self.mem` (Machine::drop shuts MT down first).
        let main_view = unsafe { self.mem.alias_view() };
        self.mt = Some(Box::new(MtState {
            shared,
            worker: None,
            worker_tid: None,
            candidate: (0, 0),
            main_view,
            spare: Cpu::new(),
            worker_instructions: 0,
            pending_frame: None,
            pending_since: None,
            frame_pool: Vec::new(),
            frames_dropped: 0,
            frames_presented: 0,
        }));
        self.log(
            LogLevel::Info,
            "mt: multi-core mode on (draw thread on its own host thread once it presents)",
        );
    }

    /// Is a draw worker running?
    pub fn mt_active(&self) -> bool {
        self.mt.as_ref().is_some_and(|m| m.worker_tid.is_some())
    }

    /// Guest thread id currently on the draw worker.
    pub fn mt_worker_tid(&self) -> Option<u32> {
        self.mt.as_ref().and_then(|m| m.worker_tid)
    }

    /// Wait/lock statistics of the multi-core mode (empty when off).
    pub fn mt_report(&self) -> String {
        let Some(mt) = &self.mt else {
            return String::new();
        };
        let p: Vec<u64> = mt
            .shared
            .prof
            .iter()
            .map(|a| a.load(SeqCst) / 1_000_000)
            .collect();
        format!(
            "mt: worker {} M instr in {} ms Cpu::run; ms: main lock wait {}, main idle {}, worker lock wait {}, worker wait {}, worker lock held {}; frames presented by main {}, dropped {}\n",
            mt.worker_instructions / 1_000_000, p[5], p[0], p[1], p[2], p[3], p[4], mt.frames_presented, mt.frames_dropped
        )
    }

    /// Called on every present by the presenting guest thread.
    pub(crate) fn mt_note_present(&mut self) {
        let tid = self.current_tid();
        let slot = self.cur;
        let Some(mt) = self.mt.as_mut() else { return };
        if slot == 0 || mt.worker_tid == Some(tid) {
            return;
        }
        if mt.candidate.0 == tid {
            mt.candidate.1 += 1;
        } else {
            mt.candidate = (tid, 1);
        }
    }

    /// Draw worker (under the lock): queue a presented frame for the main thread and return a buffer for the
    /// next one. A frame the main thread has not taken yet is replaced (dropped), like a triple-buffered swap chain.
    pub(crate) fn mt_defer_present(&mut self, fb: crate::FrameBuffer) -> crate::FrameBuffer {
        let mt = self.mt.as_mut().unwrap();
        mt.pending_since = Some(std::time::Instant::now());
        let back = match mt.pending_frame.replace(fb) {
            Some(old) => {
                mt.frames_dropped += 1;
                old
            }
            None => mt.frame_pool.pop().unwrap_or_default(),
        };
        mt.shared.wake.bump();
        back
    }

    /// Main thread: compose and present a frame queued by the draw worker.
    pub(crate) fn mt_flush_present(&mut self) {
        let delay = Duration::from_micros(PRESENT_DELAY_US.load(SeqCst) as u64);
        let Some(mt) = self.mt.as_mut() else { return };
        if mt.pending_since.is_none_or(|t| t.elapsed() < delay) {
            return;
        }
        mt.pending_since = None;
        let Some(fb) = mt.pending_frame.take() else {
            return;
        };
        let back = self.present_owned_now(fb);
        let mt = self.mt.as_mut().unwrap();
        mt.frames_presented += 1;
        if mt.frame_pool.len() < 2 {
            mt.frame_pool.push(back);
        }
    }

    /// Main thread, under the lock, at the start of every `run_slice`: keep the machine pointer current, reap a
    /// finished worker, start one for the presenting thread, present a queued frame.
    pub(crate) fn mt_maintain(&mut self) {
        let me = self as *mut Machine;
        self.mt_flush_present();
        let Some(mt) = self.mt.as_mut() else { return };
        mt.shared.machine.store(me, SeqCst);
        if mt.worker_tid.is_none() {
            if let Some(h) = mt.worker.take() {
                let _ = h.join();
            }
        }
        if mt.worker_tid.is_some() || mt.candidate.1 < OFFLOAD_AFTER_FRAMES {
            return;
        }
        let tid = mt.candidate.0;
        mt.candidate = (0, 0);
        let Some(slot) = self.thread_by_tid(tid) else {
            return;
        };
        let t = &self.threads[slot];
        if t.nested > 0 || matches!(t.state, ThreadState::Exited(_)) || t.offloaded {
            return;
        }
        self.mt_offload(slot);
    }

    fn mt_offload(&mut self, slot: usize) {
        let tid = self.threads[slot].tid;
        let mut cpu = Cpu::new();
        std::mem::swap(&mut cpu, &mut self.threads[slot].cpu);
        // The placeholder shows the real counters until the next sync.
        self.threads[slot].cpu.instructions = cpu.instructions;
        self.threads[slot].cpu.eip = cpu.eip;
        self.threads[slot].offloaded = true;
        // SAFETY: the view is dropped by the worker before Machine::drop releases the mapping (it joins).
        let view = unsafe { self.mem.alias_view() };
        let mt = self.mt.as_mut().unwrap();
        let shared = mt.shared.clone();
        let gen = mt.shared.ext_gen.load(SeqCst);
        let cpu = SendCpu(cpu);
        let view = SendView(view);
        mt.worker_tid = Some(tid);
        let h = std::thread::Builder::new()
            .name("s3-draw".into())
            .spawn(move || worker_main(shared, tid, cpu, view, gen))
            .expect("spawn draw worker");
        self.mt.as_mut().unwrap().worker = Some(h);
        self.log(
            LogLevel::Info,
            &format!("mt: guest thread {slot} (tid {tid:#x}) now runs on its own host thread"),
        );
    }

    /// Main thread: run `cpu` (moved out of the machine) for `budget` instructions with the big lock released.
    /// Out of line and given the machine pointer, so the compiler cannot keep `Machine` fields in registers across
    /// the window in which the worker may change them.
    #[inline(never)]
    pub(crate) fn run_cpu_unlocked(&mut self, slot: usize, budget: u64) -> CpuExit {
        let me: *mut Machine = self;
        // SAFETY: see module docs; `mt` is boxed (stable address) and only replaced on this thread.
        unsafe { run_window(me, slot, budget) }
    }

    /// Idle for up to `ms` (all threads blocked). With a draw worker the big lock is released meanwhile and the
    /// wait ends early when the worker changes something.
    pub fn idle(&mut self, ms: u32) {
        if !self.mt_active() {
            self.host.idle(ms);
            return;
        }
        let shared = self.mt.as_ref().unwrap().shared.clone();
        let seen = shared.wake.epoch();
        let me: *mut Machine = self;
        // SAFETY: as in run_cpu_unlocked.
        unsafe { idle_window(me, &shared, seen, ms) }
    }

    /// Tell the other host thread that HLE state may have changed (cheap when nobody waits).
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn mt_bump(&self) {
        if let Some(mt) = &self.mt {
            mt.shared.wake.bump();
        }
    }

    /// Stop and join the worker (Machine::drop). The worker's CPU is not handed back.
    pub(crate) fn mt_shutdown(&mut self) {
        let Some(mt) = self.mt.as_mut() else { return };
        mt.shared.stop.store(true, SeqCst);
        if let Some(h) = mt.worker.take() {
            mt.shared.lock.release();
            mt.shared.wake.bump();
            let _ = h.join();
        }
        self.mt = None;
    }
}

struct SendView(GuestMemory);
unsafe impl Send for SendView {}

#[inline(never)]
unsafe fn run_window(me: *mut Machine, slot: usize, budget: u64) -> CpuExit {
    let m = &mut *me;
    let mt: *mut MtState = &mut **m.mt.as_mut().unwrap();
    let shared = (*mt).shared.clone();
    let mut cpu = std::mem::replace(&mut (*mt).spare, Cpu::new());
    std::mem::swap(&mut cpu, &mut m.threads[slot].cpu);
    m.threads[slot].running_unlocked = true;
    let view: *mut GuestMemory = &mut (*mt).main_view;
    shared.lock.release();
    let exit = cpu.run(&mut *view, budget);
    timed(&shared.prof[0], || shared.lock.acquire_main());
    let m = &mut *me;
    std::mem::swap(&mut cpu, &mut m.threads[slot].cpu);
    m.threads[slot].running_unlocked = false;
    (*mt).spare = cpu;
    exit
}

#[inline(never)]
unsafe fn idle_window(_me: *mut Machine, shared: &MtShared, seen: u64, ms: u32) {
    shared.lock.release();
    timed(&shared.prof[1], || {
        shared
            .wake
            .wait(seen, Duration::from_millis(ms.max(1) as u64))
    });
    timed(&shared.prof[0], || shared.lock.acquire_main());
}

/// What the worker does after handling one CPU exit.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Step {
    /// Run the CPU again.
    Run,
    /// Blocked in a thunk (or the machine stopped): wait for a change, then run (re-dispatches the thunk).
    Wait,
    /// Suspended: wait, then check again without running.
    Suspended,
    /// The thread exited; the real CPU is back in the machine.
    Done,
}

fn worker_main(shared: Arc<MtShared>, tid: u32, cpu: SendCpu, view: SendView, mut gen: u64) {
    let mut cpu = cpu.0;
    let mut view = view.0;
    // The thread may be blocked in a thunk right now: running it re-dispatches that thunk at once.
    let mut step = Step::Run;
    let mut seen = shared.wake.epoch();
    let mut before = cpu.instructions;
    let mut ns = 0u64;
    let mut free_budgets = 0u32;
    loop {
        if matches!(step, Step::Wait | Step::Suspended) {
            let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
            timed(&shared.prof[3], || {
                shared.wake.wait(seen, Duration::from_millis(1))
            });
            if *MT_DEBUG {
                let us = t0.elapsed().as_micros();
                if us > 1500 {
                    eprintln!(
                        "mt: worker waited {us} us at {:#x} (epoch moved: {})",
                        cpu.eip,
                        shared.wake.epoch() != seen
                    );
                }
            }
        }
        if shared.stop.load(SeqCst) {
            return;
        }
        let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
        let exit = if step == Step::Suspended {
            CpuExit::Budget
        } else {
            cpu.run(&mut view, WORKER_QUANTUM)
        };
        let dt = t0.elapsed().as_nanos() as u64;
        ns += dt;
        shared.prof[5].fetch_add(dt, SeqCst);
        // A budget exit needs no HLE state: keep running without the lock (checking suspension, hooks and the
        // counters under the lock every 16th time).
        if matches!(exit, CpuExit::Budget)
            && step == Step::Run
            && free_budgets < 15
            && shared.ext_gen.load(SeqCst) == gen
        {
            free_budgets += 1;
            continue;
        }
        free_budgets = 0;
        timed(&shared.prof[2], || shared.lock.acquire_worker());
        let held = std::time::Instant::now();
        if shared.stop.load(SeqCst) {
            shared.lock.release();
            return;
        }
        // SAFETY: under the big lock (module docs); the main thread keeps the pointer current.
        let m = unsafe { &mut *shared.machine.load(SeqCst) };
        step = worker_step(m, tid, &mut cpu, exit, before, ns, &mut gen);
        before = cpu.instructions;
        ns = 0;
        if step == Step::Done {
            if let Some(mt) = m.mt.as_mut() {
                mt.worker_tid = None;
            }
        }
        seen = shared.wake.epoch();
        if step != Step::Wait && step != Step::Suspended {
            shared.wake.bump();
        }
        shared.prof[4].fetch_add(held.elapsed().as_nanos() as u64, SeqCst);
        shared.lock.release();
        if step == Step::Done {
            return;
        }
    }
}

/// Handle one CPU exit of the offloaded thread under the big lock. `cpu` is the real CPU; for the dispatch it is
/// swapped with the placeholder in `m.threads[slot]` and back.
fn worker_step(
    m: &mut Machine,
    tid: u32,
    cpu: &mut Cpu,
    exit: CpuExit,
    before: u64,
    ns: u64,
    gen: &mut u64,
) -> Step {
    let ran = cpu.instructions - before;
    m.stats.instructions += ran;
    m.stats.cpu_ns += ns;
    if let Some(mt) = m.mt.as_mut() {
        mt.worker_instructions += ran;
        let g = mt.shared.ext_gen.load(SeqCst);
        if g != *gen {
            *gen = g;
            cpu.set_hooks(m.ext.hook_addrs.clone());
            cpu.set_native_blocks(m.ext.native_blocks.clone());
        }
    }
    let Some(slot) = m.thread_by_tid(tid) else {
        return Step::Done;
    };
    m.threads[slot].cpu_ns += ns;
    match m.threads[slot].state {
        ThreadState::Exited(_) => {
            std::mem::swap(cpu, &mut m.threads[slot].cpu);
            m.threads[slot].offloaded = false;
            return Step::Done;
        }
        ThreadState::Suspended(_) if matches!(exit, CpuExit::Budget) => {
            sync_placeholder(m, slot, cpu);
            return Step::Suspended;
        }
        _ => {}
    }
    if m.is_stopped() {
        return Step::Wait;
    }
    std::mem::swap(cpu, &mut m.threads[slot].cpu); // machine: real CPU, `cpu`: placeholder
    let saved_cur = m.cur;
    m.cur = slot;
    let step = match exit {
        CpuExit::Budget => Step::Run,
        CpuExit::Thunk(a) => match m.dispatch_thunk(a) {
            Disp::Continue => Step::Run,
            Disp::Blocked | Disp::Stop => Step::Wait,
            Disp::ThreadExited => Step::Done,
        },
        CpuExit::Hook(a) => {
            m.dispatch_hook(a);
            Step::Run
        }
        CpuExit::ReturnMagic => {
            m.stop(StopReason::Error(format!(
                "thread {slot}: return to magic address outside call_guest"
            )));
            Step::Wait
        }
        other => {
            if crate::seh::handle_cpu_exit(m, other) {
                Step::Run
            } else {
                Step::Wait
            }
        }
    };
    m.cur = saved_cur;
    // The thread table may have grown during the dispatch (CreateThread); look the slot up again.
    let slot = m.thread_by_tid(tid).unwrap_or(slot);
    if step == Step::Done || matches!(m.threads[slot].state, ThreadState::Exited(_)) {
        // The real CPU stays in the machine.
        m.threads[slot].offloaded = false;
        return Step::Done;
    }
    std::mem::swap(cpu, &mut m.threads[slot].cpu); // back: `cpu` real, machine placeholder
    sync_placeholder(m, slot, cpu);
    step
}

/// Mirror the counters of the real CPU into the placeholder (S3_SAMPLE, summaries).
fn sync_placeholder(m: &mut Machine, slot: usize, cpu: &Cpu) {
    let ph = &mut m.threads[slot].cpu;
    ph.instructions = cpu.instructions;
    ph.eip = cpu.eip;
    ph.regs = cpu.regs;
}
```

`port/crates/s3-runtime/src/process.rs`:

```rs
//! PEB, process parameters, command line and environment block.

use s3_mem::layout;
use s3_mem::RegionKind;

use crate::vfs::GUEST_GAME_DIR;
use crate::Machine;

/// PEB field offsets (x86).
pub mod peb {
    pub const BEING_DEBUGGED: u32 = 0x02;
    pub const IMAGE_BASE: u32 = 0x08;
    pub const LDR: u32 = 0x0C;
    pub const PROCESS_PARAMETERS: u32 = 0x10;
    pub const PROCESS_HEAP: u32 = 0x18;
    pub const NUMBER_OF_PROCESSORS: u32 = 0x64;
    pub const OS_MAJOR: u32 = 0xA4;
    pub const OS_MINOR: u32 = 0xA8;
    pub const OS_BUILD: u32 = 0xAC;
    pub const OS_PLATFORM_ID: u32 = 0xB0;
}

/// Default environment variables the guest sees.
pub const DEFAULT_ENV: &[&str] = &["PATH=C:\\WINDOWS;C:\\WINDOWS\\SYSTEM;C:\\S3", "TEMP=C:\\TEMP", "TMP=C:\\TEMP", "windir=C:\\WINDOWS"];

pub(crate) fn setup_process(m: &mut Machine, image_base: u32, image_size: u32, entry: u32, stack_reserve: u32, exe_name: &str) {
    let peb_addr = layout::PEB_ADDR;
    let params = m
        .mem
        .alloc_region(None, 0x1_0000, RegionKind::Private, (layout::LOW_ARENA_START, layout::LOW_ARENA_END))
        .expect("low arena");
    m.mem.fill(peb_addr, 0x1000, 0);
    m.mem.write_u32(peb_addr + peb::IMAGE_BASE, image_base);
    m.mem.write_u32(peb_addr + peb::PROCESS_PARAMETERS, params);
    let heap = m.mem.process_heap();
    m.mem.write_u32(peb_addr + peb::PROCESS_HEAP, heap);
    m.mem.write_u32(peb_addr + peb::NUMBER_OF_PROCESSORS, 1);
    // Windows 98-like answers are chosen by kernel32!GetVersion*; the PEB says NT 5.1 (XP), build 2600.
    m.mem.write_u32(peb_addr + peb::OS_MAJOR, 5);
    m.mem.write_u32(peb_addr + peb::OS_MINOR, 1);
    m.mem.write_u16(peb_addr + peb::OS_BUILD, 2600);
    m.mem.write_u32(peb_addr + peb::OS_PLATFORM_ID, 2);

    let module_path = format!("{GUEST_GAME_DIR}\\{exe_name}");
    // Contract: the command line is just the exe name (kernel32 may append user arguments later).
    // Debug: `S3_EXE_ARGS` appends guest arguments (e.g. `-netmon`, the game's network trace switch).
    let cmdline = match std::env::var("S3_EXE_ARGS") {
        Ok(a) if !a.trim().is_empty() => format!("{exe_name} {}", a.trim()),
        _ => exe_name.to_string(),
    };
    // Layout inside the params block: 0x000 RTL_USER_PROCESS_PARAMETERS (0x2A0), strings from 0x400.
    let mut p = params + 0x400;
    let cmdline_a = p;
    p += m.mem.write_cstr(cmdline_a, &cmdline) as u32;
    p = (p + 3) & !3;
    let cmdline_w = p;
    p += 2 * m.mem.write_wstr(cmdline_w, &cmdline) as u32;
    p = (p + 3) & !3;
    let path_w = p;
    p += 2 * m.mem.write_wstr(path_w, &module_path) as u32;
    p = (p + 15) & !15;
    let env_a = p;
    for v in DEFAULT_ENV {
        p += m.mem.write_cstr(p, v) as u32;
    }
    m.mem.write_u8(p, 0);
    p += 1;
    p = (p + 15) & !15;
    let env_w = p;
    for v in DEFAULT_ENV {
        p += 2 * m.mem.write_wstr(p, v) as u32;
    }
    m.mem.write_u16(p, 0);

    // RTL_USER_PROCESS_PARAMETERS: ImagePathName UNICODE_STRING at 0x38, CommandLine at 0x40, Environment 0x48.
    let ustr = |m: &mut Machine, at: u32, s: &str, buf: u32| {
        let len = s.encode_utf16().count() as u32 * 2;
        m.mem.write_u16(at, len as u16);
        m.mem.write_u16(at + 2, (len + 2) as u16);
        m.mem.write_u32(at + 4, buf);
    };
    m.mem.write_u32(params, 0x2A0);
    m.mem.write_u32(params + 4, 0x2A0);
    m.mem.write_u32(params + 8, 1); // normalized
    ustr(m, params + 0x38, &module_path, path_w);
    ustr(m, params + 0x40, &cmdline, cmdline_w);
    m.mem.write_u32(params + 0x48, env_w);

    m.process = crate::ProcessInfo {
        image_base,
        image_size,
        entry,
        peb: peb_addr,
        params,
        cmdline_a,
        cmdline_w,
        module_path,
        env_a,
        env_w,
        stack_reserve,
    };
}
```
