`port/scripts/build-apk.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the Settlers 3 Port APK without Gradle.
#   cargo ndk (libs3android.so for arm64-v8a + x86_64) -> aapt2 link (manifest + res) -> javac + d8
#   (android/java -> classes.dex: the background-play service) -> add stripped libs (stored, 16 KiB page aligned)
#   -> zipalign -> apksigner (debug keystore in port/target, generated once).
# The APK never contains game files.
#
# Usage: scripts/build-apk.sh [--abi arm64-v8a|x86_64|all] [--debug] [--shell] [--game-icon]
#   --shell: build without the engine feature (status screen/input/audio only; for when other crates are broken)
#   --game-icon: PERSONAL builds only: launcher icon from your own S3.EXE (game artwork, never publish such an APK).
#                Default: our own adaptive icon (res/drawable/ic_launcher*.xml).
# Output: port/target/apk/settlers3port.apk
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
set -euo pipefail

PORT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
# Linux/WSL: ~/Android/Sdk. Windows (Git Bash): %LOCALAPPDATA%\Android\Sdk, tools have .exe/.bat suffixes.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) DEF_SDK="$(cygpath -u "$LOCALAPPDATA")/Android/Sdk"; EXE=.exe; BAT=.bat; HOSTTAG=windows-x86_64; DEF_PY=python ;;
  *) DEF_SDK="$HOME/Android/Sdk"; EXE=; BAT=; HOSTTAG=linux-x86_64; DEF_PY=python3 ;;
esac
SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-$DEF_SDK}"
BT="$SDK/build-tools/36.0.0"
PY="${PYTHON:-$DEF_PY}"
# --game-icon: the user's own S3.EXE icon becomes the launcher icon (extracted at build time, never committed).
GAME_EXE="${S3_ICON_EXE:-$PORT/../game-files/gog-s3-ultimate/S3.EXE}"
PLATFORM_JAR="$SDK/platforms/android-35/android.jar"
export ANDROID_NDK_HOME="${ANDROID_NDK_HOME:-$SDK/ndk/27.2.12479018}"
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$PORT/target"
export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
STRIP="$ANDROID_NDK_HOME/toolchains/llvm/prebuilt/$HOSTTAG/bin/llvm-strip$EXE"
JOBS="${JOBS:-4}"

ABIS=(arm64-v8a x86_64)
PROFILE=release
FEATURES=()
GAME_ICON=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --abi) shift; if [ "$1" = all ]; then ABIS=(arm64-v8a x86_64); else ABIS=("$1"); fi ;;
    --debug) PROFILE=debug ;;
    --shell) FEATURES=(--no-default-features) ;;
    --game-icon) GAME_ICON=1 ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,13p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "unknown argument: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  shift
done

avail_kb=$(df -Pk "$PORT" | awk 'NR==2 {print $4}')
if [ "$avail_kb" -lt $((2 * 1024 * 1024)) ]; then
  echo "error: less than 2 GB free on $(df -P "$PORT" | awk 'NR==2 {print $6}'); refusing to build" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# 1. Native libraries.
targs=()
for a in "${ABIS[@]}"; do targs+=(-t "$a"); done
cargo_flags=(-p s3-android -j "$JOBS" ${FEATURES[@]+"${FEATURES[@]}"})
[ "$PROFILE" = release ] && cargo_flags+=(--release)
echo "== cargo ndk ${ABIS[*]} ($PROFILE)"
(cd "$PORT" && cargo ndk "${targs[@]}" --platform 26 build "${cargo_flags[@]}")

# 2. Resources + manifest.
OUT="$PORT/target/apk"
STAGE="$OUT/stage"
rm -rf "$STAGE"
mkdir -p "$STAGE"
echo "== aapt2"
"$BT/aapt2$EXE" compile --dir "$PORT/android/res" -o "$OUT/res.zip"
ICON_FLAGS=()
if [ "$GAME_ICON" = 1 ]; then
  [ -f "$GAME_EXE" ] || { echo "error: --game-icon: no $GAME_EXE (set S3_ICON_EXE)" >&2; exit 1; }
  echo "   --game-icon: game artwork in the APK, personal use only, do not publish"
  # Game icon as drawable-*dpi PNGs; density-specific PNGs win over the adaptive drawable/ic_launcher.xml.
  rm -rf "$OUT/icon-res"
  "$PY" -I "$PORT/../tools/s3_icon.py" "$GAME_EXE" "$OUT/icon-res"
  "$BT/aapt2$EXE" compile --dir "$OUT/icon-res" -o "$OUT/icon-res.zip"
  ICON_FLAGS=(-R "$OUT/icon-res.zip")
fi
"$BT/aapt2$EXE" link -o "$OUT/unsigned.apk" -I "$PLATFORM_JAR" \
  --manifest "$PORT/android/AndroidManifest.xml" \
  --min-sdk-version 26 --target-sdk-version 35 \
  "$OUT/res.zip" ${ICON_FLAGS[@]+"${ICON_FLAGS[@]}"}

# 3. Java (GameService, docs/porting/android.md "Background play"): javac against android.jar, d8 -> classes.dex.
echo "== javac + d8"
rm -rf "$OUT/classes"
mkdir -p "$OUT/classes"
mapfile -t JAVA_SRC < <(find "$PORT/android/java" -name '*.java')
javac -nowarn -Xlint:-options --release 11 -classpath "$PLATFORM_JAR" -d "$OUT/classes" "${JAVA_SRC[@]}"
mapfile -t CLASS_FILES < <(find "$OUT/classes" -name '*.class')
"$BT/d8$BAT" --release --min-api 26 --lib "$PLATFORM_JAR" --output "$STAGE" "${CLASS_FILES[@]}"

# 4. Native libs: stripped copies, stored uncompressed (extractNativeLibs=false).
for a in "${ABIS[@]}"; do
  case "$a" in
    arm64-v8a) triple=aarch64-linux-android ;;
    x86_64) triple=x86_64-linux-android ;;
    *) echo "unsupported ABI $a" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  so="$PORT/target/$triple/$PROFILE/libs3android.so"
  mkdir -p "$STAGE/lib/$a"
  "$STRIP" --strip-debug -o "$STAGE/lib/$a/libs3android.so" "$so"
  echo "   lib/$a/libs3android.so $(du -h "$STAGE/lib/$a/libs3android.so" | cut -f1)"
done
# Stored (no compression) so the libs can be mmapped from the APK; python zipfile instead of zip (not on Windows).
(cd "$STAGE" && "$PY" -I -c '
import os, sys, zipfile
with zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1], "a", zipfile.ZIP_STORED) as z:
    for root, _, files in os.walk("lib"):
        for f in files:
            p = os.path.join(root, f)
            z.write(p, p.replace(os.sep, "/"))
    z.write("classes.dex", "classes.dex", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED)
' "$OUT/unsigned.apk")

# 5. Align + sign.
"$BT/zipalign$EXE" -f -P 16 4 "$OUT/unsigned.apk" "$OUT/aligned.apk"
KS="$PORT/target/debug.keystore"
if [ ! -f "$KS" ]; then
  echo "== generating debug keystore $KS"
  keytool -genkeypair -keystore "$KS" -storepass android -keypass android -alias androiddebugkey \
    -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000 -dname "CN=Settlers3Port Debug,O=Debug,C=US" >/dev/null 2>&1
fi
"$BT/apksigner$BAT" sign --ks "$KS" --ks-pass pass:android --key-pass pass:android \
  --out "$OUT/settlers3port.apk" "$OUT/aligned.apk"
rm -rf "$OUT/classes"
rm -f "$OUT/unsigned.apk" "$OUT/aligned.apk" "$OUT/res.zip" "$OUT/icon-res.zip" "$OUT/settlers3port.apk.idsig"
"$BT/apksigner$BAT" verify "$OUT/settlers3port.apk"
echo "== built $OUT/settlers3port.apk ($(du -h "$OUT/settlers3port.apk" | cut -f1))"

```

`port/scripts/build-ios.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build (and optionally install) the iOS app without a Mac (docs/porting/ios.md).
#   1. Rust core: cargo build --target aarch64-apple-ios -p s3-ios (static library; archiving needs no Apple linker,
#      so this runs on Windows or Linux).
#   2. Swift shell port/ios: xtool (WSL Ubuntu on Windows, or Linux) builds, signs and packages it with the iOS SDK it
#      made from Xcode.xip (`xtool setup`, once).
# The app never contains game files.
#
# Usage: scripts/build-ios.sh [--debug] [--rust-only] [--install]
#   --rust-only: only step 1 (check the core builds for iOS)
#   --install:   `xtool dev run` (build + install on the USB-connected iPhone) instead of `xtool dev build`
# Output: port/ios/xtool/S3Mobile.app (and .ipa with `xtool dev build --ipa`)
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
set -euo pipefail

PORT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
PROFILE=release
RUST_ONLY=0
XTOOL_CMD="build"
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    --debug) PROFILE=debug ;;
    --rust-only) RUST_ONLY=1 ;;
    --install) XTOOL_CMD="run" ;;
    *) echo "unknown option $a" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

export CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$PORT/target"
export IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=17.0
# No debug info in the archive (it is ~85 MB with it); the app links only what it uses.
export CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG=0
flags=(-p s3-ios --target aarch64-apple-ios)
[ "$PROFILE" = release ] && flags+=(--release)
echo "== cargo build ${flags[*]}"
(cd "$PORT" && cargo build "${flags[@]}")
LIB="$PORT/target/aarch64-apple-ios/$PROFILE/libs3ios.a"
if [ "$PROFILE" = debug ]; then
  # Package.swift links from target/aarch64-apple-ios/release.
  mkdir -p "$PORT/target/aarch64-apple-ios/release"
  cp "$LIB" "$PORT/target/aarch64-apple-ios/release/libs3ios.a"
fi
ls -la "$PORT/target/aarch64-apple-ios/release/libs3ios.a"
[ "$RUST_ONLY" = 1 ] && exit 0

echo "== xtool dev $XTOOL_CMD (port/ios)"
case "$(uname -s)" in
  MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*)
    # Windows: xtool runs in WSL Ubuntu (swiftly + ~/.local/bin/xtool), on the same files via /mnt/c.
    WPATH="$(wsl -d Ubuntu -- wslpath -a "$(cygpath -m "$PORT/ios")" | tr -d '\r')"
    # No $VARS inside: wsl.exe expands them itself (Windows PATH with "(x86)" broke the command).
    wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc ". ~/.local/share/swiftly/env.sh; cd '$WPATH' && ~/.local/bin/xtool dev $XTOOL_CMD"
    ;;
  *)
    (cd "$PORT/ios" && xtool dev "$XTOOL_CMD")
    ;;
esac
```

`port/scripts/mp-local-test.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Two headless s3run instances + a local s3-relay: host creates a LAN/relay game, the second instance joins,
# both start the same map. See docs/porting/multiplayer.md ("Local two-instance test").
#
# usage: port/scripts/mp-local-test.sh [OUT_DIR] [SECONDS]
#   env: S3RUN (default port/target/release/s3run), RELAY (port/target/release/s3-relay), PORT (7787),
#        GAME_DIR, HOST_EXTRA / JOIN_EXTRA (extra inject items, ';'-separated, times in ms), HASH_EVERY (ticks),
#        MAP=artokia (default: multi-player map "384-2-Artokia", loads in a few seconds) | random (random 384 map;
#        its start-position search can take 30-100 s, during which both peers show "Initiating player2player
#        communication" and wait for each other),
#        HOST_MT / JOIN_MT=1 (run that peer in the multi-core mode, docs/porting/multicore.md),
#        LAN=1 (no s3-relay: embedded relays + UDP LAN discovery, the out-of-the-box path),
#        PYTHON (default python3)
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
OUT="${1:-$ROOT/scratch/mp-test}"
SECS="${2:-60}"
S3RUN="${S3RUN:-$ROOT/port/target/release/s3run}"
RELAY="${RELAY:-$ROOT/port/target/release/s3-relay}"
PORT="${PORT:-7787}"
GAME_DIR="${GAME_DIR:-$ROOT/game-files/gog-s3-ultimate}"
HASH_EVERY="${HASH_EVERY:-1}"
MAP="${MAP:-artokia}"
mkdir -p "$OUT"
rm -rf "$OUT/host-data" "$OUT/join-data"
if [ -n "${LAN:-}" ]; then
  # LAN mode: no external relay; each instance runs its embedded relay and finds the host by UDP discovery.
  unset S3_RELAY_URL
else
  "$RELAY" --listen "127.0.0.1:$PORT" -v >"$OUT/relay.log" 2>&1 &
  RELAY_PID=$!
  trap 'kill $RELAY_PID 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
  sleep 0.5
  export S3_RELAY_URL="ws://127.0.0.1:$PORT/"
fi

# Menu coordinates (800x600): main menu "Multi-player Game: LAN" 165,275; LAN screen: network list entry 200,131,
# "Search for games" 175,240, first open game 200,330, "Join Game" 610,567, "New Game" 730,567;
# map picker: tab "Multi-player Map" 181,180, first map "384-2-Artokia" 165,255, OK 630,467; game setup OK 730,567; waiting room: ready buttons (right of the chat line) 723,114 (host
# row) / 723,134 (joiner row), OK (start) 730,567.
if [ "$MAP" = random ]; then PICK="9500:click 630 467"; else PICK="9000:click 181 180;10000:click 165 255;11000:click 630 467"; fi
HOST="1500:click 165 275;5000:click 200 131;6500:click 730 567;$PICK;12500:click 730 567;16000:shot $OUT/host-wait.png"
JOIN="1500:click 165 275;5000:click 200 131;17000:click 175 240;19000:shot $OUT/join-list.png;19500:click 200 330;20500:click 610 567;24000:shot $OUT/join-wait.png"
HOST="$HOST;26500:click 723 114;28000:shot $OUT/host-ready.png;29000:click 730 567;${HOST_EXTRA:-}"
JOIN="$JOIN;25000:click 723 134;${JOIN_EXTRA:-}"
for t in $(seq 40 20 "$SECS"); do
  HOST="$HOST;$((t*1000)):shot $OUT/host-$t.png"
  JOIN="$JOIN;$((t*1000)):shot $OUT/join-$t.png"
done

S3_MT="${HOST_MT:-}" S3_NET_NAME=host "$S3RUN" --headless --game-dir "$GAME_DIR" --data-dir "$OUT/host-data" --max-seconds "$SECS" \
  --mp-hash "$OUT/host.hash" --mp-hash-every "$HASH_EVERY" --inject "$HOST" >"$OUT/host.log" 2>&1 &
H=$!
S3_MT="${JOIN_MT:-}" S3_NET_NAME=join "$S3RUN" --headless --game-dir "$GAME_DIR" --data-dir "$OUT/join-data" --max-seconds "$SECS" \
  --mp-hash "$OUT/join.hash" --mp-hash-every "$HASH_EVERY" --inject "$JOIN" >"$OUT/join.log" 2>&1 &
J=$!
wait $H $J || true
grep -h "dplay:" "$OUT/host.log" | sed 's/^/host: /' | head -40 || true
grep -h "dplay:" "$OUT/join.log" | sed 's/^/join: /' | head -40 || true
if [ -s "$OUT/host.hash" ] && [ -s "$OUT/join.hash" ]; then
  "${PYTHON:-python3}" -I "$ROOT/tools/mp_hash_compare.py" "$OUT/host.hash" "$OUT/join.hash"
else
  echo "no hash files (game did not start?)"
  exit 1
fi
```

`port/scripts/run-emulator.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the Settlers 3 Port on OUR emulator (AVD s3_api35, console port 5610 -> adb serial emulator-5610).
# Never touches other AVDs/emulators (e.g. emulator-5600 belongs to another project).
#
# Usage: scripts/run-emulator.sh [command...]     (default: start install launch)
#   create-avd        create AVD s3_api35 (pixel_6, API 35 google_apis x86_64, 3 GB RAM, 6 GB data) if missing
#   start             boot the AVD headless on port 5610 if not running, wait for boot
#   install           install port/target/apk/settlers3port.apk (build it with scripts/build-apk.sh)
#   push [--minimal]  copy the user's game files to /sdcard/Android/data/com.settlers3port.app/files/game
#                     (GAME_DIR env, default ../game-files/gog-s3-ultimate). Only what the game reads; never Save/.
#                     --minimal skips S3QOTA, S3MCD, Map/MULTI and Map/User (~600 MB instead of ~1.2 GB).
#   launch            (re)start the app
#   stop              force-stop the app (the emulator keeps running)
#   logcat [secs]     print the app's log (tag s3port, last run) for up to secs seconds (default: dump and exit)
#   shot [name]       screenshot to scratch/android-shots/<name>.png
#   tap X Y           tap at screen coordinates (adb input)
#   status            show device, app pid, game dir contents
#   kill-emulator     shut the AVD down (only ours)
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
set -euo pipefail

PORT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
ROOT="$(cd "$PORT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-$HOME/Android/Sdk}"
AVD=s3_api35
CONSOLE_PORT=5610
SERIAL="${ADB_SERIAL:-emulator-$CONSOLE_PORT}"   # ADB_SERIAL=<ip:port> targets a real phone
PKG=com.settlers3port.app
APK="$PORT_DIR/target/apk/settlers3port.apk"
GAME_DIR="${GAME_DIR:-$ROOT/game-files/gog-s3-ultimate}"
DEV_GAME="/sdcard/Android/data/$PKG/files/game"
SHOTS="$ROOT/scratch/android-shots"
ADB="adb -s $SERIAL"

running() { adb devices | grep -q "^$SERIAL[[:space:]]*device"; }

create_avd() {
  if "$SDK/emulator/emulator" -list-avds | grep -qx "$AVD"; then
    echo "AVD $AVD exists"
  else
    echo "== creating AVD $AVD"
    echo no | "$SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/avdmanager" create avd -n "$AVD" \
      -k "system-images;android-35;google_apis;x86_64" -d pixel_6
  fi
  local cfg="$HOME/.android/avd/$AVD.avd/config.ini"
  # Our resource limits: 3 GB RAM, 6 GB data partition, 4 cores, no camera.
  for kv in "hw.ramSize=3072" "disk.dataPartition.size=6G" "hw.cpu.ncore=4" "hw.camera.back=none" \
            "hw.camera.front=none" "hw.keyboard=yes" "hw.gpu.enabled=yes" "hw.gpu.mode=swiftshader_indirect"; do
    local k="${kv%%=*}"
    if grep -q "^$k" "$cfg"; then sed -i "s|^$k.*|$kv|" "$cfg"; else echo "$kv" >>"$cfg"; fi
  done
}

start() {
  if running; then echo "$SERIAL already running"; return; fi
  create_avd
  local avail_kb; avail_kb=$(df -Pk "$HOME" | awk 'NR==2 {print $4}')
  if [ "$avail_kb" -lt $((3 * 1024 * 1024)) ]; then echo "error: < 3 GB free disk, not starting emulator" >&2; exit 1; fi
  echo "== starting $AVD on port $CONSOLE_PORT (headless)"
  local audio=(-no-audio)
  [ "${S3_EMU_AUDIO:-0}" = 1 ] && audio=()
  mkdir -p "$ROOT/scratch"
  nohup "$SDK/emulator/emulator" -avd "$AVD" -port "$CONSOLE_PORT" -no-window -gpu swiftshader_indirect \
    -no-boot-anim -no-snapshot-save -memory 3072 "${audio[@]}" >"$ROOT/scratch/emulator-$AVD.log" 2>&1 &
  echo "emulator pid $!"
  $ADB wait-for-device
  for _ in $(seq 1 180); do
    [ "$($ADB shell getprop sys.boot_completed 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r')" = 1 ] && { echo "booted"; return; }
    sleep 2
  done
  echo "error: boot timeout" >&2; exit 1
}

install() {
  [ -f "$APK" ] || { echo "error: $APK missing; run scripts/build-apk.sh" >&2; exit 1; }
  $ADB install -r -g "$APK"
}

push() {
  local minimal=0
  [ "${1:-}" = --minimal ] && minimal=1
  [ -f "$GAME_DIR/S3.EXE" ] || { echo "error: $GAME_DIR/S3.EXE not found" >&2; exit 1; }
  # Build the list: S3.EXE, small top-level data files, folders the game reads (wine-trace.md).
  local items=(S3.EXE)
  for f in regs.cmd DATA.DAT S3.DAT S3CD1.DAT S3CD2.DAT S3GOLD1.DAT S3GOLD2.DAT S3MCD1.DAT S3QOTA1.DAT; do
    [ -e "$GAME_DIR/$f" ] && items+=("$f")
  done
  local dirs=(SND MUSIC S3 Map/SINGLE Map/TUTORIAL)
  [ $minimal = 0 ] && dirs+=(S3QOTA S3MCD Map/MULTI Map/User)
  local bytes=0
  for i in "${items[@]}" "${dirs[@]}"; do bytes=$((bytes + $(du -sb "$GAME_DIR/$i" | cut -f1))); done
  # GFX: only the RGB565 set (*.f8007e01f.dat); the port always reports a 565 primary surface.
  local gfx=()
  while IFS= read -r f; do gfx+=("$f"); done < <(cd "$GAME_DIR/GFX" && ls | grep -i '\.f8007e01f\.dat$')
  for f in "${gfx[@]}"; do bytes=$((bytes + $(stat -c %s "$GAME_DIR/GFX/$f"))); done
  local free_kb
  free_kb=$($ADB shell df -k /sdcard | awk 'NR==2 {print $4}' | tr -d '\r')
  echo "== pushing $((bytes / 1048576)) MB to $DEV_GAME (device free: $((free_kb / 1024)) MB)"
  if [ $((bytes / 1024 + 200000)) -gt "$free_kb" ]; then echo "error: not enough space on the device" >&2; exit 1; fi
  # The app creates files/ on first start; create it from the shell too (works on API 30+ for adb shell).
  $ADB shell mkdir -p "$DEV_GAME/GFX" "$DEV_GAME/Map"
  for i in "${items[@]}"; do $ADB push -q "$GAME_DIR/$i" "$DEV_GAME/$i" >/dev/null; done
  for f in "${gfx[@]}"; do $ADB push -q "$GAME_DIR/GFX/$f" "$DEV_GAME/GFX/$f" >/dev/null; done
  # Real phones (e.g. Samsung, Android 14) refuse `adb push` creating directories under Android/data
  # ("secure_mkdirs() failed: Operation not permitted"), but `adb shell mkdir` works. So create every
  # directory first, then push file by file; files already present with the same size are skipped.
  for d in "${dirs[@]}"; do
    echo "   $d"
    local mk=()
    while IFS= read -r sub; do mk+=("'$DEV_GAME/$sub'"); done < <(cd "$GAME_DIR" && find "$d" -type d)
    $ADB shell "mkdir -p ${mk[*]}" </dev/null
    while IFS= read -r f; do
      local want have
      want=$(stat -c %s "$GAME_DIR/$f")
      have=$($ADB shell "stat -c %s '$DEV_GAME/$f' 2>/dev/null" </dev/null | tr -d '\r' || true)
      [ "$want" = "$have" ] && continue
      $ADB push -q "$GAME_DIR/$f" "$DEV_GAME/$f" >/dev/null </dev/null
    done < <(cd "$GAME_DIR" && find "$d" -type f)
  done
  $ADB shell du -sh "$DEV_GAME"
}

launch() {
  $ADB shell am force-stop "$PKG" || true
  $ADB logcat -c || true
  $ADB shell am start -n "$PKG/android.app.NativeActivity" --ez play true
}

stop_app() { $ADB shell am force-stop "$PKG"; }

logcat() {
  if [ -n "${1:-}" ]; then
    timeout "$1" $ADB logcat -v time -s s3port:V AndroidRuntime:E DEBUG:V libc:F || true
  else
    $ADB logcat -d -v time -s s3port:V AndroidRuntime:E DEBUG:V libc:F | tail -n 300
  fi
}

shot() {
  mkdir -p "$SHOTS"
  local name="${1:-shot-$(date +%H%M%S)}"
  $ADB exec-out screencap -p >"$SHOTS/$name.png"
  echo "$SHOTS/$name.png"
}

status() {
  adb devices
  echo "pid: $($ADB shell pidof $PKG || echo none)"
  $ADB shell ls -la "$DEV_GAME" 2>/dev/null | head -30 || true
}

kill_emulator() { running && $ADB emu kill || echo "$SERIAL not running"; }

[ $# -eq 0 ] && set -- start install launch
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  cmd="$1"; shift
  case "$cmd" in
    create-avd) create_avd ;;
    start) start ;;
    install) install ;;
    push) if [ "${1:-}" = --minimal ]; then push --minimal; shift; else push; fi ;;
    launch) launch ;;
    stop) stop_app ;;
    logcat) if [[ "${1:-}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then logcat "$1"; shift; else logcat; fi ;;
    shot) if [ $# -gt 0 ] && [[ "$1" != -* ]] && ! [[ "$1" =~ ^(start|install|push|launch|stop|logcat|tap|status)$ ]]; then shot "$1"; shift; else shot; fi ;;
    tap) $ADB shell input tap "$1" "$2"; shift 2 ;;
    status) status ;;
    kill-emulator) kill_emulator ;;
    -h|--help|help) sed -n '2,22p' "$0" ;;
    *) echo "unknown command $cmd" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

```

`tools/anime4k_to_gles.py`:

```py
"""Convert an Anime4K mpv user shader (CNN upscaler, e.g. Anime4K_Upscale_CNN_x2_S.glsl from
https://github.com/bloc97/Anime4K, MIT) into GLSL ES 3.00 fragment shaders for the Android presenter
(port/crates/s3-android/src/anime4k.rs). Usage: python -I tools/anime4k_to_gles.py IN.glsl OUT.rs

Supported shape (the x2 S/M/L "Conv-4x3x3x*" + "Depth-to-Space" chain): every conv pass binds one texture and
samples it with `<name>_texOff(vec2(x, y))`; the last pass binds MAIN + the last conv texture and returns the
residual + MAIN. Each pass becomes one fragment shader: conv passes read `u_tex` at texel centres (`u_pt` = 1 /
size), the depth-to-space pass reads `u_last` / `u_main`.
"""
import re
import sys

src = open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8').read()
license_lines = []
for line in src.splitlines():
    if line.startswith('//!'):
        break
    license_lines.append(line)

passes = re.split(r'(?m)^(?=//!DESC)', src)
passes = [p for p in passes if p.startswith('//!DESC')]

out = []
conv = []
for p in passes:
    meta = dict()
    binds = re.findall(r'^//!BIND (\S+)', p, re.M)
    desc = re.search(r'^//!DESC (.*)$', p, re.M).group(1)
    body = '\n'.join(l for l in p.splitlines() if not l.startswith('//!'))
    if 'Depth-to-Space' in desc:
        continue
    assert len(binds) == 1, binds
    name = binds[0]
    body = body.replace(f'{name}_texOff(', 'TEX(')
    assert 'texOff' not in body and '_tex(' not in body, body[:200]
    conv.append((desc, body))

head = '''#version 300 es
precision highp float;
uniform sampler2D u_tex;
uniform vec2 u_pt;
in vec2 v_uv;
out vec4 o;
#define TEX(off) texture(u_tex, v_uv + (off) * u_pt)
'''
shaders = []
for desc, body in conv:
    shaders.append((desc, head + body.strip() + '\nvoid main() { o = hook(); }\n'))

final = '''#version 300 es
precision highp float;
uniform sampler2D u_last;
uniform sampler2D u_main;
uniform vec2 u_last_size;
in vec2 v_uv;
out vec4 o;
void main() {
    vec2 f0 = fract(v_uv * u_last_size);
    ivec2 i0 = ivec2(f0 * vec2(2.0));
    vec4 t = texture(u_last, (vec2(0.5) - f0) / u_last_size + v_uv);
    float c0 = t[i0.y * 2 + i0.x];
    o = vec4(texture(u_main, v_uv).rgb + vec3(c0), 1.0);
}
'''

with open(sys.argv[2], 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
    f.write('//! Anime4K CNN x2 upscaler shaders (generated by tools/anime4k_to_gles.py from\n')
    f.write('//! Anime4K_Upscale_CNN_x2_S.glsl, https://github.com/bloc97/Anime4K v3.2). Do not edit by hand.\n')
    f.write('//!\n')
    for l in license_lines:
        f.write('//! ' + l.lstrip('/ ').rstrip() + '\n' if l.strip() else '//!\n')
    f.write('\n/// Convolution passes, in order (input: the game frame, then each previous pass; RGBA16F outputs).\n')
    f.write('pub const CONV: [&str; %d] = [\n' % len(shaders))
    for desc, s in shaders:
        f.write('    // %s\n    r#"%s"#,\n' % (desc, s))
    f.write('];\n\n/// Depth-to-space: 2x output = bilinear game frame + the last pass\'s residual.\n')
    f.write('pub const DEPTH_TO_SPACE: &str = r#"%s"#;\n' % final)
print(len(shaders), 'conv passes')

```

`tools/autosave.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Snapshot the settlers-3 working tree into refs/wip/autosave every 20 min.
# Uses a private index, so HEAD, the real index and the working tree are never touched.
set -u
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
export GIT_INDEX_FILE="$PWD/.git/autosave-index"
while true; do
  git add -A >/dev/null 2>&1
  tree=$(git write-tree 2>/dev/null) || { sleep 1200; continue; }
  parent=$(git rev-parse -q --verify refs/wip/autosave || git rev-parse -q --verify HEAD)
  if [ "$(git rev-parse -q --verify "$parent^{tree}")" != "$tree" ]; then
    c=$(git -c user.name=autosave -c user.email=autosave@localhost commit-tree "$tree" -p "$parent" -m "autosave $(date -Is)")
    git update-ref refs/wip/autosave "$c"
  fi
  sleep 1200
done
```

`tools/determinism-test.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Determinism test (W5): run S3.EXE twice headless with s3det (virtual clock, fixed epoch, deterministic GUIDs)
# in parallel, same inject script, and compare per-second state hashes. See docs/porting/determinism.md.
#
# usage: tools/determinism-test.sh [s3det binary] [virtual ms (75000)]
# Output (small) goes to scratch/determinism/run/. Exit 0 = identical.
set -eu
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
BIN=${1:-$ROOT/port/target/release/s3det}
VMS=${2:-75000}
G=$ROOT/game-files/gog-s3-ultimate
OUT=$ROOT/scratch/determinism/run
rm -rf "$OUT" && mkdir -p "$OUT/d1" "$OUT/d2"
# Menu -> Single Player Scenario -> OK x3 -> random map 384 (in game by ~40 000 vms), then open the build menu,
# pick the first building and place it near the castle, and right-click (cancel) once.
I="1000:move 165 235;1200:click 165 235;3000:move 630 467;3200:click 630 467;5000:move 730 567;5200:click 730 567"
I="$I;7000:move 730 567;7200:click 730 567;48000:click 25 167;50000:click 25 200;52000:click 37 237"
I="$I;54000:move 420 300;55000:click 420 300;58000:rclick 300 260"
for n in 1 2; do
  "$BIN" --game-dir "$G" --data-dir "$OUT/d$n" --vms "$VMS" --hash-every 1000 --hash-out "$OUT/h$n.txt" \
    --inject "$I;$((VMS - 100)):shot $OUT/end$n.png" > "$OUT/log$n.txt" 2>&1 &
done
wait
if diff "$OUT/h1.txt" "$OUT/h2.txt" > "$OUT/diff.txt"; then
  echo "determinism: IDENTICAL ($(wc -l < "$OUT/h1.txt") hash lines, $(tail -n 1 "$OUT/h1.txt"))"
else
  echo "determinism: DIVERGED, first differing line:"; grep -m1 '^<' "$OUT/diff.txt"
  echo "dump memory at that vms in both runs (--dump-at V --dump f) and compare with tools/memdiff.py"
  exit 1
fi
```

`tools/dis.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Disassemble a VA range of S3.EXE with IAT slots replaced by API names (local analysis aid; prints to stdout).
usage: python3 -I tools/dis.py <S3.EXE> <start_va> <end_va>"""
import sys, re, subprocess, pefile
exe, s, e = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2], 16), int(sys.argv[3], 16)
pe = pefile.PE(exe, fast_load=True); pe.parse_data_directories([1])
iat = {i.address: i.name.decode() for d in pe.DIRECTORY_ENTRY_IMPORT for i in d.imports if i.name}
out = subprocess.run(['objdump', '-d', '-M', 'intel', '--no-show-raw-insn', '--start-address=%d' % s, '--stop-address=%d' % e, exe],
                     capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.splitlines()[7:]
for l in out:
    if re.search(r'\tnop$', l) or 'int3' in l: continue
    l = re.sub(r'ds:0x([0-9a-f]+)', lambda m: '[' + iat[int(m.group(1), 16)] + ']' if int(m.group(1), 16) in iat else m.group(0), l)
    print(l.strip())
```

`tools/iat_xrefs.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""List every instruction in S3.EXE .text that references an IAT slot (call [iat], mov reg,[iat], jmp [iat]).
usage: python3 -I tools/iat_xrefs.py <S3.EXE> [name-regex]   (reads local exe; prints addresses only)"""
import sys, re, subprocess, pefile
exe = sys.argv[1]
flt = re.compile(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None
pe = pefile.PE(exe)
iat = {}
for d in pe.DIRECTORY_ENTRY_IMPORT:
    for i in d.imports:
        iat[i.address] = (d.dll.decode() + '!' + (i.name.decode() if i.name else '#%d' % i.ordinal))
text = pe.sections[0]
start = pe.OPTIONAL_HEADER.ImageBase + text.VirtualAddress
p = subprocess.Popen(['objdump', '-d', '-M', 'intel', '--start-address=%d' % start,
                      '--stop-address=%d' % (start + text.Misc_VirtualSize), exe], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
rx = re.compile(r'ds:0x([0-9a-f]+)')
for line in p.stdout:
    m = rx.search(line)
    if not m: continue
    a = int(m.group(1), 16)
    if a in iat and (flt is None or flt.search(iat[a])):
        parts = line.split('\t')
        print(parts[0].strip().rstrip(':'), iat[a], parts[-1].strip())
```

`tools/isa-census/src/main.rs`:

```rs
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
//! Recursive-descent instruction census for a 32-bit PE (built for S3.EXE).
//! Reads the user's local exe at runtime and prints statistics only (no game bytes are written).
//!
//! usage: isa-census <exe> [--data-seeds] [--list-rare]
use iced_x86::{
    Code, CpuidFeature, Decoder, DecoderOptions, FlowControl, Formatter, Instruction, IntelFormatter, Mnemonic, OpKind,
    Register,
};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap, HashSet};

struct Img {
    base: u32,
    mem: Vec<u8>,
    text: (u32, u32), // VA range [start, end)
    data_ranges: Vec<(u32, u32)>,
    entry: u32,
    imports: HashMap<u32, String>, // IAT slot VA -> "DLL!name"
}

fn rd16(b: &[u8], o: usize) -> u16 {
    u16::from_le_bytes([b[o], b[o + 1]])
}
fn rd32(b: &[u8], o: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::from_le_bytes([b[o], b[o + 1], b[o + 2], b[o + 3]])
}

fn load(path: &str) -> Img {
    let f = std::fs::read(path).expect("read exe");
    let pe = rd32(&f, 0x3c) as usize;
    let nsec = rd16(&f, pe + 6) as usize;
    let optsz = rd16(&f, pe + 20) as usize;
    let opt = pe + 24;
    let entry_rva = rd32(&f, opt + 16);
    let base = rd32(&f, opt + 28);
    let size = rd32(&f, opt + 56) as usize;
    let import_rva = rd32(&f, opt + 96 + 8) as usize;
    let mut mem = vec![0u8; size];
    mem[..0x1000.min(f.len())].copy_from_slice(&f[..0x1000.min(f.len())]);
    let mut text = (0, 0);
    let mut data_ranges = vec![];
    for i in 0..nsec {
        let s = opt + optsz + i * 40;
        let name = String::from_utf8_lossy(&f[s..s + 8]).trim_end_matches('\0').to_string();
        let vsz = rd32(&f, s + 8) as usize;
        let va = rd32(&f, s + 12) as usize;
        let rsz = rd32(&f, s + 16) as usize;
        let rptr = rd32(&f, s + 20) as usize;
        let n = rsz.min(vsz.max(rsz)).min(f.len() - rptr).min(size - va);
        mem[va..va + n].copy_from_slice(&f[rptr..rptr + n]);
        let r = (base + va as u32, base + (va + vsz) as u32);
        if name == ".text" {
            text = r;
        } else if name == ".rdata" || name == ".data" {
            data_ranges.push(r);
        }
    }
    let mut imports = HashMap::new();
    let mut d = import_rva;
    loop {
        let oft = rd32(&mem, d) as usize;
        let name_rva = rd32(&mem, d + 12) as usize;
        let ft = rd32(&mem, d + 16) as usize;
        if name_rva == 0 {
            break;
        }
        let dll = cstr(&mem, name_rva);
        let mut k = 0;
        loop {
            let thunk = rd32(&mem, if oft != 0 { oft } else { ft } + k * 4);
            if thunk == 0 {
                break;
            }
            let nm = if thunk & 0x8000_0000 != 0 { format!("#{}", thunk & 0xffff) } else { cstr(&mem, thunk as usize + 2) };
            imports.insert(base + (ft + k * 4) as u32, format!("{dll}!{nm}"));
            k += 1;
        }
        d += 20;
    }
    Img { base, mem, text, data_ranges, entry: base + entry_rva, imports }
}

fn cstr(m: &[u8], o: usize) -> String {
    let e = m[o..].iter().position(|&c| c == 0).unwrap_or(0);
    String::from_utf8_lossy(&m[o..o + e]).to_string()
}

impl Img {
    fn in_text(&self, va: u32) -> bool {
        va >= self.text.0 && va < self.text.1
    }
    fn u32_at(&self, va: u32) -> Option<u32> {
        let o = va.checked_sub(self.base)? as usize;
        if o + 4 <= self.mem.len() {
            Some(rd32(&self.mem, o))
        } else {
            None
        }
    }
}

fn main() {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let img = load(&args[1]);
    let data_seeds = args.iter().any(|a| a == "--data-seeds");
    let list_rare = args.iter().any(|a| a == "--list-rare");

    let mut work: Vec<u32> = vec![img.entry];
    if data_seeds {
        for &(s, e) in &img.data_ranges {
            let mut a = s;
            while a + 4 <= e {
                let v = img.u32_at(a).unwrap();
                if img.in_text(v) {
                    work.push(v);
                }
                a += 4;
            }
        }
    }
    let mut seen: HashSet<u32> = HashSet::new(); // instruction starts
    let mut owner: HashMap<u32, u32> = HashMap::new(); // byte -> insn start (for overlap detection)
    let mut mn: BTreeMap<String, u64> = BTreeMap::new();
    let mut feat: BTreeMap<String, u64> = BTreeMap::new();
    let mut rare: BTreeMap<String, Vec<u32>> = BTreeMap::new();
    let mut misc: BTreeMap<&str, u64> = BTreeMap::new();
    let mut misc_addr: BTreeMap<&str, Vec<u32>> = BTreeMap::new();
    let mut import_calls: BTreeMap<String, u64> = BTreeMap::new();
    let mut overlaps = 0u64;
    let mut invalid = 0u64;
    let mut jump_tables = 0u64;
    let mut fmt = IntelFormatter::new();
    let base_feats = [
        CpuidFeature::INTEL8086,
        CpuidFeature::INTEL186,
        CpuidFeature::INTEL286,
        CpuidFeature::INTEL386,
        CpuidFeature::INTEL486,
        CpuidFeature::FPU,
        CpuidFeature::FPU287,
        CpuidFeature::FPU387,
    ];

    while let Some(start) = work.pop() {
        let mut ip = start;
        loop {
            if !img.in_text(ip) || seen.contains(&ip) {
                break;
            }
            if let Some(&o) = owner.get(&ip) {
                if o != ip {
                    overlaps += 1;
                    break;
                }
            }
            let off = (ip - img.base) as usize;
            let end = (img.text.1 - img.base) as usize;
            let mut dec = Decoder::with_ip(32, &img.mem[off..end], ip as u64, DecoderOptions::NONE);
            let ins: Instruction = dec.decode();
            if ins.is_invalid() {
                invalid += 1;
                break;
            }
            seen.insert(ip);
            for b in 0..ins.len() as u32 {
                owner.insert(ip + b, ip);
            }
            let mut name = format!("{:?}", ins.mnemonic()).to_lowercase();
            if ins.has_rep_prefix() && ins.mnemonic() != Mnemonic::Ret {
                name = format!("rep {name}");
            }
            if ins.has_repne_prefix() {
                name = format!("repne {name}");
            }
            if ins.has_lock_prefix() {
                name = format!("lock {name}");
            }
            *mn.entry(name.clone()).or_default() += 1;
            for f in ins.cpuid_features() {
                *feat.entry(format!("{f:?}")).or_default() += 1;
                if !base_feats.contains(f) {
                    rare.entry(format!("{f:?} {name}")).or_default().push(ip);
                }
            }
            // segment overrides
            match ins.segment_prefix() {
                Register::FS => {
                    *misc.entry("fs: override").or_default() += 1;
                }
                Register::GS => {
                    *misc.entry("gs: override").or_default() += 1;
                    misc_addr.entry("gs: override").or_default().push(ip);
                }
                Register::None | Register::DS | Register::SS => {}
                _ => {
                    *misc.entry("es/cs override").or_default() += 1;
                    misc_addr.entry("es/cs override").or_default().push(ip);
                }
            }
            if matches!(ins.code(), Code::Rdtsc) {
                misc_addr.entry("rdtsc").or_default().push(ip);
            }
            if ins.op_count() > 0 && ins.op0_kind() == OpKind::Memory && ins.memory_base() == Register::None
                && ins.memory_index() == Register::None && img.in_text(ins.memory_displacement32())
                && ins.mnemonic() != Mnemonic::Call && ins.mnemonic() != Mnemonic::Jmp
            {
                // store to an absolute .text address = possible self-modifying code
                let info_write = matches!(ins.mnemonic(), Mnemonic::Mov | Mnemonic::Add | Mnemonic::Sub | Mnemonic::Xor | Mnemonic::Or | Mnemonic::And | Mnemonic::Inc | Mnemonic::Dec);
                if info_write {
                    *misc.entry("store to .text (SMC?)").or_default() += 1;
                    misc_addr.entry("store to .text (SMC?)").or_default().push(ip);
                }
            }
            // immediates pointing into .text = callbacks / function pointers
            for i in 0..ins.op_count() {
                if ins.op_kind(i) == OpKind::Immediate32 {
                    let v = ins.immediate32();
                    if img.in_text(v) {
                        work.push(v);
                        *misc.entry("code-address immediates").or_default() += 1;
                    }
                }
            }
            let next = ip + ins.len() as u32;
            match ins.flow_control() {
                FlowControl::Next => {}
                FlowControl::ConditionalBranch | FlowControl::UnconditionalBranch => {
                    if ins.op0_kind() == OpKind::NearBranch32 {
                        work.push(ins.near_branch32());
                    }
                    if ins.flow_control() == FlowControl::UnconditionalBranch {
                        break;
                    }
                }
                FlowControl::Call => {
                    if ins.op0_kind() == OpKind::NearBranch32 {
                        work.push(ins.near_branch32());
                    }
                }
                FlowControl::IndirectCall => {
                    if ins.memory_base() == Register::None && ins.memory_index() == Register::None {
                        if let Some(n) = img.imports.get(&ins.memory_displacement32()) {
                            *import_calls.entry(n.clone()).or_default() += 1;
                            if n.ends_with("!ExitProcess") || n.ends_with("!ExitThread") || n.ends_with("!RaiseException") && false {
                                break;
                            }
                        }
                    } else {
                        *misc.entry("indirect call via reg/mem (vtable etc.)").or_default() += 1;
                    }
                }
                FlowControl::IndirectBranch => {
                    if ins.op0_kind() == OpKind::Memory && ins.memory_index() != Register::None && ins.memory_index_scale() == 4 {
                        let t = ins.memory_displacement32();
                        let mut k = 0;
                        jump_tables += 1;
                        while k < 1024 {
                            match img.u32_at(t + k * 4) {
                                Some(v) if img.in_text(v) => work.push(v),
                                _ => break,
                            }
                            k += 1;
                        }
                    } else if ins.op0_kind() == OpKind::Memory && ins.memory_base() == Register::None && ins.memory_index() == Register::None {
                        if img.imports.contains_key(&ins.memory_displacement32()) {
                            *misc.entry("import thunks (jmp [iat])").or_default() += 1;
                        }
                    } else {
                        *misc.entry("indirect jmp other").or_default() += 1;
                    }
                    break;
                }
                FlowControl::Return | FlowControl::Interrupt | FlowControl::Exception => break,
                FlowControl::XbeginXabortXend => break,
            }
            ip = next;
            let _ = &mut fmt;
        }
    }
    let total: u64 = mn.values().sum();
    let text_bytes: usize = owner.len();
    println!("mode: {}", if data_seeds { "entry + code immediates + data pointers" } else { "entry + code immediates" });
    println!("instructions decoded: {total}, bytes covered: {text_bytes} of {} .text bytes", img.text.1 - img.text.0);
    println!("overlap conflicts: {overlaps}, invalid stops: {invalid}, jump tables followed: {jump_tables}");
    println!("\n## CPUID feature classes");
    let mut fv: Vec<_> = feat.iter().collect();
    fv.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.cmp(a.1));
    for (k, v) in fv {
        println!("{v:>8} {k}");
    }
    println!("\n## mnemonics");
    let mut v: Vec<_> = mn.iter().collect();
    v.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.cmp(a.1));
    for (k, c) in v {
        println!("{c:>8} {k}");
    }
    println!("\n## misc");
    for (k, c) in &misc {
        println!("{c:>8} {k}");
    }
    for (k, a) in &misc_addr {
        let s: Vec<String> = a.iter().take(20).map(|x| format!("{x:#x}")).collect();
        println!("  {k}: {}", s.join(" "));
    }
    if list_rare {
        println!("\n## non-386/x87 instructions (addresses, first 12)");
        for (k, a) in &rare {
            let s: Vec<String> = a.iter().take(12).map(|x| format!("{x:#x}")).collect();
            println!("{:>6} {k}: {}", a.len(), s.join(" "));
        }
    }
    println!("\n## direct import call sites (call [IAT])");
    let mut iv: Vec<_> = import_calls.iter().collect();
    iv.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.cmp(a.1));
    for (k, c) in iv {
        println!("{c:>6} {k}");
    }
}
```

`tools/make_ios_icon.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
"""Render our own app icon (port/android/res/drawable/ic_launcher_{bg,fg}.xml: roman numeral III, white with a red
outline on navy) as the 1024x1024 PNG iOS wants (port/ios/Resources/AppIcon.png, `iconPath` in xtool.yml).

Usage: python3 tools/make_ios_icon.py [out.png]
"""
import math
import re
import sys

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, PngImagePlugin  # noqa: F401 (registers PNG)

SIZE = 1024
SS = 4  # supersampling
# The adaptive icon's visible square is the inner 72 of 108 units (18..90).
VIEW0, VIEW = 18.0, 72.0

# Paths of the three bars (left, right, middle) from ic_launcher_fg.xml, with their gradient y range.
BARS = [
    ("M30.00,36.00H45.00V39.20Q41.00,39.20 41.00,42.08V63.92Q41.00,66.80 45.00,66.80V70.00H30.00V66.80Q34.00,66.80 34.00,63.92V42.08Q34.00,39.20 30.00,39.20Z", 36, 70),
    ("M63.00,36.00H78.00V39.20Q74.00,39.20 74.00,42.08V63.92Q74.00,66.80 78.00,66.80V70.00H63.00V66.80Q67.00,66.80 67.00,63.92V42.08Q67.00,39.20 63.00,39.20Z", 36, 70),
    ("M45.50,30.00H62.50V33.60Q58.00,33.60 58.00,36.84V69.16Q58.00,72.40 62.50,72.40V76.00H45.50V72.40Q50.00,72.40 50.00,69.16V36.84Q50.00,33.60 45.50,33.60Z", 30, 76),
]
RED = (0x84, 0x2B, 0x26)
GREY = (0x8A, 0x8F, 0x96)


def path_points(d):
    """M/H/V/Q/Z path (absolute) -> polygon points in path units."""
    toks = re.findall(r"[MHVQZ]|-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?", d)
    pts, cur, i = [], (0.0, 0.0), 0
    while i < len(toks):
        c = toks[i]
        i += 1
        if c == "M":
            cur = (float(toks[i]), float(toks[i + 1]))
            i += 2
            pts.append(cur)
        elif c == "H":
            cur = (float(toks[i]), cur[1])
            i += 1
            pts.append(cur)
        elif c == "V":
            cur = (cur[0], float(toks[i]))
            i += 1
            pts.append(cur)
        elif c == "Q":
            c1 = (float(toks[i]), float(toks[i + 1]))
            end = (float(toks[i + 2]), float(toks[i + 3]))
            i += 4
            for k in range(1, 13):
                t = k / 12
                x = (1 - t) ** 2 * cur[0] + 2 * (1 - t) * t * c1[0] + t * t * end[0]
                y = (1 - t) ** 2 * cur[1] + 2 * (1 - t) * t * c1[1] + t * t * end[1]
                pts.append((x, y))
            cur = end
        elif c == "Z":
            pass
    return pts


def to_px(p, dx=0.0, dy=0.0):
    s = SIZE * SS / VIEW
    return ((p[0] + dx - VIEW0) * s, (p[1] + dy - VIEW0) * s)


def main():
    out = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "port/ios/Resources/AppIcon.png"
    n = SIZE * SS
    # Background: radial gradient #24466F (centre 54,48) -> #0C1B30 at radius 70.
    bg = Image.new("RGB", (n, n))
    px = bg.load()
    s = n / VIEW
    for y in range(0, n, SS):
        for x in range(0, n, SS):
            ux, uy = x / s + VIEW0, y / s + VIEW0
            t = min(1.0, math.hypot(ux - 54, uy - 48) / 70)
            col = tuple(round(a + (b - a) * t) for a, b in zip((0x24, 0x46, 0x6F), (0x0C, 0x1B, 0x30)))
            for yy in range(SS):
                for xx in range(SS):
                    px[x + xx, y + yy] = col
    img = bg.convert("RGBA")
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    stroke = round(4.2 * s)
    for path, _, _ in BARS:
        poly = [to_px(p) for p in path_points(path)]
        # Red outline (stroke 4.2, round joins approximated by the filled polygon + thick line).
        d.polygon(poly, fill=RED)
        d.line(poly + [poly[0]], fill=RED, width=stroke, joint="curve")
        for q in poly:
            r = stroke / 2
            d.ellipse([q[0] - r, q[1] - r, q[0] + r, q[1] + r], fill=RED)
        d.polygon(poly, fill=GREY)
    for path, y0, y1 in BARS:
        poly = [to_px(p, -0.6, -0.6) for p in path_points(path)]
        mask = Image.new("L", (n, n), 0)
        ImageDraw.Draw(mask).polygon(poly, fill=255)
        grad = Image.new("RGBA", (n, n))
        gd = ImageDraw.Draw(grad)
        top, bot = to_px((0, y0 - 0.6))[1], to_px((0, y1 - 0.6))[1]
        for y in range(max(0, int(top)), min(n, int(bot) + 1)):
            t = (y - top) / max(1.0, bot - top)
            c = tuple(round(255 + (b - 255) * t) for b in (0xC9, 0xCD, 0xD3))
            gd.line([(0, y), (n, y)], fill=c + (255,))
        img.paste(grad, (0, 0), mask)
    img = img.convert("RGB").resize((SIZE, SIZE), Image.LANCZOS)
    img.save(out, format="PNG")
    print(f"wrote {out} {img.size}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

`tools/memdiff.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compare two s3det --dump files ([u32 addr][4096 bytes] records); print differing byte ranges.

usage: python3 -I tools/memdiff.py a.bin b.bin [max_ranges]
"""
import struct
import sys


def load(p):
    pages = {}
    with open(p, 'rb') as f:
        data = f.read()
    for off in range(0, len(data), 4100):
        addr = struct.unpack_from('<I', data, off)[0]
        pages[addr] = data[off + 4:off + 4100]
    return pages


def main():
    a, b = load(sys.argv[1]), load(sys.argv[2])
    limit = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 60
    only = sorted(set(a) ^ set(b))
    if only:
        print(f'pages only in one dump: {len(only)} (first {[hex(x) for x in only[:8]]})')
    ranges = []
    for addr in sorted(set(a) & set(b)):
        pa, pb = a[addr], b[addr]
        if pa == pb:
            continue
        i = 0
        while i < 4096:
            if pa[i] != pb[i]:
                j = i
                while j < 4096 and pa[j] != pb[j]:
                    j += 1
                ranges.append((addr + i, pa[i:j], pb[i:j]))
                i = j
            else:
                i += 1
    print(f'differing ranges: {len(ranges)}, bytes: {sum(len(r[1]) for r in ranges)}')
    for addr, x, y in ranges[:limit]:
        print(f'{addr:#010x} len={len(x):4}  a={x[:24].hex()}  b={y[:24].hex()}')


main()
```

`tools/mp_dump_diff.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Diff raw table dumps of two lockstep peers (`S3_MP_DUMP_STEP`, see port/crates/s3-desktop/src/mp_hash.rs).

usage: python3 -I tools/mp_dump_diff.py DIR STEP   (reads DIR/host.STEP.<table>.bin and DIR/join.STEP.<table>.bin)
Prints, per table, the differing byte offsets within an entry and a few examples (entry, host, join).
"""
import os
import sys

ENTRY = {"settlers": 0x40, "buildings": 0x3a, "econ": 0x2e0, "players": 0x148, "world": 0x18}


def main():
    d, step = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    for name, sz in ENTRY.items():
        pa, pb = os.path.join(d, f"host.{step}.{name}.bin"), os.path.join(d, f"join.{step}.{name}.bin")
        if not (os.path.exists(pa) and os.path.exists(pb)):
            continue
        a, b = open(pa, "rb").read(), open(pb, "rb").read()
        diffs = {}
        for i, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(a, b)):
            if x != y:
                diffs.setdefault(i % sz, []).append((i // sz, x, y))
        print(f"{name}: {len(a)} vs {len(b)} bytes, differing offsets: "
              + (", ".join(f"{k:#x}({len(v)})" for k, v in sorted(diffs.items())) or "none"))
        for k, v in sorted(diffs.items())[:12]:
            print(f"   +{k:#05x}: " + " ".join(f"[{e}] {x:#x}/{y:#x}" for e, x, y in v[:6]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

`tools/mp_hash_compare.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compare two `s3run --mp-hash` files (one per lockstep peer) step by step.

usage: python3 -I tools/mp_hash_compare.py host.hash join.hash
Lines look like `step=TICK rng=.. n=a/b/c settlers=.. buildings=.. ... [world=..] frame=F local=P`
(TICK = simulation ticks run so far). `frame=` (the game's frame counter, keeps running while the lockstep layer
pauses the simulation) and `local=` (local player) differ per peer by design and are not compared.
`exec at=TICK frame=F msg=HEX` lines (logic messages executed before tick TICK) are compared in order, except
local class-0x02/0x22 messages. Exit code 0 = no differing step, 1 = desync, 2 = nothing to compare, 3 = only world tiles differ.
"""
import sys


def load_exec(path):
    out = []
    with open(path, encoding="ascii", errors="replace") as f:
        for line in f:
            if line.startswith("exec "):
                kv = dict(p.split("=", 1) for p in line.split()[1:])
                kv.pop("frame", None)
                # Class 0x02 (timing) and 0x22 (a 0x58-byte message with a per-peer value in bytes 4..5, executed at
                # slightly different ticks on each peer) are local messages, not lockstep traffic (OBSERVED;
                # meaning HYPOTHESIS). Everything else (class 0x01: player commands, 0xfb sync) must match exactly.
                msg = kv["msg"]
                if msg.startswith("02") or msg.startswith("22"):
                    continue
                out.append((int(kv["at"]), msg))
    return out


def load(path):
    out = {}
    with open(path, encoding="ascii", errors="replace") as f:
        for line in f:
            if line.startswith("exec "):
                continue
            kv = dict(p.split("=", 1) for p in line.split() if "=" in p)
            if "step" not in kv:
                continue
            step = int(kv.pop("step"))
            kv.pop("local", None)
            kv.pop("frame", None)
            # Keep the first line per step (a step is hashed once per peer).
            out.setdefault(step, kv)
    return out


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        print(__doc__)
        return 2
    a, b = load(sys.argv[1]), load(sys.argv[2])
    ea, eb = load_exec(sys.argv[1]), load_exec(sys.argv[2])
    n = min(len(ea), len(eb))
    first_bad = next((i for i in range(n) if ea[i] != eb[i]), None)
    cmds = sum(1 for _, m in ea if m.startswith("01") and not m.startswith("01fb"))
    print(f"executed messages: a {len(ea)}, b {len(eb)} ({cmds} player commands in a); "
          + ("same order and steps" if first_bad is None else
             f"FIRST DIFFERENCE at #{first_bad}: a {ea[first_bad]} b {eb[first_bad]}"))
    common = sorted(set(a) & set(b))
    if not common:
        print(f"no common steps (a: {len(a)} lines, b: {len(b)} lines)")
        return 2
    bad = []
    for s in common:
        diff = [k for k in a[s] if k in b[s] and a[s][k] != b[s][k]]
        if diff:
            bad.append((s, diff))
    print(f"steps compared: {len(common)} (from {common[0]} to {common[-1]}, {len(common)} hashed ticks); "
          f"only in a: {len(set(a) - set(b))}, only in b: {len(set(b) - set(a))}")
    worlds = sum(1 for s in common if "world" in a[s] and "world" in b[s])
    print(f"world hashes compared: {worlds}")
    if not bad and first_bad is None and len(ea) == len(eb):
        print("RESULT: IDENTICAL (no desync)")
        return 0
    if not bad:
        print("RESULT: STATE IDENTICAL, but the executed message lists differ")
        return 1
    if all(d == ["world"] for _, d in bad) and first_bad is None:
        print(f"RESULT: SIMULATION TABLES IDENTICAL; world tiles differ at {len(bad)} of {worlds} world hashes "
              f"(first at tick {bad[0][0]}); diff raw dumps with S3_MP_DUMP_STEP + tools/mp_dump_diff.py")
        return 3
    s, diff = bad[0]
    print(f"RESULT: DESYNC at {len(bad)} steps; first at step {s}: {', '.join(diff)}")
    for s, diff in bad[:10]:
        print(f"  step {s}: {', '.join(diff)}")
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/perf/code_hash.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print length and FNV-1a 64 hash (s3_cpu::code_hash) of guest code ranges of a PE (for NativeBlock entries).

usage: python3 -I tools/perf/code_hash.py [--concat] S3.EXE START END [START END ...]   (hex VAs, END exclusive)
--concat: one hash over all ranges concatenated (fast_tile.rs OBJ_HASH).
Prints no code bytes (game code must not end up in our sources)."""
import struct
import sys


def sections(b):
    pe = struct.unpack_from("<I", b, 0x3C)[0]
    n = struct.unpack_from("<H", b, pe + 6)[0]
    opt = struct.unpack_from("<H", b, pe + 20)[0]
    base = struct.unpack_from("<I", b, pe + 24 + 28)[0]
    off = pe + 24 + opt
    out = []
    for i in range(n):
        s = off + 40 * i
        vsize, va, rsize, raw = struct.unpack_from("<IIII", b, s + 8)
        out.append((base + va, max(vsize, rsize), raw, rsize))
    return out


def read(b, secs, va, n):
    for sva, size, raw, rsize in secs:
        if sva <= va and va + n <= sva + size:
            return b[raw + va - sva: raw + va - sva + n]
    raise SystemExit(f"{va:#x} not in a section")


def fnv(data):
    h = 0xCBF29CE484222325
    for x in data:
        h ^= x
        h = (h * 0x100000001B3) & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    return h


def main():
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    concat = args[:1] == ["--concat"]
    if concat:
        args = args[1:]
    b = open(args[0], "rb").read()
    secs = sections(b)
    a = args[1:]
    parts = []
    for i in range(0, len(a), 2):
        s, e = int(a[i], 16), int(a[i + 1], 16)
        parts.append(read(b, secs, s, e - s))
        if not concat:
            print(f"{s:#x}..{e:#x} len {e - s} hash {fnv(parts[-1]):#018x}")
    if concat:
        print(f"{len(parts)} ranges, {sum(map(len, parts))} bytes, hash {fnv(b''.join(parts)):#018x}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

`tools/perf/fast.ps1`:

```ps1
# Run a command with Windows power throttling (EcoQoS) disabled and high priority; prints "cpu_time_s N" and its
# stdout/stderr. Processes started from an agent shell are otherwise throttled 2-4x (docs/porting/performance.md).
# usage: fast.ps1 <exe> <args...>
param([string]$exe, [Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments=$true)][string[]]$rest)
Add-Type -TypeDefinition @'
using System;
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
public static class PT {
  [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)] public struct STATE { public uint Version; public uint ControlMask; public uint StateMask; }
  [DllImport("kernel32.dll", SetLastError=true)] public static extern bool SetProcessInformation(IntPtr h, int cls, ref STATE s, uint size);
  public static bool Off(IntPtr h) { var s = new STATE { Version = 1, ControlMask = 1 | 4, StateMask = 0 }; return SetProcessInformation(h, 4, ref s, 12); }
}
'@
$psi = New-Object System.Diagnostics.ProcessStartInfo
$psi.FileName = $exe
$psi.Arguments = ($rest | ForEach-Object { if ($_ -match '[\s;"]') { '"' + ($_ -replace '"','\"') + '"' } else { $_ } }) -join ' '
$psi.UseShellExecute = $false
$psi.RedirectStandardOutput = $true
$psi.RedirectStandardError = $true
$p = [System.Diagnostics.Process]::Start($psi)
[void][PT]::Off($p.Handle)
$p.PriorityClass = 'High'
$out = $p.StandardOutput.ReadToEndAsync()
$err = $p.StandardError.ReadToEndAsync()
$p.WaitForExit()
"cpu_time_s {0:N2}" -f $p.TotalProcessorTime.TotalSeconds
$out.Result
$err.Result

```

`tools/perf_profile.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Function-level guest profile from an `S3_PROFILE` dump of s3run.

usage: python3 -I tools/perf_profile.py PROFILE FUNCS [TOP]

PROFILE: lines `thread start_eip block_len entries` (s3run, env S3_PROFILE=<file>, optional S3_PROFILE_FROM_MS).
FUNCS:   lines `0xADDR name` with function start addresses (e.g. exported from REA list_procedures; keep it in
         scratch/, it is derived from the game binary). A block is attributed to the closest function start <= it.
Prints the top functions by guest instructions (entries * block length; an approximation because blocks that
exit early still count their full length).
"""
import bisect
import sys


def main():
    prof, funcs = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    top = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 40
    starts, names = [], []
    for line in open(funcs):
        a, *n = line.split()
        starts.append(int(a, 16))
        names.append(n[0] if n else a)
    order = sorted(range(len(starts)), key=lambda i: starts[i])
    starts = [starts[i] for i in order]
    names = [names[i] for i in order]
    agg, per_thread, total = {}, {}, 0
    for line in open(prof):
        t, s, ln, n = line.split()
        s, ins = int(s, 16), int(ln) * int(n)
        total += ins
        i = bisect.bisect_right(starts, s) - 1
        key = (starts[i], names[i]) if i >= 0 and s < 0x1000000 else (s, "?")
        e = agg.setdefault(key, [0, set()])
        e[0] += ins
        e[1].add(t)
        per_thread[t] = per_thread.get(t, 0) + ins
    print(f"total {total / 1e6:.1f} M instructions; per thread (M): "
          + ", ".join(f"t{k}={v / 1e6:.0f}" for k, v in sorted(per_thread.items())))
    cum = 0
    for (a, name), (ins, ts) in sorted(agg.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1][0])[:top]:
        cum += ins
        print(f"{100 * ins / total:6.2f}% cum {100 * cum / total:5.1f}%  {a:#08x} {name:<24} threads {','.join(sorted(ts))}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

`tools/re-messages/lst.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print N lines of a local objdump listing from a VA, or grep it for a pattern (local analysis aid).
usage: python -I tools/re-messages/lst.py [ASM] ADDR [N]        (ADDR hex, no 0x)
       python -I tools/re-messages/lst.py ASM -g REGEX [MAX]  (lines matching REGEX)
The listing (scratch/re-ui/s3.asm, `objdump -d -M intel` of S3.EXE) is game-derived: keep it in scratch/."""
import sys, re
if not sys.argv[1].endswith('.asm'):
    sys.argv.insert(1, 'C:/Users/<user>/Projects/settlers-3/scratch/re-ui/s3.asm')
asm = sys.argv[1]
if sys.argv[2] == '-g':
    rx = re.compile(sys.argv[3]); mx = int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 200
    n = 0
    with open(asm, errors='replace') as f:
        for l in f:
            if rx.search(l):
                print(l.rstrip()[:140]); n += 1
                if n >= mx: break
    sys.exit()
key = '  %s:' % sys.argv[2].lower().lstrip('0x') if not sys.argv[2].startswith('0x') else '  %s:' % sys.argv[2][2:]
tgt = int(key.strip().rstrip(':'), 16)
cnt = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 80
out = None
with open(asm, errors='replace') as f:
    for l in f:
        if out is None:
            m0 = re.match(r'\s+([0-9a-f]+):', l)
            if m0 and int(m0.group(1), 16) >= tgt:
                out = 0
        if out is not None:
            s = l.rstrip()
            # drop raw bytes column
            m = re.match(r'\s*([0-9a-f]+):\t(?:[0-9a-f]{2} )+\s*\t?(.*)', s)
            print((m.group(1) + ': ' + m.group(2)) if m else s[:140])
            out += 1
            if out >= cnt: break
```

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Decode the in-game message ring dumped from logic+0x414 (5 entries x 0x1c; s3run `xdump 0x700ffee0@0x414 0x8c F`).
usage: python -I tools/re-messages/slots.py FILE...
Entry: +0 string object (+4 ptr to UTF-16, +8 length, +0xc capacity), +0x10 timer (ticks), +0x14 icon, +0x18 dirty.
Only pointers/lengths are decoded (the text lives on the guest heap; read it with xpeek)."""
import struct, sys
for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    b = open(f, 'rb').read()
    print(f)
    for i in range(len(b) // 0x1c):
        o = i * 0x1c
        _, p, l, c, t, ic = struct.unpack_from('<IIIIii', b, o)
        print('  slot %d ptr=%08x len=%3d timer=%7d icon=%#x dirty=%d' % (i, p, l, t, ic & 0xffffffff, b[o + 0x18]))
```

`tools/re-ui/diff.py`:

```py
"""Diff guest memory dumps: python3 -I diff.py BASE d1 d2 d3 ... ; lists 16/32-bit words stable in d1==d2
but changed later, with their value sequence. BASE = guest address of dump start (hex)."""
import sys, struct
base = int(sys.argv[1], 16)
ds = [open(p, 'rb').read() for p in sys.argv[2:]]
maxn = int(__import__('os').environ.get('MAXN', '400'))
n = 0
for off in range(0, len(ds[0]) - 3, 4):
    vals = [struct.unpack_from('<i', d, off)[0] for d in ds]
    if vals[0] != vals[1]:
        continue
    if len(set(vals)) == 1:
        continue
    print(f"{base+off:#x}: " + " ".join(str(v) for v in vals))
    n += 1
    if n >= maxn:
        break
```

`tools/re-ui/findstock.py`:

```py
"""findstock.py DUMPDIR : search snapshot for a window of small counters matching the panel inventory multiset."""
import os, sys, numpy as np
from collections import Counter
need = Counter({25: 2, 15: 2, 10: 1, 6: 1, 8: 1, 7: 1, 4: 1, 2: 1, 5: 2, 1: 2})
d = sys.argv[1]
for f in sorted(os.listdir(d)):
    base = int(f[:8], 16); raw = open(os.path.join(d, f), 'rb').read()
    for dt, w in (('<i4', 4), ('<i2', 2), ('u1', 1)):
        a = np.frombuffer(raw[:len(raw) // w * w], dtype=dt).astype(np.int64)
        n = 40
        if len(a) < n: continue
        # quick filter: positions where value 25 occurs
        for i in np.nonzero(a == 25)[0]:
            lo = max(0, i - n); win = a[lo:lo + 2 * n]
            if win.max() > 40 or win.min() < 0: continue
            c = Counter(win.tolist())
            if all(c[k] >= v for k, v in need.items()):
                print(f, dt, hex(base + lo * w), win.tolist()); break
```

`tools/re-ui/findstock2.py`:

```py
"""findstock2.py DUMPDIR WIDTH: windows (64 items) containing the panel inventory values, others unconstrained."""
import os, sys, numpy as np
from collections import Counter
need = Counter({25: 2, 15: 2, 10: 1, 6: 1, 8: 1, 7: 1, 4: 1, 2: 1, 5: 2})
d = sys.argv[1]; w = int(sys.argv[2]); dt = {4: '<i4', 2: '<i2', 1: 'u1'}[w]
for f in sorted(os.listdir(d)):
    base = int(f[:8], 16); raw = open(os.path.join(d, f), 'rb').read()
    a = np.frombuffer(raw[:len(raw) // w * w], dtype=dt).astype(np.int64)
    pos = np.nonzero(a == 25)[0]; last = -999
    for i in pos:
        if i - last < 64: continue
        win = a[max(0, i - 63):i + 64]
        c = Counter(win.tolist())
        if all(c[k] >= v for k, v in need.items()) and c[0] < 100 and sum(1 for x in win if 0 <= x <= 40) > 40:
            print(f, hex(base + max(0, i - 63) * w), win.tolist()[:80]); last = i
```

`tools/re-ui/panelmap.py`:

```py
"""panelmap.py ASM START END : walk the HandleInput panel-click code linearly and print, for every write of a
panel-state field (gd+0x2d284 page, +0x2d288 category, +0x2d28c slot, +0x2d298 subpage, +0x2d2f0 building type,
logic+0x54 tooltip id), the most recent grid column/row range checks (edx = column, ebp = row) and race checks.
Heuristic (linear, ignores control flow) - verify individual entries by reading the code."""
import re, sys
asm, lo, hi = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2], 16), int(sys.argv[3], 16)
st = {'col': [None, None], 'row': [None, None], 'race': None, 'page': None, 'cat': None}
line_re = re.compile(r'^\s+([0-9a-f]+):\s+(.*)$')
for ln in open(asm):
    m = line_re.match(ln)
    if not m: continue
    a = int(m.group(1), 16)
    if a < lo: continue
    if a > hi: break
    ins = m.group(2).split('  ')[-1].strip() if False else m.group(2)
    ins = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', ins)
    c = re.search(r'cmp (edx|ebp|eax|ebx),(0x[0-9a-f]+|\w+)$', ins)
    if c and c.group(2).startswith('0x'):
        v = int(c.group(2), 16)
        k = 'col' if c.group(1) == 'edx' else 'row' if c.group(1) == 'ebp' else None
        if k: st[k + '_last'] = v
    j = re.search(r'(jl|jg|jge|jle) ', ins)
    if j and 'col_last' in st:
        pass
    cm = re.search(r'cmp (\w+),(0x[0-9a-f]+)', ins)
    if cm and cm.group(1) in ('edx', 'ebp'):
        k = 'col' if cm.group(1) == 'edx' else 'row'
        pend = (k, int(cm.group(2), 16)); st['pend'] = pend
    elif j and st.get('pend'):
        k, v = st['pend']
        if j.group(1) in ('jl',): st[k][0] = v
        elif j.group(1) in ('jg',): st[k][1] = v
        st['pend'] = None
    if '0x11943e0]' in ins and 'cmp' in ins:
        r = re.search(r',(0x[0-9a-f]+|ebx|edi)$', ins); st['race'] = r.group(1) if r else '?'
    if re.search(r'cmp DWORD PTR \[e\w\w\+0x2d284\]', ins): st['page'] = ins.split(',')[-1]
    if re.search(r'cmp DWORD PTR \[e\w\w\+0x2d288\]', ins): st['cat'] = ins.split(',')[-1]
    w = re.search(r'mov DWORD PTR \[e\w\w\+(0x2d284|0x2d288|0x2d28c|0x2d298|0x2d2f0|0x54)\],(\w+)', ins)
    if w:
        print(f"{a:x} {w.group(1)}={w.group(2):6} col{st['col']} row{st['row']} page?{st['page']} cat?{st['cat']} race?{st['race']}")

```

`tools/re-ui/scan.py`:

```py
"""Find words in dumpall snapshots matching a change pattern.
python3 -I scan.py DIR_A DIR_B ... -- PATTERN  where PATTERN is a string of letters per snapshot:
same letter = equal value; for 'lin' mode values must step by a constant: use 'L' (e.g. 'aaLLL' means
snap0==snap1 then snap1..4 form a non-constant arithmetic progression).
Simple mode: pattern like 'aabcc' (equal letters == equal values, different letters == different values)."""
import sys, os, numpy as np
args = sys.argv[1:]
k = args.index('--'); dirs = args[:k]; pat = args[k+1]; width = int(args[k+2]) if len(args) > k+2 else 4
files = sorted(os.listdir(dirs[0]))
dt = {4: '<i4', 2: '<i2'}[width]
hits = 0
for f in files:
    base = int(f[:8], 16)
    raws = [open(os.path.join(d, f), 'rb').read() for d in dirs]
    for align in range(0, 4, width):
        arrs = []
        for r in raws:
            n = (len(r) - align) // width
            arrs.append(np.frombuffer(r, dtype=dt, count=n, offset=align).astype(np.int64))
        m = np.ones(len(arrs[0]), bool)
        for i in range(len(pat)):
            for j in range(i+1, len(pat)):
                if pat[i] == pat[j]:
                    m &= arrs[i] == arrs[j]
                else:
                    m &= arrs[i] != arrs[j]
        idx = np.nonzero(m)[0]
        for i in idx[:200]:
            print(f"{base + align + i*width:#x}: " + " ".join(str(a[i]) for a in arrs))
        hits += len(idx)
print("hits", hits, file=sys.stderr)

```

`tools/re-ui/strings.py`:

```py
"""strings.py DUMPDIR GFXOBJ ID... : resolve S3 text ids (table<<16 | index) like 0x5faaa0 does, from a dumpall
snapshot. GFXOBJ = render screen object (vtable 0x65a520); string table = [GFXOBJ+0x5f6b8].
ID 'all:T' prints every string of table T. Output is game text (data) - local use only, do not commit it."""
import os, struct, sys
d = sys.argv[1]
regs = []
for f in os.listdir(d):
    regs.append((int(f[:8], 16), open(os.path.join(d, f), 'rb').read()))
def rd(a, n=4):
    for b, data in regs:
        if b <= a and a + n <= b + len(data):
            return data[a - b:a - b + n]
    raise KeyError(hex(a))
u32 = lambda a: struct.unpack('<I', rd(a))[0]
u16 = lambda a: struct.unpack('<H', rd(a, 2))[0]
def cstr(a):
    out = b''
    while True:
        c = rd(a + len(out), 1)
        if c == b'\0' or len(out) > 300: return out.decode('cp1252', 'replace')
        out += c
gfx = int(sys.argv[2], 16); st = u32(gfx + 0x5f6b8); lang = u32(st + 0xc40)
def text(i):
    t, ix = i >> 16, i & 0xffff
    hdr = u32(st + 0x37c + t * 4); n = u16(hdr + 8)
    return cstr(u32(hdr + 0xc + (n * lang + ix) * 4) + u32(st + 0x264 + t * 4))
print('strtab', hex(st), 'lang', lang)
for a in sys.argv[3:]:
    if a.startswith('all:'):
        t = int(a[4:], 0); hdr = u32(st + 0x37c + t * 4); n = u16(hdr + 8)
        for ix in range(n):
            try: print(hex((t << 16) | ix), repr(text((t << 16) | ix)))
            except KeyError as e: print(hex((t << 16) | ix), 'unmapped', e)
    else:
        i = int(a, 16); print(hex(i), repr(text(i)))

```

`tools/re-units/finddw.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Find little-endian dwords in a PE image (S3.EXE) and print their VAs. Usage: finddw.py EXE 0xVAL [...]"""
import struct, sys
data = open(sys.argv[1], 'rb').read()
# section table: VA = file offset + 0x400000 for S3.EXE (all sections file-aligned to VA - 0x400000)
for v in sys.argv[2:]:
    pat = struct.pack('<I', int(v, 16))
    i = data.find(pat)
    hits = []
    while i >= 0:
        hits.append(hex(i + 0x400000))
        i = data.find(pat, i + 1)
    print(v, hits[:20])
```

`tools/res-tall/funcs.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Group instruction addresses (first word of each line of a file, hex, `addr:` ok) by enclosing function
(= the nearest preceding direct-call target in the listing) and print start, end (next call target) and count.
Usage: python -I tools/res-tall/funcs.py s3.asm sites.txt"""
import bisect, re, sys
pat = re.compile(r'^\s+([0-9a-f]+):\s+(.*)$')
call = re.compile(r'^call\s+0x([0-9a-f]+)$')
starts = set()
for l in open(sys.argv[1]):
    m = pat.match(l)
    if m:
        c = call.match(m.group(2))
        if c:
            starts.add(int(c.group(1), 16))
starts = sorted(starts)
groups = {}
for l in open(sys.argv[2]):
    w = l.split()
    if not w:
        continue
    a = int(w[0].rstrip(':'), 16)
    i = bisect.bisect_right(starts, a) - 1
    s = starts[i]
    e = starts[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(starts) else 0
    groups.setdefault((s, e), []).append(a)
for (s, e), v in sorted(groups.items()):
    print(f'{s:x} {e:x} {len(v)}')

```

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Map a memtrace dump (lines `next_eip last_addr`, hex) to the instructions of an objdump listing and classify
the last address against snapshot bases (offset from the base that contains it).
Usage: python -I tools/res-tall/map_trace.py s3.asm trace.txt [size_hex base_hex ...]"""

        insns.append((int(m.group(1), 16), m.group(2)))
nxt = {}
for i in range(len(insns) - 1):
    nxt[insns[i + 1][0]] = insns[i]
size = int(sys.argv[3], 16) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 0
bases = [int(b, 16) for b in sys.argv[4:]]
for l in open(sys.argv[2]).read().splitlines():
```

`tools/res-tall/sites.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""For each (address, value) pair print the byte offset of the 32-bit little-endian `value` inside the
instruction at `address` of the GOG S3.EXE (instruction length from the objdump listing). `value` may be negative.
For `shl r,6` sites use value `shl6`: prints the offset of the imm8 6 (`c1 /4 06`). Reads the exe as data only;
prints no code bytes.
Usage: python -I tools/res-tall/sites.py S3.EXE s3.asm addr:value [addr:value ...]"""
import re, struct, sys

exe = open(sys.argv[1], 'rb').read()
pe = struct.unpack_from('<I', exe, 0x3c)[0]
nsec = struct.unpack_from('<H', exe, pe + 6)[0]
optsz = struct.unpack_from('<H', exe, pe + 20)[0]
base = struct.unpack_from('<I', exe, pe + 24 + 28)[0]
secs = []
for i in range(nsec):
    o = pe + 24 + optsz + i * 40
    vsz, va, rsz, raw = struct.unpack_from('<IIII', exe, o + 8)
    secs.append((base + va, max(vsz, rsz), raw))


def rd(va, n):
    for s, sz, raw in secs:
        if s <= va < s + sz:
            return exe[raw + va - s: raw + va - s + n]
    raise KeyError(hex(va))


pat = re.compile(r'^\s+([0-9a-f]+):\s+(.*)$')
addrs = []
for l in open(sys.argv[2]):
    m = pat.match(l)
    if m:
        addrs.append(int(m.group(1), 16))
nxt = {addrs[i]: addrs[i + 1] for i in range(len(addrs) - 1)}
for item in sys.argv[3:]:
    a, v = item.split(':')
    a = int(a, 16)
    n = nxt[a] - a
    b = rd(a, n)
    if v == 'shl6':
        ok = n == 3 and b[0] == 0xc1 and (b[1] >> 3) & 7 == 4 and b[2] == 6
        print(f'{a:#x} shl6 len {n} {"OK" if ok else "MISMATCH"}')
        continue
    val = int(v, 16) & 0xffffffff
    offs = [k for k in range(n - 3) if struct.unpack_from('<I', b, k)[0] == val]
    print(f'{a:#x} off {offs} len {n} value {val:#x}')

```

`tools/res-tall/stride_scan.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Scan an objdump listing (intel, no raw bytes) for constants that look like render-snapshot grid strides
(130 rows per column, 0x30 bytes per cell, grid at +0x500): column displacements k*0x1860 (+ small row offsets,
+ optionally the 0x500 grid base) and index multiples k*130 (+-1..3), plus `shl r,6` (x65, part of x130).
Usage: python -I tools/res-tall/stride_scan.py s3.asm [lo hi] ... (address ranges, hex; default whole .text)"""
import re, sys

pat = re.compile(r'^\s+([0-9a-f]+):\s+(.*)$')
num = re.compile(r'(-?)0x([0-9a-f]+)\b')
ranges = []
args = sys.argv[2:]
for i in range(0, len(args), 2):
    ranges.append((int(args[i], 16), int(args[i + 1], 16)))
if not ranges:
    ranges = [(0x401000, 0x630000)]

TAB = {}
for sign in (1, -1):
    for base in (0, 0x500):
        for k in range(1, 8):
            for d in range(-0x90, 0x91):
                v = sign * (k * 0x1860 + d) + base
                if abs(v) > 0x100:
                    TAB.setdefault(v, []).append(f'{"-" if sign < 0 else ""}{k}col{d:+#x}{"+grid" if base else ""}')
    for k in range(1, 8):
        for d in (-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3):
            TAB.setdefault(sign * (k * 130 + d), []).append(f'{"-" if sign < 0 else ""}{k}*130{d:+d}')

def interesting(v):
    return TAB.get(v, [])

for l in open(sys.argv[1]):
    m = pat.match(l)
    if not m:
        continue
    a = int(m.group(1), 16)
    if not any(lo <= a < hi for lo, hi in ranges):
        continue
    txt = m.group(2)
    if re.match(r'(call|j[a-z]+)\s', txt):
        continue
    tags = []
    for s, h in num.findall(txt):
        v = int(h, 16)
        if v >= 0x80000000:
            v -= 1 << 32
        if s:
            v = -v
        tags += interesting(v)
    if re.search(r'\bshl\s+\w+,0x6$', txt):
        tags.append('shl6')
    if re.search(r'\bimul\b', txt):
        tags.append('imul')
    if tags:
        print(f'{a:x}: {txt:50s} {" ".join(sorted(set(tags)))}')

```

`tools/res-tall/x130.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Find `mov R,S; shl R,6; add R,S; ... lea X,[Y+R*2]` sequences (Y + S*130 = snapshot grid index) in an objdump
listing (intel, no raw bytes). Prints the shl address, the lea, and whether Y == S (x131, not the grid).
Usage: python -I tools/res-tall/x130.py s3.asm"""
import re, sys
pat = re.compile(r'^\s+([0-9a-f]+):\s+(.*)$')
ins = []
for l in open(sys.argv[1]):
    m = pat.match(l)
    if m:
        ins.append((int(m.group(1), 16), m.group(2).strip()))
for i, (a, s) in enumerate(ins):
    m = re.match(r'shl\s+(\w+),0x6$', s)
    if not m:
        continue
    r = m.group(1)
    add = None
    for j in range(i + 1, min(i + 4, len(ins))):
        m2 = re.match(rf'add\s+{r},(\w+)$', ins[j][1])
        if m2:
            add = (j, m2.group(1))
            break
    if not add:
        print(f'{a:x}: NOADD {s}')
        continue
    src = add[1]
    lea = None
    for j in range(add[0] + 1, min(add[0] + 8, len(ins))):
        m3 = re.match(rf'lea\s+(\w+),\[(\w+)\+{r}\*2\]$', ins[j][1])
        if m3:
            lea = (j, m3.group(1), m3.group(2))
            break
        if re.match(rf'\w+\s+{r},', ins[j][1]) and not ins[j][1].startswith('lea'):
            pass
    if not lea:
        nxt = ' | '.join(x[1] for x in ins[add[0] + 1: add[0] + 4])
        print(f'{a:x}: x65 src {src} NO-LEA*2  next: {nxt}')
        continue
    kind = 'x131' if lea[2] == src else 'GRID?'
    print(f'{a:x}: {kind} {lea[1]} = {lea[2]} + {src}*130   (lea at {ins[lea[0]][0]:x})')
```

`tools/res-zoom/snap_sites.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""List the code sites that reference the trailing fields of the render snapshot (offsets 0xc65c0..0xc7720)
in the GOG S3.EXE, with the byte offset of the 32-bit displacement/immediate inside each instruction.
Usage: python3 -I tools/res-zoom/snap_sites.py S3.EXE scratch/re-ui/s3.asm
Output: Rust table lines `(addr, disp_off, value)`. Reads the exe as data only."""
import re, struct, sys

exe = open(sys.argv[1], 'rb').read()
pe = struct.unpack_from('<I', exe, 0x3c)[0]
nsec = struct.unpack_from('<H', exe, pe + 6)[0]
optsz = struct.unpack_from('<H', exe, pe + 20)[0]
base = struct.unpack_from('<I', exe, pe + 24 + 28)[0]
secs = []
for i in range(nsec):
    o = pe + 24 + optsz + i * 40
    vsz, va, rsz, raw = struct.unpack_from('<IIII', exe, o + 8)
    secs.append((base + va, max(vsz, rsz), raw))

def rd(va, n):
    for s, sz, raw in secs:
        if s <= va < s + sz:
            return exe[raw + va - s: raw + va - s + n]
    raise KeyError(hex(va))

lines = open(sys.argv[2]).read().splitlines()
pat = re.compile(r'^\s+([0-9a-f]+):\s+(.*)$')
insns = []
for l in lines:
    m = pat.match(l)
    if m:
        insns.append((int(m.group(1), 16), m.group(2)))
val = re.compile(r'0x(c6[5-9a-f][0-9a-f]{2}|c7[0-7][0-9a-f]{2})\b')
for i, (a, txt) in enumerate(insns):
    if not (0x401000 <= a < 0x630000):
        continue
    for v in val.findall(txt):
        v = int(v, 16)
        if not (0xc65c0 <= v <= 0xc7720):
            continue
        if 'fc],0xc82828' in txt:
            continue
        n = insns[i + 1][0] - a
        b = rd(a, n)
        offs = [k for k in range(n - 3) if struct.unpack_from('<I', b, k)[0] == v]
        if len(offs) != 1:
            print(f'// AMBIGUOUS {a:#x} {txt} {offs}')
            continue
        print(f'    ({a:#x}, {offs[0]}, {v:#x}), // {txt.strip()}')
```
